5.2 The tenant's duty — AS 34.03.120
chunks.excerpt:
**AS 34.03.100(c):** for a **one- or two-family residence**, the parties may agree **in writing** that the tenant perform the landlord's duties under (a)(4), (5), (6), and (7); the tenant may agree to perform (a)(3) duties only **where rent exceeds $2,000 a month**; and they may agree in writing that the tenant perform specified repairs, maintenance, alterations, and remodeling — but **the tenant may not agree to maintain elevators**. Such agreements are allowed **only if entered into in good faith and not to evade the landlord's obligations**.

**AS 34.03.100(d):** for a dwelling unit **other than a single family residence**, a tenant-performs-work agreement is valid only if made in good faith and not to evade obligations, **set out in a separate writing signed by the parties and supported by adequate consideration**, and only if it does not diminish or affect the landlord's obligation to other tenants. **AS 34.03.100(e):** the landlord may not treat performance of such an agreement as a condition of an obligation under the rental agreement.

**AS 34.03.110** limits liability on transfer of the landlord's interest, on the terms it states.

### 5.2 The tenant's duty — AS 34.03.120

The tenant shall keep the occupied part clean and safe as conditions permit; dispose of ashes, rubbish, garbage, and waste cleanly and safely; keep plumbing fixtures clean as conditions permit; use facilities and appliances reasonably; and **maintain smoke and carbon monoxide detection devices** as AS 18.70.095 requires.

chunks.heading: 5.3 Access — AS 34.03.140
chunks.excerpt:
The tenant **may not**: deliberately or negligently destroy, deface, damage, impair, or remove part of the premises or knowingly permit another to; **unreasonably disturb** a neighbour's peaceful enjoyment or permit guests to; **change the locks** without the landlord's prior written agreement — except in an emergency when the landlord cannot be contacted after reasonable effort, and then the tenant must **within five days** give the landlord a set of keys and written notice of the change; unreasonably engage in or permit conduct resulting in a fee under a municipal ordinance adopted under AS 29.35.125; or allow occupancy to exceed the number allowed by law, by a covenant limiting the landlord's use, or by the rental agreement.

**AS 34.03.120(b):** the tenant may not knowingly engage at the premises in prostitution, illegal activity involving a place of prostitution, illegal activity involving alcoholic beverages, illegal activity involving gambling or promoting gambling, or illegal activity involving a controlled substance or imitation controlled substance — or knowingly permit others on the premises to do so.

**AS 34.03.120(c):** on terminating, the tenant shall leave the premises in **substantially the same condition, except normal wear and tear**, as at the beginning — including, **in the landlord's discretion, professionally cleaning the carpets if the carpets were professionally cleaned immediately before the tenancy began**.

### 5.3 Access — AS 34.03.140

chunks.heading: 5.4 Ending a tenancy
chunks.excerpt:
**(a)** The tenant may not **unreasonably withhold consent** for the landlord to enter to inspect, make necessary or agreed repairs, decorations, alterations, or improvements, supply necessary or agreed services, remove the landlord's personal property not covered by a written rental agreement, or **exhibit the unit to prospective or actual purchasers, mortgagees, tenants, workers, or contractors**.

**(b)** The landlord **may enter without consent in an emergency**.

**(c)** The landlord **may not abuse the right of access or use it to harass**. Except in an emergency or where impracticable, the landlord shall give **at least 24 hours notice** of intention to enter, and may enter **only at reasonable times and with the tenant's consent**.

**(d)** The landlord has **no right of access** except as .140 permits, by court order, or as AS 34.03.230(b) permits — unless the tenant has abandoned or surrendered the premises.

**AS 34.03.300** supplies the remedies. If the **tenant** refuses lawful access, the landlord may obtain injunctive relief or terminate, recovering **actual damages or one month's rent, whichever is greater**, and giving at least **10 days'** written notice if terminating. If the **landlord** enters unlawfully, enters lawfully but unreasonably, or makes repeated otherwise-lawful demands that unreasonably harass, the tenant may obtain injunctive relief or terminate, recovering **actual damages or one month's rent, whichever is greater, plus court costs and reasonable attorney fees**, on 10 days' written notice.

**This is a listing problem, not only a management problem.** Selling an occupied rental means 24 hours notice and the tenant's consent for each showing. Build it into the listing conversation before the sign goes up.

chunks.heading: Checkpoint 5.1

**AS 34.03.210** gives the tenant remedies for the landlord's **unlawful ouster, exclusion, or diminution of service** — the provision that answers a landlord who changes the locks or shuts off the heat. **AS 34.03.180** covers the landlord's wrongful failure to supply heat, water, hot water, or essential services; **AS 34.03.160** the landlord's noncompliance generally; **AS 34.03.170** failure to deliver possession; **AS 34.03.190** the landlord's noncompliance as a defence to an action for possession or rent; and **AS 34.03.200** fire or casualty damage.

**AS 34.03.310 — retaliation prohibited.** Except as (c) and (d) provide, a landlord **may not retaliate** by increasing rent, decreasing services, or bringing or threatening to bring an action for possession after the tenant has complained to the landlord of a violation of AS 34.03.100, sought to enforce rights and remedies under the chapter, or organized or become a member of a **tenants' union** or similar organization.

#### Checkpoint 5.1

A month-to-month tenant is four days late with rent. The landlord serves a seven-day notice on the fifth day and the tenant pays in full on day six. What is the tenant's position?

chunks.heading: 6. Property management under 12 AAC 64.550 – .580
chunks.excerpt:
*Answer:* The tenancy continues. **AS 34.03.220(b)** terminates the tenancy only if the tenant **fails to pay rent in full within seven days** after the landlord's written notice of nonpayment and intention to terminate. Payment in full on day six is inside the period, so the tenancy does not terminate and the landlord may not recover possession on that default. Note the landlord's two other options in the subsection: only one written notice of default need be given as to any one default, and a landlord who has given notice may accept a **partial** payment and extend the eviction date accordingly.

## 6. Property management under 12 AAC 64.550 – .580

### 6.1 The contract

**12 AAC 64.550(a):** a licensee engaged in property management shall conduct property management activity **in the registered name of the real estate company** with which the licensee is affiliated.

**12 AAC 64.550(b):** a licensee **may not conduct property management activity for another person without a prior written property management contract**, which must at minimum include:

1. the **specific responsibilities** of the property manager;
2. the **authority and powers** given by the owner to the manager;
3. the **period** of the agreement; and
4. the **management fee**.

Compare **AS 08.88.341**, which requires management contracts to be in writing and signed by both, with **exclusive** management contracts carrying a **definite expiration date** extendable only in writing signed by the client.

**12 AAC 64.550(c):** a manager may transfer funds between two or more accounts maintained for the **same** owner **only with written authorization** from that owner, and must make entries **fully identifying the transaction in each ledger affected**.

chunks.heading: 6.2 The provision that connects the two halves of this module
chunks.excerpt:
**12 AAC 64.550(d):** **selling or exchanging** a property subject to an existing management contract must be authorised by **specific language in the management contract or by a separate listing agreement**. Managing a property is not authority to sell it.

**12 AAC 64.550(e):** a licensee **who owns rental property** must disclose in writing to **all tenants and prospective tenants** that the licensee holds a real estate licence, and the name of the affiliated company. Compare **12 AAC 64.130(9)**, the same principle in a sales transaction.

### 6.2 The provision that connects the two halves of this module

**12 AAC 64.560. COMPLIANCE WITH UNIFORM RESIDENTIAL LANDLORD AND TENANT ACT.** "Failure of a licensee engaged in property management to deposit prepaid rents or security deposits in a trust account as required by AS 34.03 (Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act) is considered **fraudulent or dishonest conduct** within the meaning of AS 08.88.071(a)(3)(A)(iv)."

Read that carefully. A landlord who mishandles a deposit faces the AS 34.03.070(d) penalty of up to twice the amount withheld. A **licensee** who does it faces that **and** a disciplinary proceeding in which the failure is already characterised as fraudulent or dishonest conduct. The rules are not parallel; the licensee's exposure is greater.

**12 AAC 64.220(b)** supplies the bookkeeping: for each management contract, a transaction code identified with a specific landlord or property, a ledger tracking the landlord's funds received and disbursed, and **each tenant's funds tracked through a related but separate transaction code and ledger**.

chunks.heading: 6.3 Managing property you own
chunks.excerpt:
**12 AAC 64.240(c):** the property management fee is disbursed from the trust account on a **regular monthly basis**, after that month's receipts are collected and that month's expenses disbursed.

### 6.3 Managing property you own

**12 AAC 64.570** governs a licensee who owns rental property, and it is detailed because the conflict is obvious.

**(a)** A licensee with **sole ownership** of rental property may manage it through the employing broker, or employ another broker or property manager to do so. Notwithstanding 12 AAC 64.550, the licensee or the owner's broker need not keep records or files of rental agreements or rental transactions **if the licensee being employed keeps them**.

**(b)** In addition to the AS 08.88.615 duties from module 01, such a licensee must:

1. disclose to **each prospective lessee or tenant** (A) the items in **AS 08.88.615(a)(6) – (8)**, and (B) the licensee's **ownership**, in accordance with **AS 08.88.391** — the conflict of interest disclosure, verbal and then written, beginning with the words "Disclosure of Conflict of Interest." underlined and in bold; and
2. provide the licensee's **broker** with, for each property owned: (A) ownership position and percentage; (B) copies of all financial records and rental agreements; (C) an update whenever that information changes; (D) **security deposits and prepaid rents held in the broker's trust account** in compliance with 12 AAC 64.200, **or** held in a licensee's privately owned trust account **to which the broker has access for oversight and review** — where "prepaid rent" means money demanded at the initiation of the tenancy to ensure rent will be paid, and **does not include the first month's rent or money received as security for damage**; and (E) **written documentation** to refund

**(c)** Notwithstanding 12 AAC 64.200, **rents and other incidental income may be paid directly to the licensee as lessor** and need not go into the broker's trust account. Deposits are treated differently from rent, and this is the distinction to hold onto.

**(d)** The duration of the licensee–lessee relationship must meet **AS 08.88.660**.

**(e)** The Commission may impose a disciplinary sanction under AS 08.88.071 for violating the section, and a **recovery fund claim** under AS 08.88.460 may be filed by a person whose claim is based on fraud, misrepresentation, or deceit and who suffered a loss as a result.

**(f)** Where the property is owned by a **partnership, corporation, limited liability company, or other legal entity** in which a licensee has an interest, the licensee must disclose the ownership position and the entity to the broker. **AS 08.88.351(a)(4):** a broker authorised by an association's board to collect, control, or disburse association funds must keep a **separate account in a financial institution** for them.

**AS 08.88.351(b)(4):** a licensee must **promptly deposit** association funds or periodic assessment proceeds into a community association **reserve** account or **operating** account — and if at any time the operating account holds more than is estimated to be needed for the **next three months'** budgeted expenditures, transfer the excess to the reserve account **as soon as practicable**.

#### Checkpoint 6.1

A licensee manages a fourplex she owns, holding tenants' security deposits in her own account. What must she do to comply with 12 AAC 64.570(b)(2)(D), and what happens under 12 AAC 64.560 if she simply keeps them in her personal chequing account?

chunks.heading: Key terms
chunks.excerpt:
*Answer:* She may keep the deposits in her own trust account only if it is a **trust account to which her broker has access for oversight and review** — **12 AAC 64.570(b)(2)(D)** gives her the choice of the broker's trust account in compliance with 12 AAC 64.200 or her own on that condition. She must also give the broker her ownership position and percentage, copies of all financial records and rental agreements, updates when they change, and written documentation for any refund or deduction, and must disclose her ownership to every prospective tenant under 12 AAC 64.550(e) and AS 08.88.391. A **personal chequing account** is neither. Under **12 AAC 64.560**, failing to deposit prepaid rents or security deposits in a trust account as AS 34.03 requires is **fraudulent or dishonest conduct** within AS 08.88.071(a)(3)(A)(iv) — a disciplinary matter on top of the AS 34.03.070(d) exposure to twice the amount withheld.

## Key terms

**Automatic lapse** — the AS 08.88.095(e) consequence of not completing the 30 post-licensing hours within one year and certifying within 30 days after.

**Non-noticed audit** — the 12 AAC 64.135(b) audit conducted without prior notice; a granted 24-hour delay means the auditor seals the records.

**Premises condition statement** — the AS 34.03.020(e) document that becomes part of the rental agreement and is presumptive evidence of condition under AS 34.03.335.

**Recovery fund** — the consumer fund capped at **$50,000 per licensee** by AS 08.88.475(a), distributed pro rata among claimants.

**Retaliatory conduct** — the AS 34.03.310 prohibition on raising rent, cutting services, or bringing or threatening a possession action after protected tenant activity.

chunks.heading: Practice problems
chunks.excerpt:
**Two months' periodic rent** — the AS 34.03.070(a) cap on prepaid rent plus security deposit, inapplicable above $2,000 a month, with a separate one-month pet deposit under (h).

## Practice problems

**Problem 1.** A property manager holds a $2,400 deposit on a unit renting for $1,200. The tenant gives proper 30-day notice, moves out 31 August, and the manager finds $310 of tenant-caused damage. When must the notice and refund be mailed, and what is the exposure for getting it wrong?

*Working:* The tenant gave notice complying with AS 34.03.290, so the base deadline is **14 days** — but because costs are deducted for damages from the tenant's noncompliance with AS 34.03.120, AS 34.03.070(g) gives **30 days**, to **30 September**. The itemised written notice goes to the tenant's last known address with the $2,090 balance. A **wilful** failure to comply with .070(b) exposes the landlord to up to **twice the amount withheld** under .070(d) — and because a licensee is involved, 12 AAC 64.560 makes a failure to hold the money in trust as AS 34.03 requires **fraudulent or dishonest conduct** under AS 08.88.071(a)(3)(A)(iv).

**Problem 2.** A salesperson licensed 2 February 2026 completes 20 hours of the post-licensing education by February 2027 and nothing more.

*Working:* AS 08.88.095(a) requires **30** hours within one year. She did not complete them and cannot certify under (c). Under **AS 08.88.095(e)** the licence **automatically lapses 30 days after the end of the one-year period** — around 4 March 2027. The Commission may reinstate under AS 08.88.241, which covers a licence lapsed less than 24 months. Any licensed activity after the lapse is activity without a licence, which AS 08.88.401(g) makes a class A misdemeanor.

chunks.heading: Practice problems
chunks.excerpt:
**Problem 3.** A landlord in an undeveloped rural area rents a dry cabin with no running water. The tenant demands the landlord install plumbing under AS 34.03.100(a)(5).

*Working:* **AS 34.03.100(b)** provides that a landlord of a single family residence in an undeveloped rural area, or where public sewer or water has never been connected, is not liable for breach of (a)(3) or (a)(5) **if the unit did not have running water, hot water, sewage, or sanitary facilities from a private system at the beginning of the rental agreement**. A dry cabin that was dry at the outset falls within it. Note the limits: it applies to a **single family residence**, and it excuses what was never there — not a system that has been allowed to fail.

**Problem 4.** A broker receives a Commission inspection notice on Monday for an inspection Wednesday at 9:00 a.m.

*Working:* 12 AAC 64.135(a) requires **at least 72 hours' advance notice** for an inspection, and this is roughly 48. The broker may raise it. But note that (b) allows a **complete audit with or without prior notice**, so a broker who treats the notice rule as a shield is misreading the regulation. The records required are broad — earnest money agreements, listing agreements, trust account records, disbursal records, **communications regarding transactions**, and closing statements for all principals.

**Problem 5.** Your seller's tenant refuses to allow showings, saying he never agreed to any.

chunks.heading: Module summary
chunks.excerpt:
*Working:* Under AS 34.03.140(a) the tenant **may not unreasonably withhold consent** to entry to exhibit the unit to prospective purchasers. But .140(c) requires **at least 24 hours notice**, entry **only at reasonable times and with the tenant's consent**, and prohibits abusing access or using it to harass. If the tenant refuses lawful access, AS 34.03.300(a) gives the landlord injunctive relief or termination on 10 days' notice, plus actual damages or one month's rent, whichever is greater. Practically: schedule showings in blocks with more than 24 hours notice, and settle it with the tenant before listing.

**Problem 6.** A buyer's licensee learns a claim was paid from the recovery fund against a licensee he cooperates with. What does that tell him?

*Working:* An award means someone obtained a final judgment, arbitration award, or settlement and claimed against the fund, which is capped at **$50,000 per licensee** under AS 08.88.475(a) and distributed pro rata under (b). Under **AS 08.88.071(b)** the Commission **may suspend** that licensee's licence, lifting the suspension only on an agreed repayment arrangement. Under AS 08.88.490 the fund is **subrogated**. And under AS 08.88.071(a)(5), disciplinary action is published in a newspaper of general circulation in the locale of the offender's registered principal office.

## Module summary

**AS 08.88.161 is broad**: selling, listing, collecting rent, property management, community association management, assisting, holding out, and even attempting all require a licence, and violating it is a class A misdemeanor.

chunks.heading: Module assessment
chunks.excerpt:
**A salesperson needs 40 approved hours, age 19, E&O insurance, the examination, and an application within six months** — with the education completed within the **18 months** before application under 12 AAC 64.063(a)(2).

**AS 08.88.095(e) lapses a new licence automatically** if the 30 post-licensing hours are not completed within one year and certified within 30 days after. Diary it on day one.

**Discipline runs on AS 08.88.071(a)(3) and 12 AAC 64.130**, and two regulations — 12 AAC 64.260 for trust accounts and 12 AAC 64.560 for tenant money — pre-characterise specified failures as fraudulent or dishonest conduct.

**Audits may be non-noticed**, and a granted 24-hour delay means the auditor seals the records.

**The recovery fund caps at $50,000 per licensee** and comes back at the licensee through suspension and subrogation. **E&O lapses suspend the licence as of the day coverage stopped.**

**AS 34.03 caps deposits at two months' rent** (plus one month for a non-service-animal pet), requires trust deposit with per-tenant accounting, and imposes **14- or 30-day** refund deadlines with a **double-the-amount-withheld** penalty for a wilful failure.

**Access requires 24 hours notice and consent** except in an emergency — which makes selling an occupied rental a conversation to have before the sign goes up.

**Termination notice depends on the ground**: 24 hours to five days for deliberate substantial damage over $400 or illegal activity, ten days with a cure right for material noncompliance, seven days for unpaid rent, five days for a tenant-caused utility shutoff, and 14 or 30 days to end a periodic tenancy.

## Module assessment

chunks.heading: Module completion
chunks.excerpt:
Complete the module assessment. The mastery threshold is 80 percent, a StateCourse instructional standard rather than an Alaska requirement. An unsuccessful attempt returns an alternate explanation and a different item set on the same material, which must be answered correctly before the module is recorded as complete.

## Module completion

Completion requires all six instructional sections, all six checkpoints, and the module assessment. This module carries 6 of the 40 contact hours prescribed by 12 AAC 64.063(c).

lessons.title: Alaska Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense - Module 08

chunks.heading: Alaska Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense - Module 08
chunks.excerpt:
# Alaska Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense - Module 08

## Federal fair housing and RESPA laws

**Topic:** 12 AAC 64.063(c)(8)
**Contact hours:** 2 (a contact hour is a minimum of 50 minutes of instruction — 12 AAC 64.063(g)(1))
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Not certified. No Alaska prelicense credit is available for this course.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this module the student will be able to:

- State the seven federal protected classes, identify the practices the Fair Housing Act prohibits, and apply them to ordinary licensee conduct.
- Identify the Alaska classes that go beyond the federal list, and explain why a fair housing violation is a licence matter under 12 AAC 64.130(19).
- State what RESPA section 8 prohibits, what section 9 prohibits, and what an affiliated business arrangement requires.
- Recognise the settlement disclosures RESPA and Regulation Z require and the timing that governs them.

## Timed sequence

| Activity | Contact hours | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Section 1 — fair housing: federal law and the Alaska overlay | 1 | Section recorded as viewed, checkpoint answered |
| Section 2 — RESPA and settlement services | 1 | Section recorded as viewed, checkpoint answered |
| **Total** | **2** | Module assessment passed |

## 1. Fair housing: federal law and the Alaska overlay

### 1.1 The federal statutes

**The Civil Rights Act of 1866, 42 U.S.C. 1982.** All citizens have the same right "to inherit, purchase, lease, sell, hold, and convey real and personal property." It bars **racial** discrimination, has **no exemptions**, and is enforced by suit in federal court. It is the oldest of these laws and the reason the Fair Housing Act's exemptions never cover race.

chunks.heading: 1.2 The seven federal protected classes
chunks.excerpt:
**The Fair Housing Act — Title VIII of the Civil Rights Act of 1968, 42 U.S.C. 3601–3631**, amended in 1974 to add sex and in 1988 to add disability and familial status. Implementing regulations are at **24 C.F.R. parts 100–115**.

### 1.2 The seven federal protected classes

**Race. Color. Religion. National origin. Sex. Disability. Familial status.**

**Sex** includes sexual harassment in housing (24 C.F.R. 100.600). HUD administers the Act as prohibiting discrimination because of **sexual orientation and gender identity** as forms of sex discrimination.

**Disability** — 42 U.S.C. 3602(h) — means a physical or mental impairment substantially limiting one or more major life activities, a record of such an impairment, or being regarded as having one. It expressly **excludes current illegal use of or addiction to a controlled substance**.

**Familial status** — 42 U.S.C. 3602(k) — one or more individuals under 18 domiciled with a parent or a person with legal custody, or with the designee of such a person; and it protects a person who is **pregnant** or in the process of securing legal custody of a minor.

### 1.3 What the Act prohibits

**42 U.S.C. 3604:**

chunks.heading: 1.4 Three practices worth naming
chunks.excerpt:
- **Refusing to sell or rent**, or refusing to negotiate, or otherwise making a dwelling unavailable, because of a protected class.
- **Discriminating in terms, conditions, or privileges**, or in services or facilities.
- **Discriminatory advertising** — making, printing, or publishing any notice, statement, or advertisement indicating a **preference, limitation, or discrimination**. Note that this provision has **no exemptions at all**: an owner whose transaction is otherwise exempt still may not advertise discriminatorily.
- **Representing that a dwelling is unavailable** when it is in fact available.
- **Blockbusting** — inducing or attempting to induce a sale or rental for profit by representations about the entry into the neighbourhood of persons of a protected class.
- **Refusing a reasonable accommodation** in rules, policies, practices, or services when necessary to afford a person with a disability equal opportunity to use and enjoy a dwelling.
- **Refusing to permit a reasonable modification** of the premises at the tenant's expense when necessary for full enjoyment.
- Failing to meet the **design and construction requirements** for covered multifamily dwellings first occupied after 13 March 1991.

**42 U.S.C. 3605 — discrimination in residential real-estate-related transactions**, including making or purchasing loans and in appraising residential real property.

**42 U.S.C. 3606 — discrimination in brokerage services**, including denying access to or membership in a multiple listing service or other facility relating to the business of selling or renting dwellings.

**42 U.S.C. 3617 — coercion, intimidation, threats, or interference** with a person exercising or enjoying a fair housing right, or aiding another to do so.

### 1.4 Three practices worth naming

chunks.heading: 1.5 Assistance animals
chunks.excerpt:
**Steering** — directing prospects toward or away from neighbourhoods based on a protected class. It is often done gently and with good intentions: "you'd be more comfortable over here," "let me show you where families like yours live." Both sentences are steering. **Show what meets the client's stated criteria, and let the client choose.**

**Redlining** — refusing or varying the terms of lending or insurance based on the racial or ethnic composition of an area rather than the merits of the applicant or the property.

**Blockbusting** — profiting from inducing sales through representations about who is moving in.

### 1.5 Assistance animals

An assistance animal is not a pet. Under the Fair Housing Act, allowing an assistance animal for a person with a disability who needs it is a **reasonable accommodation** — including in housing with a no-pets policy — and **no pet deposit or pet fee may be charged for it**.

This connects directly to module 07. **AS 34.03.070(h)** permits an additional deposit of up to one month's rent for a pet **that is not a service animal**, and .070(i)(2) defines a service animal as one individually trained to do work or perform tasks directly related to and for the benefit of an individual with a disability. The Alaska statute and the federal accommodation duty point the same way: the animal that is there because of a disability is not the animal you charge for.

### 1.6 The exemptions, and why they rarely help a licensee

**42 U.S.C. 3603(b)** exempts, from most of section 3604:

chunks.heading: 1.7 Enforcement
chunks.excerpt:
- The sale or rental of a **single-family house by an owner** who owns no more than three such houses at a time, **provided** the owner does not use a real estate licensee's services and does not use discriminatory advertising, with further limits on frequency; and
- Rooms or units in a dwelling with **no more than four independent family units**, one of which the **owner occupies** — the "Mrs Murphy" exemption.

**42 U.S.C. 3607** provides exemptions for religious organizations and private clubs on the terms stated, and for **housing for older persons** meeting the statutory criteria (which is the lawful way to have age-restricted housing without violating familial status).

Three limits make these of little use to a licensee:

1. The single-family exemption **evaporates the moment a real estate licensee is used** — which is every transaction you are in.
2. **No exemption reaches the advertising prohibition** in 3604(c).
3. **No exemption reaches 42 U.S.C. 1982**, so racial discrimination is never exempt.

### 1.7 Enforcement

A complaint may be filed with **HUD** within **one year** of the alleged discriminatory housing practice — 42 U.S.C. 3610(a)(1)(A)(i). A private civil action may be brought in federal or state court within **two years** of the occurrence or termination of the practice — 42 U.S.C. 3613(a)(1)(A). The Department of Justice may bring a pattern-or-practice action under 42 U.S.C. 3614.

Remedies can include actual and punitive damages, injunctive relief, attorney fees, and civil penalties.

### 1.8 The Alaska overlay

chunks.heading: 1.8 The Alaska overlay
1.9 What this means in practice
chunks.excerpt:
r discrimination based on race, color, religion, physical or mental disability, sex, or national origin, or an intention to make one.

**AS 18.80.250** separately prohibits discriminatory financing practices, adding **parenthood** to the list of grounds and covering discriminatory inquiries by lenders.

Three things to carry away:

**Alaska protects classes federal law does not** — marital status, changes in marital status, parenthood, and age appear in Alaska's provisions and are not federal protected classes under the Fair Housing Act. Alaska's list is what governs your conduct here.

**Paragraph (3) prohibits the inquiry itself.** You do not need to act on the information; asking or recording it is the violation. That is a stricter rule than a licensee trained on federal law alone will expect, and it should change how intake forms and casual conversation are handled.

**Paragraph (5) extends to association** — refusing inspection because of the protected class of someone associated with the prospect is covered.

**And it is a licence matter. 12 AAC 64.130(19)** makes "being found guilty of violating **local, state, or federal fair housing laws**" a ground for revocation or suspension of an Alaska real estate licence. Local ordinances count too, and several Alaska municipalities have their own.

### 1.9 What this means in practice

chunks.heading: Checkpoint 1.1
chunks.excerpt:
Show every client the properties that meet their stated criteria. Answer questions about schools, crime, and demographics by naming the sources where the client can look, not by characterising a neighbourhood. Take the same steps for every prospect: same qualification questions, same follow-up, same access. Do not accept a listing instruction to exclude anyone. Advertise the property, never the buyer or tenant. Treat a request for an accommodation or modification as a process to work through rather than a request to refuse. And keep records showing you did all of this the same way every time — the file is the defence.

#### Checkpoint 1.1

A seller instructs you not to show the house to families with young children because the stairs are steep. What do you tell her, and which provisions apply?

*Answer:* Tell her you cannot follow the instruction and that she cannot lawfully give it. Refusing to show or sell because of **familial status** violates **42 U.S.C. 3604(a) and (d)**; accepting or retaining a listing with the understanding that a person may be discriminated against is separately unlawful under **AS 18.80.240(4)**; and refusing to allow inspection on a protected ground violates **AS 18.80.240(5)**. Her concern about the stairs is answered by disclosing the condition to every prospect and letting each family decide — which is also what **12 AAC 64.130(14)** requires of you as to a known material defect. And under **12 AAC 64.130(19)**, being found guilty of violating local, state, or federal fair housing law is grounds to revoke your licence.

## 2. RESPA and settlement services

### 2.1 The statute and the rule

chunks.heading: 2.2 Section 8 — the one that ends careers
chunks.excerpt:
The **Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act**, 12 U.S.C. 2601–2617, is implemented by **Regulation X, 12 C.F.R. part 1024**, administered by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.

**12 U.S.C. 2601(b)** states the purposes: more effective advance disclosure of settlement costs, elimination of **kickbacks and referral fees** that unnecessarily increase the costs of settlement services, a reduction in the amounts homebuyers must place in escrow accounts, and reform of local title recordkeeping.

RESPA applies to **federally related mortgage loans** secured by a first or subordinate lien on residential real property designed for occupancy by one to four families. Business-purpose loans and certain other categories are excluded — see 12 C.F.R. 1024.5.

### 2.2 Section 8 — the one that ends careers

**Section 8(a), 12 U.S.C. 2607(a):** "No person shall give and no person shall accept any fee, kickback, or thing of value pursuant to any agreement or understanding, oral or otherwise, that business incident to or a part of a real estate settlement service involving a federally related mortgage loan **shall be referred to any person**."

**Section 8(b), 12 U.S.C. 2607(b):** no person shall give and no person shall accept any portion, split, or percentage of any charge made or received for a settlement service **other than for services actually performed** — the prohibition on **unearned fees** and **fee splitting**.

chunks.heading: 2.2 Section 8 — the one that ends careers
chunks.excerpt:
**Section 8(c)** permits, among other things: payment of a fee by a lender to its duly appointed agent for services actually performed; payment to any person of a **bona fide salary or compensation for services actually performed**; payments pursuant to **cooperative brokerage and referral arrangements between real estate agents and brokers** — the provision that makes ordinary commission splitting between cooperating brokerages lawful; and **affiliated business arrangements** meeting the section's conditions.

**Section 8(d), 12 U.S.C. 2607(d):** violation is punishable by a **fine of up to $10,000, imprisonment for up to one year, or both**, and by liability to the person charged in an amount equal to **three times the amount of the charge** paid for the settlement service.

A "thing of value" is construed broadly: money, discounts, salaries, commissions, fees, duplicate payments of a charge, stock, dividends, distributions of partnership profits, retained earnings, services at reduced rates, trips, tickets, meals, opportunities to participate in a money-making programme, and the payment of another person's expenses.

**The practical rules for a licensee:**

chunks.heading: 2.3 Affiliated business arrangements
chunks.excerpt:
- Do not accept anything of value for **directing** business to a title company, lender, inspector, warranty company, or escrow agent.
- **Marketing services agreements** are lawful only if the payment is for **actual marketing services at fair market value** and is not tied to referrals. They are heavily scrutinised, and the enforcement history is unkind to arrangements that look like payment for volume.
- **Co-marketing** must be a genuine split of a real cost, in proportion to actual benefit.
- Ordinary **cooperative brokerage compensation** between real estate brokerages is expressly permitted by section 8(c).

### 2.3 Affiliated business arrangements

Where a licensee or brokerage has an ownership or other beneficial interest in a settlement service provider and refers business to it, section 8(c)(4) and **12 C.F.R. 1024.15** permit the arrangement only if:

1. the person referring gives the consumer a written **affiliated business arrangement disclosure at or before the time of referral**, in the form Regulation X prescribes, describing the relationship and the estimated charge or range;
2. the consumer is **not required to use** the affiliated provider — with narrow exceptions such as an attorney or an appraiser the lender selects; and
3. the only thing of value received is a **return on the ownership interest**, not a payment tied to referrals.

Compare **12 AAC 64.940(a)** from module 05: an Alaska broker must disclose in writing to the broker's principal the dollar amount or percentage of any rebate, compensation, or fee **paid to another broker** in connection with a sales transaction. Federal law and Alaska law each require disclosure of a different thing. Doing one does not satisfy the other.

### 2.4 Section 9 — title insurance

chunks.heading: 2.5 Escrow accounts and servicing
chunks.excerpt:
**12 U.S.C. 2608:** a **seller may not require**, directly or indirectly, as a condition of selling the property, that the buyer purchase **title insurance from any particular title company**. A seller who violates it is liable to the buyer for **three times all charges made for the title insurance**.

### 2.5 Escrow accounts and servicing

**12 U.S.C. 2609** limits the amount a lender may require a borrower to deposit into an escrow account for taxes and insurance, and requires an **initial escrow account statement** and **annual escrow account statements**. The cushion is limited to what Regulation X permits.

**12 U.S.C. 2605** governs servicing transfers, requiring notice to the borrower when servicing of the loan is transferred, and establishes the borrower's right to submit a **qualified written request** and the servicer's obligations to respond.

### 2.6 The disclosures and their timing

For most closed-end consumer credit transactions secured by real property, the **TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure** rules apply:

**Loan Estimate** — provided within **three business days** of the consumer's application, under 12 C.F.R. 1026.19(e).

**Closing Disclosure** — the consumer must **receive** it at least **three business days before consummation**, under 12 C.F.R. 1026.19(f). Three changes restart the three-day period: an increase in the APR beyond the tolerance, a change in the loan product, and the addition of a prepayment penalty.

**Special information booklet** — under 12 U.S.C. 2604 and 12 C.F.R. 1024.6, provided to applicants for a federally related mortgage loan within the time the rule specifies.

**Affiliated business arrangement disclosure** — at or before referral, as above.

chunks.heading: 2.7 Where RESPA meets Alaska law
chunks.excerpt:
For a licensee the operational point is the three-business-day rule. Build it into the closing calendar, and understand that a late change to a material loan term can move the closing date whether or not anyone wants it moved.

### 2.7 Where RESPA meets Alaska law

**12 AAC 64.130(7)** makes paying referral fees, sharing commissions, or otherwise compensating a person prohibited from receiving compensation under **AS 08.88.401(b)** grounds for revocation or suspension.

**AS 08.88.401(d)** prohibits a licensee from knowingly paying any part of a fee or commission to an unlicensed person (with the AS 08.88.401(e) exceptions), to another licensee **except through the licensee's responsible broker**, or to another licensee knowing that licensee will pass it to someone unlicensed.

So a referral arrangement in Alaska has to clear **both** gates. RESPA section 8 asks whether a thing of value was given for a referral of settlement service business. Alaska licence law asks whether the recipient is a person who may lawfully receive compensation, and whether it moved through the responsible broker. An arrangement can be lawful under one and unlawful under the other, and a licensee has to satisfy both.

#### Checkpoint 2.1

A title company offers to pay your brokerage $600 a month toward the cost of a shared advertisement in which each party's space is roughly equal, and the advertisement's fair market cost is $700. Separately, the title company offers a $50 gift card for each closing you send it. Analyse each under section 8.

chunks.heading: Key terms
chunks.excerpt:
*Answer:* The advertisement can be lawful; the gift cards cannot. A genuine **co-marketing** split is permitted where each party pays for the space it actually receives at **fair market value** and the payment is not tied to referrals — but $600 of a $700 advertisement for roughly half the space is not that. Paying more than the fair value of what it receives makes the excess a **thing of value** captured by **RESPA section 8(a)**, and to the extent it is a share of a charge unmatched by services actually performed, by **section 8(b)**. Restructure it to a true half, or decline. The **$50 per closing** is a fee for the referral of settlement service business on its face — squarely section 8(a), exposing a fine up to $10,000, up to a year's imprisonment, and treble the charge under section 8(d), and separately reaching AS 08.88.401(d) and 12 AAC 64.130(7). Decline it outright.

## Key terms

**Affiliated business arrangement** — a referral to a settlement provider in which the referrer has an interest; lawful only with written disclosure at or before referral, no required use, and a return limited to the ownership interest.

**Blockbusting** — inducing sales or rentals for profit by representations about the entry of persons of a protected class; prohibited by 42 U.S.C. 3604(e) and AS 18.80.240(6).

**Familial status** — one or more individuals under 18 with a parent or custodian or the custodian's designee, and persons who are pregnant or securing legal custody.

**Reasonable accommodation** — a change in rules, policies, practices, or services necessary to give a person with a disability equal opportunity to use and enjoy a dwelling.

**Steering** — directing prospects toward or away from areas based on a protected class.

chunks.heading: Practice problems
chunks.excerpt:
**Thing of value** — construed broadly under RESPA section 8; not limited to cash.

## Practice problems

**Problem 1.** A prospective tenant with a mobility disability asks to install a grab bar in the bathroom and to be allowed a trained service dog in a no-pets building.

*Working:* The grab bar is a **reasonable modification** at the tenant's expense under 42 U.S.C. 3604(f)(3)(A); the landlord may, in appropriate cases, condition permission on restoration at the end of the tenancy. The service dog is a **reasonable accommodation** under 3604(f)(3)(B) — the no-pets policy yields, and **no pet deposit or fee may be charged**. In Alaska, AS 34.03.070(h) permits an additional pet deposit only for a pet **that is not a service animal**, so the statute reaches the same result. Refusing either is a Fair Housing Act violation and, under 12 AAC 64.130(19), a licence matter.

**Problem 2.** An Alaska landlord's application form asks each applicant to state marital status.

*Working:* **AS 18.80.240(3)** makes it unlawful to make a written or oral **inquiry or record** of a person's marital status where the person is seeking to buy, lease, or rent. The inquiry itself is the violation; nothing turns on whether the landlord used the answer. Marital status is not a federal protected class, so a licensee relying on federal training alone would miss this. Remove the field.

**Problem 3.** A buyer asks you which neighbourhood has "the better sort of people."

chunks.heading: Module summary
chunks.excerpt:
*Working:* Do not characterise neighbourhoods by who lives in them; that is steering under 42 U.S.C. 3604 and is reachable under AS 18.80.240(1), (2), and (5). Answer with objective sources the buyer can consult directly — school district data, municipal crime statistics, census data — and show every property that meets the buyer's stated criteria. Note in the file what criteria the buyer gave and what you showed.

**Problem 4.** A home warranty company offers your brokerage $75 per policy sold to your clients, and you do nothing but hand over a brochure.

*Working:* That is a **thing of value** for the referral of settlement service business, prohibited by RESPA section 8(a), and to the extent it is a portion of a charge not matched by services actually performed it also engages 8(b). Section 8(d) exposes a fine up to $10,000, up to a year's imprisonment, and treble the charge. Alaska adds AS 08.88.401(d) and 12 AAC 64.130(7). Decline it.

**Problem 5.** Your brokerage and a mortgage broker are commonly owned, and you refer buyers to it.

*Working:* An **affiliated business arrangement** is permitted only if you give the consumer the prescribed written disclosure **at or before the time of referral**, describing the relationship and the estimated charge or range; the consumer is **not required to use** the affiliate; and the only thing of value you receive is a **return on your ownership interest**, not a payment tied to referrals — section 8(c)(4) and 12 C.F.R. 1024.15. Get the disclosure signed and into the file at referral, not at closing.

## Module summary

chunks.heading: Module assessment
chunks.excerpt:
**Seven federal protected classes**: race, colour, religion, national origin, sex, disability, familial status. **42 U.S.C. 1982 covers race with no exemptions**, and **no exemption reaches the advertising prohibition**.

**Alaska protects more.** AS 18.80.240 reaches **marital status, changes in marital status, pregnancy, parenthood, and age** in addition, and **AS 18.80.240(3) prohibits the inquiry itself**.

**A fair housing violation is a licence matter** — 12 AAC 64.130(19) covers local, state, and federal fair housing laws.

**RESPA section 8(a) prohibits anything of value for a referral**; **8(b) prohibits unearned fees and splits**; **8(c) preserves ordinary cooperative brokerage compensation**; **8(d) makes it a $10,000-and-a-year offence with treble liability**.

**Affiliated business arrangements need written disclosure at or before referral, no required use, and a return limited to ownership.**

**Section 9 forbids a seller requiring a particular title company**, on pain of treble the title insurance charges.

**The Closing Disclosure must be received three business days before consummation.** Put it in the calendar.

**Every RESPA question in Alaska is also an AS 08.88.401(d) and 12 AAC 64.130(7) question.**

## Module assessment

Complete the module assessment. The mastery threshold is 80 percent, a StateCourse instructional standard rather than an Alaska requirement. An unsuccessful attempt returns an alternate explanation and a different item set on the same material, which must be answered correctly before the module is recorded as complete.

## Module completion

Completion requires both instructional sections, both checkpoints, and the module assessment. This module carries 2 of the 40 contact hours prescribed by 12 AAC 64.063(c).

chunks.heading: Course completion
chunks.excerpt:
## Course completion

This is the final module of the Alaska Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense Education course. Completing it does not complete the course. Under **12 AAC 64.430(b)** a correspondence course must include an unanswered examination or a project activity **turned in to the instructor for grading upon completion of the course**, and under **12 AAC 64.410(a)(8)** the student must complete the course and the instructor evaluation before a certificate may issue. The end-of-course instrument is filed with the Commission for prior approval and is not published to students in advance.

lessons.title: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-01

chunks.heading: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-01
chunks.excerpt:
# Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-01

## Real property, ownership and interests

**Course:** Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — the **90 classroom hours** A.R.S. § 32-2124(B) requires.
**Instructional hours:** **7.0** of 90.0 · **Arizona-specific:** no — this module is general content
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Arizona prelicensure credit is available.

> ### Four things about this programme, stated before anything else
>
> **1. Arizona requires 96 hours, not 90.** **A.R.S. § 32-2124(B)** requires *"at least **ninety classroom
> hours**, or the equivalent"* in a commissioner-certified school. **§ 32-2124(L)** then requires, ***"after
> completing the requirements of subsection B,"*** certification of ***"six hours of instruction in real
> estate contract law and contract writing."*** **Ninety plus six.** The six are a **separate, additional**
> requirement proved **at the time of application**, and they are delivered by this programme's companion
> course.
>
> **2. Twenty-seven of the ninety are an Arizona-specific course, and they cannot be waived.**
> **§ 32-2124(B)** permits the commissioner to waive prelicensure course requirements for an out-of-state
> licensee *"**other than the twenty-seven-hour Arizona-specific course**,"* and **A.A.C. R4-28-401(A)(2)**
> says the same. **Modules AZ-10 through AZ-13 of this course are that 27 hours**, and each is labelled.
>
> **3. The passing score is 75 percent, and it is the Department's figure.** **R4-28-401(A)(1)**: complete
> the 90-hour course and *"**satisfactorily pass an examination on the course with a score of at least 75
> percent**."* And **§ 32-2124(B)**: *"**The applicant must complete a proctored examination on the live
>

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
classroom course or the distance learning course IN PERSON.**"*
>
> **4. This course has not been conformed to the Department's own prescribed content.** § 32-2124(B)
> requires a course *"**prescribed and approved by the commissioner**,"* and **R4-28-401(D)** provides that
> *"the Department shall provide a copy of the prelicensure course content to any person requesting it."*
> **That content was NOT obtained by this project.** Everything here is written from **A.R.S. Title 32,
> Chapter 20 and A.A.C. R4-28**, read on 2026-08-20. **Conforming it is a submission gate.**

## Learning objectives

1. Distinguish real from personal property and apply the fixture tests.
2. Identify the bundle of rights and the four government powers that limit it.
3. Distinguish freehold from leasehold estates.
4. Distinguish the forms of concurrent ownership, including Arizona's community property character.
5. Distinguish liens from non-lien encumbrances.
6. Connect each to R4-28-1101(H) and (K) — the competence limit and the duty to recommend counsel.

---

## A. Real and personal property

**Land** is the surface, what lies beneath, and the airspace above. **Real property** is land plus what is
permanently attached plus the rights running with it. **Personal property** is everything else.

The distinction decides what conveys, and **A.R.S. § 32-2124(E)(2)** names **bills of sale** among the
forms an applicant must understand — the instrument by which personal property moves.

### A.1 Fixtures

Personal property that has become real property by attachment. The tests: **method of annexation**;
**adaptation** to this property; the **relationship of the parties**; and **intention**, usually
controlling and read from the objective circumstances.

chunks.heading: B. The bundle of rights, and what limits it
chunks.excerpt:
**The practical answer is not the doctrine — it is the paperwork.** Name in writing what stays and what
goes, item by item, before anyone signs. Every fixture dispute a licensee ever sees was preventable by a
sentence.

**Trade fixtures** are articles a **tenant** attaches for a **business**; they remain the tenant's and are
removable **before the term ends**, after which they generally pass to the landlord by **accession**.

---

## B. The bundle of rights, and what limits it

**Possession. Use. Exclusion. Disposition. Encumbrance.** The sticks can be sold separately: a landowner
who grants a utility easement has sold one; one who leases has transferred possession and kept the rest;
one who grants a deed of trust has pledged, not conveyed.

### B.1 The four government powers

- **Police power** — regulation for public health, safety and welfare: zoning, building codes, subdivision
  regulation. **No compensation**, because nothing is taken.
- **Eminent domain** — taking for public use, **with just compensation**, through **condemnation**.
- **Taxation.**
- **Escheat.**

**The compensation line is the distinction to hold.**

### B.2 Appurtenant rights, and the Arizona question a licensee must never guess at

Rights running with the land: **air rights**, **subsurface and mineral rights**, **water rights**, and
**appurtenant easements**.

**Water deserves its own paragraph in Arizona.** Whether a parcel has an assured or adequate water supply,
whether it sits inside an Active Management Area, and what a buyer of unsubdivided land must be told about
water are questions governed by **Arizona statutes this project did not read** — including the groundwater
and water adequacy provisions and the **Affidavit of Disclosure** required for certain unsubdivided land
sales.

chunks.heading: C. Estates in land
chunks.excerpt:
**This course states no water rule, no disclosure requirement and no exemption from any of them.** A
licensee who tells a buyer a rural parcel "has water" has made a representation they cannot support — and
**R4-28-1101(H)** is the rule that governs it:

> *"A licensee **shall not undertake to provide professional services concerning a type of property or
> service that is outside the licensee's field of competence without engaging the assistance of a person
> who is competent** to provide those services, **unless the licensee's lack of expertise is first disclosed
> to the client in writing and the client subsequently employs the licensee**."*

**Read the exception carefully.** A licensee may proceed outside their competence **only** if the lack of
expertise is **disclosed to the client in writing first** and the client **then** employs them. Otherwise
the rule requires **engaging someone competent.**

---

## C. Estates in land

### C.1 Freehold

**Fee simple absolute** — perpetual, inheritable, freely transferable, subject to the government powers and
to whatever encumbers it.

**Fee simple defeasible** — a fee that can end on a stated condition. **Determinable** ends
**automatically** (language of duration: *so long as*, *while*, *during*), with a possibility of reverter.
**Subject to a condition subsequent** gives the grantor a **right of re-entry** that must be exercised
(language of condition: *but if*, *provided that*, *on condition that*).

**A licensee's job is to notice the language and route it**, not to construe it.

**Life estate** — measured by a life; the life tenant may possess and use and must avoid **waste**; the
estate then passes to a **remainderman** or **reverts**. A life estate **pur autre vie** is measured by
another's life.

### C.2 Leasehold

chunks.heading: D. Concurrent ownership — and Arizona's own character
chunks.excerpt:
| Estate | How it ends |
|---|---|
| **Estate for years** | Definite beginning, definite end. **Terminates on its own terms; no notice required.** |
| **Periodic tenancy** | Renews period to period **until proper notice**. |
| **Tenancy at will** | Continues at the pleasure of both parties. |
| **Tenancy at sufferance** | A holdover the landlord never agreed to. |

**Arizona's notice periods are in the Arizona Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, A.R.S. Title 33, which
this project did not read. No notice period is stated in this course.**

**A lease is two things at once** — a **conveyance** of a possessory interest for a term **and a contract**
of covenants. That is why a lease dispute can be framed either way, and why the **covenant of quiet
enjoyment** matters as much as any written clause.

**Assignment** transfers the tenant's **entire** remaining interest; a **sublease** transfers **less than
all** of it. **In both cases the original tenant generally remains liable unless expressly released.**

---

## D. Concurrent ownership — and Arizona's own character

**Tenancy in common.** Undivided interests that may be **unequal**, **no survivorship**, each co-tenant may
generally transfer or encumber their own share and seek **partition**.

**Joint tenancy.** The four unities — **possession, interest, time, title** — with a **right of
survivorship**. Severing a unity converts the severed share to a tenancy in common.

### D.1 Arizona is a community property state

**Property acquired during marriage is presumptively community property in Arizona.** That single fact
changes several questions a licensee meets weekly:

chunks.heading: D.2 And the rule that tells you what to do about it
chunks.excerpt:
- **Who must sign** a listing, a contract, or a deed.
- **What the title report shows**, and whether a separate-property characterisation is documented.
- **How the interest passes** on death, and what a will can and cannot do with it.

> **What this course does NOT state.** **Arizona's community property statutes were not read for this
> project.** This module states **no rule about what is community property, what is separate property, how
> either is characterised, how it may be conveyed, or how it passes at death.** It states **that Arizona is
> a community property state** — the fact a licensee needs in order to ask the right question — and routes
> the answer to **the title company and to counsel.**
>
> **A licensee who guesses at community property characterisation has guessed at whether the seller can
> convey.**

**Ownership in trust, by entity, and in common-interest communities** — condominium and planned community
forms — are further structures governed by **A.R.S. Title 33, which was not read for this project.**

### D.2 And the rule that tells you what to do about it

**R4-28-1101(K):**

> *"A licensee shall **recommend to a client that the client seek appropriate counsel from insurance,
> legal, tax, and accounting professionals** regarding the risks of pre-possession or post-possession of a
> property."*

**Read alongside (H)**, the pattern is clear: **Arizona expects a licensee to know the boundary of their own
competence and to bring in someone who has the answer.**

---

## E. Encumbrances

### E.1 Liens

chunks.heading: E.2 Non-lien encumbrances
chunks.excerpt:
**Deed of trust** — Arizona's dominant security instrument, and a **three-party** arrangement (trustor,
trustee, beneficiary) permitting **trustee's sale** rather than judicial foreclosure. **A.R.S. Title 33's
deed of trust provisions were not read for this project**, and **no notice period, timeline, reinstatement
right or deficiency rule is stated in this course.**

**Property tax lien** — statutory, involuntary, generally superior in priority. **Mechanics' and
materialmen's lien** — **Arizona's lien statute was not read; no deadline, threshold or priority rule is
stated.** **Judgment lien.** **Special assessments.**

**R4-28-1101(B)(4)** makes one of these a disclosure item in its own right:

> *"**The existence of a lien or encumbrance on the property being transferred.**"*

**Disclosed in writing, to all other parties.** Not merely to the client.

### E.2 Non-lien encumbrances

**Easement** — an interest in land; **appurtenant** easements run with the land, easements **in gross**
benefit a person or entity. **Licence** — revocable permission, **not** an interest in land.
**Encroachment** — found by a **survey**, not by a fence or a wall. **Restrictive covenant** — a private
limitation running with the land, commonly through a **declaration of covenants, conditions and
restrictions** in a planned community.

**A restrictive covenant is private and enforced privately; zoning is public and enforced by the
jurisdiction. Where the two differ, the more restrictive controls what the owner may actually do** — and a
licensee who checked only the zoning has checked half of it.

---

## Module AZ-01 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module AZ-01
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items — one applied scenario, five engagement items and five remediation items. The **80 percent**
engagement threshold and the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. **The 75
percent that is the Department's figure** applies to the **course examination** under **R4-28-401(A)(1)**,
which **§ 32-2124(B)** requires to be **proctored and taken in person** — a separate event from these
checks.

---

## Instructor source note for Module AZ-01

Drawn from **A.R.S. §§ 32-2124 and 32-2135**, read at azleg.gov on 2026-08-20, and from the **2026 ADRE Law
Book** — specifically **A.A.C. R4-28-401 and R4-28-1101.**

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this build:** the **Department's prescribed prelicensure course
content**; any **outline for the 27-hour Arizona-specific course**; **A.R.S. Title 33** in its own text,
including the **Residential Landlord and Tenant Act**, the **deed of trust**, **condominium**, **planned
community**, **lien** and **community property** provisions; **Arizona's groundwater, water adequacy and
assured water supply statutes** and the **Affidavit of Disclosure**; **A.R.S. §§ 32-2151, 32-2151.01,
32-2153 and 32-2174**; and any **Department examination content outline or candidate handbook.**

**No notice period, lien deadline, foreclosure timeline, community property rule, water rule, condominium
rescission period or examination score other than the 75 percent in R4-28-401(A)(1) is stated in this
module.**

lessons.title: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-02

chunks.heading: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-02
chunks.excerpt:
# Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-02

## Legal descriptions, encumbrances of record and land use control

**Course:** Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense · **Instructional hours: 7.0** of 90.0
**Arizona-specific:** no — general content
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Arizona prelicensure credit is available.

## Learning objectives

1. Read the three legal description methods and identify which Arizona uses.
2. Compute area and acreage, and apply R4-28-502(H)'s rule about the word "acre."
3. Distinguish a legal description from an address, a parcel number and a plat reference.
4. Distinguish zoning, variances, conditional uses and nonconforming uses.
5. Identify the land use questions a licensee routes rather than answers.
6. Apply R4-28-1101(B)(3) to a land use problem.

---

## A. Legal descriptions

An **address** identifies a mailbox. An **assessor's parcel number** identifies a tax record. **Neither
describes land.**

### A.1 The rectangular (government) survey — Arizona's primary system

Arizona is a **public land survey state**, and most of its land is described by **township, range and
section** referenced to the **Gila and Salt River Meridian**.

- A **township** is six miles square and contains **36 sections**.
- A **section** is **one square mile** and contains **640 acres**.
- Sections are numbered **1 through 36**, beginning in the **north-east** corner and running west across
  the top row, east across the second, and so on.

**Worked example.** *The SW ¼ of the NE ¼ of Section 22* contains 640 × ¼ × ¼ = **40 acres.** Read the
description **backwards** — start at the section, take the NE quarter, then the SW quarter of that. Each
"of" divides.

chunks.heading: A.2 Metes and bounds, and lot-and-block
chunks.excerpt:
*The N ½ of the SW ¼ of the SE ¼* = 640 × ¼ × ¼ × ½ = **20 acres.**

### A.2 Metes and bounds, and lot-and-block

**Metes and bounds** is used where the rectangular system does not neatly describe a parcel: a **point of
beginning**, **courses** and **distances**, called **monuments**, returning to the point of beginning. **A
description that does not close describes no parcel**, and that is a surveyor's problem.

**Reference to a recorded plat** — *Lot 14, Block 3, of [named] Subdivision, according to the plat recorded
in Book __ of Maps, Page __, records of __ County, Arizona.*

**A fence or a block wall is not a boundary.** It is evidence of where somebody once thought the boundary
was. Where anything sits near a line, the answer is a **current survey.**

### A.3 The Arizona advertising rule that turns on a measurement

**A.A.C. R4-28-502(H):**

> *"A licensee shall **not use the term 'acre,' either alone or modified, unless referring to an area of
> land representing at least 43,560 square feet**."*

**"Either alone or modified."** *"Nearly an acre," "a generous acre," "an acre-plus lot"* — each is the term
**modified**, and each requires **at least 43,560 square feet**. A 38,000-square-foot lot advertised as
*"almost an acre"* has used the term in a way the rule forbids.

**That is a genuinely Arizona-specific rule, and it is the reason a licensee needs the arithmetic.**
38,000 ÷ 43,560 = **0.87 acres** — describe it as **0.87 acres** or as **38,000 square feet**, and the
problem disappears.

---

## B. Encumbrances of record

A **title search** discloses what the record holds: **deeds of trust and other liens**, **easements**,
**CC&Rs**, **plat notes and dedications**, **judgments**, and **assessments**.

chunks.heading: C. Land use control
chunks.excerpt:
**A preliminary title report lists exceptions** — the matters the policy will **not** cover. **Reading the
exceptions is the point of receiving it.** A licensee who hands a buyer a preliminary report without saying
so has handed over a document the buyer will not open.

**And R4-28-1101(B)(4)** makes **the existence of a lien or encumbrance** a matter to be **disclosed in
writing to all other parties.**

---

## C. Land use control

### C.1 The instruments

**General plan.** **Zoning ordinance** — use districts plus **bulk and dimensional controls**: setbacks,
height, lot coverage, minimum lot area, frontage. **Subdivision ordinance.** **Building codes**, with
permits and a **certificate of occupancy**. **CC&Rs and community association governance**, which in much
of Arizona are as consequential as zoning.

**Arizona's planning and zoning statutes and every local ordinance were not read for this project. This
course states no setback, height limit, lot size, use category, permit fee or approval deadline.**

### C.2 The four relief mechanisms

| Mechanism | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Variance** | Permission to depart from a requirement, generally on a hardship showing not created by the owner. |
| **Conditional (special) use permit** | A use the ordinance **already contemplates** in that district, allowed once stated conditions are met. |
| **Nonconforming use** | A use that **lawfully predates** the ordinance; its scope and continuation are set by the ordinance. |
| **Rezone** | Amendment of the ordinance — a legislative act. |

**"Grandfathered" is not a legal term and it is not a licensee's conclusion.** Say what is known — *the
owner states the use predates the current zoning* — and route the rest.

---

## D. Where land use meets the Arizona disclosure duty

chunks.heading: Module AZ-02 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**R4-28-1101(B)** requires a licensee to *"**disclose in writing to all other parties any information the
licensee possesses that materially or adversely affects the consideration to be paid by any party**,"*
including **"(3) any known adverse material fact concerning the property or material defect existing in the
property being transferred."**

**And R4-28-1101(I)** goes further than most states:

> *"A licensee shall **exercise reasonable care in ensuring that the licensee OBTAINS information material
> to a client's interests and relevant to the contemplated transaction** and accurately communicates the
> information to the client. A licensee shall **take reasonable steps to assist a client in confirming the
> accuracy of information** relevant to the transaction."*

**Read (B) and (I) together and Arizona's shape appears.** **(B)** is a duty to **disclose what you
possess**, in writing, to **everyone**. **(I)** is an affirmative duty to **obtain** information material to
your **client's** interests and to **help them confirm it.**

**That is a more active standard than several other states set**, and a licensee who treats "I wasn't
required to look into it" as a complete answer has answered a question Arizona did not ask.

**But it is not a duty to become an expert.** **R4-28-1101(H)** supplies the limit: work outside your field
of competence requires **engaging someone competent**, unless the lack of expertise is **disclosed to the
client in writing first** and the client **then** employs you.

**Obtain, communicate, help confirm — and where it is beyond you, bring in someone who can.**

---

## Module AZ-02 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module AZ-02
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items, delivered as in Module AZ-01. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100 percent**
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** in R4-28-401(A)(1) applies to the
proctored course examination.

---

## Instructor source note for Module AZ-02

Drawn from the **2026 ADRE Law Book** — **A.A.C. R4-28-502(H) and R4-28-1101(B), (H) and (I)** — read on
2026-08-20.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this build:** **Arizona's planning, zoning and subdivision
statutes** and every local ordinance; **A.R.S. Title 33**, including the **planned community** and
**condominium** provisions; **Arizona's recording statutes**; any **title insurance policy form or rate
manual**; and the **Department's prescribed course content.**

**No setback, height limit, lot size, permit fee, approval deadline, title policy exception or premium is
stated in this module.** The **640-acre section**, the **36-section township** and the **43,560-square-foot
acre** are universal survey constants, and the last of them is also the figure **R4-28-502(H)** fixes.

lessons.title: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-03

chunks.heading: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-03
chunks.excerpt:
# Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-03

## Transfer of title, deeds and recording

**Course:** Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense · **Instructional hours: 7.0** of 90.0
**Arizona-specific:** no — general content
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Arizona prelicensure credit is available.

## Learning objectives

1. Distinguish voluntary from involuntary transfer.
2. State the essential elements of a valid deed and distinguish the deed types.
3. Explain what recording accomplishes and what it does not.
4. Distinguish owner's from lender's title insurance.
5. Describe an Arizona escrow closing and the licensee's role in it.
6. Apply R4-28-802(A) — the delivery duty — and R4-28-1101(J) — the possession rules.

---

## A. Transfer

**Voluntary:** by **deed** during life; by **will** at death — the maker a **testator**, the gift of real
property a **devise**; and by **dedication**.

**Involuntary:** **intestate succession** (**Arizona's intestacy statutes were not read for this project**,
and no share or priority is stated — note that **community property** bears on this directly); **escheat**;
**eminent domain**; **trustee's sale** under a deed of trust (**A.R.S. Title 33's deed of trust provisions
were not read; no notice period, timeline, reinstatement right or deficiency rule is stated**); **tax
lien foreclosure**; **adverse possession** (**Arizona's statutory period was not read and is not stated**);
and **accretion, erosion, avulsion and reliction.**

**What matters to a licensee is recognising the trigger.** A long-standing wall, a neighbour's driveway, an
outbuilding across a line — all go to a surveyor and counsel.

---

## B. The deed

chunks.heading: C. Recording
chunks.excerpt:
**Essential elements:** a **grantor** with capacity; a **grantee** identified with certainty; **words of
conveyance**; **consideration** recited; a **legal description**; the **grantor's signature**; and
**delivery and acceptance.**

**A deed takes effect on delivery, not on signing and not on recording.** The grantee does not sign a deed.
**Acknowledgement before a notary is required for recording.**

| Deed | What it warrants |
|---|---|
| **General warranty deed** | The fullest covenants, reaching back through the entire chain of title. |
| **Special warranty deed** | Covenants only against defects arising during the grantor's ownership — common in Arizona practice. |
| **Bargain and sale deed** | Implies the grantor holds title; covenants vary by form. |
| **Quitclaim deed** | Conveys whatever interest the grantor has — **possibly none** — with **no warranty**. |
| **Beneficiary deed** | An Arizona instrument by which an owner may designate who takes on death. **A.R.S. Title 33's provisions governing it were NOT read for this project**, and no requirement, revocation rule or effect is stated here. |

**A quitclaim deed is not a lesser-quality conveyance of good title. It conveys whatever the grantor happens
to hold, warranting nothing** — which is why it is the right instrument for clearing a cloud and the wrong
one for a purchase. **Recording does not improve it.**

**A.R.S. § 32-2124(E)(2)** names **deeds, mortgages, deeds of trust, security agreements, bills of sale and
land contracts of sale** among the forms an applicant must understand the **general purpose and legal effect
of.** That is the standard this module is written to — **purpose and legal effect**, not drafting.

---

## C. Recording

chunks.heading: D. Title assurance
chunks.excerpt:
Recording with the **county recorder** where the property lies gives **constructive notice** to the world.

- **Actual notice** — what a person in fact knows.
- **Constructive notice** — what the record imputes.
- **Inquiry notice** — what a person would have learned had they investigated a fact that should have
  prompted investigation. **Someone else in possession** is the classic trigger.

**What recording does NOT do:** it does not **validate an invalid instrument** — a forged deed is void
whether recorded or not; it does not **improve the estate conveyed**; and it does not **establish that the
grantor had good title.**

**Arizona's recording statutes were not read for this project.** This course **states no Arizona recording
priority rule and no recording deadline.** The practical consequence is universal: an unrecorded interest is
an exposure.

---

## D. Title assurance

**Chain of title. Title search and examination. Cloud on title** — an unreleased deed of trust, a gap in
the chain, an unsatisfied judgment, an heir who never joined in a deed. **Marketable title. Quiet title
action.**

### D.1 Two policies, two beneficiaries

- **Lender's policy** — protects the **lender**, in the amount of the loan, decreasing as the loan is paid.
- **Owner's policy** — protects the **owner**, in the amount of the purchase price.

**A buyer who pays for a lender's policy has bought the lender protection, not themselves.** That is the
single most useful sentence a licensee can say at an Arizona closing table.

**Every policy has exceptions** — often including matters a **survey** would disclose. **No policy form or
rate manual was read for this project**, and no term, exception, endorsement or premium is stated here.

---

chunks.heading: E. Closing in Arizona, and two rules that bite there
chunks.excerpt:
## E. Closing in Arizona, and two rules that bite there

Arizona closes through **escrow**, conducted by a title or escrow company as a **neutral depository**.

### E.1 The delivery duty — R4-28-802(A)

> *"**Upon execution of any transaction document a licensee shall expeditiously deliver a legible copy of
> the signed document and final agreement to each party signing the document.**"*

**Three words carry it: expeditiously, legible, each.** Not "when convenient," not a partial scan, and not
only to your own client — **to each party signing the document.**

**And R4-28-1101(C)** stands behind it: *"A licensee shall **expeditiously perform all acts required by the
holding of a license**. A licensee **shall not delay performance, either intentionally or through
neglect**."*

### E.2 Possession — R4-28-1101(J) and (K)

> **(J)** *"A licensee shall not: **1.** Permit or facilitate **access to or occupancy in a person's real
> property without prior written authorization from the owner** of the real property; or **2.** **Deliver
> possession prior to closing unless expressly instructed to do so by the owner** of the property or
> property interest being transferred."*
>
> **(K)** *"A licensee shall **recommend to a client that the client seek appropriate counsel from
> insurance, legal, tax, and accounting professionals regarding the risks of pre-possession or
> post-possession** of a property."*

**These are the rules behind the early-move-in request**, which arises in most markets and which Arizona
addresses directly.

**(J)(1) reaches ACCESS, not only occupancy**, and it requires **prior WRITTEN authorization from the
owner.** Letting a buyer's contractor in to measure, before closing, without the seller's written
authorisation, is within the prohibition.

chunks.heading: E.3 Prorations, and where a licensee stops
chunks.excerpt:
**(J)(2) requires the owner's EXPRESS instruction** to deliver possession before closing.

**(K) then requires the licensee to send the client to insurance, legal, tax and accounting professionals**
about the risks — because pre-possession raises questions about who insures the property, who is liable for
an injury, and what happens if the transaction does not close.

### E.3 Prorations, and where a licensee stops

Items paid in advance or in arrears are **prorated** as of closing — property taxes, association
assessments, rents and deposits, interest.

**A proration is always a double entry.** Whatever is credited to one party is debited to the other. **A
prorated item appearing once has been done wrong.**

**Which party owns the day of closing, and whether a 360-day or 365-day convention applies, are matters of
