contract and local practice. This course states neither as an Arizona rule**, because the statutes and rules
read for this project state neither. Practice problems specify the convention inside the problem.

**And the licensee does not conduct the escrow, prepare the deed, or opine on title.** **R4-28-1101(H)**
requires engaging someone competent outside your field, and **(K)** requires recommending counsel.

---

## Module AZ-03 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module AZ-01.

---

## Instructor source note for Module AZ-03

Drawn from **A.R.S. § 32-2124(E)** and the **2026 ADRE Law Book** — **A.A.C. R4-28-802(A) and R4-28-1101(C),
(H), (J) and (K)** — read on 2026-08-20.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module AZ-03
chunks.excerpt:
**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this build:** **A.R.S. Title 33**, including the **deed of
trust**, **beneficiary deed**, **adverse possession**, **lien** and **community property** provisions;
**Arizona's recording and intestacy statutes**; **Arizona's tax lien foreclosure** provisions; **A.R.S. §§
32-2151 and 32-2151.01** on trust accounts and records; any **title insurance policy form or rate manual**;
and the **Department's prescribed course content.**

**No recording deadline, priority rule, statutory period, intestate share, foreclosure timeline, redemption
right, title premium, policy exception or proration convention is stated in this module.**

lessons.title: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-04

chunks.heading: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-04
chunks.excerpt:
# Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-04

## Contract law principles

**Course:** Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense · **Instructional hours: 7.0** of 90.0
**Arizona-specific:** no — general content; Arizona contract law is the companion 6-hour course
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Arizona prelicensure credit is available.

> **Where this module sits.** This is the **general contract law** an Arizona licensee needs. **A.R.S.
> § 32-2124(L)'s six hours of real estate contract law and contract writing are a SEPARATE, ADDITIONAL
> requirement**, delivered by the companion course — and that course requires **participation by the
> applicant in drafting** contracts to purchase real property, listing agreements and lease agreements.
> This module supplies the framework the drafting sits on.

## Learning objectives

1. State the essential elements of a valid contract.
2. Distinguish void, voidable, unenforceable and valid.
3. Apply offer, acceptance, counteroffer and the mirror image rule.
4. Identify the defects in reality of consent.
5. State what the Statute of Frauds requires.
6. Distinguish the remedies for breach and explain why specific performance is available.
7. Apply R4-28-802(B) — the duty to submit all offers, and what does and does not end it.

---

## A. Essential elements

**Competent parties. Mutual assent. Consideration. Lawful object.** And **a writing**, where the Statute of
Frauds requires one — which it does for contracts conveying an interest in real property.

**Recording and notarisation are not elements of a contract.** A contract can be valid, fully enforceable
and never recorded.

chunks.heading: B. Offer and acceptance
chunks.excerpt:
| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Valid** | Meets all elements; enforceable by either party. |
| **Void** | Never had legal effect. |
| **Voidable** | Valid **until the party holding the power to avoid it elects to do so**. |
| **Unenforceable** | Valid in substance; a court will not enforce it — commonly for want of a writing. |

**The difference between void and voidable is who holds the power.** A contract with a minor is voidable
**at the minor's election** — the adult cannot escape it. A contract induced by fraud is voidable at the
**defrauded** party's election.

**Bilateral** (promise for promise) versus **unilateral** (promise for an act). **Executory** versus
**executed**. **A purchase contract is executory from acceptance until closing** — and that period, with
deadlines falling and money in escrow, is where a licensee does most of the work.

---

## B. Offer and acceptance

An **offer** may be **revoked at any time before acceptance**, unless consideration was given to hold it
open — which is what an **option** is.

An offer **terminates** by **revocation**, **rejection**, **lapse**, **death or incapacity of either
party**, **destruction of the subject matter**, or **counteroffer**.

### B.1 The mirror image rule

Acceptance must be **unqualified** and **mirror** the offer. **A purported acceptance that changes any term
is a counteroffer** — which **rejects and terminates the original offer** and reverses the roles.

Work it through. A buyer offers Monday. The seller signs Tuesday but strikes the close-of-escrow date and
writes a new one. **That is not an acceptance.** The buyer's offer is **gone** and cannot be revived by the
buyer signing the original on Wednesday. What exists is the seller's counteroffer.

chunks.heading: B.2 The Arizona rule that governs what you do with offers
chunks.excerpt:
**Acceptance must also be communicated.** A signed contract sitting in a drawer has accepted nothing.

### B.2 The Arizona rule that governs what you do with offers

**A.A.C. R4-28-802(B):**

> *"During the term of a listing agreement, a licensee shall **promptly submit to the licensee's client all
> offers** to purchase or lease the listed property. **Upon receiving permission from the seller or
> lessor**, the licensee ... **may disclose to all offerors or their agents the existence and terms of all
> additional offers** on the listed property. **The licensee shall submit to the client all offers made
> prior to closing and IS NOT RELEASED FROM THIS DUTY BY THE CLIENT'S ACCEPTANCE OF AN OFFER unless the
> client instructs the licensee IN WRITING to cease submitting offers** or unless otherwise provided in the
> listing agreement, lease, or purchase contract. The licensee **may voluntarily submit offers ...
> regardless of any limitations contained in the listing agreement and may submit offers after the listing
> agreement is terminated**."*

**Four things a licensee must hold.**

**Submit ALL offers, promptly.** The licensee does not filter by their own judgement of merit.

**Acceptance does NOT end the duty.** The subsection says so expressly. Offers made **prior to closing**
still go to the client.

**Only three things end it:** a **written** instruction from the client to cease; a provision in the
**listing agreement**; or a provision in the **lease or purchase contract.** An oral "don't bother me with
any more" is not one of them.

**Disclosing other offers requires the seller's permission.** The rule permits it *"upon receiving
permission from the seller or lessor"* — so it is the **seller's** decision, not the licensee's, and not
the other buyers'.

chunks.heading: C. Reality of consent
chunks.excerpt:
**And the closing sentences run the other way**: a licensee **may** submit offers **regardless of
limitations in the listing agreement**, and **may** submit them **after the listing agreement is
terminated.** The rule protects the flow of offers to the owner in both directions.

---

## C. Reality of consent

Assent must be real. It is defective where there is **fraud**, **misrepresentation** (innocent or
negligent), **duress**, **undue influence**, or **mistake**. In each case the contract is **voidable at the
election of the injured party.**

**Puffing** is opinion a reasonable person would not rely on as fact. **Misrepresentation** is a false
statement of fact — and the line moves toward misrepresentation as the statement becomes **more specific and
more verifiable.**

**A.A.C. R4-28-502(C)** states Arizona's advertising counterpart:

> *"A licensee shall ensure that all advertising contains **accurate claims and representations**, and
> **fully states factual material** relating to the information advertised. A salesperson or broker shall
> **not misrepresent the facts or create misleading or ambiguous impressions**."*

**"Create misleading or ambiguous impressions"** is broader than "make a false statement," and it reaches
what an advertisement implies as well as what it says.

---

## D. Writings

Contracts for the sale of an interest in real property must generally be **in writing and signed by the
party to be charged** to be enforceable. **Arizona's Statute of Frauds was not read for this project**, and
this course **states no Arizona lease-term threshold and no Arizona exception.**

**What was read is a set of Arizona rules requiring writings of their own**, which are licensing
requirements rather than Statute of Frauds requirements:

chunks.heading: E. Performance, breach and remedies
chunks.excerpt:
- **R4-28-1101(B)** — material adverse information, **in writing**, to **all other parties**.
- **R4-28-1101(E)** — conflicts, **in writing and before the parties enter any binding agreement.**
- **R4-28-1101(F)** — **prior written consent of all parties** before accepting compensation from, or
  representing, more than one party.
- **R4-28-1101(G)** — **prior written acknowledgement** before accepting compensation for related goods or
  services.
- **R4-28-1101(H)** — a lack of expertise **disclosed to the client in writing** before proceeding outside
  your competence.
- **R4-28-1101(J)(1)** — **prior written authorization from the owner** before permitting access.
- **R4-28-701** — the compensation sharing disclosure, **in writing at least three calendar days before
  closing.**
- **R4-28-802(B)** — a **written** instruction to cease submitting offers.
- **R4-28-502(I)** — the **written consent of the property owner** before placing a sign.

**Nine writings, and none of them comes from the Statute of Frauds.** An Arizona licensee who asks "does the
Statute of Frauds require this?" has often asked the wrong question.

**The parol evidence rule** bars evidence of prior or contemporaneous oral agreements offered to vary the
terms of a complete written contract. Combined with the list above, the working rule is: **every change goes
on paper, signed.**

---

## E. Performance, breach and remedies

A contract discharges by **performance**, **mutual agreement**, **operation of law**, or **breach**.

**Assignment** transfers rights and generally **leaves the assignor liable**. **Novation** substitutes a new
party and **releases** the original — which is why it needs everyone's agreement.

chunks.heading: E.1 Two Arizona rescission rights that are NOT contract-law rescission
chunks.excerpt:
**Remedies:** **damages**; **liquidated damages**; **rescission**; and **specific performance**.

**Specific performance is available in real estate because each parcel is unique**, so damages are often
inadequate.

### E.1 Two Arizona rescission rights that are NOT contract-law rescission

**A.A.C. R4-28-804** creates statutory rescission rights that have nothing to do with breach, and a licensee
must not confuse the two periods:

- **Unimproved subdivided lot, or any unsubdivided land** — rescission **without cause or reason of any
  kind**, by written notice, **by midnight of the SEVENTH calendar day** following execution. **And** if the
  purchaser did **not inspect the lot before execution**, they have **SIX MONTHS to inspect** and, **at the
  time of inspection**, the right to **unilaterally rescind.**
- **Time-share interval** — rescission **without cause or reason of any kind**, by written notice, **by
  midnight of the TENTH calendar day** following execution.

**Seven days for land; ten days for a time-share.** Module AZ-13 develops both, together with **R4-28-804(C)**,
which requires the seller's **complete and current name, address, telephone number and email address on the
FACE of all agreements** so the right can actually be exercised.

### E.2 Where the money sits

**R4-28-803(C)** requires the contract to **indicate where the earnest money or down payment will be
deposited**, naming **the title company, the broker's trust account, or other depository.**

**And R4-28-803(D)** requires a **bold or large-print warning**, signed or initialled by the purchaser, where
money is paid **directly to the seller and not placed in a neutral escrow depository.** Module AZ-13
transcribes it.

chunks.heading: Module AZ-04 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**Arizona's trust account provisions — A.R.S. §§ 32-2151 and 32-2151.01 — were not read for this project.**
**This course states no deposit deadline, account requirement or reconciliation interval.**

---

## Module AZ-04 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module AZ-01.

---

## Instructor source note for Module AZ-04

Drawn from **A.R.S. § 32-2124(L)** and the **2026 ADRE Law Book** — **A.A.C. R4-28-502(C) and (I),
R4-28-701, R4-28-802(B), R4-28-803(C) and (D), R4-28-804 and R4-28-1101(B), (E), (F), (G), (H) and (J)** —
read on 2026-08-20. Every other principle in this module is **general contract law**, taught as framework.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this build:** **Arizona's Statute of Frauds**; **A.R.S. §§
32-2151 and 32-2151.01**; **A.R.S. Title 33**; any **standard Arizona purchase contract, listing agreement
or lease form**; and the **Department's prescribed course content.**

**No lease-term threshold, limitations period, trust account deadline, liquidated damages rule or form
provision is stated in this module.** The **seven-day**, **six-month** and **ten-day** periods are
transcribed from **R4-28-804.**

lessons.title: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-05

chunks.heading: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-05
chunks.excerpt:
# Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-05

## Agency principles

**Course:** Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense · **Instructional hours: 7.0** of 90.0
**Arizona-specific:** no — general content; Arizona's licensee duties are Module AZ-11
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Arizona prelicensure credit is available.

> **Read this module knowing where Arizona lands.** **A.A.C. R4-28-1101(A)** opens: *"**A licensee owes a
> FIDUCIARY DUTY to the client and shall protect and promote the client's interests. The licensee shall also
> DEAL FAIRLY with all other parties to a transaction.**"* **Arizona is a fiduciary state.** Some states
> abolished common-law fiduciary duties by statute and replaced them with a closed list; Arizona did not.
> **Module AZ-11 delivers Arizona's own rule in full.** This module supplies the agency framework it rests
> on.

## Learning objectives

1. Define agency and identify the parties.
2. State the common-law fiduciary duties and what each requires.
3. Distinguish the ways an agency relationship is created and terminated.
4. Distinguish single agency, dual agency and subagency.
5. Distinguish an agent's duties to a principal from duties owed to third parties.
6. State what A.R.S. § 32-2124(E)(3) requires an applicant to understand.

---

## A. Agency, and the parties

An **agency relationship** exists where one person, the **agent**, is authorised to act on behalf of
another, the **principal**, in dealings with **third parties**.

**A.R.S. § 32-2124(E)(3)** requires the state examination to establish that an applicant has:

chunks.heading: B. The fiduciary duties
chunks.excerpt:
> *"A **thorough understanding of the obligations between principal and agent**, the **principles of real
> estate and business opportunity practice**, the **applicable canons of business ethics**, **this chapter
> and rules adopted pursuant to this chapter**."*

**"Thorough," not "general."** Compare § 32-2124(F) and (G), which require only a **"general
understanding"** of the principal-agent obligations for cemetery and membership camping applicants. **The
real estate salesperson standard is the higher one**, and this module and Module AZ-11 are written to it.

---

## B. The fiduciary duties

The common-law duties an agent owes a principal, commonly remembered as **OLD CAR**:

- **Obedience** — to follow the principal's **lawful** instructions.
- **Loyalty** — to place the principal's interests above the agent's own.
- **Disclosure** — to tell the principal what is material to their interests.
- **Confidentiality** — to protect the principal's confidences.
- **Accounting** — to account for money and property.
- **Reasonable care and diligence** — to bring competence and effort to the work.

**Obedience covers LAWFUL instructions.** An instruction to conceal a known material defect is not one, and
**R4-28-1101(B)** — disclosure in writing to **all other parties** — makes that concrete in Arizona.

**Loyalty is what an agency relationship adds.** Honesty and fair dealing are owed to everyone;
**loyalty** is owed to the client alone. **R4-28-1101(A)** states both halves in one sentence: a fiduciary
duty **to the client**, and **fair dealing with all other parties.**

---

## C. Creation and termination

chunks.heading: D. Types of representation
chunks.excerpt:
**Created by:** **express agreement** — the ordinary and correct route; **implied agreement**, from conduct;
**ratification**, where a principal adopts an unauthorised act; or **estoppel**, where a principal's conduct
led a third party reasonably to believe an agency existed.

**Terminated by:** **performance**; **expiration** of the agreed term; **mutual agreement**; **revocation or
renunciation**; or **operation of law** — death or incapacity of either party, destruction of the property,
or bankruptcy.

**The POWER to terminate and the RIGHT to terminate without consequence are different questions**, and the
second is answered in the employment agreement.

---

## D. Types of representation

**Single agency** — representing one side.

**Dual agency** — representing both. **In Arizona this is governed by R4-28-1101(F)**, and the rule is
stated as a compensation-and-representation prohibition with a consent exception:

> *"A licensee **shall not accept compensation from or represent more than one party to a transaction
> without the PRIOR WRITTEN CONSENT of all parties**."*

**Prior. Written. All parties.** Module AZ-11 develops it.

**Subagency** — a broker cooperating on behalf of another broker's principal. **And a caution that belongs
here:** cooperation and compensation are not representation, and **R4-28-701** requires a separate
**compensation sharing disclosure** to **all parties, in writing, at least three calendar days before
closing.**

---

## E. Duties to third parties

chunks.heading: F. Where an agent's authority stops
chunks.excerpt:
An agent owes the principal the fiduciary duties. **To everyone else the agent owes honesty and fair
dealing** — and in Arizona, considerably more than that, because **R4-28-1101(B)** requires written
disclosure **to all other parties** of information materially or adversely affecting the consideration to be
paid, **including a party's inability to perform on either side.**

**That is unusually broad**, and it is the single most important structural fact about Arizona agency
practice. Module AZ-11 transcribes it in full.

---

## F. Where an agent's authority stops

**An agent does not have authority to do what the principal has not authorised**, and an agent who exceeds
their authority may bind nobody and be liable themselves.

**Three Arizona rules mark the boundary in practice:**

- **R4-28-1101(J)(1)** — no permitting or facilitating **access to or occupancy in** a person's real
  property **without prior written authorization from the owner.**
- **R4-28-1101(J)(2)** — no **delivering possession prior to closing** unless **expressly instructed by the
  owner.**
- **R4-28-502(I)** — **written consent of the property owner** before placing a sign or publishing to an
  electronic medium, and **prompt removal on the owner's request.**

**Each is an authority rule wearing different clothes**: the licensee acts on the owner's property only with
the owner's authorisation, and the rule requires that authorisation **in writing.**

---

## Module AZ-05 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module AZ-01.

---

## Instructor source note for Module AZ-05

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module AZ-05
chunks.excerpt:
Drawn from **A.R.S. § 32-2124(E), (F) and (G)** and the **2026 ADRE Law Book** — **A.A.C. R4-28-502(I),
R4-28-701 and R4-28-1101(A), (B), (F) and (J)** — read on 2026-08-20. The fiduciary duty framework is
**general agency law**, taught as vocabulary for Module AZ-11.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this build:** **A.R.S. § 32-2153**; the remainder of **A.R.S.
Title 32, Chapter 20**; any **standard Arizona employment agreement or agency disclosure form**; and the
**Department's prescribed course content.**

**No penalty, sanction, form provision or agency disclosure requirement beyond those transcribed from
R4-28-1101, R4-28-502 and R4-28-701 is stated in this module.**

lessons.title: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-06

chunks.heading: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-06
chunks.excerpt:
# Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-06

## Real estate finance

**Course:** Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense · **Instructional hours: 7.0** of 90.0
**Arizona-specific:** no — general content
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Arizona prelicensure credit is available.

## Learning objectives

1. Define the finance vocabulary and compute with it.
2. Distinguish the note from the security instrument, and state which Arizona uses.
3. Identify the special note provisions and their consequences.
4. Distinguish the loan programmes and repayment types.
5. Distinguish the primary from the secondary mortgage market.
6. State what a licensee may and may not say about financing.

---

## A. Vocabulary, with the arithmetic attached

**Principal and interest. Amortization. Debt service. PITI. Equity. Loan-to-value ratio. Points. Yield.**

**Loan value is customarily the LOWER of contract price and appraised value.** That convention is why an
appraisal below contract price is a problem for the buyer: **the lender lends against the lower figure and
the difference must come from somewhere.**

**A discount point is one percent of the loan amount.**

### A.1 Worked examples, all figures given inside the problem

**Points.** A $438,000 loan with 1.25 points: 438,000 × 0.0125 = **$5,475** at closing.

**First month's split.** A $438,000 balance at 6.375 percent with a monthly payment of $2,733:
interest = 438,000 × 0.06375 ÷ 12 = **$2,326.88**; principal reduction = 2,733 − 2,326.88 = **$406.12**;
new balance = **$437,593.88.**

**Interest is always computed on the PREVIOUS balance**, and only the remainder touches principal.

chunks.heading: B. The note and the security instrument
chunks.excerpt:
**Loan-to-value.** Contract price $565,000, appraised value $548,000, loan $438,400. The lender recognises
**$548,000** — the lower — so LTV = 438,400 ÷ 548,000 = **80 percent**, and the buyer covers the **$17,000**
gap from their own funds.

---

## B. The note and the security instrument

**The promissory note** is the borrower's **promise to repay** — a contract, to which everything in Module
AZ-04 applies. **The security instrument pledges the property.** **Hypothecation** is the idea that ties
them: the borrower pledges the property **while keeping possession of it.**

### B.1 Deed of trust — Arizona's dominant instrument

| | **Mortgage** | **Deed of trust — Arizona's usual instrument** |
|---|---|---|
| Parties | **2** | **3** |
| Who they are | Mortgagor, Mortgagee | **Trustor, Trustee, Beneficiary** |
| Enforcement | **Judicial foreclosure** | **Trustee's sale** — non-judicial |

**The third party is what makes the shortcut possible.** A **trustee** holds the security for the
beneficiary's benefit and can conduct a **trustee's sale** without a lawsuit.

**A.R.S. Title 33's deed of trust provisions were NOT read for this project.** **This course states no
notice period, no timeline, no reinstatement right, no redemption right and no deficiency rule.** A licensee
asked about a trustee's sale timeline routes the question — to counsel, and to the trustee's own notices.

**A.R.S. § 32-2124(E)(2)** names **mortgages, deeds of trust and security agreements** among the forms an
applicant must understand the **general purpose and legal effect of.** That is the standard here.

### B.2 Special note provisions

chunks.heading: B.3 Priority and release
chunks.excerpt:
- **Acceleration clause** — on default the **whole balance** becomes due at once.
- **Prepayment penalty clause.**
- **Due-on-sale (alienation) clause** — the balance becomes due if the property is sold. **This is why
  assumption is rare.**

### B.3 Priority and release

**First**, **second** and further liens rank by **recording**, subject to statutory priorities such as
property tax liens. **Subordination** is the deliberate exception.

**And the release matters.** A deed of trust paid but **never released of record is still a cloud on
title** — Module AZ-03 met the same idea from the title side, and **R4-28-1101(B)(4)** makes **the existence
of a lien or encumbrance** a written disclosure item to **all other parties.**

---

## C. Loan programmes and repayment types

**Conventional** — not government insured or guaranteed; **conforming** loans meet secondary-market
standards; **private mortgage insurance (PMI)** typically appears at higher loan-to-value.

**FHA-insured** — FHA **does not build housing and does not lend**; it **insures approved lenders against
loss**; borrowers pay a **mortgage insurance premium (MIP)**.

**VA-guaranteed** — the VA **guarantees** approved lenders for eligible veterans; a **funding fee** applies;
the defining feature is the possibility of **no down payment.** **A VA release of liability does not by
itself release the original borrower from liability to the lender.**

**USDA Rural Development** — direct and guaranteed loans in eligible areas.

chunks.heading: D. Primary and secondary markets, and federal regulation in outline
chunks.excerpt:
**Arizona also has state and local down-payment assistance and bond programmes.** **No programme document
was read for this project**, and **no eligibility limit, income cap, purchase price limit or assistance
amount is stated in this course.** They are named so a licensee knows to ask a lender.

**By repayment:** **fixed-rate level payment (fully amortized)**; **adjustable rate (ARM)** with an
**index**, a **margin**, a **periodic cap** and a **lifetime cap** — and note that **a cap on the PAYMENT is
not a cap on the INTEREST**, so a payment cap can produce **negative amortization**; **interest-only /
term**; **balloon**; **graduated payment**; **buydown**. **By purpose:** **construction**, **blanket** (with
a **partial release** clause), **package**, **open-end**, **bridge**.

**Seller financing** — a **purchase money deed of trust** or an **agreement for sale.** **A.R.S. § 32-2124(E)(2)**
names **land contracts of sale** among the forms an applicant must understand. **Arizona's law on agreements
for sale was not read for this project**, and a licensee whose transaction involves one **routes it to
counsel, without exception** — **R4-28-1101(H)** requires engaging someone competent outside your field.

---

## D. Primary and secondary markets, and federal regulation in outline

The **primary market** is where a loan is **made**; the **secondary market** is where a loan already made is
**bought** — **Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and Ginnie Mae** — through **loan pooling** and **mortgage-backed
securities.** **The link is conforming standards**: a lender writes to them so the loan can be sold, and
selling it returns capital to lend again.

chunks.heading: D.1 And an Arizona compensation rule that sits beside RESPA
chunks.excerpt:
**TILA and Regulation Z** govern disclosure of the cost of consumer credit and the **advertising** of credit
terms. The **APR** folds points and certain fees into a single annualised rate — **it is not the interest
rate**, and it is normally higher.

**RESPA and Regulation X** govern settlement services and prohibit **kickbacks and referral fees** among
settlement service providers. **TRID** consolidated the two sets of disclosures into the **Loan Estimate**
and the **Closing Disclosure**, each with timing requirements.

> **None of those regulations was read for this project.** **This course states no disclosure deadline, no
> tolerance category, no trigger term list and no penalty.** Every live deadline goes to the lender.
>
> **What a licensee should carry away about advertising is the safe practice: publish no numbers other than
> the price.** A listing that says *"$2,850/month!"* has entered territory Regulation Z governs. And
> **R4-28-502(C)** independently requires **accurate claims**, **full statement of factual material**, and no
> **misleading or ambiguous impressions.**

### D.1 And an Arizona compensation rule that sits beside RESPA

**R4-28-1101(G):**

> *"A licensee shall **not accept any compensation, including rebate or other consideration, directly or
> indirectly, for any goods or services provided to a person if the goods or services are related to or
> result from a real estate transaction, without that person's PRIOR WRITTEN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT** of the
> compensation. **This prohibition does not apply to compensation paid to a broker by a broker who
> represents a party in the transaction.**"*

chunks.heading: E. What a licensee may and may not say
chunks.excerpt:
**Two bodies of law, two questions.** RESPA asks whether a payment among settlement service providers is
lawful. **R4-28-1101(G) asks whether the person got prior written acknowledgement** — and it reaches
**rebates and other consideration**, **direct or indirect**, for **any** related goods or services. The only
carve-out is **broker-to-broker.**

---

## E. What a licensee may and may not say

**"You'll qualify." "That'll appraise." "Rates are coming down before your lock expires."** Each is a
**representation.**

**R4-28-1101(H)** and **(I)** together set the standard: **obtain information material to the client's
interests, communicate it accurately, help the client confirm it** — and **do not undertake services outside
your field of competence** without engaging someone competent or disclosing the lack of expertise **in
writing** first.

**The reliable formulation is three words: ask your lender.**

---

## Module AZ-06 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module AZ-01. **Every rate, factor and payment used in any item is supplied
inside the item as a given.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module AZ-06

Drawn from **A.R.S. § 32-2124(E)** and the **2026 ADRE Law Book** — **A.A.C. R4-28-502(C) and
R4-28-1101(B), (G), (H) and (I)** — read on 2026-08-20.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this build:** **A.R.S. Title 33**, including the **deed of
trust** and **agreement for sale** provisions; **FHA, VA and USDA** handbooks; **Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and
Ginnie Mae** guides; any **Arizona housing assistance programme document**; **TILA and Regulation Z**;
**RESPA and Regulation X**; **TRID**; **ECOA**; and the **Department's prescribed course content.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module AZ-06
chunks.excerpt:
**No loan limit, insurance premium rate, funding fee, qualifying ratio, index value, trustee's sale
timeline, reinstatement right, redemption right, disclosure deadline, tolerance figure or programme
eligibility figure is stated in this module.**

lessons.title: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-07

chunks.heading: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-07
chunks.excerpt:
# Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-07

## Valuation and market analysis

**Course:** Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense · **Instructional hours: 7.0** of 90.0
**Arizona-specific:** no — general content
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Arizona prelicensure credit is available.

## Learning objectives

1. Distinguish value, cost, price and assessed value.
2. List the four elements of value and apply the economic principles.
3. Apply the sales comparison approach, including the two rules that govern adjustment.
4. Apply the cost approach and classify depreciation.
5. Apply the income approach by direct capitalization and by gross rent multiplier.
6. Distinguish an appraisal from a licensee's opinion of value, and state what a licensee may claim.

---

## A. Four figures that are not the same thing

**Value** is worth. **Cost** is what was spent to create it. **Price** is what someone actually paid.
**Assessed value** is what a taxing authority places on it, and it need not equal market value.

**A licensee who tells a seller "the county says it's worth $410,000" has confused two of the four.**

**The four elements of value: demand, utility, scarcity, transferability.** All four must be present.

**Principles:** **substitution** — the basis of the sales comparison approach; **contribution** — an
improvement adds what it **returns**, not what it **cost**; **highest and best use** — one at a time, and it
changes; **conformity**; **anticipation**; **progression and regression**; **supply and demand**;
**plottage**, the increment from merging adjacent parcels, produced by **assemblage**.

---

## B. The sales comparison approach

chunks.heading: B.1 The two rules
chunks.excerpt:
**Closed sales only.** A **current listing** is what a seller hopes for; a **property under contract** has a
price that has not yet survived appraisal, financing or inspection. **Neither is evidence of what a buyer
paid.**

Select for similarity in **location**, **physical characteristics and condition**, **terms and conditions of
sale**, and **date of sale**.

### B.1 The two rules

**Adjust the comparables, never the subject.** The subject is the unknown; adjusting it would be adjusting
the answer.

**Superior comparables adjust DOWN; inferior comparables adjust UP.** You are making each comparable into
the subject on paper.

**Worked example.** *Comparable A sold for $588,000 and has a casita the subject lacks, whose market
contribution derived from paired sales is $34,000. Comparable B sold for $551,000 and has a two-car garage
where the subject has three, the market contribution of the third bay being $9,000.*

Comparable A adjusted: 588,000 − 34,000 = **$554,000** *(superior, so down).*
Comparable B adjusted: 551,000 + 9,000 = **$560,000** *(inferior, so up).*

**A $6,000 spread is a tight range and good evidence.** If the adjusted figures were $70,000 apart, the
comparables were poorly chosen — **go back to selection rather than averaging the spread away.**

**Paired sales analysis** derives an adjustment honestly: two sales alike in everything but one feature, and
**the difference between them is what the market paid for that feature.** It is **contribution** applied to
one feature, and it yields **market value, usually less than cost.**

**Reconcile by weighted consideration, not simple averaging.** A comparable needing $5,000 of adjustment is
better evidence than one needing $60,000.

---

## C. The cost approach

chunks.heading: D. The income approach
chunks.excerpt:
Best where there are no comparables: **unique or special-use property**, and **new construction.**

1. **Estimate the land separately** by sales comparison. **Land is never depreciated.**
2. **Estimate replacement or reproduction cost** of the improvements. **Reproduction** rebuilds it as it
   was; **replacement** builds equal utility with current materials. Costing methods, most to least
   detailed: **quantity survey**, **unit-in-place**, **square foot.**
3. **Subtract accrued depreciation.**
4. **Add the depreciated improvement value to the land value.**

**Depreciation:** **physical deterioration** (curable or incurable); **functional obsolescence** (curable or
incurable); and **external (economic) obsolescence — incurable, always**, because its cause lies **outside
the property line** and the owner does not own it.

**Effective age is not chronological age.** A thirty-year-old house maintained impeccably may have an
effective age of twelve.

---

## D. The income approach

**Direct capitalization: Value = NOI ÷ capitalization rate.**

Potential gross income, **less vacancy and collection loss** → effective gross income, **less operating
expenses** → **net operating income.**

**Debt service is NOT an operating expense.** NOI describes **the property's** earning power; two buyers
could buy the same building with entirely different financing and the NOI is identical. **NOI less debt
service is before-tax cash flow — a different figure answering a different question.**

**Worked example, rate given.** *Potential gross income $312,000; vacancy and collection loss 8 percent;
operating expenses $107,500; annual debt service $128,000; market cap rate 6.25 percent.*

chunks.heading: E. What a licensee may claim about value
chunks.excerpt:
Effective gross income = 312,000 × 0.92 = **$287,040.**
NOI = 287,040 − 107,500 = **$179,540.**
Value = 179,540 ÷ 0.0625 = **$2,872,640.**
*(Before-tax cash flow = 179,540 − 128,000 = $51,540 — not the value.)*

**The cap rate measures risk and is inversely related to value:** at the same income a **higher** cap rate
gives a **lower** value, because it is the divisor.

**Gross rent multiplier.** **GRM = sale price ÷ gross rent**, derived from comparables; then **Value =
subject's gross rent × GRM.** **Be consistent about the period** — a GRM from monthly rent is applied to
monthly rent.

**Worked example.** *Comparables sell at $498,000 on $3,320 monthly gross rent: GRM = 498,000 ÷ 3,320 =
**150.** A subject renting for $3,450 is indicated at 3,450 × 150 = **$517,500.***

---

## E. What a licensee may claim about value

**A licensee is not an appraiser.** An appraisal is an appraiser's opinion produced under professional
standards; a licensee's market analysis is an opinion of probable sales price produced for a pricing or
offering decision.

**Three Arizona rules govern what you say about it.**

**R4-28-1101(H)** — do not undertake services **outside your field of competence** without engaging someone
competent, unless the lack of expertise is **disclosed to the client in writing first** and the client then
employs you.

**R4-28-1101(I)** — **obtain** information material to the client's interests, **communicate it
accurately**, and **help the client confirm** it.

**R4-28-502(C)** — advertising must contain **accurate claims and representations**, **fully state factual
material**, and must **not misrepresent the facts or create misleading or ambiguous impressions.**

chunks.heading: Module AZ-07 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**A defensible sentence:** *"This is my opinion of probable sales price, based on these three closed sales
and these adjustments. It is not an appraisal, and your lender will order one that may come in
differently."*

**Not defensible:** *"It'll appraise at six-fifty."* That is a prediction about a third party's future
opinion, and no rule shelters it.

**And the Arizona measurement rule from Module AZ-02 applies to a market analysis as much as to an
advertisement: R4-28-502(H)** — **never use "acre," alone or modified, for less than 43,560 square feet.**

---

## Module AZ-07 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module AZ-01. **Every rate, multiplier and adjustment figure is supplied
inside the item as a given.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module AZ-07

Drawn from the **2026 ADRE Law Book** — **A.A.C. R4-28-502(C) and (H) and R4-28-1101(H) and (I)** — read on
2026-08-20. Every valuation principle is **general appraisal and market analysis content**, taught as
method.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this build:** **USPAP**; **Arizona's appraiser licensing
statutes and Board rules**; **Arizona's property tax and assessment statutes**; and the **Department's
prescribed course content.**

**No appraiser requirement, USPAP standard, assessment ratio, levy rate or capitalization rate is stated in
this module.** Every figure in every worked example is supplied inside the example.

lessons.title: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-08

chunks.heading: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-08
chunks.excerpt:
# Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-08

## Fair housing, environmental issues and property condition

**Course:** Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense · **Instructional hours: 7.0** of 90.0
**Arizona-specific:** no — general content
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Arizona prelicensure credit is available.

> ### A submission gate stated at the top of this module
>
> **Arizona's fair housing statutes and the federal Fair Housing Act were NOT read for this project**, and
> neither was **Arizona's seller disclosure practice or any standard disclosure form.**
>
> **Accordingly this module states NO protected class list, NO exemption, NO complaint deadline, NO penalty
> and NO disclosure form provision.** It teaches the **structure** of fair housing law, the **conduct** that
> violates it, and the **Arizona rules that were read** — chiefly **R4-28-1101(B)**, which is Arizona's own
> disclosure duty. **Obtaining the fair housing statutes, the federal Act and the Department's prescribed
> course content, and conforming this module to them, is a submission gate.**

## Learning objectives

1. State the structure of fair housing law — federal, state and local — and which controls.
2. Identify the prohibited practices by conduct rather than by label.
3. Recognise steering, and the requests that invite it.
4. Distinguish a reasonable accommodation from a reasonable modification.
5. Apply R4-28-1101(B) to a property condition problem.
6. Identify the environmental conditions common in Arizona and who answers each.

---

## Part 1 — Fair housing

### A. Three layers

chunks.heading: B. The prohibited practices, taught as conduct
chunks.excerpt:
**Federal law sets a floor. Arizona's own law adds to it. Local ordinances in some Arizona jurisdictions add
further.** **Where the layers differ, the MOST PROTECTIVE applies.**

> **What this course does not state.** **No protected class list from any of the three was read for this
> project, and none is stated here.** This is deliberate: a fair housing list that is out of date or
> incomplete is worse than no list, because a licensee will rely on it.
>
> **The safest operating posture, and the one this course teaches: do not screen, sort, steer, describe or
> decide on ANY personal characteristic of a person.** A licensee who never uses a characteristic never
> needs the list.

### B. The prohibited practices, taught as conduct

**Refusal to deal** — including **failing to return calls**, **not sending listings**, and **being
unavailable**. A refusal does not have to be spoken.

**Different terms or conditions** — a different deposit, fee, showing hours or level of service.

**Discriminatory advertising** — any statement, in any medium, indicating a preference, limitation or
discrimination. **This reaches photographs, captions and the description of a neighbourhood's character.**

**Steering** — directing prospects toward or away from areas on the basis of a characteristic, **including
by what is shown, what is described, and what is left out.** Steering by omission is still steering.

**Blockbusting. Redlining. Discrimination in services and facilities. Retaliation or interference.**

### C. Steering, in the form a licensee actually meets it

- *"What kind of people live there?"*
- *"Is this a good neighbourhood for a family like ours?"*
- *"Where would you live if you were us?"*
- *"Which schools are the good ones?"*

chunks.heading: D. Disability
chunks.excerpt:
**Answering any of them from your own characterisation is steering, whoever asked.**

**The reliable response has three parts:** say what you can and cannot do, plainly; **route the objective
questions to objective sources** — school data, crime statistics, commute times are all published; and
**ask what they actually need in terms of the property.**

**And notice that the fourth question is also an opinion presented as fact**, which **R4-28-502(C)** reaches
independently.

### D. Disability

A **reasonable accommodation** is a change in **rules, policies, practices or services**. A **reasonable
modification** is a **physical change to the premises**. **The distinction is what is changed: a RULE or the
PREMISES.**

**An assistance animal is not a pet.** **The verification a housing provider may lawfully request is
governed by rules this project did not read** — the question goes to counsel **before** a refusal, not
after. **R4-28-1101(H)** requires engaging someone competent outside your field of competence.

### E. Advertising

**Describe the property, not the people.** *"Three bedrooms, north-facing patio, cul-de-sac"* describes
property. *"Perfect for a young family"* describes people.

**And the advertisement is more than the words** — photographs, captions, hashtags, the account it is posted
from, and **the audience it is targeted to.** **R4-28-502(J)** expressly brings electronic media within
Arizona's advertising rules, naming *"the **Internet, Artificial Intelligence**, or web site technology"* —
Module AZ-12 develops it.

---

## Part 2 — Property condition and the Arizona disclosure duty

### F. R4-28-1101(B) — the rule that governs

chunks.heading: G. And R4-28-1101(I) — the duty that goes further
chunks.excerpt:
> *"A licensee participating in a real estate transaction shall **disclose in writing to all other parties
> any information the licensee possesses that materially or adversely affects the consideration to be paid
> by any party** to the transaction, **including**:*
> **1.** *"Any information that the **seller or lessor is or may be unable to perform**;*
> **2.** *"Any information that the **buyer or lessee is, or may be, unable to perform**;*
> **3.** *"Any **known adverse material fact concerning the property or material defect existing in the
> property** being transferred; and*
> **4.** *"The **existence of a lien or encumbrance** on the property being transferred."*

**Four features.**

**"In writing."** Not orally, not by implication.

**"To all other parties."** Not merely to the client — **to everyone in the transaction.**

**"Any information the licensee POSSESSES."** The trigger is possession, not investigation.

**And the list is introduced by "including" — it is illustrative, not exhaustive.** The test is whether the
information **materially or adversely affects the consideration to be paid.**

### G. And R4-28-1101(I) — the duty that goes further

> *"A licensee shall **exercise reasonable care in ensuring that the licensee OBTAINS information material
> to a client's interests and relevant to the contemplated transaction** and accurately communicates the
> information to the client. A licensee shall **take reasonable steps to assist a client in confirming the
> accuracy of information** relevant to the transaction."*

**Read (B) and (I) together.** **(B)** requires **disclosure of what you possess**, in writing, to
**everyone**. **(I)** requires **obtaining** what is material to your **client's** interests and **helping
them confirm it.**

chunks.heading: H. Conditions a licensee routes rather than opines on
chunks.excerpt:
**Arizona expects a licensee to be active, not merely honest.** A licensee who says "nobody asked me to look
into it" has answered a question Arizona did not ask.

**The limit is R4-28-1101(H):** outside your field of competence, **engage someone competent** — unless the
lack of expertise is **disclosed to the client in writing first** and the client then employs you.

### H. Conditions a licensee routes rather than opines on

For each: **what it is, and who answers it.** The second half is the licensee's job.

**Lead-based paint** — the federal disclosure obligation attaches to **target housing**, generally
pre-1978 dwellings, and reaches **known** lead-based paint and known hazards. **Painting over it does not
remove it.** **The federal regulation was not read for this project**; no notice period or retention
requirement is stated. → **A certified inspector or risk assessor.**

**Radon.** → **A current test.** An old result is not a current reading.

**Asbestos**, common in older construction. → **A qualified inspector; a licensed abatement contractor
before any renovation.**

**Mould and moisture** — the useful question is almost never "is there mould" but **"where is the water
coming from."** → **A qualified inspector; a contractor.**

**Soils.** In parts of Arizona, **expansive soils, subsidence and earth fissures** are real and
consequential. → **A geotechnical engineer; published hazard mapping; the jurisdiction.**

chunks.heading: I. The habit
chunks.excerpt:
**Water — supply, quality and the right to use it.** Whether a rural parcel has an adequate or assured
supply, and what must be disclosed about it, are governed by **Arizona statutes this project did not read**,
including the **Affidavit of Disclosure** required for certain unsubdivided land sales. → **The Arizona
Department of Water Resources, a well professional, a testing laboratory, and counsel.**

**On-site septic and alternative wastewater systems.** → **The county environmental or health department for
the permit; a qualified inspector for the condition.**

**Flood and stormwater**, including washes and floodplain designation. → **Published mapping; the
jurisdiction; an insurer.**

**Termites and other wood-destroying organisms.** → **A licensed inspector.**

**Roof, HVAC and pool systems** — in a climate that is hard on all three. → **Qualified inspectors.**

> **This course states no action level, threshold, testing protocol, remediation standard, buffer, hazard
> designation, water rule, disclosure requirement or insurance term for ANY of the above**, because no
> federal regulation, Arizona environmental or water statute, county rule or hazard map was read for this
> project. **Every one is routed.**

### I. The habit

Separate three things and say which is which, every time:

1. **What you know** — you saw it, measured it, or hold the document.
2. **What you were told** — attributed to whoever told you.
3. **What you are guessing** — say nothing, and route it.

**Every disclosure failure in this course traces back to one of the three being presented as another.**

chunks.heading: Module AZ-08 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**And never advise a seller to remain ignorant.** *"Don't test — what you don't know you don't have to
disclose"* is bad advice legally and bad advice practically. **R4-28-1101(I)** points the other way
entirely.

---

## Module AZ-08 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module AZ-01. **No item states a protected class list, exemption, complaint
deadline, action level, testing protocol or disclosure form provision**, because the sources setting them
were not read for this project.

---

## Instructor source note for Module AZ-08

Drawn from the **2026 ADRE Law Book** — **A.A.C. R4-28-502(C) and (J) and R4-28-1101(B), (H) and (I)** —
read on 2026-08-20.

**NOT obtained, and therefore the source of NOTHING here:** **Arizona's fair housing statutes**; the
**federal Fair Housing Act** and its regulations; every **local Arizona antidiscrimination ordinance**;
**Arizona's seller disclosure practice and any standard disclosure form**; **Arizona's groundwater, water
adequacy and assured water supply statutes** and the **Affidavit of Disclosure**; **federal lead-based paint
regulations**; **county environmental and health department rules**; **hazard mapping**; and the
**Department's prescribed course content.**

**No protected class, exemption, filing period, penalty, verification standard, action level, threshold,
testing protocol, remediation standard or water rule is stated anywhere in this module.**

lessons.title: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-09

chunks.heading: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-09
chunks.excerpt:
# Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-09

## Property management, leasing and real estate mathematics

**Course:** Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense · **Instructional hours: 7.0** of 90.0
**Arizona-specific:** no — general content
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Arizona prelicensure credit is available.

> **Source note.** Arizona's landlord-tenant law is in **A.R.S. Title 33 — the Arizona Residential Landlord
> and Tenant Act**, which **this project did not read.** **Arizona's trust account and record provisions,
> A.R.S. §§ 32-2151 and 32-2151.01, were also not read.** **Accordingly this module states NO notice
> period, NO deposit limit, NO accounting deadline, NO eviction step and NO trust account requirement.** It
> teaches the structure and the arithmetic, and routes every figure.

## Learning objectives

1. Distinguish the leasehold estates and identify which requires notice to end.
2. Distinguish gross, net, percentage and ground leases.
3. Describe the property manager's functions and the management agreement's essential terms.
4. Compute the figures a manager produces.
5. Compute commissions, net-to-seller and prorations.
6. Read a settlement statement and place an entry as a debit or a credit to the correct party.

---

## A. Leasehold estates and lease types

| Estate | How it ends |
|---|---|
| **Estate for years** | Definite beginning and end. **Terminates on its own terms; no notice required.** |
| **Periodic tenancy** | Renews period to period **until proper notice**. |
| **Tenancy at will** | Continues at the pleasure of both parties. |
| **Tenancy at sufferance** | A holdover the landlord never agreed to. |

chunks.heading: B. Property management
chunks.excerpt:
**Arizona's notice periods are in A.R.S. Title 33 and are not stated in this course.** A manager who guesses
at one has guessed at whether a tenancy ended.

**Lease types by rent structure:** **gross** (landlord pays operating expenses); **net** (tenant pays rent
plus some or all of taxes, insurance and maintenance — *single, double, triple net*); **percentage** (a
share of gross sales above a breakpoint); **ground** (land leased for the tenant to build on); **index or
graduated.**

**Worked example — percentage lease.** *Base rent $5,100 monthly; 4 percent of gross sales above a $95,000
monthly breakpoint. In a month with $164,000 of sales:* overage = 164,000 − 95,000 = **$69,000**; percentage
rent = 69,000 × 0.04 = **$2,760**; total = 5,100 + 2,760 = **$7,860.**

---

## B. Property management

**Functions:** market and screen (**under fair housing law, with written criteria applied identically to
every applicant, and documented** — Module AZ-08); collect rent and enforce the lease; maintain; account to
the owner; keep records; handle deposits; serve notices correctly and on time.

**The management agreement should settle:** the parties and property; **the scope of authority**; the term;
compensation; **the owner's approval thresholds for expenditure**; reporting and accounting; the handling of
tenant funds and deposits; insurance; indemnity; and termination.

**An unwritten scope of authority is how a manager ends up having spent an owner's money on something the
owner did not authorise.** Set the threshold in dollars, in the agreement.

chunks.heading: B.1 The operating statement
chunks.excerpt:
**And two Arizona rules bear directly on management.** **R4-28-1101(J)(1)** — no permitting or facilitating
**access to or occupancy in** a person's real property **without prior written authorization from the
owner.** **R4-28-1103(A)(1)(d)** — the employing and designated broker's written policies must cover **the
handling of trust funds.**

### B.1 The operating statement

**Potential gross income**, less **vacancy and collection loss**, plus **other income** = **effective gross
income**; less **operating expenses** = **net operating income.**

**Debt service is not an operating expense.** And **omitting a replacement reserve overstates NOI and
therefore overstates value.**

**Worked example, all figures given.** *A 36-unit building; market rent $1,425 per unit per month; vacancy
and collection loss 7 percent; other income $2,100 per month; operating expenses $268,000 annually;
management fee 6 percent of effective gross income; annual debt service $341,000.*

Potential gross income = 36 × 1,425 × 12 = **$615,600.**
Vacancy and collection loss = 615,600 × 0.07 = **$43,092.**
Other income = 2,100 × 12 = **$25,200.**
Effective gross income = 615,600 − 43,092 + 25,200 = **$597,708.**
Management fee = 597,708 × 0.06 = **$35,862.48** *(charged on EGI, not on potential gross — a manager paid
on collections is paid on what came in).*
Net operating income = 597,708 − 268,000 = **$329,708.**
Before-tax cash flow = 329,708 − 341,000 = **−$11,292** *(a negative, and a real one).*

*(**This course states no management fee rate**, because compensation is negotiated and no course sets it.)*

---

## C. Real estate mathematics

### C.1 Area and the Arizona "acre" rule

chunks.heading: C.2 Commissions and net to seller
chunks.excerpt:
**1 acre = 43,560 square feet. 1 section = 640 acres = 1 square mile. 1 township = 36 sections. 1 square
yard = 9 square feet.**

**Rectangle = base × height. Triangle = ½ × base × height. Trapezoid = ½ × (base₁ + base₂) × height.** An
irregular parcel with straight sides is **decomposed**, each piece computed and added.

**Worked example.** *A lot is a rectangle 95 ft × 160 ft with a right-triangular extension 95 ft × 48 ft.*
Rectangle = **15,200 sq ft.** Triangle = ½ × 95 × 48 = **2,280 sq ft.** Total = **17,480 sq ft** =
17,480 ÷ 43,560 = **0.40 acres.**

**And R4-28-502(H) applies to how you describe it:** *"A licensee shall **not use the term 'acre,' either
alone or modified, unless referring to an area of land representing at least 43,560 square feet**."* **A
17,480-square-foot lot may not be advertised as "almost half an acre" using the word "acre" — describe it as
0.40 acres, which is accurate, or in square feet.**

### C.2 Commissions and net to seller

**This course states no commission rate, split or minimum.** Every problem supplies its rate.

*Sale price $712,000; the seller's agreement provides 5.5 percent to the listing brokerage, shared evenly
with the selling brokerage; the licensee's split with the employing broker is 65/35 in the licensee's
favour.*
Total = 712,000 × 0.055 = **$39,160.** Each brokerage = **$19,580.** The licensee = 19,580 × 0.65 =
**$12,727.**

**Price needed to NET a required sum** — algebra, not arithmetic, because the commission is a percentage
**of the unknown price.**

chunks.heading: C.3 Prorations
chunks.excerpt:
*A seller must net $340,000 after a 5.5 percent commission and $6,200 of other costs, with no loan payoff.*
**P − 0.055P − 6,200 = 340,000**, so **0.945P = 346,200**, and **P = $366,349.21.**
**Check:** 366,349.21 × 0.055 = 20,149.21; 366,349.21 − 20,149.21 − 6,200 = **$340,000.** ✓

**The classic error is to add 5.5 percent to $346,200**, which gives $365,241 — short by more than $1,100.

### C.3 Prorations

**Two conventions, and every problem must say which it uses: 365-day** (actual days) and **360-day /
30-day-month.** **Two rules that never change: a proration is always a DOUBLE ENTRY**, and **whichever party
owns the day of closing must be stated.** **This course states neither convention nor a settlement-date rule
as Arizona law**, because the statutes and rules read for this project state neither.

**Worked example — taxes paid in advance, 360-day method, seller owns the day of closing.** *Annual property
tax $4,320, paid in full by the seller for the year. Closing 21 August.*
Daily = 4,320 ÷ 360 = **$12.** Monthly = **$360.**
Seller's period = 1 January through 21 August = 7 months + 21 days = 2,520 + 252 = **$2,772.**
Buyer's share = 4,320 − 2,772 = **$1,548.**
**The seller prepaid the whole year, so the buyer reimburses: credit the seller $1,548 and debit the buyer
$1,548.** Double entry. ✓

### C.4 The settlement statement

A **debit** is what a party **owes**; a **credit** is what a party **has coming.**

For the **buyer**: the **purchase price is a debit**; the **earnest money** and the **loan amount** are
**credits.**
For the **seller**: the **purchase price is a credit**; the **loan payoff** and the **commission** are
**debits.**

**Cash to close (buyer) = buyer's debits − buyer's credits.**
**Net to seller = seller's credits − seller's debits.**

chunks.heading: Module AZ-09 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**Worked example.** *Price $565,000; earnest money $15,000 in escrow; new loan $452,000; buyer's lender and
escrow charges $9,400; seller's commission 5.5 percent; seller's loan payoff $288,600; seller's escrow and
other charges $2,150; the tax proration above credits the seller $1,548 and debits the buyer $1,548.*

**Buyer:** debits 565,000 + 9,400 + 1,548 = **$575,948**; credits 15,000 + 452,000 = **$467,000**;
**cash to close = $108,948.**
**Seller:** credits 565,000 + 1,548 = **$566,548**; debits (565,000 × 0.055) 31,075 + 288,600 + 2,150 =
**$321,825**; **net to seller = $244,723.**

**Check the double entry:** the tax proration appears **once on each side**, both $1,548. ✓

**And Arizona's transfer, property and income tax statutes were not read for this project. No rate,
threshold, exemption or exclusion is stated in this course**, and **tax advice is outside brokerage** —
**R4-28-1101(K)** requires recommending **tax and accounting professionals**, and **(H)** requires engaging
someone competent outside your field.

---

## Module AZ-09 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module AZ-01, and weighted toward calculation. **Every rate, levy, multiplier
and convention is supplied inside the item as a given.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module AZ-09

Drawn from the **2026 ADRE Law Book** — **A.A.C. R4-28-502(H), R4-28-1101(J) and (K) and R4-28-1103(A)** —
read on 2026-08-20.

**Not read, and therefore the source of no figure in this build:** **A.R.S. Title 33**, including the
**Arizona Residential Landlord and Tenant Act**; **A.R.S. §§ 32-2151, 32-2151.01 and 32-2174**; **Arizona's
transfer, property and income tax statutes**; the **Internal Revenue Code**; and the **Department's
prescribed course content.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module AZ-09
chunks.excerpt:
**No notice period, deposit limit, accounting deadline, eviction procedure, trust account requirement,
retention period, management fee rate, commission rate, tax rate or proration convention is stated as
Arizona law in this module.**
