chunks.heading: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-10
chunks.excerpt:
# Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-10

## Arizona real estate licensing and the Department

**Course:** Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense · **Instructional hours: 7.0** of 90.0
**Arizona-specific:** ★ **YES** — this module is part of the **27-hour Arizona-specific course** that
**A.R.S. § 32-2124(B)** and **A.A.C. R4-28-401(A)(2)** provide **may not be waived.**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Arizona prelicensure credit is available.

> ### The 27 hours that cannot be waived
>
> **A.R.S. § 32-2124(B)**, closing sentence: *"the commissioner may waive all or a portion of the
> prelicensure course requirement, **other than the TWENTY-SEVEN-HOUR ARIZONA-SPECIFIC COURSE**, for an
> applicant who holds a current real estate license in another state."*
>
> **A.A.C. R4-28-401(A)(2)**: an applicant may, *"**except for the 27-hour Arizona-specific course**, apply
> for and be granted a waiver of the prelicensure courses."*
>
> **Modules AZ-10, AZ-11, AZ-12 and AZ-13 are that 27 hours** — 7 + 7 + 7 + 6. An experienced licensee
> moving to Arizona from another state may be relieved of the other 63; **they may not be relieved of
> these.**
>
> **A submission gate.** **Neither the statute nor the rule states what the 27 hours must contain**, and
> **the Department's prescribed course content — which R4-28-401(D) says the Department will provide on
> request — was NOT obtained by this project.** These four modules are built from **A.R.S. Title 32,
> Chapter 20 and A.A.C. R4-28**, read on 2026-08-20. **Conforming them to the Department's own content is a
> submission gate.**

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: A. What A.R.S. § 32-2124 requires of you
chunks.excerpt:
1. State the education, age and character requirements for an Arizona salesperson's licence.
2. State the ten-year limit on course completion and the exception to it.
3. State the passing score and the proctoring requirement.
4. State what the state examination must establish, under A.R.S. § 32-2124(E).
5. State what a certified real estate school and an approved course must do.
6. State the licensing consequence of passing an examination.

---

## A. What A.R.S. § 32-2124 requires of you

### A.1 The education — subsection (B)

> *"All applicants ... for a real estate salesperson's license shall show evidence satisfactory to the
> commissioner that they have **completed a real estate salesperson's course that is prescribed and approved
> by the commissioner** and that is **at least ninety classroom hours, or the equivalent**, of instruction
> **in a real estate school certified by the commissioner** and have **satisfactorily passed an examination
> on the course**."*

**Four conditions in one sentence.** The course must be **prescribed and approved by the commissioner**; it
must be **at least ninety classroom hours or the equivalent**; it must be delivered by **a school the
commissioner has certified**; and the applicant must have **passed an examination on it.**

### A.2 Delivery — the same subsection

chunks.heading: A.3 The ten-year limit
chunks.excerpt:
> *"An applicant may complete the ... course ... through a **live classroom course or a distance learning
> course** if ... offered by a real estate school that is **certified by the commissioner**. **The applicant
> must complete a proctored examination on the live classroom course or the distance learning course IN
> PERSON.** An applicant may complete the required course or instructional segments in **any combination of
> in-person or synchronous remote delivery methods**."*

**Read the three sentences together, because they are not saying the same thing.**

**Instruction** may be **live classroom or distance learning**, and may be taken in **any combination of
in-person or synchronous remote** delivery. Arizona is permissive about how you learn.

**The examination is not.** *"**The applicant must complete a proctored examination ... IN PERSON.**"* However
the course was delivered, **the examination is proctored and it is taken in person.**

### A.3 The ten-year limit

> *"**The real estate salesperson's course completion or its equivalent may not be more than ten years before
> the date of application** unless, at the time of application, the commissioner **determines in the
> commissioner's discretion** that the applicant has **work experience in a real estate-related field and
> education that together are equivalent** to the prelicensure education requirement."*

**Ten years, measured to the DATE OF APPLICATION.** And the exception is **discretionary** — the
commissioner *"determines in the commissioner's discretion"* — and requires **work experience AND
education together**, not either alone.

### A.4 The passing score — A.A.C. R4-28-401(A)(1)

chunks.heading: A.5 Age, and the felony bar
chunks.excerpt:
> *"Complete the required **90-hour prelicensure education course** and **satisfactorily pass an examination
> on the course with a score of AT LEAST 75 PERCENT** as prescribed in A.R.S. § 32-2124."*

**Seventy-five percent is the Department's figure.** The in-module checks throughout this course are **not**
that examination.

### A.5 Age, and the felony bar

> **§ 32-2124(D):** *"Before receiving any license provided for by this chapter, an applicant must be **at
> least eighteen years of age**."*
>
> **§ 32-2124(M):** *"The commissioner **shall not issue a license** to a person who has been **convicted of
> a felony offense** and who is **currently incarcerated** for the conviction, **paroled or under community
> supervision and under the supervision of a parole or community supervision officer** or who is **on
> probation** as a result of the conviction."*

**Note what (M) is and is not.** It is a **bar while the person is in custody or under supervision** for a
felony conviction. It is **not** a general statement of how a criminal record affects licensure — that is
governed by **A.R.S. § 32-2153**, which **this project did not read**, and by the Department's own process.
**A licensee asked about a criminal record routes the question to the Department.**

### A.6 The six additional hours — subsection (L)

chunks.heading: B. What the state examination must establish — § 32-2124(E)
chunks.excerpt:
> *"An applicant for an original real estate salesperson's license, **after completing the requirements of
> subsection B of this section**, shall provide certification to the department **at the time of
> application** evidencing completion of **six hours of instruction in real estate contract law and contract
> writing**. **This instruction shall include participation by the applicant in drafting contracts to
> purchase real property, listing agreements and lease agreements.**"*

**Ninety plus six is ninety-six.** The six are **separate and additional**, proved **at the time of
application**, and they require **participation in drafting** three named document types. The companion
course delivers them.

---

## B. What the state examination must establish — § 32-2124(E)

> *"The commissioner shall ascertain by a written, electronic or other examination method that an applicant
> for a real estate license has:*
>
> **1.** *An **appropriate knowledge of the English language**, including reading, writing and spelling, and
> of **arithmetical computations common to real estate practices**.*
>
> **2.** *At a minimum, an **understanding of the general purpose and legal effect of any real estate
> practices, principles and related forms**, including **agency contracts, real estate contracts, deposit
> receipts, deeds, mortgages, deeds of trust, security agreements, bills of sale, land contracts of sale and
> property management**, and of any other areas that the commissioner deems necessary and proper.*
>
> **3.** *A **thorough understanding of the obligations between principal and agent**, the **principles of
> real estate and business opportunity practice**, the **applicable canons of business ethics**, **this
> chapter and rules adopted pursuant to this chapter**.*
>
> **4

chunks.heading: B.1 This is the closest thing to a content outline this project obtained
chunks.excerpt:
.** *An **appropriate knowledge of other real estate practices and principles** as determined by the
> commissioner."*

### B.1 This is the closest thing to a content outline this project obtained

**And it is not the Department's prescribed content**, which was not obtained. It is, however, what the
statute says the examination must establish, and it is worth reading as a map of this course:

| § 32-2124(E) requires | Delivered in |
|---|---|
| Arithmetical computations common to real estate practices | **AZ-09**, and throughout |
| Purpose and legal effect of **agency contracts** | **AZ-05**, **AZ-11** |
| Purpose and legal effect of **real estate contracts and deposit receipts** | **AZ-04**, **AZ-13**, and the companion contract writing course |
| **Deeds, mortgages, deeds of trust, security agreements, bills of sale, land contracts of sale** | **AZ-01**, **AZ-03**, **AZ-06** |
| **Property management** | **AZ-09** |
| **Obligations between principal and agent** — *thorough* | **AZ-05**, **AZ-11** |
| **Canons of business ethics** | **AZ-11**, **AZ-12** |
| **This chapter and rules adopted pursuant to it** | **AZ-10** through **AZ-13** |

**Note the word "thorough" in (3).** Compare § 32-2124(F) and (G), which require only a **"general
understanding"** of the principal-agent obligations for cemetery and membership camping applicants. **The
real estate standard is higher**, and Module AZ-11 is written to it.

### B.2 The examination itself — A.A.C. R4-28-403

chunks.heading: C. Schools, courses and instructors — the framework this course sits in
chunks.excerpt:
> **(A)** *The Department shall hold, or contract for, **at least one state licensing examination each
> week**.*
>
> **(B)** *A state licence examination **shall not be returned to the applicant**. The applicant shall be
> **notified in person** of the results by the words **"passed" or "did not pass."** The results notification
> for an applicant who did not pass **shall also show the score for the examination and the relative score
> for each content area.***
>
> **(C)** *"**Qualifying to take or passing a license examination does not constitute a waiver of the
> Commissioner's right to deny issuance of a license** if grounds exist pursuant to A.R.S. § 32-2153 or any
> other applicable statute."*

**Subsection (C) is the one to hold.** **Passing the examination is not a licence.** The Commissioner may
still deny issuance on grounds in § 32-2153 — a section **this project did not read**, and from which **no
ground, penalty or procedure is stated in this build.**

**And (B)'s failing-candidate provision is a genuine benefit**: a candidate who did not pass receives **the
score and the relative score for each content area**, which tells them where to study.

**§ 32-2124(I)** adds that *"the examination for a broker's license shall be **more exacting and stringent
and of a broader scope** than the examination for a salesperson's license."*

---

## C. Schools, courses and instructors — the framework this course sits in

### C.1 A.R.S. § 32-2135(A)

chunks.heading: C.2 What the Department may withdraw approval for — § 32-2135(C)
chunks.excerpt:
> *"before offering a course of study towards completion of the education requirement ... a school shall
> **obtain from the commissioner a certificate of approval or renewal to operate a school for a period of at
> least four years**. A school shall also **obtain a certificate of course approval for each course offered
> for credit** ... **Each school is responsible for the content of any course it offers and for the
> professional administration and teaching of the course.** **Prelicensure education live classroom courses,
> prelicensure education distance learning courses, continuing education live classroom courses and distance
> learning continuing education courses are subject to approval** pursuant to this section."*

**Two separate approvals: the SCHOOL and each COURSE.** And the sentence in the middle is the one that
matters most to a student: **the school is responsible for the content.**

**§ 32-2135(B):** *"Each approved school shall **issue a certificate of real estate course attendance** to
each person who completes an approved prelicensure or continuing education course."*

### C.2 What the Department may withdraw approval for — § 32-2135(C)

Among the grounds: **improperly certifying student attendance or performance**; ***"teaching information or
using course materials that have not been approved by the commissioner"***; **filing false or misleading
applications, reports or documentation**; and ***"teaching course content that is not current or that has
substantially changed from the course as approved."***

**"Not current" is an obligation that runs continuously**, not at approval. And **R4-28-404(H)(3)** requires
a school to **obtain approval BEFORE changing course content or course length**, or offering a new course.

chunks.heading: C.3 What a course application must contain — A.A.C. R4-28-404(B)
chunks.excerpt:
### C.3 What a course application must contain — A.A.C. R4-28-404(B)

Among the requirements:

> **4.** *"A **detailed outline of course material content** that clearly lists the subject matter to be
> covered";*
> **5.** *"The number of credit hours requested. **The time allocated by a school for examination shall not
> be included in calculating credit hours if the examination is used for overall evaluation**";*
> **7.** *"A **definition of segments** if the course is to be offered in part and in its entirety";*
> **8.** *"If any **third party recorded material** will be used as instructional aids, **they will not
> exceed 20 percent of instructional time**."*

**Two constraints on this build follow directly.**

**Examination time is not instruction.** Where the examination is used for overall evaluation, **its time
does not count towards the 90 hours.** So the ninety hours are ninety hours of **instruction**, and the
proctored examination sits outside them.

**Third party recorded material may not exceed 20 percent of instructional time.** For a 90-hour course
that is **18 hours** at most.

### C.4 School records and your enrolment agreement

**R4-28-404(D)** — the school shall maintain a record **for five years** of each student: the **name**, the
**dates of attendance**, the **title of each course**, the **course number, category and credit hours
awarded**, and **the original signature roster, if live in person instruction.**

chunks.heading: C.5 Instructor approval and school advertising
chunks.excerpt:
**R4-28-404(E)** — the enrolment agreement must include, ***"in bold type and capital letters"***: the
**course or course segment title within a curriculum**; the **total credit hours applicable for licensure or
renewal**; the **cost of each course**; a **statement of the refund policy**; a **statement related to
license pre-determination petitions**; and a **statement of any job placement service.**

**Note the pre-determination petition item.** A person with a concern about whether their history will bar
licensure may petition the Department **before** paying for a course, and **the enrolment agreement must
tell them so, in bold capitals.** **This project did not read the statute governing that petition**, and no
procedure, deadline or fee for it is stated here.

**R4-28-404(F)** — a school may advertise **job placement services** only if referrals result from **direct
contact between the school placement service and prospective employers**, with **documented evidence
maintained.** *"The Department does not consider lists of employers given to graduates to be a placement
service."*

### C.5 Instructor approval and school advertising

**R4-28-404(C)** — any person wishing to instruct an approved course shall submit **detailed information of
professional qualifications, demonstrating an ability to instruct, subject matter expertise**, or other
applicable information.

**R4-28-502(D)** — *"A **school** shall include its **name, school number, phone and email contact
information, and the name of the school administrator** in all advertising of Department-approved courses.
The school owner, director, or administrator shall **supervise all advertising**. The school owner shall
ensure that the school's advertising is **accurate**."*

chunks.heading: D. Where this build stands against all of that
chunks.excerpt:
**§ 32-2135(D)** — a school **shall not** offer a course for credit that is not approved (*"except that the
school **may advertise a course as pending approval** before its approval"*), or **promote or advertise the
school using false or misleading statistics or testimonials or any other form of deceptive advertisement.**

---

## D. Where this build stands against all of that

| Requirement | Status in this build |
|---|---|
| Course **prescribed and approved by the commissioner** — § 32-2124(B) | **NOT SATISFIED.** The Department's prescribed content was not obtained. |
| **Certificate of School Approval** — § 32-2135(A), R4-28-404(A) | **NOT HELD.** |
| **Certificate of Course Approval** — § 32-2135(A), R4-28-404(B) | **NOT HELD.** No course number issued. |
| **Instructor approval** — R4-28-404(C) | **NOT HELD.** |
| **90 hours of instruction**, examination time excluded | **Satisfied by design** — 90.0 hours across thirteen modules. |
| **27 hours Arizona-specific**, unwaivable | **Satisfied by design** — Modules AZ-10 to AZ-13. |
| **Third party recorded material ≤ 20% of instructional time** | **Satisfied by design** — this build uses none. |
| **Proctored examination in person at 75%** | **NOT BUILT.** |
| **Certificate of course attendance** — § 32-2135(B) | **Cannot issue** without approval. |

**Every "not" in that table is a submission gate**, and this course states its status on every page for that
reason.

---

## Module AZ-10 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module AZ-01. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100 percent**
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; **the 75 percent in R4-28-401(A)(1)** applies to the
**proctored, in-person course examination**, which is a separate event.

---

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module AZ-10
chunks.excerpt:
## Instructor source note for Module AZ-10

Drawn from **A.R.S. §§ 32-2124 and 32-2135**, read at azleg.gov on 2026-08-20, and from the **2026 ADRE Law
Book** — **A.A.C. R4-28-401, R4-28-403, R4-28-404 and R4-28-502(D)**.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** the **Department's prescribed prelicensure course
content**; any **outline for the 27-hour Arizona-specific course**; **A.R.S. § 32-2153**; the statute
governing **license pre-determination petitions**; and any **Department examination content outline or
candidate handbook.**

**No examination item count, time limit, application fee, course fee, pre-determination procedure, ground
for denial or penalty is stated in this module.** The **90 hours**, the **six additional hours**, the
**27-hour Arizona-specific course**, the **ten-year limit**, the **75 percent**, the **eighteen years**, the
**four-year school approval period**, the **five-year school record**, and the **20 percent recorded-material
limit** are all **transcribed from A.R.S. § 32-2124, § 32-2135 and A.A.C. R4-28.**

lessons.title: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-11

chunks.heading: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-11
chunks.excerpt:
# Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-11

## Arizona licensee duties and conflicts

**Course:** Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense · **Instructional hours: 7.0** of 90.0
**Arizona-specific:** ★ **YES** — this module is part of the **27-hour Arizona-specific course** that
**A.R.S. § 32-2124(B)** and **A.A.C. R4-28-401(A)(2)** provide **may not be waived.**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Arizona prelicensure credit is available.

> ### The module the course has been pointing at
>
> Module AZ-05 built the general agency framework and said of it: *"Module AZ-11 delivers Arizona's own rule
> in full. This module supplies the agency framework it rests on."* **This is that module.**
>
> Its whole subject is **one rule — A.A.C. R4-28-1101, "Duties to Client"** — together with **R4-28-1102**
> on property negotiations. The rule is short. It is also the rule under which Arizona licensees are
> disciplined more than any other, and **almost every subsection contains a requirement a licensee can
> breach without ever intending to.**
>
> **A.A.C. R4-28-1101 and R4-28-1102 were read in full** in the **2026 ADRE Law Book** on **2026-08-20**.
> Every quoted passage below is transcribed from that reading.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: Part 1 — The first sentence: Arizona is a fiduciary state
chunks.excerpt:
1. State, in the rule's own words, what duty an Arizona licensee owes a client and what duty is owed to
   everyone else.
2. State the four categories of information R4-28-1101(B) requires be disclosed in writing to **all other
   parties**.
3. State the four conflict situations in R4-28-1101(E) and **when** the disclosure must be made.
4. Distinguish **prior written consent** under (F) from **prior written acknowledgement** under (G), and
   state (G)'s single carve-out.
5. State the competence limit in (H) and the two ways a licensee may lawfully proceed outside it.
6. State the affirmative information duty in (I) and explain how it differs from a duty merely to pass on
   what arrives.
7. State the possession prohibitions in (J) and the counsel duty in (K).
8. State the 24-hour rule in R4-28-1102 and how a principal may alter it.

---

## Part 1 — The first sentence: Arizona is a fiduciary state

Read the opening subsection before anything else, because it settles the character of every duty that
follows.

> **A.A.C. R4-28-1101(A)**: *"A licensee owes a **fiduciary duty** to the client and shall **protect and
> promote the client's interests**. The licensee shall also **deal fairly with all other parties to a
> transaction**."*

Two duties, two audiences, in two sentences.

| To whom | Duty | Rule source |
|---|---|---|
| **The client** | **Fiduciary duty**; protect and promote the client's interests | R4-28-1101(A), first sentence |
| **All other parties** | **Deal fairly** | R4-28-1101(A), second sentence |

### Why this sentence matters more than it looks

chunks.heading: Why this sentence matters more than it looks
chunks.excerpt:
A licensee who has studied for a licence in another state may arrive in Arizona with the opposite
instinct, because **several states have deliberately legislated away the fiduciary standard.** This project
has built courses in some of them, and the contrast is exact:

| State | What that state's law says about the standard |
|---|---|
| **Arizona** | *"A licensee owes a **fiduciary duty** to the client"* — R4-28-1101(A) |
| **Washington** | Its statute provides that the duties it lists are **statutory duties and not fiduciary duties** |
| **Oklahoma** | Its statute **abrogates the common-law fiduciary duties** of a broker and substitutes a statutory list |

**Arizona did not do that.** The word is in the rule, in the first sentence, and it is not qualified
anywhere in R4-28-1101. A licensee transferring in from a statutory-duty state who assumes Arizona works
the same way is wrong, and the error is not academic — it changes what a licensee must do when the client's
interest and the licensee's convenience diverge.

**What "fiduciary" imports.** Module AZ-05 developed the general content: loyalty, obedience to lawful
instruction, disclosure to the principal, confidentiality, reasonable care and skill, and accounting.
R4-28-1101(A) adopts that standard by name and then **adds specific requirements on top of it** in
subsections (B) through (K). The rule's specific requirements are a floor, not a ceiling: nothing in the
rule says a licensee who satisfies (B) through (K) has thereby discharged the fiduciary duty in (A).

chunks.heading: Part 2 — R4-28-1101(B): what must be disclosed, in writing, to everyone else
chunks.excerpt:
**"Deal fairly" is a real duty, not a courtesy.** The second sentence is the source of the licensee's
obligation to the party across the table. Subsection (B), immediately following, is its most concrete
expression — and note that **(B) runs to *all other parties*, not to the client.**

---

## Part 2 — R4-28-1101(B): what must be disclosed, in writing, to everyone else

> **(B)**: *"A licensee participating in a real estate transaction shall **disclose in writing to all other
> parties any information the licensee possesses that materially or adversely affects the consideration to
> be paid by any party** to the transaction, **including**:*
> **1.** *"Any information that the **seller or lessor is or may be unable to perform**;*
> **2.** *"Any information that the **buyer or lessee is, or may be, unable to perform**;*
> **3.** *"Any **known adverse material fact concerning the property or material defect existing in the
> property** being transferred; and*
> **4.** *"The **existence of a lien or encumbrance** on the property being transferred."*

### Read the structure before the list

Three things are built into the opening clause, and each of them is doing work.

**1. "Information the licensee possesses."** The trigger is possession. Subsection (B) does not require a
licensee to go looking — that duty appears separately in **(I)**, and it runs to the **client**, not to
other parties. Keep the two apart: **(B) is a disclosure duty about what you have; (I) is an acquisition
duty about what you should get.**

chunks.heading: Items 1 and 2 — inability to perform, on either side
chunks.excerpt:
**2. "Materially or adversely affects the consideration to be paid by any party."** This is the standard.
The four numbered items are stated as **examples of it** — the rule says *"including"* — so a licensee who
works down the list as a checklist and stops has misread the rule. Information that materially affects what
someone will pay is disclosable whether or not it fits one of the four.

**3. "In writing to all other parties."** Not orally. Not to the client only. **In writing, to everyone
else in the transaction.**

### Items 1 and 2 — inability to perform, on either side

This is the pair a licensee from another state is least likely to expect, and it is symmetrical:

- **Item 1** — information that **the seller or lessor** is or may be unable to perform.
- **Item 2** — information that **the buyer or lessee** is, or may be, unable to perform.

Note the phrasing: **"is or may be"**. The rule does not wait for certainty.

**What this means in practice.** A licensee who learns that the buyer's financing has collapsed, or that the
seller cannot deliver clear title on the agreed date, holds information the rule treats as **materially
affecting the consideration to be paid** — and must **disclose it in writing to the other parties.** A
licensee's instinct to protect a client by keeping quiet about the client's own difficulty runs directly
into subsection (B).

**This is where (A)'s two sentences meet.** The fiduciary duty to the client does not license concealment
from the other side of something the rule names as disclosable. Where a licensee genuinely cannot see how to
satisfy both, the rule's answer is in **(C)**: notify the designated broker. The rule does **not** provide
that the client's interest overrides (B).

chunks.heading: Item 3 — known adverse material fact or material defect
chunks.excerpt:
### Item 3 — known adverse material fact or material defect

Two phrases: **"known adverse material fact concerning the property"** and **"material defect existing in
the property."** Again the trigger is **known**.

**A boundary the licensee must know and this course does not cross.** Arizona has a separate statutory
scheme on residential disclosure obligations and on facts a licensee **is not** obliged to disclose.
**Those statutes were NOT read by this project**, and **no such rule, exception, or list of
non-disclosable facts is stated anywhere in this course.** Module AZ-13 records the same gap for the
disclosure documents it covers. **A licensee's question about whether a particular fact must be disclosed
under Arizona statute is a question for the designated broker and for counsel**, and this module states
only what R4-28-1101(B) itself says.

### Item 4 — the existence of a lien or encumbrance

Stated flatly. **Existence**, disclosed in writing to all other parties. Module AZ-02 built the general
content on liens and encumbrances; this is the rule that requires the licensee to say so.

---

## Part 3 — (C) and (D): performance, delay, and controversy between licensees

> **(C)**: *"A licensee shall **expeditiously perform all acts required by the holding of a license**. A
> licensee **shall not delay performance, either intentionally or through neglect**. If a licensee is unable
> to perform any act as required by rule or statute, **they must expeditiously notify their designated
> broker of their inability to perform**."*

Three separate requirements in one subsection:

chunks.heading: Part 4 — R4-28-1101(E): four conflicts, in writing, before any binding agreement
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Perform expeditiously.**
2. **Do not delay — intentionally *or through neglect*.** The rule reaches negligent delay, not only
   deliberate stalling. A licensee who simply forgot has still breached (C).
3. **If unable, tell the designated broker — expeditiously.** This is the rule's own escape route, and it
   runs **upward**, to the broker. Module AZ-12 develops what the designated broker must then do under
   **R4-28-1103**.

> **(D)**: *"A licensee **shall not allow a controversy with another licensee to jeopardize, delay, or
> interfere with the initiation, processing, or finalizing of a transaction on behalf of a client**."*

**What (D) does not do.** The rule adds that it **does not oblige a licensee to alter compensation terms or
to relinquish the right to maintain an action.** So a commission dispute may be pursued — it simply may not
be pursued **through the transaction.** The client's transaction is not leverage.

**The pattern in (C) and (D) together:** the client's transaction moves forward, and the licensee's own
difficulties — inability, neglect, a fight with another licensee — are handled somewhere other than by
letting the transaction stall.

---

## Part 4 — R4-28-1101(E): four conflicts, in writing, before any binding agreement

chunks.heading: The timing requirement is the operative part
chunks.excerpt:
> **(E)**: *"A licensee shall not act directly or indirectly in a transaction **without informing the other
> parties in the transaction, in writing and before the parties enter any binding agreement**, of a present
> or prospective interest or conflict in the transaction, **including that the**:*
> **1.** *"**Licensee has a license and is acting as a principal**;*
> **2.** *"**Purchaser or seller is a member of licensee's or designated broker's immediate family**;*
> **3.** *"Purchaser or seller **has ownership or is the employee of the licensee's employing broker**; or*
> **4.** *"**Licensee, or a member of the licensee's immediate family, has a financial interest in the
> transaction** other than the licensee's receipt of compensation for the real estate services."*

### The timing requirement is the operative part

**"In writing and before the parties enter any binding agreement."** A disclosure made at closing, or when
the conflict becomes awkward, or when someone asks, is **late**, and lateness is the breach. The rule fixes
the deadline at a specific event — **before the parties enter any binding agreement** — and a licensee who
knows of the conflict earlier has no reason to wait.

**"Directly or indirectly."** A licensee cannot cure a conflict by routing the transaction through someone
else.

**"Present or prospective."** A conflict that has not yet materialised but is in prospect is disclosable.

**"Including."** As in (B), the four numbered items are examples of *"a present or prospective interest or
conflict"*, not an exhaustive list.

### The four named situations

chunks.heading: Part 5 — (F) and (G): consent, acknowledgement, and the subsection licensees breach without noticing
chunks.excerpt:
| # | Situation | The point of it |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Licensee is licensed and is acting as a principal** | Buying or selling for your own account. The other side is entitled to know in writing that the person across the table holds a licence. |
| **2** | **Purchaser or seller is in the licensee's — or the designated broker's — immediate family** | Note it reaches the **designated broker's** family, not just the licensee's. |
| **3** | **Purchaser or seller has ownership in, or is an employee of, the licensee's employing broker** | The conflict is at the firm level, and the licensee must disclose it even though it is not the licensee's own interest. |
| **4** | **Licensee or immediate family has a financial interest in the transaction** other than the licensee's compensation | The carve-out matters: ordinary commission is **not** the conflict. Anything else financial is. |

**Item 1 is the classic.** A licensee selling their own house is not doing anything prohibited — they are
required to say, in writing, before any binding agreement, that they hold a licence and are acting as a
principal.

---

## Part 5 — (F) and (G): consent, acknowledgement, and the subsection licensees breach without noticing

Two subsections, two different words, and the difference is examinable.

chunks.heading: Comparing them
chunks.excerpt:
> **(F)**: *"A licensee shall **not accept compensation from or represent more than one party to a
> transaction without the PRIOR WRITTEN CONSENT of all parties**."*
>
> **(G)**: *"A licensee shall **not accept any compensation, including rebate or other consideration,
> directly or indirectly, for any goods or services provided to a person if the goods or services are
> related to or result from a real estate transaction, without that person's PRIOR WRITTEN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT
> of the compensation**. **This prohibition does not apply to compensation paid to a broker by a broker who
> represents a party in the transaction.**"*

### Comparing them

| | **(F)** | **(G)** |
|---|---|---|
| **What it governs** | Compensation from **more than one party**, or **representing** more than one party | Compensation — **including rebate or other consideration** — for **goods or services** related to or resulting from a transaction |
| **What is required** | **Prior written CONSENT** | **Prior written ACKNOWLEDGEMENT** |
| **Whose** | **All parties** | **That person's** — the person to whom the goods or services were provided |
| **Timing** | **Prior** | **Prior** |
| **Exception** | None stated in (F) | **Broker-to-broker**: does not apply to compensation paid to a broker by a broker who represents a party in the transaction |

**Consent is permission. Acknowledgement is receipt.** The rule chose different words for the two
subsections and a licensee should not treat them as interchangeable. Under **(F)** the parties must
**agree**; under **(G)** the person must have **acknowledged the compensation** in writing beforehand.

### Why (G) is the one that catches people

chunks.heading: Part 6 — (H) and (I): competence, and the affirmative duty to obtain information
chunks.excerpt:
Read how wide it is: **any** compensation, **including rebate or other consideration**, **directly or
indirectly**, for **any** goods or services, if those goods or services are **related to or result from** a
real estate transaction.

That reaches referral arrangements, marketing arrangements, and consideration flowing from vendors — in each
case requiring the **prior written acknowledgement of the person to whom the goods or services were
provided.** A licensee who receives something of value because a client was sent somewhere is inside (G).

**The single carve-out is narrow and specific:** it applies **only** to compensation **paid to a broker by a
broker who represents a party in the transaction.** Ordinary co-brokerage is not caught. Nothing else is
excluded by the rule's text.

**A boundary this module does not cross.** Federal law also governs referral arrangements and settlement
services, and Module AZ-06 covers the general federal content. **This module states only what R4-28-1101(G)
requires**, and does **not** state how (G) interacts with any federal requirement — that comparison was not
worked from primary federal text for Arizona purposes and is **not stated here.**

---

## Part 6 — (H) and (I): competence, and the affirmative duty to obtain information

chunks.heading: Part 6 — (H) and (I): competence, and the affirmative duty to obtain information
chunks.excerpt:
> **(H)**: *"The services that a licensee provides to a client shall **conform to the standards of practice
> and competence recognized in the professional community** for the specific real estate discipline ... A
> licensee **shall not undertake to provide professional services concerning a type of property or service
> that is outside the licensee's field of competence without engaging the assistance of a person who is
> competent to provide those services, unless the licensee's lack of expertise is first disclosed to the
> client in writing and the client subsequently employs the licensee**."*

**(H) has two lawful routes out of an incompetence problem, and no third:**

1. **Engage the assistance of a competent person**; or
2. **Disclose the lack of expertise to the client in writing first**, *and* the client **subsequently
   employs the licensee.**

Note the sequence in route 2: **disclosure first, employment after.** A licensee who takes the engagement
and discloses afterwards has not satisfied (H). And the disclosure alone is not enough — the rule requires
that the client **then** employ the licensee, which is to say the client must have chosen with the
disclosure in hand.

**"The specific real estate discipline."** The standard is measured against the discipline, not against real
estate at large. Competence in residential resale is not competence in the commercial, land, or property
management disciplines.

chunks.heading: (I) is an acquisition duty, and that is the point
chunks.excerpt:
> **(I)**: *"A licensee shall **exercise reasonable care in ensuring that the licensee obtains information
> material to a client's interests and relevant to the contemplated transaction and accurately communicates
> the information to the client**. A licensee shall **take reasonable steps to assist a client in confirming
> the accuracy of information relevant to the transaction**."*

### (I) is an acquisition duty, and that is the point

Three obligations:

1. **Obtain** information material to the client's interests and relevant to the transaction.
2. **Accurately communicate** it to the client.
3. **Assist the client in confirming its accuracy.**

**Obligation 1 is affirmative.** The licensee is not merely a conduit for information that happens to
arrive. Compare, again, a state this project has built for: **Washington's statute expressly provides that
its licensees have no duty to investigate.** **Arizona's rule runs the other way** — (I) requires reasonable
care in **obtaining** material information. **A course that treated the two states alike would misstate
both**, and this module states Arizona's rule as Arizona wrote it.

**Obligation 3 is the one licensees forget.** The rule does not merely require accurate transmission; it
requires **reasonable steps to assist the client in confirming accuracy.** Directing a client to the source,
to an inspection, or to the professional who can verify a figure is the substance of it.

**The standard throughout is "reasonable care" / "reasonable steps"** — not a guarantee, and not perfection.
The rule does not define what is reasonable, and **this module does not invent a definition.**

---

## Part 7 — (J) and (K): access, possession, and the duty to send the client to counsel

chunks.heading: Part 7 — (J) and (K): access, possession, and the duty to send the client to counsel
chunks.excerpt:
> **(J)**: *"A licensee shall not: **1.** Permit or facilitate **access to or occupancy in a person's real
> property without prior written authorization from the owner**; or **2.** **Deliver possession prior to
> closing unless expressly instructed to do so by the owner** of the property or property interest being
> transferred."*

| | Prohibited | Cured only by |
|---|---|---|
| **(J)(1)** | Permitting or facilitating **access to or occupancy in** a person's real property | **Prior written authorization from the owner** |
| **(J)(2)** | **Delivering possession prior to closing** | **Express instruction from the owner** of the property or property interest being transferred |

**(J)(1) reaches "permit or facilitate."** A licensee who does not personally open the door but arranges for
someone else to is inside the prohibition. **"Access"** is broader than occupancy — a showing is access.
The required authorization is **prior** and **written**.

**(J)(2) is the early-possession problem.** Buyers ask to move in before closing; sellers ask to stay after.
The rule addresses the first directly: **no delivery of possession before closing** unless the **owner
expressly instructs it.**

> **(K)**: *"A licensee shall **recommend to a client that the client seek appropriate counsel from
> insurance, legal, tax, and accounting professionals regarding the risks of pre-possession or
> post-possession of a property**."*

**(K) is an affirmative duty and it names four professions:** **insurance, legal, tax, and accounting.** It
attaches to **pre-possession or post-possession** arrangements — exactly the situations (J)(2) contemplates.

chunks.heading: Part 8 — R4-28-1102: contacting another licensee's principal
chunks.excerpt:
**Note what (K) does not do.** It does not authorise the licensee to advise on those risks. It requires the
licensee to **recommend that the client get that advice from the professionals named.** Module AZ-12
develops the general boundary between real estate practice and the unauthorised practice of law; (K) is one
of the places Arizona's rule builds the referral into the licensee's own duty.

---

## Part 8 — R4-28-1102: contacting another licensee's principal

> **(A)**: *"Real estate licensees **may not contact a principal represented by another licensee** unless
> the principal's **Designated Broker, broker representative with delegated authority, and the licensee are
> unavailable for 24 hours**. A principal may **waive or alter this requirement by issuing written
> instructions**."*
>
> **(B)**: *"For a buyer and unless the buyer waives this requirement in writing, **negotiation must be
> conducted exclusively through the principal's broker or the broker's representative** unless the
> designated broker, a broker with delegated authority, and the buyer's licensee with an agency relationship
> are **unavailable for 24 hours**."*

### The 24-hour rule

The prohibition is on **contacting a principal represented by another licensee.** It lifts only when
**all three** are unavailable for **24 hours**:

1. the principal's **designated broker**;
2. a **broker representative with delegated authority**; and
3. the **licensee**.

**All three, and for 24 hours.** One unreturned call does not open the door.

**The principal controls the rule, not the licensee.** *"A principal may waive or alter this requirement by
issuing written instructions."* The waiver belongs to the represented party — the licensee who wants to make
contact cannot supply it.

chunks.heading: Part 9 — Working the rule as one instrument
chunks.excerpt:
**(B) applies the same structure to buyer-side negotiation**, requiring that negotiation be conducted
**exclusively through the principal's broker or the broker's representative** unless the buyer waives in
writing or the same three people are unavailable for 24 hours.

**Where this sits in practice.** Module AZ-04 covers the general content on presenting and negotiating
offers. **R4-28-1102 is the Arizona rule that decides *whom you may talk to* while doing it**, and it is a
rule licensees breach out of impatience rather than intent.

---

## Part 9 — Working the rule as one instrument

The eleven subsections are not eleven separate rules. Work a single ordinary transaction through them and
the shape appears.

**A licensee lists a house. The seller is the licensee's brother-in-law. The buyer, found by the same
licensee, asks to move in two weeks before closing. A title search turns up a lien. The buyer's lender has
gone quiet.**

chunks.heading: Module AZ-11 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
| Fact | Subsection | What the rule requires |
|---|---|---|
| Seller is immediate family | **(E)(2)** | Written disclosure to the other parties **before any binding agreement** |
| Licensee represents or is compensated by both sides | **(F)** | **Prior written consent of all parties** |
| Lien discovered | **(B)(4)** | **Written disclosure to all other parties** |
| Lender has gone quiet — buyer may be unable to perform | **(B)(2)** | **Written disclosure to all other parties**; *"is, or may be"* |
| Buyer asks for early possession | **(J)(2)** | **No delivery of possession before closing** unless the **owner expressly instructs** |
| Early possession is being discussed at all | **(K)** | **Recommend counsel** — insurance, legal, tax, accounting |
| Licensee has never handled early possession | **(H)** | Engage competent assistance, **or** disclose the lack of expertise in writing **first** and be employed after |
| The licensee cannot get the paperwork out in time | **(C)** | **Expeditiously notify the designated broker** |
| The co-op licensee is fighting about commission | **(D)** | The **dispute may not delay the transaction**; compensation terms need not be altered |
| Licensee wants to call the buyer's agent's client directly | **R4-28-1102(A)** | **Not unless** the designated broker, a delegated broker representative, **and** the licensee are **unavailable for 24 hours** — or the principal has waived in writing |

Nine subsections and a second rule, in one transaction, none of them exotic. **That is why this module is
7.0 hours and why the 27-hour Arizona-specific block cannot be waived for an out-of-state licensee** — the
duties are Arizona's own, and several of them run opposite to the state that licensee came from.

---

## Module AZ-11 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module AZ-11
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items, delivered as in Module AZ-01. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100 percent**
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; **the 75 percent in R4-28-401(A)(1)** applies to the
**proctored, in-person course examination**, which is a separate event.

---

## Instructor source note for Module AZ-11

Drawn entirely from **A.A.C. R4-28-1101 and R4-28-1102**, read in full in the **2026 ADRE Law Book** at
re.az.gov on **2026-08-20**, and recorded in `arizona/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`. The comparisons
to Washington and Oklahoma are to those states' own statutory text as read and recorded in this project's
Washington and Oklahoma readings files.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** Arizona's **residential seller disclosure statutes**
and any statutory list of **facts a licensee need not disclose**; **A.R.S. § 32-2153** and any other
disciplinary ground or penalty provision; any **Department substantive policy statement, advisory or
guidance document** interpreting R4-28-1101; any **Arizona case law**; and the **Department's prescribed
content for the 27-hour Arizona-specific course.**

**No disciplinary consequence, penalty, fine, licence sanction, damages measure, statute of limitations,
disclosure exception, or definition of "reasonable" is stated in this module.** The **fiduciary duty**, the
**four disclosure categories**, the **four conflict situations**, the **prior written consent** and **prior
written acknowledgement** requirements, the **broker-to-broker carve-out**, the **competence routes**, the
**possession prohibitions**, the **four professions in (K)**, and the **24 hours** in R4-28-1102 are all
**transcribed from A.A.C. R4-28-1101 and R4-28-1102.**

lessons.title: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-12

chunks.heading: Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-12
chunks.excerpt:
# Arizona Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense — Module AZ-12

## Arizona broker supervision, employment and advertising

**Course:** Real Estate Salesperson Prelicense · **Instructional hours: 7.0** of 90.0
**Arizona-specific:** ★ **YES** — this module is part of the **27-hour Arizona-specific course** that
**A.R.S. § 32-2124(B)** and **A.A.C. R4-28-401(A)(2)** provide **may not be waived.**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Arizona prelicensure credit is available.

> ### Why a salesperson studies the broker's rules
>
> Module AZ-11 delivered the duties **you** owe. This module delivers the rules that decide **who is
> answerable for what you do** — and they matter to a salesperson for a blunt reason stated in the rule
> itself: **A.A.C. R4-28-1103(D)** provides that *"an employing broker is responsible for the acts of all
> licensees and other employees acting"* in the brokerage.
>
> A salesperson works **inside** a supervision system the designated broker is required to build. Two
> practical consequences follow. **First**, the brokerage's written policies are not office preference — the
> rule **requires** them, and the broker's failure to enforce them is itself a violation. **Second**, the
> single activity a salesperson is most likely to conduct alone — **advertising** — is one the rule assigns
> to the designated broker's responsibility: **R4-28-502(G)**, *"the designated broker is responsible for
> the advertising of all real estate activity."*
>
> **A.A.C. R4-28-1103, R4-28-502 and R4-28-503** were read in the **2026 ADRE Law Book** on **2026-08-20**.
> Every quoted passage below is transcribed from that reading.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: A. Supervision: A.A.C. R4-28-1103
chunks.excerpt:
1. State the standard R4-28-1103(A) imposes on an employing and a designated broker.
2. List the areas the rule says written policies, procedures and systems must cover.
3. State what R4-28-1103(B) requires a designated broker's compliance-monitoring system to include, and
   what happens if it is not enforced.
4. State the rule on responsibility for the acts of licensees and employees.
5. State the advertising requirements in R4-28-502 that a salesperson performs personally.
6. State the "owner/agent" rule and the rule on the word "acre."
7. State what R4-28-502(J) provides about electronic media, artificial intelligence and scrolling.
8. State the prohibitions in R4-28-503 on premiums, prizes and games of chance.

---

## A. Supervision: A.A.C. R4-28-1103

### A.1 The standard — subsection (A)

> **(A)**: An employing broker and a designated broker shall exercise **reasonable supervision and control**,
> which **includes the establishment and enforcement of written policies, procedures, and systems** to
> review and manage —

| The rule names | Which in practice means |
|---|---|
| **Transactions of all licensees** | Every file, not the difficult ones only |
| **Use of disclosure forms and contracts** | Which forms the brokerage uses and how they are completed |
| **Filing, storing and maintaining documents** | Where the file lives and for how long |
| **Handling of trust funds** | Money that is not the brokerage's |
| **Use of unlicensed assistants** | What an unlicensed person may and may not do |
| **Advertising** | Everything in Part B of this module |

chunks.heading: A.2 The monitoring system and the progressive disciplinary policy — subsection (B)
chunks.excerpt:
— and, further, to **oversee delegation of authority**; to **familiarize licensees with federal, state and
local law**; and to **review and inspect** documents that may have a material effect on a party's rights or
obligations, **and advertising and marketing by licensees in the broker's employ.**

**Read two words carefully.** The rule says **"establishment and enforcement."** A written policy that
exists and is not enforced does not satisfy (A) — establishment is half of the requirement.

And the policies must be **written.** The rule does not treat an understood office practice as a policy.

**"Familiarize licensees with federal, state and local law"** is a supervision duty owed to *you*. It does
not relieve you of the duties in Module AZ-11 — R4-28-1101 runs to the licensee — but it tells you
something about how a properly run Arizona brokerage is supposed to operate, and gives you a legitimate
expectation to raise when it does not.

### A.2 The monitoring system and the progressive disciplinary policy — subsection (B)

> **(B)**: A designated broker shall establish a system for monitoring compliance that ***"must include a
> progressive disciplinary policy for managing violations of the employing broker's policies which would
> also represent a violation of any statutory requirement"*** — and **failure to enforce it is itself a
> violation.**

Three separate requirements, and licensees routinely notice only the first:

chunks.heading: A.3 Responsibility for the acts of others — subsection (D)
chunks.excerpt:
1. **A system for monitoring compliance** must exist.
2. That system **must include a progressive disciplinary policy** — aimed specifically at violations of the
   brokerage's own policies **that would also be statutory violations.**
3. **Failure to enforce it is itself a violation.** The rule closes the obvious gap: a brokerage cannot
   satisfy (B) by writing a disciplinary policy it never applies.

**"Progressive."** The rule uses the word and does not define it, and **this module does not supply a
definition, a number of steps, or a sequence of sanctions** — none is stated in the rule text read.

### A.3 Responsibility for the acts of others — subsection (D)

> **(D)**: *"An employing broker is **responsible for the acts of all licensees and other employees
> acting**"* in the brokerage.

**"And other employees."** The responsibility is not limited to licensees. Unlicensed staff are inside it,
which is why (A) requires a written policy on the **use of unlicensed assistants.**

**What this does not mean.** Broker responsibility under (D) does not remove the salesperson's own duties.
R4-28-1101 imposes them on the **licensee**, and Module AZ-11 works through them. **(D) adds a second
person who answers; it does not subtract the first.** A salesperson who assumes that a broker's
responsibility is a personal shield has misread the relationship between the two rules.

**Where (C) of R4-28-1101 fits.** Recall that when a licensee cannot perform an act required by rule or
statute, R4-28-1101(C) requires the licensee to **expeditiously notify the designated broker.** That duty
and this supervision system are the same machinery seen from the two ends.

---

## B. Advertising: A.A.C. R4-28-502

chunks.heading: B.1 The two rules about who is behind the offer
chunks.excerpt:
This is the part of the module a salesperson uses weekly, and the part where a licensee acting alone can
breach a rule in a single post.

### B.1 The two rules about who is behind the offer

> **(A)**: A licensee **shall not advertise property in a manner that implies that no salesperson or broker
> is taking part** in the offer.

The classic breach is the advertisement written to look like a private sale. **If a licensee is involved,
the advertisement may not imply otherwise.**

> **(B)**: A licensee advertising **their own or another licensee's property** shall **disclose they are
> licensed** and, **as the property owner, place the words "owner/agent" in the advertisement.**

**Two obligations here, and they are different.** Advertising your own property **or another licensee's**
requires disclosure that you are licensed. Where you are the **property owner**, the rule prescribes the
words themselves: **"owner/agent."** The rule states that term, and this module states no substitute for it.

**Note how this pairs with Module AZ-11.** R4-28-1101(E)(1) requires written disclosure to the other
parties, before any binding agreement, that the **licensee has a license and is acting as a principal.**
R4-28-502(B) requires the disclosure **in the advertisement**, before there are any parties at all. **Two
rules, two moments, both mandatory.**

### B.2 Accuracy — subsection (C)

> **(C)**: All advertising shall contain **accurate claims and representations** and **fully state factual
> material**; a licensee **shall not misrepresent the facts or create misleading or ambiguous impressions.**

chunks.heading: B.3 Identifying the employing broker — subsection (E)
chunks.excerpt:
Three standards stacked: **accurate**, **fully stated**, and **not misleading or ambiguous.** The third is
the widest — an advertisement in which every individual statement is true can still create a misleading
impression, and the rule reaches that.

### B.3 Identifying the employing broker — subsection (E)

> **(E)**: All advertising shall **identify in a clear and prominent manner the employing broker's legal
> name or the dba name(s)** on the employing broker's licence certificate.

**"Clear and prominent."** Not present somewhere. And the name used must be the **legal name or a dba
appearing on the employing broker's licence certificate** — not an informal team or personal brand name
that appears on no certificate.

### B.4 The designated broker is responsible — subsection (G)

> **(G)**: *"**The designated broker is responsible for the advertising of all real estate activity.**"*

This is the sentence that connects Part B back to Part A. It is also why **R4-28-1103(A)** requires the
broker's written policies to cover advertising, and requires the broker to **review and inspect advertising
and marketing by licensees in the broker's employ.** A salesperson who publishes without the brokerage's
process has put the designated broker in breach of a rule the salesperson does not personally hold.

### B.5 The word "acre" — subsection (H)

> **(H)**: *"A licensee shall **not use the term 'acre,' either alone or modified, unless referring to an
> area of land representing at least 43,560 square feet.**"*

**"Either alone or modified"** closes the obvious workaround — "nearly an acre," "acre-plus," "a full acre"
are all inside the rule. **43,560 square feet** is the figure the rule states, and it is the figure Module
AZ-09 uses in the general land-measurement content.

chunks.heading: B.6 Signs and electronic publication — subsection (I)
chunks.excerpt:
### B.6 Signs and electronic publication — subsection (I)

> **(I)**: Before placing a sign or publishing to an electronic medium, a licensee shall **secure the
> written consent of the property owner**, and the sign or publication **shall be promptly removed upon
> request of the property owner.**

**Written consent before**, and **prompt removal on request.** The removal duty has no stated condition —
the owner's request is enough.

### B.7 Electronic media, artificial intelligence, and the no-scroll rule — subsection (J)

This subsection is the one most likely to be new even to an experienced licensee, and it is transcribed in
full because each clause does distinct work.

> **(J)**: *"The use of an **electronic medium, such as the Internet, artificial intelligence, or web site
> technology**, that **targets residents of this State** with the offering of a property interest or real
> estate brokerage services **constitutes the dissemination of advertising** as defined in A.R.S. §
> 32-2101(2). All advertising using an electronic medium must comply with Subsection E ... and **if
> advertising online, all requirements of advertising set forth above must be satisfied on the
> advertisement without the need to scroll.**"*

chunks.heading: C. Promotional activities: A.A.C. R4-28-503
chunks.excerpt:
| Clause | What it settles |
|---|---|
| *"electronic medium, such as the Internet, **artificial intelligence**, or web site technology"* | The rule **names artificial intelligence** as an electronic medium. Output generated by such a medium is not outside the advertising rules. |
| *"**targets residents of this State**"* | The trigger is targeting Arizona residents — not where the licensee, the server, or the platform sits. |
| *"**constitutes the dissemination of advertising**"* | It is advertising. Every rule in R4-28-502 applies to it. |
| *"must comply with **Subsection E**"* | The employing broker's legal or certificate dba name, **clear and prominent**. |
| *"**without the need to scroll**"* | The requirements must be satisfied **on the advertisement itself**, visible without scrolling. |

**The no-scroll rule is a design requirement, not a disclosure preference.** A post that carries the
brokerage name only in a linked profile, a comment, a bio, or below the fold does not satisfy (J) as it is
written. **This is the rule short-form social posts break most often.**

---

## C. Promotional activities: A.A.C. R4-28-503

> A licensee **shall not** describe a premium offered at no cost or reduced cost as an ***"award"*** or
> ***"prize"*** or a similar term, and shall **clearly disclose in writing the terms, costs, conditions,
> restrictions, and expiration date** of a premium offer **before the person participates.** Unless
> otherwise provided by law, a person **shall not solicit, sell, or offer to sell an interest in a
> development by conducting a lottery contest, drawing, or game of chance.**

Three rules:

chunks.heading: D. Working the three rules together
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Vocabulary.** A premium offered at no cost or reduced cost may not be called an **"award," a "prize,"
   or any similar term.** The rule regulates the *word*, because the word is what misleads.
2. **Written disclosure, before participation.** Five things must be disclosed **in writing** and **before
   the person participates**: **terms, costs, conditions, restrictions, and expiration date.** Missing one
   is a breach; disclosing all five afterwards is a breach.
3. **No lottery, drawing or game of chance** may be used to solicit, sell or offer to sell an interest in a
   development, **unless otherwise provided by law.**

**The exception clause is real and this module does not fill it in.** *"Unless otherwise provided by law"*
points somewhere outside the rule text read, and **no such other law was read by this project.** A licensee
proposing any promotion of this kind takes it to the designated broker and to counsel.

---

## D. Working the three rules together

**A salesperson wants to run a social campaign on a listing, using an image-generation tool, offering a gift
card drawing to anyone who books a showing, and identifying the listing as "just under an acre."**

chunks.heading: Module AZ-12 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
| Element | Rule | Outcome under the rule as written |
|---|---|---|
| Social post targeting Arizona residents | **R4-28-502(J)** | It **is advertising**; all of R4-28-502 applies |
| Generated by an AI tool | **R4-28-502(J)** | The rule **names artificial intelligence** as an electronic medium — no exemption |
| Brokerage name in the linked bio only | **R4-28-502(E) and (J)** | Fails: the legal or certificate dba name must be **clear and prominent** and satisfied **without scrolling** |
| "Just under an acre" | **R4-28-502(H)** | Prohibited — *"either alone or modified"*, unless at least **43,560 square feet** |
| Gift card drawing | **R4-28-503** | A **drawing or game of chance** may not be used to solicit or offer to sell an interest in a development, unless otherwise provided by law |
| Calling the gift card a "prize" | **R4-28-503** | Prohibited vocabulary for a premium at no or reduced cost |
| Sign to go with the campaign | **R4-28-502(I)** | Requires the **owner's written consent first**; **prompt removal on request** |
| Nobody at the brokerage reviewed it | **R4-28-502(G)**, **R4-28-1103(A)** | The **designated broker is responsible for the advertising**, and the broker's written policies must cover advertising and require review and inspection |

**Seven rule references in one campaign.** Nothing in it is unusual, and that is the point of putting
supervision and advertising in the same module: **the salesperson generates the exposure and the broker
carries it.**

---

## Module AZ-12 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module AZ-12
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items, delivered as in Module AZ-01. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100 percent**
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; **the 75 percent in R4-28-401(A)(1)** applies to the
**proctored, in-person course examination**, which is a separate event.

## Instructor source note for Module AZ-12

Drawn entirely from **A.A.C. R4-28-1103, R4-28-502 and R4-28-503**, read in the **2026 ADRE Law Book** at
re.az.gov on **2026-08-20**, and recorded in `arizona/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **A.R.S. §§ 32-2151 and 32-2151.01** and any other
**trust account or records statute**; any rule on **unlicensed assistants** beyond R4-28-1103(A)'s naming of
the subject; **A.R.S. § 32-2101(2)**'s definition of advertising, which R4-28-502(J) cites but which this
project did not read; **A.R.S. § 32-2153** and any disciplinary ground; any **Department substantive policy
statement or advertising guidance**; and the law referred to by R4-28-503's *"unless otherwise provided by
law."*

**No trust account rule, records retention period, unlicensed-assistant task list, disciplinary
consequence, penalty, or definition of "progressive," "reasonable supervision," or "clear and prominent" is
