> **§ 12-10-404(3)(a)** — a seller's or landlord's agent owes no duty to the buyer or tenant *"except that
> a broker shall ... **disclose to any prospective buyer or tenant all ADVERSE MATERIAL FACTS ACTUALLY
> KNOWN** by the broker ... including ... adverse material facts pertaining to **the title and the physical
> condition of the property, any material defects in the property, and any environmental hazards** affecting
> the property that are required by law to be disclosed."*
>
> **§ 12-10-407(2)(b)(VI) and (VII)** impose the same on a transaction-broker, in both directions.
>
> And in the other direction — **§ 12-10-405(3)(a)** — a buyer's agent must disclose to a prospective seller
> all adverse material facts actually known *"**including ... adverse material facts concerning the buyer's
> or tenant's financial ability to perform the terms of the transaction and whether the buyer intends to
> occupy the property to be purchased as a principal residence.**"*

**And the counterpart:** **§§ 12-10-404(3)(b), 12-10-405(5) and 12-10-407(4) and (5)** each provide that
the broker **owes no duty to conduct an independent inspection** of the property, and **no duty to
independently verify** statements made by a party or an independent inspector.

**Environmental conditions a broker may encounter:** soil and groundwater contamination; **asbestos and
lead** in older construction; **radon**; **mould and moisture intrusion**; underground storage tanks; and,
in some areas, **methamphetamine contamination**. In every case the broker's role is the same: **recognise
that a question exists, say so, and route it to someone qualified.** **Rule 6.2** gives the four routes.

chunks.heading: F. Federal procedures and laws governing real estate
chunks.excerpt:
**The federal lead-based paint requirements for pre-1978 housing** are named by the **Current Legal Issues**
outline at its Appendix E. **The federal rule text was NOT read by this project**, and **no form, deadline,
period or penalty from it is stated anywhere in this build.**

**§ 38-35.5-101, psychologically impacted property**, is cited by **four** provisions read for this build —
§§ 12-10-404(2)(e), 12-10-405(2)(e), 12-10-407(3)(e) and 12-10-404(3)(a). **The statute itself was NOT
read**, and **this course states nothing about what it provides.** What it does state is what the duty
sections say: facts or suspicions regarding circumstances that may psychologically impact or stigmatize
real property **pursuant to § 38-35.5-101** are **not disclosed without informed consent.**

---

## F. Federal procedures and laws governing real estate

The Commission's outline names these by number. Each is here, with what it governs.

### F.1 The Federal Fair Housing Act

**Protected classes:** **race, colour, religion, national origin, sex, disability, and familial status.**

chunks.heading: F.1 The Federal Fair Housing Act
chunks.excerpt:
| Prohibited practice | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Steering** | Directing prospects toward or away from areas or properties on the basis of a protected characteristic, **whatever reason is offered** |
| **Blockbusting** | Inducing or attempting to induce owners to sell or rent by representations about the entry of persons of a protected characteristic — prohibited **whether or not the representation is true and whether or not any property changes hands** |
| **Redlining** | Denying or varying the terms of loans or insurance by the area's composition |
| **Discriminatory advertising** | Advertising indicating a preference, limitation or discrimination |
| **Refusal to make a reasonable accommodation** | Refusing a change in rules, policies, practices or services needed for a person with a disability to use a dwelling |
| **Refusal to permit a reasonable modification** | Refusing to permit a physical change to the premises |

**When asked directly about the composition of a neighbourhood:** decline to characterise it, say why, and
point the enquirer to publicly available data. **The honesty of the answer is not the issue; the effect of
it is.**

**State and local law may reach further.** **The Colorado Fair Housing Act was NOT read by this project**,
and **no additional Colorado protected class, exemption or remedy is stated in this course.** It is named
by the **Contracts and Regulations** outline at Topic I.D, and that is where it belongs.

chunks.heading: F.2 The Americans with Disabilities Act
chunks.excerpt:
**Colorado's statute puts fair housing inside the duty sections.** **§§ 12-10-404(1)(e), 12-10-405(1)(e)
and 12-10-407(2)(d)** each require the broker to *"comply with any applicable federal, state, or local
laws, rules, regulations, or ordinances **including fair housing and civil rights statutes or
regulations**"* — so a fair housing violation is also a violation of the brokerage relationship statute, and
**§ 12-10-411** makes a Part 4 violation an act the Commission may investigate.

### F.2 The Americans with Disabilities Act

Governs **accessibility in places of public accommodation and commercial facilities**, and employment. It
is not the same statute as the Fair Housing Act and it does not have the same reach: **ADA questions in
commercial property are questions for counsel and for an accessibility professional.** **The ADA text was
NOT read by this project** and **no requirement, standard, dimension or deadline from it is stated here.**

### F.3 Antitrust

**Price fixing, market allocation, group boycotts and tying arrangements** are the classic categories.

**What that means for a broker in practice:** commission rates are set **between the brokerage and its
client**, never by agreement among competing firms, and never described to a client as standard, customary,
or set by anyone. A conversation with a competitor about what to charge is the conversation to leave.

**No antitrust statute was read by this project**, and **no penalty, threshold or exemption is stated
here.** The principle is stated because the outline names the subject and because the practice consequence
does not depend on the statutory detail.

### F.4 Marketing controls

The outline names four, and each is here:

chunks.heading: F.5 Firm and licensee relationships
chunks.excerpt:
| **a. UCC** | The Uniform Commercial Code, which governs transactions in **goods** and secured interests in personal property — reached in a real estate transaction where personal property is conveyed alongside the realty. **§ 12-10-403(4)(a)** authorises a broker to complete standard forms *"including standard forms intended to convey personal property as part of the real estate transaction."* |
|---|---|
| **b. Interstate Land Sales Full Disclosure** | Federal disclosure and registration requirements applying to certain sales of subdivided land across state lines |
| **c. Telephone Consumer Protection** | Federal restrictions on telephone solicitation, automated calls and faxes — the statute behind do-not-call compliance in prospecting |
| **d. Securities laws** | Certain real estate interests, particularly fractional and passive investment interests, may be **securities**; note that **§ 12-10-201(6)** exempts licensed broker-dealers from parts of the licensing provisions, and that offering an interest that is a security is a matter for securities counsel |

**None of these four statutes was read by this project.** **No registration threshold, exemption, deadline,
call-time restriction, disclosure requirement or penalty from any of them is stated anywhere in this
build**, and a broker whose practice touches one takes it to counsel. **Rule 6.2** again: decline, obtain
the knowledge, obtain assistance, or co-list.

### F.5 Firm and licensee relationships

The outline's last sub-item, and it is the bridge to Colorado's own supervision rules.

chunks.heading: Module 03 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**The general concepts:** an employing broker and the licensees under them; the difference between an
**employee** and an **independent contractor** for tax purposes; the firm's **written office policy**; and
the firm's responsibility for what its people do.

**Colorado's own requirements were read, and three are worth stating here because a student meets them
immediately:**

> **§ 12-10-408(1)(a)**: every broker *"**shall adopt a WRITTEN OFFICE POLICY that identifies and describes
> the relationships offered to the public** by the broker."*
>
> **§ 12-10-408(1)(b)**: *"A broker **shall not be required to offer or engage in any one or in all** of the
> brokerage relationships"* — a firm may decline to offer agency, or to offer transaction-brokerage.
>
> **Rule 6.3.A.1**: employing brokers *"**must exercise authority, direction, and supervision** over any
> Associate Brokers"*, and *"**whenever a complaint is filed with the Commission against an Associate
> Broker, the Commission may investigate whether there have been violations** ... **by the Employing
> Broker.**"* **Rule 6.3.A.2** extends supervision to **all unlicensed employees**, including on-site
> managers, secretaries, bookkeepers and personal assistants.

The **Practical Applications** course develops this from the new broker's side under its Topic I, *Entering
the Field*, and the **Record Keeping and Trust Accounts** course develops the employing broker's accounting
responsibilities under **Rule 5.22**, which holds the employing broker **jointly responsible with the firm**
for Chapter 5.

---

## Module 03 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 03
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
*"**testing is required** to establish individual's satisfactory completion of the statutory
requirements"*, and **these items are not that test.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 03

Written to the **Commission's Real Estate Law and Practice qualifying education outline, approved April 1,
1998**, Topic III and its sub-topics A through F, in the outline's own order and using the outline's own
sub-item names. The hour figure is the Commission's.

The Colorado provisions quoted — **§§ 12-10-403, 12-10-404, 12-10-405, 12-10-406, 12-10-407, 12-10-408,
12-10-409 and 12-10-411**, and **Rules 5.7, 5.12, 5.22, 6.2, 6.3, 6.7 and 7.1** — are transcribed from
**C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10** and **4 CCR 725-1**, read on 2026-08-20 and recorded in
`colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** the **federal Fair Housing Act**, the **Americans
with Disabilities Act**, the **antitrust statutes**, the **Interstate Land Sales Full Disclosure Act**, the
**Telephone Consumer Protection Act**, the **UCC**, the **federal securities laws**, and the **federal
lead-based paint regulations** — every one of them in its own text; the **Colorado Fair Housing Act**;
**C.R.S. § 38-35.5-101**; Colorado's **statute of frauds**; the **Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act**;
**C.R.S. §§ 12-10-217, 12-10-219 and 12-10-222**; and **every Commission-approved form.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 03
chunks.excerpt:
**No protected class beyond the seven federal classes, no exemption, no threshold, no deadline, no penalty
and no form provision is stated in this module.** The Colorado statutory and rule provisions quoted are
transcribed verbatim from the sections named beside them.

lessons.title: Colorado Real Estate Law and Practice — Module 04

chunks.heading: Colorado Real Estate Law and Practice — Module 04
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Real Estate Law and Practice — Module 04

## Real estate finance and settlement

**Course:** Real Estate Law and Practice (48 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 12.0** of 48.0
**Commission outline topic:** **IV — Real Estate Finance and Settlement**, allocated **12 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What the Commission's outline puts in this topic
>
> | Sub-topic | Delivered in |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** Financing components — **1. Instruments** (notes, mortgages, **contract for deed (land contract)**, deeds of trust); **2. Sources** (primary market, secondary market, seller financing); **3. Loan types**; **4. Financing concepts, terminology and obligations** | Parts A–D |
> | **B.** Lender requirements | Part E |
> | **C.** Settlement/closing | Part F |
> | **D.** Settlement documents (e.g. title review, **RESPA**) | Part G |
> | **E.** Financing costs / property taxation proration calculations and other closing cost | Part H |
>
> **This is the national finance module.** The **Closings** course — 24 hours, of which the Commission
> allocates **16 to the preparation of a minimum of eight closing problems** — is where Colorado practice is
> taught, and this module points forward to it rather than duplicating it.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: A. Instruments
chunks.excerpt:
1. Distinguish the note from the security instrument and say what each does.
2. Distinguish a mortgage, a deed of trust and a contract for deed by who holds what.
3. Distinguish the primary and secondary mortgage markets and name what the secondary market does.
4. State the principal loan types and what distinguishes each.
5. Calculate loan-to-value, points, and a simple interest figure from given data.
6. State what a lender ordinarily requires and what underwriting looks at.
7. State what happens at settlement and what a broker's role is and is not.
8. Prorate a shared item across a closing date using a stated convention.

---

## A. Instruments

### A.1 The note and the security instrument are two documents

| Document | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Promissory note** | The borrower's **promise to repay**. It creates the **debt** |
| **Security instrument** | Pledges the property as **security** for that promise. It creates the **lien** |

**Two instruments, two functions.** A release of one does not by itself release the other, and a borrower
who assumes otherwise has assumed something expensive.

**What a note states:** principal, interest rate, payment amount and schedule, maturity, and the
provisions the parties negotiated — prepayment, late charges, acceleration, and default.

### A.2 Mortgage, deed of trust, and contract for deed

chunks.heading: A.2 Mortgage, deed of trust, and contract for deed
chunks.excerpt:
| Instrument | Parties | Who holds what |
|---|---|---|
| **Mortgage** | Mortgagor (borrower), mortgagee (lender) | Borrower holds title; lender holds a **lien** |
| **Deed of trust** | Borrower, lender (beneficiary), and a **third party trustee** | A **trustee** holds title or a power of sale for the lender's benefit until the debt is satisfied |
| **Contract for deed (land contract)** | Vendor (seller), vendee (buyer) | **Seller retains legal title**; buyer takes **equitable title** and possession, and receives the deed when the contract is performed |

**The contract for deed is the one the Commission's outline names explicitly and the one new brokers
understand least.** The buyer occupies and pays but does **not** hold legal title, so the buyer's position
depends entirely on the contract's terms and on the law governing forfeiture and foreclosure of such
contracts.

> **A boundary this module holds, and it matters here more than anywhere else in this course.** **Colorado's
> foreclosure statutes, its public trustee system, and its law governing contracts for deed were NOT read by
> this project.** **No Colorado foreclosure procedure, notice, period, cure right, redemption right, or
> deficiency rule is stated anywhere in this build.**
>
> Colorado uses a **public trustee** system that is distinctive among the states. **This course does not
> describe it**, because the statute establishing it was not read. A broker whose transaction involves a
> contract for deed, a foreclosure, or a deed of trust in default takes it to counsel — and **Rule 6.2.B**
> supplies the four routes: decline, obtain the knowledge, obtain assistance, or co-list.
>
> The **Contracts and Regulations** outline names **deeds of trust** and **foreclosure** under its Topic
> V.B, and the **Current

chunks.heading: A.3 Provisions that travel with security instruments
chunks.excerpt:
Legal Issues** outline names **financing, liens and foreclosures** among its
> representative areas. Those are the Colorado courses.

**Lien theory and title theory** describe two approaches: under a **lien theory** the borrower holds title
and the lender holds a lien; under a **title theory** the lender or a trustee holds legal title until the
debt is satisfied. **Which approach a state follows, and what its process is, is that state's law**, and
this course states no Colorado answer.

### A.3 Provisions that travel with security instruments

| Provision | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Acceleration clause** | On default, the whole balance becomes due |
| **Alienation (due-on-sale) clause** | On transfer of the property, the lender may call the loan |
| **Prepayment provision** | Whether, and on what terms, the borrower may pay early |
| **Subordination** | An agreement placing one lien behind another |
| **Release / partial release** | Discharge of the lien, in whole or as to part of the property |
| **Defeasance** | The provision defeating the security interest on full payment |

**The alienation clause is why an assumption needs the lender.** A buyer taking over an existing loan
ordinarily needs the lender's approval, **and without a written release the seller may remain liable on the
note.** That continuing liability is the point a broker ensures the seller understands and takes to
counsel — a release is a legal document and its absence is a legal exposure.

---

## B. Sources

### B.1 The primary mortgage market

Where loans are **originated** — the lenders who deal with borrowers directly: banks, savings
institutions, credit unions, mortgage bankers and mortgage brokers.

### B.2 The secondary mortgage market

chunks.heading: B.3 Seller financing
chunks.excerpt:
Where existing loans are **bought and sold** after origination. Its function is to give originators
liquidity: a lender that sells a loan recovers its capital and can lend again.

**Its practical consequence for a borrower** is that the entities buying loans set **underwriting
standards**, and those standards shape what a borrower is offered long before anyone meets a lender.

**A borrower's loan may be sold and its servicing transferred.** That is ordinary, and it does not change
the terms of the note.

### B.3 Seller financing

The seller takes back a note secured by the property, or sells on a contract for deed. Named by the
Commission's outline, and named again by the **Contracts and Regulations** outline's Topic IV note, which
requires the student's sales contract work to *"include examples of **new financing, loan assumption, and
owner carry financing.**"*

**"Owner carry" is the Colorado term of art**, and a broker will see it on Commission-approved forms.

---

## C. Loan types

chunks.heading: D. Financing concepts, terminology and obligations
chunks.excerpt:
| Type | What distinguishes it |
|---|---|
| **Fixed rate** | The note rate does not change for the term |
| **Adjustable rate** | The rate changes on stated dates by an **index plus a margin**, subject to any **caps** the note provides |
| **Conventional** | Not insured or guaranteed by a government programme |
| **FHA-insured** | Insured by the Federal Housing Administration |
| **VA-guaranteed** | Guaranteed by the Department of Veterans Affairs |
| **Interest-only** | Payments cover interest for a period; principal is unretired during it |
| **Balloon** | A payment schedule that does not fully amortise, leaving a lump sum at maturity |
| **Construction** | Advanced in draws against progress, ordinarily short term |
| **Blanket** | One loan secured by more than one parcel, ordinarily with a partial release provision |
| **Wraparound** | A new loan that wraps an existing one, the new lender servicing the underlying debt |
| **Reverse** | Advances against equity, with repayment deferred |
| **Home equity** | A loan or line secured by the equity in a property already owned |

**On an adjustable-rate loan the borrower's exposure is the product of four things** — the **index**, the
**margin**, the **adjustment dates**, and the **caps** — and all four are in the note. That is a
conversation with the lender.

**The Closings course requires the eight closing problems to use a mix of "cash, owner carry, assumptions
(FHA, VA and conventional), new loans (FHA, VA and conventional), and a closing involving a multi-family
property."** This table is the vocabulary that course assumes.

---

## D. Financing concepts, terminology and obligations

### D.1 Amortisation

chunks.heading: D.2 Loan-to-value ratio
chunks.excerpt:
**Repayment of principal and interest over a term in level payments.** Early payments are mostly interest;
the principal portion grows with each payment until the balance is retired at maturity.

**Why it matters to a broker:** a seller who has held a loan a few years has retired far less principal
than they expect, and the payoff figure is rarely what they guess. The number comes from the lender.

**A partially amortising loan leaves a balloon.** A fully amortising loan does not.

### D.2 Loan-to-value ratio

> **LTV = Loan Amount ÷ the LESSER of purchase price or appraised value**

**The "lesser of" is the part that matters when an appraisal comes in below contract price.** The lender
lends against the lower figure, and the gap becomes the buyer's problem to solve — with more cash, a
renegotiated price, or a contract that ends on its appraisal contingency.

### D.3 Points

**A discount point is one percent of the LOAN AMOUNT**, paid at closing to reduce the interest rate.

*Worked, with every figure given:* on a **$400,000** purchase with **25 percent** down, the loan is
**$300,000**. **Two points cost $6,000.** If those points reduce the rate by **0.25 percent**, the first
year's interest saving is **$300,000 × 0.25% = $750**, so on those figures the points take **eight years**
of holding to recover.

**Whether that is worth doing depends on how long the borrower keeps the loan**, which is the borrower's
decision with the lender and their tax adviser. **A broker can do the arithmetic with figures the lender
supplies. A broker does not tell a borrower which product to take** — §§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V),
12-10-405(1)(c)(V) and 12-10-407(2)(b)(II) each require advising the party to obtain expert advice on
material matters beyond the broker's expertise.

chunks.heading: D.4 Simple interest
chunks.excerpt:
### D.4 Simple interest

> **Interest = Principal × Rate × Time**

*Worked, with every figure given:* **$260,000** at **6.5 percent** for **one month** is
**$260,000 × 0.065 ÷ 12 = $1,408.33.**

Interest in a mortgage payment is ordinarily paid **in arrears** — the payment made on the first of a month
covers the interest that accrued the previous month. That fact is the reason for the **prepaid interest**
line at closing, covered in Part H.

### D.5 Mortgage insurance

**Private mortgage insurance protects the LENDER**, not the borrower, on a higher loan-to-value
conventional loan, and the borrower pays for it. **FHA loans carry their own mortgage insurance
premiums.** Borrowers routinely assume the coverage protects them, and correcting that assumption is
ordinary competent service. **Every rule about when it may be cancelled comes from the lender and from
federal law this project did not read.**

### D.6 Qualifying

**Underwriting looks at four things:** the borrower's **income**, their **debts**, their **credit**, and
the **collateral.** **Prequalification** is an informal estimate on stated information; **preapproval**
involves verification and a conditional commitment. **Neither is a guarantee**, and a broker representing a
seller has a duty that turns on exactly that: **§ 12-10-404(3)(a)** and **§ 12-10-407(2)(b)(VII)** require
disclosure of adverse material facts **actually known** concerning the buyer's financial ability to perform.

**No qualifying ratio, credit score, down payment minimum or loan limit is stated in this course**, because
none was read from a primary source. Those figures come from the lender and change without notice.

---

## E. Lender requirements

chunks.heading: F. Settlement and closing
chunks.excerpt:
What a lender ordinarily requires before funding, and what a broker should expect to see moving:

| Requirement | Why |
|---|---|
| **Application and documentation** | Income, assets, employment, identity |
| **Appraisal** | To establish the value the loan is measured against |
| **Title work** | Commitment and, ordinarily, a **lender's policy** of title insurance |
| **Survey or ILC**, where required | To confirm boundaries and improvements |
| **Hazard insurance** | The lender's collateral must be insured |
| **Flood determination** and, where required, flood insurance | Statutory and programme requirements |
| **Payoff and lien releases** | So the lender's lien takes the agreed priority |
| **Closing instructions** | What the closing entity must do before funds are released |

**Colorado's Improvement Location Certificate** is named by the **Contracts and Regulations** outline at
Topic V.D, alongside land descriptions and surveys.

**A lender's policy of title insurance insures the LENDER's interest.** A buyer who wants their own
coverage needs an **owner's policy**, and that is a decision the buyer makes with the title company.

---

## F. Settlement and closing

**What happens at a closing:** the deed is delivered; the consideration is paid; the loan is funded; liens
to be discharged are paid and released; prorations are settled; the closing statement is signed; and the
deed and security instrument are recorded.

**Who conducts it varies**, and Colorado contemplates both: the **Closings** outline's Topic I.A
distinguishes a **broker prepared closing** from a **title company prepared closing**, and states *"the
**individual responsibility of licensee holding listing or buyer brokerage agreement**"* separately from
both.

chunks.heading: G. Settlement documents
chunks.excerpt:
> **This is the point at which this module stops and the Closings course begins.** That course carries 24
> hours, of which the Commission allocates:
>
> | Closings course topic | Hours |
> |---|---|
> | I. Broker's responsibility relating to closing | 1.0 |
> | II. Introduction to a 6-column worksheet | 2.0 |
> | III. Closing to a prepared contract | 4.0 |
> | IV. Legal documents | 1.0 |
> | **V. Preparation of a minimum of 8 closing problems** | **16.0** |
>
> **Two-thirds of that course is the eight problems**, and its outline requires *"**ALL STUDENTS MUST
> SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETE A WRITTEN EXAMINATION COVERING ALL MAJOR TOPIC AREAS OF THIS OUTLINE.**"*

**One Colorado rule about closing was read and belongs here.** **Rule 6.19** governs closing responsibility
and **Good Funds**; the Closings outline names **Good Funds** at its Topic I.E, and names **withholding**
for a **non-resident seller** and under the **Foreign Investor Real Property Tax Act** at Topic I.D. **The
withholding statutes themselves were NOT read by this project**, and **no rate, threshold, exemption or
form is stated anywhere in this build.**

**What a broker does at closing:** review the closing statement against the contract — confirming price,
deposit, compensation and prorations — and **ask about anything that does not match.** What a broker does
**not** do is opine on the legal effect of documents or on tax consequences. **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)** requires
the broker to advise the parties that the forms **have important legal consequences** and that they
**should consult legal counsel before signing.**

---

## G. Settlement documents

chunks.heading: G. Settlement documents
chunks.excerpt:
| Document | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Title commitment** | The title company's undertaking to insure on stated terms — **its exceptions schedule is where its substance lives** |
| **Deed** | The instrument of conveyance |
| **Note and security instrument** | The debt and the lien |
| **Closing statement** | The accounting of the transaction between the parties |
| **Payoff statements and lien releases** | What discharges existing liens |
| **Escrow or closing instructions** | What the closing entity is directed to do |
| **Federal disclosures** | The disclosures required of the lender and the settlement agent |

**RESPA is named by the Commission's outline**, and it is the federal statute governing settlement
services on covered residential transactions — disclosures, the prohibition on kickbacks and unearned
fees, and limits on required use of affiliated providers.

> **The RESPA text was NOT read by this project.** **No RESPA disclosure, form, timing requirement, dollar
> threshold, exemption or penalty is stated anywhere in this build.**
>
> **What WAS read is Colorado's rule about it.** **Rule 6.21.A**: *"Brokers and Brokerage Firms **will not
> pay or receive a referral fee except in accordance with RESPA** and unless a **reasonable cause for
> payment of the referral fee exists** pursuant to section 12-10-304(1), C.R.S."* **§ 12-10-304 was not
> read**, and its content is stated nowhere.
>
> And **Rule 6.18** requires **affiliated business arrangement disclosures**. Its statutory basis,
> **§ 12-10-218**, was **not read**, and no requirement from it is stated here.
>
> Two more Colorado rules bear directly on money at settlement, and both **were** read in full: **Rule
> 5.17** requires a broker to obtain the **prior written consent** of the consumer they represe

chunks.heading: H. Prorations and closing costs
chunks.excerpt:
nt before
> assessing or receiving **mark-ups or other compensation** for services performed, and to disclose all
> mark-ups paid by any customer; and **§ 12-10-410(6)** requires that, **prior to entering into a brokerage
> or listing agreement or a contract to buy, sell or lease**, *"**the identity of those parties, persons, or
> entities paying compensation or commissions to any broker shall be disclosed to the parties to the
> transaction.**"*

---

## H. Prorations and closing costs

### H.1 The method

Every proration is the same three steps:

1. **Find the daily (or monthly) rate** — the annual amount divided by the number of days or months the
   convention uses.
2. **Count the periods on each side of the closing**, using the convention the contract states.
3. **Multiply**, and enter the result as a credit to one party and a debit to the other.

**The convention is stated in the contract**, and **this course prescribes none.** A **360-day year with
30-day months** ("statutory" or "banker's" year) and a **365-day year with actual days** are both in use,
and **which party is charged for the day of closing** is likewise a matter of the contract.

### H.2 Worked, with every figure and convention given

> **Prepaid taxes.** Annual taxes of **$3,600** were paid in full by the seller on **1 January**. Closing
> is **1 October**. Using a **360-day year with 30-day months**, and charging the **buyer** for the day of
> closing:
>
> Daily rate **$3,600 ÷ 360 = $10.00**. The buyer holds **90 of the 360** (October, November, December).
> **Buyer's share = 90 × $10.00 = $900**, credited to the seller and debited to the buyer.

chunks.heading: H.3 Items ordinarily prorated or entered
chunks.excerpt:
> **Taxes paid in arrears.** Annual taxes of **$3,600** are payable **after** the year they cover, and
> closing is again **1 October** on the same convention. The **seller** owes for the **270 days** they held
> — **270 × $10.00 = $2,700** — credited to the **buyer**, who will pay the bill.

**Whether a given item is prepaid or in arrears decides the direction of the entry**, and getting the
direction backwards is the classic error. **How Colorado property taxes are levied, assessed and billed was
NOT read by this project, and no Colorado tax convention, rate, assessment ratio or due date is stated
anywhere in this build.**

### H.3 Items ordinarily prorated or entered

| Item | Ordinarily |
|---|---|
| **Property taxes** | Prorated |
| **Rents and security deposits** | Prorated / transferred |
| **Homeowners association assessments** | Prorated |
| **Interest on an assumed loan** | Prorated |
| **Prepaid interest on a new loan** | Charged to the buyer from funding to the end of the month |
| **Insurance** | Prorated where a policy is assumed; otherwise a new premium |
| **Utilities and service contracts** | Prorated or transferred |

### H.4 Debit and credit, in one sentence each

**A debit is what a party pays. A credit is what a party receives or is credited toward what they owe.**
The purchase price is a **debit to the buyer** and a **credit to the seller**; earnest money already paid
is a **credit to the buyer**; a new loan is a **credit to the buyer**; and a lien to be paid off is a
**debit to the seller.**

chunks.heading: H.5 Seller's net — the calculation clients ask for most
chunks.excerpt:
**The six-column worksheet the Closings course teaches is this logic in a grid**, and the Record Keeping
and Trust Accounts course then requires the student to work *"from a sample contract and **6-column
settlement worksheet**"* to create journal and ledger entries and reconcile them.

### H.5 Seller's net — the calculation clients ask for most

*Worked, with every figure given:* a seller wants **$282,000** in hand after a **6 percent** commission
and **$3,000** of other closing costs.

$282,000 + $3,000 = **$285,000**, which is **94 percent** of the price, so the price is
**$285,000 ÷ 0.94 = $303,191.49.**

**The commission is a percentage of the PRICE, not of the net.** That is why the net plus costs is
**divided by the complement of the rate**, and why multiplying the net by the rate gives the wrong answer.

**The Practical Applications outline names this at its Topic VI.A.1.c** — *"Calculating seller's net
proceeds & buyers cash to close"* — and that course applies it to a live transaction.

---

## Module 04 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
*"**testing is required** to establish individual's satisfactory completion of the statutory
requirements"*, and **these items are not that test.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 04

Written to the **Commission's Real Estate Law and Practice qualifying education outline, approved April 1,
1998**, Topic IV and its sub-topics A through E, in the outline's own order and using the outline's own
sub-item names, including **"contract for deed (land contract)"** and **"RESPA"**. The hour figure is the
Commission's.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 04
chunks.excerpt:
The Colorado provisions cited — **§§ 12-10-403(4), 12-10-404(1)(c)(V) and (3)(a), 12-10-405(1)(c)(V),
12-10-407(2)(b)(II) and (VII), and 12-10-410(6)**, and **Rules 5.17, 6.2, 6.19 and 6.21.A** — are
transcribed from **C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10** and **4 CCR 725-1**, read on 2026-08-20.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **RESPA, TILA, TRID and ECOA**; Colorado's
**foreclosure statutes and public trustee provisions**; its law on **contracts for deed**; its **property
tax, assessment and levy** statutes; the **non-resident seller withholding** provisions and **FIRPTA**;
**C.R.S. §§ 12-10-218 and 12-10-304**; and **every Commission-approved form**, including the closing
instructions and settlement forms.

**No qualifying ratio, credit score, down payment minimum, loan limit, interest rate, mortgage insurance
threshold, withholding rate, tax rate, assessment ratio, proration convention, RESPA requirement, penalty
or form provision is stated in this module.** Every figure used in a worked calculation is supplied inside
that calculation as a given, and the arithmetic is shown so a reviewer can check it.

lessons.title: Colorado Real Estate Law and Practice — Module 05

chunks.heading: Colorado Real Estate Law and Practice — Module 05
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Real Estate Law and Practice — Module 05

## Property management, leases and rents

**Course:** Real Estate Law and Practice (48 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 7.0** of 48.0
**Commission outline topic:** **V — Property Management, Leases, Rents**, allocated **7 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What the Commission's outline puts in this topic
>
> | Sub-topic | Delivered in |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** Types and elements of leasehold estate, leases, lease clauses and rental agreements | Parts A and B |
> | **B.** Lessor and lessee rights, responsibilities and recourse | Part C |
> | **C.** Management contracts and obligations of parties | Part D |
>
> Seven hours, and the final topic of the 48-hour national course.
>
> **Property management is the part of Colorado practice where the rules read for this build bite hardest.**
> **Rule 5.5** requires a firm engaging in property management to keep **separate trust or escrow accounts —
> a minimum of one for rental receipts and a minimum of one for security deposits.** **Rule 5.7.A** gives
> property management money a **five business day** deposit deadline where everything else gets three.
> **Rule 5.8** governs security deposits and the transfer between firms. **Rule 6.17.C** imposes a vendor
> conflict disclosure specific to property management. All four were read in full, and all four are here.
>
> **What is NOT here is Colorado's landlord-tenant law.** The **Contracts and Regulations** outline names
> the **Landlord Tenant Act, § 38-12-101 et seq.** at its Topic V.G. **That statute was NOT read by this
> project**, and **no deposit limit, return period, notice period, entry requi

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
rement, habitability standard
> or eviction procedure is stated anywhere in this build.**

## Learning objectives

1. Name the four leasehold estates and distinguish them.
2. State what a lease must settle and identify the principal lease clauses.
3. Distinguish gross, net and percentage leases by how rent is calculated.
4. State the general rights and recourse of lessor and lessee, and say where Colorado's own law governs.
5. State what a management agreement must settle.
6. State the Colorado trust account rules that apply specifically to property management.
7. State Rule 6.17.C's vendor conflict disclosure and who it protects.
8. Calculate rent, vacancy and net operating income for a managed property from given figures.

---

## A. Leasehold estates

A lease does **two** things at once: it **conveys a leasehold estate** — possession for a term, with the
landlord keeping the **reversion** — and it **contains covenants** between the parties. A drafter who
settles one half has finished half the document.

| Estate | How it runs | How it ends |
|---|---|---|
| **Estate for years** | A **fixed term** with a stated beginning and end | **Expires by its own terms** — ordinarily no notice needed |
| **Periodic tenancy** | Period to period — month to month, year to year — **renewing automatically** | On **notice** by either party |
| **Tenancy at will** | At the will of **either** party, with no fixed term | On the will of either party, or by operation of law |
| **Tenancy at sufferance** | A **holdover** after a lawful tenancy has ended | When the holdover ends or is ended |

**The estate for years is not necessarily years long.** A three-month lease with stated dates is an estate
for years. The name describes the certainty of the term, not its length.

chunks.heading: B. What a lease settles, and the principal clauses
chunks.excerpt:
**A tenancy at sufferance is not a tenancy the landlord agreed to.** It is what remains when a tenant stays
past a lawful right to possession, and what the landlord may then do is a matter of statute.

> **The notice periods that end a periodic tenancy, and the procedure for ending a holdover, are Colorado
> statutory questions.** **§ 38-12-101 et seq. and Colorado's eviction statutes were NOT read by this
> project**, and **no notice period, no procedure and no remedy is stated anywhere in this build.**
> **Rule 6.2.B** gives the broker four routes, and for a property manager the practical one is to have the
> firm's forms and counsel settled **before** the question arises rather than after.

---

## B. What a lease settles, and the principal clauses

### B.1 The drafting checklist

**This is a checklist of what a lease must SETTLE. It is not a statement of Colorado legal requirements**,
and the exercise instruction in this course says so on its face.

1. **Parties** — landlord and tenant, identified exactly.
2. **Premises** — what is let, and anything included or excluded.
3. **Term** — beginning, end, and what happens at the end.
4. **Rent** — amount, when due, where and how paid, and what happens if it is late.
5. **Deposits** — amount, purpose, and the conditions of return.
6. **Use** — what the premises may be used for.
7. **Maintenance and repair** — allocated between the parties, item by item.
8. **Utilities and services** — who pays and who arranges.
9. **Assignment and subletting** — permitted, prohibited, or conditional.
10. **Default and remedies** — what constitutes default and what follows.
11. **Access by the landlord** — when, and on what notice.
12. **Insurance** — who carries what.
13. **Signatures.**

chunks.heading: B.2 Assignment and subletting are different
chunks.excerpt:
**Any figure or period a student writes into items 3, 4, 5, 10 or 11 must come from the brokerage's forms
and from counsel, not from this course.**

### B.2 Assignment and subletting are different

| | What transfers | Who remains liable |
|---|---|---|
| **Assignment** | The tenant's **entire remaining interest** | The original tenant, unless released |
| **Sublease** | **Part** of the term or of the premises, the sublessor keeping a reversion | The original tenant, to the landlord |

**In neither case is the original tenant released without the landlord's agreement.** That agreement is a
**novation**, and it is a legal document.

### B.3 How rent is calculated

| Lease | Who pays operating expenses |
|---|---|
| **Gross** | The **landlord**, out of the rent |
| **Net** | The **tenant** pays some or all of them in addition to base rent |
| **Percentage** | Rent varies with the **tenant's sales**, ordinarily a base rent plus a percentage over a breakpoint |
| **Ground** | The tenant leases land and ordinarily improves it, for a long term |
| **Graduated / escalated** | Rent changes on stated dates or by a stated index |

**"Net" says nothing by itself.** Which expenses a net lease actually shifts is settled item by item in the
document, and a lease that says "net" without saying which expenses has settled nothing.

**Percentage rent worked, with every figure given:** base rent **$4,000** a month plus **5 percent** of
gross sales over a **$80,000** monthly breakpoint. In a month with **$140,000** of sales, the overage is
**$60,000**, the percentage rent is **$3,000**, and total rent is **$7,000.**

---

## C. Rights, responsibilities and recourse

### C.1 The general framework

chunks.heading: C.2 Fair housing runs through leasing
chunks.excerpt:
| | Landlord | Tenant |
|---|---|---|
| **Principal right** | To receive rent, and to have the premises returned in the agreed condition | To **quiet enjoyment** — possession without wrongful interference by the landlord |
| **Principal duty** | To deliver and maintain the premises as the lease and the law require | To pay rent and to use the premises as the lease permits |
| **On the other's default** | The remedies the lease and the statute provide | The remedies the lease and the statute provide |

**Constructive eviction** describes a landlord's conduct that so interferes with the tenant's use that the
tenant is treated as evicted. **Actual eviction** is dispossession. **What either requires, and what a
tenant must do to claim it, is a matter of Colorado law this project did not read.**

> **This is the largest gap in this module and it is stated on its face.** Colorado's residential and
> commercial landlord-tenant statutes were **NOT** read. **This course states no rule on**: security deposit
> limits or return periods; notice to enter; habitability or the warranty of habitability; late fees;
> repair and deduct; retaliation; lease termination; eviction procedure or timelines; or any tenant remedy.
>
> **A property manager needs those answers before taking an assignment**, and they come from the statute,
> from the brokerage's forms, and from counsel. **Rule 6.2.A** puts it as a requirement: a broker **must
> possess the necessary experience, training, and knowledge** to provide the service and to **maintain
> compliance with the applicable federal, state and local laws.** If not, **Rule 6.2.B.1** is available:
> **decline.**

### C.2 Fair housing runs through leasing

chunks.heading: D. Management contracts and the obligations of the parties
chunks.excerpt:
Every prohibition in Module 03 Part F.1 applies to leasing as fully as to sales — **and the applications
that most often go wrong are in leasing**: screening criteria applied unevenly; occupancy standards used as
a proxy for familial status; advertising that indicates a preference; refusal of a **reasonable
accommodation** in rules, policies, practices or services; and refusal to permit a **reasonable
modification** of the premises.

**The safe practice is one written set of criteria applied to every applicant in the same order**, with the
result recorded.

---

## D. Management contracts and the obligations of the parties

### D.1 What a management agreement settles

1. **Parties**, and the property managed.
2. **Term**, and how it ends.
3. **The manager's authority** — what the manager may do without asking, and what needs the owner's
   approval, **including a dollar threshold for repairs.**
4. **Compensation** — how calculated, when taken, and out of what.
5. **Trust accounting** — which accounts, and how reported.
6. **Owner reserves** — how much is held and what it may be used for.
7. **Reporting** — what reports, and when.
8. **Leasing authority** — terms the manager may accept.
9. **Maintenance and vendors** — who selects, who pays, and what disclosures.
10. **Insurance and indemnity.**
11. **Termination**, including **what happens to funds and documents.**

**Item 11 is the one most often left thin**, and Colorado's own course outline for **Record Keeping and
Trust Accounts** devotes a topic to it: **Topic IV, Termination of Brokerage Relationship**, half an hour,
covering *"Forwarding Trust Funds and Documents"* and *"Closing Accounting Records."*

### D.2 The functions of a property manager

chunks.heading: D.3 The Colorado money rules that apply specifically to property management
chunks.excerpt:
Marketing and leasing space; screening applicants against consistent criteria; collecting rent;
maintaining the property; controlling operating costs; keeping records and reporting to the owner; and
complying with the law applicable to the tenancy.

**In Colorado the relationship is a brokerage relationship like any other.** **§ 12-10-403(2)** applies: a
broker is a **transaction-broker** unless single agency is established in **writing**. **§§ 12-10-404 and
12-10-405** speak of *"seller **or landlord**"* and *"buyer **or tenant**"* throughout, so the duty lists
run to management relationships in their own terms.

### D.3 The Colorado money rules that apply specifically to property management

**All four were read in full and each is transcribed in `colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md` § 4.**

> **Rule 5.5 — separate accounts.** A brokerage firm engaging in property management *"**must deposit rental
> receipts and security deposits and disburse money collected for such purposes in SEPARATE Trust or Escrow
> Accounts, a minimum of one for rental receipts and a minimum of one for security deposits.**"*
>
> **Rule 5.7.A — the five-day deadline.** *"All Money Belonging to Others received by a Brokerage Firm **for
> Property Management** must be deposited ... **no later than FIVE (5) BUSINESS DAYS following receipt of
> funds or mutual execution of a lease, whichever is later.**"*
>
> Compare **Rule 5.7.B**, which gives **all other** Money Belonging to Others **three business days**.
> **Property management money gets five; everything else gets three**, and both are **business** days
> measured from **the later** of the two events.
>
> **Rule 5.8.A — owner-held deposits.** A firm receipting for security deposits *"**will not deliver such
> security deposits to an o

chunks.heading: D.3 The Colorado money rules that apply specifically to property management
chunks.excerpt:
wner without the tenant's written authorization in a lease or unless written
> notice has been given to the tenant**"* — notice given so the tenant knows **who is holding the deposit**
> and **the procedure for requesting its return.** If the deposit goes to the owner, the management
> agreement **should** place financial responsibility for its return on the owner and **must** authorise
> disclosure of the owner's true name and current mailing address in a dispute.
>
> **Rule 5.8.B — changing management companies.** A firm taking over management **must disclose to the owner
> and current tenant, in writing, within 30 DAYS** of execution or assignment of the management agreement,
> the status of any security deposit held by the previous firm. **The previous firm must transfer the
> deposit within 60 DAYS** and confirm the amount. **The new firm must verify each deposit matches the
> amount in the current lease and disclose any discrepancy**, and **must inform the tenant in writing if the
> owner is holding the deposit.**

**Three more Chapter 5 rules a property manager lives inside:**

- **Rule 5.9** — money belonging to **one** beneficiary must not be used for the benefit of another, and
  never for the firm or broker.
- **Rule 5.14.B** — *"**No ledger may ever be allowed to have a negative cash balance.**"* On a managed
  portfolio that means one owner's funds cannot cover another owner's overdraft, even for a day.
- **Rule 5.15.A** — reports to beneficiaries go out as the management agreement provides and, absent a
  provision to the contrary, **within 30 days after the end of the month** in which funds were received or
  disbursed.

chunks.heading: D.4 The vendor conflict rule — Rule 6.17.C
chunks.excerpt:
**The Record Keeping and Trust Accounts course delivers all of Chapter 5**, and its outline requires an
exercise in which the student *"shall **reconcile the bank accounts for a property manager managing and
holding security deposits for a minimum of 8 properties.**"*

### D.4 The vendor conflict rule — Rule 6.17.C

This one exists because of property management specifically, and it was read in full.

> **Rule 6.17.C**: *"A Brokerage Firm or Broker engaged in **Property Management Services** has a duty to
> **disclose, in writing, any known Conflict of Interest** that may arise **in the selection or use of a
> business or vendor** that provides services applicable to lease transactions, **including property
> maintenance.** The Brokerage Firm or Broker is required to disclose **any ownership, financial, or
> familial interest** associated with the selection or use of a particular business or vendor."*

**Three interests named: ownership, financial, familial.** A manager who sends maintenance work to a
company they own a piece of, profit from, or are related to must **disclose it in writing** — and
**Rule 5.17** separately requires **prior written consent** before assessing or receiving a **mark-up** on
that work, plus disclosure of all mark-ups paid by any customer, plus records that verify both.

**Rule 6.17.A** sits above it: a **continuing** duty to disclose, in writing, **any known conflict of
interest** in the course of any real estate transaction.

### D.5 Managing property the broker owns

**Rules 5.10.D and 5.10.E** address it directly, and the trigger is the **20 percent** ownership threshold
in **§ 12-10-201(6)(b)(VII)**:

chunks.heading: E. The arithmetic of a managed property
chunks.excerpt:
- **5.10.D** — rental proceeds for a broker's own property managed **through a firm the broker is not
  licensed with** must go into a trust or escrow account for Money Belonging to Others.
- **5.10.E** — rental proceeds for property owned by a broker **licensed with that firm** must go into one
  or more trust or escrow accounts **separate from any other** accounts containing Money Belonging to
  Others, though they may hold the proceeds of **other** brokers licensed with the same firm whose own
  properties it manages.

A **broker's property** for both rules includes properties held in **partnership, joint venture or
syndication** where the broker's interest exceeds **20 percent**.

**And Rule 6.17.B** requires a broker who **sells, buys or leases on their own account** to disclose **in
the contracting instrument or a separate concurrent writing** that they are a **licensed Broker.**

---

## E. The arithmetic of a managed property

Every figure below is supplied as a given.

> **A 16-unit building.** Each unit rents at **$1,450** a month. Vacancy and collection loss runs at
> **6 percent**. Annual operating expenses are **$94,000**.
>
> | Line | Calculation | Amount |
> |---|---|---|
> | **Potential gross income** | 16 × $1,450 × 12 | **$278,400** |
> | less vacancy and collection loss | 6% of $278,400 | ($16,704) |
> | **Effective gross income** | | **$261,696** |
> | less operating expenses | | ($94,000) |
> | **Net operating income** | | **$167,696** |
>
> At a capitalisation rate of **7 percent**, the indicated value is **$167,696 ÷ 0.07 = $2,395,657**
> rounded to the nearest dollar.

chunks.heading: Module 05 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**Debt service is not an operating expense**, which is what keeps net operating income a measure of the
**property** rather than of a particular owner's financing. Module 02 Part C.2 builds the same lines.

**A management fee of 7 percent of collected rent** on the effective gross income above is
**$261,696 × 0.07 = $18,318.72** — and **Rule 5.10.A** requires money in a trust or escrow account that
becomes **due and payable to the firm** to be **withdrawn monthly**, while **Rule 5.10.C** provides that
fees are *"earned"* and available **only after all contracted services have been performed and there is no
remaining right of recall.**

---

## Module 05 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
*"**testing is required** to establish individual's satisfactory completion of the statutory
requirements"*, and **these items are not that test.**

This module completes the Commission's **Real Estate Law and Practice** outline: **10 + 7 + 12 + 12 + 7 =
48 hours.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 05

Written to the **Commission's Real Estate Law and Practice qualifying education outline, approved April 1,
1998**, Topic V and its sub-topics A through C. The hour figure is the Commission's.

The Colorado provisions quoted — **§§ 12-10-201(6)(b)(VII), 12-10-403(2), 12-10-404 and 12-10-405**, and
**Rules 5.5, 5.7, 5.8, 5.9, 5.10, 5.14.B, 5.15.A, 5.17, 6.2 and 6.17** — are transcribed from **C.R.S.
Title 12 Article 10** and **4 CCR 725-1**, read on 2026-08-20 and recorded in
`colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 05
chunks.excerpt:
**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **C.R.S. § 38-12-101 et seq.**, the Colorado
Landlord Tenant Act, in its entirety; Colorado's **eviction and unlawful detainer** statutes; any Colorado
provision on **security deposit limits, return periods, notice to enter, habitability, late fees, repair
and deduct, retaliation or lease termination**; the **Colorado Fair Housing Act** and the **federal Fair
Housing Act**; the **Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act**; and **every Commission-approved form**,
including any lease or management agreement form.

**No deposit limit, return period, notice period, entry requirement, habitability standard, late fee,
eviction timeline, occupancy standard or tenant remedy is stated in this module.** The **five business
days**, **three business days**, **30 days**, **60 days**, **monthly** withdrawal, **30 days after month
end**, and **20 percent** are all **transcribed from 4 CCR 725-1 and C.R.S. § 12-10-201(6)(b)(VII)**, and
every figure in a worked calculation is supplied inside that calculation as a given.

lessons.title: Colorado Contracts and Regulations — Module 01

chunks.heading: Colorado Contracts and Regulations — Module 01
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Contracts and Regulations — Module 01

## Regulations: the licence law, Colorado contract law, and the statutes the Commission names

**Course:** Contracts and Regulations (48 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 8.0** of 48.0
**Commission outline topic:** **I — Regulations**, allocated **8 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### This is the Colorado course
>
> **C.R.S. § 12-10-203(4)(a)(II)** requires *"**forty-eight hours** of classroom instruction ... in
> **understanding and preparation of Colorado real estate contracts**."* **Rule 2.1.A.2.b** names it
> *"Colorado Real Estate Contracts: **48 hours**."*
>
> **This is the course no applicant escapes.** **§ 12-10-203(4)(b)** relieves a broker licensed in another
> jurisdiction of everything **except** this course and **Closings**; **§ 12-10-203(4)(c)** relieves a
> salesperson licensed elsewhere of everything **except** this course and the whole 72-hour group. **Every
> applicant completes these 48 hours**, whatever they hold elsewhere.
>
> **The Commission approved its outline on June 6, 1996 and updated it 07/03/06.** Its stated objective:
> *"To protect the public by having students **prepare and understand Colorado Real Estate Commission
> approved contracts** and understand Colorado real estate regulations."*
>
> | Module | Commission topic | Hours |
> |---|---|---|
> | **01** | I. Regulations | **8** |
> | 02 | II. Colorado Statutory Relationships | 4 |
> | 03 | III. Brokerage Relationship Agreements | 16 * |
> | 04 | IV. Sales Contracts and Related Forms | 16 * |
> | 05 | V. Other Considerations in Real Estate Contracting | 4 |
> | | **TOTAL** | **48.0** |
>
> \* The outline's

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
own footnote: *"**Approximate hours; together must total 32 hours.**"*
>
> *"**Testing is required** to establish individual's satisfactory completion of the statutory
> requirements."*

## Learning objectives

1. Name the sources of Colorado real estate regulation the Commission's outline lists.
2. State what § 12-10-403(4) authorises a broker to complete and what Rule 7.1 requires.
3. State what the Commission's outline names in Colorado contract law, and say which of those this build
   read and which it did not.
4. State the Statute of Frauds requirement in general terms and identify Colorado's own as unread.
5. Name the subject-matter statutes the outline lists and say what each governs.
6. State the four-year transaction file retention rule and what it does not require.

---

## A. Colorado real estate license law

The Commission's outline names three sources at Topic I.A, and this build read all three categories of
document — though not every section within them.

### A.1 Statutes — "Title 12 Article 10, Parts 1-8 CRS"

The outline names the whole of Article 10. **What this project read is §§ 12-10-203 and 12-10-402 through
12-10-411**, and the readings file says so.

| Part | Subject | Read for this build? |
|---|---|---|
| **Part 1** | Real estate brokers — definitions, licensing, the Commission, discipline | **§ 12-10-203 only** |
| **Part 2** | (as organised in Article 10) | § 12-10-203 |
| **Part 4** | **Brokerage relationships — §§ 12-10-402 to 12-10-411** | **In full** |
| **Part 5** | Subdivisions | **No** |
| **Part 6** | Appraisers | **No** |
| **Parts 3, 7, 8** | Other regulated activities | **No** |

chunks.heading: A.2 Commission rules — 4 CCR 725-1
chunks.excerpt:
**Every disciplinary ground, penalty and procedure lives in §§ 12-10-217, 12-10-219 and 12-10-222, and
NONE of them was read.** **No sanction, fine, suspension, revocation ground or procedure is stated anywhere
in this build.** Where a rule read for this build cites one of those sections — as **Rule 5.17** cites
§§ 12-10-217(1)(d) and (t), **Rule 5.20.A** cites § 12-10-217(1)(i), **Rule 6.3.A.1** cites
§ 12-10-217(1)(r), and **§ 12-10-411** cites § 12-10-217(1)(m) — the citation is reproduced and **its
content is not.**

### A.2 Commission rules — 4 CCR 725-1

**Read in full**: 89 pages, rule version 12355, from the Secretary of State's CCR. Nine chapters:

| Chapter | Subject |
|---|---|
| **1** | Definitions |
| **2** | Licensure requirements — including **Rule 2.1**, the 168 hours |
| **3** | Licensure, renewal, license status, and insurance |
| **4** | Continuing education requirement |
| **5** | **Separate accounts and accounting** — the Trust Accounts course |
| **6** | **Practice standards** |
| **7** | **Use of standard forms** |
| **8** | Declaratory orders |
| **9** | Commission review of initial decisions and exceptions |

**Rule 2.1.A.2 is where the 168 hours are divided**, and the division is worth reading closely because the
rule does two different things in one list:

> *"a. Real Estate Law and Real Estate Practice: **48 hours**;*
> *b. Colorado Real Estate Contracts: **48 hours**;*
> *c. Real Estate Closings: **not less than 24 hours**;*
> *d. Trust Accounts and Record Keeping: **not less than 8 hours**;*
> *e. Current Legal Issues: **not less than 8 hours**; and*
> *f. Practical Application: **not less than 32 hours**."*

chunks.heading: A.3 Commission interpretations and positions on the license law
chunks.excerpt:
**The first two are exact. The other four are FLOORS.** That is not an accident of drafting: **§ 12-10-203
(4)(a)(III)** fixes *"a total of **seventy-two hours**"* for the four subjects **together** and allocates
none among them, so the Commission's rule sets minimums that add to exactly 72.

**Rule 2.1.D** gives the Commission an audit power over this course and every other: it *"**may audit
courses ... at any time and at no cost**"*, may request **all instructional materials and student
attendance records**, and *"**failure to comply with statutes and these Rules may result in the removal of
the course provider, instructor, and/or the course from the approved provider list.**"*

### A.3 Commission interpretations and positions on the license law

**The Commission issues position statements.** The **Practical Applications** outline names one by number —
**CP 41**, on gaining competency — and the **Record Keeping and Trust Accounts** outline names *"Position
Statements"* among the Commission rules and regulations a student must meet.

> **NO Commission position statement was obtained or read by this project**, and **no module of this build
> states the content of one.** This is a submission gate. A course claiming to teach *"Commission
> interpretations and positions on the license law"* — the outline's own words — cannot do so from
> statute and rule alone.

---

## B. Review of Colorado contract law

The Commission's outline names six items at Topic I.B. **This module states honestly which of them this
build can teach from primary text and which it cannot.**

### B.1 The Conway-Bogue decision — NOT READ

chunks.heading: B.2 Colorado Bar Association v. The Title Guaranty Company — NOT READ
chunks.excerpt:
**Named by the outline at I.B.1.** It is the Colorado decision that settles what a real estate broker may
do with contract documents without engaging in the unauthorized practice of law.

> **The decision was NOT read by this project**, and **no module of this build states its holding, its
> reasoning, or its limits.**
>
> **What this build DOES state comes from the statute and rule that were read**, and they are the operative
> law a broker follows daily:
>
> **§ 12-10-403(4)(a)**: a broker *"**whether acting as a single agent or transaction-broker, MAY COMPLETE
> STANDARD FORMS** for use in a real estate transaction, **including standard forms intended to convey
> personal property as part of the real estate transaction**, when a broker is performing the activities
> enumerated or referred to in section 12-10-201(6) in the transaction."*
>
> **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)**, closing sentence: *"**In any transaction described in this subsection (4), the
> broker shall advise the parties that the forms have important legal consequences and that the parties
> should consult legal counsel before signing the forms.**"*
>
> **This is a submission gate**, and the **Current Legal Issues** outline names *"**Unauthorized Practice of
> Law concerns**"* among its representative areas — which is where a course built to that outline's
> Commission-supplied materials would carry it.

### B.2 Colorado Bar Association v. The Title Guaranty Company — NOT READ

**Named at I.B.2**, and the same is true of it: **not read, holding not stated.**

### B.3 Authority to complete forms — § 12-10-403(4), READ IN FULL

**This one this build can deliver, because the section was read.** It is the statutory basis for everything
Modules 03 and 04 do.

chunks.heading: B.3 Authority to complete forms — § 12-10-403(4), READ IN FULL
chunks.excerpt:
**§ 12-10-403(4)(b) defines "standard form" in eight paragraphs:**

| # | Kind of form |
|---|---|
| **(I)** | A form **promulgated by the real estate commission** for current use by brokers — a **"commission-approved form"** |
| **(II)** | A form **drafted by a licensed Colorado attorney** representing the broker, employing broker or firm — with **the attorney's or law firm's name and the broker's or firm's name on the form itself** |
| **(III)** | A form **provided by a party** to the transaction where the broker is that party's transaction-broker or single agent — **the broker retaining written confirmation that the party provided it** |
| **(IV)** | A form **prescribed by a governmental or quasi-governmental agency, or by a lender regulated by state or federal law**, where **use of the form is mandated** |
| **(V)** | A form **issued with the written approval of the Colorado Bar Association** and specifically designated for use by brokers in Colorado, used within any guidelines or conditions the CBA specified |
| **(VI)** | A form **used for disclosure purposes only**, if it **does not purport to waive or create any legal rights or obligations** and provides only information about **the real estate specifically** or **the geographic area generally** |
| **(VII)** | A form **prescribed by a title company** providing closing services where the broker is transaction-broker or single agent for a party |
| **(VIII)** | A **letter of intent** created by the broker, employing broker or firm, **so long as it states on its face that it is nonbinding and creates no legal rights or obligations** |

**§ 12-10-403(4)(c) then states the hierarchy and the limits, and this is the operative sentence:**

chunks.heading: B.3 Authority to complete forms — § 12-10-403(4), READ IN FULL
chunks.excerpt:
> *"**A broker shall use a COMMISSION-APPROVED FORM when such a form exists and is appropriate for the
> transaction.** A broker's use of any standard form described in subsection (4)(b)(III) or (4)(b)(IV) ...
> **must be limited to inserting transaction-specific information within the form.** In using standard forms
> described in subsection (4)(b)(II), (V), (VI), (VII), or (VIII) ... **the broker may also advise the
> parties as to effects thereof** ..."*

**Read the split.** For a **client form** or a **government/lender form**, the broker may do **one thing
only — insert transaction-specific information.** For an **attorney form**, a **CBA form**, a
**disclosure-only form**, a **title company form** or a **letter of intent**, the broker **may also advise
the parties as to the effects.** And **Rule 7.1.A** says the same of a **Commission-approved form**: *"The
Broker **may advise the parties as to the effects thereof.**"*

**Rule 7.1.B adds two requirements to an attorney form that the statute does not:**

> An attorney form may be used **only if a Commission-approved form does not exist or is not appropriate**;
> it *"**must contain the language that says: 'This form has not been approved by the Colorado Real Estate
> Commission'**"*; and it *"**may not be altered by the Broker other than by completing any blank spaces in
> the form.**"*

chunks.heading: B.4 Statute of Frauds — Colorado's own NOT READ
chunks.excerpt:
> ### The gate that runs through this entire course
>
> **NO Commission-approved form was obtained, read, or reproduced by this project.** The outline requires
> students to **complete** them — one of each of **six** listing and buyer brokerage families at Topic III,
> one of each of **four** sales contract families at Topic IV, and one of each of the related forms in
> both.
>
> **Modules 03 and 04 teach what each form must settle and what the statute and rules require of its use.
> They do not reproduce any form, state any form's contents, or name any form version.** Conforming this
> course to the Commission's current forms — downloaded from the Division's website, as Rule 7.1.A directs
> — **is the largest submission gate in the Colorado build.**

### B.4 Statute of Frauds — Colorado's own NOT READ

**Named at I.B.4.** In general terms, a contract for the sale of an interest in land must be **in writing**
and **signed by the party to be charged**, identifying the **parties**, the **property**, and the **price or
a means of determining it**.

**Colorado's own statute of frauds was NOT read by this project**, and **no section number, wording,
exception or part-performance doctrine is stated anywhere in this build.**

### B.5 Uniform Power of Attorney Act — NOT READ

**Named at I.B.5.** A power of attorney authorises an agent to act for a principal, and a conveyance signed
under one raises questions about the instrument's scope, its currency, and its recording.

chunks.heading: B.6 Electronic duplication — and the rules that WERE read
chunks.excerpt:
**Colorado's Uniform Power of Attorney Act was NOT read.** **No requirement, form, scope rule, durability
rule or recording requirement from it is stated anywhere in this build.** A transaction in which a party
signs under a power of attorney is one for **counsel and the title company**, and **Rule 6.2.B** gives the
broker four routes: decline, obtain the knowledge, obtain assistance, or co-list.

### B.6 Electronic duplication — and the rules that WERE read

**Named at I.B.6.** Two Colorado rules read for this build bear on records in electronic form:

> **Rule 5.14.E**: *"The three-way reconciliation reports, ledgers, journals, and bank account statements
> **may be kept electronically.**"*
>
> **Rule 6.24** governs **electronic records and production of records**, and **Rule 5.21** requires a broker
> and firm to *"**produce for inspection by the Commission any document or record** as may be reasonably
> necessary for investigation or audit"*, with **failure within the time set being grounds for disciplinary
> action** absent an extension.

**No Colorado electronic transactions or electronic signature statute was read by this project**, and **no
rule about the validity or execution of an electronic signature is stated anywhere in this build.**

---

## C. The subject-matter statutes the outline names

Topic I names four more bodies of law at C through F. **This module states what each governs and states
plainly that none of them was read.**

### C.1 Subdividing, conversions and time sharing — Topic I.C

**C.R.S. Title 12, Article 10, Part 5** governs subdivisions, and **§ 12-10-501(3)** defines *"subdivision"*
in terms this build encountered while reading Part 4 but **did not read as a whole**.

chunks.heading: C.2 Colorado Fair Housing Act — Topic I.D
chunks.excerpt:
**No subdivision registration requirement, public report requirement, developer obligation, exemption,
threshold, conversion rule or time share provision is stated anywhere in this build.**

### C.2 Colorado Fair Housing Act — Topic I.D

**NOT read.** Module 03 of the **Real Estate Law and Practice** course delivers the **seven federal
protected classes** — race, colour, religion, national origin, sex, disability, familial status — and
**states no additional Colorado protected class, exemption, remedy or procedure.**

**What this build does state, because it was read**, is that **§§ 12-10-404(1)(e), 12-10-405(1)(e) and
12-10-407(2)(d)** each require a broker to comply with applicable law *"**including fair housing and civil
rights statutes or regulations**"* — so a fair housing violation is **also** a violation of the brokerage
relationship statute, and **§ 12-10-411** makes any Part 4 violation an act the Commission may investigate.

### C.3 Appraiser Licensing Act — Topic I.E

**NOT read.** What **was** read is **Rule 6.12**, delivered in Module 02 of the Real Estate Law and Practice
course: a broker preparing a **CMA or BPO for any reason other than an anticipated sale or purchase** must
include the notice the rule prescribes verbatim, and **brokers are prohibited from completing CMAs or BPOs
used for the purpose of obtaining financing**, the rule citing **§ 12-10-602(9)(b)(II)** for that.

**§ 12-10-602 itself was not read**, and **no appraiser licensing level, requirement, exemption or penalty
is stated anywhere in this build.**

### C.4 Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act — Topic I.F

chunks.heading: D. Two rules from Chapter 6 that belong with the regulations
chunks.excerpt:
**NOT read.** **CCIOA is article 33.3 of title 38**, and **§ 12-10-501(3)(b)(I)(A)** — encountered in the
Part 5 definitions — refers to it in defining a subdivision to include *"the conversion of an existing
structure into a common interest community ... of twenty or more residential units."*

**No CCIOA requirement, disclosure, document delivery obligation, association power, budget requirement,
resale certificate requirement or deadline is stated anywhere in this build.** The Commission promulgates a
**Common Interest Community Addendum to the Contract to Buy and Sell**, named at the outline's Topic
IV.A.2.c — **and no Commission form was obtained.**

---

## D. Two rules from Chapter 6 that belong with the regulations

### D.1 Transaction files — Rule 6.20

> *"Both a Broker and a Brokerage Firm **must retain transaction files for all transactions for a period of
> FOUR (4) YEARS** beginning from **the consummation date of the transaction or the expiration date of any
> Listing Contracts that do not consummate.** Required documents in a transaction file are designated in the
> **Commission's Transaction File Checklist** and may be found on the Division's website."*

**Two start dates, not one.** A transaction that closes runs from **consummation**; a listing that never
produces one runs from **the listing's expiration.**

**And what the rule expressly does NOT require:** a broker is not required to obtain and retain copies of
**existing public records, title commitments, loan applications, lender required disclosures, or related
affirmations from independent third party closing entities after the closing date.**

chunks.heading: D.2 Continuing education — noted, not taught
chunks.excerpt:
**The Commission's Transaction File Checklist was NOT obtained**, and **no module of this build states what
documents it designates.** That is a submission gate.

### D.2 Continuing education — noted, not taught

**Chapter 4** of the rules carries the continuing education requirement, and **Rule 4.2.A.3** is the basis
of the **Broker Reactivation Course (24 hours)** the Division publishes as an alternative method of
satisfying CE.

**This is a qualifying education course, not a continuing education course**, and **no CE requirement,
hour figure, cycle or deadline is stated in this build** beyond noting that **Rule 3** ties licensing to a
**three-year Anniversary Year Cycle** as **Rule 1.4** defines it.

---

## Module 01 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
*"**testing is required** to establish individual's satisfactory completion of the statutory
requirements"*, and **these items are not that test.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 01

Written to the **Commission's Contracts and Regulations (48 Classroom Hours) qualifying education outline,
approved June 6, 1996, updated 07/03/06**, Topic I and its sub-topics A through F, in the outline's own
order and using the outline's own item names. The hour figure is the Commission's.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 01

The provisions quoted — **§§ 12-10-203(4), 12-10-403(4), 12-10-404(1)(e), 12-10-405(1)(e), 12-10-407(2)(d)
and 12-10-411**, and **Rules 1.4, 2.1, 5.14.E, 5.21, 6.2, 6.12, 6.20, 6.24 and 7.1** — are transcribed from
**C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10** and **4 CCR 725-1**, read on 2026-08-20 and recorded in

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** the **Conway-Bogue decision**; **Colorado Bar

**No disciplinary ground, penalty, fine, sanction, subdivision threshold, public report requirement,

chunks.heading: Colorado Contracts and Regulations — Module 02
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Contracts and Regulations — Module 02

## Colorado statutory relationships — §§ 12-10-402 to 12-10-411

**Course:** Contracts and Regulations (48 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 4.0** of 48.0
**Commission outline topic:** **II — Colorado Statutory Relationships**, allocated **4 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### The Commission's outline names the sections, one by one
>
> This is the only topic in the six outlines that lists **statute section numbers as its sub-topics.** The
> Commission wrote it that way, and this module is built section by section in the outline's own order:
>
> | Outline sub-topic | Section | Delivered in |
