chunks.heading: Colorado Contracts and Regulations — Module 04
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Contracts and Regulations — Module 04

## Sales contracts and related forms: the four families

**Course:** Contracts and Regulations (48 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 16.0** of 48.0
**Commission outline topic:** **IV — Sales Contracts and Related Forms**, allocated **16 hours**
(the outline's footnote: *"Approximate hours; together [with Topic III] must total 32 hours"*)
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### The Commission's instruction for this topic, transcribed
>
> The outline heads Topic IV:
>
> ***"(Explain in detail the content and preparation of Commission approved forms)"***
>
> and closes it:
>
> > *"**Students must complete a minimum of one of each of the 4 FAMILIES of sales contracts and complete one
> > of each of the related forms. Include examples of NEW FINANCING, LOAN ASSUMPTION, and OWNER CARRY
> > FINANCING.** (May be assigned as homework)"*
>
> **Sixteen hours, and the work is preparation** — the same as Module 03. **The financing sentence is an
> additional requirement**: the student's completed contract work must show all three financing structures.

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
> ### The same gate, restated because it governs this module too
>
> **NO Commission-approved form was obtained, read, or reproduced by this project.** **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)**
> and **Rule 7.1.A** require a broker to *"**use a Commission-approved form when such a form exists and is
> appropriate for the transaction**"*, and direct the broker to the Division's website to obtain them.
>
> **This module states no form's contents, version, date, paragraph numbering or provisions.** It states
> **what each instrument must settle** and **what the statute and rules read for this build require of its
> use.**

## Learning objectives

1. Name the four families of sales contracts the Commission's outline lists.
2. State what a contract to buy and sell must settle, in the order a broker completes it.
3. State the three-part test a complete contingency must satisfy.
4. Distinguish new financing, loan assumption and owner carry, and state what each requires of the contract.
5. State what each related form does and the error each is meant to prevent.
6. State the difference between a counterproposal and an amend/extend agreement.
7. State the Colorado earnest money rules a completed contract must be consistent with.
8. State what a completed form must show for the drafting requirement to be satisfied.

---

## A. The four families

The outline lists them at Topic IV.A.

chunks.heading: A. The four families
chunks.excerpt:
| # | Family | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Residential)** | The residential sale — the contract a new broker uses most |
| **2** | **Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Commercial)** | Commercial property |
| **3** | **Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Vacant Land/Farm & Ranch)** | Land, farm and ranch |
| **4** | **Contract to Exchange Real Estate (Simultaneous Exchange)** | An exchange rather than a sale |

The outline places two further instruments inside the family list rather than among the related forms:
the **Common Interest Community Addendum to the Contract to Buy and Sell** (at IV.A.2.c) and the
**Addendum to Contract to Buy and Sell** (at IV.A.3.b, attached to the exchange contract).

**Why there are separate forms rather than one contract with options.** The three property types attract
different due diligence, different financing, different disclosures, and different appurtenances. A vacant
land or farm and ranch transaction reaches **water rights, mineral rights, growing crops, access, and
equipment**; a commercial transaction reaches **leases in place, tenant estoppels, environmental review and
the buyer's intended use**; a residential transaction reaches **the seller's property disclosure,
inspection, and the buyer's financing**.

chunks.heading: B. What a contract to buy and sell must settle
chunks.excerpt:
> **A recurring boundary.** **No Colorado water law statute, mineral rights statute, or environmental
> statute was read by this project**, and **this course states no rule on whether or how any of those pass,
> what must be disclosed about them, or what due diligence they require.** For a farm and ranch, vacant land
> or commercial listing, those are questions for **counsel and the relevant professional**, and **Rule
> 6.2.A** makes it a requirement rather than advice: a broker **must** possess the necessary experience,
> training and knowledge to provide the service, and **Rule 6.2.B** gives four routes if they do not —
> **decline**, obtain them, obtain assistance, or **co-list**.
>
> **The Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act was NOT read**, and **nothing about what the Common Interest
> Community Addendum requires, discloses or delivers is stated anywhere in this build.**

---

## B. What a contract to buy and sell must settle

**A checklist of what the instrument settles, in roughly the order a broker completes it.** It is **not** a
statement of any Commission form's contents.

### B.1 The parties and the property

1. **Buyer and seller**, identified **exactly as they hold or will hold title.** Entities, trusts and
   estates raise **authority** questions — who may sign — that go to **counsel and the title company.**
2. **The property**, by the description that identifies it **unambiguously.** A street address is an
   identifier, not a legal description.
3. **Inclusions and exclusions** — what personal property goes and what stays. **§ 12-10-403(4)(a)**
   expressly authorises a broker to complete standard forms *"**including standard forms intended to convey
   personal property as part of the real estate transaction.**"*

### B.2 The money

chunks.heading: B.3 The dates and the conditions
chunks.excerpt:
4. **Purchase price**, and **how it is to be paid** — the sum of the parts must equal the price.
5. **Earnest money** — **amount**, **who holds it**, and **what happens to it in each outcome.**
6. **The financing structure** — Part C below.

> **Three Colorado rules a completed contract must be consistent with, all read in full.**
>
> **Rule 5.12.A**: *"**Any Broker receiving earnest money must deliver such earnest money to the earnest
> money holder to be deposited in accordance with the contract.** The Broker **must obtain a dated and
> signed receipt** from the person or entity to whom the Broker has been instructed to deliver the
> deposit."*
>
> **Rule 5.12.B**: if the **brokerage firm** holds it, it is deposited under **Rule 5.7.B** — *"**no later
> than THREE (3) BUSINESS DAYS following receipt of funds or mutual execution of contract, whichever is
> later**"*; and a transfer to a lawyer or closing entity likewise requires **a dated and signed receipt.**
>
> **Rule 5.13**: if a **promissory note** is taken as earnest money, **the seller must be informed of the
> date it becomes due**, and if payment is not made by that date the broker **must promptly notify the
> seller and deliver the original promissory note.**
>
> **A contract naming an earnest money holder the broker then fails to deliver to is not a paperwork
> problem; it is a Chapter 5 problem**, and **Rule 5.22** holds the **employing broker jointly responsible
> with the firm** for Chapter 5 compliance.

### B.3 The dates and the conditions

chunks.heading: B.4 Title, closing and possession
chunks.excerpt:
7. **Every date the contract runs on**, consistent with each other. The **Practical Applications** outline
   names this at its Topic VI.D.3 — *"**Consistency of dates**"* — and it is the single most common defect
   in a new broker's completed contract: a loan objection deadline after the closing date, an inspection
   deadline before the contract is signed, a title objection deadline that leaves no time to cure.
8. **Each contingency**, complete.

> **The three-part test for a contingency.** A contingency clause is not finished until it states:
>
> 1. **WHAT EVENT** must occur;
> 2. **BY WHEN** it must occur; and
> 3. **WHAT HAPPENS** if it does not.
>
> An event with no deadline, or a deadline with no consequence, has settled nothing. **This is the check
> applied to every completed contract in this module.**

**The ordinary contingencies**: financing; inspection; appraisal; title review; survey; sale of the buyer's
existing property; and, in a common interest community, review of association documents.

### B.4 Title, closing and possession

9. **Title and conveyance** — what is to be delivered, and what the buyer may object to.
10. **Closing date and place**, and who conducts it.
11. **Possession** — **when, and by whom.** The **Practical Applications** outline names **early
    occupancy** at its Topic VI.L, and it is a question that ordinarily needs counsel and an insurance
    conversation before anyone agrees to it.
12. **Prorations** — what is prorated and **as of when**, on the convention the contract states.
13. **Signature and acceptance provisions**, including **how and by when acceptance must be communicated.**

chunks.heading: B.5 The advice the statute requires with every one of them
chunks.excerpt:
**An acceptance signed and not communicated has not been communicated.** Fixing the method and the deadline
in the document removes the argument about whether and when a contract was formed.

### B.5 The advice the statute requires with every one of them

**§ 12-10-403(4)(c)**, closing sentence: *"In any transaction described in this subsection (4), the broker
**shall advise the parties that the forms have important legal consequences and that the parties should
consult legal counsel before signing the forms.**"* **Rule 7.1** repeats it.

**It is not a formality and it is not discharged by the form's own printed language.** It is something the
broker says.

---

## C. The three financing structures the outline requires

> *"**Include examples of new financing, loan assumption, and owner carry financing.**"*

### C.1 New financing

The buyer obtains a **new loan** from a lender.

**What the contract must settle:** the **loan type and terms** the buyer will seek; the **deadlines** for
application, for the loan objection, and for the appraisal; **what happens if the loan is not obtained**;
and **who pays which loan costs.**

**The appraisal problem is the one that surfaces late.** A lender lends against the **lesser** of price or
appraised value, so an appraisal below the contract price leaves a gap the buyer must close with cash, a
renegotiated price, or a termination on the appraisal deadline. **Whether the contract permits that
termination depends on what the appraisal contingency says** — event, deadline, consequence.

### C.2 Loan assumption

The buyer **takes over the seller's existing loan** on its terms.

chunks.heading: C.3 Owner carry financing
chunks.excerpt:
**What the contract must settle:** which loan; **whether the lender's approval is required and by when**;
what happens if approval is refused; **the balance as of closing** and how the difference between it and
the price is paid; and — the item that matters most — **whether the seller is RELEASED.**

**Without a written release the seller may remain liable on the note after closing.** The alienation
(due-on-sale) clause is why the lender is involved at all, and the release is a separate document the
lender must issue. **A broker ensures the seller understands the question and takes it to counsel**;
**§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V), 12-10-405(1)(c)(V) and 12-10-407(2)(b)(II)** each require advising the party to
obtain expert advice on material matters beyond the broker's expertise.

### C.3 Owner carry financing

**The seller finances the purchase**, taking back a **note** secured by the property — or selling on a
**contract for deed**, where the seller **retains legal title** and the buyer takes **equitable title** and
possession.

**"Owner carry" is the Colorado term of art** and a broker will meet it in exactly that form.

**What the contract must settle:** the **amount carried**; the **rate, payment and term**; **whether it
amortises or balloons, and when**; **what secures it**, and **in what lien position**; **who prepares the
note and security instrument**; **what happens on default**; **insurance and taxes** during the term; and
**whether the buyer may prepay or transfer.**

chunks.heading: D. The related forms
chunks.excerpt:
> **The largest boundary in this module.** **Colorado's foreclosure statutes, its public trustee system, and
> its law governing contracts for deed were NOT read by this project.** **No Colorado foreclosure procedure,
> notice, period, cure right, redemption right, forfeiture rule or deficiency rule is stated anywhere in
> this build.**
>
> An owner carry transaction is one in which **the seller becomes a lender** and the consequences of default
> are governed entirely by law this course has not read. **The note and the security instrument are prepared
> by counsel** — they are not among the eight kinds of standard form **§ 12-10-403(4)(b)** authorises a
> broker to complete unless the Commission has promulgated one and it is appropriate for the transaction.
>
> **Module 05 of this course** carries the outline's Topic V.A, **Promissory Notes**, and Topic V.B, **liens
> and encumbrances including deeds of trust and foreclosure**, and states the same boundary there.

---

## D. The related forms

The outline lists four at Topic IV.B, and requires **one of each** completed.

### D.1 Counterproposal — IV.B.1

**What it is.** The instrument by which a party responds to an offer **on different terms.**

**What it does at law.** A counter-offer **rejects the original offer.** The original cannot then be
accepted unless it is renewed, and the counterproposal operates as a **new offer** the original offeror may
accept or reject.

**The error it prevents.** A student who changes a term on the face of the contract and initials it has
produced a document the parties will disagree about. **The counterproposal states which terms it changes
and which of the original terms survive**, so there is one answer to what the parties agreed.

chunks.heading: D.2 Agreement to Amend/Extend Contract — IV.B.2
chunks.excerpt:
**The Practical Applications outline names counter offers and multiple offers together** at its Topic
VI.E.1 and VI.E.2 — and **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(II), 12-10-405(1)(c)(II) and 12-10-407(2)(b)(I)** all require
presenting **all** offers **regardless** of an existing contract, so a counterproposal outstanding does not
stop the next offer from being presented.

### D.2 Agreement to Amend/Extend Contract — IV.B.2

**What it is.** The instrument that **changes or extends the contract to buy and sell** after it is formed —
most often a deadline, a date, or a price.

**Not to be confused with the Agreement to Amend/Extend Contract with Broker** at Topic III.B.3, which
amends the **brokerage relationship agreement.** **One amends the sale; the other amends the employment.**
Using the wrong one produces a document that changes nothing.

**The Closings outline names this too**, at its Topic III.A.1: *"**Close to contract or amend contract in
writing.**"* The instruction is the whole discipline in six words — **the closing follows the contract, and
if the parties want something different, the contract changes first, in writing.**

### D.3 Licensee's Buyout Addendum — IV.B.3

**What it is.** The instrument used where a **licensee** is buying the property — the licensee taking the
role of principal.

**Two Colorado rules attach immediately, and both were read.**

> **Rule 6.17.B**: *"If a Broker **sells, buys, or leases real property on the Broker's own account**, such
> Broker must **disclose in the contracting instrument, or in a separate concurrent writing, that they are a
> licensed Broker.**"*
>
> **Rule 6.17.A**: brokers and firms have a **continuing duty to disclose, in writing, any known Conflict of
> Interest** that may arise in the course of any real estate transaction.

chunks.heading: D.4 Inspection Notice — IV.B.4
chunks.excerpt:
**A licensee buying is not doing anything prohibited.** They are required to say, in writing, in the
contracting instrument or a separate concurrent writing, that they hold a licence.

### D.4 Inspection Notice — IV.B.4

**What it is.** The instrument by which a buyer states the result of the inspection — objecting, resolving,
or terminating — within the inspection deadline the contract set.

**The error it prevents.** An objection made by email, by telephone, or after the deadline is not the notice
the contract required, and a buyer who misses the deadline may have accepted the property's condition.
**This is the clearest illustration of the three-part contingency test**: the event (an inspection), the
deadline (a date in the contract), and the consequence (what happens if the buyer objects, and what happens
if they say nothing).

**And it is where the broker's own disclosure duty runs alongside.** Whatever the inspection reports, the
broker's obligation under **§ 12-10-404(3)(a)**, **§ 12-10-405(3)(a)** or **§ 12-10-407(2)(b)(VI) and
(VII)** is to disclose **adverse material facts ACTUALLY KNOWN** — and **§§ 12-10-404(3)(b), 12-10-405(5)
and 12-10-407(4)** each provide there is **no duty to inspect** and **no duty to verify** what an
independent inspector said.

---

## E. What a completed contract must show

**This course records each completed contract and related form separately**, and one is accepted as
complete when it shows all of the following.

chunks.heading: Module 04 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
| Check | What is looked for |
|---|---|
| **Parties correct** | Exactly as they hold or will hold title |
| **Property identified unambiguously** | Not by street address alone |
| **Price and payment reconcile** | The parts sum to the price |
| **Earnest money complete** | Amount, holder, and disposition in each outcome — consistent with **Rules 5.7.B, 5.12 and 5.13** |
| **Financing structure stated** | New financing, assumption, or owner carry, with what each requires |
| **Every contingency complete** | **Event, deadline, consequence** — all three, every time |
| **Dates consistent** | No deadline out of sequence with another |
| **Title, closing and possession settled** | Including who conducts the closing |
| **Prorations stated** | What, and as of when, on the convention the contract states |
| **Acceptance provisions stated** | How and by when acceptance must be communicated |
| **Conflict disclosed** | **Rule 6.17.B** where the broker is a principal; **Rule 6.17.A** for any known conflict |
| **Nothing invented** | No term, figure, period or provision supplied from another state or from memory |

**And across the set, the outline's own requirement:** the student's completed work must include **new
financing, loan assumption, and owner carry** examples, and **one of each of the four families** and **one
of each of the related forms.**

---

## Module 04 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 04
chunks.excerpt:
**The engagement items do NOT satisfy the Commission's completion requirement.** Topic IV requires
**completed contracts and related forms**, with the three financing structures represented. The course
engine records them separately and does not credit this course without them.

---

## Instructor source note for Module 04

Written to the **Commission's Contracts and Regulations qualifying education outline**, Topic IV and its
sub-topics A and B, using the outline's own family names and related-form names and transcribing the
outline's own bracketed instruction and completion note.

The provisions quoted — **§§ 12-10-403(4), 12-10-404(1)(c)(II) and (V) and (3), 12-10-405(1)(c)(II) and (V)
and (3) and (5), and 12-10-407(2)(b)(I), (II), (VI) and (VII) and (4)** — and **Rules 5.7.B, 5.12, 5.13,
5.22, 6.2, 6.17 and 7.1** are transcribed from **C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10** and **4 CCR 725-1**, read on
2026-08-20 and recorded in `colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **every Commission-approved form** named in this
module; Colorado's **foreclosure statutes and public trustee provisions**; its law on **contracts for
deed**; its **water law** and **mineral rights** statutes; its **environmental statutes**; the **Colorado
Common Interest Ownership Act**; Colorado's **statute of frauds**; and **RESPA, TILA and TRID**.

**No form contents, version, date, paragraph number, deadline, earnest money amount, interest rate,
foreclosure period, redemption right or proration convention is stated in this module.** The **three
business days** in Rule 5.7.B and the receipt requirements in Rule 5.12 are transcribed from **4 CCR
725-1**, and every other requirement stated is transcribed from the section or rule named beside it.

lessons.title: Colorado Contracts and Regulations — Module 05

chunks.heading: Colorado Contracts and Regulations — Module 05
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Contracts and Regulations — Module 05

## Other considerations in real estate contracting

**Course:** Contracts and Regulations (48 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 4.0** of 48.0
**Commission outline topic:** **V — Other Considerations in Real Estate Contracting**, allocated **4 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What the Commission's outline puts in this topic
>
> | Sub-topic | Delivered in |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** Promissory Notes | Part A |
> | **B.** Liens and Encumbrances — 1. Deeds of Trust, 2. Foreclosure, 3. General Property Taxes, 4. Special Districts, 5. Other liens | Part B |
> | **C.** Errors and Omissions Insurance | Part C |
> | **D.** Land Descriptions (Surveys and Improvement Location Certificates) | Part D |
> | **E.** Water Rights | Part E |
> | **F.** Financing — 1. Equity Skimming, 2. U.C.C.C., 3. Standards of Mortgage Servicing, 4. Loan Fraud | Part F |
> | **G.** Landlord Tenant Act (38-12-101 et seq. CRS) | Part G |
>
> **Four hours for seven subjects**, and this is the topic where the Commission's outline names the most
> Colorado law that **this project did not read.** **Five of the seven parts below state a gap on their
> face**, and each says what it can from what was read and stops where the reading stopped.
>
> **That is the honest position and it is stated rather than papered over.** A course that invented a
> foreclosure period, a security deposit limit, or a special district rule would be worse than one that
> names the source and sends the student to it.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: A. Promissory notes
chunks.excerpt:
1. State what a promissory note is and how it relates to the security instrument.
2. Distinguish lien from encumbrance and state the general priority principle.
3. State what a deed of trust is and identify Colorado's foreclosure law as unread.
4. State what a special district is and why it matters to a buyer.
5. State the errors and omissions insurance requirement's source and identify what this build states about it.
6. Distinguish a survey from an Improvement Location Certificate.
7. State why water rights are a separate question in Colorado and where the answer comes from.
8. Name the four financing items the outline lists and say what each describes.

---

## A. Promissory notes

**The note is the promise to repay. It creates the DEBT.** The security instrument pledges the property and
creates the **lien**. Two documents, two functions — and a release of one does not by itself release the
other.

**What a note states:** the **principal**; the **interest rate**; the **payment amount and schedule**; the
**maturity date**; and the provisions the parties negotiated — **prepayment**, **late charges**,
**acceleration**, and what constitutes **default**.

**A note may be fully amortising, partially amortising with a balloon, or interest-only.** Which it is
determines what the borrower owes at maturity, and a buyer under an owner carry arrangement who has not
understood that a balloon is coming has not understood the transaction.

### A.1 The two Colorado rules about notes that WERE read

chunks.heading: A.2 Who prepares a note
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 5.13 — a promissory note taken as earnest money.** *"If a promissory note is received as earnest
> money pursuant to an executed contract, **the seller must be informed of the date such promissory note
> becomes due.** If payment is not made by the due date of the promissory note, the Broker **must promptly
> notify the seller and deliver the original promissory note.**"*
>
> **Rule 5.18 — items in lieu of cash.** *"**Any instrument, equity, or Thing of Value taken in lieu of cash
> must be held by the Brokerage Firm, except as otherwise agreed.**"*

**The Record Keeping and Trust Accounts outline names this at its Topic III.B.1 — "Promissory Notes
(Safekeeping and Collection)"** — and that course carries it in full.

### A.2 Who prepares a note

**Not the broker, unless a Commission-approved form exists and is appropriate.** **§ 12-10-403(4)(b)**
lists the eight kinds of standard form a broker may complete; a note prepared for an owner carry
arrangement ordinarily comes from **counsel**, and **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)** requires the broker in any event to
**advise the parties that the forms have important legal consequences and that they should consult legal
counsel before signing.**

---

## B. Liens and encumbrances

**Every lien is an encumbrance; not every encumbrance is a lien.** A lien is a **claim securing payment of a
debt**. An encumbrance is **any claim, right or interest** held by someone other than the owner that
affects title or use — so easements, restrictive covenants and encroachments are encumbrances securing no
debt.

chunks.heading: B.1 Deeds of trust — V.B.1
chunks.excerpt:
| Distinction | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Voluntary / involuntary** | Created by the owner's act, as a deed of trust is / imposed by law, as a judgment or tax lien is |
| **General / specific** | Attaching to all of a debtor's property / to identified property |

**The general priority principle is first in time, first in right, established by recording** — with
statutory exceptions that ordinarily include **property tax liens** and, in many states, **mechanics' liens
relating back to an earlier date.**

> **Colorado's recording statutes and its mechanics' lien statute were NOT read by this project.** **No
> Colorado priority rule, relation-back date, filing deadline, notice requirement or lien amount is stated
> anywhere in this build.** A priority question in a live transaction goes to the **title company and
> counsel.**

### B.1 Deeds of trust — V.B.1

**Three parties**: the **borrower**, the **lender (beneficiary)**, and a **trustee** who holds title or a
power of sale for the lender's benefit until the debt is satisfied. That third party is what distinguishes
it from a mortgage, where the borrower holds title and the lender holds a lien.

### B.2 Foreclosure — V.B.2

**The enforcement of a security interest against the property.**

chunks.heading: B.3 General property taxes — V.B.3
chunks.excerpt:
> **This is the largest gap in this module, and it is stated plainly.**
>
> **Colorado's foreclosure statutes and its PUBLIC TRUSTEE system were NOT read by this project.**
> Colorado's public trustee arrangement is distinctive among the states, and **this course does not describe
> it, does not state any notice, period, cure right, redemption right, bidding procedure or deficiency
> rule, and does not state who does what.**
>
> **Where the answer lives.** The **Current Legal Issues** outline names *"**financing, liens,
> foreclosures**"* among its representative areas at Topic 3.3, and the Commission staff supplies that
> course's mandatory content to authorized providers. **This build is not on those records and has not
> received that material** — a submission gate recorded in the readings file.
>
> A broker whose transaction involves a property in foreclosure, a short sale, or a deed of trust in
> default takes it to **counsel**, and **Rule 6.2.B.1** offers the route a broker should take seriously:
> **decline.**

### B.3 General property taxes — V.B.3

An **ad valorem** lien on the parcel, ordinarily taking priority over other liens, and one of the items
**prorated** at closing.

**No Colorado property tax statute, assessment ratio, mill levy, rate, exemption, due date, delinquency
consequence or tax sale procedure was read by this project, and none is stated anywhere in this build.**
The **Closings** course prorates taxes on **the convention the contract states**, using figures the
transaction supplies.

### B.4 Special districts — V.B.4

chunks.heading: B.5 Other liens — V.B.5
chunks.excerpt:
**A special district is a local government entity formed to finance and provide infrastructure or services
for a defined area** — water, sanitation, roads, parks, fire protection, metropolitan services — funded by
a **levy on the property within it** and often by **debt the district issued.**

**Why it matters to a buyer, stated generally.** A property inside a special district may carry a **tax
burden materially above** that of an otherwise similar property outside one, and that burden runs with the
land. It is a fact about the **cost of owning** that a buyer discovers from the district's own disclosures,
the tax records and the title work.

> **Colorado's special district statutes were NOT read by this project.** **No formation requirement,
> disclosure requirement, notice, form, levy limit, debt limit or deadline is stated anywhere in this
> build.**
>
> **What IS stated, because it was read, is the broker's own duty**, which does not depend on the district
> statute: **§ 12-10-404(3)(a)** requires a seller's agent to disclose to any prospective buyer **all adverse
> material facts ACTUALLY KNOWN**, and **§ 12-10-407(2)(b)(VI)** imposes the same on a transaction-broker.
> **§§ 12-10-404(3)(b) and 12-10-407(4)** equally provide there is **no duty to conduct an independent
> investigation.** A broker who **knows** of a district's burden discloses it; a broker who does not know is
> not required by these sections to go and find out — **and a competent broker in a district-heavy market
> will know, because Rule 6.2.A requires the experience, training and knowledge to serve that market.**

### B.5 Other liens — V.B.5

chunks.heading: C. Errors and omissions insurance
chunks.excerpt:
Judgment liens; mechanics' liens; homeowners association assessment liens; federal and state tax liens;
child support liens; and any other statutory lien. **Each arises under its own statute, and none of those
statutes was read.**

---

## C. Errors and omissions insurance

The outline names it at Topic V.C.

**What it is.** Professional liability insurance covering claims arising from a licensee's professional
services — errors, omissions, and negligent acts in the course of brokerage.

**Its source in Colorado.** **Chapter 3 of 4 CCR 725-1 is titled "Licensure, Renewal, License Status, and
Insurance"**, and the Division publishes a **Broker Insurance Requirements** page.

> **The insurance rules within Chapter 3 were NOT read in detail for this build**, and **no Colorado
> coverage amount, deductible limit, carrier requirement, policy form, effective date or exemption is stated
> anywhere in this build.** **This is a submission gate**: a course claiming to teach the errors and
> omissions requirement must state the current rule, and this one does not state it.
>
> **What this module states is the practical point that does not depend on the figure**: an errors and
> omissions policy is a **condition of doing business** in Colorado, it is a **cost of entering the field**
> — the **Practical Applications** outline names *"**E/O insurance, license fees, car insurance**"* at its
> Topic I.B.4 among the costs to get started — and **a broker checks the current requirement with the
> Division and their employing broker rather than assuming last year's answer still holds.**

---

## D. Land descriptions: surveys and Improvement Location Certificates

The outline names both at Topic V.D, and the distinction is one Colorado brokers use constantly.

chunks.heading: E. Water rights
chunks.excerpt:
| | **Survey** | **Improvement Location Certificate (ILC)** |
|---|---|---|
| **What it is** | A measurement and depiction of the parcel's boundaries by a licensed surveyor | A depiction showing the **location of improvements** relative to the boundaries as the preparer understood them |
| **What it establishes** | The **boundaries** | Whether improvements **appear** to lie within the boundaries and easements |
| **What it is used for** | Boundary questions, encroachments, subdivision, construction | Commonly required by **lenders and title companies** as a condition of closing |

**An ILC is not a boundary survey and does not establish boundaries.** A buyer who needs to know where the
line is needs a survey. A lender who needs comfort that the house is not sitting in the easement is
ordinarily satisfied by an ILC.

**Why this belongs in a contracting course.** The contract decides **whether one is obtained, who pays for
it, by when, and what happens if it shows a problem** — which is the **three-part contingency test** from
Module 04 applied to one more condition: **what event, by when, what happens if it does not occur.**

**And it is where an encroachment surfaces.** A records search will not reveal one; a survey or ILC will.
Module 01 of the **Real Estate Law and Practice** course develops encroachments as an encumbrance outside
the record.

**No Colorado surveying statute, licensing requirement, standard, monument requirement or ILC form was read
by this project**, and **none is stated here.**

---

## E. Water rights

The outline names water rights at **Topic V.E of this course** and again at **Topic I.A.1.a of the Real
Estate Law and Practice course.** The Commission puts it in two of the six outlines, which is a signal about
its weight in Colorado practice.

chunks.heading: F. Financing
chunks.excerpt:
**What this module states, and it is the general point only:**

**Water rights in the western states may be owned, conveyed, leased and encumbered SEPARATELY FROM THE
LAND.** A right to divert and use water is a distinct property interest. **It does not necessarily pass
with a conveyance of the parcel**, and a contract that says nothing about it may have transferred nothing.

**What that means for a broker completing a contract.** A listing or a contract on land with a well, a
ditch, a share in a ditch company, an augmentation plan, or any recorded water right is a transaction in
which **the water is a separate subject requiring its own treatment in the document** — and getting it
wrong may transfer a farm without the means of irrigating it.

> **NO Colorado water law statute, case, decree, administrative rule or form was read by this project.**
>
> **This course states NOTHING about**: appropriation; priority dates; adjudication; augmentation plans;
> well permits; exempt wells; ditch company shares; change of use proceedings; the division engineer's role;
> or how any of these is conveyed.
>
> **This is a submission gate, and it is one a Colorado course cannot responsibly leave open** in a market
> where farm, ranch and vacant land brokerage is ordinary work.
>
> **What a broker does in the meantime is what Rule 6.2 requires:** possess the necessary experience,
> training and knowledge — or **decline**, **obtain** them, **obtain the assistance** of a competent broker
> or **legal counsel competent in the matter**, or **co-list** with a broker who has them. **Rule 6.2.B.3
> names legal counsel expressly**, and a water question is the clearest case for it.

---

## F. Financing

chunks.heading: F.1 Equity skimming — V.F.1
chunks.excerpt:
Four items at Topic V.F, and the Commission groups them because each is a way a transaction can be
structured wrongly or dishonestly.

### F.1 Equity skimming — V.F.1

**A scheme in which a person acquires property subject to existing loans, collects rents or payments, makes
no payments on the underlying debt, and allows the property to go to foreclosure.** The owner or tenants
bear the loss; the operator keeps the cash.

**What a broker should recognise:** a buyer who wants title without assuming or paying the loan, an
arrangement in which the seller stays liable while someone else collects, and a transaction whose economics
only work if the debt is not serviced.

**No Colorado or federal equity skimming statute was read by this project**, and **no element, threshold or
penalty is stated here.** The description above is of the practice, not of an offence.

### F.2 U.C.C.C. — V.F.2

The **Uniform Consumer Credit Code**, which in states that adopted it governs **consumer credit
transactions** — disclosure, rates, charges, and remedies.

> **Colorado's U.C.C.C. was NOT read by this project.** **No rate ceiling, charge limit, disclosure
> requirement, threshold, exemption or remedy from it is stated anywhere in this build.**
>
> **Why the outline puts it here:** an **owner carry** transaction may be a consumer credit transaction, and
> a seller who becomes a lender may be taking on obligations under a statute they have never read.
> **That is a question for counsel before the seller agrees to carry**, not after.

### F.3 Standards of mortgage servicing — V.F.3

**The obligations of the entity that collects payments, administers escrow, applies payments, and handles
default on a mortgage loan.**

chunks.heading: F.4 Loan fraud — V.F.4
chunks.excerpt:
**Why it matters to a broker.** A borrower's loan may be **sold and its servicing transferred** — that is
ordinary and does not change the terms of the note — and a seller's payoff figure, a buyer's assumption
approval, and a short sale all come through the servicer rather than the original lender.

**No federal or Colorado mortgage servicing statute or regulation was read by this project**, and **no
standard, timeline, requirement or penalty is stated here.**

### F.4 Loan fraud — V.F.4

**Misrepresentation to a lender to obtain a loan or better terms** — misstated income, employment or
assets; undisclosed side agreements; a price inflated to disguise a payment outside closing; occupancy
misstated as owner-occupied; or a straw buyer.

**Where a broker meets it.** In the **undisclosed side agreement**: a payment, a credit, a repair
allowance, or a rebate agreed between buyer and seller and **kept off the closing statement.**

**Two things a broker does, and both come from provisions read for this build.**

chunks.heading: G. Landlord Tenant Act — C.R.S. § 38-12-101 et seq.
chunks.excerpt:
> **§ 12-10-410(6)** requires that, **before entering into a brokerage or listing agreement or a contract to
> buy, sell or lease**, *"**the identity of those parties, persons, or entities paying compensation or
> commissions to any broker shall be disclosed to the parties to the transaction.**"*
>
> **Rule 5.17** requires **prior written consent** from the consumer the broker represents before assessing
> or receiving **mark-ups or other compensation** for services performed, **regardless of whether it
> benefits the broker or a third party**, plus disclosure of all mark-ups paid by any customer, plus
> **records verifying disclosure and consent.**
>
> And the underlying discipline: **everything the parties agreed goes into the contract or an amendment, and
> what goes into the contract appears on the closing statement.** The **Closings** outline puts it in six
> words at its Topic III.A.1 — *"**Close to contract or amend contract in writing.**"*

**No fraud statute, element, threshold or penalty is stated in this module.** **§§ 12-10-217 and 12-10-219
were not read**, and no disciplinary consequence is stated anywhere in this build.

---

## G. Landlord Tenant Act — C.R.S. § 38-12-101 et seq.

The outline names the statute by citation at Topic V.G.

chunks.heading: G. Landlord Tenant Act — C.R.S. § 38-12-101 et seq.
chunks.excerpt:
> **§ 38-12-101 et seq. was NOT read by this project.**
>
> **This course states NO Colorado rule on**: security deposit limits; deposit return periods; the
> consequences of a wrongful withholding; notice to enter; habitability or the warranty of habitability;
> late fees; repair and deduct; retaliation; lease termination notice periods; eviction or unlawful detainer
> procedure; or any tenant remedy.
>
> **This is a submission gate**, and it is a large one for anyone whose practice includes leasing or
> property management.

**What this build DOES state about leasing comes from rules that were read**, and a student meets them in
two places:

| Source | What it requires |
|---|---|
| **Rule 5.5** | A firm engaging in property management keeps **separate trust or escrow accounts — a minimum of one for rental receipts and a minimum of one for security deposits** |
| **Rule 5.7.A** | Property management money is deposited **no later than five business days** following receipt or mutual execution of a lease, **whichever is later** — where Rule 5.7.B gives all other money **three** |
| **Rule 5.8.A** | A firm **will not deliver security deposits to an owner** without the tenant's **written authorization in a lease** or **unless written notice has been given** telling the tenant who holds the deposit and how to request its return |
| **Rule 5.8.B** | On a change of management company: **written disclosure to owner and tenant within 30 days**; **transfer by the previous firm within 60 days**; the new firm **verifies each deposit against the current lease and discloses any discrepancy** |
| **Rule 6.17.C** | A property manager must **disclose in writing any known conflict of interest in the selection or use of a business or vendor**, including **any ownership, financial, or fa

chunks.heading: Module 05 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
milial interest** |
| **§§ 12-10-404 and 12-10-405** | Speak of *"seller **or landlord**"* and *"buyer **or tenant**"* throughout — the duty lists run to leasing in their own terms |

**Module 05 of the Real Estate Law and Practice course** delivers the leasehold estates, the lease drafting
checklist, and the management agreement, and states the same gap.

---

## Module 05 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
*"**testing is required** to establish individual's satisfactory completion of the statutory
requirements"*, and **these items are not that test.**

This module completes the Commission's **Contracts and Regulations** outline: **8 + 4 + 16 + 16 + 4 = 48
hours.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 05

Written to the **Commission's Contracts and Regulations qualifying education outline**, Topic V and its
sub-topics A through G, in the outline's own order and using the outline's own item names — including
**"Equity Skimming"**, **"U.C.C.C."**, **"Standards of Mortgage Servicing"**, **"Loan Fraud"** and the

The provisions quoted — **§§ 12-10-403(4), 12-10-404(3), 12-10-405, 12-10-407(2)(b)(VI) and (4), and
12-10-410(6)** — and **Rules 5.5, 5.7, 5.8, 5.13, 5.17, 5.18, 6.2 and 6.17.C** are transcribed from
**C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10** and **4 CCR 725-1**, read on 2026-08-20.

chunks.excerpt:

lessons.title: Colorado Record Keeping and Trust Accounts — Module 01

chunks.heading: Colorado Record Keeping and Trust Accounts — Module 01
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Record Keeping and Trust Accounts — Module 01

## Legal requirements

**Course:** Record Keeping and Trust Accounts (8.0 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 0.5** of 8.0
**Commission outline topic:** **I — Legal Requirements**, allocated **0.5 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What this course is
>
> **C.R.S. § 12-10-203(4)(a)(III)(A)** names **trust accounts and record keeping** among the four subjects
> making up the statutory **72 hours**. **Rule 2.1.A.2.d** fixes the floor: *"Trust Accounts and Record
> Keeping: **not less than 8 hours**."*
>
> **The Commission approved its outline on June 6, 1996, updated 8/99.** Its objective: *"To protect the
> public by instructing students in the **proper recordkeeping procedures required by the Real Estate
> Commission to maintain and account for FUNDS BELONGING TO OTHERS**."*
>
> | Module | Commission topic | Hours |
> |---|---|---|
> | **01** | I. Legal Requirements | **0.5** |
> | 02 | II. Recordkeeping | **6.0** |
> | 03 | III. Special Areas of Concern | 1.0 |
> | 04 | IV. Termination of Brokerage Relationship | 0.5 |
> | | **TOTAL** | **8.0** |
>
> **Six of the eight hours are Module 02**, and its outline requires a **minimum of two practical
> exercises** — of which the Commission then describes four.
>
> *"**All students must successfully complete a written examination covering all major topic areas of this
> outline.**"*
>
> **Chapter 5 of 4 CCR 725-1 was read in full for this build** and is transcribed in
> `colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md` § 4. **This course is written to it.**

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: A. Definition and identification of accounts — outline Topic I.A
chunks.excerpt:
1. State what Money Belonging to Others is and where it must be kept.
2. State how a trust or escrow account must be identified with the depository.
3. State in whose name accounts must be maintained and who may withdraw.
4. State the deposit deadlines and how each is measured.
5. State the record retention period and identify its source.
6. Name the rules the Commission's outline names by number and say what each does.

---

## A. Definition and identification of accounts — outline Topic I.A

### A.1 The core rule — Rule 5.2

> *"**All Money Belonging to Others accepted by a Broker or Brokerage Firm MUST BE KEPT SEPARATE from other
> money belonging to the Broker or Brokerage Firm and MUST BE DEPOSITED into one or more of the Broker's or
> Brokerage Firm's Trust or Escrow Accounts.** The Broker or Brokerage Firm **must identify the FIDUCIARY
> NATURE of each separate Trust or Escrow Account in deposit agreements with a Recognized Depository by the
> use of the WORD 'TRUST' OR 'ESCROW' and a LABEL identifying the purpose of such account**, such as **'sales
> escrow', 'rental escrow', 'security deposit escrow'**, or other abbreviated form defined in the deposit
> agreement. The Broker or Brokerage Firm **must retain a copy of each executed Trust or Escrow Account
> deposit agreement for inspection by the Commission.**"*

**Three requirements, and each is checkable by an auditor in about a minute:**

chunks.heading: A.2 FDIC insurance coverage — outline Topic I.A.3
chunks.excerpt:
| # | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **1. Type of account** | A **Trust or Escrow Account** at a **Recognized Depository**, separate from the firm's own money |
| **2. Trust account designation** | The **word "trust" or "escrow"** in the deposit agreement, **plus a label identifying the purpose** |
| **3. The deposit agreement retained** | A copy of each executed agreement kept **for inspection by the Commission** |

**The label is not decoration.** *"Sales escrow"*, *"rental escrow"*, *"security deposit escrow"* — the
label tells the depository, the auditor and the broker what the account is for, and **Rule 5.5** then
requires property management money to be in **separate** accounts by purpose.

### A.2 FDIC insurance coverage — outline Topic I.A.3

The Commission's outline names *"**Relevance to FDIC insurance coverage**"* as a sub-item.

> **No FDIC regulation, coverage limit, pass-through requirement or titling rule was read by this project**,
> and **no coverage amount or requirement is stated anywhere in this build.**
>
> **What this module states is the point that does not depend on the figure:** an account's **titling and
> the records behind it** are what determine how deposit insurance applies to funds held for many
> beneficiaries. **A broker holding other people's money asks their depository how the account is titled
> and what that means**, and confirms it in the deposit agreement **Rule 5.2** requires them to retain.
>
> **This is a submission gate** — the outline names FDIC coverage and this build cannot state its rules.

### A.3 Number of accounts, and when none is needed — Rules 5.3, 5.4 and 5.5

chunks.heading: A.4 Funds must be available — Rule 5.6
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 5.3 — whose name.** A firm acting **in the name of the Employing Broker or Independent Broker as a
> sole proprietor** maintains accounts **in that broker's name**; a firm licensed as a **partnership,
> corporation or limited liability company** maintains them **in the entity's name.** The **Employing Broker
> or Independent Broker are responsible for, must maintain and be able to withdraw** from each account, and
> **may authorize other licensed or unlicensed cosigners** — but *"**such authorization will not relieve the
> Employing Broker or Independent Broker of any responsibility under the Commission statutes and these
> Rules.**"*
>
> **Rule 5.4 — from zero to unlimited.** A firm is **not limited** in the number of accounts. *"**If the
> Brokerage Firm is not in possession of Money Belonging to Others, there is no obligation to maintain a
> separate Trust or Escrow Account.**"*
>
> **Rule 5.5 — where property management is concerned, separate accounts are REQUIRED.** A firm engaging in
> property management *"**must deposit rental receipts and security deposits and disburse money collected
> for such purposes in SEPARATE Trust or Escrow Accounts, a MINIMUM OF ONE for rental receipts and a MINIMUM
> OF ONE for security deposits.**"*

**Rule 5.4 is the one brokers are surprised by.** A firm that never holds other people's money **is not
required to have a trust account at all.** Many Colorado firms operate that way, with earnest money going
straight to a title company under **Rule 5.12.A.**

**And Rule 5.3's last sentence is the one employing brokers should read twice.** Authorising a cosigner —
licensed or unlicensed — **transfers none of the responsibility.**

### A.4 Funds must be available — Rule 5.6

chunks.heading: B. Acting broker's responsibilities — outline Topic I.B
chunks.excerpt:
> *"Unless otherwise agreed to in writing by the parties, **Money Belonging to Others must not be invested
> in any type of account, security, or certificate of deposit that has a FIXED TERM FOR MATURITY or imposes
> ANY FEE OR PENALTY FOR WITHDRAWAL prior to maturity.**"*

**Other people's money must be reachable on the day it is needed**, which is a different question from
whether it earns anything.

---

## B. Acting broker's responsibilities — outline Topic I.B

### B.1 Opening and maintaining the account — outline Topic I.B.1

**Rules 5.2 and 5.3 above**, plus:

> **Rule 5.1 — Establishment of Internal Accounting Controls.** *"Any Brokerage Firm or Broker who receives
> Money Belonging to Others **must establish WRITTEN accounting control policies and procedures**, which
> must include **adequate checks and balances over the financial activities of the Broker, Brokerage Firm,
> AND UNLICENSED PERSONS**, as well as **manage the risk of fraud or illegal acts.**"*

**Written**, and reaching **unlicensed persons** expressly — the bookkeeper, the assistant, the
office manager. Module 03 of this course develops why, under the outline's *"Separation of Duties"* and
*"Employee Theft and internal controls."*

### B.2 Timely deposit — outline Topic I.B.2, and Rule 5.7

| Money | Deadline | Measured from |
|---|---|---|
| **Property management** | **No later than 5 BUSINESS DAYS** | receipt of funds **or mutual execution of a lease, whichever is LATER** |
| **All other** Money Belonging to Others | **No later than 3 BUSINESS DAYS** | receipt of funds **or mutual execution of contract, whichever is LATER** |

chunks.heading: C. Acknowledgment of trust account status by bank or other depository — outline Topic I.C
chunks.excerpt:
**Business days, not calendar days.** And the clock starts at **the later** of the two events — so money
received before a contract is mutually executed does not start the clock until it is.

**Rule 5.12** then governs earnest money specifically: a broker receiving it **must deliver it to the
earnest money holder to be deposited in accordance with the contract** and **obtain a dated and signed
receipt**; if the **firm** holds it, **Rule 5.7.B**'s three business days apply; and a transfer to a lawyer
or closing entity also requires **a dated and signed receipt.**

---

## C. Acknowledgment of trust account status by bank or other depository — outline Topic I.C

**Rule 5.2's second and third sentences are the whole of this sub-topic**: the **fiduciary nature** of each
account is identified **in the deposit agreement** by the **word "trust" or "escrow" plus a purpose label**,
and **a copy of each executed deposit agreement is retained for inspection by the Commission.**

**The deposit agreement is the acknowledgment.** A broker who cannot produce one has not satisfied
Rule 5.2, whatever the account is called on the statement.

---

## D. Commission rules and regulations — outline Topic I.D

The outline names four sub-items, and three of them name rules **by number.**

### D.1 Record retention period — outline Topic I.D.1

> **Rule 6.20**: *"Both a Broker and a Brokerage Firm **must retain transaction files for all transactions
> for a period of FOUR (4) YEARS** beginning from **the consummation date of the transaction or the
> expiration date of any Listing Contracts that do not consummate.**"*

chunks.heading: D.2 Position Statements — outline Topic I.D.2
chunks.excerpt:
**Four years, two possible start dates**, and the rule expressly does **not** require a broker to obtain and
retain **existing public records, title commitments, loan applications, lender required disclosures, or
related affirmations from independent third party closing entities after the closing date.**

**The Commission's Transaction File Checklist, which Rule 6.20 says designates the required documents, was
NOT obtained by this project** — a submission gate.

**And Rule 5.14.E** permits the **three-way reconciliation reports, ledgers, journals and bank account
statements** to be **kept electronically**; **Rule 6.24** governs electronic records and production.

### D.2 Position Statements — outline Topic I.D.2

> **NO Commission position statement was obtained or read by this project**, and **no module of this build
> states the content of one.** **This is a submission gate**, and it is the second course in this build to
> record it — the **Practical Applications** outline names **CP 41** by number for the same reason.

### D.3 Audits — outline Topic I.D.3

The outline's own words: *"**Audit(s) — repeated audit findings are subject to disciplinary action (Rules
5.21., 6.25.A.)**"*

chunks.heading: D.4 Overview of key rules — outline Topic I.D.4
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 5.21 — Production of Documents and Records.** *"A Broker and Brokerage Firm **must produce for
> inspection by the Commission any document or record as may be reasonably necessary for investigation or
> audit** in the enforcement of the Commission statutes and these Rules. **Failure to submit such documents
> or records within the time set by the Commission in its notification will be GROUNDS FOR DISCIPLINARY
> ACTION** unless the Commission has granted an extension of time for such production."*
>
> **Rule 6.25 — Investigations or Audits by Commission.** Read for this build; the outline cites **6.25.A**
> for the proposition it states in its own text — that **repeated audit findings are subject to disciplinary
> action.**

**No disciplinary ground, sanction, penalty or procedure is stated anywhere in this build.** **§§ 12-10-217
and 12-10-219 were not read.** What is stated is what **Rule 5.21** itself says: **failure to produce within
the time set is grounds for disciplinary action.**

### D.4 Overview of key rules — outline Topic I.D.4

The outline names three by number: **5.2., 5.8.A. and 6.3.B.** All three were read.

chunks.heading: Module 01 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
| Rule | What it does |
|---|---|
| **5.2** | **Trust or escrow accounts** — Part A.1 of this module |
| **5.8.A** | **Owner-held security deposits** — a firm **will not deliver security deposits to an owner without the tenant's written authorization in a lease or unless written notice has been given** telling the tenant **who is holding the deposit** and **the specific requirements for the procedure in which the tenant may request return.** If the deposit goes to the owner, the management agreement **should** place financial responsibility for its return on the owner and **must** authorize disclosure of the owner's **true name and current mailing address** in a dispute |
| **6.3.B** | **The employing broker's responsibilities** — to **maintain all trust and escrow accounts and records as set forth in Chapter 5**; **maintain all transaction records as set forth in Rule 6.20**; **develop the firm's written policies as set forth in Rule 6.4**; and **provide a "Reasonable-Level of Supervision" for all Associate Brokers** |

**And the rule that closes the loop on responsibility:**

> **Rule 5.22**: *"The **Employing Broker or Independent Broker are held JOINTLY RESPONSIBLE with the
> Brokerage Firm** in complying with Chapter 5 of these Rules."*

---

## Module 01 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
**all students successfully complete a written examination covering all major topic areas**, and **these
items are not that examination.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 01

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 01
chunks.excerpt:
Written to the **Commission's Record Keeping and Trust Accounts (8.0 Classroom Hours) qualifying education
outline, approved June 6, 1996, updated 8/99**, Topic I and its sub-topics A through D, in the outline's own
order and citing the rules **the outline itself names by number** — **5.2, 5.8.A, 5.21, 6.3.B and 6.25.A**.
The hour figure is the Commission's.

**Chapter 5 of 4 CCR 725-1 was read in full**, together with **Rules 6.3, 6.20, 6.24 and 6.25**, on
2026-08-20, and is transcribed in `colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md` § 4.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **FDIC regulations** and any deposit insurance
coverage limit or titling rule; **every Commission position statement**; the **Commission's Transaction File
Checklist**; **C.R.S. §§ 12-10-217, 12-10-219 and 12-10-222** and every disciplinary ground and penalty;
**C.R.S. § 38-12-101 et seq.**; and **every Commission-approved form.**

**No FDIC coverage amount, position statement content, checklist item, disciplinary sanction, penalty,
