lessons.title: Colorado Record Keeping and Trust Accounts — Module 02

chunks.heading: Colorado Record Keeping and Trust Accounts — Module 02
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Record Keeping and Trust Accounts — Module 02

## Recordkeeping

**Course:** Record Keeping and Trust Accounts (8.0 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 6.0** of 8.0
**Commission outline topic:** **II — Recordkeeping**, allocated **6.0 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### Six of the eight hours, and the Commission requires exercises
>
> The outline's Topic II has two halves:
>
> | Sub-topic | What it is |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** Transaction File Documents | Part A |
> | **B.** Accounting Records — **1. Journal; 2. Ledgers; 3. Bank Reconciliation; 4. PREPARATION OF MINIMUM OF 2 PRACTICAL EXERCISES** | Parts B to E |
>
> **The Commission states the reconciliation identity in its own notation** at Topic II.B.3:
>
> ***"Bank Reconciliation: Journal Balance + Sum of Ledger Balances = Bank Balance = Transaction File
> Liabilities"***
>
> and then requires *"**Preparation of Minimum of 2 Practical Exercises**"* — **describing four**, lettered
> (a) through (d). **This course delivers all four and records each separately**, because the Commission
> describes four and a student who has done two has done half of what the outline sets out.

## Learning objectives

1. State what a journal records and every field each entry must contain.
2. State what a ledger records and the two rules a ledger can never break.
3. Perform a three-way reconciliation and state what it proves.
4. State the outline's reconciliation identity and explain each term.
5. Complete the four exercises the Commission describes.
6. State the method of accounting required absent written agreement.
7. State the reporting deadline to beneficiaries absent a contrary provision.

chunks.heading: A. Transaction file documents — outline Topic II.A
chunks.excerpt:
---

## A. Transaction file documents — outline Topic II.A

**Rule 6.20** requires both a broker and a firm to **retain transaction files for four years** — from
**consummation**, or from **the expiration of a listing contract that does not consummate.**

**Rule 5.14** then requires the accounting records for each trust or escrow account, and **Rule 5.15.B**
requires supporting records:

> *"The Brokerage Firm must maintain supporting records, which accurately detail all cash received and
> disbursed under the terms of any Management Agreement.*
> **1.** *"**All deposits** of funds into a Trust or Escrow Account **must identify each person tendering
> funds, the amount of funds tendered, types of funds received from each person, and the property address
> affected.**
> **2.** *"**All disbursements** of funds from a Trust or Escrow Account **must be supported by documents
> such as bids, invoices, contracts, etc.** Ledger and journal records must **identify the payees, property
> addresses affected and amount of funds transferred for each property.**"*

**Money in must be traceable to a person and a property. Money out must be supported by a document.** That
is the whole of the file discipline, and it is what makes the reconciliation in Part D provable rather than
merely arithmetical.

**The Commission's Transaction File Checklist, which Rule 6.20 names as designating the required documents,
was NOT obtained by this project**, and **no module of this build states what it lists.** That is a
submission gate.

---

## B. The journal — outline Topic II.B.1, and Rule 5.14.A

> **Rule 5.14.A**: *"A **'journal' or an equivalent accounting system which records, IN CHRONOLOGICAL ORDER,
> ALL Money Belonging to Others which is received or disbursed** by the Brokerage Firm."*

chunks.heading: C. The ledger — outline Topic II.B.2, and Rule 5.14.B
chunks.excerpt:
**Every field the rule requires, and there is no discretion about any of them:**

| For funds RECEIVED — Rule 5.14.A.1 | For funds DISBURSED — Rule 5.14.A.2 |
|---|---|
| **a.** The **date of receipt AND deposit** | **a.** The **date of payment** |
| **b.** The **name of the person giving the money** | **b.** The **check number or electronic transfer record** |
| **c.** The **name of the person AND property** for which received | **c.** The **name of the payee** |
| **d.** The **purpose** of the receipt | **d.** A **reference to vendor documentation or other physical records verifying purpose for payment** |
| **e.** The **amount** | **e.** The **amount paid** |
| **f.** **A resulting CASH BALANCE for the account** | **f.** **A resulting cash balance for the account** |

**Two fields new brokers routinely omit.**

**Receipt field (a) is TWO dates** — the date received and the date deposited. The gap between them is
exactly what **Rule 5.7** measures, and a journal recording only one date cannot show compliance with the
three- or five-business-day deadline.

**Disbursement field (d) is a reference to a document.** Not a description. **Rule 5.15.B.2** says which
kinds: *"bids, invoices, contracts, etc."* A disbursement with no supporting document is a disbursement
nobody can justify to an auditor.

**And field (f) on both sides:** the journal carries a **running cash balance** after every entry. That
balance is the first term of the reconciliation identity.

---

## C. The ledger — outline Topic II.B.2, and Rule 5.14.B

chunks.heading: C. The ledger — outline Topic II.B.2, and Rule 5.14.B
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 5.14.B**: *"A **'ledger' or an equivalent component of an accounting system which records, in
> chronological order, all money which is received or disbursed by the Broker ON BEHALF OF EACH PARTICULAR
> BENEFICIARY** of a Trust or Escrow Account. The ledger record must show the monetary transactions
> **affecting each individual beneficiary** and must **SEGREGATE such transactions from those pertaining to
> other beneficiaries.** The ledger record for each beneficiary **must contain the same transactional
> information** as set forth in subsection A. **NO LEDGER MAY EVER BE ALLOWED TO HAVE A NEGATIVE CASH
> BALANCE. The sum of all ledger balances must agree AT ALL TIMES with the corresponding journal after each
> transaction has been posted.**"*

**The journal is the account. The ledgers are the people.** One journal per trust or escrow account; one
ledger per beneficiary within it.

**Two rules a ledger can never break, and both are absolute on their face:**

> **1. NO NEGATIVE BALANCE — EVER.** A negative ledger means **one beneficiary's money has been used for
> another's**, which is exactly what **Rule 5.9** prohibits: *"Money Belonging to Others belonging to one
> beneficiary **must not be used for the benefit of another beneficiary.**"* On a managed portfolio it
> happens when a disbursement for one property exceeds that property's balance — and it is a violation the
> moment it is posted, not at month end.
>
> **2. THE SUM OF LEDGER BALANCES EQUALS THE JOURNAL — AT ALL TIMES, after each transaction is posted.**
> Not monthly. Not at reconciliation. **After each posting.**

chunks.heading: D. Reconciliation — outline Topic II.B.3, and Rule 5.14.C
chunks.excerpt:
**Rule 5.19** adds: if a **branch office** maintains a trust or escrow account separate from the main
office's, **a separate record keeping system must be maintained in the branch**, and the **employing
broker** is responsible for it.

---

## D. Reconciliation — outline Topic II.B.3, and Rule 5.14.C

### D.1 The rule

> **Rule 5.14.C**: *"**THREE-WAY RECONCILIATION must be performed MONTHLY to show that ON THE SAME DATE the
> cash balance shown in the JOURNAL, the sum of the cash balances for all LEDGERS, and the RECONCILED BANK
> BALANCE are the same. A three-way reconciliation report must be COMPLETED AND MAINTAINED MONTHLY** to show
> such three-way reconciliation. The Broker is **not required to maintain records or reconcile any Trust or
> Escrow Account when such account does not contain Money Belonging to Others.**"*
>
> **Rule 5.14.D**: a firm **may deposit personal funds as may be required to pay bank charges** incurred in
> connection with maintaining the account **without violating Rule 5.10** — with **an entry in the journal
> and on the ledger.**
>
> **Rule 5.14.E**: the reports, ledgers, journals and bank statements **may be kept electronically.**

### D.2 The Commission's identity, term by term

> ***"Journal Balance + Sum of Ledger Balances = Bank Balance = Transaction File Liabilities"***

**Read carefully, this states three separate equalities and the Commission wrote it as a memory device
rather than as arithmetic** — the journal balance and the sum of ledger balances are the **same number**,
not two numbers to be added. What the outline is naming is the **four things that must agree**:

chunks.heading: D.3 Reconciling the bank balance
chunks.excerpt:
| Term | What it is | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| **Journal balance** | The running cash balance of the account | **Rule 5.14.A.1.f and A.2.f** |
| **Sum of ledger balances** | Every beneficiary's balance, added | **Rule 5.14.B** |
| **Reconciled bank balance** | The bank statement balance adjusted for deposits in transit and outstanding items | The bank statement plus the reconciliation |
| **Transaction file liabilities** | What the firm actually owes to the beneficiaries, from the files | **Rule 5.15.B** and the transaction files |

**The fourth term is the one that makes this an audit rather than a bookkeeping check.** The first three can
agree with each other and still be wrong if the records do not match **what the firm actually owes the
people whose money it holds.**

### D.3 Reconciling the bank balance

> **Bank statement balance**
> **plus** deposits in transit (received and journalled, not yet on the statement)
> **minus** outstanding checks and transfers (disbursed and journalled, not yet cleared)
> **plus or minus** bank errors
> **= RECONCILED BANK BALANCE**

**Bank charges and interest posted by the bank but not yet journalled are corrected in the JOURNAL, not in
the reconciliation** — and **Rule 5.14.D** permits the firm to deposit its own money to cover charges, with
entries in the journal and the ledger.

### D.4 A three-way reconciliation worked

**Every figure supplied as a given.**

> **Sales escrow account, 31 May.** Bank statement balance **$92,400.00**. Deposits in transit
> **$18,000.00**. Outstanding checks **$7,250.00** and **$2,150.00**. The journal shows a cash balance of
> **$101,000.00**. Ledgers: Alvarez **$15,000.00**, Boone **$22,000.00**, Chen **$8,000.00**, Delgado
> **$31,000.00**, Everly **$25,000.00**.

chunks.heading: E. The four practical exercises the Commission describes
chunks.excerpt:
| Step | Calculation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Bank statement balance | | 92,400.00 |
| plus deposits in transit | +18,000.00 | 110,400.00 |
| less outstanding checks | −7,250.00 −2,150.00 | **101,000.00** |
| **Reconciled bank balance** | | **$101,000.00** |
| **Journal balance** | given | **$101,000.00** |
| **Sum of ledger balances** | 15,000 + 22,000 + 8,000 + 31,000 + 25,000 | **$101,000.00** |

**Three agree. The fourth term — transaction file liabilities — is then checked against the files**: does
the firm in fact owe Alvarez $15,000, Boone $22,000, and so on? If a file shows a $16,000 deposit for
Alvarez, **the reconciliation balanced and the records are still wrong.**

> **A worked failure, because the failures are what a broker must recognise.**
>
> Same account, and the ledgers are Alvarez **$15,000**, Boone **$22,000**, Chen **−$1,200**, Delgado
> **$31,000**, Everly **$25,000**. The sum is **$91,800**, the journal shows **$91,800**, and the bank
> reconciles to **$91,800**. **All three agree.**
>
> **And it is a violation.** **Rule 5.14.B**: *"**No ledger may ever be allowed to have a negative cash
> balance.**"* Chen's negative balance means **$1,200 of somebody else's money is standing behind Chen's
> disbursement** — which is **Rule 5.9**'s diversion prohibition. **A reconciliation that balances proves
> the arithmetic, not compliance.**

---

## E. The four practical exercises the Commission describes

> The outline requires *"**Preparation of Minimum of 2 Practical Exercises**"* and then describes four.
> **This course delivers all four and records each separately.**

### E.1 Exercise (a) — a broker-closed sale

chunks.heading: E.2 Exercise (b) — a property manager's reconciliation
chunks.excerpt:
> *"Working from a **sample contract and 6-column settlement worksheet**, student shall **create journal and
> ledger entries leading to the closing of a real estate sale by a broker.** **Reconcile the ledger totals
> to the journal balance and a sample bank statement.**"*

**What the student produces:**

1. A **six-column worksheet** for the transaction — the instrument taught in the **Closings** course,
   Module 02.
2. **Journal entries** in chronological order for every receipt and disbursement, with **all six fields**
   Rule 5.14.A requires on each.
3. A **ledger** for the beneficiary, segregated, with the same transactional information.
4. A **reconciliation** of the ledger total to the journal balance and to a sample bank statement.

**The connection this exercise exists to make.** The **closing statement** says what the parties owe each
other. The **journal and ledger** say what the brokerage received and disbursed. **They are two views of
the same money**, and a student who can produce both from one contract understands trust accounting.

**The deposit deadline is part of the exercise.** **Rule 5.7.B** — earnest money into the firm's account
**no later than three business days** following receipt **or mutual execution of contract, whichever is
later** — and the journal's **two dates** (received and deposited) are what show it.

### E.2 Exercise (b) — a property manager's reconciliation

> *"Working from **sample files, journals and ledgers**, student shall **reconcile the bank accounts for a
> property manager managing and holding security deposits for a MINIMUM OF 8 PROPERTIES.** (Lease
> information may be provided as necessary to show amount of security deposits and other needed lease
> data.)"*

chunks.heading: E.2 Exercise (b) — a property manager's reconciliation
chunks.excerpt:
**What makes this harder than exercise (a):** **eight ledgers**, not one; **two accounts**, not one, because
**Rule 5.5** requires **a minimum of one for rental receipts and a minimum of one for security deposits**;
and every ledger subject to **Rule 5.14.B's no-negative-balance rule** at every posting.

**A worked fragment, figures given.**

> **Security deposit escrow, eight properties.** Deposits held: **$1,400, $1,150, $1,600, $975, $1,825,
> $1,300, $1,450, $1,100.**
>
> **Sum = $10,800.00.** That is what the **ledger total**, the **journal balance** and the **reconciled bank
> balance** must all equal — and what the **eight leases** must show the firm owing.
>
> **The fourth term is the point of the exercise.** If a lease shows a $1,500 deposit for a property whose
> ledger shows $1,450, the reconciliation balances and **the firm owes $50 it has not recorded.** **Rule
> 5.8.B** requires a firm taking over management to **verify each deposit transferred matches the amount in
> the current lease and disclose any discrepancy** to owner and tenant — the same check, done at the point
> of transfer.

**And the Chapter 5 rules that shape the exercise:**

chunks.heading: E.3 Exercise (c) — the same sale, closed by a title company
chunks.excerpt:
| Rule | What it requires here |
|---|---|
| **5.5** | Separate accounts — minimum one for rental receipts, minimum one for security deposits |
| **5.7.A** | Property management money deposited **no later than five business days** after receipt or mutual execution of a lease, **whichever is later** |
| **5.8.A** | No delivery of deposits to an owner without the **tenant's written authorization in a lease or written notice** naming who holds them and how to request return |
| **5.10.A** | Money **due and payable to the firm withdrawn MONTHLY** |
| **5.10.C** | Fees are *"earned"* and available **only after all contracted services are performed and there is no remaining right of recall** |
| **5.15.A** | Reports to beneficiaries per the management agreement; absent a contrary provision, **within 30 days after the end of the month** in which funds were received or disbursed |

### E.3 Exercise (c) — the same sale, closed by a title company

> *"**Repeat exercise (a) above where the broker holds an earnest money deposit but the CLOSING IS PERFORMED
> BY A TITLE COMPANY.**"*

**What changes, and it is the point of the exercise:** the brokerage's records now show **a receipt of
earnest money and a single disbursement of it to the closing entity** — not the whole closing.

**Rule 5.12.B**: the firm **may transfer the earnest money from its trust or escrow account to a lawyer or
a closing entity closing the transaction**, and **must obtain a dated and signed receipt** from the person
or entity providing settlement services.

chunks.heading: E.4 Exercise (d) — software, backup and imaging
chunks.excerpt:
**And Rule 6.19.A does not change.** The broker with the brokerage relationship is *"**responsible for the
proper closing of the transaction**"* **whoever conducts it**, must ensure the consumer receives a closing
statement that is **accurate, complete and detailed and signed by the broker**, and must **deliver closing
statements and other closing documents to the brokerage firm immediately following closing.**

**A student who thinks a title company closing means the brokerage has no records has misunderstood the
exercise.** The trust account entries are fewer; **the responsibility is the same.**

### E.4 Exercise (d) — software, backup and imaging

> *"**Proper backup and printouts for software accounting systems, CD-ROM imaging of records.**"*

**The outline was written in 1996 and updated in 1999, and its media references show it.** What the
requirement is about has not changed: **records kept in a system must be producible, and must survive the
system.**

**Rule 5.14.E** permits the reconciliation reports, ledgers, journals and bank statements to be **kept
electronically.** **Rule 6.24** governs **electronic records and production of records.** And **Rule 5.21**
supplies the test that matters:

> *"A Broker and Brokerage Firm **must PRODUCE FOR INSPECTION by the Commission any document or record as
> may be reasonably necessary for investigation or audit** ... **Failure to submit such documents or records
> within the time set by the Commission in its notification will be GROUNDS FOR DISCIPLINARY ACTION** unless
> the Commission has granted an extension of time."*

chunks.heading: F. Method of accounting and reporting
chunks.excerpt:
**What the student produces:** a demonstration that the system's **journal, ledgers and reconciliation
reports can be produced on demand**, that **backups exist and have been tested**, and that the records
remain available for the **four years Rule 6.20 requires** — including after a change of software.

**"We can't get at those records any more" is not an answer to a Commission notification**, and **Rule 5.21
makes the failure itself the ground.**

---

## F. Method of accounting and reporting

> **Rule 5.16 — Method of Accounting.** *"In the absence of a written agreement to the contrary, the **'CASH
> BASIS' of accounting MUST BE USED** for maintaining all required Trust or Escrow Accounts and
> corresponding records. A Brokerage Firm **may use another method of accounting IF IT IS AGREED UPON IN
> WRITING** by the Brokerage Firm and the beneficiary. The Brokerage Firm **must maintain SEPARATE Trust and
> Escrow Accounts and corresponding records for each beneficiary using a different accounting method.**"*
>
> **Rule 5.15.A — Reports to beneficiaries.** Prepared and delivered **according to the terms of the
> Management Agreement**; *"**in the absence of a provision in the Management Agreement to the contrary,
> Brokerage Firms must deliver these reports WITHIN THIRTY (30) DAYS after the end of the month in which
> funds were either received or disbursed.**"*

**Cash basis is the default and a different method needs the beneficiary's written agreement — and its own
separate accounts and records.** A firm that lets one owner use accrual has just created a second account
and a second set of records.

---

## Module 02 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 02
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**.

**The engagement items do NOT satisfy the Commission's requirement.** Topic II.B.4 requires **prepared
practical exercises**; the outline describes four and this course records each separately. The course engine
does not credit this course without them.

---

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 02
chunks.excerpt:

lessons.title: Colorado Record Keeping and Trust Accounts — Module 03

chunks.heading: Colorado Record Keeping and Trust Accounts — Module 03
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Record Keeping and Trust Accounts — Module 03

## Special areas of concern

**Course:** Record Keeping and Trust Accounts (8.0 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 1.0** of 8.0
**Commission outline topic:** **III — Special Areas of Concern**, allocated **1.0 hour**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What the Commission's outline puts in this topic
>
> | Sub-topic | Delivered in |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** Separation of Duties — 1. Employee theft and internal controls; 2. The broker's need to personally perform bank reconciliations or periodically compare reconciliations against source documents; 3. Use of practitioner aids at auditing website | Part A |
> | **B.** Sales — 1. Promissory notes; 2. Void and/or NSF checks; 3. Earnest money disputes and interpleaders; 4. Good Funds | Part B |
> | **C.** Property Management — 1. Separate trust account; 2. Commingling/negative ledgers; 3. Security and advance deposits; 4. Owner reserves; 5. Account for broker commissions earned vs. taken | Part C |
> | **D.** Broker Ledger | Part D |
> | **E.** Broker Acting as Principal and Licensee (Partnerships; Joint Ventures, etc.) | Part E |
> | **F.** Duplicate Signatures | Part F |
>
> **One hour for six subjects**, and the Commission chose them because each is a place where a firm with
> tidy books still ends up with a problem.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: A. Separation of duties — outline Topic III.A
chunks.excerpt:
1. State the internal control requirement and who it must reach.
2. State why the outline puts the broker personally into the reconciliation.
3. State what a broker does with an earnest money dispute and what a broker must not do.
4. State the property management rules that create separate accounts and forbid negative ledgers.
5. State when commissions become available to the firm.
6. State the rules that apply when a broker holds or manages their own property.

---

## A. Separation of duties — outline Topic III.A

### A.1 Employee theft and internal controls — III.A.1

> **Rule 5.1**: *"Any Brokerage Firm or Broker who receives Money Belonging to Others **must establish
> WRITTEN accounting control policies and procedures, which must include adequate CHECKS AND BALANCES over
> the financial activities of the Broker, Brokerage Firm, AND UNLICENSED PERSONS, as well as MANAGE THE RISK
> OF FRAUD OR ILLEGAL ACTS.**"*

**Read the three things the rule requires and the one it names expressly.**

| Requirement | Note |
|---|---|
| **Written** policies and procedures | Not an understood office practice |
| **Adequate checks and balances** over financial activities | The separation of duties this topic is named for |
| Reaching **the broker, the firm, AND UNLICENSED PERSONS** | The bookkeeper, the assistant, the office manager |
| **Manage the risk of fraud or illegal acts** | The rule states the purpose, so the test is whether the controls actually do it |

chunks.heading: A.2 The broker performs or checks the reconciliation — III.A.2
chunks.excerpt:
**The classic separation, and the one an auditor looks for:** the person who **receives** money is not the
person who **records** it is not the person who **reconciles** the account is not the person who **signs
the checks.** In a small firm one person may do more than one of those — which is precisely why the rule
requires the broker's own involvement in Part A.2.

**Rule 5.3.C is the sentence that closes the loophole.** The employing or independent broker **may authorize
other licensed or unlicensed cosigners** — but *"**such authorization will not relieve the Employing Broker
or Independent Broker of any responsibility under the Commission statutes and these Rules.**"*

**And Rule 6.3.A.2**: employing brokers **must supervise all unlicensed employees**, *"including, but not
limited to, Unlicensed On-Site Managers, secretaries, bookkeepers, and personal assistants of Associate
Brokers."*

### A.2 The broker performs or checks the reconciliation — III.A.2

The outline's own words: *"**Broker's need to personally perform bank reconciliations or periodically
compare reconciliations against source documents (transaction files).**"*

**Two alternatives, and the Commission names both:**

1. **Perform the reconciliation personally**; or
2. **Periodically compare the reconciliations against SOURCE DOCUMENTS** — the transaction files.

**Alternative 2 is the one that catches what alternative 1 alone would miss.** A bookkeeper who is diverting
funds can produce a reconciliation that balances every month — the journal, the ledgers and the bank all
agree. **What they cannot do is make the transaction files agree**, which is why the Commission's identity
at Topic II.B.3 ends with **"= Transaction File Liabilities"** and why this sub-topic exists.

chunks.heading: A.3 Practitioner aids — III.A.3
chunks.excerpt:
**Rule 5.14.C** requires the **three-way reconciliation monthly, with a report completed and maintained**;
**Rule 5.22** makes the **employing or independent broker jointly responsible with the firm** for all of
Chapter 5.

### A.3 Practitioner aids — III.A.3

The outline names *"**Use of practitioner aids at auditing Website**"* — material the Division publishes for
brokers.

> **No Division practitioner aid, audit guide, checklist or template was obtained by this project**, and
> **no module of this build states the content of one.** **This is a submission gate.**

---

## B. Sales — outline Topic III.B

### B.1 Promissory notes: safekeeping and collection — III.B.1

> **Rule 5.13**: *"If a **promissory note is received as earnest money** pursuant to an executed contract,
> **the seller must be INFORMED OF THE DATE such promissory note becomes due.** If payment is not made by
> the due date, the Broker **must PROMPTLY NOTIFY THE SELLER and DELIVER THE ORIGINAL promissory note.**"*
>
> **Rule 5.18**: *"**Any instrument, equity, or Thing of Value taken in lieu of cash MUST BE HELD BY THE
> BROKERAGE FIRM, except as otherwise agreed.**"*

**Three obligations in Rule 5.13, in sequence:** tell the seller **the due date**; watch it; and if it
passes unpaid, **notify promptly and hand over the original.** A note is not earnest money in the account —
it is a promise, and **Rule 5.18** says the firm holds it.

### B.2 Void and NSF checks — III.B.2

**A check that does not clear was never funds.** The journal recorded a receipt; the bank did not.

**What has to happen:** the journal and the affected ledger are **corrected**; the **parties are told**;
and — the point of the sub-topic — **nothing is disbursed against it.**

chunks.heading: B.3 Earnest money disputes and interpleaders — III.B.3
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 6.19.E** — the Good Funds rule — states it directly for closing: a broker or firm *"**must not
> disburse or authorize disbursement of funds UNTIL THOSE FUNDS HAVE BEEN RECEIVED and are ... available
> for immediate withdrawal AS A MATTER OF RIGHT** from the financial institution ... **or available for
> immediate withdrawal as a consequence of an agreement with a financial institution** ... **If the
> agreement contains contingencies or reservations, NO DISBURSEMENTS CAN BE MADE until these are
> satisfied.**"*

**And the ledger consequence:** a disbursement made against a check that then bounces leaves that
beneficiary's ledger **negative**, which **Rule 5.14.B** forbids absolutely — *"**No ledger may ever be
allowed to have a negative cash balance.**"*

### B.3 Earnest money disputes and interpleaders — III.B.3

**Three things are true about disputed earnest money whatever the contract says**, and none of them depends
on a statute this build did not read:

> **1. The broker holds.** The broker does **not** decide who is entitled to it.
> **2. The parties or a court decide.** An **interpleader** is the proceeding by which a stakeholder pays
> disputed funds into court and lets the claimants litigate between themselves.
> **3. Nothing is disbursed on the broker's own judgement.**

**Why a broker must not simply release it.** **Rule 5.9**: money belonging to one beneficiary **must not be
used for the benefit of another.** Releasing disputed funds to the wrong claimant is exactly that — and
**Rule 5.14.B**'s no-negative-ledger rule bites the moment it is posted.

chunks.heading: B.4 Good funds — III.B.4
chunks.excerpt:
**What the broker does:** stop, tell the designated broker, and get **legal advice before the money moves.**
**Rule 6.2.B.3** names the route expressly — obtain the assistance of *"the Employing Broker, Supervisory
Broker, a Broker who meets the requirements ... **or LEGAL COUNSEL that is competent in the matter.**"*

> **No Colorado interpleader statute or rule of civil procedure was read by this project**, and **no
> procedure, deadline, filing requirement, fee or cost rule is stated anywhere in this build.** The
> **Contracts and Regulations** outline names *"**remedies including damages and specific performance**"*
> among the **Current Legal Issues** representative areas, and the Commission supplies that course's
> mandatory material to authorized providers.

### B.4 Good funds — III.B.4

The outline names six arrangements a broker meets, and **Rule 6.19.E** is the rule behind all of them:

chunks.heading: C. Property management — outline Topic III.C
chunks.excerpt:
| The outline's item | What it is |
|---|---|
| **a. Cashier's or teller's check** | An instrument drawn by the bank itself |
| **b. Broker check in advance of closing** | The brokerage's own check issued before the closing funds arrive |
| **c. Wire transfer** | Funds moved bank to bank |
| **d. Tri-party agreements** (broker–title company–broker's bank) | The **agreement** contemplated by Rule 6.19.E.2 — and *"**if the agreement contains contingencies or reservations, no disbursements can be made until these are satisfied**"* |
| **e. Netting earned commission against earnest money deposit** (security deposits also) | Offsetting rather than moving money — permitted only within **Rule 5.10.C**, which makes fees available **only after all contracted services are performed and there is no remaining right of recall** |
| **f. Requirements of the Great Colorado Payback Program for unclaimed funds** | The state's unclaimed property programme |

> **§ 38-35-125, which Rule 6.19.E cites, was NOT read by this project**, and **no definition of good funds,
> clearing period or list of acceptable instruments from the statute is stated anywhere in this build.**
>
> **The Great Colorado Payback Program and Colorado's unclaimed property statute were NOT read**, and **no
> dormancy period, reporting deadline, remittance requirement or form is stated anywhere in this build.**
> **This is a submission gate**, and a real one: a brokerage that holds money it cannot return has an
> obligation somewhere, and this course does not state what it is.

---

## C. Property management — outline Topic III.C

Five sub-items, and every one of them is a rule read in full.

### C.1 Separate trust account — III.C.1

chunks.heading: C.2 Commingling and negative ledgers — III.C.2
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 5.5**: a firm engaging in property management *"**must deposit rental receipts and security deposits
> and disburse money collected for such purposes in SEPARATE Trust or Escrow Accounts, a MINIMUM OF ONE for
> rental receipts and a MINIMUM OF ONE for security deposits.**"*

**Two accounts minimum, by purpose** — and **Rule 5.2** then requires each to carry **the word "trust" or
"escrow" plus a label identifying the purpose** in the deposit agreement.

### C.2 Commingling and negative ledgers — III.C.2

> **Rule 5.10**: *"A Broker's or Brokerage Firm's **personal or business operating funds must not be
> commingled** with Money Belonging to Others."*
>
> **Rule 5.9**: money belonging to **one beneficiary must not be used for the benefit of another**, and
> **never** for the firm or the broker.
>
> **Rule 5.14.B**: *"**No ledger may ever be allowed to have a negative cash balance.**"*

**On a managed portfolio the negative ledger is how commingling shows up.** One owner's account overdrawn
means another owner's money is standing behind it, however briefly, and the rule admits no *however
briefly.*

**The one permitted exception is narrow and stated:** **Rule 5.14.D** lets a firm deposit **personal funds
as may be required to pay bank charges** on the account **without violating Rule 5.10** — with an entry in
**both the journal and the ledger.**

### C.3 Security and advance deposits — separate accounts — III.C.3

**Rule 5.5** again, and **Rule 5.8**:

chunks.heading: C.4 Owner reserves — III.C.4
chunks.excerpt:
> **5.8.A — owner-held.** A firm receipting for security deposits *"**will not deliver such security deposits
> to an owner without the tenant's WRITTEN AUTHORIZATION IN A LEASE or unless WRITTEN NOTICE has been given
> to the tenant**"* — notice given so the tenant knows **who is holding the deposit** and **the specific
> requirements for the procedure in which the tenant may request return.** If the deposit goes to the
> owner, the management agreement **should** place financial responsibility for its return on the owner and
> **must** authorize disclosure of the owner's **true name and current mailing address** in a dispute.
>
> **5.8.B — a change of management company.** **Written disclosure to owner and current tenant within 30
> DAYS** of execution or assignment of a management agreement, of the status of any deposit held by the
> previous firm; the **previous firm transfers within 60 DAYS** and confirms the amount; the **new firm
> verifies each deposit matches the amount in the current lease and discloses any discrepancy**; and the
> tenant is **informed in writing if the owner is holding the deposit.**

**Rule 5.11** adds a case brokers do not expect: **money accepted for activities NOT involving real estate
brokerage services** — **guest deposits for short-term rentals**, **security deposits for the broker's own
rental properties**, **deposits from a buyer where the broker is acting as a builder**, and any other
non-brokerage purpose — **must still go into a trust or escrow account**, and if into the broker's own
rather than the firm's, must comply with **Rules 5.6, 5.9, 5.10, a journal with monthly two-way
reconciliation, and 5.21.**

### C.4 Owner reserves — III.C.4

chunks.heading: C.5 Commissions earned versus taken — III.C.5
chunks.excerpt:
**Reserves are the owner's money held for future expenses.** They are Money Belonging to Others, they sit
on that owner's ledger, and they are subject to every rule in Chapter 5.

**What the management agreement must settle:** **how much** is held, **what it may be used for**, and **when
it is replenished.** Module 05 of the **Real Estate Law and Practice** course carries the management
agreement checklist.

### C.5 Commissions earned versus taken — III.C.5

> **Rule 5.10.C**: *"In the absence of a specific written agreement to the contrary, **commissions, fees, and
> other charges collected by a Brokerage Firm for performing any service on behalf of another are considered
> 'EARNED' and available for use by the Brokerage Firm ONLY AFTER ALL CONTRACTED SERVICES HAVE BEEN PERFORMED
> and there is NO REMAINING RIGHT OF RECALL by others for such money.**"*
>
> **Rule 5.10.A**: money in the account that becomes **due and payable to the firm must be withdrawn
> MONTHLY.**

**Two different failures, and the outline names the distinction: "earned vs. taken."**

- **Taken before earned** — the firm has used money that is still somebody else's. That is **Rule 5.9**.
- **Earned and not taken** — the firm's own money is sitting in the trust account past month end. That is
  **Rule 5.10.A**, and it is commingling in the other direction.

chunks.heading: D. The broker ledger — outline Topic III.D
chunks.excerpt:
**Rule 5.10.C's recording requirement:** the firm **must identify and record all commissions, fees or other
charges withdrawn** on the **account journal and the individual ledgers of those against whom they are
charged** — and where a single disbursement covers more than one transaction, rental period or beneficiary,
must on request produce **a schedule detailing the individual components and identifying the affected
beneficiary or property ledgers.**

---

## D. The broker ledger — outline Topic III.D

**A ledger for the brokerage firm itself, within the trust or escrow account.** It is where **Rule 5.14.D's
bank-charge deposits** are recorded, where **money that has become due and payable to the firm** sits until
it is withdrawn under **Rule 5.10.A**, and where **advances made under Rule 5.10.B** are identified.

> **Rule 5.10.B**: money **advanced by the firm for the benefit of another** may be placed in the account
> and **identified as an advance**, but may be **withdrawn by the firm only on behalf of that person** — and
> **must be identified and recorded in the journal and the ledger and disclosed in the accounting to the
> beneficiary** as **Rule 5.15** requires.

**The broker ledger is not an exception to Rule 5.10's prohibition on commingling.** It is the mechanism by
which the three narrow permitted cases — bank charges, advances, and earned-but-not-yet-withdrawn fees —
are made **visible** rather than invisible.

---

## E. Broker acting as principal and licensee — outline Topic III.E

**Partnerships, joint ventures and syndications**, as the outline names them. **Rules 5.10.D and 5.10.E**
address exactly this, and the trigger is the **20 percent** ownership threshold in **§ 12-10-201(6)(b)(VII)**.

chunks.heading: F. Duplicate signatures — outline Topic III.F
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 5.10.D** — rental proceeds for a broker's own property managed **through a firm the broker is NOT
> licensed with** must be deposited in a **trust or escrow account maintained for Money Belonging to
> Others**, subject to **Rules 5.2 and 5.14.**
>
> **Rule 5.10.E** — rental proceeds for property **owned by a broker who IS licensed with the firm** must be
> deposited into **one or more trust or escrow accounts SEPARATE from any other accounts containing Money
> Belonging to Others** — though those accounts **may hold the proceeds of other brokers licensed with the
> same firm** whose own properties it manages. Subject to **Rules 5.2 and 5.14.**
>
> **A "broker's property" for both rules includes properties held in PARTNERSHIP with others, JOINT
> VENTURES, or SYNDICATIONS**, provided the broker's ownership in the entity or property is **more than the
> 20% threshold** in § 12-10-201(6)(b)(VII).

**And the disclosure that goes with it, from Chapter 6:**

> **Rule 6.17.B**: *"If a Broker **sells, buys, or leases real property on the Broker's own account**, such
> Broker **must disclose in the contracting instrument, or in a separate concurrent writing, that they are a
> licensed Broker.**"*
>
> **Rule 6.17.A**: a **continuing duty** to disclose, in writing, **any known Conflict of Interest** arising
> in the course of any real estate transaction.

**Twenty percent is the line, and a broker whose interest is in an entity rather than in the property
directly still has to compute it.**

---

## F. Duplicate signatures — outline Topic III.F

**The outline names it and states nothing further**, and this module states what the rules read support and
no more.

chunks.heading: Module 03 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**What the sub-topic is about:** who may sign on a trust or escrow account, and the control risk that
arises when signature authority is duplicated or delegated.

> **Rule 5.3.C** is the provision: the **Employing Broker or Independent Broker** are *"**responsible for,
> must maintain and be able to withdraw money from each separate account**"*, and **may authorize other
> licensed or unlicensed cosigners** — *"**However, such authorization will not relieve the Employing Broker
> or Independent Broker of any responsibility under the Commission statutes and these Rules.**"*

**Two requirements and one warning.** The broker **must be able to withdraw** — authority cannot be
delegated away entirely. Cosigners **may** be authorised, licensed or not. And **the responsibility does not
move with the authority.**

**Read against Rule 5.1's internal controls, the point of the sub-topic emerges:** every additional
signature is a control weakened, so a firm that adds one adds a compensating control — which is the
separation of duties in Part A, and the broker's own reconciliation or source-document comparison in A.2.

> **No Commission rule on duplicate or facsimile signatures beyond Rule 5.3.C was found in the reading**,
> and **no requirement about signature cards, dual signature thresholds, electronic signature authority or
> signature stamps is stated anywhere in this build.**

---

## Module 03 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
**all students successfully complete a written examination covering all major topic areas**, and **these
items are not that examination.**

---

**Chapter 5 of 4 CCR 725-1 was read in full** — **Rules 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.5, 5.8, 5.9, 5.10, 5.11, 5.13,

lessons.title: Colorado Record Keeping and Trust Accounts — Module 04

chunks.heading: Colorado Record Keeping and Trust Accounts — Module 04
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Record Keeping and Trust Accounts — Module 04

## Termination of brokerage relationship

**Course:** Record Keeping and Trust Accounts (8.0 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 0.5** of 8.0
**Commission outline topic:** **IV — Termination of Brokerage Relationship**, allocated **0.5 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What the Commission's outline puts in this topic
>
> | Sub-topic | Delivered in |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** Forwarding Trust Funds and Documents | Part B |
> | **B.** Closing Accounting Records and paperwork reduction | Part C |
>
> Half an hour, and it is the topic most courses skip. The Commission gave it its own place because **the
> obligations that survive a relationship are the ones a broker is least likely to have planned for.**

## Learning objectives

1. State when a brokerage relationship ends and the one-year backstop.
2. State what survives termination for a single agent and what survives for a transaction-broker.
3. State what happens to trust funds and documents on termination.
4. State what happens to security deposits when management passes to another firm, and by when.
5. State the retention obligation that outlives the relationship.

---

## A. When the relationship ends — § 12-10-409

chunks.heading: A.1 What survives, and it differs by relationship
chunks.excerpt:
> **(1)(a)** The relationship **commences when the broker is engaged** and continues **until performance or
> completion** of the agreement by which the broker was engaged.
>
> **(1)(b)** If the agreement is **not performed or completed for any reason**, the relationship ends at the
> **EARLIER** of:
> **(I)** any **date of expiration agreed** by the parties;
> **(II)** any **termination or relinquishment** of the relationship by the parties; or
> **(III)** **ONE YEAR after the date of the engagement.**

**The one-year backstop runs whether or not anyone remembers it.** A file left open ends by statute at a
date neither party chose.

### A.1 What survives, and it differs by relationship

| | **Single agent** — § 12-10-409(2)(b) | **Transaction-broker** — § 12-10-409(3) |
|---|---|---|
| **Accounting** | **Survives** — *"accounting for all money and property related to and received during the engagement"* | **Survives** — the same words |
| **Confidentiality** | **Survives** — *"keeping confidential all information received during the course of the engagement **that was made confidential by request or instructions from the engaging party**"* | **Not stated in (3)** |
| **Everything else** | *"**owes no further duty or obligation**"* — (2)(a) | *"**owes no further obligation or responsibility**"* |

**The accounting obligation is the one this course is about, and it survives for BOTH.**

**And the surviving confidentiality is not unlimited.** **§ 12-10-409(2)(b)(II)** lifts it where **(A)** the
engaging party **grants written consent to disclose**, **(B)** disclosure is **required by law**, or **(C)**
the information **is made public or becomes public by the words or conduct of the engaging party or from a
source other than the broker.**

---

chunks.heading: B. Forwarding trust funds and documents — outline Topic IV.A
chunks.excerpt:
## B. Forwarding trust funds and documents — outline Topic IV.A

### B.1 The money

**Money Belonging to Others does not become the firm's money because the relationship ended.** It is the
beneficiary's, and **every Chapter 5 rule continues to apply to it until it is properly delivered.**

| Rule | What it still requires |
|---|---|
| **5.9** | It **must not be used** for another beneficiary, or for the firm or broker |
| **5.10** | It **must not be commingled** with the firm's own funds |
| **5.14.B** | The ledger **must not go negative**, and the ledgers must still sum to the journal |
| **5.14.C** | **Three-way reconciliation monthly** while the account holds Money Belonging to Others |
| **5.15** | The **accounting** to the beneficiary is still owed |
| **5.21** | The records **must still be produced** to the Commission on request |
| **5.22** | The **employing or independent broker remains jointly responsible** with the firm |

**Rule 5.14.C's own relief is the only thing that changes:** the broker is *"**not required to maintain
records or reconcile any Trust or Escrow Account when such account does not contain Money Belonging to
Others.**"* — which is to say, **when the money has actually gone.**

**And where entitlement is disputed, nothing changes about that either.** The broker **holds**; the parties
or a court decide; and **Rule 6.2.B.3** offers the route — obtain the assistance of the employing broker,
a supervisory broker, a competent broker, **or legal counsel competent in the matter.**

### B.2 Security deposits when management passes to another firm — Rule 5.8.B

This is the case the outline's sub-topic is really about, and the rule fixes **two deadlines.**

chunks.heading: B.2 Security deposits when management passes to another firm — Rule 5.8.B
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 5.8.B**: A firm which **begins management** of a property most recently managed by another firm
> *"**must disclose to the owner and the current tenant, IN WRITING, and WITHIN THIRTY (30) DAYS after
> execution or assignment of a Management Agreement, the STATUS of any security deposit held by the previous
> Brokerage Firm.**"*
>
> *"The **PREVIOUS Brokerage Firm must TRANSFER the security deposit WITHIN SIXTY (60) DAYS after the
> execution or assignment** of a management agreement to the new Brokerage Firm **and CONFIRM to the owner
> and the tenant the amount of the funds transferred.**"*
>
> *"The **NEW Brokerage Firm must VERIFY that each security deposit transferred to them MATCHES THE AMOUNT
> LISTED IN THE CURRENT LEASE and DISCLOSE ANY DISCREPANCY to the owner and current tenant.** The Brokerage
> Firm **must inform the tenant, in writing, IF THE OWNER IS HOLDING the security deposit.**"*

| Who | What | By when |
|---|---|---|
| **New firm** | **Written disclosure of the deposit's status** to **owner and current tenant** | **Within 30 days** of execution or assignment |
| **Previous firm** | **Transfer the deposit**, and **confirm the amount** to owner and tenant | **Within 60 days** of execution or assignment |
| **New firm** | **Verify each deposit against the current lease** and **disclose any discrepancy** to owner and tenant | On receipt |
| **New firm** | **Inform the tenant in writing if the owner is holding it** | — |

**The verification step is the fourth term of the reconciliation identity in the field.** *"= Transaction
File Liabilities."* A transfer that balances against the previous firm's ledgers can still be wrong against
**the leases**, and the rule puts the check on the incoming firm.

chunks.heading: B.3 The documents
chunks.excerpt:
**And Rule 5.8.A governs delivery to an owner at any time**: no delivery **without the tenant's written
authorization in a lease or written notice** telling the tenant **who holds the deposit** and **how to
request its return.**

### B.3 The documents

**Rule 6.19.A** requires a broker licensed with a firm to *"**deliver closing statements to the Brokerage
Firm along with any other closing documents, IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING CLOSING**"* — so on a transaction that
closed, the documents are already with the firm.

**Rule 6.20** then requires **both the broker and the firm** to retain the transaction file for **four
years**, from **consummation** or from **the expiration of a listing contract that does not consummate.**

**Rule 5.19** applies where a **branch office** maintained its own trust or escrow account and record
keeping system: **the employing broker is responsible for it**, which does not end when the branch does.

---

## C. Closing accounting records and paperwork reduction — outline Topic IV.B

### C.1 Closing the records

**An account is closed when it holds nothing.** Until then **Rule 5.14.C** requires the **monthly three-way
reconciliation**, and **Rule 5.2**'s deposit agreement and its retained copy remain the firm's.

**The final reconciliation is the one that matters most.** It should show **zero** across all four terms —
journal balance, sum of ledger balances, reconciled bank balance, and transaction file liabilities. **A
final reconciliation that does not reach zero means money is still owed to somebody**, and the firm needs to
know to whom before the account is closed.

chunks.heading: C.2 Paperwork reduction — what may be reduced and what may not
chunks.excerpt:
**Money the firm cannot return to its owner does not become the firm's.** The outline names the answer's
location at its Topic III.B.4.f — *"**Requirements of Great Colorado Payback Program for unclaimed
funds**"*.

> **The Great Colorado Payback Program and Colorado's unclaimed property statute were NOT read by this
> project**, and **no dormancy period, reporting deadline, remittance requirement or form is stated anywhere
> in this build.** **This is a submission gate**, and it is exactly the situation this module describes: a
> firm winding up an account with funds it cannot deliver has an obligation this course cannot state.

### C.2 Paperwork reduction — what may be reduced and what may not

**Rule 5.14.E** permits the **three-way reconciliation reports, ledgers, journals and bank account
statements** to be **kept electronically**, and **Rule 6.24** governs **electronic records and production of
records.**

**What may NOT be reduced is the ability to produce.**

> **Rule 5.21**: *"A Broker and Brokerage Firm **must produce for inspection by the Commission any document
> or record as may be reasonably necessary for investigation or audit** ... **Failure to submit such
> documents or records within the time set by the Commission in its notification will be GROUNDS FOR
> DISCIPLINARY ACTION** unless the Commission has granted an extension of time for such production."*

**A firm that converts to a new system, closes an office, or ends a relationship still has to produce
records for four years.** Module 02's exercise (d) — *"proper backup and printouts for software accounting
systems"* — exists for this moment, and the test of whether it was done properly is whether the records can
be produced **after** the system that made them is gone.

chunks.heading: C.3 What a broker should have when a relationship ends
chunks.excerpt:
### C.3 What a broker should have when a relationship ends

| Item | Source |
|---|---|
| **A final reconciliation showing zero, or showing exactly what is still held and for whom** | Rule 5.14.C |
| **A dated and signed receipt for every delivery of funds** | Rule 5.12.A and 5.12.B |
| **Written confirmation of every security deposit transferred, to owner and tenant** | Rule 5.8.B |
| **The accounting owed to each beneficiary** | Rule 5.15 |
| **The transaction file, retained four years** | Rule 6.20 |
| **The records, producible on demand for that period** | Rules 5.21, 5.14.E, 6.24 |
| **Confidences kept** — for a single agent, subject to the three exceptions | § 12-10-409(2)(b)(II) |

---

## Module 04 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
**all students successfully complete a written examination covering all major topic areas**, and **these
items are not that examination.**

This module completes the Commission's **Record Keeping and Trust Accounts** outline: **0.5 + 6.0 + 1.0 +
0.5 = 8.0 hours.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 04

Written to the **Commission's Record Keeping and Trust Accounts qualifying education outline, approved June
6, 1996, updated 8/99**, Topic IV and its sub-topics A and B, using the outline's own item names —
*"**Forwarding Trust Funds and Documents**"* and *"**Closing Accounting Records and paperwork
reduction**"*.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 04
chunks.excerpt:
**§ 12-10-409** and **Rules 5.2, 5.8, 5.9, 5.10, 5.12, 5.14, 5.15, 5.19, 5.21, 5.22, 6.2, 6.19, 6.20 and
6.24** are transcribed from **C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10** and **4 CCR 725-1**, read on 2026-08-20 and
recorded in `colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** the **Great Colorado Payback Program** and
Colorado's **unclaimed property** statute; **C.R.S. § 38-12-101 et seq.**; **every Commission position
statement**; the **Commission's Transaction File Checklist**; and **C.R.S. §§ 12-10-217 and 12-10-219** and
every disciplinary ground and penalty.

**No dormancy period, unclaimed property deadline, remittance requirement, deposit limit, tenant remedy,

**30 days** and **60 days** in Rule 5.8.B, and the **four years** in Rule 6.20 are transcribed from the

chunks.heading: Colorado Current Legal Issues — Module 01
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Current Legal Issues — Module 01

## Colorado rules, regulations, policies, position statements and instructive disciplinary proceedings

**Course:** Current Legal Issues (8.0 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 3.0** of 8.0
**Commission outline topic:** **1 — Colorado Real Estate Rules, Regulations, Policies, Position Statements,
and instructive Disciplinary Proceedings** (the first of the outline's three major topic areas)
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### This course is unlike the other five, and the reason is in the Commission's own note
>
> The outline, approved **July 2, 1996**, carries this note in brackets before its topic list. It is
> transcribed in full because it governs how the course must be built:
>
> > *"[NOTE: **Staff of the Colorado Real Estate Commission shall supply on a timely but periodic basis to
> > real estate education providers (shown on its records as authorized to provide this course) certain
> > references, source materials, topics, areas, and direction for the teaching of this course. The
> > Commission staff will periodically specify to the respective schools the various items which will be
> > MANDATORY in the course coverage.**]"*
>
> **No other course in this project has a content requirement that changes on the regulator's schedule.**
> This one does. The Commission names three major topic areas and then tells providers that **staff will
> specify what is mandatory, periodically.**
>
> > **THE GATE, STATED AT THE TOP.** **This project is not on the Commission's records as an authorized
> > provider of this course and has NOT received that material.** The three modules of this course are built
> > from

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
**the outline's own three topic areas** and from **the statutes and rules this project read on
> > 2026-08-20.** **Conforming this course to whatever Commission staff currently specifies is a submission
> > gate that RECURS every time the Commission issues new material** — it is not satisfied once.

> ### The hours, and a discrepancy this build records rather than resolves
>
> **The outline is headed "8.1 Classroom Hours."** The Division's Broker Qualifying Education page says
> *"Current Legal Issues (**8 Hours**)"*, and **Rule 2.1.A.2.e** says *"Current Legal Issues: **not less than
> 8 hours**."*
>
> **This build delivers 8.0** — which satisfies the rule's floor and produces the statutory 168 exactly —
> **and records the 8.1 as an open question for the Division.** No module states 8.1 as a requirement.
>
> **The outline states no hours for its three topic areas.** The 3.0 / 3.0 / 2.0 division across this
> course's three modules is a **StateCourse decision**, labelled as one, and it is the only course in the
> Colorado build where the module hours are not the Commission's own.
>
> | Module | Commission topic area | Hours |
> |---|---|---|
> | **01** | 1. Colorado rules, regulations, policies, position statements, and instructive disciplinary proceedings | **3.0** |
> | 02 | 2. Recent and relevant federal and state case law and statutory law | 3.0 |
> | 03 | 3. "Other" — the sixteen representative areas | 2.0 |
> | | **TOTAL** | **8.0** |

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: A. Where the rules live, and how a broker finds them
chunks.excerpt:
1. State where Colorado's real estate rules live and how a broker finds the current version.
2. Name the nine chapters of 4 CCR 725-1 and what each governs.
3. State what a Commission position statement is and why this course states none.
4. State what an instructive disciplinary proceeding is and what a broker learns from one.
5. State the rules a broker must check for currency, and how.
6. State the audit and production obligations that make currency enforceable.

---

## A. Where the rules live, and how a broker finds them

### A.1 The two bodies of authority

| Source | Where it is published |
|---|---|
| **C.R.S. Title 12, Article 10** — the statute | The Colorado Revised Statutes, published by the legislature |
| **4 CCR 725-1 — Rules Regarding Real Estate Brokers** | The **Code of Colorado Regulations**, published by the **Secretary of State** |

**Rules change, and they change by rulemaking.** The Secretary of State's CCR carries **every version** of
4 CCR 725-1 with the rulemaking docket behind it, so a broker can see **what changed, when, and under which
proceeding.**

**The version read for this build** is rule version **12355**, 89 pages, read on **2026-08-20**. **A broker
reading this course later must check whether it is still current**, and the readings file names the version
precisely so that check is possible.

### A.2 The nine chapters

chunks.heading: B. Position statements — outline Topic 1, and the second gate
chunks.excerpt:
| Chapter | Subject |
|---|---|
| **1** | Definitions |
| **2** | **Licensure Requirements** — including Rule 2.1, the **168 hours** |
| **3** | Licensure, Renewal, License Status, and **Insurance** |
| **4** | Continuing Education Requirement |
| **5** | **Separate Accounts and Accounting** |
| **6** | **Practice Standards** |
| **7** | **Use of Standard Forms** |
| **8** | Declaratory Orders |
| **9** | Commission Review of Initial Decisions and Exceptions |

**Chapters 5, 6 and 7 are where a practising broker spends their time**, and this project's courses deliver
them: **Chapter 5** in the **Record Keeping and Trust Accounts** course; **Chapters 6 and 7** across
**Contracts and Regulations**, **Closings** and **Practical Applications**.

**Chapters 8 and 9 were read but are not taught in this build.** A **declaratory order** proceeding and the
**Commission's review of initial decisions and exceptions** are procedural matters that arise after
something has gone wrong, and **no procedure, deadline, filing requirement or standard of review from either
chapter is stated anywhere in this build.**

---

## B. Position statements — outline Topic 1, and the second gate

**A Commission position statement states the Commission's view on a question the statute and rules do not
answer on their face.** The Commission publishes them, and its own course outlines cite them:

chunks.heading: C. Instructive disciplinary proceedings — outline Topic 1
chunks.excerpt:
- The **Record Keeping and Trust Accounts** outline names *"**Position Statements**"* at its Topic I.D.2,
  among the Commission rules and regulations a student must meet.
- The **Practical Applications** outline names one **by number** at its Topic I.D — *"Gaining competency
  (**CP 41**)"*.
- The **Contracts and Regulations** outline names *"**Commission interpretations and positions on the
  license law**"* at its Topic I.A.3.

> **NO Commission position statement was obtained or read by this project.** **No module of this build
> states the content, number, date or effect of one**, and **CP 41 is named only because the Practical
> Applications outline names it.**
>
> **This is the second submission gate in this course**, and it reaches three of the six Colorado courses. A
> course that claims to teach *"Commission interpretations and positions on the license law"* — the
> Contracts outline's own words — **cannot do so from statute and rule alone.**

**What a broker does about it in the meantime.** Position statements are published by the Division, and a
broker whose question is not answered by the statute or the rule **looks for one before guessing** — and
takes it to their employing broker and, where the question is legal, to counsel. **Rule 6.2.B.3** names
*"legal counsel that is competent in the matter"* as one of the four routes.

---

## C. Instructive disciplinary proceedings — outline Topic 1

**The outline's phrase is "instructive Disciplinary Proceedings", and the word "instructive" is doing the
work.** The Commission's point is not that a student should memorise sanctions; it is that **the proceedings
show which rules get broken and how.**

chunks.heading: C. Instructive disciplinary proceedings — outline Topic 1
chunks.excerpt:
> **NO Colorado disciplinary decision, stipulation, consent order or final agency order was read by this
> project**, and **no case, outcome, sanction or penalty is stated anywhere in this build.** **C.R.S.
> §§ 12-10-217, 12-10-219 and 12-10-222 were not read**, so **no disciplinary GROUND is stated either.**
>
> **This is the third submission gate in this course**, and the Commission's own note says where the
> material comes from: **staff supplies it to authorized providers.**

**What this module states instead is what the rules themselves say about enforcement**, because those
provisions **were** read:

| Provision | What it says |
|---|---|
| **§ 12-10-411** | A violation of **any provision of Part 4** — the brokerage relationship sections — *"constitutes an act pursuant to section 12-10-217(1)(m) for which the real estate commission **may investigate and take administrative action**"* |
| **Rule 5.21** | Failure to **produce documents or records** within the time the Commission sets *"**will be grounds for disciplinary action**"* absent an extension |
| **Rule 6.3.A.1** | *"**Whenever a complaint is filed with the Commission against an Associate Broker, the Commission MAY INVESTIGATE whether there have been violations of section 12-10-217(1)(r) by the EMPLOYING BROKER.**"* |
| **Rule 2.1.D** | The Commission **may audit courses at any time and at no cost**, may request **all instructional materials and student attendance records**, and **failure to comply may result in removal of the provider, instructor and/or course from the approved provider list** |
| **Record Keeping outline, Topic I.D.3** | *"**Audit(s) — repeated audit findings are subject to disciplinary action (Rules 5.21., 6.25.A.)**"* |

chunks.heading: D. What a broker must keep current, and how
chunks.excerpt:
**Three of those five reach somebody other than the licensee who did the thing.** **Rule 6.3.A.1** reaches
the **employing broker** on a complaint against an associate. **Rule 2.1.D** reaches the **school**.
**Rule 5.22** holds the employing or independent broker **jointly responsible with the firm** for all of
Chapter 5. **That is the structure of Colorado enforcement**, and it is stateable from the rules without any
case at all.

---

## D. What a broker must keep current, and how

**This is the practical core of Topic 1, and it is what a student can take away from a course whose
mandatory content they have not received.**

### D.1 The things that change

| What | Where to check | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **4 CCR 725-1** | Secretary of State's **CCR**, with the rulemaking docket | Every rule in five of this project's six Colorado courses |
| **C.R.S. Title 12, Article 10** | The Colorado Revised Statutes | The statute the rules sit under |
| **Commission-approved forms** | *"To obtain the forms promulgated by the Commission, **visit the Division's website**"* — **Rule 7.1.A** | **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)** requires a broker to **use** a Commission-approved form when one exists and is appropriate |
| **Commission position statements** | The Division | Named by three of the six course outlines |
| **The Transaction File Checklist** | *"may be found on the Division's website"* — **Rule 6.20** | It **designates** the documents a transaction file must contain |
| **Practitioner aids at the auditing website** | Named by the Record Keeping outline, Topic III.A.3 | Trust account compliance |
| **Online Course Approval Checklist** | Named by the Practical Applications outline | Every distance-delivered course in this build |

chunks.heading: D.2 The rule that makes currency a form question
chunks.excerpt:
**Four of those seven were NOT obtained by this project**, and each is recorded as a submission gate:
**the forms**, **the position statements**, **the Transaction File Checklist**, and **the Online Course
Approval Checklist** — together with the **practitioner aids**.

### D.2 The rule that makes currency a form question

> **Rule 7.1.A**: A *"Commission-Approved Form"* is *"a form **promulgated by the Commission FOR CURRENT USE
> by Brokers.**"* A broker *"**must use a Commission-Approved Form when such form exists and is appropriate
> for the transaction.**"*

**"For current use" is the operative phrase.** A superseded form is not a Commission-approved form, and a
broker using last year's version has not satisfied **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)**.

**And where no approved form exists or one is not appropriate**, **Rule 7.1.B** permits an **Attorney
Form** — which **must carry the words *"This form has not been approved by the Colorado Real Estate
Commission"***, must name the attorney or law firm and the broker or firm it was prepared for, and **may not
be altered by the broker other than by completing blank spaces.**

### D.3 The rule that makes currency the provider's problem too

> **Practical Applications outline**: *"**Providers should address each applicable Statute, Rule and Position
> Statement during the course. COURSE PROVIDERS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR ENSURING THAT THE STATUTES, RULES AND
> POSITION STATEMENTS USED DURING THE COURSE PRESENTATION ARE ACCURATE AND UP-TO-DATE.**"*

chunks.heading: E. The rules a broker checks first
chunks.excerpt:
**The Commission put the currency obligation on the provider in writing**, in a different outline, and it
applies to this build as much as to any other. **The readings file names the exact rule version and the
exact date read** so that a reviewer can determine whether this build is current, rather than having to
take its word.

---

## E. The rules a broker checks first

For a broker who finishes this course and wants a short list, these are the provisions read for this build
that a licensee touches most often — and therefore the ones whose currency matters most.

| Rule or section | What it governs |
|---|---|
| **§ 12-10-403(2)** | **Transaction-broker by default** unless single agency is established **in writing** |
| **§ 12-10-406** | **Dual agency prohibited** |
| **§§ 12-10-404, 12-10-405, 12-10-407** | The three duty lists |
| **§ 12-10-408** and **Rule 6.5** | The disclosures, and that they come **before eliciting or discussing confidential information** |
| **§ 12-10-409** | Duration, and the **one-year** backstop |
| **§ 12-10-410** | Compensation — and that **payment does not establish agency** |
| **Rule 5.2, 5.5, 5.7, 5.14** | Trust accounts, separate accounts, deposit deadlines, journal, ledger, **monthly three-way reconciliation** |
| **Rule 6.2** | Competency, and the **four routes** |
| **Rule 6.3** | Employing broker supervision, reaching **unlicensed employees** |
| **Rule 6.10** | **Advertising** |
| **Rule 6.11** | **Square footage disclosure**, on the Commission-approved form |
| **Rule 6.12** | The **CMA/BPO notice**, verbatim, and the **prohibition** on those used to obtain financing |
| **Rule 6.13** | Presenting offers **to the other consumer's broker**, then the employing broker, then the consumer |
| **Rule 6.17** | **Continuing** duty to dis

chunks.heading: Module 01 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
close conflicts in writing |
| **Rule 6.19** | Closing responsibility, the **signed** closing statement, and **Good Funds** |
| **Rule 6.20** | **Four-year** transaction file retention |
| **Rule 7.1** | Standard forms, and **use the Commission-approved form** |

---

## Module 01 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**.

**The Commission's outline states no examination requirement for this course**, unlike the Closings and

Practical Applications outlines, which state that testing is required. **This build does not supply one the
Commission did not state**, and the in-module items remain what they are — progression checks at this
school's own thresholds.

---
