chunks.heading: Colorado Current Legal Issues — Module 02
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Current Legal Issues — Module 02

## Recent and relevant federal and state case law and statutory law

**Course:** Current Legal Issues (8.0 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 3.0** of 8.0
**Commission outline topic:** **2 — Recent and relevant Federal and State case law and statutory law** (the
second of the outline's three major topic areas)
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What this module can and cannot be
>
> The outline's topic area 2 is *"**Recent and relevant Federal and State case law and statutory law**"*, and
> the Commission's bracketed note says its **staff supplies the references, source materials, topics, areas
> and direction** for teaching this course, and **periodically specifies what is mandatory.**
>
> > **THE GATE.** **This project has not received that material**, and **NO Colorado or federal case was
> > read by this project.** **No case name, holding, reasoning, date or outcome is stated in this module or
> > anywhere in this build.**
> >
> > Two Colorado decisions are **named** in this build — **Conway-Bogue** and **Colorado Bar Association v.
> > The Title Guaranty Company** — and they are named **only because the Contracts and Regulations outline
> > names them at its Topic I.B.1 and I.B.2.** **Neither was read and neither holding is stated.**
>
> **What this module delivers instead is the thing a student can actually use**: how statutory and case law
> reach a Colorado broker, which statutes this build read and which it did not, and how a broker recognises
> that a question has left the rules and entered the law.
>
> **The 3.0 hours is a StateCourse decision.** The outline states no hours for its topic areas

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
.

## Learning objectives

1. State how statute, rule and case law relate to each other for a Colorado broker.
2. State which statutes this build read and which it named but did not read.
3. Recognise when a question has passed from the rules into law and route it correctly.
4. State the rules that require a broker to send a party to counsel, in their own words.
5. State what a broker does when the law changes.

---

## A. How the law reaches a broker

### A.1 Four layers

| Layer | For a Colorado broker |
|---|---|
| **Statute** | **C.R.S. Title 12, Article 10**, and the many other titles a transaction touches — 38 (property), 39 (taxation), and others |
| **Rule** | **4 CCR 725-1**, promulgated by the Commission under the statute |
| **Commission interpretation** | **Position statements** — named by three of the six course outlines, **none read by this project** |
| **Case law** | Court decisions construing all of the above — **none read by this project** |

**A rule cannot contradict its statute, and a court's construction of either governs both.** That is why
the Commission's outline asks for **recent and relevant** case law: the rules a broker reads may have been
construed in a way the text does not reveal.

### A.2 Where this build's statutory reading actually stopped

**This is the honest map, and it is the most useful thing this module contains.**

chunks.heading: B. Recognising when a question has left the rules
chunks.excerpt:
| Body of law | Read for this build? |
|---|---|
| **C.R.S. § 12-10-203** — application, education, examination | **Yes, in full** |
| **C.R.S. §§ 12-10-402 to 12-10-411** — brokerage relationships | **Yes, in full** |
| **4 CCR 725-1** — all nine chapters | **Yes, in full** |
| **C.R.S. §§ 12-10-217, 12-10-219, 12-10-222** — discipline, supervision | **No** |
| **C.R.S. §§ 12-10-218, 12-10-304** — affiliated business arrangements, referral fees | **No** |
| **C.R.S. § 12-10-602** — appraisers | **No** |
| **C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10 Part 5** — subdivisions | **No** |
| **C.R.S. § 38-35-125** — good funds, cited by Rule 6.19.E | **No** |
| **C.R.S. § 38-35.5-101** — psychologically impacted property, cited by four duty provisions | **No** |
| **C.R.S. § 38-12-101 et seq.** — Landlord Tenant Act | **No** |
| **C.R.S. article 33.3 of title 38** — CCIOA | **No** |
| Colorado's **statute of frauds**, **Uniform Power of Attorney Act**, **electronic transactions**, **recording**, **mechanics' lien**, **adverse possession**, **foreclosure and public trustee**, **water law**, **special districts**, **entity, trust and probate**, **unclaimed property**, **U.C.C.C.**, **property tax** | **No** |
| The **Colorado Fair Housing Act** | **No** |
| **RESPA, TILA, TRID, ECOA**, the **federal Fair Housing Act**, the **ADA**, **antitrust**, **ILSA**, the **TCPA**, the **UCC**, **federal securities law**, the **federal lead-based paint regulations**, **FIRPTA** | **No** |

**Twelve of those unread bodies are named by the Commission's own outlines**, which is why each course that
names one says so on its face rather than filling the gap with something plausible.

---

## B. Recognising when a question has left the rules

chunks.heading: B. Recognising when a question has left the rules
chunks.excerpt:
**A broker does not need to know the law to recognise a legal question.** These are the signals, and each
one appears somewhere in this build.

| Signal | Example from this build |
|---|---|
| **The question is about who owns something, or what an instrument does** | Survivorship on a deed; what a quitclaim conveys; whether a water right passed |
| **The question is about who may sign** | An entity, a trust, an estate, a power of attorney |
| **The question is about what happens on default** | An owner carry note; a foreclosure; a lease default |
| **The question is about a period, a notice or a procedure** | Adverse possession; eviction; interpleader; redemption |
| **Two parties disagree about money the broker holds** | An earnest money dispute |
| **The answer would change what someone signs** | Any of the above |

**In every one of those, the routing is the same** — and Colorado's own rules say so in three separate
places.

chunks.heading: C. The unauthorized practice of law
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 6.2.B** — a broker without the necessary experience, training and knowledge must **1. decline;
> 2. obtain** them; **3. obtain the assistance** of the employing broker, a supervisory broker, a competent
> broker **or legal counsel that is competent in the matter**; or **4. co-list.**
>
> **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V) and 12-10-405(1)(c)(V)** — a single agent must **advise the party to obtain expert
> advice** as to material matters known to the broker but whose specifics are **beyond the broker's
> expertise.**
>
> **§ 12-10-407(2)(b)(II)** — a transaction-broker must **advise the parties regarding the transaction and
> SUGGEST that the parties obtain expert advice** as to material matters known to the broker but beyond
> their expertise.
>
> **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)** — in any transaction where the broker completes a standard form, the broker
> *"**shall advise the parties that the forms have important legal consequences and that the parties should
> consult legal counsel before signing the forms.**"*

**Note the difference between the single agent and the transaction-broker formulations.** A single agent
**advises the party to obtain** expert advice. A transaction-broker **advises the parties regarding the
transaction and suggests** they obtain it. **Both are duties; neither authorises the broker to give the
advice.**

---

## C. The unauthorized practice of law

The **Current Legal Issues** outline names *"**Unauthorized Practice of Law concerns**"* at its topic area
3.11, and the **Contracts and Regulations** outline names the two decisions that settle the question in
Colorado at its Topic I.B.1 and I.B.2.

> **Neither decision was read by this project.** **No holding, limit or test from either is stated anywhere
> in this build.** **This is a submission gate.**

chunks.heading: D. What a broker does when the law changes
chunks.excerpt:
**What IS stated, because the provisions were read, is the statutory authority a broker actually has:**

> **§ 12-10-403(4)(a)** — a broker *"**whether acting as a single agent or transaction-broker, may COMPLETE
> STANDARD FORMS** for use in a real estate transaction"* when performing licensed activities.
>
> **§ 12-10-403(4)(b)** — **eight kinds** of standard form, of which the first is a **form promulgated by
> the Commission for current use.**
>
> **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)** — a broker **shall use a Commission-approved form when one exists and is
> appropriate**; use of a **client form** or a **government/lender form** is *"**limited to inserting
> transaction-specific information within the form**"*; for an **attorney form**, a **CBA form**, a
> **disclosure-only form**, a **title company form** or a **letter of intent**, the broker *"**may also
> advise the parties as to effects thereof**"*; and in every case the broker **shall advise the parties to
> consult legal counsel before signing.**
>
> **Rule 7.1.A** — of a Commission-approved form: *"The Broker **may advise the parties as to the effects
> thereof.**"*

**The line the statute draws is between completing a form and advising on its effects**, and it draws that
line **differently for different kinds of form.** A broker who knows which category a document falls into
knows what they may do with it — **and knows that drafting a new provision is in none of the categories.**

---

## D. What a broker does when the law changes

### D.1 Where change shows up

chunks.heading: D.2 The provider's own obligation, in the Commission's words
chunks.excerpt:
| Change | Where a broker sees it |
|---|---|
| **A rule amendment** | The **Secretary of State's CCR**, with the rulemaking docket behind it |
| **A statutory amendment** | The Colorado Revised Statutes; the Division's **legislative summaries** |
| **A new or revised Commission form** | The **Division's website** — **Rule 7.1.A** directs a broker there |
| **A new position statement** | The Division |
| **A decision construing any of the above** | The mandatory material Commission staff supplies for **this course** |

### D.2 The provider's own obligation, in the Commission's words

> **Practical Applications outline**: *"**COURSE PROVIDERS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR ENSURING THAT THE STATUTES,
> RULES AND POSITION STATEMENTS USED DURING THE COURSE PRESENTATION ARE ACCURATE AND UP-TO-DATE.**"*

**And the Commission's own audit power backs it.** **Rule 2.1.D**: the Commission *"**may audit courses ...
at any time and at no cost**"*, may request **all instructional materials and student attendance records**,
and *"**failure to comply with statutes and these Rules may result in the removal of the course provider,
instructor, and/or the course from the approved provider list.**"*

**This build states the rule version it read (12355) and the date it read it (2026-08-20)** in the readings
file and in every instructor source note, so that the currency question can be answered by a reviewer
rather than assumed.

### D.3 The broker's own obligation

**Rule 6.2.A** puts it as a competency requirement rather than a courtesy: a broker *"**must possess the
necessary experience, training, and knowledge to provide Real Estate Brokerage Services and MAINTAIN
COMPLIANCE WITH THE APPLICABLE FEDERAL, STATE AND LOCAL LAWS, RULES, REGULATIONS AND ORDINANCES.**"*

chunks.heading: E. What this module honestly leaves undone
chunks.excerpt:
**"Maintain compliance" is continuous.** A broker who was compliant with the rule as it stood is not
compliant with the rule as it stands, and **Rule 6.2.B's first route remains available**: **decline.**

---

## E. What this module honestly leaves undone

**Stated plainly, because the alternative is to imply a coverage this build does not have.**

| The outline asks for | This build delivers | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| **Recent and relevant federal case law** | Nothing — **no federal case was read** | **Open** |
| **Recent and relevant state case law** | Nothing — **no Colorado case was read**; two are named because an outline names them | **Open** |
| **Recent and relevant statutory law** | **C.R.S. §§ 12-10-203 and 12-10-402 to 12-10-411**, read in full; the rest of the map in Part A.2 | **Partly open** |
| **The mandatory items Commission staff specifies** | Nothing — **not received** | **Open, and RECURRING** |

**A course that named none of this and taught general principles instead would look more complete and be
less useful.** The Commission's own note tells providers where the content comes from; **this build says it
did not receive it.**

---

## Module 02 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline states no
examination requirement for this course, and **this build does not supply one the Commission did not
state.**

ground and no penalty is stated in this module.** The unread map in Part A.2 is a statement about this
build, not about the law.

lessons.title: Colorado Current Legal Issues — Module 03

chunks.heading: Colorado Current Legal Issues — Module 03
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Current Legal Issues — Module 03

## The representative areas, and the outline's appendices

**Course:** Current Legal Issues (8.0 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 2.0** of 8.0
**Commission outline topic:** **3 — "Other"**, and the outline's five appendices (the third of the outline's
three major topic areas)
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What the Commission's outline says about this topic area
>
> After naming its three major topic areas, the outline adds:
>
> > *"\* **In addition to the above prescribed areas which will be specified from time to time by the Real
> > Estate Commission, the following representative areas, among others, MAY, AS CLASSROOM TIME PERMITS, be
> > included:**"*
>
> and then lists **sixteen.** It closes with **five appendices.**
>
> **Read the qualifiers: "representative", "among others", "may", "as classroom time permits."** These are
> **not** mandatory content — the mandatory content is what Commission staff specifies, and **this project
> has not received it.** The sixteen are the Commission's illustration of the range this course can cover.
>
> **This module takes each of the sixteen, states what it concerns in one or two lines, and says where a
> Colorado answer comes from** — which for most of them is a statute **this build did not read.** That is
> the useful thing a student can be given: **a map of where the questions live**, rather than sixteen
> shallow accounts of law nobody here read.
>
> **The 2.0 hours is a StateCourse decision.** The outline states no hours for its topic areas.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: A. The sixteen representative areas
chunks.excerpt:
1. State what each of the sixteen representative areas concerns.
2. Identify, for each, whether this build read the governing Colorado law.
3. State the five appendices the outline names.
4. State what a broker does with a question in an area this course did not cover.

---

## A. The sixteen representative areas

**Each row states what the area concerns and where a Colorado answer comes from. "NOT READ" means this
project did not read the governing law, and therefore states none of it anywhere in this build.**

### 1. Brokerage relationships

**Delivered in full elsewhere in this build.** **§§ 12-10-402 to 12-10-411** were **read in full** and are
the subject of **Contracts and Regulations Module 02**. The transaction-broker default (§ 12-10-403(2)), the
dual agency prohibition (§ 12-10-406), designated brokerage (§ 12-10-403(6)), the three duty lists, the
disclosures, duration and compensation — all stated from primary text.

**Rules 6.5 through 6.9** supplement them and were read.

### 2. Licensing concerns — the broker and the real estate company

**Partly delivered.** **§ 12-10-203** and **Chapter 2 of 4 CCR 725-1** were **read**: the **168 hours**, the
**two-part examination**, the **one-year validity of a passing score**, the **fingerprint requirement**, and
the education waivers in **§ 12-10-203(4)(b) and (c)**.

**NOT READ:** **§§ 12-10-217, 12-10-219 and 12-10-222** — every **disciplinary ground, sanction, penalty and
procedure**; and the **insurance rules in Chapter 3** in detail, including every **errors and omissions**
requirement.

### 3. Real property law

chunks.heading: 4. Local government legal developments
chunks.excerpt:
The outline's own list under this head: *"annexation, condemnation, easements, landlord and tenant, lease,
financing, liens, foreclosures, unclaimed property, real estate contracts, remedies including damages and
specific performance, zoning, common interest ownership, various forms of ownership and entities, title
insurance and other evidence of ownership."*

**The general content is delivered** in **Real Estate Law and Practice** Modules 01, 03, 04 and 05.

**NOT READ, and stated nowhere:** Colorado's **condemnation** procedure; its **easement** and
**prescription** law; **§ 38-12-101 et seq.**, the **Landlord Tenant Act**; its **foreclosure statutes and
public trustee** system; its **unclaimed property** statute and the **Great Colorado Payback Program**; its
**statute of frauds**; its **mechanics' lien**, **recording** and **adverse possession** statutes; its
**zoning and land use** statutes and every local ordinance; **CCIOA (article 33.3 of title 38)**; its
**entity, trust and probate** statutes; and every **remedies** provision.

### 4. Local government legal developments

**Zoning, subdivision regulation, building codes, licensing, and local disclosure or transfer requirements
vary by jurisdiction.**

**NOT READ:** **no Colorado local ordinance of any jurisdiction was read**, and **no local requirement,
threshold, fee or procedure is stated anywhere in this build.**

### 5. Commercial law affecting real estate transactions (including sale and purchase of a business)

**The UCC**, secured transactions in personal property, bulk transfers, and the interaction between a
business sale and the real property it occupies.

**NOT READ:** the **UCC**; the **U.C.C.C.**, named separately by the **Contracts and Regulations** outline
at its Topic V.F.2.

chunks.heading: 6. Environmental law
chunks.excerpt:
**What WAS read and bears on it:** **§ 12-10-403(4)(a)** authorises a broker to complete standard forms
*"**including standard forms intended to convey personal property as part of the real estate
transaction**"*; **§ 12-10-201(6)** contains an exemption touching **licensed broker-dealers**.

### 6. Environmental law

Contamination, hazardous materials, asbestos, lead, radon, mould, underground storage tanks, and
methamphetamine contamination.

**NOT READ:** every **federal and Colorado environmental statute**, and the **federal lead-based paint
regulations** — which the outline names at its **Appendix E**.

**What WAS read:** the disclosure duties themselves. **§ 12-10-404(3)(a)**, **§ 12-10-405(3)(a)** and
**§ 12-10-407(2)(b)(VI)** each require disclosure of **adverse material facts ACTUALLY KNOWN**, expressly
including *"**any environmental hazards affecting the property that are required by law to be
disclosed**"* — and **§§ 12-10-404(3)(b), 12-10-405(5) and 12-10-407(4)** each provide there is **no duty to
inspect or verify.**

### 7. Business organizations and real estate

Corporations, limited liability companies, partnerships, trusts — **who may sign, and what authority they
hold.**

**NOT READ:** every Colorado **entity, trust and probate** statute, and the **Uniform Power of Attorney
Act**, named by the Contracts outline at Topic I.B.5.

chunks.heading: 8. Bankruptcy and real estate
chunks.excerpt:
**What WAS read:** **§ 12-10-203(6)** — a partnership, LLC or corporation applying for a licence must
**designate a qualified active broker** responsible for management and supervision, and **no licence issues
until that broker passes the examination on the entity's behalf**; **Rule 5.3.B** — a firm licensed as an
entity maintains trust accounts **in the entity's name**; and **Rules 5.10.D and 5.10.E** with the **20
percent** threshold in **§ 12-10-201(6)(b)(VII)**.

### 8. Bankruptcy and real estate

The effect of a bankruptcy filing on a pending transaction, a listing, a lease, or a lien.

**NOT READ:** the **federal Bankruptcy Code** and every provision of it. **No stay, deadline, procedure,
exemption or effect is stated anywhere in this build.**

**What a broker does:** a party in bankruptcy is a transaction that needs **counsel before anything else
happens**, and **Rule 6.2.B.1 — decline — is a legitimate answer** for a broker without the experience.

### 9. Intellectual property law and real estate transactions and business

Photographs, floor plans, listing copy, virtual tours, trademarks and trade names in advertising, and
database rights in listing data.

**NOT READ:** every **copyright, trademark and trade secret** statute.

**What WAS read and constrains advertising regardless:** **Rule 6.10 — Advertising** — and **Rule 1.2**,
which defines *"Advertise or Advertising"* to include *"business cards, brochures, websites, signage,
property flyers, mailings (paper or electronic), **social media**, letterhead, email signatures, and
contract documents."*

### 10. Taxation

**Real and personal property taxation; federal income and related taxes; sales, use and transfer taxes.**

chunks.heading: 11. Unauthorized practice of law concerns
chunks.excerpt:
**NOT READ:** Colorado's **property tax, assessment and levy** statutes; **every federal tax provision**;
and every **sales, use or transfer tax**.

**What this build states:** taxes are **prorated at closing on the convention the contract states**, using
figures the transaction supplies — **Closings** Modules 02, 03 and 05. **No rate, ratio, cycle or due date
is stated anywhere.** Tax questions go to the client's **accountant**, and **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V),
12-10-405(1)(c)(V) and 12-10-407(2)(b)(II)** make advising the party to obtain expert advice a duty.

### 11. Unauthorized practice of law concerns

**Delivered as far as this build can.** **§ 12-10-403(4)** and **Rule 7.1** were **read in full** and are
stated in **Contracts and Regulations Module 01 Part B.3** and **Current Legal Issues Module 02 Part C** —
the eight kinds of standard form, the requirement to use a Commission-approved form, the **advise-versus-
insert split**, and the duty to tell the parties to consult counsel.

**NOT READ:** the **Conway-Bogue decision** and **Colorado Bar Association v. The Title Guaranty Company**,
both named by the Contracts outline. **No holding from either is stated anywhere in this build.**

### 12. Legal issues involved with property management and appraisals

**Property management:** delivered from the rules that **were** read — **Rules 5.5, 5.7.A, 5.8, 5.10.D and
E, 5.11, 5.15, 6.17.C** — in **Real Estate Law and Practice Module 05** and the **Record Keeping and Trust
Accounts** course.

**NOT READ:** the **Landlord Tenant Act** and every deposit, notice, habitability and eviction provision.

chunks.heading: 13. Local legal issues
chunks.excerpt:
**Appraisals:** **Rule 6.12** was **read** and is delivered verbatim in **Real Estate Law and Practice
Module 02** — the required CMA/BPO notice, and the **prohibition** on CMAs or BPOs used to obtain
financing.

**NOT READ:** **§ 12-10-602**, the **Appraiser Licensing Act** named by the Contracts outline at Topic I.E,
and **USPAP**.

### 13. Local legal issues

**NOT READ:** as with area 4, **no Colorado local ordinance or local practice requirement was read**, and
none is stated anywhere in this build.

### 14. Legal issues involving Colorado Real Estate Commission approved contracts and other forms

**The largest gate in the whole Colorado build.**

**NO Commission-approved form was obtained, read or reproduced by this project.** **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)** and
**Rule 7.1.A** require a broker to **use a Commission-approved form when one exists and is appropriate**, and
the **Contracts and Regulations** outline requires students to **complete** one of each of **six** listing
and buyer brokerage families, one of each of **four** sales contract families, and one of each of the
**related forms.**

**This build states no form's contents, version, date, paragraph numbering or provisions**, and obtaining
the current forms from the Division's website is a submission gate recorded in the course engine.

### 15. Legal issues and closings

**Delivered from the rules that were read.** **Rule 6.19** in full — closing responsibility, the **signed**
closing statement, attendance or reasonable availability, joint responsibility of a substitute, and **Good
Funds**; **Rule 6.20** — **four-year** retention; **Rules 5.12 and 5.7.B** — earnest money.

chunks.heading: 16. Others
chunks.excerpt:
**NOT READ:** **RESPA**; the **non-resident seller withholding** statute and **FIRPTA**, both named by the
Closings outline at its Topic I.D; **C.R.S. § 38-35-125**, cited by Rule 6.19.E; and the **Commission's
Transaction File Checklist**, named by Rule 6.20.

### 16. Others

The outline's own examples: *"insurance and real estate; family and probate affecting real estate; mining,
oil and gas, water laws and public lands law; legal concerns related to technological developments and
practices such as facsimile transmissions, email, privacy and consent issues, wireless and cordless
telephonic communications, Internet, copyright issues, etc."*

**NOT READ:** every statute in that list — including Colorado's **water law**, named by **two** of the six
Commission outlines and identified in **Contracts and Regulations Module 05 Part E** as a gate this build
cannot responsibly leave open in a state where farm, ranch and vacant land brokerage is ordinary work.

**What WAS read and bears on the technology items:** **Rule 1.2's** definition of advertising, which
expressly reaches **websites, electronic mailings and social media**; **Rule 5.14.E**, permitting electronic
records; and **Rule 6.24**, on electronic records and production.

---

## B. The outline's five appendices

The outline ends by naming five appendices, and this build states what each is and whether it received it.

chunks.heading: C. What a broker does with a question in an area this course did not cover
chunks.excerpt:
| Appendix | What it is | Received? |
|---|---|---|
| **A: Disciplinary Actions** | The instructive proceedings from major topic area 1 | **No** — no Colorado disciplinary decision, stipulation, consent order or final agency order was read |
| **B: Complaints** | The complaints that generate them | **No** |
| **C: Audit Cases** | Trust account audit findings — the Record Keeping outline's *"repeated audit findings are subject to disciplinary action"* | **No** |
| **D: Other Issues** | As Commission staff specifies | **No** |
| **E: Lead Based Paint Disclosure** | The federal requirement for pre-1978 housing | **No** — the federal rule text was not read, and **no form, deadline, period, exemption or penalty from it is stated anywhere in this build** |

**All five come from the material Commission staff supplies to authorized providers**, and **this project
has received none of it.** That is the gate stated at the top of Module 01, and it recurs every time the
Commission issues new material.

---

## C. What a broker does with a question in an area this course did not cover

**The same three things, every time, and all three are in rules this build read in full.**

chunks.heading: Module 03 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
> **1. Recognise it.** Module 02 Part B lists the signals: ownership, authority to sign, default, a period
> or procedure, a dispute over money the broker holds, or anything that would change what someone signs.
>
> **2. Route it.** **Rule 6.2.B** — **decline**; **obtain** the experience, training and knowledge; **obtain
> the assistance** of the employing broker, a supervisory broker, a competent broker **or legal counsel
> competent in the matter**; or **co-list.**
>
> **3. Tell the party to get advice.** **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V) and 12-10-405(1)(c)(V)** — **advise the party
> to obtain expert advice** as to material matters beyond the broker's expertise. **§ 12-10-407(2)(b)(II)**
> — for a transaction-broker, **advise the parties and suggest they obtain expert advice.**
> **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)** — on any standard form, **advise the parties that the forms have important legal
> consequences and that they should consult legal counsel before signing.**

**And the continuing obligation underneath all of it:** **Rule 6.2.A** — a broker **must possess the
necessary experience, training and knowledge** to provide the service and to **maintain compliance with the
applicable federal, state and local laws, rules, regulations and ordinances.**

---

## Module 03 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline states no
examination requirement for this course, and **this build does not supply one the Commission did not
state.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 03
chunks.excerpt:
This module completes the Commission's **Current Legal Issues** outline as this build can deliver it:
**3.0 + 3.0 + 2.0 = 8.0 hours**, against the outline's heading of **8.1** — a discrepancy recorded in
Module 01 and left open for the Division.

---

## Instructor source note for Module 03

Written to the **Commission's Current Legal Issues qualifying education outline, approved July 2, 1996**,
major topic area 3 and its five appendices, using **the outline's own sixteen representative areas in the
outline's own order and its own wording.** **The outline states no hours for its topic areas; the 2.0 hours
for this module is a StateCourse decision** and is labelled as one.

Every provision cited as read — **§§ 12-10-201(6)(b)(VII), 12-10-203, 12-10-402 to 12-10-411**, and **Rules
1.2, 5.3, 5.5, 5.7, 5.8, 5.10, 5.11, 5.12, 5.14.E, 5.15, 6.2, 6.10, 6.12, 6.17.C, 6.19, 6.20, 6.24 and
7.1** — is transcribed from **C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10** and **4 CCR 725-1** (rule version 12355), read on
**2026-08-20** and recorded in `colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Everything marked NOT READ in this module is not read, and is the source of nothing anywhere in this
build.** The five appendices were **not received**, and their content is stated nowhere.

**No case holding, position statement, disciplinary ground, sanction, penalty, form provision, local
ordinance, tax figure, environmental standard, bankruptcy effect, intellectual property rule, water law
rule or lead-based paint requirement is stated in this module.**

lessons.title: Colorado Closings — Module 01

chunks.heading: Colorado Closings — Module 01
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Closings — Module 01

## The broker's responsibility relating to closing

**Course:** Closings (24 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 1.0** of 24.0
**Commission outline topic:** **I — Broker's Responsibility Relating to Closing**, allocated **1.0 hour**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What this course is
>
> **C.R.S. § 12-10-203(4)(a)(III)(B)** names **real estate closings** as one of the four subjects making up
> the statutory **72 hours**. **Rule 2.1.A.2.c** fixes the floor: *"Real Estate Closings: **not less than 24
> hours**."*
>
> **This is the second course an out-of-state broker cannot escape.** **§ 12-10-203(4)(b)** relieves a
> broker licensed in another jurisdiction of everything **except** the **Contracts** course and **this
> one.**
>
> **The Commission approved its outline on June 6, 1996**, and its objective is unusually specific: *"To
> protect the public by students **exhibiting the basic skills necessary to properly close a real estate
> transaction**, including responsibilities **from the contract through and after the closing**, plus
> **accounting for all funds received and disbursed** as well as a **comprehensive review of the legal
> documents prepared by the broker.**"*
>
> | Module | Commission topic | Hours |
> |---|---|---|
> | **01** | I. Broker's Responsibility Relating to Closing | **1.0** |
> | 02 | II. Introduction to a 6-Column Worksheet | 2.0 |
> | 03 | III. Closing to a Prepared Contract | 4.0 |
> | 04 | IV. Legal Documents | 1.0 |
> | 05 | **V. Preparation of a Minimum of 8 Closing Problems** | **16.0** |
> | | **TOTAL** | **24.0** |
>
> **Two-thirds of this course is the eight problems.** A Closings

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
course delivered as lecture has not been
> delivered, and the course engine records each of the eight separately.
>
> The outline's own testing requirement, in its own capitals: *"**ALL STUDENTS MUST SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETE A
> WRITTEN EXAMINATION COVERING ALL MAJOR TOPIC AREAS OF THIS OUTLINE.**"*

## Learning objectives

1. Distinguish a broker prepared closing from a title company prepared closing.
2. State Rule 6.19's allocation of closing responsibility and who signs the closing statement.
3. State what a broker must do if unavailable to attend closing.
4. State the Good Funds rule in Rule 6.19.E and what it prohibits.
5. State what the Commission's outline names about RESPA and withholding, and identify both as unread.
6. State the individual responsibility of the licensee holding the listing or buyer brokerage agreement.

---

## A. Who closes, and who is responsible — outline Topic I.A

The Commission's outline distinguishes three things at I.A, and Colorado's rule allocates responsibility
across all of them.

| Outline sub-item | What it is |
|---|---|
| **A.1 Broker prepared closing** | The broker prepares the closing documents and closing statements and conducts the closing |
| **A.2 Title company prepared closing** | A title company or other closing entity prepares and conducts it |
| **A.3 Individual responsibility of licensee holding listing or buyer brokerage agreement** | The duty that attaches to the broker with the **brokerage relationship**, whoever conducts the closing |

**Rule 6.19 was read in full and it settles all three.** It is the operative rule of this entire course.

### A.1 The core allocation — Rule 6.19.A

chunks.heading: A.2 Broker prepared closings — Rule 6.19.B
chunks.excerpt:
> *"Pursuant to section 12-10-217(1)(j), C.R.S, **at the time of closing, the Broker who has established a
> Brokerage Relationship with one or multiple Consumers in a transaction WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE PROPER
> CLOSING OF THE TRANSACTION.** The Broker **must ensure such Consumer receives an ACCURATE, COMPLETE AND
> DETAILED closing statement THAT IS SIGNED BY THE BROKER.** If Broker is licensed with a Brokerage Firm,
> Broker **must deliver closing statements to the Brokerage Firm along with any other closing documents,
> IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING CLOSING.** Nothing in this Rule **relieves an Employing Broker of the responsibility
> for fulfilling supervisory responsibilities** pursuant to sections 12-10-203(5)(c)(I), 12-10-217(1)(r),
> and 12-10-222, C.R.S."*

**Four separate requirements in one paragraph, and this is the outline's Topic I.A.3 in the rule's own
words:**

1. **The broker with the brokerage relationship is responsible for the proper closing** — **whoever
   conducts it.** Handing the file to a title company does not transfer this.
2. **The consumer must receive a closing statement that is accurate, complete and detailed — and SIGNED BY
   THE BROKER.**
3. **The closing statements and other closing documents go to the brokerage firm IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING
   CLOSING.**
4. **The employing broker's supervisory responsibility is untouched.**

**Point 2 is the one new brokers do not expect.** The closing statement carries **the broker's own
signature**, and a broker who signs an inaccurate one has certified it.

### A.2 Broker prepared closings — Rule 6.19.B

chunks.heading: A.3 Attendance, and the substitute — Rule 6.19.C
chunks.excerpt:
> *"If closing documents and closing statements are **prepared and closed by a Broker**, the Broker is
> **responsible for the ACCURACY and COMPLETENESS of the closing statements and closing documents.**"*

**A heavier standard than 6.19.A, and it applies when the broker does the work.** Modules 02 through 05
build the skill this rule presupposes.

### A.3 Attendance, and the substitute — Rule 6.19.C

> *"If a Broker has a Brokerage Relationship with a Consumer in a transaction, the Broker **must review
> closing documents AND attend closing OR BE REASONABLY AVAILABLE.** If a Broker will not be available to
> attend closing and review closing documents, **another Broker designated by the Brokerage Firm may review
> and attend closing on the Broker's behalf** and **will assume JOINT RESPONSIBILITY with the absent Broker**
> for its accuracy, completeness, and delivery of the signed closing statement."*

**"Attend closing or be reasonably available" is a real alternative**, and *"reasonably available"* is not
defined by the rule. **This course supplies no definition**, because the rule states none.

**The substitute takes on joint responsibility, and does not relieve the absent broker.** Both are
responsible.

### A.4 Earnest money at closing — Rule 6.19.D

> *"**Any Broker receiving earnest money must deliver earnest money as set forth in Rule 5.12.A.**"*

**Rule 5.12.A**: deliver it **to the earnest money holder to be deposited in accordance with the
contract**, and **obtain a dated and signed receipt** from the person or entity instructed to receive it.

---

## B. Real Estate Commission statutes and rules — outline Topic I.B

The rules a broker works inside at closing, all read in full for this build.

chunks.heading: B. Real Estate Commission statutes and rules — outline Topic I.B
chunks.excerpt:
| Rule | What it requires at closing |
|---|---|
| **6.19** | Responsibility, the signed closing statement, attendance, and Good Funds — Parts A and D of this module |
| **6.20** | **Transaction files retained FOUR YEARS** from consummation or from a non-consummating listing's expiration |
| **5.12** | Earnest money delivered to the holder per the contract, **with a dated and signed receipt** |
| **5.7.B** | If the firm holds it: deposited **no later than three business days** following receipt or mutual execution, whichever is later |
| **5.14** | The **journal**, the **ledger** with **no negative balance ever**, and **monthly three-way reconciliation** |
| **5.10.C** | Commissions are *"earned"* and available to the firm **only after all contracted services have been performed and there is no remaining right of recall** |
| **5.17** | **Prior written consent** for any **mark-up** the broker assesses or receives, and disclosure of mark-ups paid by any customer |
| **§ 12-10-410(6)** | The **identity of anyone paying compensation** disclosed **before** the brokerage agreement or the contract is entered into |
| **6.21.A** | **No referral fee except in accordance with RESPA** and unless a **reasonable cause** exists under § 12-10-304(1) |

**Rule 6.20's four years runs from two possible dates** — **consummation** for a transaction that closes,
and **the listing contract's expiration** for one that does not. And the rule expressly does **not** require
a broker to obtain and retain **existing public records, title commitments, loan applications, lender
required disclosures, or related affirmations from independent third party closing entities after the
closing date.**

chunks.heading: C. RESPA — outline Topic I.C
chunks.excerpt:
**The Commission's Transaction File Checklist, which Rule 6.20 says designates the required documents, was
NOT obtained by this project**, and **no module of this build states what it lists.** That is a submission
gate.

---

## C. RESPA — outline Topic I.C

The Commission's outline names the **Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act** at Topic I.C.

**What it is, in general terms:** the federal statute governing **settlement services** on covered
residential transactions — the disclosures required, the prohibition on **kickbacks and unearned fees**, and
limits on **required use** of affiliated providers.

> **The RESPA text was NOT read by this project.** **No RESPA disclosure, form, timing requirement, dollar
> threshold, exemption, tolerance or penalty is stated anywhere in this build.**
>
> **What WAS read is Colorado's rule about it.** **Rule 6.21.A**: *"Brokers and Brokerage Firms **will not
> pay or receive a referral fee except in accordance with RESPA** and unless a **reasonable cause for
> payment of the referral fee exists** pursuant to section 12-10-304(1), C.R.S."* — and **§ 12-10-304 was
> not read either.**
>
> **Rule 6.18** requires **affiliated business arrangement disclosures**; its statutory basis,
> **§ 12-10-218**, was **not read**, and **Rule 1.3** defines the term by reference to it.
>
> **This is a submission gate.** A Closings course that teaches RESPA must read it.

---

## D. Withholding — outline Topic I.D

The Commission's outline names two withholding regimes:

chunks.heading: E. Good Funds — outline Topic I.E, and Rule 6.19.E
chunks.excerpt:
| Outline sub-item | What it concerns |
|---|---|
| **D.1 Non-resident seller** | Withholding from the proceeds of a seller who is not a Colorado resident |
| **D.2 Foreign Investor Real Property Tax Act** | Federal withholding on dispositions of U.S. real property by foreign persons |

> **NEITHER statute was read by this project.** **No withholding rate, threshold, exemption, certificate,
> form, filing deadline or remittance requirement is stated anywhere in this build.**
>
> **What this module states is the practical point that does not depend on the figures:** withholding is
> **taken out of the seller's proceeds at closing**, so a seller who learns of it at the closing table
> learns of it too late. **A broker who knows the seller is a non-resident or a foreign person raises it
> early and routes it to the closing entity, the seller's accountant and counsel** —
> **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V) and 12-10-407(2)(b)(II)** each require advising the party to obtain expert advice
> on material matters beyond the broker's expertise, and this is one.
>
> **This is a submission gate.**

---

## E. Good Funds — outline Topic I.E, and Rule 6.19.E

The outline names **Good Funds** at Topic I.E, and the rule was read in full.

chunks.heading: E. Good Funds — outline Topic I.E, and Rule 6.19.E
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 6.19.E**: *"Pursuant to section **38-35-125, C.R.S**, a Broker or a Brokerage Firm **MUST NOT
> DISBURSE OR AUTHORIZE DISBURSEMENT OF FUNDS UNTIL THOSE FUNDS HAVE BEEN RECEIVED** and are either:*
> **1.** *"**Available for immediate withdrawal AS A MATTER OF RIGHT** from the financial institution in
> which the funds have been deposited; or*
> **2.** *"**Available for immediate withdrawal as a consequence of an agreement** with a financial
> institution in which the funds are to be deposited or a financial institution upon which the funds are to
> be drawn. **The agreement ... must be for the benefit of the Broker and Brokerage Firm providing the
> closing service. If the agreement contains contingencies or reservations, NO DISBURSEMENTS CAN BE MADE
> until these are satisfied.**"*

**Read what the rule prohibits: disbursing OR AUTHORIZING disbursement before the funds are both received
and available.** A broker who releases funds against a deposit that has not cleared, or against an
agreement whose contingencies are unsatisfied, has breached it.

**"As a matter of right" in paragraph 1** means the broker can withdraw the money now, not that the bank
will probably honour it.

**§ 38-35-125 itself was NOT read by this project.** This module states **only what Rule 6.19.E says**, in
the rule's own words, and **states no definition of good funds, no clearing period, and no list of
acceptable instruments from the statute.**

chunks.heading: F. The shape of the rest of this course
chunks.excerpt:
**The Record Keeping and Trust Accounts outline names Good Funds at its Topic III.B.4** and lists the
arrangements a broker meets in practice: **cashier's or teller's check; broker check in advance of closing;
wire transfer; tri-party agreements (broker–title company–broker's bank); netting earned commission against
earnest money deposit; and the requirements of the Great Colorado Payback Program for unclaimed funds.**
That course delivers them.

---

## F. The shape of the rest of this course

| Module | What the student does |
|---|---|
| **02** | Learns the **six-column worksheet** — the instrument every closing problem is worked on |
| **03** | Works a closing **to a prepared contract**, reads a **sample title commitment**, and calculates costs, prorations, prepaids and cash due to or from each party |
| **04** | Reviews the **legal documents**, the **title commitment as it relates to them**, and **transaction file retention** |
| **05** | Prepares the **minimum of eight closing problems** the Commission requires — *"using a mix of **cash, owner carry, assumptions (FHA, VA and conventional), new loans (FHA, VA and conventional), and a closing involving a multi-family property. THREE PROBLEMS SHALL BE USING SAMPLES OF PREPARED CONTRACTS.**"* |

the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that

lessons.title: Colorado Closings — Module 02

chunks.heading: Colorado Closings — Module 02
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Closings — Module 02

## Introduction to a six-column worksheet

**Course:** Closings (24 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 2.0** of 24.0
**Commission outline topic:** **II — Introduction to a 6-Column Worksheet**, allocated **2.0 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### Why the Commission gives this its own topic
>
> The **six-column worksheet** is the instrument on which every closing problem in Module 05 is worked, and
> the Commission names it twice across its six outlines:
>
> - **Closings outline, Topic II** — *"Introduction to a 6-column worksheet"*, **2.0 hours**;
> - **Record Keeping and Trust Accounts outline, Topic II.B.4.a** — *"Working from a sample contract and
>   **6-column settlement worksheet**, student shall create journal and ledger entries leading to the
>   closing of a real estate sale by a broker."*
>
> **The same worksheet, used twice, for two different purposes.** Here it produces the closing figures.
> There it feeds the brokerage's own trust accounting. **A student who does not have the worksheet cold
> cannot do either.**
>
> **No Commission form, template or worksheet was obtained by this project.** This module teaches **the
> structure and the arithmetic**, which are the same whatever form the columns are printed on, and states
> **no form's layout, column headings, line numbering or version.**

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: A. The structure
chunks.excerpt:
1. Name the six columns and say what each accumulates.
2. State the meaning of debit and credit for each of the buyer and the seller.
3. Place any ordinary closing item in the right column with the right sign.
4. State the balancing identity the worksheet must satisfy.
5. Distinguish an item that is prorated from one that is a single-party charge.
6. Compute cash due from the buyer and cash due to the seller from a completed worksheet.

---

## A. The structure

The worksheet arranges every item of a transaction across **three pairs of columns** — a **debit** and a
**credit** column for each of three accounts.

| Pair | Columns | What it accumulates |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Buyer debit** / **Buyer credit** | Everything the buyer owes and everything the buyer is credited with |
| **2** | **Seller debit** / **Seller credit** | Everything charged to and credited to the seller |
| **3** | **Broker (or settlement) debit** / **Broker credit** | The money actually passing through the broker's or closing entity's hands |

**Six columns.** The third pair is what makes this a **broker's** worksheet rather than a settlement
statement: it tracks **the funds the broker receives and disburses**, which is exactly what **Rule 5.14**
requires the **journal** and **ledger** to record.

---

## B. Debit and credit, said in one sentence each

> **A DEBIT is what a party PAYS or is CHARGED. A CREDIT is what a party RECEIVES or is credited toward what
> they owe.**

Applied to the two parties:

| | Buyer | Seller |
|---|---|---|
| **Debit means** | The buyer must bring this money | This is charged against the seller's proceeds |
| **Credit means** | This reduces what the buyer must bring | This increases the seller's proceeds |

chunks.heading: C. Placing the ordinary items
chunks.excerpt:
**The purchase price is the anchor, and it is the one item every student places correctly:**

| Item | Buyer | Seller |
|---|---|---|
| **Purchase price** | **Debit** — the buyer owes it | **Credit** — the seller is owed it |

Everything else follows from asking two questions in order: **who bears this cost**, and **has it already
been paid?**

---

## C. Placing the ordinary items

| Item | Buyer | Seller | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Purchase price** | Debit | Credit | The anchor |
| **Earnest money already paid** | **Credit** | — | The buyer has already put it up; it reduces what they bring |
| **New loan proceeds** | **Credit** | — | The lender is funding part of what the buyer owes |
| **Loan assumed by the buyer** | **Credit** | **Debit** | The buyer takes on the debt; the seller is relieved of it |
| **Seller carry note taken back** | **Credit** | **Debit** | The same logic — the seller is financing part of the price |
| **Existing loan to be paid off** | — | **Debit** | Paid from the seller's proceeds |
| **Broker's compensation** | Per contract | Usually **Debit** | Whoever the contract says pays it |
| **Buyer's loan costs** | **Debit** | — | Origination, points, appraisal, credit |
| **Prepaid interest on the new loan** | **Debit** | — | Funding date to the end of the month |
| **Taxes paid in advance by the seller** | **Debit** | **Credit** | The buyer reimburses the unused part |
| **Taxes payable in arrears** | **Credit** | **Debit** | The seller owes their share; the buyer will pay the bill |
| **Rents collected by the seller for the current period** | **Credit** | **Debit** | The buyer owns the days after closing |
| **Security deposits held** | **Credit** | **Debit** | They belong to tenants and must travel to the buyer |
| **HOA assessments paid in ad

chunks.heading: D. The balancing identity
chunks.excerpt:
vance** | **Debit** | **Credit** | Same logic as prepaid taxes |
| **Title insurance premium** | Per contract | Per contract | Whoever the contract says |
| **Recording fees** | Usually **Debit** | Sometimes **Debit** | Deed vs. release |
| **Repairs the seller agreed to pay** | — | **Debit** | Only if the contract or an amendment says so |

**The last row is the discipline of the whole course**, and the Commission's outline states it at Topic
III.A.1 in six words: ***"Close to contract or amend contract in writing."*** A charge that is not in the
contract or in a written amendment does not belong on the worksheet.

**Two items students place backwards more than any others:**

**Security deposits.** They are **not** the seller's money and **not** the buyer's — they belong to the
tenants. They are **debited to the seller and credited to the buyer** because the buyer will have to return
them. And in Colorado, if a brokerage is holding them, **Rule 5.5** requires them in a **separate trust or
escrow account** from rental receipts, and **Rule 5.8** governs their transfer.

**Rents.** The seller has collected the whole month; the buyer owns the days from closing forward. So the
**buyer is credited** and the **seller debited** with the buyer's share.

---

## D. The balancing identity

**A completed worksheet must balance in two ways at once.**

> **1. Each party's own columns settle to a single figure.**
>
> **Buyer:** total debits − total credits = **cash the buyer must bring** (or, if credits exceed debits,
> cash back to the buyer).
>
> **Seller:** total credits − total debits = **cash the seller receives** (or, if debits exceed credits,
> cash the seller must bring).

chunks.heading: E. A worked worksheet
chunks.excerpt:
> **2. The money in equals the money out.**
>
> Everything received at closing — the buyer's cash, the earnest money, the loan proceeds — must equal
> everything disbursed: the payoff, the compensation, the fees, and the seller's proceeds.
>
> **This is the third column pair**, and it is the one that ties the closing to **Rule 5.14**: *"**The sum
> of all ledger balances must agree AT ALL TIMES with the corresponding journal after each transaction has
> been posted**"*, with **three-way reconciliation performed monthly** to show that the journal balance, the
> sum of the ledger balances, and the reconciled bank balance are the same.
>
> **The Record Keeping and Trust Accounts outline states the identity in its own notation** at Topic II.B.3:
> ***"Journal Balance + Sum of Ledger Balances = Bank Balance = Transaction File Liabilities."***

**A worksheet that does not balance has an error, not a rounding difference.** Find it before the closing,
because **Rule 6.19.A** requires the consumer to receive a closing statement that is **accurate, complete
and detailed — and signed by the broker**, and **Rule 6.19.B** makes a broker who prepares the documents
responsible for their **accuracy and completeness.**

---

## E. A worked worksheet

**Every figure below is supplied as a given.**

chunks.heading: E. A worked worksheet
chunks.excerpt:
> **The transaction.** Price **$480,000**. Earnest money of **$10,000** already paid and held by the
> brokerage. The buyer obtains a **new loan of $384,000**. The seller's existing loan payoff is
> **$212,400**. Compensation of **6 percent of the price**, charged to the seller. Buyer's loan costs
> **$4,200**. Title insurance premium **$1,850**, charged to the seller. Recording fees **$180** to the
> buyer and **$40** to the seller. Annual property taxes of **$4,320** are payable **in arrears**; closing
> is **1 September** on a **360-day year with 30-day months**, and the **seller** is charged through the day
> before closing.

**Step 1 — the tax proration.** Daily rate **$4,320 ÷ 360 = $12.00**. The seller held **240 days**
(January through August, 8 × 30). **Seller's share = 240 × $12.00 = $2,880**, and because the taxes are
**in arrears** the buyer will pay the bill — so it is a **credit to the buyer** and a **debit to the
seller.**

**Step 2 — the worksheet.**

| Item | Buyer debit | Buyer credit | Seller debit | Seller credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Purchase price | **480,000.00** | | | **480,000.00** |
| Earnest money | | **10,000.00** | | |
| New loan proceeds | | **384,000.00** | | |
| Existing loan payoff | | | **212,400.00** | |
| Compensation (6% of 480,000) | | | **28,800.00** | |
| Buyer's loan costs | **4,200.00** | | | |
| Title insurance premium | | | **1,850.00** | |
| Recording fees | **180.00** | | **40.00** | |
| Tax proration (240 days, in arrears) | | **2,880.00** | **2,880.00** | |
| **TOTALS** | **484,380.00** | **396,880.00** | **245,970.00** | **480,000.00** |

**Step 3 — the two settlement figures.**

chunks.heading: F. What the worksheet does NOT decide
chunks.excerpt:
> **Cash the buyer must bring = 484,380.00 − 396,880.00 = $87,500.00**
>
> **Cash the seller receives = 480,000.00 − 245,970.00 = $234,030.00**

**Step 4 — prove the money.**

| Received at closing | | Disbursed at closing | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Buyer's cash | 87,500.00 | Existing loan payoff | 212,400.00 |
| Earnest money | 10,000.00 | Compensation | 28,800.00 |
| New loan proceeds | 384,000.00 | Title insurance premium | 1,850.00 |
| | | Recording fees (180 + 40) | 220.00 |
| | | Buyer's loan costs | 4,200.00 |
| | | Seller's proceeds | 234,030.00 |
| **TOTAL IN** | **481,500.00** | **TOTAL OUT** | **481,500.00** |

**In equals out.** That third pair of columns is the proof, and it is the figure the brokerage's **journal**
must show.

---

## F. What the worksheet does NOT decide

**It does not decide who pays what.** The **contract** does. The worksheet records the contract's
allocation; it does not create one.

**It does not decide the proration convention.** The contract states it, and **this course prescribes
none** — a 360-day year with 30-day months and a 365-day year with actual days are both in use, and
**whether the day of closing is charged to the buyer or the seller is likewise the contract's.**

**It does not decide Colorado property tax timing.** **No Colorado property tax statute, assessment ratio,
mill levy, due date or billing cycle was read by this project**, and **none is stated anywhere in this
build.** Whether taxes in a given transaction are prepaid or in arrears, and for what period, comes from
**the tax records and the closing entity**, not from this course.

chunks.heading: Module 02 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**And it does not disburse anything.** **Rule 6.19.E** — the Good Funds rule from Module 01 — prohibits a
broker or firm from **disbursing or authorizing disbursement until the funds have been received and are
available for immediate withdrawal.** A balanced worksheet is not money in the account.

---

## Module 02 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
**all students successfully complete a written examination covering all major topic areas**, and **these
items are not that examination.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 02

Written to the **Commission's Closings qualifying education outline, approved June 6, 1996**, Topic II. The
hour figure is the Commission's. The cross-reference to the **Record Keeping and Trust Accounts** outline
Topic II.B.3 and II.B.4.a is to that Commission outline, read the same day.

**Rules 5.5, 5.8, 5.14, 6.19.A, 6.19.B and 6.19.E** are transcribed from **4 CCR 725-1**, read on
2026-08-20 and recorded in `colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** any **Commission form, worksheet or settlement
statement template**; Colorado's **property tax, assessment and levy** statutes; **RESPA** and the federal
settlement disclosure forms; **C.R.S. § 38-35-125**; and the **Commission's Transaction File Checklist.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 02
chunks.excerpt:
**No form layout, column heading, line number, tax rate, assessment ratio, billing cycle, proration
convention or fee is stated in this module.** Every figure in the worked worksheet is supplied inside the
problem as a given, and the arithmetic is shown in full so a reviewer can check it.

lessons.title: Colorado Closings — Module 03

chunks.heading: Colorado Closings — Module 03
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Closings — Module 03

## Closing to a prepared contract

**Course:** Closings (24 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 4.0** of 24.0
**Commission outline topic:** **III — Closing to a Prepared Contract**, allocated **4.0 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What the Commission's outline puts in this topic
>
> | Sub-topic | Delivered in |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** Interpreting the prepared contract — **1. Close to contract or amend contract in writing; 2. Non-contractual fees and costs** | Part A |
> | **B.** Reading and understanding a **sample title commitment** | Part B |
> | **C.** **Accurately calculating closing costs, prorations, prepaid and cash due to/from buyers and sellers at closing** | Parts C and D |
>
> **Four hours, and Topic III.A.1 is the sentence the whole course turns on:**
>
> ***"Close to contract or amend contract in writing."***
>
> **Three problems in Module 05 must use samples of prepared contracts**, and this is where the student
> learns to read one.

## Learning objectives

1. State the rule in Topic III.A.1 and apply it to a charge nobody agreed to.
2. Identify a non-contractual fee and say what a broker does about one.
3. Read a title commitment's four schedules and say what each does.
4. Identify what on a commitment must be cleared before closing.
5. Calculate a proration on a stated convention, in either direction.
6. Calculate prepaid interest, and distinguish it from a proration.
7. Compute cash due from the buyer and cash to the seller and prove the total.

---

## A. Interpreting the prepared contract

### A.1 "Close to contract or amend contract in writing"

chunks.heading: A.2 Non-contractual fees and costs — Topic III.A.2
chunks.excerpt:
**The contract is the instruction sheet, and the closing follows it.** If the parties want something
different from what the contract says, **the contract changes first, in writing** — and the instrument is
the **Agreement to Amend/Extend Contract**, named at the **Contracts and Regulations** outline's Topic
IV.B.2.

**Where this bites, in order of how often it happens:**

| Situation | The rule's answer |
|---|---|
| A repair the seller said they would make, not in the contract | **Amend, or it is not a closing charge** |
| A credit the parties agreed on the phone | **Amend** |
| A cost allocated differently from the contract | **Amend** |
| A date moved | **Amend** |
| A party wants something added at the closing table | **Amend, and everyone signs** |

**Why it matters beyond tidiness.** A closing statement carrying a charge no contract supports is not
**accurate**, and **Rule 6.19.A** requires the consumer to receive a closing statement that is *"**accurate,
complete and detailed ... SIGNED BY THE BROKER.**"* **Rule 6.19.B** makes a broker who prepares the
documents responsible for their **accuracy and completeness.** The broker signs it.

**And a side agreement kept off the statement is the loan fraud problem** the **Contracts and Regulations**
outline names at its Topic V.F.4: a payment, credit or allowance agreed between the parties and not
disclosed to the lender. **Everything the parties agreed goes into the contract or an amendment, and what
is in the contract appears on the statement.**

### A.2 Non-contractual fees and costs — Topic III.A.2

chunks.heading: A.2 Non-contractual fees and costs — Topic III.A.2
chunks.excerpt:
**A non-contractual fee is a charge that arises at closing but is not allocated by the contract** — a
lender's late-appearing fee, a closing entity's administrative charge, a payoff statement fee, a wire fee,
a courier charge, an HOA transfer or status letter fee.

**Three questions, in order:**

1. **Is it real?** Someone is charging for something. What?
2. **Does the contract allocate it?** If it does, it is contractual and it goes where the contract says.
3. **If not, who is going to pay it, and have they agreed?**

**A charge nobody agreed to does not become agreed by appearing on a statement.** The broker raises it
**before** the closing, and if the parties resolve it differently from the contract, the answer is A.1 —
**amend in writing.**

> **Two Colorado rules bear directly on charges the broker themselves assesses or receives, and both were
> read.**
>
> **Rule 5.17 — Mark-Ups.** The broker and firm *"**must obtain PRIOR WRITTEN CONSENT from the Consumer they
> represent to assess and receive mark-ups and/or other compensation for services performed, regardless if
> for the benefit of the Broker or another third party.**"* They must also **disclose all mark-ups paid for
> by any Customer**, and **retain accurate on-going records** verifying disclosure and consent and fully
> accounting for the amounts.
>
> **§ 12-10-410(6).** *"**Prior to entering into a brokerage or listing agreement or a contract to buy,
> sell, or lease, the identity of those parties, persons, or entities paying compensation or commissions to
> any broker shall be disclosed to the parties to the transaction.**"*
>
> And **Rule 6.21.A**: **no referral fee except in accordance with RESPA** and unless a **reasonable cause**
> exists under **§ 12-10-304(1)**. **Neither RESPA nor § 12-10-304 was

chunks.heading: B. Reading a title commitment
chunks.excerpt:
read**, and neither is stated here.

---

## B. Reading a title commitment

The outline requires the student to read and understand a **sample title commitment** at Topic III.B.

**A commitment is the title company's undertaking to issue a policy on stated terms.** It is arranged in
schedules, and each does a different job.

| Schedule | What it contains | What the broker looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **Schedule A** | The **commitment date**; the **policy or policies** to be issued and the **amounts**; the **estate** covered; **who currently holds title**; and the **legal description** | Does the vested owner match the seller on the contract? Does the description match the property? Is the policy amount right? |
| **Schedule B-1** | **Requirements** — what must be **done** before the policy issues | Every item here is a task with an owner and a deadline |
| **Schedule B-2** | **Exceptions** — what the policy will **NOT** cover | Every item here is a risk the buyer takes unless it is removed |
| **Schedule C / notes** | Further matters, as the company arranges its commitment | Read them |

**The two schedules that matter to a broker are B-1 and B-2, and they matter for opposite reasons.**

**Schedule B-1 is a to-do list.** Payoff and release of an existing deed of trust; satisfaction of a
judgment; a corporate resolution or trustee's certificate; a death certificate; a survey or ILC; an
executed deed. **Each item needs someone assigned to it and a date**, and an item nobody owns is the item
that stops the closing.

**Schedule B-2 is what the buyer is taking subject to.** Easements, restrictive covenants, mineral
reservations, special district obligations, the standard printed exceptions. **A buyer who has not read
Schedule B-2 does not know what they are buying.**

chunks.heading: C. Calculating: prorations
chunks.excerpt:
**What the broker does and does not do with it.**

> **Does:** deliver it promptly; make sure the **buyer knows the objection deadline the contract set**;
> make sure each **B-1 requirement is assigned**; and raise anything that does not match the contract.
>
> **Does not:** opine on the legal effect of an exception, advise whether a title defect is material, or
> tell a party whether to object. **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V), 12-10-405(1)(c)(V) and 12-10-407(2)(b)(II)**
> each require **advising the party to obtain expert advice** as to material matters beyond the broker's
> expertise, and **Rule 6.2** requires the broker to possess the necessary experience, training and
> knowledge — or **decline**, **obtain** them, **obtain the assistance** of a competent broker or **legal
> counsel competent in the matter**, or **co-list.**

**And the title objection deadline is a contingency**, so the three-part test from the Contracts course
applies: **what event, by when, what happens if it does not occur.**

**Rule 6.20** expressly does **not** require a broker to obtain and retain copies of **title commitments**
after the closing date, along with existing public records, loan applications, lender required disclosures,
and related affirmations from independent third party closing entities.

---

## C. Calculating: prorations

### C.1 The method, again

1. **Find the daily or monthly rate** — the annual amount ÷ the number of periods the **contract's**
   convention uses.
2. **Count the periods on each side of closing**, using the contract's convention for the **day of
   closing**.
3. **Multiply**, and place the result with the right sign for each party.

**Prepaid or in arrears decides the direction:**

chunks.heading: C.2 Worked both ways, on given figures
chunks.excerpt:
| | Seller | Buyer |
|---|---|---|
| **Paid in ADVANCE by the seller** | **Credit** — reimbursed for the unused part | **Debit** |
| **Payable in ARREARS** | **Debit** — owes their share | **Credit** — will pay the bill |

### C.2 Worked both ways, on given figures

> **Annual amount $5,400. Closing 1 October. 360-day year, 30-day months. Seller charged through the day
> before closing.**
>
> Daily rate: **$5,400 ÷ 360 = $15.00**. Seller's days: **270** (January–September). Buyer's days: **90**.
>
> | If the amount is | Seller | Buyer |
> |---|---|---|
> | **Prepaid by the seller** | **Credit $1,350** (90 × $15) | **Debit $1,350** |
> | **Payable in arrears** | **Debit $4,050** (270 × $15) | **Credit $4,050** |

**Same transaction, same date, same convention — two entirely different entries.** The question that
decides it is whether the money has already been paid.

### C.3 On a 365-day year with actual days

> **Annual amount $5,475. Closing 15 April. 365-day year, actual days. Buyer charged for the day of
> closing.**
>
> Daily rate: **$5,475 ÷ 365 = $15.00**. Seller's days: 31 + 28 + 31 + 14 = **104** (through 14 April).
> **Seller's share = 104 × $15.00 = $1,560.** Buyer's days: 365 − 104 = **261**, **$3,915.**
>
> **$1,560 + $3,915 = $5,475.** The two shares always sum to the whole — which is the check to run before
> entering either.

### C.4 Rents and deposits on an income property

chunks.heading: D. Calculating: prepaid interest, and cash to close
chunks.excerpt:
> **A four-unit building at $1,600 per unit per month. Closing 20 June, 30-day month, buyer charged for the
> day of closing. Rents for June were collected in full by the seller. Security deposits of $1,600 per unit
> are held.**
>
> June rent collected: **4 × $1,600 = $6,400**. Daily: **$6,400 ÷ 30 = $213.3333**.
> Buyer's days: **11** (20th through 30th). **Buyer's share = 11 × $213.3333 = $2,346.67.**
>
> | Entry | Buyer | Seller |
> |---|---|---|
> | Rent proration | **Credit $2,346.67** | **Debit $2,346.67** |
> | Security deposits (4 × $1,600) | **Credit $6,400.00** | **Debit $6,400.00** |
>
> **The deposits transfer in full, not prorated** — they are the tenants' money, and the buyer will have to
> return them.
>
> **And in Colorado a brokerage holding them is inside Chapter 5:** **Rule 5.5** requires **separate trust
> or escrow accounts — a minimum of one for rental receipts and a minimum of one for security deposits**;
> **Rule 5.8.A** forbids delivering deposits to an owner without the **tenant's written authorization in a
> lease or written notice** telling the tenant who holds them and how to request return; and **Rule 5.8.B**
> governs a transfer between firms — **written disclosure within 30 days**, **transfer within 60 days**, and
> the new firm **verifying each deposit against the current lease.**

---

## D. Calculating: prepaid interest, and cash to close

### D.1 Prepaid interest is not a proration

chunks.heading: D.2 A full cash-to-close calculation
chunks.excerpt:
**Mortgage interest is paid in arrears** — the payment made on the first of a month covers the interest that
accrued the **previous** month. So a loan funding mid-month produces no payment until the month after next,
and the lender collects the intervening interest **at closing**. That is **prepaid interest**, and it is a
**buyer debit only** — there is no seller side to it.

> **A new loan of $384,000 at 6.5 percent funds on 12 September. A 365-day year is used. Interest is
> collected from funding through the end of the month.**
>
> Daily interest: **$384,000 × 0.065 ÷ 365 = $68.3836** (rounded at the end).
> Days 12 through 30 inclusive: **19 days.**
> **Prepaid interest = 19 × $68.3836 = $1,299.29**, **debited to the buyer.**

### D.2 A full cash-to-close calculation

**Every figure supplied as a given.**

> Price **$525,000**. Earnest money **$15,000** already paid. New loan **$420,000**. Buyer's loan costs
> **$5,600**, including the prepaid interest. Buyer's recording **$180**. Buyer's share of prepaid HOA dues
> **$310**. Buyer's title endorsement **$150**.
>
> | Buyer debit | | Buyer credit | |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | Purchase price | 525,000.00 | Earnest money | 15,000.00 |
> | Loan costs | 5,600.00 | New loan proceeds | 420,000.00 |
> | Recording | 180.00 | | |
> | HOA proration | 310.00 | | |
> | Title endorsement | 150.00 | | |
> | **TOTAL** | **531,240.00** | **TOTAL** | **435,000.00** |
>
> **Cash due from the buyer = 531,240.00 − 435,000.00 = $96,240.00.**

chunks.heading: D.3 The check to run before signing anything
chunks.excerpt:
> And the seller's side of the same transaction: existing loan payoff **$268,900**; compensation at
> **5.5 percent** of the price; title insurance premium **$1,940**; recording of the release **$40**; HOA
> proration **$310** credited.
>
> | Seller debit | | Seller credit | |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | Existing loan payoff | 268,900.00 | Purchase price | 525,000.00 |
> | Compensation (5.5%) | 28,875.00 | HOA proration | 310.00 |
> | Title insurance | 1,940.00 | | |
> | Recording | 40.00 | | |
> | **TOTAL** | **299,755.00** | **TOTAL** | **525,310.00** |
>
> **Cash to the seller = 525,310.00 − 299,755.00 = $225,555.00.**

**The proof:**

| In | | Out | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Buyer's cash | 96,240.00 | Payoff | 268,900.00 |
| Earnest money | 15,000.00 | Compensation | 28,875.00 |
| Loan proceeds | 420,000.00 | Title insurance | 1,940.00 |
| | | Recording (180 + 40) | 220.00 |
| | | Buyer's loan costs | 5,600.00 |
| | | Buyer's title endorsement | 150.00 |
| | | Seller's proceeds | 225,555.00 |
| **TOTAL** | **531,240.00** | **TOTAL** | **531,240.00** |

**In equals out.** Note that the **HOA proration nets to zero across the two sides** — a debit to the buyer
and a credit to the seller of the same $310 — which is what a proration between the parties should do.

### D.3 The check to run before signing anything

1. **Does every charge trace to the contract or a written amendment?** (Topic III.A.1)
2. **Does each proration's two halves sum to the whole?**
3. **Does each party's column settle to a single figure?**
4. **Does in equal out?**
5. **Is the statement accurate, complete and detailed?** **Rule 6.19.A** — and the broker signs it.

---

## Module 03 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 03
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
**all students successfully complete a written examination covering all major topic areas**, and **these
items are not that examination.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 03

Written to the **Commission's Closings qualifying education outline, approved June 6, 1996**, Topic III and
its sub-topics A through C, using the outline's own wording — including *"**Close to contract or amend
contract in writing**"* and *"**Non-contractual fees and costs**"*. The hour figure is the Commission's.

**Rules 5.5, 5.8, 5.17, 6.2, 6.19, 6.20 and 6.21.A** and **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V), 12-10-405(1)(c)(V),
12-10-407(2)(b)(II) and 12-10-410(6)** are transcribed from **4 CCR 725-1** and **C.R.S. Title 12 Article
10**, read on 2026-08-20.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** any **Commission-approved form**, including the
Agreement to Amend/Extend Contract; any **title company commitment form** — the schedule structure described
is the general industry arrangement and no company's form was read; **RESPA**; **C.R.S. § 12-10-304**;
Colorado's **property tax and assessment** statutes; and the **Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act** and
every HOA statute.

**No form provision, title commitment form, tax rate, assessment ratio, billing cycle, proration
convention, HOA requirement, interest rate, referral fee threshold or fee amount is stated in this
module.** Every figure in every worked calculation is supplied inside the problem as a given, the
conventions are stated as given, and the arithmetic is shown in full.

lessons.title: Colorado Closings — Module 04

chunks.heading: Colorado Closings — Module 04
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Closings — Module 04

## Legal documents

**Course:** Closings (24 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 1.0** of 24.0
**Commission outline topic:** **IV — Legal Documents**, allocated **1.0 hour**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What the Commission's outline puts in this topic
>
> | Sub-topic | Delivered in |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** The title commitment **as it relates to legal documents** | Part A |
> | **B.** **Review** of prepared legal and financial documents | Part B |
> | **C.** **Transaction files — retention of file documents** | Part C |
> | **D.** Other closing documents — **escrow instructions, etc.** | Part D |
>
> One hour, and it is the topic that connects the commitment read in Module 03 to the documents that
> actually get signed and recorded.
>
> **The course objective names it expressly:** *"...plus accounting for all funds received and disbursed as
> well as **a comprehensive review of the LEGAL DOCUMENTS PREPARED BY THE BROKER.**"*

## Learning objectives

1. State how each Schedule B-1 requirement becomes a document at closing.
2. Name the documents ordinarily signed and recorded at a closing and say what each does.
3. State what a broker reviews a document for, and what a broker does not do with it.
4. State the four-year retention rule, its two start dates, and what it excludes.
5. State what escrow or closing instructions do.

---

## A. The title commitment as it relates to legal documents

Module 03 read the commitment. **This part turns Schedule B-1 into paper.**

**Every requirement on Schedule B-1 becomes a document someone must produce.**

chunks.heading: B. Review of prepared legal and financial documents
chunks.excerpt:
| A typical B-1 requirement | The document that satisfies it | Who produces it |
|---|---|---|
| Pay and release the existing deed of trust | **Payoff statement**, then the **release** | Lender / public trustee, through the closing entity |
| Satisfy a judgment lien | **Satisfaction or release of judgment** | Judgment creditor's counsel |
| Evidence of authority for an entity seller | **Corporate resolution**, **statement of authority**, or operating agreement excerpt | The entity, through counsel |
| Evidence of authority for a trust or estate | **Trustee's certificate**, **letters testamentary**, **death certificate** | Counsel or the probate court |
| Deed from the vested owner | **The deed** | Prepared by counsel or on a form appropriate to the transaction |
| Survey or ILC where required | **Survey** or **Improvement Location Certificate** | Licensed surveyor / preparer |
| Payment of taxes and assessments | **Tax certificate**, receipts | Treasurer, through the closing entity |

**The broker's job with Schedule B-1 is assignment and tracking, not production.** Each item needs **an
