owner and a date**, and an item nobody owns is the item that stops the closing.

> **A boundary this module holds.** **Who may sign for an entity, a trust or an estate is a question of
> Colorado law this project did not read.** **No Colorado entity, trust, probate or statement-of-authority
> statute was read**, and **no requirement, form or authority rule from any of them is stated anywhere in
> this build.** Those requirements come from **the title company and counsel.**

---

## B. Review of prepared legal and financial documents

### B.1 The documents

chunks.heading: B.2 What a broker reviews for, and what a broker does not do
chunks.excerpt:
| Document | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Deed** | Conveys the property — and **which deed** determines what the grantor warrants |
| **Promissory note** | Creates the **debt** |
| **Deed of trust** | Creates the **lien**, with a **trustee** holding title or a power of sale for the lender |
| **Release of the existing deed of trust** | Discharges the seller's lien |
| **Closing statement** | The accounting between the parties — and **Rule 6.19.A requires it to be signed by the broker** |
| **Bill of sale** | Conveys personal property included in the transaction |
| **Affidavits and certifications** | As the closing entity, the lender or the title company requires |
| **Escrow or closing instructions** | Direct the closing entity — Part D |

**A broker does not select the form of deed.** The choice determines what the grantor warrants and what the
grantee receives, which is a legal question — and **§ 12-10-403(4)(b)** lists the eight kinds of standard
form a broker may complete, of which a deed is one only if a **Commission-approved form** exists and is
appropriate, or one of the other seven categories applies.

**§ 12-10-403(4)(c)**, closing sentence: the broker *"**shall advise the parties that the forms have
important legal consequences and that the parties should consult legal counsel before signing the
forms.**"*

### B.2 What a broker reviews for, and what a broker does not do

chunks.heading: C. Transaction files — retention of file documents
chunks.excerpt:
> **Reviews for:** does the **name** match how title is vested and how the contract reads; does the **legal
> description** match the commitment; does the **price** match the contract; do the **loan figures** match
> the lender's; do the **prorations** match the worksheet; are the **dates** consistent; is anything on the
> statement that is not in the contract or a written amendment.
>
> **Does not do:** opine on the **legal effect** of a document; advise which **deed form** to use; advise
> whether a **title exception** is acceptable; or advise on **tax consequences.**

**Rule 6.19.C** states the attendance requirement that makes this review possible: a broker with a
brokerage relationship *"**must review closing documents AND attend closing OR BE REASONABLY AVAILABLE**"*,
and where they will not be, **another broker designated by the firm may review and attend on their behalf**
and **assumes joint responsibility** for accuracy, completeness and delivery of the signed closing
statement.

**Rule 6.2** governs what happens when the review runs past the broker's competence: **decline**, **obtain**
the experience, training and knowledge, **obtain the assistance** of the employing broker, a supervisory
broker, a competent broker **or legal counsel competent in the matter**, or **co-list.**

---

## C. Transaction files — retention of file documents

chunks.heading: C. Transaction files — retention of file documents
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 6.20**: *"Both a Broker and a Brokerage Firm **must retain transaction files for all transactions
> for a period of FOUR (4) YEARS** beginning from **the consummation date of the transaction OR the
> expiration date of any Listing Contracts that do not consummate.** Required documents in a transaction
> file are designated in the **Commission's Transaction File Checklist** and may be found on the Division's
> website. A Broker is **not required to obtain and retain copies of existing public records, title
> commitments, loan applications, lender required disclosures, or related affirmations from independent
> third party closing entities after the closing date.**"*

**Three things to hold onto:**

1. **Four years**, and **both** the broker and the firm must retain.
2. **Two start dates.** A transaction that **closes** runs from **consummation**. A **listing that never
   produces a closing** runs from **the listing contract's expiration** — so a file with no transaction in
   it still has a retention clock.
3. **Five categories are expressly excluded**, and every one of them is a document generated by somebody
   else: existing public records, **title commitments**, loan applications, lender required disclosures,
   and related affirmations from independent third party closing entities **after the closing date.**

**And Rule 6.19.A adds the delivery step at the front of it:** if the broker is licensed with a brokerage
firm, they *"**must deliver closing statements to the Brokerage Firm along with any other closing documents,
IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING CLOSING.**"*

chunks.heading: D. Other closing documents — escrow instructions
chunks.excerpt:
> **The Commission's Transaction File Checklist was NOT obtained by this project**, and **no module of this
> build states what documents it designates.** **This is a submission gate**, and it is one a Closings
> course cannot leave open — the rule points to the checklist by name for exactly this content.

**Two more retention-adjacent rules read for this build:**

- **Rule 5.14.E** — the three-way reconciliation reports, ledgers, journals and bank statements **may be
  kept electronically.**
- **Rule 5.21** — a broker and firm **must produce for inspection by the Commission any document or record**
  reasonably necessary for investigation or audit, and **failure within the time set is grounds for
  disciplinary action** absent an extension. **Rule 6.24** governs electronic records and production.

---

## D. Other closing documents — escrow instructions

**Escrow or closing instructions tell the closing entity what to do**: what documents to obtain, what
conditions must be satisfied, what to disburse and to whom, and what to record and in what order.

**Their function is that neither party has to perform first on trust.** The neutral third party holds
documents and funds and releases them only when the stated conditions are met — which is why a closing
entity that is asked to disburse into a dispute should not, and why **a broker who directs one to do so has
asked for something the entity should refuse.**

chunks.heading: E. What this module is checked on
chunks.excerpt:
**Colorado's Good Funds rule applies to the broker and the firm directly.** **Rule 6.19.E**: a broker or
firm *"**must not disburse or authorize disbursement of funds until those funds have been received and are
either ... available for immediate withdrawal as a matter of right ... or available for immediate withdrawal
as a consequence of an agreement with a financial institution ... If the agreement contains contingencies or
reservations, NO DISBURSEMENTS CAN BE MADE until these are satisfied.**"*

**§ 38-35-125, which Rule 6.19.E cites, was NOT read by this project**, and **no definition of good funds,
clearing period or list of acceptable instruments from the statute is stated anywhere in this build.**

**Other documents that travel with a closing**, none of whose contents this build states: the **seller's
property disclosure**; the **inspection notice**; **lead-based paint** disclosure and acknowledgment for
pre-1978 housing; **HOA status letters and association documents**; **withholding certificates** for a
non-resident or foreign seller; and the **lender's own disclosures.**

---

## E. What this module is checked on

chunks.heading: Module 04 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
| Check | Source |
|---|---|
| Every Schedule B-1 requirement has an owner and a date | Module 03 Part B |
| The names, description, price and figures match across the contract, the commitment, the worksheet and the statement | Rule 6.19.A and 6.19.B |
| Nothing on the statement is unsupported by the contract or a written amendment | Closings outline Topic III.A.1 |
| The statement is **signed by the broker** | **Rule 6.19.A** |
| Closing statements and documents delivered to the firm **immediately following closing** | **Rule 6.19.A** |
| The file is retained **four years** from consummation or from a non-consummating listing's expiration | **Rule 6.20** |
| No document's legal effect is opined on by the broker | **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)**, **Rule 6.2** |

---

## Module 04 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
**all students successfully complete a written examination covering all major topic areas**, and **these
items are not that examination.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 04

Written to the **Commission's Closings qualifying education outline, approved June 6, 1996**, Topic IV and
its sub-topics A through D, using the outline's own item names — including *"**Transaction files —
retention of file documents**"* and *"**Other closing documents — escrow instructions, etc.**"* The hour
figure is the Commission's.

**Rules 5.14.E, 5.21, 6.2, 6.19, 6.20 and 6.24** and **§ 12-10-403(4)** are transcribed from **4 CCR 725-1**
and **C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10**, read on 2026-08-20 and recorded in
`colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 04
chunks.excerpt:
**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** the **Commission's Transaction File Checklist**;
**every Commission-approved form**; **C.R.S. § 38-35-125**; Colorado's **entity, trust, probate and
statement-of-authority** statutes; its **recording** statutes; the **federal lead-based paint regulations**;
**RESPA** and the federal settlement disclosures; the **non-resident seller withholding** statute and
**FIRPTA**; and the **Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act.**

**No form provision, checklist item, deed form requirement, recording requirement, authority rule, good
funds definition, clearing period, disclosure requirement or penalty is stated in this module.** The **four
years** and the **two start dates** in Rule 6.20, and every requirement in **Rule 6.19**, are transcribed
from **4 CCR 725-1**.

lessons.title: Colorado Closings — Module 05

chunks.heading: Colorado Closings — Module 05
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Closings — Module 05

## Preparation of a minimum of eight closing problems

**Course:** Closings (24 classroom hours) · **Instructional hours: 16.0** of 24.0
**Commission outline topic:** **V — Preparation of a Minimum of 8 Closing Problems**, allocated **16.0
hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### The Commission's requirement, transcribed in full
>
> > **V.** *"**Preparation of a minimum of eight (8) closing problems** using a mix of **cash, owner carry,
> > assumptions (FHA, VA and conventional), new loans (FHA, VA and conventional), and a closing involving a
> > multi-family property. THREE PROBLEMS SHALL BE USING SAMPLES OF PREPARED CONTRACTS.**"*
> >
> > *"**ALL STUDENTS MUST SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETE A WRITTEN EXAMINATION COVERING ALL MAJOR TOPIC AREAS OF THIS
> > OUTLINE.**"*
>
> **Sixteen of the twenty-four hours are this module.** Two-thirds of the Closings course is the student
> **working problems**, and a course that delivers it as lecture has not delivered it.
>
> **The course engine records each of the eight separately and does not credit this course until all eight
> are recorded complete**, with the mix the Commission requires and **at least three worked from samples of
> prepared contracts.** Reading about a closing is not preparing one.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: A. How a problem is worked
chunks.excerpt:
1. Work a closing problem end to end on a six-column worksheet and prove that in equals out.
2. Work a cash closing, and say what is absent from it.
3. Work a new loan closing on FHA, VA and conventional terms as given.
4. Work an assumption, and identify what the contract must settle about release.
5. Work an owner carry closing, and identify what the seller has become.
6. Work a multi-family closing with rents, deposits and a partial month.
7. Work three problems from prepared contracts, closing to the contract as written.
8. Identify, in any problem, a charge that is not supported by the contract.

---

## A. How a problem is worked

**The same seven steps every time.**

| Step | What is done |
|---|---|
| **1** | **Read the contract** — price, earnest money and its holder, financing structure, closing and possession dates, every contingency, and every cost allocation |
| **2** | **List every item** the transaction produces, and mark each **contractual** or **non-contractual** |
| **3** | **Compute each proration** — daily rate, days each side, direction by prepaid or in arrears |
| **4** | **Place every item** on the six-column worksheet with the right party and the right sign |
| **5** | **Total each column** and derive **cash from the buyer** and **cash to the seller** |
| **6** | **Prove the money** — everything received equals everything disbursed |
| **7** | **Check against the contract** — nothing on the statement that the contract or a written amendment does not support |

**Step 7 is the Commission's own sentence from Topic III.A.1:** ***"Close to contract or amend contract in
writing."*** A charge the parties agreed to informally is amended in first, or it does not appear.

---

## B. The eight problems

chunks.heading: C. Problem 1 worked in full — a cash closing
chunks.excerpt:
The Commission specifies a **mix**, not a list. This module delivers eight that cover every element the
outline names, and **at least three are worked from samples of prepared contracts** as the outline
requires.

| # | Structure | Elements it exercises | From a prepared contract? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Cash** | The worksheet with no loan on either side | |
| **2** | **New loan — conventional** | Loan proceeds, loan costs, prepaid interest, prepaid taxes | **Yes** |
| **3** | **New loan — FHA** | The same, on FHA terms as given, with mortgage insurance | |
| **4** | **New loan — VA** | The same, on VA terms as given | |
| **5** | **Assumption — conventional** | Loan assumed, balance as of closing, interest proration, release | **Yes** |
| **6** | **Assumption — FHA or VA** | The same, on the terms given | |
| **7** | **Owner carry** | Seller-carried note, security instrument, what the seller has become | |
| **8** | **Multi-family** | Rents, security deposits, partial month, Chapter 5 consequences | **Yes** |

**Every rate, term, fee, premium and figure in every problem is supplied inside the problem as a given.**
**No Colorado tax rate, assessment ratio, billing cycle, insurance premium, loan limit, FHA or VA
requirement or proration convention is stated anywhere in this course**, because none was read from a
primary source.

---

## C. Problem 1 worked in full — a cash closing

**Every figure given.**

chunks.heading: C. Problem 1 worked in full — a cash closing
chunks.excerpt:
> Price **$395,000**, all cash. Earnest money **$12,000**, held by the brokerage. Compensation **5.5
> percent** of the price, charged to the seller. Seller's existing loan payoff **$147,300**. Title insurance
> premium **$1,720**, seller. Recording: buyer **$180**, seller **$40**. Annual taxes **$3,600**, **payable
> in arrears**; closing **1 July**; **360-day year, 30-day months**, seller charged through the day before
> closing.

**Step 3 — the proration.** Daily **$3,600 ÷ 360 = $10.00**. Seller's days **180** (January–June).
**Seller's share $1,800**, and because the taxes are in arrears it is a **credit to the buyer** and a
**debit to the seller.**

**Steps 4 and 5 — the worksheet.**

| Item | Buyer debit | Buyer credit | Seller debit | Seller credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Purchase price | 395,000.00 | | | 395,000.00 |
| Earnest money | | 12,000.00 | | |
| Existing loan payoff | | | 147,300.00 | |
| Compensation (5.5%) | | | 21,725.00 | |
| Title insurance | | | 1,720.00 | |
| Recording | 180.00 | | 40.00 | |
| Tax proration (arrears) | | 1,800.00 | 1,800.00 | |
| **TOTALS** | **395,180.00** | **13,800.00** | **172,585.00** | **395,000.00** |

> **Cash from the buyer = 395,180.00 − 13,800.00 = $381,380.00**
> **Cash to the seller = 395,000.00 − 172,585.00 = $222,415.00**

**Step 6 — prove it.**

| In | | Out | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Buyer's cash | 381,380.00 | Payoff | 147,300.00 |
| Earnest money | 12,000.00 | Compensation | 21,725.00 |
| | | Title insurance | 1,720.00 |
| | | Recording (180 + 40) | 220.00 |
| | | Seller's proceeds | 222,415.00 |
| **TOTAL** | **393,380.00** | **TOTAL** | **393,380.00** |

chunks.heading: D. Problem 5 worked in full — an assumption
chunks.excerpt:
**What a cash closing is missing, and why it is problem 1.** No loan proceeds credit, no loan costs, no
prepaid interest, no lender's requirements to satisfy. **Everything left is the transaction itself** — which
is why it is the clearest place to learn the worksheet before the loan lines are added.

---

## D. Problem 5 worked in full — an assumption

**Every figure given.**

> Price **$362,000**. Earnest money **$8,000**. The buyer **assumes** the seller's existing conventional
> loan; the **principal balance as of closing is $228,450**, and **interest accrued and unpaid to the
> closing date is $604**. Assumption fee **$450**, charged to the buyer. The buyer pays the balance of the
> price in cash. Compensation **6 percent**, seller. Title insurance **$1,610**, seller. Recording: buyer
> **$180**, seller **$40**. Annual taxes **$4,800**, **prepaid by the seller for the calendar year**;
> closing **1 May**; **360-day year, 30-day months**; buyer charged from the closing date.

**The tax proration.** Daily **$4,800 ÷ 360 = $13.3333**. Buyer's days: **240** (May–December).
**Buyer's share = 240 × $13.3333 = $3,200.00** — and because the seller **prepaid**, it is a **debit to the
buyer** and a **credit to the seller.**

**The accrued interest.** The seller used the money and has not paid the interest; the buyer is taking over
the loan and will pay it. So **$604 is a credit to the buyer and a debit to the seller.**

chunks.heading: D. Problem 5 worked in full — an assumption
chunks.excerpt:
| Item | Buyer debit | Buyer credit | Seller debit | Seller credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Purchase price | 362,000.00 | | | 362,000.00 |
| Earnest money | | 8,000.00 | | |
| Loan assumed | | 228,450.00 | 228,450.00 | |
| Accrued interest on assumed loan | | 604.00 | 604.00 | |
| Assumption fee | 450.00 | | | |
| Compensation (6%) | | | 21,720.00 | |
| Title insurance | | | 1,610.00 | |
| Recording | 180.00 | | 40.00 | |
| Tax proration (prepaid) | 3,200.00 | | | 3,200.00 |
| **TOTALS** | **365,830.00** | **237,054.00** | **252,424.00** | **365,200.00** |

> **Cash from the buyer = 365,830.00 − 237,054.00 = $128,776.00**
> **Cash to the seller = 365,200.00 − 252,424.00 = $112,776.00**

**Prove it.**

| In | | Out | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Buyer's cash | 128,776.00 | Compensation | 21,720.00 |
| Earnest money | 8,000.00 | Title insurance | 1,610.00 |
| | | Recording (180 + 40) | 220.00 |
| | | Assumption fee to lender | 450.00 |
| | | Seller's proceeds | 112,776.00 |
| **TOTAL** | **136,776.00** | **TOTAL** | **136,776.00** |

**Note that the assumed loan never becomes cash.** It appears as a **credit to the buyer and a debit to the
seller** and cancels between them — no money moves, because the debt simply changes hands.

chunks.heading: E. Problem 8 worked in full — a multi-family closing
chunks.excerpt:
> **What the contract must settle, and what a broker raises before it is signed.**
>
> **Is the seller RELEASED?** Without a **written release from the lender**, the seller may remain liable on
> the note after closing. The alienation (due-on-sale) clause is why the lender is involved at all, and the
> release is a separate document the lender must issue. **A broker ensures the seller understands the
> question and takes it to counsel** — **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V) and 12-10-407(2)(b)(II)** each require
> advising the party to obtain expert advice on material matters beyond the broker's expertise.
>
> **And the contract must state what happens if the lender refuses approval** — the three-part contingency
> test: **what event, by when, what happens if it does not occur.**

---

## E. Problem 8 worked in full — a multi-family closing

**Every figure given.**

> A **six-unit** building at **$1,375** per unit per month. Price **$1,240,000**. Earnest money **$25,000**.
> New loan **$930,000**; buyer's loan costs **$11,800**. Compensation **5 percent**, seller. Seller's payoff
> **$486,200**. Title insurance **$3,100**, seller. Recording: buyer **$180**, seller **$40**. **June rents
> collected in full by the seller**; **security deposits of $1,375 per unit** are held by the seller's
> managing brokerage. Closing **20 June**; **30-day month**; **buyer charged for the day of closing**.

**Rents.** June rent collected **6 × $1,375 = $8,250**. Daily **$8,250 ÷ 30 = $275.00**. Buyer's days
**11** (20th through 30th). **Buyer's share = 11 × $275.00 = $3,025.00** — **credit to the buyer, debit to
the seller.**

**Security deposits.** **6 × $1,375 = $8,250**, transferred **in full and not prorated** — **credit to the
buyer, debit to the seller.**

chunks.heading: E. Problem 8 worked in full — a multi-family closing
F. The three problems from prepared contracts
chunks.excerpt:
> **The Chapter 5 consequences a multi-family closing produces, all from rules read in full.**
>
> **Rule 5.5** — a firm engaging in property management must hold **rental receipts and security deposits in
> SEPARATE trust or escrow accounts**, a minimum of one for each.
>
> **Rule 5.8.A** — a firm receipting for security deposits **will not deliver them to an owner** without the
> **tenant's written authorization in a lease** or **written notice** telling the tenant **who holds the
> deposit** and **the procedure for requesting its return.**
>
> **Rule 5.8.B** — where management passes to a **new** brokerage firm: **written disclosure to owner and
> current tenant within 30 DAYS** of execution or assignment of the management agreement; **transfer by the
> previous firm within 60 DAYS**; the new firm **verifies each deposit against the amount in the current
> lease and discloses any discrepancy**; and the tenant is **informed in writing if the owner is holding
> the deposit.**
>
> **Rule 5.7.A** — property management money is deposited **no later than FIVE BUSINESS DAYS** following
> receipt or mutual execution of a lease, **whichever is later**, where **Rule 5.7.B** gives all other money
> **three.**
>
> **Rule 5.14.B** — *"**No ledger may ever be allowed to have a negative cash balance.**"*
>
> **And nothing about the tenancies themselves is stated in this build.** **C.R.S. § 38-12-101 et seq. was
> NOT read**, so this course states **no deposit limit, return period, notice period, entry requirement,
> habitability standard or eviction procedure.** Those come from the statute, the leases, and counsel.

---

## F. The three problems from prepared contracts

chunks.heading: G. What a completed problem must show
chunks.excerpt:
The Commission requires that **three problems shall be using samples of prepared contracts.** In those
three the student is given **the contract itself** and works from it, rather than from a list of figures.

**What changes when the source is a contract:**

1. **The student must find the figures**, not receive them. Price, earnest money and its holder, the
   financing structure, the closing and possession dates, and every cost allocation are **in the document**.
2. **The student must notice what the contract does NOT say.** A cost the contract does not allocate is a
   **non-contractual fee** (Module 03 Part A.2) and needs an answer before closing.
3. **The student must notice inconsistency.** Dates out of sequence, a figure that appears twice
   differently, a contingency with no consequence.
4. **The student must resist closing to something other than the contract.** ***"Close to contract or amend
   contract in writing."***

> **A gate stated on this module's face.** **NO Commission-approved form was obtained, read, or reproduced
> by this project**, and **this course reproduces no contract.** The three prepared-contract problems
> require **samples of Colorado Commission-approved contracts**, obtained from the Division's website as
> **Rule 7.1.A** directs.
>
> **Building those three problems on the current forms is a submission gate**, and it is recorded as one in
> the course engine alongside the Contracts and Regulations course's form requirements.

---

## G. What a completed problem must show

chunks.heading: Module 05 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
| Check | What is looked for |
|---|---|
| **Every item placed** | Right party, right column, right sign |
| **Every proration correct** | Daily rate, day count, and **direction** — prepaid or in arrears |
| **Prorations sum to the whole** | Each party's share, added, equals the full amount |
| **Each party settles to one figure** | Cash from the buyer; cash to the seller |
| **In equals out** | The proof table balances to the cent |
| **Nothing unsupported** | Every charge traces to the contract or a written amendment |
| **Non-contractual items identified** | Named, and resolved before closing |
| **Nothing invented** | No rate, convention, fee or requirement supplied from memory or from another state |

**A problem that balances but carries a charge the contract does not support is not correct**, and that is
the point of Step 7. **Rule 6.19.A** requires an **accurate, complete and detailed** closing statement
**signed by the broker**; **Rule 6.19.B** makes a broker who prepares the documents responsible for their
**accuracy and completeness**; and **Rule 6.19.E** forbids **disbursing or authorizing disbursement** before
the funds are received and available.

---

## Module 05 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**.

**The engagement items do NOT satisfy the Commission's requirement.** Topic V requires **preparation of a
minimum of eight closing problems**, with the stated mix and with **three from prepared contracts**. The
course engine records the eight separately and does not credit this course without them.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 05
chunks.excerpt:
The outline's own examination requirement stands over the whole course: *"**ALL STUDENTS MUST SUCCESSFULLY
COMPLETE A WRITTEN EXAMINATION COVERING ALL MAJOR TOPIC AREAS OF THIS OUTLINE.**"* **These items are not
that examination.**

This module completes the Commission's **Closings** outline: **1.0 + 2.0 + 4.0 + 1.0 + 16.0 = 24.0 hours.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 05

Written to the **Commission's Closings qualifying education outline, approved June 6, 1996**, Topic V, whose
requirement is transcribed in full at the head of this module. The hour figure is the Commission's, and the
allocation of **16 of the 24 hours** to the problems is the Commission's own.

**Rules 5.5, 5.7, 5.8, 5.14.B, 6.19 and 7.1** and **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V) and 12-10-407(2)(b)(II)** are
transcribed from **4 CCR 725-1** and **C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10**, read on 2026-08-20 and recorded in
`colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **every Commission-approved form**, including the
contracts the three prepared-contract problems require; **C.R.S. § 38-12-101 et seq.**; Colorado's
**property tax, assessment and levy** statutes; **RESPA, TILA and TRID**; the **FHA and VA** programme
requirements; the **non-resident seller withholding** statute and **FIRPTA**; and **C.R.S. § 38-35-125.**

**No tax rate, assessment ratio, billing cycle, proration convention, interest rate, mortgage insurance
premium, FHA or VA requirement, loan limit, assumption fee, title premium or recording fee is stated in
this module.** Every figure in every worked problem is supplied inside that problem as a given, every
convention is stated as a given, and the arithmetic is shown in full so a reviewer can check it.

lessons.title: Colorado Practical Applications — Module 01

chunks.heading: Colorado Practical Applications — Module 01
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Practical Applications — Module 01

## Entering the field

**Course:** Practical Applications (32 hours) · **Instructional hours: 3.0** of 32.0
**Commission outline topic:** **I — Entering the Field**, allocated **3 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What this course is, and why its outline is the newest of the six
>
> **C.R.S. § 12-10-203(4)(a)(III)(D)** names **practical applications** among the four subjects making up
> the statutory **72 hours**. **Rule 2.1.A.2.f** fixes the floor: *"Practical Application: **not less than 32
> hours**."*
>
> **The Commission approved a revised outline at its meeting of August 7, 2012**, effective for teaching
> from **1 January 2013** and **mandatory for all providers from 1 July 2013.** The Commission's own note
> says why: the update *"covers **additional specialty areas of practice**, incorporates a **basic
> understanding of competency**, and allows education providers to **update market trends.**"*
>
> **Its objective:** *"To protect the public by providing a course of study for **new real estate brokers in
> the application of laws, rules, and standard of practices.** This course, upon completion, will give a
> **working knowledge of the practical applications of entering the real estate industry, a basic
> understanding in determining competency, the necessary components of a successful transaction, and an
> overview of market trends.**"*
>
> | Module | Commission topic | Hours |
> |---|---|---|
> | **01** | I. Entering the Field | **3** |
> | 02 | II. Residential Competency | 4 |
> | 03 | III. Property Management Competency | 3 |
> | 04 | IV. Commercial Competency | 2 |
> | 05 | V. Other Com

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
petency | 1 |
> | 06 | **VI. Offer to Closing** | **16** |
> | 07 | VII. Current Market Trends | 3 |
> | | **TOTAL** | **32** |
>
> **Half the course is Topic VI.** And the Commission adds two requirements a provider must meet:
>
> > *"**Providers should address EACH APPLICABLE STATUTE, RULE AND POSITION STATEMENT during the course.
> > COURSE PROVIDERS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR ENSURING THAT THE STATUTES, RULES AND POSITION STATEMENTS USED
> > DURING THE COURSE PRESENTATION ARE ACCURATE AND UP-TO-DATE.**"*
> >
> > *"**A test is required** to establish a participant's satisfactory completion of the statutory
> > requirements for the Practical Applications Course. **Courses taught online must meet the requirements
> > set forth in the ONLINE COURSE APPROVAL CHECKLIST created by the Division of Real Estate.**"*
>
> **Two gates follow immediately.** **No Commission position statement was obtained by this project** —
> including **CP 41**, which this module's own outline names. And **the Online Course Approval Checklist was
> NOT obtained**, which is a gate for **every** distance-delivered course in this build, not only this one.

## Learning objectives

1. State what a new broker interviews a brokerage firm about, and why each item matters.
2. State the Colorado supervision rules that stand behind an employment relationship.
3. Identify the costs of entering the field the Commission's outline names.
4. State how a new broker may lawfully find buyers and sellers, and the advertising rules that constrain it.
5. State the competency requirement in Rule 6.2 and its four routes.
6. State what the outline means by "gaining competency" and identify CP 41 as unread.

---

## A. Interviewing brokerage firms — outline Topic I.A

chunks.heading: A.1 The employment agreement — I.A.1
chunks.excerpt:
The outline names four sub-items, and Colorado's rules give each of them a legal edge.

### A.1 The employment agreement — I.A.1

**A new broker is licensed to a firm, and the firm's employing broker supervises them.** What the agreement
settles: **compensation** — how calculated, when paid, on what; **the split and any fees**; **expenses** —
who bears what; **term and termination**, including what happens to pending transactions and to the
broker's files; **whether the relationship is employment or independent contractor** for tax purposes; and
**what the broker may and may not do** — which is the office policy manual in Part A.2.

**One Colorado rule bears directly on compensation and new brokers miss it.**

> **Rule 6.12**, on CMAs and BPOs prepared for a reason **other than an anticipated sale, purchase or
> lease**: such preparation *"**is not considered Real Estate Brokerage Services. As such, any compensation
> received for such preparation IS NOT REQUIRED TO BE PAID TO THE BROKER'S BROKERAGE FIRM UNLESS STATED
> OTHERWISE IN BROKERAGE FIRM'S OFFICE POLICY MANUAL.**"*

**Check the manual before assuming.**

### A.2 Office policies — I.A.2

**Two Colorado requirements make the manual a legal document rather than a handbook.**

chunks.heading: A.3 Support — I.A.3
chunks.excerpt:
> **§ 12-10-408(1)(a)**: every broker *"**shall adopt a WRITTEN OFFICE POLICY that identifies and describes
> the relationships offered to the public** by the broker."*
>
> **§ 12-10-408(1)(b)**: *"A broker **shall not be required to offer or engage in any one or in all** of the
> brokerage relationships enumerated in section 12-10-404, 12-10-405, or 12-10-407."*
>
> **Rule 6.3.B.3**: employing brokers must **develop the Brokerage Firm's written policies as set forth in
> Rule 6.4.**
>
> **Rule 5.1**: a firm receiving Money Belonging to Others must establish **written accounting control
> policies and procedures** including **checks and balances over the financial activities of the broker, the
> firm and UNLICENSED PERSONS**, and **manage the risk of fraud or illegal acts.**

**The first question a new broker asks about the manual is which relationships the firm offers.** A firm may
decline to offer **single agency**, or decline to offer **transaction-brokerage**. That decision shapes
every transaction the new broker will do — and **§ 12-10-408(1)(c)** requires that where a consumer asks
about a relationship the firm does **not** offer, the broker **provide the Commission's own written
definition of it.**

### A.3 Support — I.A.3

Forms, systems, transaction coordination, marketing, technology, errors and omissions coverage, and access
to the employing broker.

chunks.heading: A.4 Training and supervision — I.A.4
chunks.excerpt:
**Support is not a courtesy; some of it is required.** **Rule 6.3.B.4** requires the employing broker to
provide *"a **'Reasonable-Level of Supervision'** for all Associate Brokers"*, and **Rule 6.2.B.3** names
*"the Employing Broker, Supervisory Broker, a Broker who meets the requirements ... or legal counsel that is
competent in the matter"* as one of the four routes out of an incompetence problem — which presupposes the
new broker can reach one of them.

### A.4 Training and supervision — I.A.4

> **Rule 6.3.A.1**: employing brokers *"**must exercise authority, direction, and supervision over any
> Associate Brokers** shown in the records of the Commission as supervised by the Employing Broker **to
> ensure conformance to the Commission statutes and these Rules**"* — and *"**whenever a complaint is filed
> with the Commission against an Associate Broker, the Commission MAY INVESTIGATE whether there have been
> violations ... by the EMPLOYING BROKER.**"*
>
> **Rule 6.3.A.2**: employing brokers **must also supervise all unlicensed employees**, *"including, but not
> limited to, Unlicensed On-Site Managers, secretaries, bookkeepers, and personal assistants of Associate
> Brokers."*
>
> **Rule 6.3.B**: employing brokers must **maintain all trust and escrow accounts and records** (Chapter 5),
> **maintain all transaction records** (Rule 6.20), **develop the firm's written policies** (Rule 6.4), and
> **provide a reasonable level of supervision.**

**A new broker should read Rule 6.3.A.1's second sentence carefully**, because it explains why a
well-supervised firm is stricter than a new broker expects: **a complaint against the associate can become
an investigation of the employing broker.**

chunks.heading: B. Cost to get started — outline Topic I.B
chunks.excerpt:
**And a statutory limit on independence a new broker meets immediately.** **§ 12-10-203(5)(c)(I)**: a
broker licensed after 31 December 1996 *"**shall [not] engage in an independent brokerage practice without
first having served actively as a real estate broker for at least TWO YEARS**"*, and the Commission *"shall
adopt rules requiring an employing broker to ensure that **a HIGH LEVEL OF SUPERVISION** is exercised over
such a broker during the two-year period."*

**§ 12-10-203(5)(c)(II)**: no such broker may **employ another broker** without first completing **24 clock
hours in brokerage administration**; and **(5)(c)(III)**: from **1 January 2019**, a broker may not act as
an **employing broker** without first demonstrating, under Commission rules, **experience and knowledge
sufficient to employ and adequately supervise other brokers.**

**Rule 2.1.B** carries the education half of that: an applicant for an **Employing Broker level licence**
must complete **24 hours of classroom instruction or equivalent distance learning in Brokerage
Administration.**

---

## B. Cost to get started — outline Topic I.B

The outline names four sub-items, and this module states what each is without inventing a figure.

| Sub-item | What it covers |
|---|---|
| **1. Signs, business cards, brochures, etc.** | Marketing materials — **all of which are Advertising under Rule 1.2** |
| **2. Home office vs. desk fee** | Where the broker works and what the firm charges for it |
| **3. Memberships** | Realtor boards, **multiple listing services**, showing services |
| **4. E/O insurance, license fees, car insurance** | The costs of being licensed and insured |

chunks.heading: C. How to find buyers and sellers — outline Topic I.C
chunks.excerpt:
> **No figure is stated for any of them.** Fees, dues, premiums and splits are set by the Division, by
> private organisations, and by firms, and **none was read from a primary source by this project.**
>
> **Errors and omissions insurance in particular.** **Chapter 3 of 4 CCR 725-1 is titled "Licensure,
> Renewal, License Status, and Insurance"**, and the Division publishes a **Broker Insurance Requirements**
> page. **The insurance rules in Chapter 3 were not read in detail for this build**, and **no coverage
> amount, deductible, carrier requirement, policy form or effective date is stated anywhere in this
> build.** **This is a submission gate**, and the **Contracts and Regulations** outline names errors and
> omissions insurance at its Topic V.C for the same reason.

**Rule 1.2 is worth reading at the point a new broker orders business cards**, because it settles what
counts as advertising:

> *"**Advertise or Advertising**: The promotion, solicitation, or representation of Real Estate Brokerage
> Services requiring a License. Advertising may include, but is not limited to, **business cards, brochures,
> websites, signage, property flyers, mailings (paper or electronic), SOCIAL MEDIA, letterhead, EMAIL
> SIGNATURES, and contract documents.** A uniform resource locator (URL) and an email address are **not**
> considered Advertising for purposes of Rule 6.10 so long as they are **not directly used to promote or
> solicit** Real Estate Brokerage Services."*

**Email signatures and social media are advertising.** **Rule 6.10** then governs what advertising must
contain and must not do, and Module 02 of this course delivers it.

---

## C. How to find buyers and sellers — outline Topic I.C

chunks.heading: C. How to find buyers and sellers — outline Topic I.C
chunks.excerpt:
The outline names three: **networking**, **family and friends**, and **marketing**.

**All three are lawful, and all three are constrained by the same three provisions.**

> **1. Disclosure comes before confidential information.** **Rule 6.5.A**: written disclosures under
> § 12-10-408 *"**must be made to a Consumer PRIOR TO ELICITING OR DISCUSSING CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION**"*.
> **Rule 6.5.B**: this does **not** include *"**preliminary conversations or 'small talk' concerning price
> range, location and property styles**, or **responding to general factual questions** ... concerning
> properties which have been Advertised."*
>
> **A conversation at a family gathering that moves from "what are prices doing" to "what could we afford"
> has crossed the line**, and the disclosure is already due.
>
> **2. Everything published is advertising.** **Rule 1.2** and **Rule 6.10.**
>
> **3. Conflicts are disclosed in writing, continuously.** **Rule 6.17.A**: brokers and firms have a
> *"**continuing duty to disclose, in writing, any known Conflict of Interest that may arise in the course
> of any real estate transaction.**"* **Rule 6.17.B**: a broker who **sells, buys or leases on their own
> account must disclose in the contracting instrument or a separate concurrent writing that they are a
> licensed Broker.**

**Working with family and friends is where new brokers most often meet Rule 6.17.** A relationship that
would affect how the broker acts is a conflict, and the duty to disclose it is **continuing** and **in
writing.**

chunks.heading: D. Gaining competency — outline Topic I.D
chunks.excerpt:
**And fair housing runs through prospecting as fully as through showing.** **§§ 12-10-404(1)(e),
12-10-405(1)(e) and 12-10-407(2)(d)** each require compliance with applicable law *"**including fair housing
and civil rights statutes or regulations**"*, so a targeting decision that excludes on a protected basis is
**also** a brokerage relationship violation, and **§ 12-10-411** makes any Part 4 violation an act the
Commission may investigate.

---

## D. Gaining competency — outline Topic I.D

The outline names three sub-items — **acquiring knowledge**, **experience**, and **types of training** — and
cites **CP 41** for the topic.

> **CP 41 was NOT obtained or read by this project.** **No position statement content is stated anywhere in
> this build.** **This is a submission gate**, and it is the second course in this build to record it — the
> **Record Keeping and Trust Accounts** outline names *"Position Statements"* at its Topic I.D.2 for the
> same reason.

**What IS stated comes from Rule 6.2, which was read in full and is the rule the 2012 outline revision was
written around.**

chunks.heading: D. Gaining competency — outline Topic I.D
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 6.2 — Competency**
>
> **A.** *"In order to conduct Real Estate Brokerage Services, a Broker **must possess the necessary
> experience, training, and knowledge** to provide Real Estate Brokerage Services and **maintain compliance
> with the applicable federal, state and local laws, rules, regulations and ordinances.**"*
>
> **B.** *"**If a Broker does not have the necessary experience, training, and knowledge, the Broker
> must:**"*
> **1.** *"**DECLINE** to provide Real Estate Brokerage Services;"*
> **2.** *"**OBTAIN** the necessary experience, training, and knowledge;"*
> **3.** *"**OBTAIN THE ASSISTANCE** of their Employing Broker, Supervisory Broker, a Broker who meets the
> requirements as set forth in subsection A., **or LEGAL COUNSEL that is competent in the matter**;"* or
> **4.** *"**CO-LIST** with another Broker who meets the requirements as set forth in subsection A."*

**Four routes, and the FIRST is to decline.** That ordering is deliberate and a new broker should notice
it: **the rule does not treat declining as a failure.**

**And the outline's own footnote, attached to Topics II through V, states the purpose:**

> *"**Educators should make sure students understand HOW COMPETENCY IS GAINED in each specialty e.g. through
> working with an experienced mentor or partner and/or taking educational courses to become competent in the
> field or area SO NO HARM IS DONE TO A MEMBER OF THE PUBLIC.**"*

**"So no harm is done to a member of the public" is the Commission's own statement of why competency is a
rule and not an aspiration.**

**Modules 02 through 05 of this course are the four specialties the Commission then names** — residential,
property management, commercial, and other — **and each is a competency module**, not a survey of the
specialty.

chunks.heading: Module 01 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
---

## Module 01 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
*"**a test is required** to establish a participant's satisfactory completion of the statutory requirements
for the Practical Applications Course"*, and **these items are not that test.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 01

Written to the **Commission's Practical Applications qualifying education outline, approved 7 August 2012**,
Topic I and its sub-topics A through D, in the outline's own order and using the outline's own item names —
including *"**Home office vs. desk fee**"*, *"**E/0 insurance, license fees, car insurance**"* and
*"**Gaining competency (CP 41)**"*. The hour figure is the Commission's.

The provisions quoted — **§§ 12-10-203(5)(c), 12-10-404(1)(e), 12-10-405(1)(e), 12-10-407(2)(d), 12-10-408
(1) and 12-10-411** and **Rules 1.2, 2.1.B, 5.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.5, 6.10, 6.12, 6.17 and 6.20** — are
transcribed from **C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10** and **4 CCR 725-1** (rule version 12355), read on
**2026-08-20** and recorded in `colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **CP 41** and **every Commission position
statement**; the **Online Course Approval Checklist**; the **insurance rules in Chapter 3 of 4 CCR 725-1**,
which were not read in detail; **C.R.S. §§ 12-10-217, 12-10-219 and 12-10-222**; the **Colorado Fair Housing
Act** and the **federal Fair Housing Act**; and every **fee schedule, membership due, insurance premium or
commission split.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 01
chunks.excerpt:
**No position statement content, checklist item, insurance coverage amount, licence fee, membership due,
commission split, disciplinary ground or penalty is stated in this module.** The **two years** and **24
hours** in § 12-10-203(5)(c), and the four routes in Rule 6.2.B, are transcribed from the statute and rule
named beside them.

lessons.title: Colorado Practical Applications — Module 02

chunks.heading: Colorado Practical Applications — Module 02
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Practical Applications — Module 02

## Residential competency

**Course:** Practical Applications (32 hours) · **Instructional hours: 4.0** of 32.0
**Commission outline topic:** **II — Residential Competency**, allocated **4 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### The Commission's footnote, which governs Modules 02 through 05
>
> Topics II, III, IV and V each carry an asterisk, and the outline explains it once:
>
> > *"\***Educators should make sure students understand HOW COMPETENCY IS GAINED in each specialty** e.g.
> > through working with an experienced mentor or partner and/or taking educational courses to become
> > competent in the field or area **SO NO HARM IS DONE TO A MEMBER OF THE PUBLIC.**"*
>
> **These four modules are competency modules, not surveys.** The question each answers is: **what does a
> broker need to know before taking this kind of work, and what do they do if they do not have it?**
>
> **Rule 6.2 supplies the legal frame for all four**, and its four routes are the answer to the second half
> of that question: **decline**; **obtain** the experience, training and knowledge; **obtain the
> assistance** of the employing broker, a supervisory broker, a competent broker **or legal counsel
> competent in the matter**; or **co-list.**

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
> ### What the Commission's outline puts in Topic II
>
> | Sub-topic | Delivered in |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** Broker relationships — 1. Disclosures; 2. Approved commission forms; 3. Relationship between employing brokers and employed licensees; 4. Relationship between listing and selling brokers | Part A |
> | **B.** Specialties & competency requirements — 1. Current market trends for selling and buying; 2. Investors; 3. Miscellaneous | Part B |
> | **C.** Third party providers — 1. Title companies; 2. Home inspection companies; 3. Mortgage companies; 4. Specialty vendors | Part C |
> | **D.** Comparative Market Analysis / Broker Price Opinions | Part D |

## Learning objectives

1. State which disclosures are required in a residential transaction and when each is due.
2. State the rule requiring use of Commission-approved forms.
3. State the supervision relationship and how a complaint reaches the employing broker.
4. State how offers pass between listing and selling brokers.
5. State the advertising rules a residential broker works inside daily.
6. State the square footage disclosure requirement.
7. State Rule 6.12's CMA/BPO notice verbatim and the prohibition that accompanies it.
8. State what a broker does and does not do with third-party providers.

---

## A. Broker relationships — outline Topic II.A

### A.1 Disclosures — II.A.1

**Delivered in full in Contracts and Regulations Module 02**, and summarised here as a residential broker
meets them in order.

chunks.heading: A.1 Disclosures — II.A.1
chunks.excerpt:
| When | What | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Before eliciting or discussing confidential information** | The § 12-10-408 written disclosure | **Rule 6.5.A** — and 6.5.B excludes *"preliminary conversations or 'small talk' concerning price range, location and property styles"* |
| **Before engaging in any licensed activity, as a transaction-broker** | Written disclosure that the broker **is not acting as agent** and **is a transaction-broker**, with a **signature block** — and **if the party does not sign, the broker notes that on a copy and retains it** | **§ 12-10-408(2)(a)** |
| **Before engaging in any licensed activity, for single agency** | A **written agency agreement** disclosing the § 12-10-404 or § 12-10-405 duties | **§ 12-10-408(2)(b)** |
| **Working with a buyer as the seller's agent** | Written disclosure: broker is the **seller's** agent, **a list of the tasks** the agent will perform with the buyer, and that the buyer is **not vicariously liable** | **§ 12-10-408(2)(c)(I)** |
| **In any written agreement** | That the relationship **exists only with the designated broker** and **does not extend to the employing broker or the firm** | **§ 12-10-408(2)(e)(I)** |
| **At the earliest reasonable opportunity** | Advising other potential parties or their agents of an established relationship | **§ 12-10-408(2)(d)** |
| **On changing from single agent for one to transaction-broker for both** | The Commission-approved **"Change of Status"** form, **at the time the broker begins to assist both** and **not later than when the consumer signs the contract** | **Rule 6.9** |
| **Continuously** | Any **known conflict of interest**, in writing; and that the broker is licensed if buying, selling or leasing **on their own account** | **Rule 6.17.A and B** |

chunks.heading: A.2 Approved commission forms — II.A.2
chunks.excerpt:
**And the default that stands behind all of it:** **§ 12-10-403(2)** — a broker is a **transaction-broker**
unless single agency is established **in writing**.

### A.2 Approved commission forms — II.A.2

> **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)**: *"**A broker shall use a COMMISSION-APPROVED FORM when such a form exists and is
> appropriate for the transaction.**"*
>
> **Rule 7.1.A**: a Commission-approved form is one *"promulgated by the Commission **for CURRENT USE** by
> Brokers"*; the broker **may advise the parties as to the effects thereof**; and *"**To obtain the forms
> promulgated by the Commission, visit the Division's website.**"*
>
> **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)**, closing sentence: the broker *"**shall advise the parties that the forms have
> important legal consequences and that the parties should consult legal counsel before signing.**"*

**"For current use" means a superseded form is not a Commission-approved form.**

> **NO Commission-approved form was obtained, read or reproduced by this project**, and **no module of this
> build states any form's contents, version, date or provisions.** It is the largest submission gate in the
> Colorado build.

### A.3 Employing brokers and employed licensees — II.A.3

**Rule 6.3** in full, delivered in Module 01 Part A.4: supervision over associate brokers **and all
unlicensed employees**; the employing broker's four responsibilities under **6.3.B**; and the sentence a new
broker should hold onto — *"**whenever a complaint is filed with the Commission against an Associate Broker,
the Commission may investigate whether there have been violations ... by the EMPLOYING BROKER.**"*

chunks.heading: A.4 Listing and selling brokers — II.A.4
chunks.excerpt:
**And § 12-10-403(6)(b) with its savings clause.** The **relationship** does not extend to the employing
broker or the firm — but **§ 12-10-408(2)(e)(II)**: *"**Nothing ... shall be construed to limit the
employing broker's or firm's responsibility to supervise licensees ... nor to shield the broker or firm from
vicarious liability.**"*

### A.4 Listing and selling brokers — II.A.4

> **Rule 6.13**: *"A Broker **must present all offers to the OTHER CONSUMER'S BROKER** if such other Consumer
> has an unexpired Listing Contract. If the Broker has made **reasonable, but unsuccessful, attempts** to
> present an offer to the other Consumer's Broker, the Broker **must present the offer to the other
> Consumer's Broker's EMPLOYING BROKER.** If **no Employing Broker exists**, or if reasonable attempts to
> present the offer to the Employing Broker have failed, **the Broker MAY present the offer directly to the
> other Consumer.**"*

**A three-step ladder, and the rule states no time period.** **No module of this build supplies one.**

**And the duty on the receiving side.** **§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(II)** requires a seller's agent to **present all
offers to and from the seller in a timely manner REGARDLESS of whether the property is subject to a contract
for sale** — while **(c)(I)** says the broker **is not obligated to SEEK additional offers** once under
contract. **Not seeking and not presenting are different acts.**

chunks.heading: B. Specialties and competency requirements — outline Topic II.B
chunks.excerpt:
**Compensation between brokers** is governed by **§ 12-10-410**: it may be paid by any party or shared
between brokers; **payment does not establish an agency relationship**; a **buyer's agent must obtain the
buyer's WRITTEN APPROVAL before proposing** to be compensated from the listing side (**(5)**); and the
**identity of anyone paying compensation must be disclosed before the brokerage agreement or contract is
entered into** (**(6)**).

---

## B. Specialties and competency requirements — outline Topic II.B

### B.1 Current market trends for selling and buying — II.B.1

**Named here and given its own three hours at Topic VII**, which **Module 07** delivers. The outline leaves
market content to the provider's discretion precisely because it changes.

### B.2 Investors — II.B.2

**A residential broker working with an investor is working outside ordinary residential competency**, and
this is where **Rule 6.2** first bites for most new brokers.

**What the work requires that a primary-residence transaction does not:** **income and expense analysis** —
potential gross income, vacancy and collection loss, effective gross income, operating expenses, net
operating income, and capitalisation, all delivered in **Real Estate Law and Practice Module 02 Part C.2 and
D**; **an understanding of leases in place** and what the buyer is inheriting; **tax consequences** the
broker does **not** advise on; and, where the property is tenanted, **everything in Module 03 of this
course.**

**The routing when a broker does not have it:** **Rule 6.2.B** — **decline**, **obtain**, **obtain
assistance**, or **co-list.**

### B.3 Miscellaneous — II.B.3

chunks.heading: B.4 The advertising rules a residential broker works inside daily — Rule 6.10
chunks.excerpt:
The outline's own catch-all. **This build states nothing under it** beyond the general point that a
residential broker meets transactions that are not ordinary — new construction, relocation, estates,
divorce, short sales, foreclosures — **and that each is a competency question under Rule 6.2 before it is
anything else.**

**Two of those reach law this build did not read.** **Colorado's foreclosure statutes and public trustee
system were NOT read**, and **its entity, trust and probate statutes were NOT read** — so **no procedure,
period, notice, authority rule or requirement from any of them is stated anywhere in this build.**

### B.4 The advertising rules a residential broker works inside daily — Rule 6.10

**Read in full for this build**, and this is where it belongs in the course.

> **A. Names.**
> **A.1** No broker may be licensed under **more than one brokerage firm** (§ 12-10-203(9)).
> **A.2** No broker or firm may conduct or promote brokerage services **except in the name under which they
> appear in the Commission's records.**
> **A.3** Brokers **will not advertise so as to mislead the public** concerning the identity of the broker or
> the firm.
> **A.4** *"**All Advertising must be done clearly and conspicuously IN THE NAME OF THE BROKER'S BROKERAGE
> FIRM.**"* — **with one exception:** a broker advertising **real property owned by the broker which is NOT
> listed with the broker's firm** is **exempt** from advertising it in the firm's name.
> **A.5** A firm may use a **Trade Name**, which **must be filed with the Commission.**
> **A.6** A firm may use a **Trademark** with the owner's permission — and a firm using a third party's trade
> name or trademark **must use one of two statements, clearly and conspicuously**: *"**Each (insert general
> Trade Name) b

chunks.heading: B.4 The advertising rules a residential broker works inside daily — Rule 6.10
chunks.excerpt:
rokerage business is independently owned and operated**"* or *"**Each office independently
> owned and operated.**"*
> **A.7** **No firm may use more than one Trade Name**; more than one Trademark requires written request and
> Commission consent.
> **A.8** **No professional designation** in advertising unless the broker is **in good standing** and the
> designation is **easily verifiable by the public and the Commission** — and a broker advertising an
> **award, membership or achievement** must be able to **provide verification on request** from any member
> of the public or the Commission.
>
> **B. Teams.**
> **B.1** Team advertising **must not mislead the public as to the identity of the team's brokerage firm**,
> and a team name **may not use**: *"**Realty, Real estate, Realtors, Company, Corporation, Corp., Inc.,
> LLC, LP or LLP, or any other term that would imply a separate entity from the Brokerage Firm.**"*
> **B.2** All team advertising **must clearly and conspicuously include and be in conjunction with the legal
> name or trade name of the brokerage firm.**
> **B.3** On request by a consumer, the Commission, another firm or broker, **the firm will provide the names
> of the brokers belonging to any team.**
> **B.4** Brokers **may not allow use of the team's name by brokers outside the team's firm.**
>
> **C. Accuracy.** Firms and brokers are **responsible for ensuring all advertising is accurate and complies
> with copyright laws and other applicable laws** — *"including ... **the accuracy of information entered
> into Multiple Listing Services** regarding property data, sales information, and the identification of
> Brokers who participated."* And: *"**The Broker does not have a duty to investigate the information
> provided to the broker by the seller or ob

chunks.heading: B.4 The advertising rules a residential broker works inside daily — Rule 6.10
chunks.excerpt:
tained from a third party source (e.g. assessor records,
> building plans).**"*
>
> **D. Electronic Media.**
> **D.1** Where a broker owns or controls electronic media, **EACH VIEWABLE PAGE must include the brokerage
> firm's name**, and **expired listings must be removed within THREE (3) DAYS of a listing contract
> expiring.**
> **D.2** Where a **third party** is authorised for the broker's electronic media advertising, the broker is
> responsible for the accuracy of the information supplied — and **must submit a WRITTEN REQUEST to any
> third party syndicators to remove expired listings within three days.**
> **D.3** A broker communicating by **email, chat, instant messages, newsgroups, discussion lists, bulletin
> boards, blogs or similar means** for advertising purposes **must use the firm's name** — though **once the
> firm has been disclosed to a specific consumer, the broker need not repeat it to that consumer.**
> **D.4** Where space is limited and disclosure is **not reasonable**, the firm's name **must be disclosed
> clearly and conspicuously WITHIN THE FIRST CLICK OF THE MOUSE.**
>
> **E. Past Sales Data.** General sales data advertising recapping activity over a period in a subdivision
> or area **must cite the source** and **include a disclaimer, if accurate**, that reported sales **were not
> necessarily listed or sold by the broker** and **are intended only to show trends** or **will separately
> identify the broker's own sales activity.**
>
> **F. Authority to advertise.** *"**Brokers may not Advertise the availability or price of a property
> whether for sale or lease WITHOUT AUTHORITY FROM THE OWNER OR THE OWNER'S BROKER.**"* An owner's broker
> **may not withhold** that authority unless doing so is **contradictory to the owner's instructions as
> mem

chunks.heading: C. Third party providers — outline Topic II.C
chunks.excerpt:
orialized in the listing contract or other writing.** A broker disseminating **another broker's**
> advertising needs that **broker's written permission**, must **disclose the owner's firm conspicuously**,
> and must be accurate; a broker disseminating an **unrepresented owner's** advertising needs the **owner's
> written permission**, must **disclose conspicuously that the owner is not represented**, and **may not
> submit the information into a property exchange or multiple listing service.**
>
> **G. Price set by owner.** *"**The price quoted in any Advertising will not be anything other than the
> price agreed upon between the Broker and the owner.**"*

**Three of those a new residential broker breaks first:** advertising a property **without the owner's or
owner's broker's authority** (F); a **team name** implying a separate entity (B.1); and **failing to remove
an expired listing within three days** (D.1 and D.2).

---

## C. Third party providers — outline Topic II.C

chunks.heading: C. Third party providers — outline Topic II.C
chunks.excerpt:
| Provider | What a broker does | What a broker does not do |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Title companies** | Deliver the commitment promptly; ensure each **Schedule B-1 requirement** has an owner and a date; confirm the objection deadline | Opine on the **legal effect** of an exception, or advise whether a defect is material |
| **2. Home inspection companies** | Ensure the inspection deadline is known and met; ensure the **Inspection Notice** goes out in time | **Assess the property** — **Rule 6.2** requires competency, and condition assessment is not a broker's field |
| **3. Mortgage companies** | Do arithmetic with figures the lender supplies; track the loan deadlines | **Advise which product to take**, or predict approval |
| **4. Specialty vendors** — *"structural engineer, electricians, industrial hygienists, etc."* | Provide more than one name where possible; let the client choose | **Recommend as guaranteed**, or take undisclosed value for the referral |

**Two Colorado rules govern what a broker may receive for sending work to any of them, and both were read.**

chunks.heading: D. Comparative Market Analysis and Broker Price Opinions — outline Topic II.D
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 6.21.A**: *"Brokers and Brokerage Firms **will not pay or receive a referral fee EXCEPT IN
> ACCORDANCE WITH RESPA** and unless a **reasonable cause for payment** of the referral fee exists pursuant
> to section 12-10-304(1), C.R.S."*
>
> **Rule 5.17**: the broker and firm *"**must obtain PRIOR WRITTEN CONSENT from the Consumer they represent
> to assess and receive mark-ups and/or other compensation for services performed, REGARDLESS IF FOR THE
> BENEFIT OF THE BROKER OR ANOTHER THIRD PARTY**"*, must **disclose all mark-ups paid for by any Customer**,
> and must **retain accurate on-going records** verifying disclosure and consent.
>
> **Rule 6.18** requires **affiliated business arrangement disclosures**; **Rule 1.3** defines the term by
> reference to **§ 12-10-218**.
>
> **Neither RESPA, nor § 12-10-304, nor § 12-10-218 was read by this project**, and **no requirement,
> threshold, exemption or penalty from any of them is stated anywhere in this build.**

**And Rule 6.17.C for anyone doing property management:** a **continuing duty to disclose in writing any
known conflict of interest in the selection or use of a business or vendor** — including **any ownership,
financial, or familial interest.** Module 03 of this course develops it.

---

## D. Comparative Market Analysis and Broker Price Opinions — outline Topic II.D

**The rule was read in full, and it prescribes the words.**

chunks.heading: D. Comparative Market Analysis and Broker Price Opinions — outline Topic II.D
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 6.12**: *"When a Broker prepares a CMA or BPO **for any reason other than the anticipated sale or
> purchase of the property**, the Broker **must include a notice stating**:*
>
> ***"'This evaluation was prepared by a licensed real estate broker and is not an appraisal. This evaluation
> cannot be used for the purposes of obtaining financing.'***
>
> *"Pursuant to section 12-10-602(9)(b)(II), C.R.S, **Brokers are PROHIBITED from completing CMAs or BPOs
> that are used for the purpose of obtaining financing.** Preparation of CMAs or BPOs for reasons other than
> anticipated sale, purchase, or lease **is not considered Real Estate Brokerage Services.** As such, any
> compensation received for such preparation **is not required to be paid to the Broker's Brokerage Firm
> unless stated otherwise in Brokerage Firm's Office Policy Manual.**"*

**Four things, and Module 02 of the Real Estate Law and Practice course works through them.** The trigger;
the prescribed words; the **prohibition** on CMAs or BPOs used to obtain financing; and the compensation
consequence — **check the office policy manual.**

**And the square footage rule a residential broker meets on every listing.**

chunks.heading: Module 02 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 6.11**: when a broker **advertises the square footage** of a residential property, **including for
> submission to a multiple listing service**, the broker **must disclose the SOURCE ... on the
> COMMISSION-APPROVED FORM.**
>
> **A. Broker measurement.** *"**A Broker is not required to measure** ... If the Broker takes an actual
> measurement, **it does not have to be exact**; however, the Broker's objective **must be to measure
> accurately and calculate competently in a manner that is not misleading**"* — and the broker must
> **disclose the standard, methodology or manner used**; **advise it is for marketing and not for loan,
> valuation or any other purpose**; and **advise that if exact square footage is a concern the property
> should be independently measured.**
>
> **B. Other sources.** Any other source — actual measurement, building plans, prior appraisals, assessor's
> office — **must include the date of issuance, if any**, and be **disclosed in writing in a timely manner on
> the Commission-Approved Form.** *"A Broker **may not provide information to a person from a source known to
> be unreliable** and **is responsible for indicating obvious mismeasurement by others.**"*

**Read Rule 6.11.B's last sentence against Rule 6.10.C's.** **6.10.C** says the broker has **no duty to
investigate** information from the seller or a third-party source. **6.11.B** says the broker **may not use
a source known to be unreliable** and **is responsible for indicating obvious mismeasurement.** **No duty to
investigate is not the same as permission to pass on what you can see is wrong.**

**No Commission-approved square footage form was obtained by this project**, and **no form's contents are
stated anywhere in this build.**

---

## Module 02 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 02
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
*"**a test is required** to establish a participant's satisfactory completion of the statutory requirements
for the Practical Applications Course"*, and **these items are not that test.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 02

Written to the **Commission's Practical Applications qualifying education outline, approved 7 August 2012**,
Topic II and its sub-topics A through D, in the outline's own order and using the outline's own item names —
including *"**Specialty vendors (structural engineer, electricians, industrial hygienists, etc.)**"*. The
hour figure is the Commission's, and the competency footnote is transcribed in full at the head.

**Rules 6.10, 6.11 and 6.12 were read in full** and are transcribed here, together with **§§ 12-10-403,
12-10-404, 12-10-408 and 12-10-410** and **Rules 1.2, 1.3, 5.17, 6.2, 6.3, 6.5, 6.9, 6.13, 6.17, 6.18, 6.21
and 7.1**, from **C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10** and **4 CCR 725-1** (rule version 12355), read on
**2026-08-20** and recorded in `colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **every Commission-approved form**, including the
square footage disclosure form and the Change of Status form; **CP 41** and every **Commission position
statement**; **RESPA**; **C.R.S. §§ 12-10-218, 12-10-304 and 12-10-602**; Colorado's **foreclosure and
public trustee** statutes; its **entity, trust and probate** statutes; the **Appraiser Licensing Act** and
**USPAP**; and **copyright law**, which Rule 6.10.C requires advertising to comply with.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 02
chunks.excerpt:
**No form provision, position statement, referral fee threshold, affiliated business requirement, appraisal
standard, copyright rule, foreclosure procedure or penalty is stated in this module.** The **three days** in
Rule 6.10.D, the **prohibited team-name terms**, the **two independently-owned-and-operated statements**,
and **Rule 6.12's notice** are quoted verbatim from **4 CCR 725-1**.

lessons.title: Colorado Practical Applications — Module 03

chunks.heading: Colorado Practical Applications — Module 03
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Practical Applications — Module 03

## Property management competency

**Course:** Practical Applications (32 hours) · **Instructional hours: 3.0** of 32.0
**Commission outline topic:** **III — Property Management Competency**, allocated **3 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What the Commission's outline puts in Topic III
>
> | Sub-topic | Delivered in |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** Broker relationships and overview of practice | Part A |
> | **B.** Overview of management agreement | Part B |
> | **C.** When the employing broker has to be involved — 1. Office policy; 2. Trust accounts | Part C |
> | **D.** Management reports | Part D |
> | **E.** Specialties — 1. Residential; 2. Office; 3. Commercial properties | Part E |
> | **F.** Federal & State laws | Part F |
> | **G.** Pitfalls | Part G |
>
> **The competency footnote applies**: *"Educators should make sure students understand **how competency is
> gained in each specialty** ... **so no harm is done to a member of the public.**"*
>
> **Property management is the specialty where a broker without competency does the most damage fastest**,
> because it involves **holding other people's money continuously** rather than once per transaction — and
> because the law governing the tenancies themselves is a statute **this project did not read.**

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: A. Broker relationships and overview of practice — outline Topic III.A
chunks.excerpt:
1. State what brokerage relationship arises in property management and how it is established.
2. State what a management agreement must settle.
3. State when the employing broker is necessarily involved.
4. State the trust account rules specific to property management.
5. State the reporting deadline absent a contrary provision.
6. State the vendor conflict disclosure and the three interests it names.
7. Identify the pitfalls the Commission's outline points at, and state which ones this build can answer.

---

## A. Broker relationships and overview of practice — outline Topic III.A

**Property management in Colorado is a brokerage relationship like any other.** **§§ 12-10-404 and
12-10-405** speak of *"seller **or landlord**"* and *"buyer **or tenant**"* throughout, so the duty lists run
to a management relationship in their own terms — and **§ 12-10-403(2)** applies: a broker is a
**transaction-broker unless single agency is established through a WRITTEN agreement.**

**What that means at the outset.** A property manager engaged by an owner who signs a management agreement
establishing single agency is the **landlord's agent** under § 12-10-404. One who signs nothing establishing
agency is a **transaction-broker** — **not an agent for either party**, under § 12-10-407(1).

**And the disclosure timing is the same:** **Rule 6.5.A** requires the written § 12-10-408 disclosure
**before eliciting or discussing confidential information**, which in a management context arrives early —
the moment the conversation moves from *"what do units like this rent for"* to the owner's finances or
motives.

**Two structural points a residential broker moving into management has to absorb.**

chunks.heading: B. Overview of the management agreement — outline Topic III.B
chunks.excerpt:
**First, the money is continuous.** Rent arrives monthly, deposits are held for years, and the trust account
is never empty. **Every rule in Chapter 5 is live all the time**, not just around a closing.

**Second, there are two customers.** The **owner** is the client. The **tenant** is not — but the tenant's
deposit is the tenant's money, and **Rule 5.8** protects it specifically.

---

## B. Overview of the management agreement — outline Topic III.B

**What it must settle**, delivered at greater length in **Real Estate Law and Practice Module 05 Part D.1**:

1. **Parties**, and the property managed.
2. **Term**, and how it ends.
3. **The manager's authority** — including a **dollar threshold** above which repairs need the owner's
   approval.
4. **Compensation** — how calculated, when taken, out of what.
5. **Trust accounting** — which accounts, and how reported.
6. **Owner reserves** — how much, what for, and when replenished.
7. **Reporting** — what reports, and **when**.
8. **Leasing authority** — the terms the manager may accept.
9. **Maintenance and vendors** — who selects, who pays, and **what disclosures**.
10. **Insurance and indemnity.**
11. **Termination** — including **what happens to funds and documents.**

**Three of those eleven are settled by rule if the agreement is silent**, and a manager should know which:

chunks.heading: B. Overview of the management agreement — outline Topic III.B
chunks.excerpt:
> **Item 5 — accounting method.** **Rule 5.16**: *"In the absence of a written agreement to the contrary, the
> **'cash basis' of accounting MUST BE USED**"*; another method requires **written agreement with the
> beneficiary** and **separate accounts and records** for that beneficiary.
>
> **Item 7 — reporting.** **Rule 5.15.A**: reports go out **as the management agreement provides**, and *"in
> the absence of a provision in the Management Agreement to the contrary ... **WITHIN THIRTY (30) DAYS after
> the end of the month in which funds were either received or disbursed.**"*
>
> **Item 11 — deposits on termination.** **Rule 5.8.A**: a firm receipting for security deposits *"**will not
> deliver such security deposits to an owner without the tenant's written authorization in a lease or unless
> written notice has been given to the tenant**"* — telling the tenant **who is holding the deposit** and
> **the specific requirements for the procedure in which the tenant may request return.** If the deposit
> does go to the owner, the management agreement **should** place financial responsibility for its return on
> the owner and **must** authorize disclosure of the owner's **true name and current mailing address** in a
> dispute.

chunks.heading: C. When the employing broker has to be involved — outline Topic III.C
chunks.excerpt:
> **A gate stated here because a manager meets it on day one.** **C.R.S. § 38-12-101 et seq., the Colorado
> Landlord Tenant Act, was NOT read by this project.** **This course states NO rule on**: security deposit
> limits; deposit return periods or the consequences of wrongful withholding; notice to enter; habitability;
> late fees; repair and deduct; retaliation; lease termination notice; eviction or unlawful detainer
> procedure; or any tenant remedy.
>
> **Any figure or period a manager writes into a lease or a management agreement comes from the statute, the
> firm's forms, and counsel — not from this course.**

---

## C. When the employing broker has to be involved — outline Topic III.C

### C.1 Office policy — III.C.1

**Rule 6.3.B.3** requires the employing broker to **develop the firm's written policies** under **Rule 6.4**.
**Rule 5.1** requires **written accounting control policies and procedures** with **checks and balances over
the financial activities of the broker, the firm and unlicensed persons**, managing the **risk of fraud or
illegal acts.**

**In a management operation the policy has to answer questions a sales-only firm never asks:** who may sign
on the trust accounts; who reconciles them; what a manager may spend without the owner's approval; how
