vendors are selected and how conflicts are disclosed; how deposits are handled on move-out; and what happens
when a ledger is about to go negative.

### C.2 Trust accounts — III.C.2

**This is the part of the outline where the employing broker's involvement is not optional.**

chunks.heading: C.2 Trust accounts — III.C.2
chunks.excerpt:
> **Rule 5.3.C**: the **Employing Broker or Independent Broker** are *"**responsible for, must maintain and
> be able to withdraw money from each separate account**"*, and may authorise cosigners — *"**However, such
> authorization will not relieve the Employing Broker or Independent Broker of any responsibility.**"*
>
> **Rule 5.22**: *"The **Employing Broker or Independent Broker are held JOINTLY RESPONSIBLE with the
> Brokerage Firm** in complying with Chapter 5 of these Rules."*
>
> **Rule 6.3.B.1**: employing brokers must **maintain all trust and escrow accounts and records as set forth
> in Chapter 5.**
>
> **Record Keeping outline, Topic III.A.2**: *"**Broker's need to personally perform bank reconciliations or
> periodically compare reconciliations against source documents (transaction files).**"*

**The property management rules specifically:**

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **5.5** | **Separate** trust or escrow accounts — **a minimum of one for rental receipts and a minimum of one for security deposits** |
| **5.7.A** | Property management money deposited **no later than FIVE BUSINESS DAYS** after receipt **or mutual execution of a lease, whichever is later** — where **5.7.B** gives all other money **three** |
| **5.9** | Money belonging to **one beneficiary must not be used for another's**, or for the firm |
| **5.10.A** | Money **due and payable to the firm** must be **withdrawn MONTHLY** |
| **5.10.C** | Fees are *"earned"* and available **only after all contracted services are performed and there is no remaining right of recall** |
| **5.14.B** | *"**No ledger may ever be allowed to have a negative cash balance**"*, and the **sum of ledger balances must agree with the journal AT ALL TIMES** after each posting |
| **5.14.C** | **Three-way reconciliati

chunks.heading: D. Management reports — outline Topic III.D
chunks.excerpt:
on MONTHLY**, with a report **completed and maintained** |
| **5.11** | Money for **non-brokerage** activities — **guest deposits for short-term rentals**, **deposits on the broker's own rentals**, **buyer deposits where the broker is acting as a builder** — **still goes into a trust or escrow account** |
| **5.10.D and E** | Rental proceeds on a **broker's own property**, with the **20 percent** threshold in **§ 12-10-201(6)(b)(VII)** deciding what counts as the broker's |

**The Record Keeping and Trust Accounts course delivers all of these**, and its Commission outline requires
an exercise in which the student *"shall **reconcile the bank accounts for a property manager managing and
holding security deposits for a MINIMUM OF 8 PROPERTIES.**"*

---

## D. Management reports — outline Topic III.D

> **Rule 5.15.A**: firms holding Money Belonging to Others *"**must provide DETAILED reports to each
> beneficiary.**"* Reports are prepared and delivered **according to the management agreement**; absent a
> contrary provision, **within 30 days after the end of the month** in which funds were received or
> disbursed.
>
> **Rule 5.15.B**: the firm **must maintain supporting records accurately detailing all cash received and
> disbursed** under any management agreement —
> **1.** every **deposit must identify each person tendering funds, the amount, the types of funds received
> from each person, and the PROPERTY ADDRESS affected**; and
> **2.** every **disbursement must be supported by documents such as bids, invoices, contracts, etc.**, with
> ledger and journal records **identifying the payees, property addresses affected and amount transferred
> for each property.**

chunks.heading: E. Specialties — outline Topic III.E
chunks.excerpt:
**A report that says "maintenance — $840" and cannot be traced to an invoice does not satisfy 5.15.B.2.**
Every disbursement has a document behind it, and the property address is on both sides of the record.

**And Rule 5.10.C's schedule requirement** where a single disbursement of fees or commissions covers more
than one transaction, rental period, occupancy or beneficiary: the firm must, **on request**, produce a
schedule detailing the **individual components** and **identifying the affected beneficiary or property
ledgers.**

---

## E. Specialties — outline Topic III.E

The outline names **residential**, **office**, and **commercial properties**, with the competency footnote
attached.

| Specialty | What differs |
|---|---|
| **Residential** | Tenancies governed by Colorado's landlord-tenant statutes — **NOT read by this project**; deposits held per tenant; fair housing exposure in screening; turnover-driven |
| **Office** | Longer leases; **net** structures with expense pass-throughs; tenant improvement allowances; common area maintenance reconciliation |
| **Commercial** | The above, plus percentage rent, use and exclusivity clauses, co-tenancy, and the buyer's or tenant's own due diligence |

**The competency point the Commission is making with this list:** the three are **not interchangeable**. A
manager competent in residential turnover is not thereby competent to reconcile CAM on an office building
or to administer a percentage rent clause — and **Rule 6.2.B** gives the four routes.

chunks.heading: F. Federal and state laws — outline Topic III.F
chunks.excerpt:
**And one commercial-specific relief in the duty rules is worth knowing**, though it belongs to Module 04:
**§ 12-10-405** and the commercial exception in other states have no Colorado analogue read for this build.
**Colorado's own statute states no commercial carve-out from the brokerage relationship requirements in any
provision read for this build**, and **none is stated here.**

---

## F. Federal and state laws — outline Topic III.F

**The outline names the subject; this build states which laws it read.**

| Law | Read? | What this build states |
|---|---|---|
| **Federal Fair Housing Act** | **No** | The **seven protected classes** and the prohibited practices, in **Real Estate Law and Practice Module 03 Part F.1** — **no exemption, threshold, remedy or procedure** |
| **Colorado Fair Housing Act** | **No** | **Nothing** — **no additional protected class, exemption or remedy** |
| **C.R.S. § 38-12-101 et seq.** | **No** | **Nothing** — see the gate in Part B |
| **Colorado eviction / unlawful detainer** | **No** | **Nothing** |
| **Americans with Disabilities Act** | **No** | That it governs **public accommodations and commercial facilities** and is **not** the Fair Housing Act — **no standard, dimension or deadline** |
| **Federal lead-based paint regulations** | **No** | **Nothing** — named at the Current Legal Issues outline's Appendix E |
| **4 CCR 725-1 Chapters 5 and 6** | **YES, in full** | Everything in Parts C, D and G of this module |
| **§§ 12-10-402 to 12-10-411** | **YES, in full** | Part A |

chunks.heading: G. Pitfalls — outline Topic III.G
chunks.excerpt:
**What the statute does say, and it was read:** **§§ 12-10-404(1)(e), 12-10-405(1)(e) and 12-10-407(2)(d)**
each require the broker to comply with applicable federal, state and local law *"**including fair housing
and civil rights statutes or regulations**"* — so a fair housing failure in tenant screening is **also** a
brokerage relationship violation, and **§ 12-10-411** makes any Part 4 violation an act the Commission may
investigate.

**The screening discipline that follows:** **one written set of criteria, applied to every applicant in the
same order, with the result recorded.**

---

## G. Pitfalls — outline Topic III.G

The outline names the topic and leaves it to the provider. **These are the pitfalls the rules read for this
build actually describe**, each with the provision that makes it one.

| Pitfall | The rule |
|---|---|
| **A negative ledger, even for a day** | **Rule 5.14.B** — *"no ledger may ever be allowed to have a negative cash balance"*; and **Rule 5.9**, because the shortfall is another beneficiary's money |
| **Rental receipts and security deposits in one account** | **Rule 5.5** — a minimum of one account for each |
| **Missing the five-business-day deposit deadline** | **Rule 5.7.A** — and the journal's **two dates** (received and deposited) are what prove it either way |
| **Taking a fee before it is earned** | **Rule 5.10.C** — *"only after all contracted services have been performed and there is no remaining right of recall"* |
| **Leaving an earned fee in the trust account past month end** | **Rule 5.10.A** — **withdrawn monthly**; commingling in the other direction |
| **Handing an owner the tenant's deposit** | **Rule 5.8.A** — not without the **tenant's written authorization in a lease or written notice** |
| **Taking over a portfolio wit

chunks.heading: G. Pitfalls — outline Topic III.G
chunks.excerpt:
hout checking the deposits** | **Rule 5.8.B** — **30 days** to disclose, **60 days** for the previous firm to transfer, and the new firm **verifies each against the current lease and discloses any discrepancy** |
| **Sending maintenance to a company the manager has an interest in, silently** | **Rule 6.17.C** — a duty to **disclose in writing any known conflict of interest in the selection or use of a business or vendor**, including **any ownership, financial, or familial interest** |
| **Marking up a repair without consent** | **Rule 5.17** — **prior written consent** from the consumer represented, **disclosure** of mark-ups paid by any customer, and **records verifying both** |
| **A report the owner cannot trace to invoices** | **Rule 5.15.B.2** — disbursements **supported by documents** |
| **Managing the broker's own property in the same accounts** | **Rules 5.10.D and E**, with the **20 percent** threshold |
| **No written accounting controls** | **Rule 5.1** — written, reaching **unlicensed persons**, managing the **risk of fraud** |
| **Advertising a unit without authority** | **Rule 6.10.F** — *"**Brokers may not Advertise the availability or price of a property whether for sale or lease without authority from the owner or the owner's Broker.**"* |
| **Quoting a price the owner did not agree** | **Rule 6.10.G** — *"the price quoted in any Advertising will not be anything other than the price agreed upon between the Broker and the owner"* |
| **An expired listing left up** | **Rule 6.10.D.1 and D.2** — removed within **three days**, including a **written request to third-party syndicators** |

chunks.heading: Module 03 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**Fourteen pitfalls, every one of them stateable from rules this project read in full** — and **not one of
them requiring the landlord-tenant statute.** That is the honest shape of what this course can teach: **the
money and the disclosure rules completely, and the tenancy law not at all.**

---

## Module 03 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
*"**a test is required** to establish a participant's satisfactory completion of the statutory requirements
for the Practical Applications Course"*, and **these items are not that test.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 03

Written to the **Commission's Practical Applications qualifying education outline, approved 7 August 2012**,
Topic III and its sub-topics A through G, in the outline's own order and using the outline's own item names.
The hour figure is the Commission's, and the competency footnote applies.

**Chapter 5 of 4 CCR 725-1 was read in full**, together with **Rules 6.2, 6.3, 6.5, 6.10, 6.17 and 6.20**
and **§§ 12-10-201(6)(b)(VII), 12-10-403, 12-10-404, 12-10-405, 12-10-407, 12-10-408 and 12-10-411**, on
**2026-08-20**, and recorded in `colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 03
chunks.excerpt:
**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **C.R.S. § 38-12-101 et seq.** in its entirety;
Colorado's **eviction and unlawful detainer** statutes; the **Colorado Fair Housing Act**; the **federal Fair
Housing Act**; the **Americans with Disabilities Act**; the **federal lead-based paint regulations**; **CP
41** and every **Commission position statement**; and **every Commission-approved form**, including any
lease or management agreement form.

**No deposit limit, return period, notice period, entry requirement, habitability standard, late fee,
eviction timeline, occupancy standard, tenant remedy, protected class beyond the seven federal classes,
accessibility standard or lead-based paint requirement is stated in this module.** The **five business
days**, **three business days**, **30 days**, **60 days**, **monthly** withdrawal and reconciliation, **three
days** in Rule 6.10.D, and **20 percent** threshold are transcribed from **4 CCR 725-1** and **C.R.S.
§ 12-10-201(6)(b)(VII)**.

lessons.title: Colorado Practical Applications — Module 04

chunks.heading: Colorado Practical Applications — Module 04
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Practical Applications — Module 04

## Commercial competency

**Course:** Practical Applications (32 hours) · **Instructional hours: 2.0** of 32.0
**Commission outline topic:** **IV — Commercial Competency**, allocated **2 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What the Commission's outline puts in Topic IV
>
> | Sub-topic | Delivered in |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** Broker relationships and overview of practice | Part A |
> | **B.** Elements of commercial real estate | Part B |
> | **C.** Financial composition of commercial real estate | Part C |
> | **D.** Marketing | Part D |
> | **E.** Leasing | Part E |
> | **F.** Pitfalls | Part F |
>
> **The competency footnote applies**: *"Educators should make sure students understand **how competency is
> gained in each specialty** ... **so no harm is done to a member of the public.**"*
>
> **Two hours, and the Commission's purpose is not to make a commercial broker.** It is to make a
> residential broker able to **recognise that a commercial transaction is not a residential one** and to
> act on **Rule 6.2** rather than proceed.

## Learning objectives

1. State what brokerage relationship arises in a commercial transaction and how it is established.
2. Name the property types and the elements that distinguish commercial from residential work.
3. Compute the financial measures a commercial party will expect, from given figures.
4. State the advertising rules that apply to commercial marketing.
5. State what a commercial lease settles that a residential lease does not.
6. Identify the pitfalls and state which of them this build can answer from primary text.

---

chunks.heading: A. Broker relationships and overview of practice — outline Topic IV.A
chunks.excerpt:
## A. Broker relationships and overview of practice — outline Topic IV.A

**Colorado's brokerage relationship statute makes NO commercial exception in any provision read for this
build.**

That is worth stating plainly because **other states do**. This project's Washington build records that
**RCW 18.86.020(3)** removes the services-agreement requirement where a broker acts as a buyer's agent
*"solely for commercial real estate"*, substituting a written compensation disclosure. **Colorado's
§§ 12-10-403 through 12-10-411 contain no analogous carve-out in the text read**, and **no module of this
build states one.**

**So the same rules apply, in the same order:**

| Provision | In a commercial transaction |
|---|---|
| **§ 12-10-403(2)** | **Transaction-broker by default** unless single agency is established **in writing** |
| **§ 12-10-406** | **Dual agency prohibited** — and **Rule 6.7**'s three lawful configurations |
| **§§ 12-10-404 / 405 / 407** | The duty lists, including **presenting all offers regardless** of an existing contract **or LETTER OF INTENT** |
| **§ 12-10-408** and **Rule 6.5** | The disclosures, **before eliciting or discussing confidential information** |
| **§ 12-10-409** | Duration, with the **one-year** backstop |
| **§ 12-10-410** | Compensation — **payment does not establish agency**; the **buyer-side written approval** in (5); the **identity disclosure before** the agreement in (6) |
| **Rule 6.2** | Competency — **decline**, **obtain**, **obtain assistance**, or **co-list** |

**Note the letters of intent.** **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(I) and (II), 12-10-405(1)(c)(I) and (II) and
12-10-407(2)(b)(I)** each mention **a letter of intent to lease** alongside a contract for sale — the
statute contemplates the commercial practice expressly.

chunks.heading: B. Elements of commercial real estate — outline Topic IV.B
chunks.excerpt:
**And § 12-10-403(4)(b)(VIII)** authorises a broker to complete **a letter of intent** as a standard form
*"**so long as the letter of intent states on its face that it is nonbinding and creates no legal rights or
obligations.**"* **That sentence is a requirement, not a description.**

---

## B. Elements of commercial real estate — outline Topic IV.B

| Type | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Office** | Space let by the square foot, ordinarily on multi-year leases with expense structures |
| **Retail** | Space where the tenant's **sales** matter to the landlord — percentage rent, co-tenancy, exclusivity |
| **Industrial** | Warehouse, distribution, manufacturing — clear height, loading, power, zoning |
| **Multi-family** | Income residential — **and note it sits in both worlds**, since the tenancies are residential |
| **Land** | Held for development, with entitlement, access and utilities as the value drivers |
| **Special purpose** | Built for one use, with few comparable sales — where the **cost approach** does the work |

**What differs from a residential transaction, item by item:**

chunks.heading: C. Financial composition — outline Topic IV.C
chunks.excerpt:
| Element | Commercial |
|---|---|
| **The buyer's decision basis** | **Income and return**, not preference |
| **Due diligence** | Longer, and its own contingency — surveys, environmental review, leases and estoppels, financials, zoning and entitlement |
| **Leases in place** | The buyer is buying **the leases**, and inherits every term in them |
| **Environmental** | A phase of the diligence rather than an incident of it |
| **Financing** | Underwritten against the **property's income**, with different terms and often recourse questions |
| **Documents** | Letters of intent; estoppel certificates; subordination, non-disturbance and attornment agreements; assignment of leases |
| **Timeframe** | Longer, at every stage |

> **A gate stated plainly.** **No Colorado environmental statute, zoning or land use statute, or local
> ordinance was read by this project**, and **none of the federal environmental statutes was read.** **No
> requirement, standard, threshold, liability rule, procedure or deadline from any of them is stated
> anywhere in this build.**
>
> What **was** read is the disclosure duty: **§§ 12-10-404(3)(a), 12-10-405(3)(a) and 12-10-407(2)(b)(VI)**
> each require disclosure of **adverse material facts ACTUALLY KNOWN**, expressly including *"**any
> environmental hazards affecting the property that are required by law to be disclosed**"* — and
> **§§ 12-10-404(3)(b), 12-10-405(5) and 12-10-407(4)** each provide there is **no duty to inspect or
> verify.**

---

## C. Financial composition — outline Topic IV.C

**A commercial party will expect these figures and will expect them right.** Every figure below is supplied
as a given.

### C.1 The income statement

chunks.heading: C.2 Worked
chunks.excerpt:
| Line | |
|---|---|
| **Potential gross income** | Full occupancy, full collection |
| less **vacancy and collection loss** | |
| plus **other income** | Parking, storage, fees |
| = **Effective gross income** | |
| less **operating expenses** | Fixed, variable, and reserves — **not** debt service, depreciation or capital improvements |
| = **Net operating income** | The property measure |
| less **debt service** | |
| = **Cash flow before tax** | The equity measure |

### C.2 Worked

> **A 22,000 square foot office building.** Rent **$26.00 per square foot per year**. Vacancy and collection
> loss **8 percent**. Other income **$14,000**. Operating expenses **$196,000**. A loan with annual debt
> service of **$183,000**. Purchase price **$4,150,000**, with **$1,245,000** of equity.
>
> | Line | Calculation | Amount |
> |---|---|---|
> | Potential gross income | 22,000 × $26.00 | **$572,000** |
> | less vacancy and collection loss | 8% of 572,000 | (45,760) |
> | plus other income | | 14,000 |
> | **Effective gross income** | | **$540,240** |
> | less operating expenses | | (196,000) |
> | **Net operating income** | | **$344,240** |
> | less debt service | | (183,000) |
> | **Cash flow before tax** | | **$161,240** |

**The three measures a commercial party asks for, from those figures:**

> **Capitalisation rate** = NOI ÷ price = **$344,240 ÷ $4,150,000 = 8.29 percent** (to two decimals).
>
> **Cash-on-cash return** = cash flow before tax ÷ equity = **$161,240 ÷ $1,245,000 = 12.95 percent.**
>
> **Debt coverage ratio** = NOI ÷ debt service = **$344,240 ÷ $183,000 = 1.88.**

chunks.heading: D. Marketing — outline Topic IV.D
chunks.excerpt:
**The capitalisation rate measures the PROPERTY; the cash-on-cash return measures THIS BUYER'S POSITION.** A
client who conflates them will misjudge leverage in both directions. **The debt coverage ratio is the
lender's figure**, and it is why a lender may decline a purchase the buyer's own arithmetic supports.

**Expense ratio** = operating expenses ÷ effective gross income = **$196,000 ÷ $540,240 = 36.28 percent** —
the figure a buyer compares across candidate properties.

**A broker can do all of this with figures the parties and the lender supply.** What a broker does **not**
do is tell the client whether the investment is right for them: **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V), 12-10-405(1)(c)(V)
and 12-10-407(2)(b)(II)** each require **advising the party to obtain expert advice** on material matters
beyond the broker's expertise, and **tax treatment, entity structure and financing suitability are all
outside it.**

---

## D. Marketing — outline Topic IV.D

**Rule 6.10 applies in full to commercial marketing**, and three of its subsections bite hardest here.

chunks.heading: D. Marketing — outline Topic IV.D
chunks.excerpt:
> **6.10.F — authority.** *"**Brokers may not Advertise the availability or price of a property whether for
> sale or lease WITHOUT AUTHORITY FROM THE OWNER OR THE OWNER'S BROKER.**"* An owner's broker **may not
> withhold** it unless doing so is **contradictory to the owner's instructions as memorialized in the
> listing contract or other writing.** Disseminating **another broker's** advertising requires that broker's
> **written permission** and **conspicuous disclosure of the owner's firm**; disseminating an
> **unrepresented owner's** advertising requires the **owner's written permission**, **conspicuous
> disclosure that the owner is not represented**, and **must not include submitting the information into a
> property exchange or multiple listing service.**
>
> **6.10.G — price.** *"**The price quoted in any Advertising will not be anything other than the price
> agreed upon between the Broker and the owner.**"*
>
> **6.10.C — accuracy.** Firms and brokers are **responsible for ensuring all advertising is accurate**,
> including **information entered into multiple listing services** — with **no duty to investigate**
> information from the seller or a third-party source.
>
> **6.10.E — past sales data.** Sales recaps for a subdivision or area **must cite the source** and **carry
> the disclaimer**, if accurate, that the sales **were not necessarily listed or sold by the broker** and
> **are intended only to show trends** or **will separately identify the broker's own activity.** Commercial
> brokers publish market reports; **this is the rule that governs them.**

chunks.heading: E. Leasing — outline Topic IV.E
chunks.excerpt:
**And confidentiality constrains what may be said about a live deal.** **§ 12-10-404(2)** and
**§ 12-10-405(2)** each forbid disclosing, without informed consent, that a party **will accept less or pay
more**, their **motivating factors**, or that they **will agree to other financing terms** — and
**§ 12-10-407(3)** binds a transaction-broker to a **six-item** list requiring the **informed consent of all
parties.**

---

## E. Leasing — outline Topic IV.E

**What a commercial lease settles that a residential lease does not:**

| Term | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Rentable vs. usable area, and the load factor** | Decides what the tenant pays for versus occupies |
| **The expense structure** | **Gross**, **net**, or a **base year with escalations** — and *"net"* alone settles nothing until the document says **which** expenses |
| **CAM reconciliation** | How common area costs are estimated, billed and trued up |
| **Percentage rent** | A base rent plus a percentage of sales over a **breakpoint** |
| **Tenant improvement allowance** | Who builds, who pays, and who owns the improvements at the end |
| **Use and exclusivity** | What the tenant may do, and what the landlord may not let a neighbour do |
| **Co-tenancy** | Relief if anchor tenants leave |
| **Assignment and subletting** | Ordinarily conditional on the landlord's consent |
| **Options** | To renew, expand, terminate, or purchase |
| **Estoppel and SNDA** | What the tenant certifies to a buyer or lender, and how the lease survives a foreclosure |
| **Guaranty** | Who stands behind the tenant entity |

chunks.heading: F. Pitfalls — outline Topic IV.F
chunks.excerpt:
**Percentage rent worked, figures given:** base rent **$7,500** a month plus **6 percent** of gross sales
over a **$125,000** monthly breakpoint. In a month with **$210,000** of sales the overage is **$85,000**, the
percentage rent is **$5,100**, and total rent is **$12,600.**

**A load factor worked, figures given:** a suite of **8,400 usable** square feet in a building with a
**15 percent** load factor is **8,400 × 1.15 = 9,660 rentable** square feet. At **$28.00** per rentable
square foot the annual base rent is **$270,480** — **$32.20 per USABLE foot**, which is the number the
tenant actually feels.

> **A gate.** **No Colorado commercial landlord-tenant statute was read by this project**, and **no rule on
> commercial deposits, notice, default, remedies or eviction is stated anywhere in this build.** Commercial
> leases are heavily negotiated documents, and **the lease itself is prepared by counsel** — it is not among
> the eight kinds of standard form **§ 12-10-403(4)(b)** authorises a broker to complete unless a
> Commission-approved form exists and is appropriate, or another category applies.

---

## F. Pitfalls — outline Topic IV.F

chunks.heading: F. Pitfalls — outline Topic IV.F
chunks.excerpt:
| Pitfall | The rule or the reason |
|---|---|
| **Treating a letter of intent as harmless** | **§ 12-10-403(4)(b)(VIII)** — a broker-prepared LOI **must state on its face that it is nonbinding and creates no legal rights or obligations** |
| **Assuming commercial work is outside the relationship rules** | **§ 12-10-403(2)** applies; **no commercial carve-out appears in any provision read for this build** |
| **Advertising a listing or a price without authority** | **Rule 6.10.F and G** |
| **A market report with no source and no disclaimer** | **Rule 6.10.E** |
| **Disclosing a party's position to move a deal along** | **§§ 12-10-404(2), 12-10-405(2), 12-10-407(3)** |
| **Quoting a capitalisation rate as though it were a fact about the property** | It is derived from **price and NOI**, both of which are inputs the parties supply |
| **Advising on tax, entity structure or suitability** | **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V), 12-10-405(1)(c)(V), 12-10-407(2)(b)(II)** — advise the party to **obtain expert advice** |
| **Taking a commercial engagement without commercial competency** | **Rule 6.2.B** — **decline**, obtain, obtain assistance, or **co-list** |
| **Missing that the buyer is buying the leases** | Estoppels and lease review are the diligence; a lease term the buyer did not read is a term they now own |
| **Treating environmental review as optional** | The **duty to disclose actually known** adverse material facts including environmental hazards — and **no duty to investigate** is not a reason for a buyer to skip diligence |

chunks.heading: Module 04 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**The last row is the competency point of the whole module.** A residential broker's instinct — that
inspection is a contingency the buyer either exercises or waives — **does not transfer.** In commercial work
the diligence **is** the transaction, and a broker who does not know that should be reaching for **Rule
6.2.B.4 — co-list** — before the letter of intent goes out.

---

## Module 04 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
*"**a test is required** to establish a participant's satisfactory completion of the statutory requirements
for the Practical Applications Course"*, and **these items are not that test.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 04

Written to the **Commission's Practical Applications qualifying education outline, approved 7 August 2012**,
Topic IV and its sub-topics A through F, in the outline's own order. The hour figure is the Commission's,
and the competency footnote applies.

The provisions quoted — **§§ 12-10-403, 12-10-404, 12-10-405, 12-10-406, 12-10-407, 12-10-408, 12-10-409 and
12-10-410** and **Rules 6.2, 6.5, 6.7 and 6.10** — are transcribed from **C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10** and
**4 CCR 725-1** (rule version 12355), read on **2026-08-20** and recorded in
`colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`. The comparison to Washington is to that state's own statute
as read and recorded in this project's Washington readings file.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 04
chunks.excerpt:
**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** every **federal and Colorado environmental
statute**; Colorado's **zoning, land use and subdivision** statutes and every **local ordinance**; any
Colorado **commercial landlord-tenant** provision; the **Americans with Disabilities Act**; **every federal
tax provision**; the **UCC** and **U.C.C.C.**; **federal securities law**; and **every Commission-approved
form**, including any letter of intent, lease or commercial contract form.

chunks.heading: Colorado Practical Applications — Module 05
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Practical Applications — Module 05

## Other competency

**Course:** Practical Applications (32 hours) · **Instructional hours: 1.0** of 32.0
**Commission outline topic:** **V — Other Competency**, allocated **1 hour**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### What the Commission's outline puts in Topic V
>
> | Sub-topic | Delivered in |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** Business opportunities | Part A |
> | **B.** Oil and Gas leasing | Part B |
> | **C.** Farm and Ranch | Part C |
>
> **One hour for three specialties, and the competency footnote applies to all three:** *"Educators should
> make sure students understand **how competency is gained in each specialty** ... **so no harm is done to a
> member of the public.**"*
>
> **The Commission is not trying to make a broker competent in any of these in twenty minutes.** It is
> making sure a broker **recognises** each one as a specialty and reaches for **Rule 6.2** rather than
> proceeding.
>
> **This is the module where this build has the least to state from primary text and says so on every
> page.** All three specialties turn on Colorado statutes **this project did not read.**

## Learning objectives

1. State what a business opportunity transaction involves and what makes it different.
2. State what an oil and gas lease is and why severed mineral interests matter in Colorado.
3. State why water rights make farm and ranch a specialty in Colorado.
4. For each, state which Colorado law governs and identify it as unread.
5. State the four routes in Rule 6.2.B and apply them to a specialty engagement.

---

## A. Business opportunities — outline Topic V.A

### A.1 What it is

chunks.heading: A.2 What Colorado law says, and what this build read
chunks.excerpt:
**The sale or purchase of a business**, which in a real estate broker's hands ordinarily involves **real
property** — owned or leased — **plus** everything else the business consists of.

| Component | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Real property** | Owned, or a **leasehold** the buyer must succeed to |
| **Tangible personal property** | Equipment, fixtures, inventory |
| **Intangibles** | Goodwill, trade name, customer lists, contracts |
| **Intellectual property** | Marks, copyrights, licences |
| **Licences and permits** | Often **not transferable**, and often the thing that stops the deal |
| **Contracts and leases** | Assignable, or not |
| **Employees** | Retained, or not |
| **Liabilities** | Assumed, or excluded |

**The structural question that governs everything else: is this an ASSET sale or an EQUITY sale?** An asset
sale transfers named assets; an equity sale transfers the entity and everything in it, including
liabilities the buyer may not know about. **That is a legal and tax question and it is not the broker's.**

### A.2 What Colorado law says, and what this build read

**§ 12-10-201(6)** — the definition of the activities requiring a licence — reaches transactions involving
**a business opportunity that owns an interest in real estate or in a leasehold**, with an exemption for
**broker-dealers licensed under article 51 of title 11** actually engaged generally in the securities
business.

**And § 12-10-403(4)(a)** authorises a broker to complete standard forms *"**including standard forms
intended to convey personal property as part of the real estate transaction.**"*

chunks.heading: A.3 What a broker does
chunks.excerpt:
> **NOT READ, and stated nowhere in this build:** the **UCC** — including secured transactions and bulk
> transfers; the **U.C.C.C.**, named by the Contracts and Regulations outline at Topic V.F.2; **federal and
> Colorado securities law** beyond the § 12-10-201(6) exemption's existence; Colorado's **entity, trust and
> probate** statutes; **every tax provision**; and **every licensing and permitting statute** governing any
> particular trade.
>
> **No requirement, threshold, exemption, filing, notice, tax treatment or penalty from any of them is
> stated anywhere in this build.**

### A.3 What a broker does

**Recognise that an equity sale, a securities question, a liquor or professional licence, or an assumed
liability is not a real estate question** — and apply **Rule 6.2.B**: **decline**; **obtain** the
experience, training and knowledge; **obtain the assistance** of the employing broker, a supervisory broker,
a competent broker **or legal counsel competent in the matter**; or **co-list.**

**And the duty that runs alongside:** **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V), 12-10-405(1)(c)(V) and 12-10-407(2)(b)(II)**
each require **advising the party to obtain expert advice** as to material matters known to the broker but
whose specifics are beyond the broker's expertise. **A business sale generates several of those in the first
meeting.**

---

## B. Oil and gas leasing — outline Topic V.B

### B.1 Why the Commission names it

**In Colorado, mineral interests are frequently SEVERED from the surface**, and the person who owns the
house may not own what is beneath it.

chunks.heading: B.2 Why it reaches an ordinary residential broker
chunks.excerpt:
**An oil and gas lease** grants a lessee the right to explore for and produce oil and gas from a tract, in
exchange for a bonus, delay rentals and a **royalty**. The terms a party will encounter — the **primary
term**, the **habendum** or "so long as produced" clause, **pooling and unitisation**, **surface use**, and
the **royalty fraction** — are the substance of the instrument.

### B.2 Why it reaches an ordinary residential broker

**Because a residential buyer may be buying a surface estate whose minerals belong to someone else, and
because that someone else may have rights to use the surface.**

That is a fact about the property, and Colorado's duty rules speak to facts about the property:

> **§ 12-10-404(3)(a)** — a seller's agent must **disclose to any prospective buyer all ADVERSE MATERIAL
> FACTS ACTUALLY KNOWN** by the broker, *"including but not limited to adverse material facts pertaining to
> **the title** and the physical condition of the property."*
>
> **§ 12-10-407(2)(b)(VI)** — the same for a transaction-broker.
>
> **§§ 12-10-404(3)(b) and 12-10-407(4)** — and **no duty to conduct an independent inspection** or to
> **verify** statements made by the seller or an independent inspector.

**"Actually known" and "no duty to investigate" together mean a broker who knows discloses, and a broker who
does not know is not required by these sections to go and find out — but Rule 6.2.A requires the experience,
training and knowledge to serve the market they are in**, and in parts of Colorado severed minerals are
ordinary.

**Where the answer comes from:** the **title commitment**, whose **Schedule B-2 exceptions** are where a
mineral reservation appears — read in the **Closings** course, Module 03 Part B — and **counsel.**

chunks.heading: C. Farm and ranch — outline Topic V.C
chunks.excerpt:
> **NOT READ, and stated nowhere in this build:** Colorado's **oil and gas statutes**; its **severed mineral
> interest**, **surface use** and **dormant mineral** provisions; every **Colorado Oil and Gas Conservation
> Commission** rule; every **local ordinance** governing operations; and every **disclosure requirement**
> attaching to mineral estates.
>
> **No royalty fraction, term, pooling rule, setback, notice, disclosure requirement or procedure is stated
> anywhere in this build.**

---

## C. Farm and ranch — outline Topic V.C

### C.1 Why it is a specialty, and it is not mainly about acreage

**The Commission names water rights in TWO of its six outlines** — here by implication, and expressly at
**Contracts and Regulations Topic V.E** and **Real Estate Law and Practice Topic I.A.1.a.** That repetition
is the signal.

> **Water rights in the western states may be owned, conveyed, leased and encumbered SEPARATELY FROM THE
> LAND.** A right to divert and use water is a distinct property interest. **It does not necessarily pass
> with a conveyance of the parcel**, and a contract that says nothing about it may have transferred nothing.
>
> **Getting it wrong can transfer a farm without the means of irrigating it** — which is the clearest
> example in this whole build of the Commission's phrase *"so no harm is done to a member of the public."*

### C.2 What else distinguishes the work

chunks.heading: C.3 What this build states, and what it does not
chunks.excerpt:
| Element | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **Water** | As above — and the single largest value driver on irrigated land |
| **Mineral interests** | Frequently severed, as in Part B |
| **Access** | Legal access, easements, and roads that may not be public |
| **Growing crops, and the crop year** | Whether they pass, and how they are apportioned |
| **Livestock and equipment** | Personal property conveyed alongside — **§ 12-10-403(4)(a)** |
| **Grazing leases and federal or state land permits** | Often not transferable as of right |
| **Conservation easements** | A recorded restriction that changes what the land may be used for permanently |
| **Government programme participation** | Enrolments that may or may not follow the land |
| **Fencing, wells, ditches and headgates** | Physical infrastructure attached to legal rights |

**And the Commission's own form structure recognises the difference.** The **Contracts and Regulations**
outline's Topic IV.A names a distinct family — **Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Vacant Land/Farm &
Ranch)** — and its Topic III requires the student to *"include **by comparison the differences between
residential, commercial and farm and ranch/vacant land** form."*

### C.3 What this build states, and what it does not

chunks.heading: C.4 What a broker does before taking the listing
chunks.excerpt:
> **NOT READ, and stated nowhere in this build:** Colorado's **water law** in its entirety — appropriation,
> priority dates, adjudication, augmentation plans, well permits, exempt wells, ditch company shares, change
> of use proceedings, and the division engineer's role; its **conservation easement** statutes; its **fence
> law**; its **agricultural** statutes; and every **federal or state grazing and land programme.**
>
> **No period, priority, permit requirement, decree, procedure, exemption or programme rule is stated
> anywhere in this build.**
>
> **This is a submission gate**, and **Contracts and Regulations Module 05 Part E** records it as one this
> build **cannot responsibly leave open** in a state where farm, ranch and vacant land brokerage is ordinary
> work.

### C.4 What a broker does before taking the listing

**Rule 6.2.A is a requirement, not advice:** a broker *"**must possess the necessary experience, training,
and knowledge** to provide Real Estate Brokerage Services **and maintain compliance with the applicable
federal, state and local laws.**"*

**Rule 6.2.B, applied to a farm and ranch listing offered to a residential broker:**

| Route | What it looks like here |
|---|---|
| **1. Decline** | The honest answer for most residential brokers, and the rule lists it **first** |
| **2. Obtain** the experience, training and knowledge | Coursework and mentoring in the specialty **before** taking the work |
| **3. Obtain the assistance** — including **legal counsel competent in the matter** | For water in particular: **counsel and a water engineer** |
| **4. Co-list** with a broker who meets subsection A | The ordinary answer when the opportunity is real and the competency is not |

---

## D. The pattern across all three

chunks.heading: Module 05 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**The three specialties in this topic have the same shape, and a student should leave able to state it.**

| | Business opportunities | Oil and gas | Farm and ranch |
|---|---|---|---|
| **What is really being conveyed** | More than the real property | An interest **beneath** the surface, often severed | Land **plus** water, minerals, access and programme rights |
| **The governing law** | UCC, securities, tax, entity, licensing | Oil and gas statutes and COGCC rules | Water law, conservation easements, agricultural statutes |
| **Read by this project?** | **No** | **No** | **No** |
| **What this build states** | The § 12-10-201(6) reach and the § 12-10-403(4)(a) personal property authority | The **actually known** disclosure duty and where a reservation appears | The **actually known** disclosure duty and that water may not pass |
| **The broker's move** | **Rule 6.2.B** | **Rule 6.2.B** | **Rule 6.2.B** |

**In every one of the three the transaction contains something a residential broker has no training to
value, describe, or convey — and in every one the rule gives four routes, the first of which is to
decline.**

---

## Module 05 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
*"**a test is required** to establish a participant's satisfactory completion of the statutory requirements
for the Practical Applications Course"*, and **these items are not that test.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 05

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 05
chunks.excerpt:
Written to the **Commission's Practical Applications qualifying education outline, approved 7 August 2012**,
Topic V and its sub-topics A through C, using the outline's own item names — *"**Business opportunities**"*,
*"**Oil and Gas leasing**"*, *"**Farm and Ranch**"*. The hour figure is the Commission's, and the competency
footnote applies.

The provisions cited — **§§ 12-10-201(6), 12-10-403(4)(a), 12-10-404(1)(c)(V) and (3), 12-10-405(1)(c)(V),
and 12-10-407(2)(b)(II) and (VI) and (4)** and **Rule 6.2** — are transcribed from **C.R.S. Title 12 Article
10** and **4 CCR 725-1** (rule version 12355), read on **2026-08-20** and recorded in
`colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** the **UCC** and **U.C.C.C.**; **federal and Colorado
securities law**; Colorado's **entity, trust and probate** statutes; **every tax provision**; **every trade
licensing and permitting statute**; Colorado's **oil and gas statutes**, **severed mineral**, **surface use**
and **dormant mineral** provisions, and every **COGCC rule**; Colorado's **water law in its entirety**; its
**conservation easement**, **fence** and **agricultural** statutes; and every **federal or state grazing and
land programme.**

**No securities threshold, licensing requirement, tax treatment, royalty fraction, lease term, pooling rule,
setback, water priority, permit requirement, decree, easement rule or programme condition is stated in this
module.** What is stated is the **actually known** disclosure standard and the four routes in Rule 6.2.B,
both transcribed from the sections and rule named beside them.

chunks.heading: Colorado Practical Applications — Module 06
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Practical Applications — Module 06

## Offer to closing

**Course:** Practical Applications (32 hours) · **Instructional hours: 16.0** of 32.0
**Commission outline topic:** **VI — Offer to Closing**, allocated **16 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### Half the course
>
> The Commission gives this topic **16 of the 32 hours** and fourteen sub-topics, lettered **A through N**.
> It is the transaction from the first conversation to the recorded deed, taught as **what a broker
> actually does** — the outline's objective calls it *"**the necessary components of a successful
> transaction.**"*
>
> | Sub-topic | Delivered in |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** Working with buyers & sellers | Part A |
> | **B.** Preparing the house to be listed | Part B |
> | **C.** Showing a property | Part C |
> | **D.** Preparing and presenting an offer | Part D |
> | **E.** Presenting the offer to the seller | Part E |
> | **F.** Under contract (what's next) | Part F |
> | **G.** Working with 3rd parties | Part G |
> | **H.** Tracking contingencies and suspense dates | Part H |
> | **I.** Final walk-through | Part I |
> | **J.** Setting the closing & notifying the parties | Part J |
> | **K.** Verifying figures and documents prior to closing | Part K |
> | **L.** Early occupancy | Part L |
> | **M.** Failed transactions | Part M |
> | **N.** Closing the transaction | Part N |

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: A. Working with buyers and sellers — outline Topic VI.A
chunks.excerpt:
1. Sequence the disclosures and agreements against the events that trigger them.
2. Calculate seller's net proceeds and buyer's cash to close from given figures.
3. State what a broker may and may not say about an exclusive relationship and a holdover period.
4. State the rules governing showings, access and property information.
5. Prepare and present an offer with complete contingencies and consistent dates.
6. State the multiple-offer and counter-offer duties.
7. Build a suspense date schedule and say what happens when one is missed.
8. State what a broker does with a failed transaction and disputed earnest money.

---

## A. Working with buyers and sellers — outline Topic VI.A

### A.1 Pricing and motivation — VI.A.1

**a. CMAs.** Delivered in **Real Estate Law and Practice Module 02** and **Module 02 Part D of this
course** — including **Rule 6.12**'s prescribed notice for a CMA or BPO prepared for any reason **other
than an anticipated sale or purchase**, and the **prohibition** on CMAs or BPOs **used to obtain
financing.**

**b. Neighborhood analysis; fair housing concerns.** The outline names them **in the same breath**, and so
does this course. A broker may discuss **the property and the physical, economic, governmental and legal
characteristics of an area** using sources a client can check. A broker may **not** characterise an area by
the **protected characteristics** of the people in it — that is **steering**, whatever reason is offered.

**§§ 12-10-404(1)(e), 12-10-405(1)(e) and 12-10-407(2)(d)** each make compliance with **fair housing and
civil rights statutes** part of the brokerage relationship duties, and **§ 12-10-411** makes a Part 4
violation an act the Commission may investigate.

chunks.heading: A.1 Pricing and motivation — VI.A.1
chunks.excerpt:
**c. Calculating seller's net proceeds and buyer's cash to close.** The Commission names this expressly, and
it is the calculation clients ask for most.

> **Seller's net, figures given.** Price **$620,000**. Compensation **5.5 percent**. Payoff **$341,800**.
> Title insurance **$2,240**. Recording **$40**. Estimated prorated taxes charged to the seller
> **$2,150**.
>
> | Line | Amount |
> |---|---|
> | Price | 620,000.00 |
> | less compensation (5.5%) | (34,100.00) |
> | less payoff | (341,800.00) |
> | less title insurance | (2,240.00) |
> | less recording | (40.00) |
> | less tax proration | (2,150.00) |
> | **Estimated net to seller** | **$239,670.00** |

> **The reverse — a seller who wants a stated net.** A seller wants **$250,000** after a **5.5 percent**
> compensation and **$4,500** of other costs.
>
> $250,000 + $4,500 = **$254,500**, which is **94.5 percent** of the price, so the price is
> **$254,500 ÷ 0.945 = $269,312.17.**
>
> **The compensation is a percentage of the PRICE, not of the net** — which is why the net plus costs is
> divided by the complement of the rate.

> **Buyer's cash to close, figures given.** Price **$620,000**. Down payment **10 percent**. Loan costs
> **$7,400**. Prepaid interest **$1,120**. Prepaid taxes and insurance escrow **$3,900**. Recording
> **$180**. Earnest money already paid **$15,000**.
>
> | Line | Amount |
> |---|---|
> | Down payment (10%) | 62,000.00 |
> | Loan costs | 7,400.00 |
> | Prepaid interest | 1,120.00 |
> | Escrow deposits | 3,900.00 |
> | Recording | 180.00 |
> | **Subtotal** | **74,600.00** |
> | less earnest money | (15,000.00) |
> | **Estimated cash to close** | **$59,600.00** |

chunks.heading: A.2 Explaining the right to sell / buy agreements — VI.A.2
chunks.excerpt:
**Every figure is an estimate until the closing entity produces the statement**, and a broker says so.
**Rule 6.19.A** puts the accuracy obligation at closing on the broker with the brokerage relationship, and
**Rule 6.19.B** on the broker who prepares the documents.

### A.2 Explaining the right to sell / buy agreements — VI.A.2

**a. Effects of an exclusive relationship.** Under an **exclusive right-to-sell**, compensation is earned by
**a sale during the term, however it comes about** — including one the owner finds themselves. Under an
**exclusive agency**, the owner may still sell it themselves without compensation. Under an **open
listing**, only the broker who produces is paid.

**Explaining this BEFORE signature is the substance of the broker's job at that stage.**

**b. Explaining the holdover period.** A holdover clause continues the compensation obligation for a stated
period after the term where a sale is made to a **protected** buyer. **What the period is, who is protected
and how they become protected are terms of the agreement** — and **no Commission form was obtained by this
project**, so **no holdover period, protection mechanism or form provision is stated anywhere in this
build.**

**And § 12-10-409(1)(b)(III) stands behind every agreement:** where it is not performed or completed, the
relationship ends at the **earlier** of an agreed expiration, a termination by the parties, or **one year
after the engagement.**

### A.3 Changing brokerage relationships — VI.A.3

chunks.heading: B. Preparing the house to be listed — outline Topic VI.B
chunks.excerpt:
**Rule 6.9** and the **Change of Status** form, delivered in **Module 02 Part A.1**: on changing **from
single agent for one consumer to transaction-broker for both**, the Commission-approved form goes to the
consumer whose relationship changed *"**at the time the Broker begins to assist both Consumers ... but not
later than at the time the Consumer signs the contract.**"*

**And Rule 6.7's three lawful configurations**, because **§ 12-10-406 prohibits dual agency outright.**

---

## B. Preparing the house to be listed — outline Topic VI.B

**What a broker does:** advise on condition, presentation and access; gather what the listing needs —
**legal description**, **square footage and its SOURCE**, inclusions and exclusions, association
information, and any known condition matters; and get the **seller's property disclosure** completed by the
seller.

**Two Colorado rules bite here.**

> **Rule 6.11** — advertising square footage, **including for submission to a multiple listing service**,
> requires **disclosing the SOURCE on the Commission-approved form**, with the **date of issuance** where
> the source has one. *"A Broker **may not provide information to a person from a source known to be
> unreliable** and **is responsible for indicating obvious mismeasurement by others.**"*
>
> **Rule 6.10.C** — the broker is **responsible for the accuracy of advertising including MLS entries**, but
> *"**does not have a duty to investigate the information provided ... by the seller or obtained from a third
> party source (e.g. assessor records, building plans).**"*

**Read together: no duty to investigate is not permission to pass on what you can see is wrong.**

chunks.heading: C. Showing a property — outline Topic VI.C
chunks.excerpt:
**And the seller's disclosure does not discharge the broker's own duty.** **§ 12-10-404(3)(a)** requires
disclosure to any prospective buyer of **all adverse material facts ACTUALLY KNOWN by the broker** —
including title, physical condition, material defects and environmental hazards required by law to be
disclosed. **A fact the broker knows that the seller did not state is still the broker's to disclose.**

---

## C. Showing a property — outline Topic VI.C

**Access is the owner's to give.** **Rule 6.10.F** governs advertising availability without authority;
**Rule 6.16** governs **access information for a property**; and the listing agreement governs how showings
are arranged.

**Fair housing governs who is shown what.** Every prospect gets the same information and the same sources,
and **the decision about which properties to see is the prospect's.**

**Confidentiality governs what is said.** **§ 12-10-404(2)** forbids a seller's agent disclosing, without
informed consent, that the **seller will accept less**, their **motivating factors**, or that they **will
agree to other financing terms.** **§ 12-10-407(3)** binds a transaction-broker to a **six-item** list
requiring the **informed consent of all parties.**

**And the disclosure timing from Rule 6.5 applies at the door.** A showing conversation that moves to what
the prospect can afford or why they are moving has reached **confidential information**, and the written
§ 12-10-408 disclosure was due **before** it.

---

## D. Preparing and presenting an offer — outline Topic VI.D

The outline names four sub-items, and each is a check.

### D.1 Forms and computer generated contracts — VI.D.1

chunks.heading: D.2 Proper contingencies — VI.D.2
chunks.excerpt:
> **§ 12-10-403(4)(c)** and **Rule 7.1.A**: *"**A broker shall use a Commission-approved form when such a
> form exists and is appropriate for the transaction**"* — a form *"promulgated by the Commission **for
> CURRENT USE**"*, obtained from **the Division's website.**
>
> And the advice that goes with every one: the broker *"**shall advise the parties that the forms have
> important legal consequences and that the parties should consult legal counsel before signing.**"*

**"Computer generated" changes nothing about which form must be used**, and a generated document that is not
the current Commission form is not a Commission-approved form.

### D.2 Proper contingencies — VI.D.2

**The three-part test, applied to every one:**

> **1. WHAT EVENT** must occur; **2. BY WHEN**; and **3. WHAT HAPPENS** if it does not.

**An event with no deadline, or a deadline with no consequence, has settled nothing.**

### D.3 Consistency of dates — VI.D.3

**The Commission names this expressly, and it is the most common defect in a new broker's completed
contract.**

**The check:** lay every date in the contract on one line in order and ask whether each is **possible**. A
loan objection deadline **after** closing; an inspection deadline **before** the contract is signed; a title
objection deadline leaving **no time to cure**; a possession date **before** closing without an early
occupancy agreement — each of these appears in real contracts, and each is caught by reading the dates in
sequence.

### D.4 Inclusions and exclusions — VI.D.4

**What stays and what goes**, named in the contract. **§ 12-10-403(4)(a)** authorises a broker to complete
standard forms *"**including standard forms intended to convey personal property as part of the real estate
transaction.**"*

chunks.heading: E. Presenting the offer to the seller — outline Topic VI.E
chunks.excerpt:
**Anything anyone might argue about goes in by name.**

---

## E. Presenting the offer to the seller — outline Topic VI.E

### E.1 The presentation duty

> **§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(II)**: **present all offers to and from the seller in a timely manner REGARDLESS of
> whether the property is subject to a contract for sale.**
>
> **§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(I)**: the broker **is not obligated to SEEK additional offers** while the property is
> under contract.
>
> **Rule 6.13**: present **to the other consumer's broker**; on **reasonable but unsuccessful attempts**, to
> that broker's **employing broker**; and if none exists or those attempts fail, **directly to the other
> consumer.** **The rule states no time period, and this build supplies none.**

### E.2 Counter offers — VI.E.1

**A counter-offer REJECTS the original offer.** The original cannot then be accepted unless renewed, and the
counter operates as a new offer. The **Counterproposal** is the instrument, named at the **Contracts and
Regulations** outline's Topic IV.B.1.

**A term changed on the face of the contract and initialled produces a document the parties will disagree
about.** The counterproposal states **which terms change and which survive.**

### E.3 Multiple offers — VI.E.2

**What the rules require:** every offer is **presented** — **§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(II)**. **What may be
disclosed about competing offers is the seller's decision**, and **§ 12-10-404(2)(d)** forbids disclosing
**material information about the seller** without informed consent.

**And every offeror is treated the same way.** Fair housing runs through multiple-offer handling, and so
does **§ 12-10-404(1)(e)**'s requirement to comply with fair housing and civil rights statutes.

chunks.heading: E.4 Acceptance — VI.E.3
chunks.excerpt:
**A broker does not tell a buyer what to offer to beat another offer**, and does not disclose the terms of
one offer to another offeror without the seller's informed consent.

### E.4 Acceptance — VI.E.3

**Acceptance must be unqualified and COMMUNICATED.** One signed and left unsent has not been communicated.
The contract should state **how and by when** acceptance must be communicated, and the broker should know
which document and which moment formed the contract, because **every suspense date in Part H runs from
it.**

---

## F. Under contract — outline Topic VI.F

### F.1 The listing broker's role — VI.F.1

Deliver the executed contract; deliver **earnest money per the contract and obtain a dated and signed
receipt** (**Rule 5.12.A**); order what the seller must produce; track the seller's deadlines; keep the
seller informed; and **continue presenting offers** unless released as **Rule 6.13** and § 12-10-404
contemplate.

### F.2 The selling broker's role — VI.F.2

Deliver the contract to the buyer; ensure the **loan application** goes in; order the **inspection**;
deliver the **title commitment** and diarise the objection deadline; track the buyer's deadlines; and keep
the buyer informed.

**§ 12-10-407(2)(b)(IV) and (V)** state it for a transaction-broker in the statute's own words: **keep the
parties fully informed**, and **assist the parties in complying with the terms and conditions of any
contract including closing the transaction.**

---

## G. Working with third parties — outline Topic VI.G

chunks.heading: H. Tracking contingencies and suspense dates — outline Topic VI.H
chunks.excerpt:
**Lenders, title companies, home inspectors and appraisers** — the four the outline names, developed in
**Module 02 Part C** with the two rules that govern what a broker may receive for the referral: **Rule
6.21.A** (no referral fee **except in accordance with RESPA** and unless a **reasonable cause** exists under
§ 12-10-304(1)) and **Rule 5.17** (**prior written consent** for mark-ups, disclosure of mark-ups paid by
any customer, and records verifying both). **Rule 6.18** requires **affiliated business arrangement
disclosures.**

**Neither RESPA, nor § 12-10-304, nor § 12-10-218 was read by this project**, and **no requirement,
threshold, exemption or penalty from any of them is stated anywhere in this build.**

---

## H. Tracking contingencies and suspense dates — outline Topic VI.H

**This is the operational core of the module, and it is what most often fails.**

**A suspense date schedule lists every date in the contract, what must happen by it, who must do it, and
what happens if it passes.**

chunks.heading: H. Tracking contingencies and suspense dates — outline Topic VI.H
chunks.excerpt:
| Date | What must happen | Who | If missed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Earnest money delivery | Delivered to the holder per the contract, **dated signed receipt obtained** | Broker | **Rule 5.12.A** breach |
| Earnest money deposit | If the firm holds it, deposited **within three business days** of receipt or mutual execution, **whichever is later** | Firm | **Rule 5.7.B** breach |
| Loan application | Application submitted | Buyer | Contract's consequence |
| Inspection | Inspection performed | Buyer | Objection right may lapse |
| Inspection objection | **Inspection Notice** delivered | Buyer | Condition may be accepted |
| Title documents delivered | Commitment and documents to buyer | Seller / title | Contract's consequence |
| Title objection | Objection delivered | Buyer | Exceptions may be accepted |
| Association documents | Delivered and reviewed | Seller / association | Contract's consequence |
| Appraisal | Completed | Lender | Contract's consequence |
| Loan objection | Buyer's decision on financing | Buyer | Financing contingency may lapse |
| Survey or ILC | Obtained | Per contract | Contract's consequence |
| Closing | Closing occurs | All | Default provisions engage |
| Possession | Possession delivered | Seller | Default provisions engage |

**Three disciplines that make the schedule work:**

> **1. Every date is diarised the day the contract is executed**, not the week it falls due.
> **2. Every date has an OWNER.** A date nobody owns is the date that passes.
> **3. Nothing changes without a writing.** *"**Close to contract or amend contract in writing**"* — the
> Closings outline's Topic III.A.1 — and the instrument is the **Agreement to Amend/Extend Contract.**

chunks.heading: I. Final walk-through — outline Topic VI.I
chunks.excerpt:
**And § 12-10-407(2)(b)(V)** makes assisting the parties in complying with the contract's terms an express
obligation of a transaction-broker.

---

## I. Final walk-through — outline Topic VI.I

**What it is:** the buyer's opportunity, before closing, to confirm the property is in the condition the
contract requires and that agreed repairs and inclusions are as agreed.

**What it is not:** an inspection, a new objection right, or a renegotiation. **What the buyer may do if
something is wrong depends on the contract**, and if the parties resolve it differently, **the contract is
amended in writing.**

**Access is still the owner's to give**, and **Rule 6.16** governs access information.

---

## J. Setting the closing and notifying the parties — outline Topic VI.J

**Confirm the closing entity, date, time and place; confirm what each party must bring; confirm how funds
will move; and notify everyone who must be there.**

**Two Colorado requirements bear on it.**

> **Rule 6.19.C** — a broker with a brokerage relationship *"**must review closing documents AND attend
> closing OR BE REASONABLY AVAILABLE.**"* If not available, **another broker designated by the firm may
> review and attend on their behalf** and **assumes JOINT RESPONSIBILITY** for accuracy, completeness and
> delivery of the signed closing statement.
>
> **Rule 6.19.E — Good Funds.** A broker or firm *"**must not disburse or authorize disbursement of funds
> until those funds have been RECEIVED and are ... available for immediate withdrawal AS A MATTER OF RIGHT
> ... or available for immediate withdrawal as a consequence of an agreement with a financial institution
> ... If the agreement contains contingencies or reservations, NO DISBURSEMENTS CAN BE MADE until these are
> satisfied.**"*

chunks.heading: K. Verifying figures and documents prior to closing — outline Topic VI.K
chunks.excerpt:
**How the buyer's funds will arrive is a question asked days before closing, not on the morning.**

---

## K. Verifying figures and documents prior to closing — outline Topic VI.K

**The check, and it is the Closings course's Module 03 Part D.3 applied here:**

1. **Does every charge trace to the contract or a written amendment?**
2. **Does each proration's two halves sum to the whole?**
3. **Does each party's column settle to one figure?**
4. **Does money in equal money out?**
5. **Do the names, legal description, price and loan figures match across the contract, the commitment, the
   worksheet and the statement?**
6. **Is the statement accurate, complete and detailed?**

> **Rule 6.19.A**: the broker with the brokerage relationship **must ensure the consumer receives a closing
> statement that is ACCURATE, COMPLETE AND DETAILED and SIGNED BY THE BROKER**, and must **deliver closing
> statements and other closing documents to the brokerage firm IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING CLOSING.**
>
> **Rule 6.19.B**: a broker who **prepares** the documents is responsible for their **accuracy and
> completeness.**

**The broker signs the statement.** That is why this sub-topic exists.

---

## L. Early occupancy — outline Topic VI.L

**A buyer in possession before closing, or a seller in possession after it.**

**What it needs:** a **written agreement** stating who occupies, from when, on what terms, who insures, who
maintains, what rent or consideration is paid, what happens if the closing does not occur, and how
possession is recovered.

chunks.heading: M. Failed transactions — outline Topic VI.M
chunks.excerpt:
> **A boundary this module holds firmly.** **Colorado's landlord-tenant statutes were NOT read by this
> project**, and **whether an early or holdover occupancy creates a tenancy — and what would then be
> required to end it — is a question this course does not answer.**
>
> **Insurance is the other half**, and it is not the broker's field either: whose policy covers an occupant
> who does not own, and an owner who does not occupy, is a question for **the carriers.**
>
> **§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V), 12-10-405(1)(c)(V) and 12-10-407(2)(b)(II)** each require **advising the party to
> obtain expert advice** as to material matters beyond the broker's expertise. **Early occupancy is the
> clearest case in an ordinary residential file**, and the advice needed is **legal and insurance advice
> before anyone moves in.**

---

## M. Failed transactions — outline Topic VI.M

### M.1 Handling earnest money deposits — VI.M.1

**Three things are true whatever the contract says:**

> **1. The broker HOLDS.** The broker does not decide entitlement.
> **2. The parties or a court decide.**
> **3. Nothing is disbursed on the broker's own judgement.**

**Why:** **Rule 5.9** — money belonging to one beneficiary **must not be used for the benefit of another**;
and **Rule 5.14.B** — *"**no ledger may ever be allowed to have a negative cash balance**"*, which is what a
wrong release produces.

**Rule 6.2.B.3** supplies the route: obtain the assistance of the employing broker, a supervisory broker, a
competent broker **or legal counsel competent in the matter** — **before the money moves.**

chunks.heading: M.2 Alternative dispute resolution — VI.M.2
chunks.excerpt:
**The Record Keeping and Trust Accounts outline names the mechanism** at its Topic III.B.3 — *"**Earnest
Money Disputes and Interpleaders**"* — and **no Colorado interpleader procedure, deadline or cost rule is
stated anywhere in this build**, because none was read.

### M.2 Alternative dispute resolution — VI.M.2

**Mediation and arbitration**, where the contract provides for them. **What the contract requires, and what
it does to a party's other remedies, is a legal question**, and **no Colorado statute or rule on mediation
or arbitration was read by this project.**

### M.3 Evictions — VI.M.3

**Named by the outline under failed transactions**, which places it where a failed early occupancy or a
holdover seller would land it.

> **Colorado's eviction and unlawful detainer statutes were NOT read by this project.** **No ground, notice
> period, procedure, timeline or remedy is stated anywhere in this build.** **This is a submission gate**,
> and it is one a Practical Applications course cannot leave open — the outline names evictions expressly.

---

## N. Closing the transaction — outline Topic VI.N

### N.1 Responsibilities of the listing and selling brokers — VI.N.1

**Rule 6.19.A** — the broker with the brokerage relationship is **responsible for the proper closing of the
transaction**, whoever conducts it; must ensure the consumer receives a **closing statement that is
accurate, complete and detailed and signed by the broker**; and must **deliver closing statements and other
closing documents to the firm immediately following closing.**

### N.2 Responsibilities of associate brokers — VI.N.2

chunks.heading: N.3 Changes to contract terms, amend/extend agreements — VI.N.3
chunks.excerpt:
**Rule 6.19.C's substitute provision**, and behind it **Rule 6.3.A.1** — employing brokers **exercise
authority, direction and supervision**, and a complaint against an associate **may become an investigation
of the employing broker.**

### N.3 Changes to contract terms, amend/extend agreements — VI.N.3

***"Close to contract or amend contract in writing."*** A change made at the closing table is **amended in
writing and signed by everyone**, or it does not appear on the statement. **A side agreement kept off the
statement is the loan fraud problem** the Contracts and Regulations outline names at its Topic V.F.4.

### N.4 Follow up on recordings, issuance of title policy, etc. — VI.N.4

**The transaction is not finished at signing.** The deed and security instrument are **recorded**; the
**title policy** issues; the **releases** of paid-off liens are recorded; and the file is completed.

> **Rule 6.20**: **four years** of retention, from **consummation** or from **the expiration of a listing
> contract that does not consummate** — and expressly **not** requiring the broker to obtain and retain
> **existing public records, title commitments, loan applications, lender required disclosures, or related
> affirmations from independent third party closing entities after the closing date.**
>
> The **Commission's Transaction File Checklist**, which Rule 6.20 says designates the required documents,
> **was NOT obtained by this project** — a submission gate.

**And § 12-10-409(2)(b)** — for a **single agent**, **accounting** and **confidentiality** survive
termination; for a **transaction-broker**, **§ 12-10-409(3)** carries **accounting** only.

---

## Module 06 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 06
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items — one applied, five engagement, five remediation. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and
the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. The Commission's outline requires that
*"**a test is required** to establish a participant's satisfactory completion of the statutory requirements
for the Practical Applications Course"*, and **these items are not that test.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module 06

Written to the **Commission's Practical Applications qualifying education outline, approved 7 August 2012**,
Topic VI and its fourteen sub-topics **A through N**, in the outline's own order and using the outline's own
item names — including *"**Consistency of dates**"*, *"**Early occupancy**"* and *"**Follow up on
recordings, issuance of title policy, etc.**"* The hour figure — **16 of the course's 32** — is the
Commission's.

The provisions quoted — **§§ 12-10-403(4), 12-10-404, 12-10-405, 12-10-406, 12-10-407, 12-10-408, 12-10-409
and 12-10-411** and **Rules 5.7, 5.9, 5.12, 5.14.B, 5.17, 6.2, 6.5, 6.7, 6.9, 6.10, 6.11, 6.12, 6.13, 6.16,
6.18, 6.19, 6.20, 6.21 and 7.1** — are transcribed from **C.R.S. Title 12 Article 10** and **4 CCR 725-1**
(rule version 12355), read on **2026-08-20** and recorded in
`colorado/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 06
chunks.excerpt:
**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **every Commission-approved form**, including the
Counterproposal, the Inspection Notice, the Change of Status form, the square footage disclosure form and
the Agreement to Amend/Extend Contract; the **Commission's Transaction File Checklist**; **RESPA**; **C.R.S.
§§ 12-10-218 and 12-10-304**; **C.R.S. § 38-12-101 et seq.** and Colorado's **eviction and unlawful
detainer** statutes; any Colorado **mediation or arbitration** statute or rule; any **interpleader**
procedure; the **Colorado Fair Housing Act** and the **federal Fair Housing Act**; and Colorado's **property
tax** statutes.

**No form provision, holdover period, checklist item, referral fee threshold, eviction ground or timeline,
arbitration rule, interpleader procedure, protected class beyond the seven federal classes, tax rate or
proration convention is stated in this module.** Every figure in every worked calculation is supplied inside
that calculation as a given, and the arithmetic is shown in full.

lessons.title: Colorado Practical Applications — Module 07

chunks.heading: Colorado Practical Applications — Module 07
chunks.excerpt:
# Colorado Practical Applications — Module 07

## Current market trends

**Course:** Practical Applications (32 hours) · **Instructional hours: 3.0** of 32.0
**Commission outline topic:** **VII — Current Trends**, allocated **3 hours**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Colorado qualifying education hours are available.

> ### The only topic in the six outlines the Commission leaves to the school
>
> | Sub-topic | The outline's own allocation |
> |---|---|
> | **A.** Financing Trends | *"1-4 (**Schools discretion**)"* |
> | **B.** Current Housing Trends | *"1-4 (**Schools discretion**)"* |
> | **C.** Marketing and Advertising Trends | *"1-4 (**Schools discretion**)"* |
> | **D.** Division of Real Estate "hot issues" | *"1-4 (**Schools discretion**)"* |
>
> **"Schools discretion" appears four times**, and the Commission's own note on the 2012 revision explains
> it: the updated outline *"**allows education providers to UPDATE MARKET TRENDS.**"*
>
> **This is deliberate.** Market content dates faster than any course cycle, so the Commission fixed the
> **subjects** and left the **content** to the provider — under the obligation it states at the head of the
> same outline: *"**COURSE PROVIDERS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR ENSURING THAT THE STATUTES, RULES AND POSITION
> STATEMENTS USED DURING THE COURSE PRESENTATION ARE ACCURATE AND UP-TO-DATE.**"*
>
> > **What this module therefore is.** It states, for each of the four subjects, **what a broker must be able
> > to do**, **which rules constrain how they do it**, and **where current data comes from** — and it states
> > **no market figure of any kind.**
> >
> > **No rate, price, inventory number, days-on-market figure, absorption rate, forecast or trend is stated
> > anywher

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
e in this module or anywhere in this build**, because a figure stated in a course file is wrong
> > the month after it is written and a student cannot tell which month that was.
> >
> > **The delivery instruction for this module is that the trend content is prepared afresh for each
> > presentation, from current sources, and is dated.**

## Learning objectives

1. State what a broker must be able to explain about financing conditions without advising on products.
2. State what a broker must be able to explain about housing market conditions, and from what data.
3. State the advertising rules that govern how any trend claim may be published.
4. State where Division "hot issues" come from and identify what this build did not obtain.
5. State the rule that makes currency the broker's own continuing obligation.

---

## A. Financing trends — outline Topic VII.A

### A.1 What a broker must be able to do

**Explain how the current financing environment affects a client's transaction**, using figures the **lender
supplies**:

chunks.heading: A.2 The line a broker does not cross
chunks.excerpt:
- What a change in rate does to a payment, and to a buyer's qualifying position.
- What products are available in the market the client is buying in — and that availability is the
  **lender's** statement, not the broker's.
- What **points** cost and what the break-even is: **one point is one percent of the LOAN AMOUNT**, and the
  break-even is the cost divided by the annual saving. *(Worked in Real Estate Law and Practice Module 04
  Part D.3, on figures supplied inside that problem.)*
- What an **appraisal below contract price** does — the lender lends against the **lesser** of price or
  appraised value, and the gap is the buyer's to close.
- What **assumption** and **owner carry** structures require of the contract. *(Contracts and Regulations
  Module 04 Part C.)*

### A.2 The line a broker does not cross

**§§ 12-10-404(1)(c)(V), 12-10-405(1)(c)(V) and 12-10-407(2)(b)(II)** each require the broker to **advise
the party to obtain expert advice** as to material matters known to the broker but whose specifics are
beyond the broker's expertise.
