not Missouri market, tax or fee data.**

lessons.title: Missouri Real Estate Practice Course — Module MREP-06

chunks.heading: Missouri Real Estate Practice Course — Module MREP-06
chunks.excerpt:
# Missouri Real Estate Practice Course — Module MREP-06

## Hours 22–24 · Contracts, earnest money, and avoiding misrepresentation

**Commission topics covered:** 20 CSR 2250-6.060(2)(M) Contracts · (N) Earnest Money · (O) Avoiding
Misrepresentation
**Clock hours:** 3. A Missouri clock hour is **60 minutes containing at least 50 minutes of actual
instruction** — 20 CSR 2250-7.070(2).
**Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Commission review; 20 CSR 2250-6.060(2) allocates no
hours among its sixteen topics.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Missouri pre-license credit is available.

## Learning objectives

1. Take a contract from offer through acceptance and identify the date every deadline runs from.
2. Distinguish an amendment from a notice and use each correctly.
3. State what earnest money is, what it is not, and the three rules that govern a licensee's handling.
4. State who decides the disposition of disputed earnest money.
5. Distinguish innocent, negligent and fraudulent misrepresentation, and puffing from a statement of
   fact.
6. Apply the § 339.710(1) adverse material fact definition and the two disclosure standards.
7. Describe the working method that prevents misrepresentation before it happens.
8. State what a Missouri salesperson carries out of the 24-hour practice course.

## Timed sequence

| Hour | Content | Instruction |
|---|---|---:|
| 22 | Contracts in Missouri practice | 50 min |
| 23 | Earnest money | 50 min |
| 24 | Avoiding misrepresentation; what you carry forward | 50 min |

---

## Hour 22 — Contracts — 20 CSR 2250-6.060(2)(M)

### 22.1 From offer to contract

chunks.heading: 22.2 Match each deadline to its contractual trigger
chunks.excerpt:
An **offer** is a definite proposal, communicated to the offeree, showing an intention to be bound on
acceptance. It ends by **acceptance**, **rejection**, **counter-offer**, **revocation** before
acceptance is communicated, or **lapse**.

**A counter-offer rejects the original offer and substitutes a new one.** The original is dead and can
no longer simply be accepted. That is why a seller with three offers cannot counter all three without
destroying all three, and why a multiple counter-proposal instrument exists where the firm's forms
supply one.

**Acceptance** must be unqualified and **communicated in the manner the offer requires.** Signature and
delivery are different events and may fall on different days.

### 22.2 Match each deadline to its contractual trigger

**Use the formation or effective date where the particular provision makes it the starting point.**
Signature, delivery, and receipt are different events. Other deadlines may start on receipt of a
title document, delivery of a notice, another defined event, or a fixed calendar date. Do not assume
that every deadline shares the same anchor or that every form defines formation identically.

**The discipline:** record acceptance as the contract directs, then enter each deadline in the file
and calendar with its clause, trigger, counting rule, cut-off time, permitted delivery method, and
recipient. Track later trigger events and amendments when they occur. If a hypothetical clause allows
five days after receipt of the title commitment, use documented receipt and that clause's counting
rules; a separately stated closing date remains its own calendar entry.

chunks.heading: 22.3 The § 339.780.7 obligation, applied
chunks.excerpt:
A deadline calculated from the wrong event can impair the client's rights. Have the designated broker
review uncertain calculations and route disputed legal interpretation to counsel. This lesson's
hypothetical counting period is not a statewide Missouri form requirement.

### 22.3 The § 339.780.7 obligation, applied

Recall the statutory minimum for an **exclusive** brokerage agreement: the broker will provide, at a
minimum, **accepting delivery of and presenting** offers and counteroffers; **assisting** in developing,
communicating, negotiating and presenting offers, counteroffers and notices **until a lease or purchase
agreement is signed and all contingencies are satisfied or waived**; and **answering** the client's or
customer's questions about them.

**"Until all contingencies are satisfied or waived" is the operative phrase.** The statutory floor runs
past contract signature and through the contingency period. A firm that treats its work as done at
signature has not met it.

### 22.4 Presenting offers

Section 339.730.1(3)(b) — and § 339.740.1(3)(b) — requires **presenting all written offers to and from
the client in a timely manner regardless of whether the property is subject to a contract** for sale or
lease.

**All of them. In writing. Promptly. Even after the property is under contract.** What the seller then
does with a late-arriving offer is a legal question about their existing contract, and it goes to
counsel.

Section 339.755(2)(a) imposes the same presentation duty on a transaction broker, unless the agreement
with the party provides otherwise.

### 22.5 Three instruments, distinguished

chunks.heading: 22.6 The drafting boundary
chunks.excerpt:
- An **offer** or **counter-offer** proposes terms **before** there is a contract.
- An **amendment** changes a contract that **already exists** and requires the agreement of all parties.
- A **notice** exercises a right the contract **already gives** — removing a contingency, giving notice
  of a defect, giving notice of an inability to obtain financing. A notice is **unilateral**: it does not
  need the other side's agreement, but it must be given in the manner and by the deadline the contract
  specifies.

**Using the wrong one is a common and expensive error.** A buyer who "amends" when they should have given
notice has asked permission for something they were entitled to do — and has handed the other side a
negotiation they did not have to have.

### 22.6 The drafting boundary

**Inside the licence:** completing the forms your firm supplies by filling in the facts of the
transaction; selecting among the provisions the forms offer; explaining what a provision says in its
ordinary sense; and advising the client to obtain expert advice, as § 339.730.1(3)(d) requires.

**Outside the licence:** composing new legal language to solve a client's specific legal problem;
advising which form of ownership to take title in; opining on the legal effect of a provision; drafting
an addendum to address something the forms do not cover.

**When the forms do not fit, counsel drafts it and it is attached.** A licensee who composes a clause has
practised law — and has usually produced a clause that does not do what the client wanted.

---

## Hour 23 — Earnest money — 20 CSR 2250-6.060(2)(N)

### 23.1 What it is, and what it is not

**Earnest money is a deposit evidencing the buyer's good faith**, held in trust, and applied to the
purchase price at closing.

chunks.heading: 23.2 The three rules
chunks.excerpt:
**It is not the consideration for the contract** — the consideration is the mutual promises. **It is not
a fee.** **It is not the licensee's or the firm's money at any point.** And a contract without earnest
money is not automatically invalid; earnest money is a commercial feature, not an element of formation.

Its practical functions are two: it signals seriousness to the seller, and it constitutes a fund from
which the seller may be made whole if the buyer defaults — which is why many forms designate it as
**liquidated damages** for a buyer's default, and why the amount matters.

### 23.2 The three rules

**One: it is trust money from the moment it comes into your hands.**

It goes to the firm for handling under the firm's trust account procedures. It never touches an operating
account. Section 339.730.1(4), RSMo, states the statutory duty: **to account in a timely manner for all
money and property received.**

**Two: you do not hold it.**

Not uncashed in a drawer as a favour to a buyer who asked you to wait until their contingency clears.
Not over a weekend because the broker is away. A licensee who is asked to hold a cheque says no and
explains why, and if the buyer wants a later deposit that is a **term of the contract** to be negotiated
in writing — not an informal arrangement with the licensee.

**Three: you do not release it on request.**

Not to a seller as a show of good faith. Not to a buyer who has changed their mind. Not on the strength
of both parties saying it is fine, unless the release is documented in the way your firm's procedures
require.

### 23.3 Who decides a disputed disposition

**Not the licensee, and not the firm on its own judgment.** The two questions are **what the contract
provides** and **what the parties or a court determine.**

chunks.heading: 23.4 The Missouri rules this course does not state
chunks.excerpt:
Where the parties disagree, the firm's options are those its procedures and counsel identify —
customarily holding the funds until a written mutual release or a court order, or interpleading them.
The licensee's role is to route it, not to resolve it.

**Releasing disputed funds on your own judgment is a licence problem regardless of who turns out to have
been right about the contract.**

### 23.4 The Missouri rules this course does not state

**This course states no Missouri deposit deadline, trust account requirement, threshold, exception or
retention period**, because **§ 339.105, RSMo, and 20 CSR 2250 chapters 1 through 5 and 8 were not read
from primary text for this project.**

That is a real gap and it is named rather than filled. **Read § 339.105 and the trust account chapter in
current text, and read your firm's written procedures, before you accept your first cheque.**

Two reasons it matters more than most gaps. First, **trust account failures are the fastest route out of
this profession**, and they are almost never theft — they are convenience, helpfulness and sloppiness,
which look identical on an audit. Second, the deposit deadline is a **specific number of days** that
differs between states, and a licensee working from another state's habit will breach Missouri's without
noticing.

### 23.5 A working routine

1. **Receive it and deliver it to the firm the same day**, following the firm's procedure exactly.
2. **Document what you received, from whom, in what form, and when.**
3. **Confirm the deposit to the buyer in writing.**
4. **Diarise the deadline** the contract sets for the deposit.
5. **On any dispute, escalate immediately** to the designated broker. Do nothing else.

---

## Hour 24 — Avoiding misrepresentation — 20 CSR 2250-6.060(2)(O)

chunks.heading: 24.1 The three kinds
chunks.excerpt:
### 24.1 The three kinds

**Innocent misrepresentation** — a false statement of material fact the speaker believed true and had
reasonable grounds to believe. **It can still support rescission**, and it is still a licence problem,
because the buyer relied on it either way.

**Negligent misrepresentation** — a false statement made without reasonable care as to its truth. This
is the one licensees commit most, and it is almost always by **repeating something without checking it**.

**Fraudulent misrepresentation** — a false statement made knowingly or recklessly, with intent to induce
reliance. This is the one with the largest consequences and it includes **active concealment** — painting
over a stain, running a dehumidifier before every showing.

**And the fourth, which is not a statement at all: failure to disclose an adverse material fact.**
Silence is actionable in Missouri where the statute requires speech, and §§ 339.730.1(3)(c), 339.730.3,
339.740.3 and 339.755(2)(d) require it.

### 24.2 Puffing, and where it stops

**Puffing** is obvious opinion nobody could reasonably rely on: *lovely home; wonderful natural light;
you'll love the kitchen.* It is not actionable because it is not a statement of fact.

**It stops the moment a statement is specific, factual and checkable:**

| Puffing | A statement of fact |
|---|---|
| "Great location" | "It's a fifteen-minute drive to the hospital" |
| "Beautiful lot" | "The lot is half an acre" |
| "Solid house" | "The roof was replaced in 2019" |
| "Plenty of room" | "It's 2,100 square feet" |
| "Won't last long" | "There are two other offers" |

Every entry in the right-hand column is a representation. **If you cannot show where the number came
from, do not say it.**

### 24.3 Where misrepresentation actually comes from

chunks.heading: 24.4 The statutory frame, restated
chunks.excerpt:
Not from lying. From **repeating**:

- **The square footage from a tax record.** An assessment record is not a measurement.
- **The acreage from a prior listing.** Somebody else's figure, which may have been wrong then.
- **The school assignment.** Boundaries change. Route it to the district.
- **The zoning.** Route it to the municipality.
- **"The seller says the basement is dry."** Attribute it, or verify it, and disclose what you know.
- **"The roof is about ten years old."** Where did "about" come from?
- **The flood zone.** An inventory map is not a determination. Route it.
- **The lender's estimate of the buyer's payment**, restated as their payment.
- **The net sheet**, presented as a promise rather than an estimate.

**The rule that prevents nearly all of it: attribute or verify. Never assert.** *"The tax record shows
1,940 square feet; if the exact figure matters to you, have it measured."* That sentence costs nothing
and is complete protection.

### 24.4 The statutory frame, restated

**Section 339.710(1)** defines an **adverse material fact** as *a fact related to the property not
reasonably ascertainable or known to a party which negatively affects the value of the property*, and
lists environmental hazards, physical condition adversely affecting value, material defects in the
property, **material defects in title**, and **material limitation of the party's ability to perform
under the terms of the contract.**

**The two standards:**

chunks.heading: 24.5 The method
chunks.excerpt:
- A **limited agent** discloses adverse material facts **actually known or that should have been known**
  — to the **client** under § 339.730.1(3)(c), and to any **customer** under § 339.730.3 and § 339.740.3.
- A **transaction broker** discloses those **of which the licensee has actual notice or knowledge** —
  § 339.755(2)(d).

**"Should have been known" makes wilful ignorance unavailable.** A licensee who arranges not to learn
something has not escaped the duty.

**And confidentiality does not override it.** Sections 339.730.2 and 339.740.2 permit disclosure of
confidential information where **failure to disclose would constitute a misrepresentation** — and
provide that **no cause of action arises against a licensee for making any required or permitted
disclosure.** A seller who tells you in confidence that the basement floods has told you an adverse
material fact; they have not sealed your mouth.

**Say so at the time.** *"I have to tell you that this is something I will need to disclose. Let's talk
about how we handle it."* Sellers accept that far better than they accept discovering it afterwards.

### 24.5 The method

Six habits, and they prevent nearly every misrepresentation problem a licensee will ever have:

chunks.heading: 24.6 What you carry out of the 24-hour practice course
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Attribute or verify. Never assert.**
2. **Put it in writing.** Disclosures, material conversations, and every figure with its source.
3. **Disclose early.** A defect disclosed at listing is information. The same defect disclosed the week
   of closing is a crisis, and looks like concealment whether or not it was.
4. **Disclose to everyone entitled to it** — clients under § 339.730.1(3)(c), customers under
   § 339.730.3 and § 339.740.3.
5. **Route what is not yours.** Legal, tax, engineering, environmental, appraisal, zoning, boundary,
   flood, well, septic. Section 339.730.1(3)(d) requires it.
6. **When you get something wrong, correct it in writing immediately**, tell your designated broker, and
   document it. The alternative — quietly fixing it and hoping — converts an error into a concealment,
   and concealment is what turns a survivable problem into a licence problem.

### 24.6 What you carry out of the 24-hour practice course

**The sixteen topics 20 CSR 2250-6.060(2) requires**, and behind them one structure:

**Who is this person?** Client or customer, decided by a written agreement and by nothing else — not
rapport, not time, not who pays.

**What do I owe them?** To a client, the six duties of § 339.730.1 or § 339.740.1. To a customer,
adverse material fact disclosure. In dual agency, both sets of duties minus the five items of
§ 339.750.4. As a transaction broker, neutrality with the § 339.755.2 duties.

**What has to be in writing?** The broker disclosure form at first substantial contact under
§ 339.770.1. The brokerage agreement under § 339.780, with the contents that section specifies. Every
compensation arrangement. Every disclosure. Every material conversation.

chunks.heading: 24.7 The status of this course
chunks.excerpt:
**What is not mine?** Legal, tax, engineering, environmental and appraisal questions; the disposition of
disputed earnest money; what a municipality will permit; what a lender will approve; and what a price
will be next year.

### 24.7 The status of this course

This is a **version 1.0 submission draft**. It is **not approved**. **No Missouri pre-license credit is
available for it.** Under 20 CSR 2250-7.010(1)(L)6 no course may be announced or advertised for credit
until the Commission approves it in writing.

And the honest list of what this course could not read from primary text — § 339.100, § 339.105, 20 CSR
2250 chapters 1 through 5 and 8, every Commission-prescribed form, and Missouri's foreclosure,
landlord-tenant, probate, lien and tax chapters — is set out in
`missouri/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`. **Each must be read in current text before it is relied
on.** A school that would not tell you that list is not a school to buy education from.

### Module MREP-06 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module MREP-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the 75 percent final examination standard is the
Commission's, from 20 CSR 2250-7.080(1)(E).

---

## Instructor source note for Module MREP-06

Sections 339.710, 339.730, 339.740, 339.750, 339.755, 339.770 and 339.780, RSMo, and 20 CSR 2250-6.060,
2250-7.010, 2250-7.070 and 2250-7.080 were read from primary text on 2026-08-20 and are transcribed in
`missouri/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module MREP-06
chunks.excerpt:
**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this module:** § 339.100; § 339.105 and the trust account

and no deadline, threshold or figure from any of them appears.

lessons.title: North Carolina Broker Prelicensing Course — Module NC-01

chunks.heading: North Carolina Broker Prelicensing Course — Module NC-01
chunks.excerpt:
# North Carolina Broker Prelicensing Course — Module NC-01

## Section I · North Carolina Real Estate Licensure

**Commission syllabus section:** I — NC Real Estate Licensure
**Instructional Level:** **1**. At this level, students should be able to recall, define, classify,
describe, and explain the basic licensing facts and procedures.
**Licence examination weight:** **3 items** on the scored State-section distribution in the Commission's published
prelicensing syllabus.
**Recommended allocation:** **2.0 instructional hours.** This is the Commission's curriculum
allocation, not a claim that the present text by itself supplies two hours. Student-visible words,
media, activities, and assessments must be measured in the final unit timing ledger.
**Course version:** 1.1 development draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No North Carolina education credit is available.

> North Carolina prescribes the subjects, depth, activities, and completion standards for this
> course. StateCourse authors the explanations and practice. It does not use or attempt to obtain
> actual license-examination questions.

## Learning objectives

After completing this module, a student should be able to:

chunks.heading: 1. One license title, several status questions
chunks.excerpt:
1. distinguish the standard prelicensing route from the route for a person already licensed in
   another jurisdiction;
2. identify the threshold qualifications for an individual broker license;
3. sequence education, application, criminal-record review, examination, license issuance, and
   activation without treating any one step as permission to practice;
4. explain the three-year education clock, six-month criminal-report clock, and 180-day examination
   eligibility period;
5. describe the National and State examination sections, current published fees, results, and
   refiling rule;
6. distinguish inactive, active, provisional, nonprovisional, and broker-in-charge status; and
7. state the basic postlicensing, annual renewal, and continuing-education obligations that follow
   initial licensure.

---

## 1. One license title, several status questions

North Carolina licenses an individual as a **broker**. A new licensee is usually a **provisional
broker**, often abbreviated **PB**. “Provisional” is a status attached to the broker license; it is not
a separate salesperson license.

Every student should ask two independent questions before performing brokerage:

- **Is the license current or expired?** North Carolina licenses expire annually unless renewed.
- **Is the license active or inactive?** A current license can still be inactive. An inactive license
  does not authorize brokerage activity.

A provisional broker has an additional constraint: the license must be active **and** the provisional
broker must work under a broker-in-charge's supervision. Passing an examination does not activate a
license. Receiving an inactive license does not authorize practice. Affiliation and activation are
separate steps after issuance.

### Status map

chunks.heading: 2. Threshold qualifications
chunks.excerpt:
| Term | What it tells you | What it does not prove |
|---|---|---|
| applicant | the person has asked the Commission for a license | approval, examination success, or authority to practice |
| provisional broker | the individual holds the entry-level broker status | that the license is active |
| nonprovisional or “full” broker | provisional status has been removed or comparable status was issued | that the license is active or that the broker is BIC Eligible |
| active | the current license is eligible for brokerage activity, subject to all other limits | independent-practice or BIC authority |
| inactive | the person may hold a current license but may not perform brokerage | that the license has expired |
| broker-in-charge | a properly qualified and designated broker responsible for an office | that every nonprovisional broker is automatically a BIC |

The practical discipline is simple: **never infer authority from a title alone.** Verify the current
Commission record, including license status and any affiliation or designation required for the work.

---

## 2. Threshold qualifications

[G.S. 93A-4](https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_93A/GS_93A-4.html)
and the Commission's April 2026 *Real Estate Licensing in North Carolina* guide (**RELINC**) establish
the basic individual-license framework. An applicant must:

chunks.heading: Character is not a last-minute checkbox
chunks.excerpt:
- be at least **18 years old**;
- have the citizenship, lawful-presence, or federal work-authorization status described in the
  current application instructions;
- satisfy the education or permitted equivalent-qualification route;
- submit a complete application and current criminal record report;
- pass the examination section or sections required for that applicant, unless a specific exception
  applies; and
- satisfy the Commission as to competency, honesty, truthfulness, integrity, good character, and
  general fitness.

The statute does not turn course completion into an automatic entitlement to a license. Education is
one qualification. The application, examination when required, and character determination remain
independent Commission decisions.

### Character is not a last-minute checkbox

Every applicant must make complete and accurate disclosures. A criminal conviction is not the only
possible character issue. RELINC also directs applicants to disclose matters such as occupational
license discipline, unpaid judgments or liens, and other items asked on the current application.

An individual with a criminal history may use the Commission's **Petition for Pre-Determination**
process to ask whether that history is likely to disqualify the person. A predetermination is not a
license and does not eliminate the later application. It is a planning tool that can be used before
paying for the prelicensing course.

---

## 3. Standard prelicensing route

For most first-time applicants, the process is:

chunks.heading: The education clock
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Complete the 75-hour North Carolina Broker Prelicensing Course** with a Commission-certified
   Education Provider and pass its mandatory end-of-course examination.
2. **Wait for the provider's electronic completion report.** A student may start the online
   application, but the standard-course applicant cannot finalize it until the Commission has the
   provider's passing-completion report.
3. **Order the Commission-designated criminal record report.** The completed report is linked to the
   application.
4. **Submit the complete application and application fee.** The current published application fee is
   **$105**.
5. **Receive the Notice of Exam Eligibility** after the Commission processes a qualifying complete
   application.
6. **Schedule and pass the required National and State examination sections** through Pearson VUE.
7. **Wait for the Commission to issue the license.** Pearson and the test center do not issue it.
8. **Activate and affiliate the license before performing brokerage.** A new provisional broker and
   broker-in-charge use the Commission's License Activation/Affiliation process.

The order protects the applicant from a common mistake: treating a course certificate, eligibility
notice, or passing result as a license. None of those documents authorizes brokerage.

### The education clock

For the standard route, the Commission-approved North Carolina Broker Prelicensing Course must have
been completed within the **three years preceding the license application**. The syllabus describes
the measuring point as the course-completion date shown on the certificate issued after the student
passes the end-of-course examination.

chunks.heading: The criminal record report clock
chunks.excerpt:
That clock is not an exam-appointment deadline and it is not the license's renewal period. It answers
one question only: whether the course can still be used to support the application.

### The criminal record report clock

The criminal record report must be prepared by the Commission-designated reporting service within
the **six months before the application is filed**. The search must address the places and names
required by the current instructions. Multi-state, international, or multiple-name searches can take
longer and cost more.

Plan the report so it is recent enough to remain valid but early enough not to hold up filing. If the
report expires before a required new application, a new report is needed. Use only the service linked
from the current Commission application workflow; a consumer background report obtained elsewhere is
not a substitute.

---

## 4. Applicants with an existing license in another jurisdiction

An applicant who holds a current real estate salesperson or broker license in another qualifying
jurisdiction, and whose license was active within the preceding three years, may have a different
education and examination route under
[21 NCAC 58A .0511](https://reports.oah.state.nc.us/ncac/title%2021%20-%20occupational%20licensing%20boards%20and%20commissions/chapter%2058%20-%20real%20estate%20commission/subchapter%20a/21%20ncac%2058a%20.0511.pdf).
The applicant supplies an official certification of licensure meeting the Commission's current
requirements and elects one of two materially different paths:

chunks.heading: 5. License examination
chunks.excerpt:
| Election | Examination | Possible initial NC status |
|---|---|---|
| take the NC State section | National section is not repeated; State section must be passed | status the Commission determines comparable to the qualifying out-of-jurisdiction license |
| waive the NC State section | no NC license examination under this option | provisional broker status, with North Carolina postlicensing obligations |

“Comparable” is a Commission determination, not a promise a provider or applicant can make. An
out-of-state title that contains the word “broker” does not automatically establish what North
Carolina status will issue. The applicant must read the issued record.

The two elections also have different downstream consequences. RELINC states that a provisional
broker who used the no-State-exam option is not eligible for the out-of-state experience/education
postlicensing waiver under Rule 58A .1905. A candidate choosing speed at the application stage may
therefore accept a significant postlicensing obligation.

This special route should never be presented as the standard path for an unlicensed student. It
depends on a qualifying existing license and official documentation.

---

## 5. License examination

The North Carolina examination has separately timed and separately scored **National** and **State**
sections. Most standard-route applicants must pass both in the same eligibility period.

| Section | Scored items | Unscored pretest items | Time allowed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| National | 80 | 5 | 2.5 hours |
| State | 60 | 5 | 2.0 hours |

chunks.heading: Eligibility and fees
chunks.excerpt:
The five pretest items in each section are mixed among the scored items. Candidates cannot identify
them, and they do not count toward the score. The published passing score is **75 for each required
section**, calculated separately.

The Commission's syllabus distributes the 140 scored items by subject so a student can allocate
study effort. That distribution is not permission to ignore a “low-weight” topic, and it does not
reveal actual examination questions.

### Eligibility and fees

The official April 2026 RELINC guide publishes:

- **$105** to the Commission for each license-application submission;
- **$63** to Pearson for an attempt containing both sections; and
- **$53** to Pearson for an attempt containing one section.

These are the current published figures captured for this course. Fees and vendor terms can change;
the candidate must confirm the amount in the live Commission and Pearson workflows before paying.

The Notice of Exam Eligibility creates a **180-calendar-day examination eligibility period**. All
sections required for that candidate must be passed within the same period. A section passed in an
expired eligibility period does not carry into a new one.

### Results, failure, and refiling

Each application submission and application fee cover **one examination attempt**. A candidate who
fails a required section must return to the Commission application portal, verify or update the
application, refile, and pay another application fee before scheduling a retake. Pearson also charges
the applicable examination fee for the new appointment.

chunks.heading: Examination integrity
chunks.excerpt:
If the 180-day period expires before all required sections are passed, the applicant needs a new
eligibility period, a new application fee, and a new criminal record report. There is no published
limit on the number of times an otherwise qualified person may refile, but repeated attempts do not
extend the original 180-day clock.

The test center does not issue a license. Pearson reports the result to the Commission. The
Commission issues a license only after the required examination sections are timely passed and the
character requirement is satisfied. A person may not perform brokerage until the issued license has
been placed on the required active status.

### Examination integrity

The syllabus quotes Commission Rule 58H .0304(b): instructors must not obtain, use, or attempt to
obtain or use North Carolina license-examination questions in any manner or form. StateCourse
questions are independently authored from the prescribed curriculum and public official sources.
They are study checks, not recalled or reconstructed state-examination items.

---

## 6. After the license is issued

### Initial inactive provisional status

Most applicants licensed by examination receive an **inactive provisional broker license**. Before
performing brokerage, the provisional broker must affiliate with and be supervised by a
broker-in-charge and complete the Commission's License Activation/Affiliation process. Brokerage is
not lawful merely because an email reports a passing exam result.

An applicant who qualified through licensure in another jurisdiction and passed the State section
may instead be issued a comparable nonprovisional status. Because the Commission decides
comparability, the applicant must verify the status actually issued before relying on it.

### Postlicensing

chunks.heading: Renewal and continuing education
chunks.excerpt:
A provisional broker must complete **90 instructional hours of North Carolina Postlicensing
education within 18 months after initial licensure** to remain eligible for active status. The program
contains three 30-hour courses:

- Post 301 — Broker Relationships and Responsibilities;
- Post 302 — Contracts and Closing; and
- Post 303 — NC Law, Rules, and Legal Concepts.

After all three are reported, the Commission removes provisional status. If the deadline is missed,
the license is placed on inactive status until the education deficiency and reactivation requirements
are satisfied. Postlicensing is a one-time transition requirement; it is not the same as annual
continuing education.

### Renewal and continuing education

North Carolina real estate licenses expire at midnight on **June 30** unless renewed. The current
published renewal window is **May 15 through June 30**, and the current annual renewal fee is **$50**.
A recently issued license can still expire on the next June 30, so the licensee must check the actual
record rather than assume a full year from issuance.

For active-status eligibility, the ordinary annual continuing-education requirement is **8 hours**:
a 4-hour Update Course and a 4-hour Commission-approved elective. CE is due by **June 10** during the
applicable license period. RELINC identifies a limited initial-year exception: a broker newly licensed
by examination or reinstatement has no CE requirement during the initial license year and must meet
the annual requirement before the second renewal to renew on active status.

Renewal and CE answer different questions. Paying the renewal fee keeps the license current; timely
education is part of maintaining active-status eligibility. A current but inactive broker may not
perform brokerage.

chunks.heading: No authority to practice law
chunks.excerpt:
### No authority to practice law

G.S. 93A-4 states that the broker license does not authorize the practice of law. Later modules teach
the operational boundary between completing permitted preprinted forms and composing legal language.
When a transaction requires legal advice or drafting, the broker refers the parties to a qualified
attorney.

---

## 7. Worked decisions

### Decision 1 — “I passed today, so I can show property tonight.”

No. A passing result is transmitted to the Commission; it is not the issued and activated license.
The candidate must wait for issuance and then satisfy the activation/affiliation requirements that
apply to the issued status.

### Decision 2 — “My course certificate is two years and eleven months old.”

The certificate may still satisfy the three-year education window if the complete application is
filed before the period ends and every other requirement is met. The student should not schedule the
plan so tightly that an incomplete application or expired criminal report pushes filing beyond the
deadline.

### Decision 3 — “I am licensed elsewhere, so North Carolina must issue a full broker license.”

No. A qualifying out-of-jurisdiction license can open the Rule .0511 route. If the applicant elects
and passes the State section, the Commission determines comparable status. If the applicant waives
the State section, the rule provides provisional status. The final issued Commission record controls.

### Decision 4 — “I failed one section; I will just book Pearson again.”

chunks.heading: Decision 5 — “I renewed online, so my license is active.”
chunks.excerpt:
Not yet. The candidate must first return to the Commission portal, refile the application for another
attempt, and pay the application fee. Only after a new eligibility notice authorizes the remaining
section may the candidate pay Pearson and schedule it. The remaining section must still be passed
within the same 180-day eligibility period.

### Decision 5 — “I renewed online, so my license is active.”

Not necessarily. Renewal prevents expiration, but active-status eligibility also depends on the
education and affiliation requirements applicable to the licensee. Verify the Commission record
before performing brokerage.

---

## StateCourse application-clock activity

This is a StateCourse practice activity, not a Commission-prescribed Required Activity for Section I.
Complete it before the module assessment.

For each scenario, write the document or date you would verify next and explain why:

1. A student's course certificate will reach three years of age in 35 days, but the criminal record
   report has not been ordered.
2. An applicant has passed the National section, has 20 days left in the examination eligibility
   period, and has not passed the State section.
3. A newly issued provisional broker has an inactive status and an offer to conduct an open house.
4. A broker pays the renewal fee on June 25 but has not satisfied the CE requirement that applies to
   that license period.
5. An out-of-state broker wants to waive the State section but also expects immediate
   nonprovisional status.

chunks.heading: Module NC-01 assessment
chunks.excerpt:
An acceptable response identifies the controlling clock or status and does not invent an extension.
The purpose is to connect dates to decisions: three years governs education use; six months governs
the criminal report; 180 days governs required exam sections; June 10 is the ordinary CE deadline;
June 30 is the license-expiration and renewal deadline; and issuance is separate from activation.

## Module NC-01 assessment

The module contains one applied scenario, five engagement checks, and five remediation checks. The
applied item must be correct; the engagement and remediation sets use an 80% StateCourse practice
threshold.

That 80% threshold is not the Commission's end-of-course standard. The separate regulated
end-of-course examination must be comprehensive, closed-book, proctored, and passed at **75% or
higher** under the applicable Commission rule. This development build does not yet administer that
protected final or award credit.

---

## Instructor source note for Module NC-01

**Primary and official sources reviewed for this revision (2026-09-07):**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module NC-01
chunks.excerpt:
- [G.S. 93A-4](https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_93A/GS_93A-4.html),
  current official General Assembly text: age, education framework, examination, character, initial
  provisional status, postlicensing authority, annual expiration, criminal-record authority, and
  no authority to practice law;
- [21 NCAC 58A .0301](https://reports.oah.state.nc.us/ncac/title%2021%20-%20occupational%20licensing%20boards%20and%20commissions/chapter%2058%20-%20real%20estate%20commission/subchapter%20a/21%20ncac%2058a%20.0301.pdf)
  and [.0302](https://reports.oah.state.nc.us/ncac/title%2021%20-%20occupational%20licensing%20boards%20and%20commissions/chapter%2058%20-%20real%20estate%20commission/subchapter%20a/21%20ncac%2058a%20.0302.pdf),
  current official OAH indexed rule text: application content, criminal report, and fee;
- [21 NCAC 58A .0511](https://reports.oah.state.nc.us/ncac/title%2021%20-%20occupational%20licensing%20boards%20and%20commissions/chapter%2058%20-%20real%20estate%20commission/subchapter%20a/21%20ncac%2058a%20.0511.pdf),
  current official OAH indexed rule text: other-jurisdiction elections and status;
- NCREC, *Real Estate Licensing in North Carolina*, April 2026 (**RELINC**), official 36-page PDF
  captured in `north-carolina/regulatory/captures/2026-09-06/`: workflow, examination details,
  status, postlicensing, CE, renewal, and current published fees; and
- NCREC, *North Carolina Real Estate Prelicensing Course Syllabus*, March 2024 Edition, amended May
  2026: prescribed Section I topics, level, hours, examination weight, and course standards.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module NC-01
chunks.excerpt:
The official OAH PDF endpoints did not return retained PDF bytes during the September 6 integrity
capture, although current indexed rule text was reviewed. They remain transport-lock dependencies
for the formal filing package. That evidence limitation does **not** justify telling a student that
the governing rules are unknown; it is tracked in the regulatory ledger and rechecked before
submission. Fees, vendor procedures, and forms must also be revalidated at enrollment and filing.

lessons.title: North Carolina Broker Prelicensing Course — Module NC-02

chunks.heading: North Carolina Broker Prelicensing Course — Module NC-02
chunks.excerpt:
# North Carolina Broker Prelicensing Course — Module NC-02

## Section II · Broker Supervision & Compensation

**Commission Syllabus section:** II — Broker Supervision & Compensation
**Instructional Level:** **3** unless otherwise noted. *Assigned by the Commission; providers and
instructors are **REQUIRED to comply**.* At Level 3 the instructor reviews and discusses the topic **in
substantial depth**, using examples, **and requires students to complete practical work assignments**
demonstrating both understanding and the ability to apply the knowledge **to common fact situations
that will be encountered in real estate practice**.
**Licence examination weight:** **State Exam Category — 4 items.**
**Recommended allocation:** **2.0 instructional hours**, within the Commission's recommended 13.0
hours for the Agency subject area. This label is not timing proof; student-visible time belongs in
the final unit ledger.
**Course version:** 1.1 development draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No North Carolina prelicensing credit is available.

> **Instructor Note, from the Syllabus:** *"This Section is not discussed in the LLCR but must be
> covered."* So a student who reads only the License Law and Commission Rules booklet will not find
> this material there. It is covered here because the Commission requires it to be.

## Learning objectives

At Level 3 — justify, judge, weigh, apply to fact situations:

chunks.heading: A. Supervision
chunks.excerpt:
1. Explain what a broker-in-charge is and what supervision of a provisional broker means.
2. State the four legal requirements for a listing agent to establish a claim to compensation.
3. Apply the procuring cause doctrine to a disputed commission.
4. Identify the six situations in which a broker may be entitled to a fee **even though the
   transaction does not close**.
5. Explain how an earned brokerage fee is shared in an in-house sale and in a co-brokered sale.
6. State who may lawfully pay a provisional broker, and who may pay an affiliated full broker.
7. Apply the out-of-state co-brokerage conditions to a referral fact pattern.
8. State the three legal requirements for a buyer agent to establish a claim to compensation.
9. Apply the active-licence rule to a payment made after a licence has lapsed.

---

## A. Supervision

### A.1 Broker supervision of provisional brokers

A **provisional broker** does not practise on their own account. They practise **under the supervision
of a broker-in-charge**, and the supervision is a real, ongoing obligation on the supervising broker
rather than a formality of registration.

Statutory and rule references the Syllabus names: **NCGS 93A-2(b)** and **Commission Rule 58A .0506**.

The current official text of Rule 58A .0506 makes the control operational:

chunks.heading: A.2 Broker-in-charge — *Level 1 for this subtopic*
chunks.excerpt:
- the provisional broker may engage in or hold themself out as engaging in licensed activity only
  while the license is active and the broker is supervised by the BIC of the affiliated firm or
  office;
- ordinarily the PB has one supervising BIC; the narrow exception permits no more than two BICs of
  two affiliated firms sharing the same physical location and acting as co-listing or co-selling
  agents, with both carrying full supervision responsibility;
- the PB and BIC submit the Commission's License Activation and Broker Affiliation form;
- upon submission, the PB may work under supervision, but if written Commission acknowledgment is
  not received within **30 days of the date shown on the form**, the PB must stop licensed activity
  pending acknowledgment; and
- when the supervisory relationship ends, both PB and BIC notify the Commission in writing no later
  than **10 days after termination**.

The rule defines supervision by its purpose: the BIC must supervise in a manner that assures the PB
performs licensed acts in accordance with the License Law and Commission rules. It does not create a
universal “BIC must be physically present” test, nor does a promise to be available by telephone by
itself prove adequate supervision. The work, the PB's competence, risk, review, and actual compliance
all matter.

### A.2 Broker-in-charge — *Level 1 for this subtopic*

*The Commission drops this subtopic to Level 1: review and discuss the basic facts; in-depth
instruction is not required.*

A **broker-in-charge (BIC)** is the broker designated as responsible for a real estate office. The BIC
carries the supervisory duties for the provisional brokers and other licensees affiliated with that
office.

chunks.heading: B. Earning a Real Estate Brokerage Fee (Sales)
chunks.excerpt:
Statutory and rule references the Syllabus names: **NCGS 93A-2(a1)** and **93A-4.2**, and **Commission
Rule 58A .0110(g)(1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 10)**.

Current Rule 58A .0110 ordinarily requires one designated BIC for a firm's principal office and one
for each branch. To obtain BIC Eligible status, a broker must be active and meet the rule's experience
route — generally at least two years of brokerage experience equivalent to 40 hours per week within
the previous five years, or the stated North Carolina-attorney alternative — and complete the
12-hour BIC Course in the permitted window: no earlier than one year before application and no later
than 120 days after it.

The designated BIC's duties include assuring affiliated brokers' license/status compliance,
supervising provisional brokers, responsibility for office advertising, trust accounts and
transaction records, and compliance with agency-agreement and disclosure requirements. The precise
current rule controls; a firm cannot reduce these duties by contract.

---

## B. Earning a Real Estate Brokerage Fee (Sales)

References the Syllabus names: **NCGS 93A-6(a)(9)** and **Commission Rule 58A .0109**.

This is the Level 3 heart of the section, and it is worth understanding precisely, because compensation
disputes are common and they are decided on these elements.

### B.1 Earning compensation as a listing agent

**Four legal requirements for establishing a claim to compensation:**

1. **A current real estate licence on active status.**
2. **A valid written listing contract.**
3. **Procurement of a ready, willing and able buyer.**
4. **The procuring cause doctrine.**

Take them one at a time.

**Current licence on active status.** Not merely held — **active**. B.2 below returns to what happens
when it is not.

chunks.heading: B.2 Entitlement to a fee where the transaction does NOT close
chunks.excerpt:
**A valid written listing contract.** Written. An oral listing does not support a compensation claim.

**A ready, willing and able buyer.** *Ready* and *willing* to buy on the seller's terms, and *able* —
financially capable of completing. A buyer who wants the property and cannot fund it is not an able
buyer.

**Procuring cause.** The doctrine that asks **whose efforts actually produced the ready, willing and
able buyer** — an unbroken chain from the broker's efforts to the buyer's decision. It is the doctrine
that resolves the argument between two brokers who both had contact with the same buyer, and it is
decided on facts: who introduced the property, who maintained the relationship, who was continuously
involved, and whether anything broke the chain.

### B.2 Entitlement to a fee where the transaction does NOT close

The Syllabus lists six situations in which a broker who has **fulfilled their contract duties** may be
entitled to a fee even though the contract does not close. Transcribed:

- **The seller refuses to close.**
- **The seller's spouse will not sign the contract or deed.**
- **The seller has an uncorrected defect in the title.**
- **The seller is unable to deliver possession within a reasonable time.**
- **The seller insists on sales terms and conditions not stated in the listing contract.**
- **The buyer and seller conspire after the sales contract has been signed and agree to cancel the
  contract.**

**Read what those six have in common.** In every one, **the failure to close is the seller's doing, or
a collusive act, rather than the broker's failure to perform.** The broker produced what the listing
contract asked for; the transaction failed for a reason on the seller's side of the line.

chunks.heading: B.3 Sharing the listing broker's compensation
chunks.excerpt:
**And read what they are not.** They are not a general rule that a broker is paid when a deal collapses.
A buyer who cannot obtain financing, a property that does not appraise, an inspection that ends the
transaction — none of those is on this list.

**Whether a fee is actually owed in a given case is a legal question**, and a broker with a disputed
claim takes it to their broker-in-charge and to counsel. What a licensee must be able to do is
**recognise which category a failed transaction falls into**, and that is what Level 3 asks for here.

### B.3 Sharing the listing broker's compensation

Before tracing payment through a firm, apply Rule 58A .0109:

- a licensee may not take more than nominal value from a vendor or supplier for an expenditure made
  for the principal without the principal's written consent;
- compensation for a service recommended, procured, or arranged for a party requires full and timely
  disclosure to that party;
- in a sales transaction, compensation from the broker's principal must be provided for in the
  written agency contract;
- compensation from another person requires full and timely disclosure to the principal; an oral
  disclosure must be confirmed in writing before the principal makes or accepts an offer;
- the disclosure identifies the compensation or consideration, its value, and who will or may pay it;
  and
- the Commission does not set commission rates or arbitrate private fee and split disputes.

Rule .0109 also prohibits sharing compensation with an unlicensed person or entity for an act
performed in North Carolina that requires a license, except for the rule's narrow vacation-rental
travel-agent provision. That exception has its own conditions and is not a general referral-fee rule.

chunks.heading: B.4 Co-brokerage with a broker licensed in another state
chunks.excerpt:
**The in-house sale** — where the same firm is on both sides:

- **How the earned brokerage fee is split** is settled between the parties and the firm.
- **A licensee's ability to receive compensation is determined by the employment agreement between the
  broker and the brokerage company.**
- **Affiliated provisional brokers must be compensated by their supervising broker-in-charge** —
  **NCGS 93A-6(a)(5)**.
- **Affiliated "full" brokers must be compensated by their supervising broker-in-charge** —
  **Commission Rule 58A .0120(b)**.

**Those last two are the ones a new licensee must know cold.** Rule 58A .0120(b) says an affiliated
broker may not be paid a commission or referral fee directly by anyone other than the broker's current
BIC or the person who served as BIC at the time of the transaction. That applies to an affiliated
broker whether provisional or nonprovisional. The rule is about lawful payment flow; the affiliation
agreement and other applicable law determine whether and how much is owed.

**The co-brokered sale** — where two firms are involved:

- **The ability to receive compensation from the listing company is negotiated between the parties.**
- **Cooperative listing service agreements** may govern how that negotiation is conducted.

Note what "negotiated between the parties" excludes: **there is no automatic entitlement.** A
cooperating broker's compensation comes from an agreement, and where there is no agreement there is no
claim.

### B.4 Co-brokerage with a broker licensed in another state

The Syllabus states two conditions and both must be met:

chunks.heading: B.5 Earning compensation as a buyer agent
chunks.excerpt:
- **The out-of-state (foreign) broker must hold an active real estate licence in the state from which
  they are conducting the brokerage activity**, such as placing a referral; **and**
- **The foreign broker does not enter North Carolina at any time during the transaction to engage in
  any brokerage activity related to the transaction.**

**"Does not enter NC at any time during the transaction to engage in any brokerage activity" is the
condition that catches people.** A referring broker who flies in to attend a showing, or to meet the
client at the property, has done brokerage activity in North Carolina without a North Carolina licence.

### B.5 Earning compensation as a buyer agent

**Three legal requirements for establishing a claim:**

1. **A current real estate licence on active status.**
2. **A valid written buyer agency contract.**
3. **Procurement of property described in the agency agreement that the buyer agrees to purchase by
   enforceable contract.**

Note how requirement 3 differs from the listing side. On the listing side the broker procures a **ready,
willing and able buyer**; on the buyer side the broker procures **property described in the agency
agreement** which the buyer then agrees to purchase **by enforceable contract**.

Two compensation structures the Syllabus names on the buyer side:

- a **retainer fee** and a **success fee**; and
- **sharing in the listing broker's fee.**

### B.6 Payment where a licence has expired or become inactive

The rule and the exception, both from the Syllabus:

- **The licence must be on active status when the brokerage activity is performed.**
- **A broker must stop all brokerage activity when their licence expires or becomes inactive.**

**Instructor Note, transcribed:**

chunks.heading: Required Activities in this section
chunks.excerpt:
> **If the licences of the firm and the individual broker were both on active status at the time that
> any brokerage service was rendered in the transaction, then the firm may be paid compensation and the
> firm may in turn pay the individual broker, even if their licence is not active at the time of
> payment. Payment is forfeited if either of the licences were not active at any time that services
> were being performed.**

Read that twice, because it cuts both ways.

**The permission:** payment may be received after a licence has lapsed, **provided both licences were
active throughout the period services were rendered.** A licence that expires between closing and
disbursement does not destroy a properly earned fee.

**The forfeiture:** **"Payment is forfeited if EITHER of the licences were not active at ANY time that
services were being performed."** Not reduced — forfeited. And it turns on **both** the firm's licence
and the individual's, at **any** point during the work.

**The practical consequence:** know your renewal date, know your firm's, and **stop working the moment
either lapses.** Continuing to work through a lapse does not merely risk discipline; it destroys the
fee for the whole transaction.

---

## Required Activities in this section

**The Syllabus prescribes no Required Activity for Section II.** Its Level 3 assignment nonetheless
carries an instructional requirement of its own: Level 3 instruction **requires students to complete
practical work assignments** applying the material to common fact situations. **This module's applied
assessment item and its compensation fact patterns are that work**, and they are a completion condition
rather than optional practice.

## Module NC-02 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module NC-02
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items, delivered as in Module NC-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, under Commission Rule 58H .0207 as the Syllabus quotes it.

---

## Instructor source note for Module NC-02

Drawn from **Section II** of the Commission's Prelicensing Course Syllabus, March 2024 Edition amended
May 2026, read on 2026-08-20 and recorded in `north-carolina/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`. On
2026-09-07, the module was reconciled to the current official OAH text of **21 NCAC 58A .0109,
.0110, .0120, and .0506**, and to the April 2026 RELINC guide. The

The official OAH PDF endpoints were readable through the official indexed source but retained bytes
