chunks.heading: North Carolina Broker Prelicensing Course — Module NC-11
chunks.excerpt:
# North Carolina Broker Prelicensing Course — Module NC-11

## Section XI · Contracts & Closing in NC

**Commission Syllabus section:** XI — Contracts & Closing in NC
**Instructional Level:** **2** except as noted. *Assigned by the Commission; providers and instructors
are **REQUIRED to comply**.* **The Offer to Purchase and Contract (Part B) is Level 3**, and **Sales
Contract Procedures (Part D) is Level 3.**
**Licence examination weight:** **State Exam Category — 7 items.**
**Instructional hours:** **8.0**, the second-largest allocation in this course, drawn from the
Commission's recommended 18.0 hours for the Contracts and Closing subject area.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No North Carolina prelicensing credit is available.

> ### A submission gate stated at the top of this module
>
> **The Commission prescribes a Required Activity for this section that this project cannot yet
> satisfy.** Transcribed:
>
> *"The **NCAR/NCBA OPC Standard Form 2-T**, **Guidelines for Completing The Offer to Purchase and
> Contract Form**, and the **most commonly used standard addenda forms** designed for use with the 2-T
> form **must be provided to students and used in this instruction**. Conduct a **detailed review of
> each paragraph** in the Standard Form 2-T, including any prompts to attach a completed standard
> addendum as part of the offer/contract. Be sure to discuss **the purpose of each paragraph, and common
> issues in filling various blanks**."*
>
> **This project has NOT obtained Form 2-T, the Guidelines, or any standard addendum.** Accordingly:
>
> - **No document in this build reproduces, describes, paraphrases or explains any provision of Form
>   2-T or of any addendum.**
> - What follows is **the Syllabus'

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
s own account of the form's structure and its notes**, which was
>   read — the paragraph subjects, the Commission's warnings, and the structural facts the Syllabus
>   states about how the North Carolina contract works.
> - **The paragraph-by-paragraph review the Commission requires cannot be delivered from this module as
>   it stands.** Obtaining the current Form 2-T, the Guidelines and the addenda, and building that
>   review, is a **submission gate for this course.**

## Learning objectives

1. State the general rules for interpreting contracts.
2. State the prohibition on drafting and what a broker may lawfully do with a preprinted form.
3. State where standardized forms come from and which forms the Commission itself authors.
4. Reconcile the current 18-item Rule 58A .0112(a) list and the 2025 compensation amendment with the
   older 19-item/two-prohibition syllabus wording.
5. **Explain the North Carolina due diligence model and why it differs from a contingency model.**
   *(Level 3)*
6. Distinguish the Due Diligence Fee from the Earnest Money Deposit.
7. Distinguish Settlement from Closing.
8. **Separate prompt offer presentation from Rule .0106's three-day executed-instrument delivery and
   apply the offer-disclosure rules.** *(Level 3)*
9. Describe the settlement agent's role and what a broker provides them.
10. Work through the buyer's due diligence process and the pre-closing matters.
11. State the broker's settlement statement responsibility.

---

## A. Introduction

### A.1 General rules for the interpretation of contracts

Six, transcribed:

chunks.heading: A.2 Drafting by brokers is prohibited
chunks.excerpt:
- **The parol evidence rule.**
- **Written overrides oral.**
- **Contracts are interpreted as a whole.**
- **Words will be interpreted per their ordinary meaning unless other intent is clearly noted.**
- **Written overrides preprinted language, if there is a conflict.**
- **The writer of ambiguous language will be held liable for the confusion; the court generally rules in
  favour of the party that did NOT draft the confusing language.**

**The last two together explain why a broker must not independently improvise legal language.** Rule
58A .0111 allows a broker to complete a compliant preprinted form when a party authorizes or directs
the broker to do so, and it allows a party-directed change to be marked on the form. It does not let the
broker decide what legal language the party needs, rewrite the form in advance, or interpret its legal
effect. Route unique language and legal-effect questions to a North Carolina attorney.

### A.2 Drafting by brokers is prohibited

NCGS 93A-6(a)(11); Commission Rule 58A .0111; NCGS 84-2.1.

- **Preparing a legal instrument or giving legal advice for another person is unauthorized practice of
  law unless a statutory exception applies.**
- **Rule 58A .0111 permits a broker-agent to complete a preprinted offer, option, sales-contract or lease
  form when authorized or directed by the parties.** The broker may record a party-directed change on
  the form, but may not alter the preprinted form before presentation or independently compose the
  change.
- **Instructor Note:** *"Have an attorney draft any unique contract language."*

### A.3 Sources of standardized sales contract forms

chunks.heading: B. The Offer to Purchase and Contract *(Level 3)*
chunks.excerpt:
- **REALTORS® may obtain and use the contract forms created by NC REALTORS® as part of their membership
  benefits.**
- **Non-REALTOR® brokers may NOT initiate use of forms bearing only the REALTOR® logo.**
- **Non-REALTOR® brokers may obtain and use the sales contract forms and standard addenda that are
  JOINTLY APPROVED by North Carolina REALTORS® and the North Carolina Bar Association (NCBA), bearing
  only the NCBA logo/approval, through an attorney or forms vendor.**

**Instructor Note, transcribed — and it is important for understanding what the Commission does and
does not control:**

> *"**NCREC does not create the standardized sales contract forms used by the majority of NC
> licensees.** The **only** standardized forms authored by the Commission are:*
>
> - ***Working With Real Estate Agents Disclosure***
> - ***Residential Property and Owners' Association Disclosure Statement (RPOADS)***
> - ***Mineral and Oil and Gas Mandatory Disclosure Statement (MOG)***"

**Those are the three Commission-authored forms identified by the syllabus.** Do not infer that every
other document in every residential file comes from one publisher; lenders, settlement counsel,
inspectors, insurers, associations and public agencies may supply other transaction documents. The
standard offer and addenda assigned here are joint NC REALTORS®/North Carolina Bar Association forms.
None of the three Commission-authored forms has been retained and reviewed in this project.

---

## B. The Offer to Purchase and Contract *(Level 3)*

### B.1 Current requirements for a broker-provided preprinted sales form — Rule 58A .0112

chunks.heading: B.1a Level 3 evidence — current-rule reconciliation
chunks.excerpt:
The May 2026 syllabus still says the rule contains **19** required items and prohibits both brokerage
compensation and a broker-liability disclaimer. The current controlling sources no longer say that:

- **Rule 58A .0112(a) now contains 18 numbered items, not 19.** They cover party/property identity,
  personal property, price/payment, financing or assumption terms if used, earnest money, assessments,
  closing/possession, signatures and dates, title/conveyance, prorations, expenses, inspection/repairs,
  condition at closing, brokerage identity/agency, and other disclosures required by law. The syllabus
  says students need not memorize the list, but the provider must teach the current rule rather than
  preserve the obsolete count.
- **Session Law 2025-52 directed the Commission to allow** a broker-agent to use a preprinted offer or
  sales contract containing a provision for commission or compensation, including forfeiture of
  earnest money, to a broker or firm. Current Rule .0112(b)(1) now says the broker **may** use such a
  preprinted form.
- **Rule .0112(b)(2) still prohibits** a preprinted provision attempting to disclaim a broker's
  liability for the broker's representations in the transaction.
- This change does **not** authorize independent broker drafting. Rule .0111 still controls completion
  and party-directed changes; legal drafting and advice go to counsel.

#### B.1a Level 3 evidence — current-rule reconciliation

chunks.heading: B.2 Proper use of the OPC form
chunks.excerpt:
| Source presented | Student classification | Operational result |
|---|---|---|
| syllabus says 19 items | older prescribed-course wording | flag the discrepancy; do not teach 19 as current rule text |
| current Rule .0112(a) numbers 1-18 | controlling administrative rule | use 18 for compliance review |
| syllabus says compensation provision prohibited | superseded syllabus statement | do not use as the current answer |
| Session Law 2025-52 and current Rule .0112(b)(1) say `may use` | controlling current law/rule | a compliant preprinted compensation provision is permitted |
| Rule .0112(b)(2) bars a broker-liability disclaimer | controlling current rule | reject the form/provision and route correction to counsel |

**Student output:** identify the source, effective sequence and action for each row. A statement that
the current rule still prohibits two provisions fails the exercise.

### B.2 Proper use of the OPC form

- **Primarily intended for the sale of EXISTING SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENCES.**
- **Use standard addenda to tailor it to the needs of the parties.**
- **Do NOT use it for a lease-option agreement, a lease-purchase agreement, or an installment land
  contract.**

*(Module NC-07 F: those three require an attorney, and using a standard sales contract for them is
expressly warned against.)*

### B.3 General guidelines for contract completion

Transcribed from the Syllabus:

chunks.heading: B.4 The structural facts about the North Carolina contract
chunks.excerpt:
- **Type or print legibly.**
- **Fill in ALL the blanks; enter "N/A" or "none" as appropriate.**
- **Be precise; avoid abbreviations, acronyms, or unclear terminology.**
- **BOTH Buyer and Seller should initial and date EVERY change, addition, or deletion.**
- **Rewrite the offer if there are numerous changes; retain copies of all offers and contracts.**
- **Review ALL contract provisions with the parties and RECOMMEND THEY OBTAIN LEGAL ADVICE to answer
  legal questions.**
- **Instructor Note:** *"Be sure to highlight all the **Notes and Warnings** in the form."*

**"Fill in ALL the blanks" is a real discipline.** A blank left empty is an ambiguity, and A.1's last
rule says ambiguity is construed against the person who created it.

### B.4 The structural facts about the North Carolina contract

**This is the syllabus's account of the residential contract model.** It is not a substitute for the
required review of the current form itself. The current 2026 Form 2-T and Form 2G downloads are listed
by NC REALTORS® but require member access; this repository has not lawfully obtained and page-reviewed
those files.

#### Defined terms

**Instructor Note, transcribed:** *"Whenever a term that would not normally be capitalized appears in
the body of a contract and begins with a capital letter, it indicates that **the word or phrase is a
defined term** that can be found somewhere earlier in that contract. Most of the defined terms in Form
2-T are defined in Paragraph #1. **Words that appear in parenthesis** … **are optional words to be used
or ignored as appropriate.**"*

chunks.heading: The due diligence model — the single most important structural fact in North Carolina practice
chunks.excerpt:
The Syllabus names the defined terms in Paragraph 1 as including: **Names of Seller and Buyer; Property
Description; Purchase Price; Earnest Money Deposit (EMD); Escrow Agent; Effective Date; Due Diligence,
comprising the Due Diligence Fee (DDF) and the Due Diligence Period (DDP); Settlement; Closing; and
Special Assessments.**

#### The due diligence model — the single most important structural fact in North Carolina practice

**Instructor Note, transcribed:**

> ***"There are NO FINANCING OR APPRAISAL CONTINGENCIES in this contract.** Buyer should be strongly
> encouraged to meet with a mortgage lender prior to starting a property search. Ideally, DDP should be
> long enough for Buyer to receive the appraisal and to feel confident in their ability to obtain loan
> approval."*

**And from Part E, transcribed:**

> *"**Standard 2-T contract is NOT contingent on loan approval.**"*
> *"**Inability of the buyer to secure financing AFTER the DDP would result in a buyer's BREACH of the
> contract.**"*

**Read those together, because they describe a system fundamentally different from the contingency model
taught in most national materials.**

In a contingency state, a buyer whose loan fails may terminate under the financing contingency and
recover their deposit. **In North Carolina, under the standard form, there is no financing contingency
at all.** Instead:

- The buyer has a **Due Diligence Period** during which they may terminate **for any reason or no
  reason**.
- The buyer pays a **Due Diligence Fee** for that right.
- **After the DDP ends**, the buyer's right to terminate without penalty is gone — and **a failure to
  obtain financing at that point is a breach.**

chunks.heading: DDF and EMD are different money
chunks.excerpt:
**Instructor Note on the DDP, transcribed:** *"Buyers should be **strongly advised to perform due
diligence activities as quickly as possible** to allow time for negotiation about any discovered issues
to be resolved **prior to the end of the DDP**. **The Buyer is not limited to the investigative items
listed** … **Seller is not obligated to engage in repair negotiations or extend the DDP.** If the Buyer
does not terminate the contract prior to the end of the DDP, **the Buyer may continue to investigate the
Property after the DDP but has WAIVED THEIR RIGHT TO TERMINATE without penalty unless there is a Seller
breach.**"*

**Three consequences a licensee must be able to state to a buyer:**

1. **The DDP is the buyer's whole protection**, and it runs whether or not anyone is working.
2. **The seller need not extend it and need not negotiate repairs.**
3. **After it ends, financing failure is the buyer's breach.**

**Which is why the Commission tells you to get the buyer to a lender BEFORE the search begins, and to
make the DDP long enough for the appraisal to arrive.**

#### DDF and EMD are different money

The **Due Diligence Fee** and the **Earnest Money Deposit** are separately defined and handled
differently. **The DDF is paid for the due diligence right; the EMD is a deposit held in escrow.**

chunks.heading: DDF and EMD are different money
chunks.excerpt:
> **Required Activity — prescribed by the Commission:** *"Use various scenarios to explore how **initial
> and additional types of EMD should be handled and when it should be delivered to the Escrow Agent** at
> various points during the transaction. Pay particular attention to application of **Commission Rule
> 58A .0116(b)(3-4)** regarding following Buyer's instructions for delivery to and the timing of deposit
> by the Escrow Agent."*
>
> **Worked activity:** classify the payee, instrument, recipient's license status and offer status before
> starting any clock.
>
> | Scenario | Rule .0116 result | Evidence to record |
> |---|---|---|
> | active broker receives ordinary trust money; no exception applies | deposit in a qualifying trust/escrow account no later than three **banking** days after receipt | amount, form, receipt time, account and deposit time |
> | provisional broker receives any trust money | deliver it **upon receipt** to the affiliated broker | receipt and handoff times |
> | non-currency initial EMD accompanies a pending offer | deposit no later than three days after acceptance; the agreement states the acceptance date | offer status, acceptance date and deposit time |
> | non-currency additional EMD is received after the contract is already effective | the pending-offer exception does not fit; apply the ordinary three-banking-day baseline unless another exception does | contract status, receipt and deposit times |
> | negotiable instrument is payable to seller for option/DDF or to designated escrow agent | safeguard it; follow the buyer's delivery/return instruction; do not retain it more than three business days after contract acceptance | payee, buyer instruction, acceptance and delivery/return times |
>
> Contractual deadlines for initial or additi

chunks.heading: Settlement and Closing — identify which source owns the vocabulary
chunks.excerpt:
onal EMD are separate from the broker-custody rules above.
> The unavailable current Form 2-T and Form 2G must be reviewed before teaching their contractual due
> dates. Do not manufacture a form deadline from Rule .0116.

**Disputed EMD** — NCGS 93A-12; Rule 58A .0116(d). Module NC-10.

#### Settlement and Closing — identify which source owns the vocabulary

**Instructor Note, transcribed:** *"**The settlement meeting and closing do not always happen on the same
day**, especially if settlement occurs late in the day."*

The syllabus uses **Settlement** and **Closing** as two separate capitalized contract concepts and warns
that possession should not be promised before the later event contemplated by the form. The current
form must supply the exact contractual definitions; it has not been obtained here.

Do not cite the Good Funds Settlement Act as if it used those terms the same way. **G.S. 45A-3 has its
own statutory vocabulary:** it defines *Closing* as the agreed execution and delivery of the documents
needed to consummate the transaction, and *Settlement* as the time the settlement agent has received
the executed deed, security instrument, other loan documents and required funds. **G.S. 45A-4 then
separately requires recordation and generally bars disbursement of other closing funds until required
documents are recorded and collected-funds conditions are met.**

**Broker practice rule:** name the source whenever using either term. Do not promise possession,
recordation or disbursement from the label alone; verify the current contract, counsel's status report,
the funds and the land records.

#### Other structural notes the Syllabus states

chunks.heading: Other structural notes the Syllabus states
chunks.excerpt:
- **Prorations and adjustments are based on 365 days per year** — taxes on real property, taxes on
  personal property, rents if any, and dues.
- **Buyer representations and Seller representations** are **"informational only and do not rise to the
  level of a contract condition or contingency absent relevant attached addenda"** — though each party
  **"is liable for the accuracy of all representations made"** and the other **"is entitled to rely on
  the information."**
- **The condition of property / risk of loss paragraph SURVIVES expiration of the DDP.**
- **A party may in stated circumstances be entitled to a seven (7) day delay in Settlement.**
- **"Good and workmanlike manner" is a term of art** — **Instructor Note:** *"It means the work has been
  completed to the standard of the industry."*
- On seller breach: **"Buyer may terminate the Contract and receive a refund of any EMD and DDF paid"**,
  and may **"obtain reimbursement from Seller for reasonable costs incurred in conducting the Due
  Diligence"** — with the Commission's caution that **"an attorney should be consulted to determine if a
  breach has occurred."**
- **Instructor Note on addenda:** *"**A NC real estate broker is NOT permitted to suggest or draft any
  addenda for others** (unless they are an actively licensed NC attorney)."*
- **Instructor Note on the Notice Information page:** *"Entry of any Buyer or Seller contact information
  in the Notice Information section **authorizes communication directly to a Party rather than the
  standard practice of communicating through the agents**."*
- The signature page carries a **Wire Fraud Warning**.
- Mechanic's lien protection appears through an **Affidavit and Indemnification Agreement** — NCGS
  44A-8 — and **Designation of Lien Agent** where requir

chunks.heading: B.5 Commonly used standard addenda
chunks.excerpt:
ed by **NCGS 44A-11.1**.

*(Every item above is the Syllabus's statement about the form. **None of the form's own language is
reproduced here**, and the paragraph-level review the Commission requires remains outstanding.)*

### B.5 Commonly used standard addenda

The Syllabus names eight for review: **Additional Provisions Addendum (2A11-T); Back-Up Contract Addendum
(2A1-T); FHA/VA Financing Addendum (2A4-T); Lead-Based Paint or Lead-Based Paint Hazard Addendum
(2A9-T); Short Sale Addendum (2A14-T); Buyer Possession Before Closing Agreement (2A7-T); Seller
Possession After Closing Agreement (2A8-T); Vacation Rental Addendum (2A13-T).**

**Instructor Note on conflicts, transcribed:** *"In an event of a conflict between information in an
addendum and the contract, **the ADDENDUM will control** — **unless** the conflict involves **the
description of the Property or the identity of Buyer or Seller**, in which case **the CONTRACT will
control**."*

**Instructor Note, transcribed:** *"If a licensee is **not a REALTOR®, an attorney must prepare any
contract-related forms provided by the licensee to the parties if the content of the document will
affect the parties' legal rights.**"*

> **Required Activity — prescribed by the Commission:** *"Discuss the **advantages and disadvantages of
> allowing possession at a time other than Closing**. Be sure to address **insurance issues** and **what
> happens if the transaction does not close**. Remind brokers to **encourage their clients to consult an
> attorney** about risks/implications of possession before/after closing."*
>
#### B.5a Required Activity evidence — possession away from Closing

The activity is a risk-classification exercise, not permission to draft an occupancy agreement:

chunks.heading: C. Sales Contract Procedures *(Level 3)*
chunks.excerpt:
| Timing | Possible advantage | Risks that must be surfaced | If the sale never closes |
|---|---|---|---|
| buyer enters before the form-defined Closing | move or repair schedule may start earlier | buyer has possession before title; casualty, liability, property-condition, lender, utility and insurance responsibilities may not align | the buyer may have to leave and disputes may arise over damage, improvements, payment, personal property and restoration |
| seller remains after the form-defined Closing | seller gains moving time and buyer may preserve the transaction schedule | buyer owns while seller occupies; coverage, liability, keys/access, damage, utilities, payment/security and holdover must be addressed | this row applies only if title transferred; failure to surrender possession becomes a fact-specific legal enforcement issue |

For either row, the broker identifies the risks, confirms insurer and lender requirements, recommends
separate legal advice, and uses only the current authorized standard addendum or attorney-drafted
agreement. The broker does not promise that an ordinary homeowner policy covers the arrangement and
does not draft eviction, holdover, indemnity, repair or default language. The actual Forms 2A7-T and
2A8-T remain required-review artifacts.

**None of the eight syllabus-named addenda was obtained for this project and none is described.** The
current forms library also shows 2026 revisions and additional forms beyond that eight-item syllabus
list, so the filing review must reconcile the syllabus with the then-current library rather than assume
the list is exhaustive.

---

## C. Sales Contract Procedures *(Level 3)*

### C.1 Presenting an offer and delivering the executed instrument are separate duties

chunks.heading: C.2 Disclosure of an offer and its terms
chunks.excerpt:
- Present every offer promptly, including multiple and backup offers and an offer received while the
  property is under contract; do not rank, filter or hold it while negotiating compensation.
- **Rule 58A .0106(a) is an instrument-delivery rule:** each broker delivers a copy of the executed offer
  or other covered transaction document to that broker's own customer or client within three days after
  receipt. An oral summary does not satisfy delivery of the written instrument.
- Record receipt, presentation and document-delivery timestamps separately. “Present within three
  days” collapses two duties and is not the rule text.

### C.2 Disclosure of an offer and its terms

- Current Commission guidance says **the existence of multiple offers is not a material fact** and need
  not be volunteered. The listing broker follows the seller's direction about announcing their
  existence and communicates fairly, equally and honestly if authorized.
- **Rule 58A .0115 separately** prohibits sharing an offering party's **price or other material offer
  terms** with a competing party without the **express authority of the offering party**.
- Seller consent to announce multiple offers does not authorize disclosure of a competing buyer's
  price, due diligence fee, escalation language, closing date or another material term.

*(Module NC-10 B.5 states the same three rules. They appear in both sections of the Syllabus.)*

### C.3 Counteroffers and contract modifications

- **Retain ALL offers, even if rejected, amended, or replaced** — Rule 58A .0108.

### C.4 Rule .0106 delivery runs to the broker's customer or client

chunks.heading: D. NC Closing Procedures
chunks.excerpt:
The rule does not say that one broker must deliver a copy to every party in the transaction. Each
broker keeps evidence that the broker timely delivered the executed document to the customer or client
served by that broker and supplied the firm file as separately required by Rule .0108.

---

## D. NC Closing Procedures

### D.1 Settlement agent, closing lawyer and party choice

The syllabus describes the common pattern of a buyer-selected lawyer representing the buyer and lender
and performing limited work for the seller. Treat that as a pattern, not a universal agency rule.

- North Carolina State Bar Authorized Practice Advisory Opinion 2002-1 says a lawyer must provide the
  legal services in a residential closing; a nonlawyer may perform only identified ministerial tasks
  without legal judgment.
- The lawyer must be selected by the party receiving the legal services. A broker may recommend or,
  with actual authority, engage counsel, but should not silently choose counsel for a party.
- A lawyer may sometimes represent more than one party only after the lawyer performs the required
  conflict analysis and obtains the necessary consent. A broker does not decide that ethics question.
- G.S. 10B-134.25 confirms that a North Carolina lawyer supervises the residential real estate closing
  and performs the legal services that constitute practice of law.

**Provide information to the settlement agent as soon as possible** — the Syllabus lists eight items:

chunks.heading: D.2 The buyer's due diligence process
chunks.excerpt:
1. **A copy of the sales contract with all addenda and/or amendments.**
2. **Contact information for all parties.**
3. **Have the parties provide any required taxpayer-identification information directly to the
   settlement professional through the professional's secure channel; the broker should not collect or
   transmit it casually.**
4. **Contact information for the buyer's lender.**
5. **The seller's lender information for loan payoff.**
6. **A copy of any survey.**
7. **Copies of any required inspection reports.**
8. **The property insurance binder.**

### D.2 The buyer's due diligence process

**Buyer's loan** — as B.4 established: **not contingent on loan approval**, and **inability to secure
financing after the DDP is a buyer's breach.**

**Appraisal. Property survey.**

**Property insurance:**

- **The lender will usually require adequate homeowner insurance coverage in effect as of the day of
  closing.**
- **The lender makes the flood-hazard determination.** The federal mandatory-purchase rule focuses on a
  loan secured by an insurable **building or mobile home** located in a Special Flood Hazard Area; it is
  not correctly stated as an automatic requirement merely because any edge of the parcel crosses the
  map boundary. An elevation certificate may be relevant to rating or underwriting but is not a
  universal requirement for every mapped parcel.
- **Instructor Note, transcribed:** *"It is **extremely important** for the buyer and seller to have
  appropriate insurance coverage **when the closing is delayed, when the buyer will occupy the property
  before closing, or when the seller will occupy the property after closing.** Failure to have proper
  coverage in these situations may result in **the property being uninsured for some period of time**."*

chunks.heading: D.2 The buyer's due diligence process
chunks.excerpt:
**Property inspections.** **Instructor Note:** *"Buyer should be advised to perform their own inspections
**instead of only relying on the information in the Residential Property and Owners' Association
Disclosure Statement**."*

**Chapter 47E boundary:** for a covered transaction, the owner supplies the prescribed residential
property and owners'-association disclosures no later than the buyer's offer, subject to the statute's
coverage, exceptions and cancellation provisions. That owner-form process does not replace the
broker's independent duty under Rule .0114 and G.S. 93A-6 to disclose material facts the broker knows
or reasonably should know. The current Commission forms themselves remain required artifacts.

- **Wood-destroying insect (termite) inspection.**
- **Property inspection usually performed by qualified professionals** — **"as soon as possible to allow
  time for any needed repair negotiations to be completed prior to the end of the DDP."**
- **Physical inspection by the buyer and the agent working with the buyer.** **Instructor Note:** *"A
  broker working with a buyer is **expected to recognize 'red flag' situations and to assist the buyer in
  checking into such situations**."* Examples the Syllabus gives to investigate: **tenants; easements and
  encroachments; recent construction or renovations; violations of zoning or restrictive covenants** —
  and **"Buyer should obtain and read a copy of any subdivision covenants prior to physical
  inspection."**

**Onsite septic system:**

chunks.heading: D.3 Other pre-closing matters
chunks.excerpt:
- **Improved property** — **obtain a copy of the septic permit from the county health department, if
  possible.** **Instructor Note, transcribed:** *"**Broker cannot advertise more bedrooms than allowed by
  septic permit regardless of how many rooms are designed as bedrooms.**"*
- **Unimproved property** — **order a soil suitability test** to determine whether the property will
  support a septic system, **previously called a perc test**. **"Even lots within an approved subdivision
  should be evaluated."**

**The septic bedroom rule is a genuine advertising trap** and it is a North Carolina one: the permit
governs what may be advertised, not the floor plan.

**Other common inspections:** **radon; lead-based paint; asbestos; mould; well water.**

**Resolution of repair issues:**

- **Anything can be negotiated during the DDP.**
- **Repairs themselves do not have to be completed prior to the end of the DDP — only prior to
  Settlement.**
- **There are standard forms available to ratify repair agreements as part of the sales contract.**

**Review of covenants and homeowners' association documents** — **"especially important if the buyer is
planning to add improvements, enlarge existing structures, or use the property for business
purposes."**

**Other matters subject to government regulation:** **permitted property use; plans for adjacent
undeveloped property; public or private status of subdivision streets; school assignment.**

### D.3 Other pre-closing matters

chunks.heading: Required Activities in this section — all three must be completed
chunks.excerpt:
- **Title examination by an attorney, including a personal property lien search and a mechanic's lien
  inquiry.**
- **Clearing of title defects by the seller, if needed.**
- **The loan closing package provided to the settlement agent by the buyer's lender.**
- **Brokers perform an advance review of the settlement statement, if available.**
- **Under 12 C.F.R. § 1026.19(f), the creditor must ensure the consumer receives the Closing Disclosure
  at least three business days before consummation.** A settlement agent may provide it for the creditor,
  but the creditor remains responsible. Most later corrections do not restart the waiting period; an
  inaccurate APR, inaccurate loan-product information or an added prepayment penalty does.

**Broker control:** review transaction figures within the broker's competence, promptly route a
suspected error to the client and the professional responsible for the affected figure, and document
the correction. G.S. 93A-6(a)(14) directly disciplines failure to deliver a detailed and accurate
closing statement to the broker's own client; it does not make the broker the creditor, settlement
agent or closing lawyer.

---

## Required Activities in this section — all three must be completed

chunks.heading: Module NC-11 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Provide Form 2-T, the Guidelines, and the commonly used standard addenda to students, and conduct a
   detailed paragraph-by-paragraph review.** **← OUTSTANDING. Submission gate.**
2. **Scenarios exploring initial and additional EMD handling and escrow delivery timing**, applying
   Commission Rule 58A .0116(b)(3)–(4). **← DELIVERED at B.4; current form deadlines remain gated.**
3. **Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of possession at a time other than Closing**, addressing
   insurance and what happens if the transaction does not close. **← DELIVERED at B.5a; the current
   standard addenda remain gated.**

## Module NC-11 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module NC-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, under Commission Rule 58H .0207 as the Syllabus quotes it.

**No item in this module tests the text of Form 2-T or of any addendum**, because this project has not
read them. Items test the structural facts the syllabus states and the current-law corrections above —
the due diligence model, DDF versus EMD, source-specific Settlement/Closing vocabulary, Rule .0112's
current 18-item/compensation treatment, the addendum conflict exceptions, the split
presentation/delivery duties, the offer-disclosure rules, the closing-lawyer boundary, TRID and the
septic advertising rule.

---

Drawn from **Section XI** of the Commission's Prelicensing Course Syllabus, March 2024 Edition amended
May 2026, read on 2026-08-20. Every Instructor Note, Required Activity and structural statement above is
**transcribed from the Syllabus.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module NC-11
chunks.excerpt:
**Not obtained, and therefore reproduced, described or paraphrased NOWHERE in this build:** **NCAR/NCBA
Offer to Purchase and Contract Standard Form 2-T**; the **Guidelines for Completing the Offer to Purchase

chunks.heading: North Carolina Broker Prelicensing Course — Module NC-12
chunks.excerpt:
# North Carolina Broker Prelicensing Course — Module NC-12

## Section XII · Financing & Settlement

**Commission Syllabus section:** XII — Financing & Settlement
**Instructional Level:** **1** except as noted. *Assigned by the Commission; providers and instructors
are **REQUIRED to comply**.* Within this section the Commission raises specific subtopics to **Level 2**
— Sale of Mortgaged Property, the General Categories of Residential First Mortgage Loans, Fixed-Rate
Level-Payment loans, Mortgage Priorities, Residential Lending Practices under TRID, Truth-in-Lending,
and RESPA — and raises **The Settlement Statement (Part J) to Level 3**. It also drops named subtopics
back to Level 1 inside otherwise Level-2 blocks: *Purchase Subject to Seller's Existing Mortgage*, *other
FHA loan programs*, *USDA Rural Development*, and *Seller Financing*.
**Licence examination weight:** **National Exam Category — 7 items.**
**Instructional hours:** **7.0**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No North Carolina prelicensing credit is available.

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
> ### Instructional Levels, as the Commission defines them
>
> **Level 1 — Knowledge and comprehension.** The student can recall and restate.
> **Level 2 — Application.** The student can use the concept in a situation.
> **Level 3 — Analysis and evaluation.** The student can break a problem apart and judge it.
>
> Most of this section is **Level 1**: the student must *know* the vocabulary of finance. The Commission
> lifts only the parts a broker actually operates — how a sale of mortgaged property is handled, which
> loan category fits which buyer, where a mortgage sits in priority, what TRID and RESPA require of the
> timeline — to **Level 2**. It lifts the **settlement statement to Level 3**, and explains why in its own
> note, transcribed below.

## Learning objectives

1. Define the basic finance vocabulary the Commission lists, including the two meanings of a discount point.
2. Distinguish a mortgage from a deed of trust, and state which North Carolina uses.
3. State the foreclosure methods and distinguish North Carolina's 10-day **upset-bid** window from a
   post-sale statutory right of redemption.
4. **Handle a sale of mortgaged property — cash sale, assumption, subject-to, and short sale.** *(Level 2)*
5. **Distinguish conventional, FHA, VA and USDA loans by their defining features.** *(Level 2)*
6. Classify loans by repayment term and by purpose.
7. **Apply mortgage priority, recordation and subordination.** *(Level 2)*
8. Describe the Fed's role, the primary market and the secondary market.
9. **Work a borrower and property analysis under the qualifying ratios the Commission lists.** *(Level 2)*
10. **State what TILA/Regulation Z and RESPA require, and the timing rules a broker must know.** *(Level 2)*
11. **Analyse a settlement statement entry — debit or cr

chunks.heading: A. Basic finance concepts, terminology and calculations
chunks.excerpt:
edit, which party, and the proration.** *(Level 3)*

---

## A. Basic finance concepts, terminology and calculations

### A.1 Basic concepts and terminology

The Commission lists these by name: **principal and interest; amortization; debt service; PITI; equity;
usury; discount points; yield; loan value; loan-to-value ratio.**

On **discount points** the Syllabus states two figures itself, and both are examinable in the
Commission's calculation model:

> **1 point = 1% of the mortgage loan amount for the borrower**
> **1 point = 1/8 % yield for the investor**

Read them together, but do not turn the second line into a market promise. **One point is exactly one
percent of the loan amount as a charge.** The one-eighth-percent yield relationship is the Syllabus's
expressly assigned **rule of thumb** for examination calculations; actual pricing and investor yield
depend on rate, term, prepayment and market conditions. Use the shortcut only when the question or
Syllabus model calls for it.

**PITI** is the four-part housing payment — principal, interest, taxes, insurance. It matters later, in
qualifying: the ratios in Part G are computed on the *housing expense*, which is PITI, not on principal
and interest alone.

**Equity** is the difference between what the property is worth and what is owed against it. **Loan
value** is the figure the loan is computed on, and the Commission's own note in Part G settles how it is
chosen: *"Loan value will be calculated on the contract sales price or the appraised value, whichever is
lower."* **Loan-to-value ratio** is loan value over that figure.

**Usury** is charging interest above the lawful maximum. **Debt service** is the periodic payment
required to service the debt.

### A.2 Mortgages and deeds of trust

chunks.heading: A.2.b The mortgage note
chunks.excerpt:
**Basic terminology the Commission lists:** mortgage; promissory note (mortgage note); deed of trust;
hypothecation; lien theory; title theory; default; foreclosure.

**Hypothecation** is the concept that ties the whole section together: the borrower pledges the property
as security *while keeping possession of it*. Nothing about a mortgage loan moves the borrower out.

#### A.2.b The mortgage note

The Commission notes:

> **"A promissory note is a form of contract."**

That is not filler. Everything Module NC-09 taught about contract validity applies to the note. The
Syllabus asks for the **essential elements of a valid note**, and then three **special note provisions**:

- **Acceleration clause** — on default the whole balance becomes due at once, not just the missed payment.
- **Prepayment penalty clause** — a charge for paying the loan off early.
- **Due-on-sale clause (alienation clause)** — the balance becomes due if the property is sold.

Also examinable: **negotiable note vs. nonnegotiable note**, and the Commission's aside that **some
states use a bond in lieu of a promissory note.**

The due-on-sale clause is the reason Part A.3 exists in the form it does. Hold it.

#### A.2.c The mortgage (or deed of trust) instrument

Here the Commission writes a note that is unusually pointed, transcribed in full:

> *"The term **mortgage** is commonly used incorrectly to refer to the actual loan vs. the legal
> instrument that pledges the property for the loan (e.g., 'I am going to get a mortgage' vs. 'I am going
> to give a deed of trust to get a mortgage loan'). **Brokers are expected to know the difference and the
> technical difference between a mortgage and a deed of trust.**"*

chunks.heading: A.2.d Rights
chunks.excerpt:
The Commission's own classroom comparison follows. It is a useful taxonomy, not a substitute for the
security instrument and the governing foreclosure statute:

| | **Mortgage** | **Deed of trust** — *"Commonly used in NC"* |
|---|---|---|
| Parties | **2** | **3** |
| Who they are | Mortgagor, Mortgagee | Grantor/trustor, Trustee, Beneficiary |
| Theory | **Lien theory** | **Title theory** |
| Foreclosure | **Judicial** | **Power of sale (non-judicial)** |

Two columns, four rows, and the practical consequence sits in the last row. Because North Carolina
commonly uses the **deed of trust**, a power-of-sale foreclosure is common. The authority is not created
merely by adding a third party: it comes from an express power of sale in the instrument and the
procedures in **G.S. Chapter 45, Article 2A**. A trustee or mortgagee exercising that power must follow
the statute; judicial foreclosure remains a distinct court process.

The Commission adds: **"A mortgage or deed of trust is a form of contract."** It asks for the
**essential elements** and the **obligations of the borrower and the lender.**

**Signature of spouse.** The Commission's note, transcribed:

> *"If husband and wife are buying as tenants by the entirety (joint tenants in many other states) and
> **only one spouse signs the mortgage note, both spouses must still sign the mortgage or deed of
> trust**."*

The two documents do different things and are signed by different people. The **note** is the promise to
repay — one spouse can make it alone. The **deed of trust** pledges the property — and a tenancy by the
entirety cannot be pledged by half of it. Module NC-06 established that North Carolina recognises
tenancy by the entirety; this is one of the places it bites.

#### A.2.d Rights

chunks.heading: Current-law reconciliation: upset bids, not statutory redemption
chunks.excerpt:
**Rights of borrowers**, as listed: **right to possession and use; right of defeasance; right (equity)
of redemption.**

**Rights of mortgage lenders:** the **right to transfer (assign) the mortgage**, and the **right to
foreclose.**

**Foreclosure methods:** **judicial; power of sale (nonjudicial); strict.**

**Foreclosure procedures**, as the Commission lists them:

- **Proper notice of foreclosure**
- **Foreclosure sale at public auction**
- **A 10-day period after the reported sale or latest upset bid**
- **Disbursement of sale proceeds**
- **A creditor may pursue a deficiency only where the obligation and governing law permit it**

And a North Carolina limit, transcribed:

> *"In NC, **seller financing is prohibited from using deficiency judgments** to recover deficit."*

### Current-law reconciliation: upset bids, not statutory redemption

The current statute corrects the first label. **G.S. 45-21.27** creates a 10-day window in which another
person may file a qualifying **upset bid** after the report of sale or latest notice of upset bid; every
new upset bid starts another 10-day window. Under **G.S. 45-21.29A**, if no timely upset bid is filed,
the parties' rights become fixed without a separate confirmation order. The North Carolina Judicial
Branch describes the same process as an upset-bid period. Those sources do **not** call it a 10-day
statutory redemption period, so the stale Syllabus label must not be taught as current law.

chunks.heading: A.3 Sale of mortgaged property *(Level 2 except as noted)*
chunks.excerpt:
The deficiency shortcut also needs precision. **G.S. 45-21.38** bars a deficiency on a qualifying
seller purchase-money obligation when the evidence of debt shows on its face that it is for the balance
of the real-estate purchase price. **G.S. 45-21.38A** separately bars deficiencies for defined
nontraditional and rate-spread home loans secured by an occupied principal dwelling, subject to its
definitions and exclusions. Where **G.S. 45-21.36** applies after a creditor buys at a power-of-sale
foreclosure, the borrower may prove fair value as a defense or offset. None of that means every
unsatisfied creditor simply "appeals" for a deficiency. A live foreclosure or deficiency question goes
to North Carolina counsel.

### A.3 Sale of mortgaged property *(Level 2 except as noted)*

The Commission opens with a note that frames the whole part:

> *"**Assumptions of mortgages and purchases subject to a mortgage occur very infrequently** because of
> **due on sale clauses** in most modern mortgages."*

That is why the due-on-sale clause was flagged in A.2.b. The clause is what killed assumption as a
routine practice.

Four ways the Commission lists:

**a. Cash sale.** *"Most common in residential transactions."* And the point students most often miss,
in the Commission's own words: *"Includes transactions where buyer obtains a new mortgage loan."* From
the seller's side the transaction is cash — the seller's loan is paid off and the seller is out. That
the buyer borrowed to get the cash does not change the category.

**b. Sale with assumption of seller's existing mortgage.** The buyer takes on the seller's loan.

chunks.heading: B. General categories of residential first mortgage loans *(Level 2 except as noted)*
chunks.excerpt:
**c. Purchase subject to seller's existing mortgage.** *(Level 1 — this subtopic.)* The Commission drops
this one back to Level 1: know what it is, do not be asked to work it.

**d. Short sale.** The Commission asks for a **basic overview of procedure** and then the **broker's
role**, which it states in three parts:

> - *"Existence of a possible short sale situation **is a material fact**"*
> - *"**Listing agent** should attempt to identify potential prior to listing and advise seller-client
>   about the process"*
> - *"**Buyer agent** should advise buyer client about the process and use appropriate contract addenda
>   when making an offer; **buyer agent is not expected to discover** possibility of a short sale"*

Two different standards for two different roles, and the difference is deliberate. The **listing agent
must look** — the seller's loan balance is the listing agent's business. The **buyer agent need not
discover** it, but must advise the client once it appears.

And a boundary, transcribed:

> *"**Broker cannot negotiate a 'workout agreement' with the lender on the borrower's behalf** because
> it would be **unauthorized practice of law**."*

Module NC-09 established the drafting prohibition. This is the same principle reaching into finance: the
line is not what the broker knows, it is what the broker *does on someone else's behalf*.

That the possibility of a short sale is a **material fact** places it alongside the items in Module
NC-10. Material facts are disclosed. This one is a material fact about the *transaction*, not about the
property.

---

## B. General categories of residential first mortgage loans *(Level 2 except as noted)*

### B.1 Conventional

The Commission's note:

chunks.heading: B.2 FHA-insured
chunks.excerpt:
> *"Conventional loans are typically seen as **the most secure loans for lenders** because they usually
> have **the lowest loan-to-value ratio**."*

Under it: **conforming vs. nonconforming**; **private mortgage insurance (PMI)**; **home equity loan and
home equity line of credit (HELOC).**

Conforming means the loan meets the purchase standards of the secondary market entities in Part F.
Nonconforming does not, which is why a nonconforming loan is priced differently — the lender may have to
keep it.

### B.2 FHA-insured

- Administered by the **Federal Housing Administration (FHA)**, part of **HUD**.
- **"FHA does not build housing or lend money for housing purchases."**
- **"FHA insures FHA-approved lenders against loss if borrowers default; similar to PMI."**

The **Title II, Section 203(b) Program** is *"the most widely used FHA program."* It applies to
**residential 1–4 unit property loans, including manufactured housing.** Its general characteristics, as
listed:

- **Fixed-rate loans with up to 30-year terms** made by lenders under FHA guidelines
- **FHA provides mortgage insurance**
- **Mortgage insurance premium (MIP)**
- **Owner (borrower) occupancy required**
- **Maximum loan amount**
- **Interest rates set by lender, not FHA**
- **Appraisal**
- **No prepayment penalty**
- **Assumability**
- **Original borrower may remain secondarily liable for repayment of an assumed loan**

*Other FHA programs* — senior borrowers, rehabilitation, condominium purchases, graduated payment
mortgages, adjustable rate mortgages — are **Level 1**, and the Commission's note limits the demand
exactly: **"It is only necessary to be aware that other FHA programs exist."**

chunks.heading: B.3 VA-guaranteed
chunks.excerpt:
**Current-program boundary.** FHA insures loans made by approved lenders; it does not make the ordinary
Section 203(b) purchase loan. Eligibility, mortgage-insurance treatment, property standards and the
applicable loan limit depend on the current version of HUD Handbook 4000.1, the property and the lender's
underwriting. The list above is the Commission's exam taxonomy, not a promise that a borrower qualifies.

### B.3 VA-guaranteed

- Administered by the **U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).**
- **"VA does not build housing and only directly funds loans for housing for Native American veterans
  living on Federal trust land."**
- **"VA guarantees (or backs) VA-approved lenders against loss if borrowers default."**

Applies generally to **residential 1–4 unit property loans under VA guidelines, including manufactured
housing**, and requires a **VA Certificate of Eligibility.**

General characteristics, as listed:

- **"Most significant feature — possibility of no down payment"**
- **Owner (borrower) occupancy required**
- **Property must meet VA property condition standards**
- **"No maximum VA-guaranteed loan amount"**
- **Qualifying requirements**
- **Lender sets interest rate, not the VA**
- **Funding fee**
- **Certificate of reasonable value (CRV)**
- **No prepayment penalty**
- **Assumption is possible for an approved, creditworthy transferee, subject to the governing VA and
  loan-servicer process**

The Syllabus prints this warning:

> *"**A VA release of liability does not release the original borrower from liability to the lender**;
> lender must provide a **separate release** for original borrower to be fully absolved of all
> responsibility for an assumed VA loan."*

chunks.heading: B.4 USDA Rural Development *(Level 1 — this subtopic)*
chunks.excerpt:
**Current-program correction.** Do not teach that quoted sentence as a universal current rule. For a VA
loan committed on or after **March 1, 1988**, the transferee must obtain the holder's or VA's prior
approval and the veteran must obtain the required release from liability before closing. Current VA
servicing guidance says approval, with exceptions, releases the veteran from future liability to VA; the
governing regulation separately says the holder may also release the veteran from liability on the loan
when the stated conditions are met. Older loans and special approvals follow different rules. A release
from personal liability is also different from restoration of the veteran's entitlement. The servicer
and VA must resolve every applicable release and the entitlement issue before a veteran relies on them.

Notice also what is *the same* in FHA and VA and worth learning as a pair: **the lender sets the interest
rate, not the agency**; **no prepayment penalty**; and the programs generally require intended occupancy
for the original purchase borrower. Both permit assumptions only under their current program rules. FHA
**insures**; VA **guarantees**; FHA charges **MIP** and VA generally charges a **funding fee** unless an
exemption applies. VA's statement that a veteran with full entitlement has no county loan limit does not
mean unlimited borrowing: the lender still underwrites the borrower and the property, and the guaranty
calculation still matters.

### B.4 USDA Rural Development *(Level 1 — this subtopic)*

chunks.heading: B.5 Seller financing *(Level 1 — this subtopic)*
chunks.excerpt:
Operated through the **Rural Housing Service of the U.S. Department of Agriculture**, providing **both
direct and guaranteed single-family housing loans.** Keep the two programs separate. The **Section 502
Direct** program may offer payment assistance, ordinarily uses a 33-year term and may use 38 years for a
very-low-income applicant who cannot afford a 33-year term; no down payment is typically required. The
**guaranteed** program is a lender-originated program with its own current handbook, term, income,
property and underwriting rules. The Syllabus's combined list — **33–38 years, 100% financing/no down
payment, subsidized interest rates and qualifying requirements** — must not be read as if every feature
applies identically to both programs.

The Commission directs: *"Contact the NC state office at https://www.rd.usda.gov/nc to obtain loan and
area office information."* Current income limits, eligible areas and lender/program terms must be checked
on the USDA site for the specific applicant and property; none is inferred from this overview.

### B.5 Seller financing *(Level 1 — this subtopic)*

Two instruments named: **purchase money mortgage**, and **land contract / contract for deed.**

Carry forward from A.2.d: **in North Carolina seller financing is prohibited from using deficiency
judgments to recover a deficit.**

---

## C. Types of mortgage loans

### C.1 By repayment terms

**a. Fixed rate — level payment mortgage (fully amortized)** *(Level 2 — this subtopic)*. The Commission
calls it *"the most commonly used residential loan repayment plan"* and asks for **amortization** under it.

chunks.heading: C.2 By purpose or special feature
chunks.excerpt:
**b. Adjustable rate mortgage (ARM).** **Cap rates** — **periodic (or anniversary) cap**, **lifetime (or
aggregate) cap**, **index**. Then **payment cap**, with the consequence the Commission states: it
**"may result in negative amortization."**

That is the concept to hold: a cap on the *payment* is not a cap on the *interest*. If the payment is
held below the interest accruing, the shortfall is added to principal and the balance grows. A rate cap
limits what is charged; a payment cap only limits what is collected.

**c. Graduated payment mortgage (GPM).**

**d. Term mortgage (interest only or straight mortgage).** *"Term period is usually very short (e.g.,
3–5 years) and may be renewable."* *"Frequently used for construction loans or junior mortgages."*

**e. Growing equity mortgage (GEM).**

**f. Buydown mortgage.** *"Interest rate is temporarily or permanently reduced ('bought down')."* *"A
lump sum (usually stated as points) is paid at closing to the lender to offset reduced payments; **may be
paid by buyer, seller, or third party**."*

**g. Balloon mortgage (partially amortized).**

### C.2 By purpose or special feature

**Construction**; **open end** — *"repaid and reused without additional closing costs,"* *"acts as a line
of credit or equity line"*; **blanket**; **package**; **bridge.**

### C.3 Mortgage priorities *(Level 2 — this subtopic)*

- **Types by priority:** **first (or senior)**; **second, third, etc. (junior).**
- **"Effect and importance of recordation of mortgages (deeds of trust) AND the cancellation or release
  of a mortgage/deed of trust."**
- **Subordination of mortgages.**

chunks.heading: D. U.S. monetary policy
chunks.excerpt:
Recordation sets priority; that is Module NC-05's recording principle applied to liens rather than to
title. **Subordination** is the deliberate exception — a lender agreeing to sit behind a lender who would
otherwise sit behind it. And the Commission's emphasis on **cancellation or release** connects to Module
NC-11: a paid-off deed of trust that was never cancelled of record is still a cloud, which is why the
Syllabus flagged that seller liens are sometimes cancelled 30–60 days post-closing.

---

## D. U.S. monetary policy

Three items: the **role of the Federal Reserve (the Fed)**; its **effect on mortgage interest rates**;
its **effect on the availability of mortgage funds.**

## E. The primary mortgage market

**Purpose**, and the **sources of mortgage loans** the Commission lists: **direct lenders (banks, savings
associations, credit unions, etc.); mortgage banking companies; mortgage brokers; others.**

## F. The secondary mortgage market

**General concepts and operation:** **purpose; loan pooling; mortgage-backed securities.**

**The secondary-market participants named by the Commission:**

- **Federal National Mortgage Association (FNMA — Fannie Mae)**
- **Government National Mortgage Association (GNMA — Ginnie Mae)**
- **Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (FHLMC — Freddie Mac)**

**Current classification correction.** Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are the two housing government-
sponsored enterprises regulated by FHFA. **Ginnie Mae is not a GSE**; it is a wholly owned U.S.
government corporation within HUD that guarantees eligible mortgage-backed securities. All three
support mortgage liquidity, but they do so under different legal structures.

chunks.heading: G. Residential lending practices and procedures in transactions subject to TRID *(Level 2)*
chunks.excerpt:
The primary market is where a loan is *made*. The secondary market is where a loan already made is
*bought*. The link between them is conforming standards from B.1: a lender writes to those standards
precisely so the loan can be sold, and selling it returns capital to lend again.

---

## G. Residential lending practices and procedures in transactions subject to TRID *(Level 2)*

### G.1 Loan application procedures

**Information typically required**, in three groups: **borrower's personal information** (employment,
earnings, assets, outstanding financial obligations); **property information** (legal description,
improvements, title, survey, taxes); **loan information** (purpose, proposed amount, repayment terms,
interest rate).

Then: **lender's loan estimate (LE)**; **rate lock**; and **"lender denial must be in writing."**

### G.2 Loan underwriting practices

**a. Borrower analysis (qualifying a buyer/borrower).** The Commission's note:

> *"**Brokers are encouraged to prequalify prospective buyers early** in the home buying process to
> minimize wasting time and energy on showing and writing offers on properties that cannot be afforded by
> the buyer."*

Factors listed: **credit history and credit score; adequacy of assets to close the transaction; stability
of income; types of acceptable income; occupancy of the property; adequacy of income.**

The ratios, exactly as the Commission states them:

| Loan type | Housing expense to gross income | Recurring debt to gross income |
|---|---|---|
| **Conventional** | **28%** | **36%** |
| **FHA** | **31%** | **43%** |
| **VA** | *considers several factors including an analysis of the borrower's **residual income*** | **43% maximum**; *"exceptions are possible"* |

And the rule that governs their use, transcribed:

chunks.heading: G.2 Loan underwriting practices
chunks.excerpt:
> **"A buyer must qualify on both the income and the debt ratios."**

Both, not either, **inside a Syllabus calculation problem that gives or invokes these ratios**. A buyer
who passes the housing ratio and fails the debt ratio fails that classroom model. The percentages are
the Commission's exam figures, not universal live underwriting limits. A real lender applies the current
program guide, automated-underwriting findings, residual-income or compensating-factor rules and its own
lawful overlays. A broker may calculate an estimate but may not tell a consumer that these figures alone
approve or deny the loan.

**b. Property analysis.** **Title opinion and title insurance**; and an independent appraisal or other
permitted valuation. The Syllabus says **"appraisal assigned randomly through an appraisal management
company."** Treat that as one possible workflow, not a universal legal requirement. Current Regulation Z
requires valuation independence and prohibits coercion, bribery and material misrepresentation; it does
not require every creditor to use an AMC or random assignment. The Commission's note:

> **"Loan value will be calculated on the contract sales price or the appraised value, whichever is lower."**

That single sentence is the reason an appraisal below contract price is a problem, and — carried back to
Module NC-11 — the reason it is a problem *for the buyer* in North Carolina, where **there is no appraisal
contingency in the standard contract.**

**c. Loan analysis.** **Yield (interest rate and discount points); loan term; loan-to-value ratio;
mortgage insurance.**

chunks.heading: H. Federal financing legislation
chunks.excerpt:
**d. Loan commitment and closing.** **Lender's letter of commitment**; **"loan principal disbursed at
settlement; 'loan closing'."** For a North Carolina purchase, do not equate signing with recordation or
authorized disbursement. Chapter 45A governs receipt of required funds and documents, recordation and the
conditions for disbursement; the closing attorney or settlement agent confirms the live status.

---

## H. Federal financing legislation

The Commission's framing note, transcribed:

> *"Pursuant to the **Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act**, the **Consumer
> Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB)** was assigned the consumer protection responsibilities of **seven
> (7) different federal agencies** (including the Federal Reserve Board, HUD and the FTC). The CFPB is
> responsible for promulgating rules for the **Truth-in-Lending Act, RESPA, the Fair Credit Reporting
> Act, and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act.** One express mandate of the Dodd-Frank Act was that the
> CFPB **consolidate the duplicate lender disclosures under TILA and RESPA, yielding the TRID rules
> (TILA/RESPA Integrated Disclosures)**."*

That paragraph explains why one form now does two statutes' work.

### H.1 Truth-in-Lending *(Level 2 — this subtopic)*

**TILA** is a compilation of the initial Act, the **Truth in Lending Simplification and Reform Act
(TILSRA)** and the **Disclosure Improvement Act**; its rules are known as **Regulation Z**; it is
**administered by the CFPB.**

chunks.heading: H.2 and H.3 Fair Credit Reporting Act and ECOA
chunks.excerpt:
**Applicability.** Regulation Z applies to consumer credit offered or extended regularly when the credit
is subject to a finance charge or is payable by written agreement in more than four installments, subject
to the regulation's definitions, thresholds and exemptions. Advertising provisions can reach anyone who
advertises covered credit, including a broker who repeats credit terms.

**Disclosure of credit information to borrowers:** the **loan estimate (LE)**; **delivery of preliminary
and final LE**; and *"significant change will probably require a new LE and a possible closing delay."*

**The four chief disclosures:**

1. **Annual percentage rate (APR)** — and the Commission's note: **"It is not the interest rate."**
2. **Finance charges**
3. **Amount financed**
4. **Total amount of all payments**

The APR note is there because the confusion is universal. The APR folds the cost of credit — points and
certain fees — into a single annualised rate, so it is normally higher than the note rate. Two loans at
the same interest rate can carry different APRs, and that is the whole point of requiring it.

**Advertising.** The Commission states: *"Regulation Z governs **any** advertisement for consumer credit,
**regardless of who places the ad**."* Then **trigger terms**, and the disclosures required for any ad
that includes one:

- **The amount or percentage of down payment**
- **Terms of loan repayment**
- **APR**

And the practical instruction, transcribed:

> *"**Brokers may avoid Regulation Z issues by not including any numbers in their advertising, other than
> the list or lease price.**"*

### H.2 and H.3 Fair Credit Reporting Act and ECOA

The Syllabus reverses the two implementing-regulation labels. The current pairing is:

chunks.heading: I. Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA) *(Level 2)*
chunks.excerpt:
- **Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) → Regulation B, 12 C.F.R. part 1002.** Regulation B bars a
  creditor from discriminating in any aspect of a credit transaction on the prohibited bases stated in
  the rule, and § 1002.9 governs notice of action taken and specific reasons for adverse action.
- **Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) → Regulation V, 12 C.F.R. part 1022.** Regulation V implements
  specified FCRA duties involving consumer-report information.

The ECOA/Regulation B list is not identical to the Fair Housing Act list taught in Module NC-09. Keep
housing discrimination and credit discrimination analytically separate, even when one transaction may
implicate both.

---

## I. Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA) *(Level 2)*

**Applicability**, as stated:

> *"**All mortgage loans for 1-4 family dwelling** (including manufactured housing) involving a
> **federally related mortgage loan made by institutional lenders.**"*
> *"**Does not apply to loans for commercial, business, or agricultural purposes.**"*

**Enforced by the CFPB and implemented by rules referred to as Regulation X.**

**Major requirements and consumer protections:**

chunks.heading: I. Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA) *(Level 2)*
chunks.excerpt:
- **Special information booklet.**
- **Loan Estimate (LE)** — for a covered transaction, the creditor generally must deliver or place it in
  the mail no later than the third business day after application. Before the consumer receives the LE
  and indicates an intent to proceed, the creditor or other person generally may not impose a fee other
  than a bona fide and reasonable credit-report fee.
- **Lender credits.** The Syllabus's older "yield spread premium" shorthand is not a permission to pay
  for referrals. A lender credit shown on the LE or CD is part of the disclosed pricing; it does not
  override RESPA's anti-kickback rule or loan-originator-compensation restrictions.
- **Closing Disclosure (CD).** The **creditor is responsible** for ensuring the consumer receives the CD
  on time and with the required content. A settlement agent may provide it, but using an agent does not
  transfer the creditor's legal responsibility.
- **The kickback prohibition**, transcribed:

> *"RESPA **prohibits the payment of a kickback or referral fee to any settlement service provider for
> referring consumers**."*
>
> *"Real estate agents may **neither pay nor accept any referral fee from a settlement service provider**,
> such as an appraiser, home inspector, attorney, etc. **Real estate brokers are only permitted to pay and
> receive referral fees from each other.** The law/rules also regulate **controlled or affiliated business
> arrangements (CBA)** that provide real estate services (e.g., brokerage, mortgage loan, legal services,
> home inspections, etc.) under a one-stop shopping approach."*

chunks.heading: I.5 The Loan Estimate
chunks.excerpt:
That shorthand also needs a boundary. Regulation X contains an exception for cooperative brokerage and
referral arrangements **between real estate agents and brokers**, but it does not legalize a payment for
referring a consumer to a lender, attorney, appraiser, inspector or other settlement-service provider.
Compensation must be for actual services performed or fit a stated exception; a label cannot convert a
referral payment into lawful compensation. An affiliated-business arrangement has disclosure, no-
required-use and return-on-ownership conditions under § 1024.15; it is not a blanket exemption.

- **Regulates reserve (impound or escrow) accounts.**
- **Loan servicing information.**

### I.5 The Loan Estimate

*"A federal form with details of proposed mortgage terms including written estimate of settlement charges
the borrower will incur."*

**Tolerance limits for changes to settlement charges** — the Commission lists **three categories**:
**no tolerance**, **10% tolerance**, **unlimited tolerance**. *"Lender must credit borrower for excess
charges over the permissible limits."* Use Regulation Z's actual category and changed-circumstance rules
for a live file. A revised LE is not available merely because a cost increased.

The timing rules must be kept separate:

chunks.heading: I.6 The Borrower Closing Disclosure
chunks.excerpt:
- initial LE: deliver or mail no later than the third business day after application;
- before consummation: the consumer must receive the initial LE no later than seven business days before
  consummation;
- revised LE: when permitted, provide it within three business days after receiving enough information
  to establish the reason for revision, and ensure receipt no later than four business days before
  consummation; a creditor may not provide a revised LE on or after the CD is provided; and
- **a revised LE does not itself start a new three-business-day waiting period.**

### I.6 The Borrower Closing Disclosure

*"Written detailed statement of final loan terms, prorations, and closing costs that borrower should
compare to information on the sales contract and the LE."* It **includes tolerance limits and the four
chief disclosures required by TILA.** The Commission asks for **delivery requirements** and for
**"changes that require a new BCD and a new 3 business day waiting period before settlement."**

The creditor must ensure that the consumer receives the CD no later than three business days before
consummation. Only three post-disclosure changes restart that waiting period: the disclosed APR becomes
inaccurate beyond the applicable tolerance, the loan product changes, or a prepayment penalty is added.
Other changes may require a corrected CD, but do not automatically restart the wait.

**I.7 Penalties.**

chunks.heading: J. The settlement statement *(Level 3 — this subtopic)*
chunks.excerpt:
**Instructor note on timing.** Regulation Z § 1026.19 is now the authority for the timing summary above.
Do not collapse the initial three-business-day LE deadline, the seven-business-day pre-consummation
minimum, the revised-LE delivery limits and the three-business-day CD waiting period into one rule. A
broker facing a live deadline confirms receipt dates and changes with the creditor and closing attorney.

---

## J. The settlement statement *(Level 3 — this subtopic)*

The Commission explains the Level 3 assignment itself, and it is the clearest statement of purpose in the
Syllabus:

> *"Because a broker will **not normally be tasked with the preparation** of the actual settlement
> statement for closing, **a license candidate will not be expected to complete a settlement statement
> problem on the license examination.** However, **a broker cannot properly review a statement for
> accuracy without a thorough understanding of each party's responsibilities under the contract terms and
> the calculation of each entry.** A license candidate **will be expected to perform some calculations for
> individual entries and to know how the calculations will appear on the settlement statement** (e.g.,
> debits and credits)."*

Read that carefully, because it defines the examination boundary exactly. **Not** a whole statement.
**Yes** individual entries, and **yes** whether each lands as a debit or a credit and to whom.

### J.1 Basic settlement statement concepts

**Settlement statement. Debit. Credit. Prorations.**

**Prorations.** The Commission's note: **"Students should be able to calculate prorations using both
methods listed below."**

chunks.heading: Required Activities in this section — all four must be completed
chunks.excerpt:
- **365-Day Year Method** — *"Most commonly used method in practice."*
- **360-Day Year / 30-Day Month Method** — ***"Method used on Prelicensing course end-of-course
  examination and real estate license examination."***

Both must be taught. One is what you will use in practice; the other is what you will be tested on. That
is the Commission's own division and it is stated in its own words above.

Two further rules:

> *"License exam proration problems **will specify which party is responsible for ('owns') the date of
> settlement**; **in NC, the seller 'owns' the date of settlement**."*
>
> *"**Always a double entry on the settlement statement.**"*

The double-entry rule is the checking mechanism. A prorated item that appears once has been done wrong:
if the seller is credited, someone is debited the same amount.

**Items commonly prorated**, as listed:

- **Real estate taxes**
  - **When taxes have not been paid prior to settlement** — closing before or after the statutory due date
  - **When taxes have been paid prior to settlement**
- **Homeowners' association dues**
- **Rents (on rented properties being sold)**

*Current-law correction.* The Syllabus's August date is not current law. Under **G.S. 105-360**, North
Carolina property taxes are due **September 1** of the tax year, may be paid at face amount before
**January 6**, and accrue statutory interest on or after January 6. A settlement proration is still
computed from the contract, the actual tax bill and the chosen day-count convention; the statutory due
date does not decide which party owns the settlement date. The exercises here use the given figures and
the Commission's 360-day/30-day examination convention.

---

## Required Activities in this section — all four must be completed

chunks.heading: Required Activities in this section — all four must be completed
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Integrate mathematical calculations related to mortgage finance into the teaching of the essential
   concepts and terminology** — the Commission names *"simple lifetime interest, monthly principal and
   interest payment, mortgage debt reduction, loan origination fees, discount points, loan-to-value
   ratios, and yield,"* and directs: *"Refer to Section XVI. Real Estate Math Calculations for descriptions
   of the required calculations."* **Delivered here and carried in Module NC-16.**

   *(Source note: this Required Activity is printed at the Section XI / Section XII page boundary in the
   Syllabus. It is placed here because every calculation it names is mortgage finance, which is this
   section's subject.)*

2. **Review a completed sample LE form to teach this topic. — DELIVERED.** The retained CFPB fixed-rate
   purchase sample is at `regulatory/captures/2026-09-07/module-12-forms/cfpb-loan-estimate-fixed-rate-sample.pdf`.
   Use the completed form pages after the CFPB cover page: page 1 for loan terms, projected payments and
   costs at closing; page 2 for loan costs, other costs and calculating cash to close; page 3 for the
   comparison table, other considerations and contacts. Have the student identify the note rate and APR,
   rate-lock status, estimated closing costs, cash to close and whether taxes/insurance are escrowed.

chunks.heading: Module NC-12 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
3. **Review a completed sample CD form to teach this topic. — DELIVERED.** The retained CFPB fixed-rate
   purchase sample is at `regulatory/captures/2026-09-07/module-12-forms/cfpb-closing-disclosure-fixed-rate-sample.pdf`.
   Review completed form pages 1–5: final loan terms and projected payments; closing-cost detail and
   paid-by columns; calculating cash to close and transaction summaries; additional loan/escrow
   disclosures; and loan calculations, contact information and confirmation of receipt. Compare it to the
   LE as an estimate-to-final exercise; do not infer a tolerance violation without the file's changed-
   circumstance and provider-selection facts.

4. **Show examples of both a HUD-1 and an ALTA settlement statement. — DELIVERED.** The CFPB historical
   comparison PDF at `regulatory/captures/2026-09-07/module-12-forms/cfpb-final-til-hud1-comparison.pdf`
   contains the completed HUD-1 on pages 3–5. Use page 3 for the borrower/seller summaries, page 4 for
   settlement-charge line groups, and page 5 for the comparison and loan terms. The blank ALTA Combined
   Settlement Statement at `regulatory/captures/2026-09-07/module-12-forms/alta-settlement-statement-combined.pdf`
   shows seller debit/credit and buyer debit/credit columns across its three pages. Explain that the HUD-1
   is a historical/non-TRID teaching form and that an ALTA statement may supplement transaction
   accounting; neither replaces the required CD for a covered current consumer mortgage.

**All four Section XII Required Activities are now delivered.** The four retained PDFs, extracted text,
SHA-256 hashes and page-by-page visual-review record are held together in the dated capture directory.

## Module NC-12 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module NC-12
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items, delivered as in Module NC-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, under Commission Rule 58H .0207 as the Syllabus quotes it.

Items in this module test the finance vocabulary at Level 1, the loan categories and the qualifying
ratios at Level 2, and individual settlement statement entries — debit or credit, and to which party — at
Level 3, which is the boundary Part J's note draws. **No item asks the student to complete a settlement
statement**, because the Commission states the licence examination will not.

---
