chunks.heading: Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-03
chunks.excerpt:
# Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-03

## Hours 12–18 · Law of agency — and why Oklahoma does not have one

**Commission area of study covered:** 605:10-3-1(a)(1)(V) Law of Agency
**Clock hours:** 7 — the largest single allocation in this course · **Hour allocation:** a StateCourse
proposal for Commission review; 605:10-3-1(a)(1) allocates no hours among its twenty-two areas.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Oklahoma pre-license credit is available.

> **The information presented in this course should not be used as a substitute for competent legal
> advice.** — 605:10-5-3(i)(6).

## Overview

The Commission's area of study is called *Law of Agency*. **The most important thing an Oklahoma
licensee can learn about it is that Oklahoma abolished it.**

Section 858-360(A) of the Oklahoma Real Estate License Code provides that the statutory duties in
§§ 858-351 through 858-363 **"shall replace and abrogate the fiduciary or other duties of a broker to a
party based on common law principles of agency."** Section 858-360(B) provides that **"a broker shall
not be an agent, subagent, or dual agent and an offer of subagency shall not be made to other
brokers."**

So this module teaches the common-law vocabulary — because it is the frame the statute displaced, and
because it is what every national textbook and every out-of-state colleague will use — and then teaches
what Oklahoma actually requires, which is a closed statutory list. **A licensee who learns Oklahoma
agency out of a national textbook will learn it wrongly.**

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: Timed sequence
chunks.excerpt:
1. State the common-law agency vocabulary and explain what § 858-360(A) did to it.
2. State what § 858-360(B) forbids, and identify the three relationships Oklahoma brokers cannot have.
3. Recite the seven § 858-353(A) duties owed to **all** parties.
4. Recite the two further § 858-353(B) duties owed only to a party the broker is serving.
5. State the four items § 858-353(A)(4) makes confidential, and explain why the list being exhaustive
   changes practice.
6. State the three circumstances in which confidential information may nevertheless be disclosed.
7. Apply § 858-353(A)(7) to a compensation disclosure, including the one-year cap and the sixty-day
   default.
8. Describe the § 858-355.1 and § 858-356 written disclosure and confirmation requirements.
9. Explain what a broker must disclose when providing **fewer** services than a transaction requires.
10. State what survives termination under § 858-358.
11. Apply § 858-359(A) to a question about who pays.
12. Explain §§ 858-362 and 858-363 and what each means for a provisional sales associate.
13. Identify a § 858-312 ground for discipline arising from a breach of these duties.
14. Describe the § 858-364 deed theft notification obligation and route its form.

## Timed sequence

chunks.heading: Hour 12 — Common-law agency and its abrogation
chunks.excerpt:
| Hour | Content | Instruction |
|---|---|---:|
| 12 | Common-law agency, and § 858-360's abrogation of it | ≥50 min |
| 13 | The seven duties to all parties — § 858-353(A)(1) to (3) | ≥50 min |
| 14 | Confidentiality — § 858-353(A)(4), an exhaustive list | ≥50 min |
| 15 | Disclosure duties — § 858-353(A)(5) to (7) | ≥50 min |
| 16 | Duties to the party served; serving both parties | ≥50 min |
| 17 | Brokerage agreements, written disclosures, confirmation | ≥50 min |
| 18 | Compensation, termination, liability, and the associate's position | ≥50 min |

---

## Hour 12 — Common-law agency and its abrogation

### 12.1 The common-law frame

Agency is the relationship in which one person, the **agent**, acts on behalf of another, the
**principal**, in dealings with third parties. The common law described the agent's duties with **OLD
CAR**: Obedience, Loyalty, Disclosure, Confidentiality, Accounting, Reasonable care.

It classified agents by scope — **universal**, **general** (a property manager), **special** (a listing
broker, traditionally) — and authority as **express**, **implied**, or **apparent**, the last created by
the principal's conduct leading a third party reasonably to believe authority exists.

It also produced the relationships every other state's course spends hours on: **seller's agent**,
**buyer's agent**, **subagent**, **dual agent**, and **designated agent**.

**Learn this vocabulary.** You will meet it in national materials, in conversation with out-of-state
colleagues, and in the general body of real estate knowledge the licensing examination draws on.

### 12.2 And then read § 858-360

chunks.heading: 12.2 And then read § 858-360
chunks.excerpt:
> **A.** The duties and responsibilities of a broker specified in Sections 858-351 through 858-363 of
> The Oklahoma Real Estate License Code **shall replace and abrogate the fiduciary or other duties of a
> broker to a party based on common law principles of agency.** The remedies at law and equity
> supplement the provisions of Sections 858-351 through 858-363…
>
> **B.** A broker may cooperate with other brokers in a transaction. Pursuant to Sections 858-351
> through 858-363…, **a broker shall not be an agent, subagent, or dual agent and an offer of subagency
> shall not be made to other brokers.**

Read both subsections twice.

**(A) means the fiduciary duties are gone.** Not modified, not codified — **replaced and abrogated.** An
Oklahoma broker does not owe a party undivided loyalty as a matter of common-law fiduciary obligation,
because that obligation no longer attaches. What the broker owes is **the statutory list, and the
statutory list is what this module spends the next six hours on.**

**(B) means three relationships do not exist in Oklahoma real estate brokerage:**

- **No agency.** A broker is not a party's agent.
- **No subagency.** And an **offer of subagency shall not be made** to other brokers — so the
  cooperative-compensation-creates-subagency structure that other states spent decades unwinding does
  not arise here at all.
- **No dual agency.** Which is why Oklahoma has no dual agency consent form, no dual agency disclosure
  regime and no list of things a dual agent may not say. A broker serving both parties in Oklahoma is
  not occupying a special reduced-duty status — see Hour 16.

chunks.heading: 12.3 The word "agent" survives; the relationship does not
chunks.excerpt:
**What remains is "brokerage services" provided by a "broker" to a "party."** Those are defined terms —
§ 858-351(2), (1) and (5) — and they carry the whole structure.

### 12.3 The word "agent" survives; the relationship does not

**§ 858-361:**

> A real estate broker and the associates of a real estate broker **are permitted** under the provisions
> of Sections 858-351 through 858-363 of this title **to use the word "agent" in a trade name and as a
> general reference for designating themselves as real estate licensees.**

So "agent" is permitted **vocabulary** — on a sign, on a card, in conversation. It is not a description
of a legal relationship. A licensee who says "I'm your agent" has not committed a violation; a licensee
who *believes* it, and acts on common-law fiduciary instincts instead of the statute, will breach the
statute sooner or later.

### 12.4 The definitions that carry the structure — § 858-351

chunks.heading: Hour 13 — The seven duties to all parties, part one
chunks.excerpt:
- **"Broker"** — a real estate broker, an associated broker associate, sales associate, **or provisional
  sales associate** authorised by a real estate broker to provide brokerage services. **Note this
  carefully: the statutory word "broker" includes you**, once you hold a provisional sales associate
  licence. Every duty in § 858-353 is yours personally, not merely your broker's.
- **"Brokerage services"** — those services provided by a broker to a party in a transaction.
- **"Party"** — a seller, buyer, landlord or tenant, or a person involved in an option or exchange.
- **"Firm"** — a sole proprietor, corporation, association or partnership.
- **"Transaction"** — an activity or process to buy, sell, lease, rent, option or exchange real estate,
  which **may include soliciting, advertising, showing or viewing real property, presenting offers or
  counteroffers, entering into agreements, and closing them.**

That last definition is broader than new licensees expect. **Showing a property is part of a
transaction.** So is advertising one. The duties do not wait for a signature.

---

## Hour 13 — The seven duties to all parties, part one

### 13.1 The opening words, which matter

> **A broker shall have the following duties and responsibilities to ALL PARTIES in a transaction, which
> are MANDATORY and MAY NOT BE ABROGATED OR WAIVED by a broker.**

Three things in one sentence. The duties run to **all parties**, not to a client. They are
**mandatory**. And a broker **cannot waive them** — not by agreement, not by disclosure, not by the
party's consent.

*(One narrow exception appears inside duty 2 itself and is examined below: a **party** may specifically
waive the offer-handling duty in writing. The broker cannot waive it unilaterally.)*

chunks.heading: 13.2 Duty 1 — honesty, reasonable skill and care
chunks.excerpt:
### 13.2 Duty 1 — honesty, reasonable skill and care

> **Treat all parties with honesty and exercise reasonable skill and care.**

To **all parties**. Not to a client. The other side of your transaction is owed honesty and competence
by you, personally, as a matter of statute.

In daily practice "reasonable skill and care" is mostly unglamorous: calendaring every deadline the day
the contract becomes effective; confirming material conversations in writing; checking that what you
repeated matches what the document says; raising a problem before it becomes one.

**And it is where misrepresentation lives.** § 858-312(2) makes **substantial misrepresentations or
false promises in the conduct of business, or through licensees, or advertising** a ground for
suspension or revocation. The habit that prevents it is **attribute or verify, never assert** — the same
rule as Module OK-01 Hour 5.

### 13.3 Duty 2 — offers and counteroffers

> **Unless specifically waived in writing by a party to the transaction:**
> **a.** receive all written offers and counteroffers,
> **b.** **reduce offers or counteroffers to a written form upon request of any party** to a
> transaction, and
> **c.** present timely all written offers and counteroffers.

Three obligations, and (b) is the one that surprises people. **Upon request of ANY party** — not your
party — you must reduce an offer or counteroffer to written form. A buyer with no relationship to you at
all may ask you to put their offer in writing, and you must.

chunks.heading: 13.4 Duty 3 — accounting
chunks.excerpt:
**"Unless specifically waived in writing by a party"** is the statute's own carve-out. A seller
inundated with offers below a threshold may waive in writing. **Specifically, and in writing.** An oral
instruction is not a waiver, and a general "don't bother me with lowballs" is not specific.

**Note what is absent.** Nothing here says the duty stops when the property goes under contract. If a
written offer arrives, it is received and presented.

### 13.4 Duty 3 — accounting

> **Timely account for all money and property received by the broker.**

Earnest money, deposits, rents, keys, documents. It is other people's property from the moment it comes
into your hands.

Two § 858-312 grounds attach directly. **(6)** — failing within a reasonable time to account for or
remit monies, documents or other property belonging to others. And **(16)** — **commingling** the money
or property of others with the licensee's own, **unless held in an escrow account containing only the
money or property of others.**

**This course states no Oklahoma trust or escrow account threshold, deadline or procedure**, because
those provisions were not read from primary text for this project. The principle from § 858-312(16) was
read and is stated: **other people's money never mixes with the firm's.** Read the trust account rules
and your broker's written procedures before you accept your first cheque.

And a related ground worth knowing now: **§ 858-312(22)** makes it a ground **to offer, loan, pay, or
make to appear to have been paid, a down payment or earnest money deposit for a purchaser or seller.**
Funding a buyer's earnest money to save a deal is not generosity; it is a licence problem.

---

## Hour 14 — Confidentiality, and an exhaustive list

### 14.1 The duty

chunks.heading: 14.2 And then the sentence that makes Oklahoma different
chunks.excerpt:
> **Keep confidential information received from a party or prospective party confidential.** The
> confidential information shall not be disclosed by a firm without the consent of the party disclosing
> the information unless **consent to the disclosure is granted in writing** by the party or prospective
> party disclosing the information, **the disclosure is required by law**, or **the information is made
> public or becomes public as the result of actions from a source other than the firm.**

**Three exceptions and only three:** written consent; disclosure required by law; the information
becoming public otherwise than through the firm.

### 14.2 And then the sentence that makes Oklahoma different

> **The following information shall be considered confidential and SHALL BE THE ONLY INFORMATION
> CONSIDERED CONFIDENTIAL in a transaction:**
>
> **a.** that a party or prospective party **is willing to pay more or accept less** than what is being
> offered,
> **b.** that a party or prospective party **is willing to agree to financing terms that are different
> from those offered**,
> **c.** **the motivating factors** of the party or prospective party purchasing, selling, leasing,
> optioning or exchanging the property, and
> **d.** **information specifically designated as confidential by a party** unless such information is
> public.

**"Shall be the only information considered confidential in a transaction."**

That is a closed list, and it is unusual. Other states define confidential information broadly and let
practice work out the edges. Oklahoma names four items and shuts the door.

### 14.3 What follows in practice

chunks.heading: 14.4 And it survives the relationship
chunks.excerpt:
**First, the four items are learnable and should be learned.** (a) will pay more or accept less. (b)
will accept different financing terms. (c) motivating factors. (d) anything a party specifically
designates — the escape valve, and the one a licensee should actually use.

**Second, item (d) is how anything else becomes confidential.** A seller who wants their divorce, their
job relocation or their health kept quiet should **specifically designate it as confidential** — and a
competent licensee prompts them to. Note the qualifier: *unless such information is public.* Designating
something already public does not make it confidential.

**Third, and most importantly: confidentiality is not a defence to disclosure duties.** The exception
"the disclosure is required by law" does real work here. **§ 858-353(A)(5)** requires disclosure of
information pertaining to the property as required by the Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act.
A seller cannot designate a defect as confidential and thereby suppress it. If the law requires it out,
it goes out — and the statute says so in the same paragraph.

**Fourth, note what is NOT on the list.** The price a seller paid. The existence of other offers. The
fact a property has been on the market twice. None of those is confidential unless a party specifically
designates it under (d). That does not make it *wise* to broadcast them — but the licensee should know
where the legal line actually is rather than guessing.

### 14.4 And it survives the relationship

**§ 858-358**, taken up in Hour 18: after termination, expiration or completion, one of only two
surviving duties is **to keep confidential all confidential information received during the broker's
relationship with a party.**

---

## Hour 15 — The disclosure duties

chunks.heading: 15.1 Duty 5 — property condition
chunks.excerpt:
### 15.1 Duty 5 — property condition

> **Disclose information pertaining to the property as required by the Residential Property Condition
> Disclosure Act.**

The duty is stated by cross-reference, and § 858-312(23) makes **violation of the Residential Property
Condition Disclosure Act** an independent ground for suspension or revocation.

**This course states no form, deadline, exemption or content requirement from that Act**, because the
Act's own text was not read from primary text for this project. What was read, and is therefore stated,
is that the duty exists, that it is a duty owed to **all parties**, and that breaching it is a licence
ground on two separate tracks.

**Read the Act.** It is short, it is the operative source, and it governs the single most common
disclosure question an Oklahoma residential licensee will face.

### 15.2 Duty 6 — comply with everything else

> **Comply with all requirements of The Oklahoma Real Estate License Code and all applicable statutes
> and rules.**

Which folds the whole Code and Title 605 into the broker-relationships duties, and means a violation
anywhere is also a § 858-353 violation — and § 858-312(3) separately makes **failing to comply with
§§ 858-351 through 858-363** a ground for discipline.

### 15.3 Duty 7 — compensation, and two numbers

> **Disclose:**
> **a.** information pertaining to **compensation and fees assessed on each transaction to the
> represented party**, which shall be **communicated in writing BEFORE THE EFFECTIVE DATE of the
> contract for sale or lease**, and
> **b.** **the time frame for which the compensation agreement is valid, NOT TO EXCEED ONE (1) YEAR. If
> no time frame is specified, the compensation agreement shall default to SIXTY (60) DAYS.**

Four operative facts:

chunks.heading: Hour 16 — Duties to the party served, and serving both parties
chunks.excerpt:
1. **In writing.**
2. **Before the effective date of the contract** — not at closing, not when the question arises.
3. **A compensation agreement may not run more than one year.**
4. **Silence is not indefinite — it is sixty days.** A compensation agreement with no stated term
   expires in sixty days by operation of the statute.

That fourth point is worth stating twice, because a licensee who assumes an undated compensation
agreement runs until someone cancels it is wrong by statute, and will discover it at the worst possible
moment.

---

## Hour 16 — Duties to the party served, and serving both parties

### 16.1 The two additional duties — § 858-353(B)

> A broker shall have the following duties and responsibilities **only to a party for whom the broker is
> providing brokerage services** in a transaction, **which are mandatory and may not be abrogated or
> waived**:
>
> 1. **Inform the party in writing when an offer is made that the party will be expected to pay certain
>    costs, brokerage service costs and approximate amount of the costs**; and
> 2. **Keep the party informed regarding the transaction.**

**Duty (B)(1) is a cost-estimate obligation with a trigger and a form.** The trigger is **when an offer
is made**. The form is **writing**. The content is **the costs the party will be expected to pay,
including brokerage service costs, and their approximate amount.**

This is Module OK-08's subject — Estimating Transaction Expenses — arriving as a statutory duty rather
than a courtesy. It is also why that module insists a cost sheet is labelled an estimate and shows its
sources: the statute requires an approximate amount, and an approximation presented as a promise is a
different thing.

chunks.heading: 16.2 Serving both parties — § 858-353(C)
chunks.excerpt:
**Duty (B)(2) — keep the party informed — is the one most complaints are actually about.** Not fraud.
Silence. A party who cannot reach their licensee and does not know what is happening will complain, and
under this subsection they will be right.

### 16.2 Serving both parties — § 858-353(C)

> **When working with both parties to a transaction, the duties and responsibilities set forth in this
> section shall remain in place for both parties.**

And § 858-355.1(B): **a broker may provide brokerage services to one or both parties in a transaction.**

**This is not dual agency, because Oklahoma has no dual agency.** § 858-360(B) forbids it outright.
Serving both parties in Oklahoma is not a special status with a consent form and a reduced duty set. It
is the ordinary duty set, **applied in full to both sides at once.**

Which raises the obvious question and answers it. *How can I owe both sides the same duties?* Because
the duties are honesty, skill and care, offer handling, accounting, confidentiality, disclosure and
compliance — **not loyalty.** Loyalty is precisely the fiduciary duty § 858-360(A) abrogated. Nothing in
the statutory list requires you to advance one party's interests against the other's, so there is no
contradiction to resolve.

**What still has to happen** is § 858-355.1(D): a firm providing brokerage services to both parties
**shall provide written notice to both parties that it is doing so, prior to the parties signing a
contract** to purchase, lease, option or exchange.

**And the confidentiality list becomes load-bearing.** Serving both sides, you may hold each party's
willingness to pay more or accept less. Those are §§ 858-353(A)(4)(a) items and they stay in — from
everyone, including the other party you are also serving.

---

chunks.heading: Hour 17 — Brokerage agreements and the written disclosures
chunks.excerpt:
## Hour 17 — Brokerage agreements and the written disclosures

### 17.1 § 858-355.1(A) — the duties go into the agreement

> **All brokerage agreements shall incorporate as material terms the duties and responsibilities set
> forth in Section 858-353.**

Not summarised, not referenced in passing — **incorporated as material terms.** A party reading their
brokerage agreement is entitled to see what they are owed.

### 17.2 § 858-355.1(C) — disclose in writing, before signing

> A broker who is providing brokerage services to one or both parties **shall describe and disclose in
> writing the broker's duties and responsibilities set forth in Section 858-353 prior to the party or
> parties signing a contract to sell, purchase, lease, option, or exchange real estate.**

**The trigger is the contract, not the brokerage agreement.** The disclosure must be made before the
party signs the **transaction** contract. In practice it happens far earlier, and should.

### 17.3 § 858-356 — and then it is confirmed

> The written disclosures as required by subsection C of Section 858-355.1 **shall be confirmed by each
> party in writing in a separate provision, incorporated in or attached to the contract** to purchase,
> lease, option, or exchange real estate. In those cases where **a broker is involved in a transaction
> but does not prepare the contract**, compliance with the disclosure requirements **shall be documented
> by the broker.**

Two mechanisms. Ordinarily the confirmation is **a separate provision in or attached to the contract**,
signed by each party. Where the broker did not prepare the contract, the broker **documents compliance**
some other way — and that documentation is the broker's own protection.

### 17.4 § 858-355.1(E) — providing fewer services

chunks.heading: Hour 18 — Compensation, termination, liability, and your own position
chunks.excerpt:
The provision new licensees never expect and should:

> **If a broker intends to provide fewer brokerage services than those required to complete a
> transaction**, the broker shall provide **written disclosure** to the party for whom the broker is
> providing brokerage services. Such disclosure shall include **a description of those steps in the
> transaction for which the broker will not provide brokerage services**, and also state that **the
> broker assisting the other party in the transaction is not required to provide assistance with these
> steps in any manner.**

So limited-service brokerage is permitted in Oklahoma, and it is permitted **on conditions**: written
disclosure, a **description of the specific steps** not covered, and an express statement that **the
other side's broker is not required to pick them up.**

That last requirement exists because the predictable harm of limited service is a party who assumes
somebody will handle the gap. The statute requires them to be told, in writing, that nobody will.

**Note also what § 858-355.1(E) does NOT permit.** It allows fewer *services*. It does not allow fewer
**duties** — § 858-353(A) and (B) are mandatory and unwaivable.

---

## Hour 18 — Compensation, termination, liability, and your own position

### 18.1 Compensation — § 858-359

**(A)** **The payment or promise of payment or compensation by a party to a broker does not determine
what relationship, if any, has been established** between the broker and a party.

**Who pays does not decide whom you serve.** In Oklahoma this is even cleaner than elsewhere, because
there is no agency to be created by implication in the first place.

chunks.heading: 18.2 Termination — § 858-358
chunks.excerpt:
**(B)** Receiving a fee or compensation **based on a selling price or lease cost** does not constitute a
breach of duty or obligation to any party. A percentage fee is not, by itself, a conflict.

**(C)** A broker **or a real estate owner of record** may compensate or offer compensation to **any real
estate professional licensed by the Commission** for providing brokerage services in connection with a
transaction of Oklahoma real estate.

**(D)** Nothing **requires or prohibits** charging a separate fee for each duty or service, and nothing
**requires** a broker or owner of record **to offer compensation** to any real estate professional.

**And the associate's own position — § 858-312(4):** it is a ground for discipline for an associate to
accept **a commission or other valuable consideration for the performance of any acts as an associate,
except from the real estate broker with whom the associate is associated.** You are paid by your broker.
Not by a seller, not by a buyer, not by a cooperating firm.

**Related ground — § 858-312(21):** paying any part of a fee or commission **to any person not
licensed.** Referral fees to unlicensed persons are a licence problem.

### 18.2 Termination — § 858-358

> Except as may be provided in a written brokerage agreement…, the broker owes **no further duties or
> responsibilities to the party after termination, expiration, or completion of performance** of the
> transaction, **except**:
> **1.** To **account for all monies and property** relating to the transaction; and
> **2.** To **keep confidential all confidential information** received during the broker's relationship
> with a party.

chunks.heading: 18.3 Liability — § 858-362
chunks.excerpt:
**Two duties survive; everything else stops.** A listing expires and six months later you are working
the same house for a buyer. The former seller's motivating factors and their willingness to accept less
are still § 858-353(A)(4) items, and § 858-358(2) keeps them in.

Note the opening words: **"except as may be provided in a written brokerage agreement."** The agreement
can extend duties past termination. Read it.

### 18.3 Liability — § 858-362

> **A party to a real estate transaction shall not be vicariously liable for the acts or omissions of a
> real estate licensee** who is providing brokerage services under Sections 858-351 through 858-363.

A seller is not automatically on the hook for what their broker did. This follows naturally from the
abolition of agency: vicarious liability was a consequence of the principal-agent relationship, and
Oklahoma removed the relationship.

**It says nothing about the LICENSEE's own liability**, which is untouched, nor about the broker's
responsibility for their associates.

### 18.4 Your own position — § 858-363

> Each broker associate, sales associate, and provisional sales associate **shall be associated with a
> real estate broker.** Associates **shall not enter into a brokerage agreement with a party in the
> associate's name** and shall only be allowed to enter into the agreement **in the name of the
> broker.** A real estate broker **may authorize associates to provide brokerage services in the name of
> the real estate broker**, which may include the execution of written agreements.

Three things you will need on your first day:

chunks.heading: 18.5 Deed theft — § 858-364, and something new
chunks.excerpt:
1. **You must be associated with a broker.**
2. **Every brokerage agreement is in the broker's name.** Never yours.
3. **You act under the broker's authorisation**, which may extend to executing written agreements — and
   you should know the scope of yours.

**§ 858-312(5)** adds the corollary: representing or attempting to represent a broker **other than the
one with whom you are associated**, without that broker's express knowledge and consent, is a ground for
discipline.

### 18.5 Deed theft — § 858-364, and something new

> As part of **each closing** of a transaction, notification of the signs and risks of **deed theft**, as
> defined in Section 858-351, **shall be required to be given to the buyer by a licensed real estate
> broker. The buyer shall confirm receipt of such notification by affixing his or her signature** to
> such notification. The Oklahoma Real Estate Commission shall promulgate rules to enact the provisions
> of this section.

**Deed theft** is defined at § 858-351(3) as intentionally altering, falsifying, forging or
misrepresenting a document relating to real property with intent to deceive, defraud or unlawfully
transfer or encumber ownership rights; misrepresenting oneself as the owner or the owner's authorised
representative to obtain ownership or possession; or, with intent to defraud, taking, obtaining,
stealing or transferring title or ownership by fraud, forgery, larceny or any other fraudulent or
deceptive practice.

**The obligation is on the broker, at every closing, and the buyer signs.**

chunks.heading: 18.6 The whole module in one page
chunks.excerpt:
**This course states no wording or format for the notification**, because the Commission's implementing
rules and the form itself were not located in the publication read for this project. **Obtain the current
form from the Commission**, and confirm the rules have issued before relying on any version of it.

Relatedly, **§ 858-307.2(F)** requires licensees to complete Commission-specified continuing education
on deed theft **on or before 1 November 2028.**

### 18.6 The whole module in one page

**There is no agency.** § 858-360(A) abrogated the fiduciary duties; § 858-360(B) forbids agency,
subagency and dual agency.

**To ALL parties, mandatory and unwaivable** — § 858-353(A): honesty and reasonable skill and care;
receive, reduce to writing on any party's request, and timely present all written offers and
counteroffers, unless a party specifically waives in writing; timely accounting; confidentiality of
**four listed items and only those**; property disclosure as the Residential Property Condition
Disclosure Act requires; compliance with the Code and all applicable statutes and rules; and written
compensation disclosure **before the contract's effective date**, with a term **capped at one year** and
**defaulting to sixty days** if unstated.

**To the party you serve, additionally** — § 858-353(B): written notice of the costs they will be
expected to pay when an offer is made, including brokerage service costs and their approximate amount;
and keeping them informed.

**Both parties?** Same duties, both sides, plus written notice to both under § 858-355.1(D).

**In writing, before signing, confirmed in or attached to the contract** — §§ 858-355.1(C) and 858-356.

chunks.heading: Module OK-03 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**Fewer services?** Written disclosure of exactly which steps you will not perform, and a statement that
the other broker need not perform them either — § 858-355.1(E).

**Afterwards:** account, and keep confidences — § 858-358.

**And breach of any of it is § 858-312(3): failing to comply with §§ 858-351 through 858-363.**

### Module OK-03 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module OK-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, from 605:10-5-3(f).

---

## Instructor source note for Module OK-03

Every section cited in this module — 59 O.S. §§ 858-301.2, 858-307.2, 858-312, 858-351, 858-353,
858-355.1, 858-356, 858-358, 858-359, 858-360, 858-361, 858-362, 858-363 and 858-364, and 605:10-3-1 and
605:10-5-3 — was read on 2026-08-20 from the Commission's *Oklahoma Real Estate License Code and Rules*
effective 1 November 2025, and is transcribed in `oklahoma/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this module:** the **Residential Property Condition
Disclosure Act**, 60 O.S. § 831 et seq., whose existence and whose status as a duty and a discipline
ground ARE stated because §§ 858-353(A)(5) and 858-312(23) were read, but none of whose content is;
**59 O.S. § 858-208**, the sanctions section § 858-312 cross-refers to, so no sanction available under it
is named; **the Commission's rules implementing § 858-364** and the form of the deed theft notification;
Oklahoma's trust and escrow account provisions; and the Oklahoma Real Estate Contract Form Committee's
promulgated forms. Where this module reaches one of those it names the question and routes it.

chunks.heading: Supplemental source review — 2026-09-06
chunks.excerpt:
## Supplemental source review — 2026-09-06

This required reading clarifies the existing topics; no additional clock-hour credit or regulator approval is claimed.

### supervision

Related module 03, §18.4. Opening a branch is not just creating a web page. Under 59 O.S. 858-310(B),
branch licensing and separate broker direction requirements apply. The responsible broker must
supervise licensed activity; an associate cannot appoint themselves independent broker by using a
different trade name. OAC 605:10-9-1 supplies further brokerage responsibilities. Check the actual
license, assignment and activity, not merely an office sign or an individual's seniority.

Sources: [OREC License Code and Rules, as of November 1, 2025](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/orec/documents/meetings/Nov%201%202025%20Oklahoma%20Real%20Estate%20Commission%20Code%20and%20Rules%20Book.pdf).

### conflicts

Related module 14, §80.2 and module 03. A broker serving both parties must provide the written notice
required by 59 O.S. 858-355.1(D). Section 858-312(3), not (6), makes failure to comply with the Broker
Relationships Act a disciplinary ground. Section (6) concerns accounting and remittance. Payment alone
does not establish a brokerage relationship under 858-359(A). The Oklahoma Broker Relationships Act
abrogates common-law agency duties within its scope (858-360), but permits additional agreed services
that do not displace statutory duties. The word "agent" as a trade description does not recreate a
different common-law regime (858-361).

chunks.heading: conflicts
chunks.excerpt:
Confidential information under 858-353(A)(4) includes specified price/financing flexibility, motivation
and designated information; the statutory exceptions include written consent, legal requirement and
information becoming public from a source other than the firm. Do not call every physical defect
confidential or disclose negotiations just because a transaction ended. Both-side service does not
permit a broker to sacrifice honesty, accounting or timely communication. Fees can be separately
negotiated under 858-359(D); competing firms cannot agree on a common fee floor. An independent firm's
own fee policy is not, by itself, an agreement among competitors. Sources include the current OREC
Code and the DOJ's primary horizontal-price-fixing enforcement record.

Sources: [OREC License Code and Rules, as of November 1, 2025](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/orec/documents/meetings/Nov%201%202025%20Oklahoma%20Real%20Estate%20Commission%20Code%20and%20Rules%20Book.pdf); [DOJ — United States v. Atlanta Real Estate Board, horizontal price fixing](https://www.justice.gov/atr/case/us-v-atlanta-real-estate-board).

chunks.heading: Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-04
chunks.excerpt:
# Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-04

## Hours 19–24 · Title search, encumbrances, and land use control

**Commission area of study covered:** 605:10-3-1(a)(1)(E) Title Search, Encumbrances, and Land Use
Control
**Clock hours:** 6 · **Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Commission review;
605:10-3-1(a)(1) allocates no hours among its twenty-two areas of study.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Oklahoma pre-license credit is available.

> **The information presented in this course should not be used as a substitute for competent legal
> advice.** — 605:10-5-3(i)(6).

## Overview

How title is proved, what can be wrong with it, and what the public and private controls on land use
do to what a buyer may actually do with a property. This module takes the title commitment apart
schedule by schedule, because that document is where most title problems are either caught or missed,
and then covers zoning, subdivision regulation and private covenants — with the licensee's boundary
stated at every point.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: Timed sequence
chunks.excerpt:
1. Explain what a title search establishes and what a chain of title is.
2. Name the three kinds of notice and explain why possession is checked as well as the records.
3. Read a title commitment's Schedules A, B-I and B-II and say what each does.
4. State what an owner's policy covers and what it excepts, and distinguish it from a lender's policy.
5. Explain the survey exception and what removes it.
6. Identify a cloud on title and name the instruments that clear one.
7. Distinguish the four government powers and identify which operates in a fact pattern.
8. Distinguish variance, conditional use, rezoning and legal nonconforming use.
9. Explain why private covenants are separate from zoning and which controls.
10. Describe subdivision regulation and plat approval at the level of principle.
11. State the licensee's boundary on every land-use question and route accordingly.
12. Recognise a severed mineral estate and a pipeline easement as title questions.

## Timed sequence

| Hour | Content | Instruction |
|---|---|---:|
| 19 | The title search, the chain of title, and notice | ≥50 min |
| 20 | The title commitment, schedule by schedule | ≥50 min |
| 21 | Title insurance: coverage, exceptions, and the survey | ≥50 min |
| 22 | Clouds on title and how they are cleared | ≥50 min |
| 23 | Public land use control: zoning and its instruments | ≥50 min |
| 24 | Subdivision regulation and private controls | ≥50 min |

---

## Hour 19 — The title search, the chain, and notice

### 19.1 What a title search establishes

chunks.heading: 19.2 The chain of title
chunks.excerpt:
A **title search** is an examination of the public records to determine the condition of title: who owns
the property, what interests burden it, and whether anything in the record casts doubt on the owner's
ability to convey what the contract says they will convey.

**Where the records live.** Real property records are maintained at the **county** level — in Oklahoma,
the **county clerk** records instruments affecting title. Judgments, tax liens, probate proceedings and
court actions may sit in other indices in the same county or elsewhere, which is why a competent search
is not one look at one book.

### 19.2 The chain of title

The **chain of title** is the successive record of conveyances from an accepted starting point to the
present owner. Each link should connect: the grantee of one deed is the grantor of the next.

A **gap** in the chain — a missing conveyance, an estate that never went through probate, a name that
does not match, a signature that is absent — is a **cloud**, and clouds are resolved before closing
rather than explained away at it.

An **abstract of title** is a compiled history of the recorded instruments affecting a parcel. Oklahoma
practice retains a real role for abstracts, and an abstract that is brought current and examined by an
attorney produces an **attorney's title opinion**. Title insurance is the other route, and the two
coexist. **Which form of title evidence a transaction uses is settled in the contract**, which is one
more reason the contract is read before it is signed.

### 19.3 Three kinds of notice

**Actual notice** — the party in fact knows.

chunks.heading: 19.4 What recording does and does not do
chunks.excerpt:
**Constructive notice from the records** — the party is charged with knowing what a proper search of the
public records would reveal, **whether or not they searched.** This is what recording accomplishes and
it is why recording matters.

**Inquiry notice, or notice from possession** — the party is charged with what a reasonable **inspection
of the property** would reveal, and with following up on what that inspection would make a reasonable
person ask about.

**The possession problem is the classic trap and a real one.** Someone living in the house. A tenant
with an unrecorded lease. A neighbour openly using a strip of the yard. A gate, a drive or a fence in a
place the plat does not explain. Each is a fact a purchaser is expected to have noticed.

**Title is checked in the records AND on the ground.**

### 19.4 What recording does and does not do

Recording gives **constructive notice to the world**, protecting the recorded interest against later
takers. It does **not** transfer title — delivery and acceptance do that — and it does **not** validate
an otherwise invalid instrument.

The practical rule is short: **record immediately.** The entire risk lives in the interval between
delivery and recording.

### 19.5 Two Oklahoma questions that belong in every title search

**Minerals.** Surface and mineral estates are frequently severed in Oklahoma. **A licensee never states
what mineral interest a property carries.** Raise it at listing, get it into the title work early, and
route the answer to counsel.

**Pipeline, gathering line and utility easements.** They cross a great deal of Oklahoma land and they
carry rights of access, surface use and sometimes future construction that a buyer will not infer from
looking at the ground.

chunks.heading: Hour 20 — The title commitment, schedule by schedule
chunks.excerpt:
**This course states no Oklahoma rule of mineral title or of easement scope**, because those provisions
were not read from primary text for this project. The recognition and the routing are what a licensee
carries.

---

## Hour 20 — The title commitment, schedule by schedule

### 20.1 What a commitment is

A **title commitment** is the title company's **conditional promise to insure**. It is not a title
opinion, not a coverage summary, and not a guarantee that anything is clear. It says: *on these facts,
if these requirements are satisfied, we will issue a policy subject to these exceptions.*

### 20.2 Schedule A — the facts

The proposed insured; the amount of insurance; the estate or interest to be insured; the current record
owner; and the **legal description**.

**Read Schedule A against the contract.** Is the legal description the property everyone thinks is being
sold? Is the record owner the person who signed the listing? Is the amount right? Discrepancies at
Schedule A are cheap to fix and expensive to discover later.

### 20.3 Schedule B-I — Requirements

**What must be done before the policy will issue.** Typically:

- Payoff and **release** of existing mortgages and liens.
- **Corrective instruments** for defects in the chain.
- **Evidence of authority** — a corporate resolution, a trustee's certificate, letters testamentary.
- **Satisfaction of judgments**, or evidence that a judgment debtor with a similar name is not this
  seller. A name match is not an identification, and resolving it is the title company's work, not the
  licensee's.
- Resolution of **probate** where the seller is an estate.

chunks.heading: 20.4 Schedule B-II — Exceptions
chunks.excerpt:
**Every item on Schedule B-I is a task with an owner and a deadline.** The licensee's job is to make
sure each one has both, early enough that the closing date survives.

### 20.4 Schedule B-II — Exceptions

**What the policy will NOT cover.** This is where the policy's actual scope is decided and it is the
part a buyer is least likely to read.

Standard exceptions commonly include:

- **Rights of parties in possession** — the possession problem, again.
- **Survey matters and encroachments** absent a survey.
- **Easements** not shown by the public records.
- **Mineral rights** and prior reservations or severances — which in Oklahoma is frequently the most
  consequential exception on the page.
- **Taxes and assessments** not yet due and payable.

### 20.5 What a licensee does with a commitment

**Get it into the buyer's hands early.** Tell them to read Schedules B-I and B-II. Route every question
to the title company and counsel. **Watch the objection deadline in the contract**, because it will pass
while everyone assumes the title work is "in progress."

**And never say "the title policy will take care of it."** That characterises another party's contract
that the licensee has not read and cannot bind, and under § 858-353(A)(1) — honesty and reasonable skill
and care to all parties — it is exactly the kind of casual reassurance that becomes a complaint.

---

## Hour 21 — Title insurance

### 21.1 Owner's and lender's policies

An **owner's policy** insures the owner against loss from covered title defects **existing at the date
of policy** — forged instruments, undisclosed heirs, incompetent grantors, recording errors, defective
deeds, undisclosed liens. Coverage is **retrospective**: it insures the past, not future events.

chunks.heading: 21.2 What is excepted
chunks.excerpt:
A **lender's policy** insures the lender's **lien position** in the amount of the loan and decreases as
the loan is repaid. **A lender's policy does not protect the buyer**, and buyers regularly believe that
it does. Say so, plainly, every time.

### 21.2 What is excepted

Everything in Schedule B-II, plus:

- defects **created, assumed or agreed to by the insured**;
- defects **known to the insured and not disclosed** to the company;
- matters arising **after** the date of policy.

That second item is worth a licensee's attention. A buyer who learns of a title problem and closes
anyway without telling the title company may have excluded it from their own coverage.

### 21.3 The survey exception

The practically important one. **Encroachments, boundary discrepancies, and anything a survey would
disclose are typically excepted unless a survey is furnished and the exception removed.**

A buyer who declines a survey has accepted that risk, and should be told so in exactly those words —
**not** "you probably don't need one." Whether a survey is needed is the buyer's decision on advice; the
licensee's job is to make sure the decision is informed and made before the deadline.

### 21.4 Endorsements

Coverage can be extended by **endorsement** — for access, for zoning, for restrictions, for survey
matters where a survey is provided. Which endorsements are available and appropriate is a question for
the title company and counsel. **A licensee neither recommends nor characterises endorsements.**

---

## Hour 22 — Clouds on title and how they clear

### 22.1 Common clouds

chunks.heading: 22.2 The instruments that clear them
chunks.excerpt:
- An **unreleased mortgage** long since paid. Payment alone does not clear the record.
- A **missing signature** — a spouse, a co-owner, a person whose interest nobody noticed.
- A **name discrepancy** — the grantee took as one name and conveyed as another.
- An **estate that never went through probate**, so the heirs' interests were never established.
- A **judgment** against someone with the seller's name.
- A **defective legal description** in an earlier deed.
- An **unreleased oil and gas lease** or a **severed mineral interest** whose owner cannot be located.

### 22.2 The instruments that clear them

- A **release** or **satisfaction**, recorded.
- A **corrective deed**, to fix a description or a name.
- A **quit claim deed**, to convey away a possible interest.
- An **affidavit** — of identity, of heirship, of scrivener's error — where the title company will
  accept one.
- A **probate proceeding**, where an estate must be administered.
- A **suit to quiet title**, where nothing else will do. It is a lawsuit, it takes months, and a closing
  date built around one that nobody has filed is a closing date that will move.

**Every one of these is prepared and decided by counsel and the title company.** A licensee identifies
the problem early, routes it, and manages the timetable.

### 22.3 The timetable is the licensee's real contribution

The licensee is not the person who clears title. The licensee is the person who **notices in week one
that title work has not been ordered**, who **reads Schedule B-I the day it arrives**, and who **tells
the client in writing that the closing date depends on an item nobody has started.**

That is § 858-353(A)(1) — reasonable skill and care — and § 858-353(B)(2) — keeping the party informed —
doing their actual work.

---

chunks.heading: Hour 23 — Public land use control
chunks.excerpt:
## Hour 23 — Public land use control

### 23.1 The four powers, applied

Module OK-02 named them; here they operate. **Police power** is the one that produces zoning, building
codes, subdivision regulation and environmental controls, and it operates **without compensation**.
**Eminent domain** takes, through condemnation, with just compensation. **Taxation** charges. **Escheat**
reverts.

### 23.2 The comprehensive plan and zoning

The **comprehensive plan** is a municipality's long-range policy document. **Zoning** is meant to
implement it, dividing a jurisdiction into districts and regulating **use** and **dimension** — setbacks,
height, lot coverage, density, parking.

The instruments a licensee will hear named:

**Variance.** Permission to depart from a **dimensional** requirement because of a hardship arising from
the property itself. Granted by a board of adjustment on its own standards. **A licensee never tells a
buyer a variance will be granted.**

**Conditional or special use permit.** A use the ordinance contemplates subject to review and
conditions.

**Rezoning.** A legislative change to the district or the map. It is a political process as much as a
legal one and its outcome cannot be predicted.

**Legal nonconforming use.** A use that lawfully predates the current ordinance and is allowed to
continue **subject to limits** on expansion, on resumption after abandonment, and on rebuilding after
destruction. **Those limits are the point.** A buyer who assumes the use is permanent and unrestricted
may find they cannot rebuild after a fire or resume after a vacancy.

**Spot zoning** — rezoning a single parcel inconsistently with the surrounding area — is disfavoured and
vulnerable to challenge.

### 23.3 Building codes

chunks.heading: 23.4 The licensee's boundary, stated once for the hour
chunks.excerpt:
Minimum construction standards enforced through **permits and inspections**. Separate from zoning: zoning
governs use and dimension, codes govern construction.

Two things a licensee must know:

- **A code-compliant building is not a defect-free building.** Codes are minimums.
- **A permit history records what was applied for, not what was built.** Unpermitted work is a routine
  finding on older houses, and it is routed to the municipality — not characterised by the licensee as
  "fine" or "no problem."

### 23.4 The licensee's boundary, stated once for the hour

**Identify the question, tell the client which authority answers it, and see that it is answered before
their contingencies expire.**

**Never** state what a municipality will permit. **Never** assume a current use is permitted merely
because it exists — it may be nonconforming, unpermitted, or about to become impossible to continue.

Timing is where the licensee actually adds value: getting the buyer's question in front of the
municipality in week one rather than week four.

---

## Hour 24 — Subdivision regulation and private controls

### 24.1 Subdivision regulation

Governs the **division of land into lots** and the standards for the plat, the streets, the utilities,
the drainage and the dedications. It is a municipal and county process, and the **recorded plat** it
produces becomes the legal description for every lot in it.

A licensee working raw land, or a lot in a new development, routes plat questions to the municipality,
the county and a surveyor **before anything is marketed.**

**This course states no Oklahoma platting requirement, dedication standard or approval timetable**,
because Oklahoma's subdivision provisions were not read from primary text for this project.

### 24.2 Private controls

chunks.heading: 24.3 Homeowners' associations
chunks.excerpt:
**Restrictive covenants** — conditions and restrictions recorded against the land, usually as a
declaration governing a subdivision, enforced by an owners' association or by benefited owners. They
**run with the land**.

**Two facts a buyer needs and usually does not have:**

1. **Covenants are separate from zoning, and the more restrictive controls.** A city may permit a use the
   covenants forbid, and the covenants win.
2. **Covenants are enforced privately.** No municipal official will tell a buyer they are about to breach
   one. The association or a neighbour will — after the garage is built.

**A buyer who intends to run a business from home, park a recreational vehicle or boat, keep animals,
build an outbuilding, install a fence, or rent the property short-term needs the covenants read BEFORE
the offer is written.**

### 24.3 Homeowners' associations

Where a declaration creates one, it typically has power to levy **assessments**, to enforce the
covenants, to maintain common areas and to adopt rules. What a buyer must get in writing before their
contingencies expire: the assessment and what it covers; reserves; any pending or implied special
assessment; litigation; the rules on pets, rentals, vehicles and occupancy; and whether their lender
will lend on this project.

### 24.4 Discriminatory covenants

Racially restrictive covenants appear in the older records of essentially every American city,
Oklahoma's included. **They are void and unenforceable**, and they have no legal effect whatever the
record says.

chunks.heading: Module OK-04 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
A licensee who encounters one does not repeat it, does not describe a neighbourhood by reference to it,
and routes the question of removing it from the record to counsel. Module OK-13 takes fair housing up in
full; the point here is that a recorded restriction is not automatically an enforceable one.

### Module OK-04 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module OK-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, from 605:10-5-3(f).

---

## Instructor source note for Module OK-04

Oklahoma citations in this module — 59 O.S. § 858-353, and 605:10-3-1 and 605:10-5-3 — were read on
2026-08-20 and are recorded in `oklahoma/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this module:** Oklahoma's recording, limitations, mechanic's
lien, subdivision, condominium and mineral title provisions; Oklahoma's zoning and planning enabling
statutes; and any municipal ordinance. No period, threshold, standard or figure from any of them
appears, and every land-use determination is routed to the authority that makes it.

chunks.heading: Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-05
chunks.excerpt:
# Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-05

## Hours 25–29 · Transfer of rights

**Commission area of study covered:** 605:10-3-1(a)(1)(F) Transfer of Rights
**Clock hours:** 5 · **Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Commission review;
605:10-3-1(a)(1) allocates no hours among its twenty-two areas of study.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Oklahoma pre-license credit is available.

> **The information presented in this course should not be used as a substitute for competent legal
> advice.** — 605:10-5-3(i)(6).

## Overview

How ownership actually moves from one person to another — voluntarily by deed, at death by will or
intestacy, and involuntarily by foreclosure, tax sale, condemnation, adverse possession and the
processes of nature. The module covers the requirements of a valid deed, the deed types and what each
warrants, and the transactions where a licensee most often meets an authority problem: estates,
trusts, entities and powers of attorney.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: Timed sequence
chunks.excerpt:
1. Name the requirements of a valid deed and explain why recording is not one of them.
2. Explain delivery and acceptance and identify the moment title passes.
3. Distinguish the deed types by what the grantor warrants and say when each is used.
4. Identify a fiduciary's deed and state what question it raises.
5. Distinguish testate from intestate succession and describe probate's role.
6. State what a licensee must establish before taking a listing from an estate.
7. Name the forms of involuntary alienation and identify which is operating in a fact pattern.
8. Describe adverse possession's elements and route the question correctly.
9. Explain the natural processes that move boundaries along watercourses.
10. Identify a power-of-attorney or entity-authority question and route it.
11. State the deed theft obligation under § 858-364 and route the form.
12. State why a licensee never advises which deed to use or how to take title.

## Timed sequence

| Hour | Content | Instruction |
|---|---|---:|
| 25 | Requirements of a valid deed; delivery and acceptance | ≥50 min |
| 26 | Deed types and what each warrants | ≥50 min |
| 27 | Transfer at death: wills, intestacy, probate, estate sales | ≥50 min |
| 28 | Involuntary alienation | ≥50 min |
| 29 | Authority problems, and the deed theft notification | ≥50 min |

---

## Hour 25 — The valid deed

### 25.1 What a deed requires

A **deed** is the instrument that conveys an interest in real estate. To be valid it needs:

chunks.heading: 25.2 Delivery and acceptance — where title actually passes
chunks.excerpt:
- a **grantor** with legal capacity;
- a **grantee** identified with certainty;
- **words of conveyance** — the granting clause;
- an **adequate legal description**;
- the **grantor's signature**, and in practice **acknowledgement** before a notary so the instrument may
  be recorded;
- **delivery** by the grantor and **acceptance** by the grantee.

**And note what is NOT required:** the grantee's signature; consideration in any particular amount —
deeds routinely recite nominal consideration; and **recording**, which is not a requirement of validity
at all.

### 25.2 Delivery and acceptance — where title actually passes

**Title passes at delivery and acceptance**, not at signature and not at recording.

**Delivery** requires the grantor's present intent to pass title. A deed signed and locked in a drawer
has not been delivered. A deed handed over with instructions to record it only after the grantor's death
raises a delivery question that ends up in court.

**Acceptance** by the grantee is generally presumed where the conveyance benefits them.

**The consequence:** an unrecorded but delivered deed is **valid between the parties** — and can still
lose to a later interest taken and recorded by someone without notice of it. Which is why the rule is
**record immediately.**

### 25.3 The parts of a deed

Beyond the essentials, a deed customarily contains: the **premises** clause naming the parties and the
consideration; the **granting** clause; the **habendum** clause — "to have and to hold" — describing the
estate conveyed; the **legal description**; any **reservations or exceptions** — and in Oklahoma this is
frequently where **minerals** are reserved; the **covenants**, if any; the **execution** and the
**acknowledgement**.

chunks.heading: Hour 26 — Deed types
chunks.excerpt:
**Read the reservations and exceptions.** A deed conveying the surface and reserving the minerals says so
there, and a buyer who did not have it explained will not have understood what they bought.

---

## Hour 26 — Deed types

### 26.1 By what the grantor warrants

**General warranty deed.** The broadest covenants. The grantor warrants title against defects arising at
**any** time, including before the grantor's own ownership. Traditional covenants: seisin, right to
convey, against encumbrances, quiet enjoyment, further assurance, warranty forever. This is the ordinary
residential sale deed.

**Special or limited warranty deed.** The grantor warrants **only against defects arising during the
grantor's own ownership.** Common where the grantor is an entity, a lender, or a fiduciary that cannot
speak to what came before.

**Quit claim deed.** Conveys whatever interest the grantor has — **if any** — and **warrants nothing.**
It is a **clearing** instrument: removing a cloud, correcting a name, releasing a possible interest,
transferring between related parties. It is **not** a sale instrument, and a buyer offered one in an
arm's-length purchase should ask why and take the answer to counsel.

### 26.2 Fiduciary deeds

**Personal representative's deed. Trustee's deed. Guardian's deed. Sheriff's deed.**

Each carries the authority of the proceeding behind it and **warrants little or nothing.** The question
each raises is the same: **does this person actually have authority to convey?** That authority comes
from a court order, letters, a trust instrument or a statute — and it is a **legal determination**
established **before** a listing is taken, not discovered at closing.

### 26.3 The licensee's boundary

chunks.heading: Hour 27 — Transfer at death, and estate sales
chunks.excerpt:
**Which deed is used in a particular transaction is a legal decision for counsel and the closing agent.**
A licensee who tells a client which deed to take or give has practised law.

And so is **how to take title** — tenancy in common, joint tenancy, a trust, an entity. That is a legal
and tax question for counsel and the buyer's tax adviser. The licensee's contribution is to raise it
early enough that it is decided deliberately.

---

## Hour 27 — Transfer at death, and estate sales

### 27.1 Testate and intestate

**Testate** — the owner died leaving a valid will. Real property passes by **devise** to a **devisee**.

**Intestate** — no valid will. Property passes to heirs under the state's descent and distribution
statute.

**This course states no Oklahoma rule of descent and distribution, no will formality and no probate
timetable**, because Oklahoma's probate provisions were not read from primary text for this project.

### 27.2 Probate

**Probate** is the court proceeding that proves the will, appoints a personal representative, gives
notice to creditors, settles claims and authorises distribution.

**Why a licensee cares:** because probate answers **who may sign**, and because **probate timing can
control the closing date.**

### 27.3 What must be established before taking an estate listing

1. **Who has authority to convey**, and what document establishes it. Letters testamentary or of
   administration; a court order; a trustee's certificate where the property is in trust.
2. **Whether court confirmation of the sale is required**, and if so what that adds to the timetable.
3. **Whether all necessary parties will sign** — heirs, devisees, a surviving spouse.
4. **What deed will be used**, which will typically be a fiduciary's deed warranting little.

chunks.heading: 27.4 What a licensee says to the family
chunks.excerpt:
**Estate sales fail on authority and on timetable far more often than on price.** Building a closing date
around a probate step nobody has confirmed is the avoidable error, and it is the one that happens most.

### 27.4 What a licensee says to the family

That the questions above must be answered by counsel and the title company; that the answers will shape
the timetable; and that the sale should not be marketed with a closing date the probate cannot support.

That is honesty and reasonable skill and care under § 858-353(A)(1), owed to **all parties** — including
the buyer who is being asked to rely on a date.

---

## Hour 28 — Involuntary alienation

### 28.1 The forms

**Escheat.** To the state where an owner dies with no heirs and no will.

**Eminent domain.** Through condemnation, with just compensation.

**Foreclosure.** Enforcement of a lien — Module OK-11's subject.

**Tax sale.** Enforcement of the tax lien.

**Adverse possession.** A court's determination that long possession has ripened into title.

**Natural processes.** **Accretion** — gradual addition of soil by water action, which the riparian owner
gains. **Erosion** — gradual loss. **Reliction** — land uncovered by permanently receding water.
**Avulsion** — sudden removal of land by water, which traditionally does **not** change the boundary.

### 28.2 Adverse possession

Possession that is **actual, open and notorious, hostile** to the true owner's interest, **exclusive**,
and **continuous for the statutory period** may ripen into title. **Tacking** allows successive
possessors in privity to add their periods together.

**It is established by a court, not asserted by a party.**

chunks.heading: 28.3 Tax sale and foreclosure, at the level of principle
chunks.excerpt:
**This course states no Oklahoma statutory period**, because Oklahoma's limitations provisions were not
read from primary text for this project.

**What a licensee carries is a practice rule:** a **fence, drive, dock, garden, outbuilding or gate in
the wrong place, in place for a long time**, is routed to counsel and a surveyor. It is never resolved by
asking the neighbours what they think, and it is never described to a buyer as "nothing to worry about."

### 28.3 Tax sale and foreclosure, at the level of principle

Both extinguish the owner's interest through a process the law prescribes, and both may extinguish junior
interests while leaving senior ones. **The specifics — notice, timing, redemption, deficiency, the effect
on junior liens — are entirely statutory**, and **this course states none of them for Oklahoma**, because
Oklahoma's foreclosure and tax provisions were not read from primary text for this project.

A licensee working a distressed file identifies the questions and routes them: the seller's deficiency
exposure, tax consequences and credit consequences go to counsel and an accountant, and the timetable
goes to counsel and the title company.

---

## Hour 29 — Authority problems and the deed theft notification

### 29.1 The recurring question: who may sign?

Most closing-table failures in transfer are authority failures, and they are all the same question in
different costumes:

chunks.heading: 29.2 Deed theft — 59 O.S. § 858-364
chunks.excerpt:
- **A life estate.** The life tenant cannot convey the fee; the remainderman must join — Module OK-02.
- **An estate.** Authority comes from the probate proceeding.
- **A trust.** Authority comes from the trust instrument, and the title company will want to see it or a
  certificate of trust.
- **An entity** — corporation, LLC, partnership. Authority comes from the governing documents and usually
  a resolution or consent. **A signature by someone who turns out not to have been authorised does not
  convey.**
- **A power of attorney.** Must be valid, must be broad enough to cover a real estate conveyance, must
  usually be recorded, and **must still be in force** — a power of attorney generally terminates on the
  principal's death, and sometimes on incapacity unless it is durable.
- **Co-owners**, and any spouse whose joinder may be required.

**One question, asked at the listing appointment, catches nearly all of them: "Who else has to sign?"**
Asked then, it is a five-minute conversation. Asked at closing, it is a postponement.

**Every answer is a legal determination for counsel and the title company.** The licensee asks, routes,
and manages the timetable.

### 29.2 Deed theft — 59 O.S. § 858-364

> As part of **each closing** of a transaction, notification of the signs and risks of **deed theft**, as
> defined in Section 858-351 of Title 59 of the Oklahoma Statutes, **shall be required to be given to the
> buyer by a licensed real estate broker. The buyer shall confirm receipt of such notification by
> affixing his or her signature to such notification.** The Oklahoma Real Estate Commission shall
> promulgate rules to enact the provisions of this section.

**Deed theft** is defined at § 858-351(3) as:

chunks.heading: 29.3 Why this sits in the transfer module
chunks.excerpt:
- intentionally **altering, falsifying, forging or misrepresenting a document relating to real property**
  with intent to deceive, defraud, or unlawfully transfer or encumber the ownership rights of the owner;
- **misrepresenting oneself as the owner or the owner's authorised representative** in order to obtain
  ownership or possession; or
- with intent to defraud, **taking, obtaining, stealing or transferring title or ownership** by fraud,
  forgery, larceny or any other fraudulent or deceptive practice.

**The obligation is on the broker, at every closing, and the buyer signs.**

**This course states no wording or format for the notification**, because the Commission's implementing
rules and the form itself were not located in the publication read for this project. **Obtain the current
form from the Commission** and confirm the rules have issued before relying on any version of it.

**§ 858-307.2(F)** separately requires licensees to complete Commission-specified continuing education on
deed theft **on or before 1 November 2028.**

### 29.3 Why this sits in the transfer module

Because deed theft is a **transfer** crime. It attacks the same machinery this module has described —
delivery, acknowledgement, recording, authority to sign — and the defences against it are the same
disciplines: verify identity, verify authority, use the title company, and treat an unusual instruction
about how a conveyance is to be executed as a reason to slow down rather than a reason to hurry.

A licensee who has understood Hours 25 through 29 already knows what the notification is warning about.

### Module OK-05 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module OK-05
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items, delivered as in Module OK-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, from 605:10-5-3(f).

---

## Instructor source note for Module OK-05

Oklahoma citations in this module — 59 O.S. §§ 858-307.2, 858-351, 858-353 and 858-364, and 605:10-3-1
and 605:10-5-3 — were read on 2026-08-20 and are recorded in
`oklahoma/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this module:** Oklahoma's probate, descent and distribution,
recording, limitations, foreclosure and tax sale provisions; its power of attorney and trust statutes;
the Commission's rules implementing § 858-364 and the form of the deed theft notification; and the
Oklahoma Real Estate Contract Form Committee's promulgated forms. No period, threshold or figure from any
of them appears.
