chunks.excerpt:
# Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-09

## Hours 47–53 · Contract law overview, and contract law and performance

**Commission areas of study covered:** 605:10-3-1(a)(1)(L) Contract Law Overview · (M) Contract Law and
Performance
**Clock hours:** 7 · **Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Commission review;
605:10-3-1(a)(1) allocates no hours among its twenty-two areas of study.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Oklahoma pre-license credit is available.

> **The information presented in this course should not be used as a substitute for competent legal
> advice.** — 605:10-5-3(i)(6).

## Overview

Contract law as a licensee must know it: the elements, the classifications, the statute of frauds, the
life of an offer, and then performance — discharge, breach and remedies. The module closes on the
boundary between completing a form and drafting one, which in Oklahoma has a particular shape because
the state uses **promulgated contract forms** that this project has not read and therefore does not
describe.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: Timed sequence
chunks.excerpt:
1. Name the elements of a valid contract and identify which is missing from a defective fact pattern.
2. Distinguish valid, void, voidable and unenforceable.
3. Distinguish executory from executed, bilateral from unilateral, express from implied.
4. Explain the statute of frauds as it applies to real estate.
5. Trace an offer through acceptance, rejection, counter-offer, revocation and lapse.
6. Identify the moment a contract is formed and why every deadline runs from it.
7. Distinguish an amendment from a notice and use each correctly.
8. Explain genuine assent and the ways it fails.
9. Name the ways a contract is discharged.
10. Name the remedies for breach and explain why specific performance is available in real estate.
11. Distinguish assignment from novation and state who remains liable.
12. State the licensee's drafting boundary and route accordingly.
13. Relate offer handling to § 858-353(A)(2) and identify the written-waiver carve-out.

## Timed sequence

| Hour | Content | Instruction |
|---|---|---:|
| 47 | Elements of a valid contract | ≥50 min |
| 48 | Classifications; the statute of frauds | ≥50 min |
| 49 | Offer, acceptance, counter-offer; the date everything runs from | ≥50 min |
| 50 | Genuine assent and how it fails | ≥50 min |
| 51 | Performance and discharge | ≥50 min |
| 52 | Breach and remedies; assignment and novation | ≥50 min |
| 53 | The drafting boundary and Oklahoma's promulgated forms | ≥50 min |

---

## Hour 47 — Elements of a valid contract

### 47.1 The elements

A contract is a legally enforceable agreement to do or refrain from doing a legal act.

chunks.heading: 47.2 Where a licensee supplies the defect
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Offer and acceptance** — mutual assent. A definite offer and an unqualified acceptance of it.
2. **Consideration** — something of legal value exchanged. In a purchase contract the consideration is
   the **mutual promises**: the buyer promises to pay, the seller promises to convey. **Earnest money is
   not the consideration.**
3. **Legal capacity** — parties competent to contract. Minors, persons adjudicated incompetent, and
   persons acting under an inadequate power of attorney all raise capacity questions, and every one is a
   question for counsel and the title company.
4. **Lawful object** — a legal purpose. A contract to do something illegal is void.
5. **Genuine assent** — agreement not produced by fraud, misrepresentation, mistake, duress or undue
   influence. Hour 50.
6. **A writing**, for a conveyance of an interest in real estate, under the statute of frauds.

### 47.2 Where a licensee supplies the defect

One avoidable defect is at element 5: a false material representation may undermine genuine assent.
Do not infer a frequency claim or that every honestly attributed third-party figure is unlawful.
For area figures, 59 O.S. 858-515.1 specifically permits identified sources such as tax-assessor
records and imposes no independent verification duty; this is not a general immunity for other conduct.

Which is why **attribute or verify, never assert** is a contract-formation rule and not merely a
courtesy, and why § 858-312(2) makes substantial misrepresentations in the conduct of business a ground
for suspension or revocation.

---

## Hour 48 — Classifications and the statute of frauds

### 48.1 By validity

**Valid** — meets all elements and is enforceable.

chunks.heading: 48.2 By performance, promise and formation
chunks.excerpt:
**Void** — never had legal effect at all. There is nothing to enforce and nothing to disaffirm.

**Voidable** — **valid and binding unless and until** a party with the power to disaffirm elects to do
so. Consent induced by fraud may supply a ground for rescission under 15 O.S. 233. Do not apply the
generic "minor's contract is voidable" example to Oklahoma real-property transactions: **15 O.S. 17
restricts a minor's capacity to contract concerning real property**, except as specially provided by
statute. A judicial incapacity determination also raises 15 O.S. 24. Refer capacity questions to counsel.

**Unenforceable** — has the elements but cannot be enforced in court, typically because it is not in
writing or a limitation period has run.

**Void versus voidable is tested relentlessly.** Void is a nullity. Voidable is real and binding on at
least one party until the other gets out of it.

### 48.2 By performance, promise and formation

**Executory** — something remains to be done. A signed purchase contract before closing is executory.
**Executed** — fully performed. **Note the trap:** "executed" in this sense means *completed*, not
*signed*, and ordinary practice uses the word both ways.

**Bilateral** — a promise for a promise; both bound. A purchase contract. **Unilateral** — a promise for
an act; only the offeror is bound until someone performs. An **open listing** and an **option** are the
standard examples.

**Express** — stated in words. **Implied** — inferred from conduct.

### 48.3 The statute of frauds

chunks.heading: Hour 49 — Offer, acceptance, and the date everything runs from
chunks.excerpt:
**15 O.S. 136(4)** generally requires a writing subscribed by the party to be charged (or the party's
agent) for a sale of real property or an interest in it and for a lease **longer than one year**.
The same subsection requires written authority for an agent making such an agreement for that party.
The statute uses the word "invalid" for agreements within its rule; do not promise that every oral
land agreement has one automatic legal outcome without considering the facts and possible exceptions.
The writing must identify the essential agreement. Counsel determines enforceability where a writing,
signature, description or authority is disputed. The practical rule is to document terms and signatures
before relying on a covered agreement, not to assume an oral promise is an adequate substitute.

And in Oklahoma the practice rule has a statutory partner. **§ 858-353(A)(2)(b)** requires a broker to
**reduce offers or counteroffers to a written form upon request of any party to a transaction.** Not your
party. **Any** party.

---

## Hour 49 — Offer, acceptance, and the date everything runs from

### 49.1 Offer

A **definite proposal, communicated to the offeree, showing an intention to be bound on acceptance.**

An advertisement is generally **not** an offer; it is an invitation to make one — which is why a listing
at a price is not a promise to sell at that price.

An offer ends by:

- **Acceptance** — it becomes a contract.
- **Rejection** by the offeree.
- **Counter-offer**, which is a rejection plus a new offer.
- **Revocation** by the offeror **before acceptance is communicated**.
- **Lapse** — the stated time expires, or a reasonable time passes where none is stated.

**Death or incapacity** of a party before acceptance also terminates an offer.

### 49.2 Acceptance

chunks.heading: 49.3 The date everything runs from
chunks.excerpt:
Must be **unqualified** — the mirror image of the offer — and **communicated in the manner the offer
requires.**

**Signature and delivery are different events and may fall on different days.**

### 49.3 The date everything runs from

**Every deadline in the contract runs from the moment the contract is formed** — on most forms, the date
acceptance is **delivered**, not the date the last party signed.

**The discipline:** on the day acceptance is delivered, **write the date in the place the contract
provides, and compute every deadline from it that same day**, into the file and into your calendar. Then
work backwards from each deadline to the date the underlying work must **start** — an inspection deadline
is useless if the inspector is booked out ten days.

**A deadline miscounted from the wrong anchor shifts every subsequent date.** It is among the most common
and most avoidable failures in residential practice, and it is squarely a § 858-353(A)(1) reasonable
skill and care problem.

### 49.4 Counter-offers, and the multiple-offer problem

**A counter-offer rejects the original and substitutes a new one.** The original is dead and can no
longer simply be accepted.

So a seller with three offers cannot counter all three without destroying all three. Where the firm's
forms supply a **multiple counter-proposal** instrument reserving the right to accept only one, that is
the tool. **Where they do not, a licensee does not invent language to solve it** — Hour 53.

### 49.5 Three instruments, distinguished

chunks.heading: 49.6 And the Oklahoma offer-handling duty
chunks.excerpt:
- An **offer** or **counter-offer** proposes terms **before** there is a contract.
- An **amendment** changes a contract that **already exists** and requires the agreement of all parties.
- A **notice** exercises a right the contract **already gives** — removing a contingency, giving notice of
  a defect or of an inability to obtain financing. A notice is **unilateral**: no agreement needed, but
  the **form and the deadline the contract specifies** are.

**A buyer who "amends" when they should have given notice has asked permission for something they were
entitled to do**, and handed the other side a negotiation they did not have to have.

### 49.6 And the Oklahoma offer-handling duty

**§ 858-353(A)(2)**, to **all parties**, **unless specifically waived in writing by a party**:

**(a)** receive all written offers and counteroffers; **(b)** **reduce offers or counteroffers to a
written form upon request of any party**; **(c)** **present timely** all written offers and counteroffers.

**Nothing in it stops when the property goes under contract.** If a written offer arrives, it is received
and presented. What the seller then does about it is a legal question about their existing contract,
routed to counsel.

And the waiver is the **party's**, **specific**, and **in writing.** An oral "don't bring me lowballs" is
neither specific nor written.

---

## Hour 50 — Genuine assent and how it fails

### 50.1 The five failures

**Fraud** — a knowing or reckless misstatement of material fact, or active concealment, made to induce
reliance, and relied on.

**Misrepresentation** — a false statement of material fact. **Innocent** (believed true, on reasonable
grounds), **negligent** (made without reasonable care as to truth), or **fraudulent**.

chunks.heading: 50.2 The one licensees actually commit
chunks.excerpt:
**Mistake** — mutual, where both parties are wrong about a material fact; or unilateral, which rarely
avoids a contract.

**Duress** — assent compelled by wrongful threat.

**Undue influence** — assent obtained by improper pressure in a relationship of trust or dependence.

### 50.2 The one licensees actually commit

**Negligent misrepresentation, by repeating something without checking it.**

Square footage from a county record. Acreage from a prior listing. A school assignment that changed.
Zoning nobody confirmed. "The seller says the basement is dry." "The roof is about ten years old." A
flood zone read off a map rather than determined. A payment figure restated from a lender's estimate. A
net sheet presented as a promise.

**Attribute or verify. Never assert.**

### 50.3 Puffing, and where it stops

**Puffing** is obvious opinion nobody could reasonably rely on — *lovely home; wonderful light; you'll
love the kitchen.* Not actionable, because not a statement of fact.

**It stops the moment a statement is specific, factual and checkable.**

| Puffing | A statement of fact |
|---|---|
| "Great location" | "It's twelve minutes to the turnpike entrance" |
| "Beautiful lot" | "The lot is half an acre" |
| "Solid house" | "The roof was replaced in 2019" |
| "Plenty of room" | "It's 2,100 square feet" |
| "Won't last long" | "There are two other offers" |

**If you cannot show where the number came from, do not say it.**

### 50.4 And the guarantee that is a named ground

**§ 858-312(10)** makes it a ground for suspension or revocation to guarantee, or to authorise or permit
any licensee to guarantee, **future profits which may result from the resale of real estate.**

chunks.heading: Hour 51 — Performance and discharge
chunks.excerpt:
*"You'll make money on this."* *"This'll be worth $X in five years."* *"You can't lose."* Every one of
those is the conduct paragraph (10) names.

---

## Hour 51 — Performance and discharge

### 51.1 Performance

Most contracts end by **performance** — everyone does what they promised. In a real estate purchase that
is closing: the buyer pays, the seller conveys, the deed is delivered and recorded.

**Time is of the essence** where the contract says so, and where it does, a deadline missed is a breach
rather than a delay. Read whether the contract says so before assuming either way.

**Substantial performance** — performance meeting the essential purpose with minor deviations — may
suffice in some contexts and not in others. Whether it does in a given case is a legal question.

### 51.2 The ways a contract is discharged

- **Performance.**
- **Agreement** — mutual rescission; **novation**, substituting a party or an obligation; **accord and
  satisfaction**, agreeing to and performing a different obligation.
- **Operation of law** — bankruptcy; expiration of a limitation period; **destruction of the subject
  matter**; **impossibility**; illegality arising after formation.
- **Breach.**

### 51.3 Contingencies

A **contingency** is a condition that must be satisfied or waived before a party is obliged to perform.
**It is not a general right to change one's mind.**

Every contingency has **four** parts and all four must be read:

1. **The condition** — what must happen.
2. **The deadline** — by when.
3. **The method of notice** — how, in what form, delivered how.
4. **The effect of silence** — what happens if the deadline passes with no notice. Sometimes waiver,
   sometimes termination. **It depends entirely on the form**, and assuming is how transactions die.

chunks.heading: Hour 52 — Breach, remedies, assignment
chunks.excerpt:
**Contingencies fail through inattention, not through the condition.** The prevention is the calendar
work in Hour 49.3.

---

## Hour 52 — Breach, remedies, assignment

### 52.1 Breach

A failure to perform without legal excuse. **Material** breach goes to the essence and excuses the other
party's performance; **minor** breach sounds in damages only.

**Anticipatory breach** — a party states before performance is due that they will not perform — may allow
the other party to treat the contract as breached immediately.

### 52.2 The remedies

- **Compensatory damages** — money to put the injured party where performance would have.
- **Liquidated damages** — an amount the parties fixed in advance. In residential practice earnest money
  is frequently the agreed liquidated damages for a buyer's default, which is one reason the amount
  matters.
- **Specific performance** — a court order compelling the actual transfer. **Available in real estate
  because each parcel is unique**, so money may not make the injured party whole. This is Module OK-01's
  uniqueness characteristic doing legal work.
- **Rescission** — unwinding the contract and restoring the parties to their prior positions.
- **Reformation** — correcting a writing to reflect what the parties actually agreed.

**None of these is a licensee's to advise on.** A party asking what they can do about a breach is asking a
legal question. **What a licensee contributes is an accurate factual record of what happened and when** —
which is exactly what the file will be worth if it goes anywhere.

### 52.3 Assignment and novation

chunks.heading: 52.4 Earnest money on a failed contract
chunks.excerpt:
**Assignment** transfers rights under a contract. Unless the contract prohibits it or the duties are
personal, contract rights are generally assignable — **but the original party ordinarily remains liable.**

**Novation** substitutes a new party for an original one **and releases the original.** It requires the
consent of **all** parties.

**The practical difference is who can be sued when performance fails.** A buyer who assigns a purchase
contract and believes they have walked away usually has not. Only a novation does that, and a novation is
a document everyone signs.

### 52.4 Earnest money on a failed contract

**Its disposition is decided by what the contract provides and by the parties or a court — not by the
licensee.**

Two Oklahoma provisions bear. **§ 858-353(A)(3)** — timely account for all money and property received.
**§ 858-312(6)** — failing within a reasonable time to account for or remit monies belonging to others is
a ground for suspension or revocation. And **§ 858-312(16)** — commingling.

**This course states no Oklahoma escrow deadline or procedure**, because those provisions were not read
from primary text for this project. Read them and your broker's written procedures before you accept your
first cheque. **On any dispute: escalate to your broker immediately and do nothing else.**

---

## Hour 53 — The drafting boundary, and Oklahoma's promulgated forms

### 53.1 The boundary

**Inside the licence:** completing the forms your firm supplies by filling in the facts of the
transaction; selecting among the provisions the forms offer; explaining what a provision says in its
ordinary sense; and telling a party to get expert advice.

chunks.heading: 53.2 Oklahoma uses promulgated forms — and this course does not describe them
chunks.excerpt:
**Outside the licence:** composing new legal language to solve a party's specific legal problem; advising
which form of ownership to take title in; opining on the legal effect of a provision; drafting an
addendum to cover something the forms do not.

**When the forms do not fit, counsel drafts it and it is attached.** A licensee who composes a clause has
practised law — and has usually produced a clause that does not do what the party wanted.

### 53.2 Oklahoma uses promulgated forms — and this course does not describe them

**Oklahoma residential transactions are conducted on contract forms promulgated by the Oklahoma Real
Estate Contract Form Committee.** That is a fact about Oklahoma practice that a licensee must know.

**This project has not read those forms, and no document in this build reproduces, describes, paraphrases
or explains any of them or any of their provisions.** Not the contingency structures, not the deadlines,
not the earnest money provisions, not the notice mechanisms, not the default remedies.

**That is a real gap and it is named rather than filled.** Every structural statement in Hours 47 through
52 is general contract law from the body of pre-license knowledge. **How any of it is implemented in the
Oklahoma promulgated forms must be learned from the forms themselves**, from your broker, and from the
Commission — and it must be learned before you write your first offer.

### 53.3 What that means for you, practically

chunks.heading: 53.4 The one-page summary
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Get the current promulgated forms** and read every one of them, front to back, before you use one.
2. **Read them again when they change**, and they do change. Note that 605:10-5-3(k) requires all
   materials distributed to students to be **current and up-to-date with the License Code and Rules and
   state or federal laws** — the same currency discipline applies to the forms you practise on.
3. **Learn where each of Hour 51.3's four contingency elements lives in the form** — the condition, the
   deadline, the method of notice, the effect of silence.
4. **Never improvise.** If the form does not cover it, counsel drafts it.

### 53.4 The one-page summary

**Elements:** offer and acceptance, consideration, capacity, lawful object, genuine assent, writing.
**Validity:** valid, void, voidable, unenforceable. **Performance:** executory, executed.
**Offer ends by:** acceptance, rejection, counter-offer, revocation before communication of acceptance,
lapse. **A counter-offer kills the original.** **Deadlines run from formation.** **Discharge:**
performance, agreement, operation of law, breach. **Remedies:** damages, liquidated damages, specific
performance, rescission, reformation. **Assignment leaves you liable; novation does not.**

**And the Oklahoma overlay:** receive, reduce to writing on any party's request, and timely present all
written offers and counteroffers — § 858-353(A)(2) — unless a party specifically waives in writing.

### Module OK-09 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module OK-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, from 605:10-5-3(f).

---

## Instructor source note for Module OK-09

chunks.heading: Supplemental source review — 2026-09-06
chunks.excerpt:
Oklahoma citations in this module — 59 O.S. §§ 858-312 and 858-353, and 605:10-3-1 and 605:10-5-3 — were
read on 2026-08-20 and are recorded in `oklahoma/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Supplemental review on 2026-09-06:** Oklahoma Legislature Title 15, including capacity, consent,
formation, writing and rescission provisions, and the January 2026 OREC Residential Sale form were
read for the assessment repair. Sections 47.2, 48.1 and 48.3 above supersede the previous unqualified
tax-record, minor-capacity and oral-agreement statements. The assessment-source supplement identifies
the limited current-form terms taught; illustrative deadlines elsewhere are not promulgated deadlines.
No comprehensive limitations-period review or legal approval is claimed by this update.

<!-- OK-SOURCE-SUPPLEMENT:START -->

## Supplemental source review — 2026-09-06

This required reading clarifies the existing topics; no additional clock-hour credit or regulator approval is claimed.

### capacity

chunks.heading: writing
chunks.excerpt:
Related module 09, §47.1 and §48.1. A contract requires capable parties, consent, a lawful object and
consideration under 15 O.S. 2. Capacity is not established merely by a signature. Oklahoma's 15 O.S. 17
restricts a minor's power to contract about real property, except as specially provided. Under 15 O.S.
24, a judicially determined incapacity is not cured by an informal statement that the person now feels
competent; judicial restoration and the actual order matter. Do not import the generic claim that
every minor's real-property contract is simply voidable. Seek legal guidance on authority to sign.
A single unlawful contractual object is not made lawful by payment (15 O.S. 102–104). Fraud, duress
and qualifying mistake may undermine consent (15 O.S. 53, 58, 63); remedy and rescission depend on facts.

Sources: [Oklahoma Legislature, Title 15 — Contracts](https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os15.pdf).

### writing

Related module 09, §48.3. Under 15 O.S. 136(4), real-property sales and leases longer than one year
generally require a signed writing; agent authority for such an agreement must also be written.
For example, a proposed eighteen-month tenancy raises this writing requirement. This is not a rule
that every oral promise is enforceable or that every disputed oral transaction has the same remedy.
Read the actual agreement and refer exceptions and enforcement to counsel. Acceptance must conform
to the offer (15 O.S. 71). If the offer prescribes a particular method, evaluate compliance with that
method (15 O.S. 68); do not confuse a hypothetical receipt deadline with a universal receipt rule.
Section 69 addresses when properly transmitted consent is deemed communicated.

chunks.heading: electronic
chunks.excerpt:
An assignment transfers contractual rights; it does not by itself establish the original obligor's
release. A novation case expressly supplies substitution and release with required consent. That
distinction is taught as a contractual concept, not falsely attributed to an unrelated statutory
novation section. Written amendments record changed terms. Under 15 O.S. 237, a written contract can
also be altered by an executed oral agreement; that exception is not advice to rely on unperformed
oral changes. Stipulated damages require lawful entitlement, not simply a broker's preference. In
real-estate sales, 15 O.S. 215(B) distinguishes amounts at or below five percent of the price from
larger amounts whose reasonableness must be established. This is not an automatic right to disburse
escrow. Counsel resolves disputed remedies and the holder follows applicable escrow requirements.

Sources: [Oklahoma Legislature, Title 15 — Contracts](https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os15.pdf).

### electronic

Related module 09, §48.3. The January 2026 OREC Residential Sale form, printed page 1, states that
electronic signatures have the same force and effect as original signatures and permits identical
contract counterparts, including electronic copies. This is a
specific current-form term, not a claim that every electronic message forms a contract. The parties,
material terms, assent, signature and delivery still must be established. A screenshot of negotiations
does not substitute for the agreed executed instrument. Preserve the final version and its delivery
record. Never enter a signature for another person without authority.

chunks.heading: forms
chunks.excerpt:
Sources: [OREC Residential Sale, January 1, 2026](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/orec/documents/contracts-and-forms-page/2026-contract-forms/2026%20Residential%20Sale.pdf).

### forms

Related module 09, §53.2. The January 2026 Residential Sale PDF begins with a separate one-page
acknowledgment of disclosures, followed by the seven-page Residential Contract. Its first printed
contract page lists supplemental agreements and addenda to identify which are part of the agreement;
the listed or attached documents must be read together. The Parties clause makes signatures with
delivery to their respective brokers, if applicable, binding. It supersedes prior negotiations and
requires a further written agreement of buyer and seller for modification or assignment. Negotiation, counteroffer,
execution, delivery, notice, amendment and closing are distinct events. An addendum supplies terms;
an amendment changes existing terms; a notice communicates or exercises an existing right. In an
assessment that explicitly supplies a different deadline or clock convention, calculate from those
stated facts rather than inventing an OREC deadline.

OREC develops standardized forms for voluntary use under 59 O.S. 858-208(14). Availability of a form
does not make every form mandatory or make a licensee qualified to draft custom legal clauses. Select
the suitable current form, complete factual fields accurately, attach applicable documents and refer
unfamiliar legal drafting to counsel. Neither a published form nor a course draft is evidence that
StateCourse has provider, instructor or course approval.

chunks.heading: forms
chunks.excerpt:
Sources: [OREC Residential Sale, January 1, 2026](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/orec/documents/contracts-and-forms-page/2026-contract-forms/2026%20Residential%20Sale.pdf); [OREC License Code and Rules, as of November 1, 2025](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/orec/documents/meetings/Nov%201%202025%20Oklahoma%20Real%20Estate%20Commission%20Code%20and%20Rules%20Book.pdf).

chunks.heading: Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-10
chunks.excerpt:
# Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-10

## Hours 54–59 · Offers and purchase contracts

**Commission area of study covered:** 605:10-3-1(a)(1)(N) Offers and Purchase Contracts
**Clock hours:** 6 · **Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Commission review;
605:10-3-1(a)(1) allocates no hours among its twenty-two areas of study.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Oklahoma pre-license credit is available.

> **The information presented in this course should not be used as a substitute for competent legal
> advice.** — 605:10-5-3(i)(6).

## Overview

Module OK-09 covered contract law. This module covers the transaction: what a purchase contract must
settle, how offers are prepared and presented under § 858-353(A)(2), how contingencies are managed
through their deadlines, and what happens in a multiple-offer situation. It also covers earnest money,
which in Oklahoma carries three separate § 858-312 grounds a licensee should know before touching a
cheque.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: Timed sequence
chunks.excerpt:
1. Name the questions every purchase contract must settle.
2. Prepare an offer accurately, from sourced facts.
3. State the § 858-353(A)(2) offer-handling duty and its written-waiver carve-out.
4. Present an offer correctly and record that it was presented.
5. Manage a multiple-offer situation without breaching § 858-353(A)(4).
6. Identify the four elements of a contingency and diarise them.
7. Describe the common contingencies and what each actually protects.
8. State what earnest money is and is not.
9. Identify the § 858-312 grounds that govern earnest money handling.
10. State who decides a disputed earnest money disposition.
11. Handle a party's request to cancel correctly.
12. State the compensation disclosure timing § 858-353(A)(7) requires.

## Timed sequence

| Hour | Content | Instruction |
|---|---|---:|
| 54 | What a purchase contract must settle | ≥50 min |
| 55 | Preparing an offer | ≥50 min |
| 56 | Presenting offers, and § 858-353(A)(2) | ≥50 min |
| 57 | Multiple offers | ≥50 min |
| 58 | Contingencies and deadline management | ≥50 min |
| 59 | Earnest money | ≥50 min |

---

## Hour 54 — What a purchase contract must settle

Whatever form is used — and in Oklahoma that will be a promulgated form this course does not describe —
a residential purchase contract has to answer the same questions, and a licensee must be able to find
each of them:

chunks.heading: 54.1 Equitable title, and the gap
chunks.excerpt:
- **Parties.** Full legal names of everyone who must sign. Module OK-05 established this is not answered
  by looking at the deed.
- **Property.** The legal description, taken from the deed or supplied by the title company. **And in
  Oklahoma: whether the conveyance includes the mineral estate.**
- **Price, and how it will be paid** — cash, financing, or a combination, and the terms of the financing
  the buyer will seek.
- **Earnest money** — the amount, who holds it, when it is deposited, and what happens to it in each way
  the contract can end.
- **Included and excluded items** — the fixture discipline from Module OK-01, reduced to two lists.
- **Contingencies** — each with its condition, deadline, method of notice and effect of silence.
- **Title evidence** — abstract and attorney's opinion, or a title commitment and policy; who furnishes
  it, by when, and what happens if the buyer objects.
- **Closing date and possession.** **These are not the same date.** If they differ, the contract must say
  so, and possession before or after closing needs its own written agreement.
- **Prorations** — taxes, assessments, rents, association dues, and the basis for each.
- **Risk of loss** before closing.
- **Default and remedies** — what each party may do if the other fails.
- **Signatures and the date of acceptance.**

### 54.1 Equitable title, and the gap

Between formation and closing the buyer holds **equitable title** — a recognised interest in the property
— while the seller retains legal title. The contract allocates the **risk of casualty loss** in that
interval, and it should be read rather than assumed.

chunks.heading: Hour 55 — Preparing an offer
chunks.excerpt:
**Possession before closing** is a bad idea executed badly more often than it is a bad idea. If it must
happen it needs a separate written agreement addressing rent, insurance, utilities, damage, maintenance,
and what happens if the sale does not close. **A buyer already living in the house who cannot close is a
problem with no good solution.**

---

## Hour 55 — Preparing an offer

### 55.1 Fill nothing in from memory

- **Legal description** — from the deed or the title company. Not a tax record, not a prior listing.
- **Names** — from identification, spelled as they will be spelled on the deed.
- **Figures** — from the documents. Loan amount from the lender. Payoff from the payoff statement.
- **Dates** — computed, not estimated.

### 55.2 What the buyer must understand before signing

**What they are committing to**, in plain terms: the price, the deposit, the deadlines, and what happens
to their money in each way this can end.

**That a pre-approval is not a commitment**, which is why the financing contingency exists — Module OK-11.

**Their costs.** And this is not optional: **§ 858-353(B)(1)** requires the broker to **inform the party
in writing, when an offer is made, that the party will be expected to pay certain costs, brokerage
service costs and the approximate amount of the costs.** Module OK-08 supplies the arithmetic. **The
duty attaches when the offer is made** — not at closing, not when the buyer asks.

**And § 858-353(A)(7)**: compensation and fees disclosed **in writing before the effective date of the
contract**, with the compensation agreement's term **not exceeding one year** and **defaulting to sixty
days** if unstated.

### 55.3 What a licensee does not do

**Does not compose new legal language.** Module OK-09 Hour 53.

chunks.heading: Hour 56 — Presenting offers
chunks.excerpt:
**Does not advise on how to take title.** Legal and tax question.

**Does not predict what the seller will accept**, or characterise the other side's position beyond what
is known and disclosable.

---

## Hour 56 — Presenting offers

### 56.1 The duty — § 858-353(A)(2)

To **all parties**, mandatory and unwaivable except as the paragraph itself provides:

> **Unless specifically waived in writing by a party to the transaction:**
> **a.** receive all written offers and counteroffers,
> **b.** **reduce offers or counteroffers to a written form upon request of any party** to a transaction,
> and
> **c.** **present timely** all written offers and counteroffers.

**Three obligations. Read (b) again.** Upon request of **any party** — including a party you are not
serving, including an unrepresented buyer who walks up at an open house — you must reduce their offer or
counteroffer to written form.

**And the waiver is narrow:** it is the **party's**, it must be **specific**, and it must be **in
writing.** A seller who says "don't bother me below $250,000" has not waived anything.

### 56.2 Nothing here stops at contract

There is no language in § 858-353(A)(2) suspending the duty when the property goes under contract. **A
written offer that arrives is received and presented.** What the seller may lawfully do about it, given
their existing contract, is a legal question routed to counsel.

### 56.3 Presenting well

chunks.heading: 56.4 Communicating the response
chunks.excerpt:
- **Present promptly**, and confirm receipt to whoever submitted it.
- **Present all terms**, not just price. A cash offer at less, closing in fourteen days with no
  contingencies, may be worth more to a particular seller than a higher financed offer — and it is the
  seller's judgment to make, not yours.
- **Present the net.** Module OK-08's arithmetic, labelled as an estimate.
- **Record that you presented it**, with the date and time. If it ever matters, that record is the whole
  case.
- **Do not characterise the buyer.** Not their circumstances, not their family, not anything that would
  offend Module OK-13. Present the offer.

### 56.4 Communicating the response

Acceptance, rejection or counter-offer, communicated in the manner the offer requires, and confirmed in
writing.

**And § 858-353(B)(2) throughout: keep the party informed.** Silence between presentation and response is
where most complaints begin.

---

## Hour 57 — Multiple offers

### 57.1 The structural problem

**A counter-offer rejects the offer it responds to.** Countering three offers destroys all three. Where
the forms supply a multiple counter-proposal instrument reserving the right to accept only one, that is
the tool; where they do not, **a licensee does not invent one.**

### 57.2 What may be disclosed, and what may not

**§ 858-353(A)(4) is the controlling provision, and it is a closed list.** The **only** confidential
information in an Oklahoma transaction is:

chunks.heading: 57.3 A workable procedure
chunks.excerpt:
**(a)** that a party or prospective party **is willing to pay more or accept less** than what is being
offered; **(b)** that a party **is willing to agree to financing terms different from those offered**;
**(c)** **the motivating factors** of a party; and **(d)** **information specifically designated as
confidential by a party**, unless public.

So in a multiple-offer situation:

- **The terms of a competing offer are NOT on the confidential list** — unless the offering party
  specifically designated them confidential under (d), or unless disclosing them would reveal a listed
  item such as that buyer's willingness to pay more.
- **The seller's willingness to accept less IS on the list** — item (a) — and stays in, from everyone.
- **A buyer's willingness to pay more IS on the list** — item (a) — and stays in, from everyone,
  including your own seller if you are also serving that buyer.

**Knowing where the legal line is is not the same as practising up to it.** The seller decides what is
disclosed about the process, within those limits, and a licensee follows lawful instructions and records
them. What a licensee must never do is **misstate the situation** — inventing a competing offer, or
implying one exists when it does not, is a § 858-312(2) misrepresentation and a § 858-312(28) deceptive
practice.

### 57.3 A workable procedure

chunks.heading: Hour 58 — Contingencies and deadlines
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Agree the process with the seller in advance**, in writing: how offers will be handled, whether a
   deadline will be set, whether the existence or terms of other offers will be disclosed.
2. **Tell every submitting party what the process is**, consistently and identically.
3. **Present every written offer** — § 858-353(A)(2)(c).
4. **Record everything**: what was received, when, what was presented, when, what the seller instructed.
5. **Treat every party the same way.** Different handling by protected characteristic is a fair housing
   violation before it is anything else — Module OK-13.

---

## Hour 58 — Contingencies and deadlines

### 58.1 The four elements, again

**Condition. Deadline. Method of notice. Effect of silence.** All four are read before the contingency is
relied on, and the fourth differs by form.

### 58.2 The common contingencies

**Financing.** The buyer's obligation conditioned on obtaining a loan of a stated type and amount on
stated terms. **A pre-approval is not a commitment** — which is the whole reason this exists.

**Inspection.** The buyer may inspect within a period and then, depending on the form, object, request
repairs, or terminate. Note what it is **not**: a warranty of condition, a price renegotiation clause, or
a general escape — though it is used as the last of these constantly.

**Appraisal.** The property must appraise at or above a value for the lender's purposes. **A low
appraisal does not lower the price by itself**; it creates a gap someone must close — Module OK-07 Hour
41.4.

**Title.** The buyer may examine the abstract or commitment and object to defects within a period.

chunks.heading: 58.3 The method that prevents contingency failure
chunks.excerpt:
**Survey.** Where boundaries, encroachments and easements must be established — and the only way to remove
the survey exception from a title policy.

**Sale of the buyer's existing home.** The most fragile contingency in residential practice, because it
makes this transaction depend on another one nobody in the room controls.

**And in Oklahoma, worth naming: a mineral or oil-and-gas question.** Where the conveyance of minerals
matters to the buyer, that is settled in the contract and confirmed in the title work — not assumed.

### 58.3 The method that prevents contingency failure

1. On the day of acceptance, **write every deadline in the file and the calendar**, computed from that
   date.
2. **Work backwards** from each deadline to the date the underlying work must **start.**
3. **Confirm every notice in the form the contract requires**, and keep proof of delivery.
4. **When a deadline is at risk, raise it with the party BEFORE it passes, in writing.**

**This is what § 858-353(A)(1) reasonable skill and care and § 858-353(B)(2) keeping the party informed
look like in daily practice. It is almost entirely calendar work**, and it is the single highest-value
thing a residential licensee does.

---

## Hour 59 — Earnest money

### 59.1 What it is, and is not

**A deposit evidencing the buyer's good faith**, held pending closing and applied to the purchase price.

**It is not the consideration for the contract** — the mutual promises are. **It is not a fee.** **It is
not the licensee's or the broker's money at any point.** And a contract without earnest money is not
automatically invalid; it is a commercial feature, not an element of formation.

chunks.heading: 59.2 Three § 858-312 grounds, and one duty
chunks.excerpt:
Its functions: signalling seriousness, and constituting a fund from which a seller may be made whole on a
buyer's default — which is why many forms designate it as **liquidated damages**, and why the amount
matters.

### 59.2 Three § 858-312 grounds, and one duty

**§ 858-353(A)(3)** — **timely account for all money and property received.** A duty to **all parties**,
mandatory and unwaivable.

**§ 858-312(6)** — **failing, within a reasonable time, to account for or to remit any monies, documents,
or other property coming into possession of the licensee which belong to others.**

**§ 858-312(16)** — **commingling with the licensee's own money or property the money or property of
others**, unless received and held in **an escrow account that contains only money or property of
others.**

**§ 858-312(22)** — and this is the one licensees do not expect: **offering, loaning, paying, or making to
appear to have been paid, a down payment or earnest money deposit for a purchaser or seller.** Funding a
buyer's earnest money to save a transaction is not generosity. It is a named ground for suspension or
revocation.

### 59.3 The three rules

**One: it is other people's money from the moment it reaches your hands.** It goes to the broker for
handling under the firm's escrow procedures. It never touches an operating account.

**Two: you do not hold it.** Not uncashed in a drawer as a favour to a buyer waiting on a contingency.
Not over a weekend because the broker is away. If a buyer wants a later deposit, that is a **term of the
contract** to be negotiated in writing — not an informal arrangement with you.

chunks.heading: 59.4 A disputed disposition
chunks.excerpt:
**Three: you do not release it on request.** Not to a seller as a show of good faith. Not to a buyer who
changed their mind. Not on both parties saying it is fine, unless the release is documented as your
firm's procedures require.

**This course states no Oklahoma escrow deadline, threshold or procedure**, because those provisions were
not read from primary text for this project. **Read them and your broker's written procedures before you
accept your first cheque.**

### 59.4 A disputed disposition

**Not the licensee's decision, and not the broker's on their own judgment.** The questions are **what the
contract provides** and **what the parties or a court determine.**

**On any dispute: escalate to your broker immediately and do nothing else.** Releasing disputed funds on
your own judgment is a licence problem regardless of who turns out to have been right about the contract.

### 59.5 The routine

1. **Receive it and deliver it to the broker the same day**, following the firm's procedure exactly.
2. **Document** what you received, from whom, in what form, and when.
3. **Confirm the deposit to the buyer in writing.**
4. **Diarise** the deadline the contract sets for the deposit.
5. **On any dispute, escalate.**

### Module OK-10 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module OK-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, from 605:10-5-3(f).

chunks.heading: Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-11
chunks.excerpt:
# Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-11

## Hours 60–67 · Financing real estate

**Commission area of study covered:** 605:10-3-1(a)(1)(O) Financing Real Estate
**Clock hours:** 8 — the largest allocation in this course after Law of Agency · **Hour allocation:** a
StateCourse proposal for Commission review; 605:10-3-1(a)(1) allocates no hours among its twenty-two
areas of study.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Oklahoma pre-license credit is available.

> **The information presented in this course should not be used as a substitute for competent legal
> advice.** — 605:10-5-3(i)(6).

## Overview

How a residential purchase is paid for, and the arithmetic a licensee must be able to do. The module
covers underwriting and the qualifying ratios, the note and the security instrument and the clauses that
decide outcomes, the loan programme categories, default and its alternatives, the secondary market, and
the mathematics — loan-to-value, points, interest, amortisation, and the calculations Commission topic
(H) and this module share.

Throughout, one boundary holds: **a licensee explains structures and routes pricing.**

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: Timed sequence
chunks.excerpt:
1. Describe what underwriting examines and compute both qualifying ratios.
2. Distinguish pre-qualification, pre-approval and commitment and explain the financing contingency.
3. Distinguish the note from the security instrument and state what each does.
4. Name the clauses that decide outcomes and explain each.
5. Distinguish assumption with a release from taking subject to.
6. Describe each loan programme category structurally without recommending one.
7. Distinguish fixed from adjustable and compute an ARM's worst case from its caps.
8. Describe default and the alternatives to foreclosure at the level of principle.
9. Explain the secondary market and what a borrower actually experiences from it.
10. Compute loan-to-value, down payment and the effect of a low appraisal.
11. Compute points, simple interest and a commission split.
12. Read an amortisation schedule and explain why early payments are mostly interest.
13. State what a licensee may and may not say about financing.
14. Identify the § 858-312 grounds that bear on financing conduct.

## Timed sequence

| Hour | Content | Instruction |
|---|---|---:|
| 60 | Underwriting and the qualifying ratios | ≥50 min |
| 61 | Pre-qualification, pre-approval, commitment, and the contingency | ≥50 min |
| 62 | The note, the security instrument, and the clauses | ≥50 min |
| 63 | Loan programme categories | ≥50 min |
| 64 | Rate and payment structures | ≥50 min |
| 65 | Default, foreclosure, and the alternatives | ≥50 min |
| 66 | The secondary market | ≥50 min |
| 67 | Real estate mathematics | ≥50 min |

---

## Hour 60 — Underwriting

### 60.1 The four Cs

**Capacity** — can the borrower repay from income? The ratios below.

**Credit** — have they repaid before? Score, and the record behind it.

chunks.heading: 60.2 The ratios
chunks.excerpt:
**Capital** — what do they have for down payment, closing costs and reserves, **and where did it come
from?** Sourcing and seasoning of funds are real underwriting steps and they surprise buyers who were
gifted money last week.

**Collateral** — is the property worth enough and acceptable as security? Where the appraisal enters —
Module OK-07.

### 60.2 The ratios

**Housing ratio** = proposed monthly housing payment ÷ gross monthly income. The housing payment is
**PITI** — principal, interest, taxes and insurance — plus mortgage insurance and any association dues.

**Total debt ratio** = housing payment plus all other recurring monthly obligations ÷ gross monthly
income. Car payments, student loans, minimum card payments, court-ordered support.

*Worked.* Gross monthly income $6,800. Proposed PITI $1,564. Car $385, student loan $240, card minimums
$95.

Housing ratio: 1,564 ÷ 6,800 = **23.0%.**
Total obligations: 1,564 + 385 + 240 + 95 = 2,284. Total debt ratio: 2,284 ÷ 6,800 = **33.6%.**

**The thresholds are the lender's and the programme's, not the licensee's.** They differ by programme,
they move, and they yield to compensating factors and automated underwriting decisions no licensee sees.
**A licensee who quotes a qualifying ratio as a rule has stated an underwriting standard as law.**

---

## Hour 61 — Pre-qualification, pre-approval, commitment

**Pre-qualification** — an estimate from information the borrower stated. Nothing verified.

**Pre-approval** — follows verification and underwriting of the borrower. Stronger, and still conditional.

**Commitment** — the lender's actual undertaking to lend, on conditions.

**Neither pre-qualification nor pre-approval is a commitment.**

chunks.heading: 61.1 What can still go wrong after pre-approval
chunks.excerpt:
**That gap is the entire reason the financing contingency exists.** A buyer who believes a pre-approval is
a promise will not understand why the contingency matters, will resent the seller's anxiety about it, and
will be blindsided if underwriting turns.

**Say it at the beginning, plainly:** *this is what the lender expects today, based on what has been
verified; the commitment comes later; the contingency protects you until it does.*

### 61.1 What can still go wrong after pre-approval

New debt taken on before closing. A change of employment. A credit inquiry. A large unexplained deposit.
A gift that was not documented. The **property** failing — appraisal, condition, insurability, or a
condominium project the lender will not lend on.

**Tell the buyer, in writing, at the beginning:** do not buy a car, do not open credit accounts, do not
change jobs, do not move money around, until after closing. That advice costs nothing and saves
transactions.

### 61.2 The contingency

Four elements — **condition, deadline, method of notice, effect of silence.** Module OK-10 Hour 58.

**The licensee's job is calendar work:** the application deadline, the loan-commitment deadline, the date
the appraisal must be ordered, and the point at which a slipping date must be raised in writing.

---

## Hour 62 — The note, the security instrument, and the clauses

### 62.1 Two documents, two jobs

The **promissory note** is the borrower's promise to repay — **the debt**. Amount, rate, term, payment,
consequences of default.

The **security instrument** pledges the property as security — **the lien**. Without it the lender has a
promise and no property; without the note, a lien securing nothing.

chunks.heading: 62.2 The clauses that decide outcomes
chunks.excerpt:
Two forms exist across the United States. A **mortgage** is a two-party instrument enforced by
**judicial** foreclosure. A **deed of trust** is a three-party instrument — borrower, lender, and a
**trustee** holding a **power of sale** — typically enforced **non-judicially.**

**Oklahoma practice uses the mortgage, and Oklahoma foreclosure is predominantly JUDICIAL** — a court
proceeding rather than a trustee's sale. That is a real structural difference from neighbouring states,
and it changes the timetable.

**This course states no Oklahoma foreclosure timetable, notice requirement, redemption right, deficiency
rule or election-of-remedies provision**, because Oklahoma's foreclosure provisions were not read from
primary text for this project. **The structural fact — judicial foreclosure — is what a licensee carries;
every specific is routed to counsel.**

### 62.2 The clauses that decide outcomes

**Acceleration.** On default, the lender may declare the entire balance immediately due. Without it,
default would mean suing over each missed payment.

**Alienation, or due-on-sale.** On transfer of the property, the lender may call the balance. **This is
why "taking subject to" an existing loan is not a workaround a licensee arranges**, and why **assumption
requires the lender's consent.**

**Prepayment.** Whether early repayment is permitted and on what terms.

**Escrow, or impound.** The lender collects taxes and insurance monthly and pays them when due. **This is
why the payment is PITI**, and why an **escrow analysis can change a payment after closing without the
rate having moved** — warn buyers, because it arrives as a shock otherwise.

**Subordination.** An agreement that a lien takes a lower priority than it otherwise would.

chunks.heading: 62.3 Assumption, subject to, release
chunks.excerpt:
**Release, or partial release.** Releasing part of the security as principal is repaid — used in
subdivision and land development lending.

**Defeasance.** The clause under which the lien is discharged on full repayment.

### 62.3 Assumption, subject to, release

**Assumption with the lender's written release** — the buyer takes over the loan and **the seller is off
the obligation.**

**Assumption without a release** — the buyer pays; **the seller remains liable** for a loan on a house
they no longer own.

**Taking subject to** — the buyer makes payments without assuming the obligation. The seller remains
fully liable and the alienation clause is generally triggered by the transfer.

**A licensee explains these structures and routes the decision to counsel. A licensee does not arrange
them.**

---

## Hour 63 — Loan programme categories

**Conventional.** Not insured or guaranteed by a government agency. Below a threshold down payment the
lender requires **private mortgage insurance**, which **protects the lender, not the borrower** — buyers
consistently believe otherwise and telling them is a genuine service — and which can generally be removed
once equity conditions are met.

**FHA-insured.** Insured by the Federal Housing Administration. Lower down payment requirements, mortgage
insurance premiums on their own terms, and **property condition standards applied through the
appraisal**, which can affect whether a particular house qualifies at all.

**VA-guaranteed.** For eligible veterans and service members. Typically no down payment, a **funding fee**
in place of monthly mortgage insurance, and its own appraisal and property requirements.

chunks.heading: 63.1 The rule that governs the hour
chunks.excerpt:
**USDA rural development.** For eligible properties in eligible areas with eligible borrowers. **Relevant
across a great deal of Oklahoma**, and worth knowing whether a given address qualifies before a buyer
falls in love with it.

**State and local assistance programmes** — down payment assistance, first-time buyer and bond
programmes. **This course states no eligibility criterion, income limit or purchase price limit for any
Oklahoma programme**, because none was read from primary source for this project. Routed to the
administering agency and the lender.

**Seller financing**, including the **land contract or contract for deed**, in which the buyer takes
possession and equitable title while the seller retains legal title until the payments are complete.
**This is the arrangement in which a buyer has the least protection**, the consequences of default are a
legal question with real stakes, and **a licensee explains the structure and routes the decision to
counsel.**

### 63.1 The rule that governs the hour

**A licensee explains structures and routes pricing.**

Which programme is cheapest for a particular borrower depends on rate, term, mortgage insurance
treatment, fees, tax position and holding period. A licensee controls none of those and knows some of
them not at all.

**Naming the categories is education. Recommending one is advice a licensee is not licensed to give.**

---

## Hour 64 — Rate and payment structures

**Fixed rate.** The rate does not change for the life of the loan.

**Adjustable rate.** An **index plus a margin**, adjusting on a schedule, with **caps** on the periodic
adjustment and on the **lifetime** rate.

chunks.heading: Hour 65 — Default, foreclosure, and the alternatives
chunks.excerpt:
*Worked.* A 5/1 ARM at 5.75% start, index plus 2.75 margin, caps 2/2/5. First adjustment may rise at most
2 points to **7.75%**; each later adjustment at most 2 points; the **lifetime cap of 5** puts the maximum
possible rate at **10.75%.**

**A buyer considering an ARM needs the worst case, not the teaser — and the worst case is computable from
the caps.** Compute it and put it in writing.

**Interest-only** — payments cover interest only for a period, after which the payment rises sharply.

**Balloon** — a large sum falls due on a stated date. **A buyer who has not diarised that date has a
problem waiting for them.**

**Graduated payment** — payments start low and rise on a schedule.

**Biweekly** — half a payment every two weeks, producing thirteen monthly equivalents a year and shortening
the term.

---

## Hour 65 — Default, foreclosure, and the alternatives

### 65.1 Default and acceleration

**Default** is failure to perform under the note or the security instrument — most often non-payment, but
also failure to pay taxes, failure to insure, or waste.

**Acceleration** makes the whole balance due, and it is what makes foreclosure practical.

### 65.2 Foreclosure

**Oklahoma foreclosure is predominantly judicial** — a court proceeding culminating in a sheriff's sale.

**This course states no Oklahoma timetable, notice requirement, redemption right or deficiency rule**,
because those provisions were not read from primary text for this project. **Every one of them is routed
to counsel**, and a licensee who states one from memory or from another state's practice will state it
wrongly.

chunks.heading: 65.3 The alternatives
chunks.excerpt:
**What a licensee must understand structurally:** a foreclosure extinguishes the interests junior to the
lien being foreclosed and leaves senior ones in place; a purchaser at such a sale takes subject to what
survived; and title after a foreclosure is a title question for the title company and counsel.

### 65.3 The alternatives

**Reinstatement** — curing the default and restoring the loan.

**Forbearance or modification** — agreements with the lender to change the terms.

**Deed in lieu of foreclosure** — conveying voluntarily to the lender. **It does not automatically
eliminate junior liens**, which is why lenders often refuse it.

**Short sale** — the lender agrees to accept less than the balance. It is a lender approval process with
its own timetable and its own tax and credit consequences.

**A licensee working a distressed file identifies the questions and routes them.** The seller's deficiency
exposure, tax position and credit consequences go to **counsel and an accountant** — every one of them,
every time. Section 858-353(A)(1) requires honesty and reasonable skill and care; guessing at any of
these is neither.

---

## Hour 66 — The secondary market

### 66.1 Primary and secondary

The **primary market** is where loans are made. The **secondary market** is where they are bought and sold
after origination.

It exists because it **returns capital to originators**, who can lend again. Without it, a lender's
capacity would be limited to its own balance sheet, and thirty-year fixed-rate lending at scale would not
exist.

### 66.2 What a borrower actually experiences

chunks.heading: Hour 67 — Real estate mathematics
chunks.excerpt:
**Standardisation.** Originators write to the purchaser's guidelines, which is why underwriting looks
broadly similar across lenders, why documentation requirements feel identical, and **why an unusual
property or an unusual borrower is harder to finance than the numbers alone suggest.**

**Servicing transfer.** The right to collect payments is an asset and is bought and sold. A borrower may
make their first payment to one company and their second to another they never chose. **Tell buyers this
will probably happen and that it does not change their loan terms** — otherwise the notice arrives looking
like a scam.

**Rate transmission.** Mortgage rates track the yields investors demand on mortgage-backed securities more
closely than any single policy rate, which is why mortgage rates sometimes move opposite to the direction
a news story implies. **It is also why a licensee does not forecast them.**

---

## Hour 67 — Real estate mathematics

### 67.1 The one relationship

> **Part = Whole × Rate**

Rearranged: Rate = Part ÷ Whole. Whole = Part ÷ Rate. **Nearly every commission, interest, appreciation,
ratio and profit problem on any examination is this relationship in a costume.**

### 67.2 Loan-to-value and the low appraisal

**LTV = loan amount ÷ the LESSER of price or appraised value.**

*Worked.* Price $268,000, appraised $268,000, 10 percent down. Down payment 268,000 × 0.10 = **$26,800**;
loan **$241,200**; LTV 241,200 ÷ 268,000 = **90%.**

chunks.heading: 67.3 Points and interest
chunks.excerpt:
*Worked, low appraisal.* Same price, appraisal **$256,000**. The lender lends 90 percent **of the lesser
figure**: 256,000 × 0.90 = **$230,400.** The buyer now needs 268,000 − 230,400 = **$37,600** in cash, not
$26,800. **A $12,000 appraisal gap became a $10,800 cash problem.** That is what the appraisal contingency
exists to handle.

### 67.3 Points and interest

**A point is one percent of the LOAN AMOUNT**, not the price. Get that wrong and every points problem is
wrong.

*Worked.* 1.25 points on $241,200: 241,200 × 0.0125 = **$3,015.**

**Simple annual interest = principal × rate.** Monthly = ÷ 12.

*Worked.* $241,200 at 6.5%: annual 241,200 × 0.065 = $15,678. Monthly 15,678 ÷ 12 = **$1,306.50.**

### 67.4 Amortisation

The payment is constant; its **composition** changes every month. Interest is computed on the **current**
balance; the remainder reduces principal; the balance falls; next month's interest is smaller.

*Worked, first three months.* $241,200 at 6.5%, monthly payment $1,524.53.

| Month | Interest | Principal | Ending balance |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 241,200 × .065 ÷ 12 = **1,306.50** | 218.03 | 240,981.97 |
| 2 | 240,981.97 × .065 ÷ 12 = **1,305.32** | 219.21 | 240,762.76 |
| 3 | 240,762.76 × .065 ÷ 12 = **1,304.13** | 220.40 | 240,542.36 |

**Three payments totalling $4,573.59 reduced the balance by $657.64.** That is not a defect; it is what
amortisation is. A buyer who understands it will not be shocked by their first annual statement, and
explaining it is genuinely useful.

### 67.5 Commission

*Worked.* Sale price $268,000, total compensation 6 percent, split evenly between two firms, and the
associate's agreement with their broker is 60/40 in the associate's favour.

chunks.heading: 67.6 Area and per-unit
chunks.excerpt:
Total: 268,000 × 0.06 = **$16,080.** Listing broker: ÷ 2 = **$8,040.** Associate: 8,040 × 0.60 =
**$4,824.** The broker retains $3,216.

**Compensation is negotiable and is set by no board, association, listing service or rule.** And
**§ 858-312(4)**: an associate may accept compensation **only from the broker with whom the associate is
associated.**

### 67.6 Area and per-unit

Rectangle: length × width. Triangle: ½ × base × height. Irregular: divide, compute, add.

**1 acre = 43,560 sq ft. 1 section = 640 acres. 1 mile = 5,280 ft.**

*Worked.* A house of 46 × 28 feet with a 24 × 22 addition: 1,288 + 528 = **1,816 sq ft.** At $152 per
square foot of construction cost: 1,816 × 152 = **$276,032.**

### 67.7 What a licensee may and may not say

**May:** explain what the categories are and how they differ structurally; explain what the ratios
measure; explain the difference between pre-qualification, pre-approval and commitment; insist the buyer
speak to a lender early; explain what a rate lock is and that it expires; compute and explain the
arithmetic above.

**May not:** recommend a programme as cheapest; **compute a payment and give it to the buyer as their
payment**; quote a rate; predict what rates will do; characterise what a lender will approve; or —
**§ 858-312(10)** — guarantee future profits from resale.

### Module OK-11 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module OK-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, from 605:10-5-3(f).

---

## Instructor source note for Module OK-11

chunks.heading: Supplemental source review — 2026-09-06
chunks.excerpt:
Oklahoma citations in this module — 59 O.S. §§ 858-312 and 858-353, and 605:10-3-1 and 605:10-5-3 — were
read on 2026-08-20 and are recorded in `oklahoma/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this module:** Oklahoma's foreclosure provisions and every
timetable, notice, redemption, deficiency and election-of-remedies rule in them; Oklahoma's land contract
provisions; the eligibility rules of every state and local assistance programme; and RESPA, TILA and
their implementing regulations in their own text. **That Oklahoma foreclosure is predominantly judicial is
stated as a structural fact of Oklahoma practice, and every specific consequence of it is routed to

market or rate data.**

## Supplemental source review — 2026-09-06

This required reading clarifies the existing topics; no additional clock-hour credit or regulator approval is claimed.

### finance

Related module 11, §63.1. A conventional mortgage is not insured or guaranteed by a federal housing
program. This does not mean every conventional loan has identical down-payment, insurance or credit
rules. FHA insures eligible mortgages and VA guarantees a portion of eligible loans; neither label
eliminates lender underwriting or guarantees approval. Eligibility is not the same as affordability.

chunks.heading: finance
chunks.excerpt:
For the stated hypothetical, loan-to-value equals loan divided by value, and a payment-to-income ratio
equals the specified monthly housing payment divided by gross monthly income. Use the value and
cost definitions provided; do not invent a universal qualification threshold. A discount point is one
percent of the loan amount. Compare upfront points with the quoted periodic savings and expected
holding period; a simple break-even calculation excludes time value and future refinance risk unless
the question includes them. Interest is calculated on the applicable outstanding principal, while
principal reduction builds equity. Mortgage insurance protects the lender from a covered loss; it is
not a homeowner warranty or a promise to forgive borrower debt. Sources: CFPB conventional, FHA, VA,
points and amortization explainers listed in the source manifest.

Sources: [CFPB — What is a conventional loan?](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-conventional-loan-en-117/); [CFPB — What is an FHA loan?](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-an-fha-loan-en-112/); [CFPB — What is a VA loan?](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-va-loan-en-113/); [CFPB — Lender credits and points](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-should-i-use-lender-credits-and-points-also-called-discount-points-en-136/); [CFPB — How paying down a mortgage works](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-does-paying-down-a-mortgage-work-en-1943/).
