chunks.heading: Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-12
chunks.excerpt:
# Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-12

## Hours 68–72 · Closing a transaction

**Commission area of study covered:** 605:10-3-1(a)(1)(P) Closing a Transaction
**Clock hours:** 5 · **Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Commission review;
605:10-3-1(a)(1) allocates no hours among its twenty-two areas of study.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Oklahoma pre-license credit is available.

> **The information presented in this course should not be used as a substitute for competent legal
> advice.** — 605:10-5-3(i)(6).

## Overview

What happens between contract and keys, who does each part of it, and what a licensee's actual role is —
which is narrower and more useful than new licensees expect. The module covers the closing sequence, the
settlement statement, the walkthrough, federal disclosure timing, and the two Oklahoma obligations that
attach at or before closing: the § 858-353(A)(3) accounting duty and the § 858-364 deed theft
notification.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: Timed sequence
chunks.excerpt:
1. Describe the closing sequence in order and identify who performs each step.
2. State what a licensee does at closing and what they must not do.
3. Read a settlement statement against the contract and identify a discrepancy.
4. Distinguish a debit from a credit on each side of a settlement statement.
5. Explain the purpose of the final walkthrough and what it is not.
6. State what RESPA section 8 and section 9 prohibit.
7. State the TRID three-business-day rule and the licensee's part in protecting it.
8. Describe what happens after closing — recording, funding, disbursement.
9. State the § 858-364 deed theft notification obligation and route its form.
10. Apply § 858-353(A)(3) and § 858-312(6) to post-closing accounting.
11. Identify what can delay a closing and raise it in time.
12. Explain what a licensee says when a closing will not happen on time.

## Timed sequence

| Hour | Content | Instruction |
|---|---|---:|
| 68 | The closing sequence, and who does what | ≥50 min |
| 69 | The settlement statement | ≥50 min |
| 70 | The walkthrough, and what delays closings | ≥50 min |
| 71 | RESPA, TRID, and the licensee's part | ≥50 min |
| 72 | At and after closing: recording, accounting, deed theft | ≥50 min |

---

## Hour 68 — The closing sequence

### 68.1 What closing is

The simultaneous exchange in which the buyer's funds and the seller's deed change hands and the
instruments are recorded. In Oklahoma practice it is customarily conducted by a **title company or closing
agent**, and it may be conducted with the parties present or in escrow.

### 68.2 The steps, in order

chunks.heading: 68.3 Who does what
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Title work ordered and examined.** The abstract brought current and examined, or the title commitment
   issued. Module OK-04.
2. **Schedule B-I requirements cleared** — payoffs and releases, corrective instruments, evidence of
   authority, probate, judgments.
3. **Buyer's inspections completed** and any repair agreement reached, within the contingency deadlines.
4. **Appraisal completed** and any valuation issue resolved.
5. **Loan underwriting completed** and a clear-to-close issued.
6. **Closing Disclosure delivered** — and the three-business-day clock starts. Hour 71.
7. **Settlement statement prepared** and reviewed against the contract.
8. **Final walkthrough** by the buyer.
9. **Signing.**
10. **Funding.**
11. **Recording** of the deed and the security instrument.
12. **Disbursement**, including payoff of the seller's loans and payment of compensation.

**Note the order of 10, 11 and 12.** Money does not become the seller's until it is disbursed, and title
is not protected until it is recorded.

### 68.3 Who does what

**The closing agent or title company** prepares the settlement statement, handles funds, records the
instruments and issues the policy. **The lender** funds and sets its own conditions. **Counsel** advises
on legal questions and drafts anything needing drafting. **The abstractor** brings the abstract current
where one is used.

**The licensee does none of those things.**

### 68.4 What the licensee actually does

chunks.heading: Hour 69 — The settlement statement
chunks.excerpt:
- **Makes sure everyone has what they need before the day.**
- **Reviews the settlement statement against the contract** for the items the contract allocated — the
  prorations, the credits, the agreed repairs, the compensation — and **raises any discrepancy before
  signing.**
- **Attends**, where the parties want them there.
- **Declines to answer questions that belong to the closing agent, the lender or counsel.**

That last one is the discipline most often broken. A buyer at a closing table asking "what does this
paragraph mean" is asking the closing agent or counsel, not you.

---

## Hour 69 — The settlement statement

### 69.1 Debits and credits

A **credit** to a party is money in their favour. A **debit** is money against them.

**Buyer's side.** Debits: the purchase price, the buyer's closing costs, prepaid items, escrow deposits,
and the buyer's share of anything the seller prepaid. Credits: the loan amount, the earnest money already
deposited, seller concessions, and prorated items paid in arrears that the buyer will pay later. **The
difference is cash to close.**

**Seller's side.** Credits: the sale price, and prorated items the seller prepaid. Debits: loan payoffs
with per-diem interest, brokerage service compensation, the seller's closing costs, agreed credits to the
buyer, and prorated items paid in arrears. **The difference is net proceeds.**

**Every prorated item appears twice** — a credit to one party and a debit to the other — and the two must
match.

### 69.2 What to check, in order

chunks.heading: 69.3 When something is wrong
chunks.excerpt:
1. **The parties and the property.** Names spelled as they will be on the deed; the legal description
   matching the contract and the commitment.
2. **The price.**
3. **The earnest money**, credited to the buyer in the amount actually deposited.
4. **Every prorated item**: the annual figure, the basis, the closing-day convention, the day count, and
   the direction. Module OK-08 Hour 43.
5. **Every credit the contract created** — repair credits, closing-cost concessions.
6. **The payoff**, and its good-through date against the closing date.
7. **The compensation**, against the brokerage agreement.
8. **The totals.**

**Do this before the parties sit down**, not while they are signing.

### 69.3 When something is wrong

Raise it with the closing agent, in writing where there is time, **before signing.** A discrepancy caught
before signing is a correction. The same discrepancy caught after is a dispute.

**And do not fix it yourself.** The settlement statement is the closing agent's document.

---

## Hour 70 — The walkthrough, and what delays closings

### 70.1 The final walkthrough

**What it is:** a confirmation that the property is in the agreed condition, that agreed repairs were
made, that the included items are still there, and that the excluded items are gone.

**What it is not:** an inspection. Not a second chance to discover defects. Not a renegotiation.

**Do it as close to closing as the contract allows** — a walkthrough three days early misses what happens
in the last three days, which is when the seller moves out.

**What buyers actually find:** items that were supposed to convey and are gone; damage from moving;
utilities shut off; agreed repairs done badly or not at all; a garage full of things nobody removed.

chunks.heading: 70.2 What delays closings
chunks.excerpt:
**What a licensee does with a problem:** document it — photographs, in writing, immediately — tell the
other side's broker and the closing agent at once, and route the remedy to the contract and, if it is
disputed, to counsel. **Do not agree on the buyer's behalf to a holdback, a credit or a repair
arrangement.** Those are the parties' decisions and usually the closing agent's mechanics.

### 70.2 What delays closings

In rough order of frequency:

- **Title requirements nobody started** — a release, an heirship affidavit, a judgment to clear. Module
  OK-04.
- **Underwriting conditions** — a document the borrower has not produced, a deposit not sourced, an
  employment verification.
- **The appraisal** — late, or low. Module OK-07.
- **Repairs** — agreed late, scheduled late, done late, or done by someone whose invoice arrives after
  closing.
- **Survey**, ordered late.
- **Insurance**, not bound — which in parts of Oklahoma can be a real problem rather than a formality,
  and is worth starting early.
- **A TRID redisclosure**, triggered by a late change. Hour 71.
- **Probate or entity authority**, unresolved. Module OK-05.
- **The other transaction**, where a party's purchase depends on their own sale closing first.

### 70.3 What a licensee says when a closing will slip

**Immediately, in writing, to the party they serve** — § 858-353(B)(2), keep the party informed — with:
what the cause is; who is working on it; what the realistic new date is; and what the contract says about
the consequences, routed to counsel where it matters.

**What a licensee does not do is wait and hope.** A closing that slips is a problem. A closing that slips
and nobody was told is a complaint.

---

## Hour 71 — RESPA, TRID, and the licensee's part

### 71.1 RESPA

chunks.heading: 71.2 TRID
chunks.excerpt:
The **Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act** governs settlement services on most federally related
residential mortgage loans. Two prohibitions matter directly:

**Section 8** prohibits **kickbacks and unearned fees** for the referral of settlement service business. A
payment, a thing of value, or a fee for a service not actually performed, in exchange for referrals, is
prohibited. **This is the provision that ends careers**, and it does not require anyone to have intended
anything corrupt.

**Section 9** prohibits a **seller from requiring the buyer to use a particular title company** as a
condition of sale.

RESPA also requires disclosure of **affiliated business arrangements** — where the licensee or the firm
has an ownership interest in a settlement service provider they refer business to. The interest is
disclosed in writing, and the consumer is told they are not required to use the affiliate.

**The Oklahoma parallel.** § 858-312(21) makes it a ground to pay any part of a fee, commission or other
valuable consideration **to any person not licensed**, and § 858-312(14) to pay compensation to any person
performing the services of a licensee who has not secured a licence. **Referral arrangements are a place
where a licensee can breach federal law and state licence law with the same act.**

**This course states no dollar threshold, fee tolerance or exemption under RESPA**, because neither the
statute nor Regulation X was read from primary text for this project.

### 71.2 TRID

The **TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure** rule requires:

- the **Loan Estimate**, delivered within **three business days of application**; and
- the **Closing Disclosure**, which the consumer must receive **at least three business days before
  consummation.**

chunks.heading: 71.3 The licensee's part in TRID: protect the timeline
chunks.excerpt:
**Certain changes restart that three-day period.**

### 71.3 The licensee's part in TRID: protect the timeline

**Late-breaking changes move closing dates.** A repair credit agreed two days before closing. A change in
the loan amount. A concession added at the last minute.

**Getting changes decided early and telling the lender promptly is a real service and costs nothing.**
When a change is unavoidable late, tell the party in writing what it may do to the date — before they
plan a move around it.

---

## Hour 72 — At and after closing

### 72.1 Recording

The deed and the security instrument are recorded, giving **constructive notice to the world.** Recording
does not transfer title — delivery and acceptance did that — **but the entire risk lives in the interval
before it**, which is why it happens immediately.

### 72.2 Disbursement and accounting

Funds are disbursed: payoffs, prorations, costs, credits, and compensation.

**§ 858-353(A)(3)** — a duty to **all parties**, mandatory and unwaivable — requires the broker to
**timely account for all money and property received.** That obligation does not end at closing; it covers
anything still held.

**§ 858-312(6)** makes **failing, within a reasonable time, to account for or to remit any monies,
documents, or other property coming into possession of the licensee which belong to others** a ground for
suspension or revocation.

**And § 858-358** — after termination, expiration or completion, the two surviving duties are **to account
for all monies and property relating to the transaction** and **to keep confidential all confidential
information received.** Closing does not release you from either.

### 72.3 The deed theft notification — § 858-364

chunks.heading: 72.4 The file after closing
chunks.excerpt:
> **As part of each closing of a transaction**, notification of the signs and risks of **deed theft**, as
> defined in Section 858-351 of Title 59 of the Oklahoma Statutes, **shall be required to be given to the
> buyer by a licensed real estate broker. The buyer shall confirm receipt of such notification by affixing
> his or her signature to such notification.** The Oklahoma Real Estate Commission shall promulgate rules
> to enact the provisions of this section.

**Every closing. To the buyer. By a licensed broker. Signed by the buyer.**

**Deed theft** is defined at § 858-351(3) as intentionally **altering, falsifying, forging or
misrepresenting a document relating to real property** with intent to deceive, defraud or unlawfully
transfer or encumber ownership rights; **misrepresenting oneself as the owner or the owner's authorised
representative** to obtain ownership or possession; or, with intent to defraud, **taking, obtaining,
stealing or transferring title or ownership** by fraud, forgery, larceny or any other fraudulent or
deceptive practice.

**This course states no wording or format for the notification**, because the Commission's implementing
rules and the form itself were not located in the publication read for this project. **Obtain the current
form from the Commission**, and confirm the rules have issued before relying on any version of it.

**§ 858-307.2(F)** separately requires licensees to complete Commission-specified continuing education on
deed theft **on or before 1 November 2028.**

### 72.4 The file after closing

**Keep it.** Everything: the agreement, the disclosures, the offers, the notices, the settlement
statement, the correspondence, the record of what was presented and when.

chunks.heading: 72.5 What closing feels like when it is done properly
chunks.excerpt:
Two reasons. **§ 858-312(26)** makes **failure to provide an adequate written response to the Commission
within fifteen (15) days** after written notice of a complaint or investigation a ground for suspension or
revocation — and you cannot respond adequately from memory. And the Commission **may on its own motion,
and SHALL upon written complaint filed by any person**, investigate the business transactions of any
licensee — § 858-312.

**This course states no Oklahoma licensee record retention period**, because that provision was not read
from primary text for this project. *(605:10-5-1(i)(2)'s five-year retention applies to education
entities' enrolment records and roll sheets, not to a licensee's transaction files, and the two must not
be confused.)* **Read the retention rule and your broker's written policy.**

### 72.5 What closing feels like when it is done properly

Nothing happens. Everyone signs, the funds move, the deed records, and the parties leave with what the
contract said they would get.

**That outcome is produced weeks earlier**, by the licensee who ordered title work in week one, calendared
every deadline the day the contract was accepted, read Schedule B-I the day it arrived, checked the
settlement statement against the contract before anyone sat down, and told the party in writing every time
something moved.

### Module OK-12 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module OK-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, from 605:10-5-3(f).

---

## Instructor source note for Module OK-12

chunks.heading: Supplemental source review — 2026-09-06
chunks.excerpt:
Oklahoma citations in this module — 59 O.S. §§ 858-307.2, 858-312, 858-351, 858-353, 858-358 and 858-364,
and 605:10-3-1, 605:10-5-1 and 605:10-5-3 — were read on 2026-08-20 and are recorded in
`oklahoma/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this module:** RESPA, Regulation X, TILA and Regulation Z in
their own text; Oklahoma's recording, documentary stamp and property tax provisions; Oklahoma's licensee
record retention rule; the Commission's rules implementing § 858-364 and the form of the deed theft
notification; and the Oklahoma Real Estate Contract Form Committee's promulgated forms. The RESPA and TRID
material is stated at the level of principle from the general body of pre-license knowledge and every
specific is routed to the lender and the closing agent.

<!-- OK-SOURCE-SUPPLEMENT:START -->

## Supplemental source review — 2026-09-06

This required reading clarifies the existing topics; no additional clock-hour credit or regulator approval is claimed.

### closing

Related module 12, §§71.2–71.3. The Closing Disclosure must be distinguished from an earlier estimate
and reconciled to the actual contract, lender instructions and settlement figures. Under Regulation
Z, 12 CFR 1026.19(f)(2)(ii), a new three-business-day waiting period is triggered by an inaccurate APR,
a loan-product change, or addition of a prepayment penalty. Other corrections can require a corrected
disclosure without automatically restarting that period. The lender determines the applicable APR
tolerance and timing; do not substitute the phrase "every correction restarts the clock."

chunks.heading: records
chunks.excerpt:
In a settlement worksheet, a seller credit reduces buyer cash needed and seller proceeds. Recording
it twice understates both amounts. Reconcile credits, deposits, payoff figures and prorations against
their source; do not fix an imbalance by inventing a fee. Possession follows the agreement, not merely
the delivery of keys or a signature. Under 59 O.S. 858-364 a broker gives the required deed-theft notice
at closing and obtains the buyer's signed acknowledgment. Account and confidentiality duties can
survive termination under 858-358; closing does not erase them.

Sources: [Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.19](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/19/); [OREC License Code and Rules, as of November 1, 2025](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/orec/documents/meetings/Nov%201%202025%20Oklahoma%20Real%20Estate%20Commission%20Code%20and%20Rules%20Book.pdf).

### records

Related module 12, §72.4. OAC 605:10-13-1(l) requires transaction records for at least five years from
consummation or termination, and trust records for five years from disbursal. The different triggering
events matter. Paragraph (m) addresses original trust documents, later retention of qualifying copies
and record accessibility. Five years is a minimum, not permission to destroy material subject to a
longer legal hold. Preserve legible, retrievable files and audit trails rather than merely an empty
folder. Section 858-312(26) addresses an adequate written response to a Commission request within
fifteen days; acknowledgment alone is not necessarily adequate.

Sources: [OREC License Code and Rules, as of November 1, 2025](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/orec/documents/meetings/Nov%201%202025%20Oklahoma%20Real%20Estate%20Commission%20Code%20and%20Rules%20Book.pdf).

chunks.excerpt:
# Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-13

## Hours 73–77 · Fair housing

**Commission area of study covered:** 605:10-3-1(a)(1)(K) Fair Housing
**Clock hours:** 5 · **Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Commission review;
605:10-3-1(a)(1) allocates no hours among its twenty-two areas of study.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Oklahoma pre-license credit is available.

> **The information presented in this course should not be used as a substitute for competent legal
> advice.** — 605:10-5-3(i)(6).

## Overview

The federal fair housing framework, the practices it forbids, and the disciplines that prevent a licensee
from committing them by accident — which is how most fair housing violations by licensees actually
happen.

Oklahoma adds a licence consequence that runs alongside the federal one: **§ 858-312(17)** makes
**conviction in a court of competent jurisdiction of having violated any provision of the federal fair
housing laws, 42 U.S.C. § 3601 et seq.**, a ground for suspension or revocation of an Oklahoma real
estate licence. And **§ 858-353(A)(6)** requires compliance with all applicable statutes, which folds
fair housing into the broker-relationships duties as well.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: Timed sequence
chunks.excerpt:
1. Name the seven federal protected classes and the statutes that created them.
2. Describe the acts the Fair Housing Act prohibits.
3. Recognise steering in ordinary language, including when unintended.
4. Distinguish blockbusting from redlining.
5. Distinguish reasonable accommodation from reasonable modification and apply each.
6. Audit an advertisement against the advertising prohibition.
7. Describe the exemptions and explain why they change nothing for a licensee.
8. Describe enforcement, remedies and timing at the level of principle.
9. State what a licensee does when a client gives a discriminatory instruction.
10. Describe ECOA and the two classes it protects that the Fair Housing Act does not.
11. Describe the ADA's application in a real estate context.
12. State the § 858-312(17) and § 858-353(A)(6) licence consequences.
13. Apply the objective-criteria method to a buyer's question about an area.

## Timed sequence

| Hour | Content | Instruction |
|---|---|---:|
| 73 | The protected classes and the prohibited acts | ≥50 min |
| 74 | Steering, blockbusting, redlining | ≥50 min |
| 75 | Disability: accommodation, modification, design | ≥50 min |
| 76 | Advertising, and auditing a listing | ≥50 min |
| 77 | Enforcement; ECOA and the ADA; the Oklahoma licence consequence | ≥50 min |

---

## Hour 73 — The classes and the acts

### 73.1 The seven federal protected classes

**Race. Colour. Religion. National origin. Sex. Familial status. Disability.**

**Race and colour came first**, in the **Civil Rights Act of 1866**, which prohibits **all** racial
discrimination in the sale or rental of property and has **no exemptions at all.**

chunks.heading: 73.2 The federal list is a floor
chunks.excerpt:
**Title VIII of the Civil Rights Act of 1968** — the Fair Housing Act — added religion, colour and
national origin. **Sex** was added in 1974. **Familial status and disability** — the statute's term is
*handicap* — were added by the **Fair Housing Amendments Act of 1988.**

**Familial status** means households with children under eighteen, and includes **pregnant persons** and
those **in the process of securing custody.** The principal exemption is qualified **housing for older
persons.**

### 73.2 The federal list is a floor

State and local law may protect **additional** classes, and a licensee's actual obligations are the sum of
federal, state and any applicable local ordinance.

**This course states no Oklahoma or local protected class**, because Oklahoma's own fair housing
provisions and municipal ordinances were not read from primary text for this project. **Read them.** A
licensee who works from the federal list alone, in a state or a city that protects more, will eventually
be wrong — and being wrong here is not a paperwork problem.

### 73.3 What the Act prohibits

chunks.heading: 73.4 The exemptions, and why they change nothing for you
chunks.excerpt:
- **Refusing to sell, rent or negotiate**, or otherwise **making housing unavailable**, because of a
  protected characteristic.
- **Discriminating in the terms, conditions, privileges, services or facilities.**
- **Advertising** that indicates a preference, limitation or discrimination.
- **Representing that housing is unavailable when it is available.**
- **Blockbusting.**
- **Steering.**
- **Redlining** — discrimination in lending or insurance based on the composition of an area.
- **Denying access** to a multiple listing service or other facility on a protected basis.
- **Coercing, intimidating, threatening or interfering** with a person exercising a fair housing right, or
  **retaliating** against someone who asserted one or helped another to.

### 73.4 The exemptions, and why they change nothing for you

The Act contains narrow exemptions — certain single-family sales by an owner without a broker and without
discriminatory advertising, and owner-occupied dwellings of up to four units.

**Every one of them is lost the moment a licensee is involved.** They also do not apply to **race** under
the 1866 Act, and they never permit discriminatory advertising.

**Know the exemptions exist. Never expect to operate inside one.**

---

## Hour 74 — Steering, blockbusting, redlining

### 74.1 Steering, in ordinary conversation

Steering is directing prospects toward or away from areas on the basis of a protected characteristic. **It
rarely announces itself.** It arrives as a helpful remark:

> "You'd probably be more comfortable on the north side."
> "That area is really more for young families."
> "Let me show you where people like you tend to buy."
> "I'd stay west of the highway if I were you."

**None of those names a protected class.** All of them are steering.

chunks.heading: 74.2 The method that prevents it
chunks.excerpt:
**And steering is committed by OMISSION as easily as by statement** — by simply not showing, not
mentioning, or not searching areas that meet the buyer's own stated criteria.

### 74.2 The method that prevents it

**Answer with data the buyer can verify. Describe property, never people.**

| The buyer asks | What you do |
|---|---|
| "How are the schools?" | Give them the district's published data and the state report card, and tell them to visit. **Do not characterise a school as good or bad** — "good schools" functions as a proxy in practice. |
| "Is it safe?" | Route them to the police department's published statistics. |
| "What kind of people live there?" | *"I can't characterise the people in an area, and I wouldn't be much good at it. Tell me what you need in a property and I'll search on that."* |
| "I'd like a neighbourhood with more people like me." | The answer is still no — gently and clearly. **A buyer's own request does not create an exemption.** |

**Then redirect to criteria you CAN research and supply:** price, size, age, condition, lot, commute time
to a named address, school district boundary as published, property tax, association status, flood zone
determination.

### 74.3 Blockbusting

**Inducing or attempting to induce a sale or rental for profit by representations about the entry or
prospective entry into a neighbourhood of persons of a protected class.** Historically called panic
selling.

Modern forms are subtler: a solicitation implying an area is "changing," a mailer implying values will
fall, a conversation implying now is the time to sell before something happens.

### 74.4 Redlining

**Discrimination in lending or insurance based on the racial or ethnic composition of an area** rather
than the merits of the borrower or the property.

chunks.heading: 74.5 The client's discriminatory instruction
chunks.excerpt:
A licensee is not a lender, but a licensee who **steers a buyer toward or away from a lender**, or who
**tells a buyer an area is hard to finance** without knowing it, is close to the same territory. Route
financing questions to lenders and let the buyer choose.

### 74.5 The client's discriminatory instruction

A seller says: *don't show it to anyone who would change the character of the street.* A landlord says:
*no children upstairs.*

**Refuse. Say plainly that you cannot follow the instruction. Withdraw from the engagement if it stands.**

Three things that are **not** compliance:

1. Following the instruction while noting your objection in the file.
2. Applying it "informally."
3. Asking the client to put it in writing. **A written discriminatory instruction is evidence against the
   licensee, not authority for them.**

And note the Oklahoma overlay: § 858-353(A)(1) requires **honesty and reasonable skill and care to ALL
parties** — including the buyer being steered away — and § 858-353(A)(6) requires compliance with all
applicable statutes. **Following such an instruction breaches the broker-relationships duties as well as
federal law.**

---

## Hour 75 — Disability

### 75.1 Accommodation and modification

**Reasonable accommodation** — a change in a **rule, policy, practice or service** necessary to give a
person with a disability equal opportunity to use and enjoy a dwelling. Waiving a no-pets rule for an
assistance animal; a reserved accessible parking space; a rent payment date matching a benefit deposit.
Generally at the **housing provider's** expense.

chunks.heading: 75.2 Assistance animals
chunks.excerpt:
**Reasonable modification** — a **physical change** to the premises. A grab bar, a ramp, a widened
doorway, a lowered counter. Generally at the **requesting person's** expense, and the provider may in
appropriate cases require restoration of the interior at the end of the tenancy.

**Rule-change versus physical-change is the whole distinction**, and it is tested constantly and confused
constantly.

### 75.2 Assistance animals

**An assistance animal is not a pet.** Pet rules, pet rent and pet deposits **do not apply** to it, and the
questions that may be asked about it are narrowly limited.

### 75.3 What may not be asked

Whether a prospect **has** a disability. The **nature or severity** of one. To see **medical records**.

A prospect may volunteer information, and a request for an accommodation or modification may itself
require limited verification in some circumstances — but the licensee does not go looking.

### 75.4 Design and construction

**Covered multifamily dwellings built for first occupancy after March 1991** must meet the Act's
accessibility requirements. A licensee marketing new multifamily should know the requirement exists and
route the compliance question to the developer and counsel.

---

## Hour 76 — Advertising

### 76.1 The rule

**Describe the property. Never the buyer, the tenant, or the neighbours.**

chunks.heading: 76.2 Auditing an advertisement, line by line
chunks.excerpt:
| Phrase | Problem |
|---|---|
| "Perfect for a young professional couple" | age, familial status, marital status |
| "Great family neighbourhood" | familial status |
| "Walk to First Baptist" | religion |
| "Adult building" | familial status |
| "Must be able to climb stairs" | disability |
| "Exclusive area" | historically coded, and describes people |
| "Bachelor pad" | sex, familial status |
| "Safe neighbourhood" | frequently a proxy, and a claim you cannot support |
| "Ideal for empty nesters" | familial status, age |

**Acceptable in the same breath:** "three bedrooms"; "second floor, no lift"; "0.4 miles from the Route 66
frontage"; "1,940 square feet"; "attached two-car garage"; "in the Deer Creek school district, per the
district's published boundary map, which buyers should confirm."

### 76.2 Auditing an advertisement, line by line

Three questions for every sentence:

1. **Who is speaking?** **§ 858-312(20)** makes it a ground to advertise to buy, sell, rent or exchange
   real estate **without disclosing in writing that the licensee is a real estate licensee.** Every
   advertisement, including one placed to buy.
2. **What is claimed?** Can every factual claim be supported by something written down? Is any of it a
   guarantee of future profit — **§ 858-312(10)** — or a misrepresentation — **§ 858-312(2)**?
3. **Who is described?** **If the answer is a person rather than a building, rewrite it.**

### 76.3 Photographs and virtual tours

chunks.heading: Hour 77 — Enforcement, other federal law, and the Oklahoma licence consequence
chunks.excerpt:
The same rule applies to images. Photographs showing only certain kinds of people, or staged to signal
who the property is "for," carry the same message as the words. And a photograph must show the property
**as it is** — an image edited to remove a defect or a neighbouring condition is a misrepresentation
under § 858-312(2) whatever the caption says.

---

## Hour 77 — Enforcement, other federal law, and the Oklahoma licence consequence

### 77.1 Enforcement and remedies

A complaint may be filed with **HUD**, generally within **one year** of the alleged act, or a **civil
action** brought in federal court within **two years**. Remedies include **actual and punitive damages,
injunctive relief, civil penalties and attorney's fees.** The **Department of Justice** may bring a
pattern-or-practice action.

**And a fair housing complaint does not require proof of intent.** Disparate treatment and disparate
impact are both theories of liability, and "I didn't mean it that way" is not a defence.

### 77.2 The Oklahoma licence consequence

**§ 858-312(17)** makes it a ground for the Commission to impose sanctions:

> **Conviction in a court of competent jurisdiction of having violated any provision of the federal fair
> housing laws, 42 U.S.C. Section 3601 et seq.**

And **§ 858-353(A)(6)** — a duty to **all parties**, mandatory and unwaivable — requires the broker to
**comply with all requirements of The Oklahoma Real Estate License Code and all applicable statutes and
rules**, which includes the federal fair housing laws.

**So a fair housing violation by an Oklahoma licensee runs on more than one track**, and the tracks do not
wait for each other.

### 77.3 ECOA

chunks.heading: 77.4 The ADA
chunks.excerpt:
The **Equal Credit Opportunity Act** prohibits discrimination in **credit** on the basis of race, colour,
religion, national origin, sex, **marital status**, **age** (provided the applicant can contract), because
income derives from a **public assistance programme**, or because the applicant exercised a right under
the Consumer Credit Protection Act.

**Note two classes ECOA covers that the Fair Housing Act does not: marital status and age.** And a
rejected applicant is entitled to **notice of the reasons.**

### 77.4 The ADA

The **Americans with Disabilities Act** governs **places of public accommodation** and commercial
facilities — Title III — and employment — Title I. In a real estate context it reaches offices, retail,
restaurants and other commercial premises, requiring removal of architectural barriers **where readily
achievable.**

**A real estate office is itself a place of public accommodation.** So is an open house held in a
commercial property.

**FHA and ADA cover different ground and are frequently confused.** FHA is about **housing**; ADA Title
III is about **public accommodations.** Some property is both.

### 77.5 The one-page summary

**Seven federal classes** — race, colour, religion, national origin, sex, familial status, disability —
and that is a **floor**. **Steering, blockbusting, redlining, discriminatory advertising, and making
housing unavailable** are prohibited. **Accommodation changes a rule; modification changes the premises.**
**Describe the property, never the people.** **A client's instruction is not a defence, and documenting an
objection is not compliance.** **Answer questions about areas with published data, not characterisation.**
**Treat every party identically, at every stage, in every transaction.**

chunks.heading: Module OK-13 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
And in Oklahoma: **§ 858-312(17)** and **§ 858-353(A)(6)**.

### Module OK-13 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module OK-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, from 605:10-5-3(f).

---

## Instructor source note for Module OK-13

Oklahoma citations in this module — 59 O.S. §§ 858-312 and 858-353, and 605:10-3-1 and 605:10-5-3 — were
read on 2026-08-20 and are recorded in `oklahoma/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this module:** the Fair Housing Act, the Civil Rights Act of

§ 3601 et seq. a ground for discipline IS stated, because that paragraph was read.**

lessons.title: Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-14

chunks.heading: Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-14
chunks.excerpt:
# Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-14

## Hours 78–82 · Regulations affecting real estate, and professional standards of conduct

**Commission areas of study covered:** 605:10-3-1(a)(1)(Q) Regulations Affecting Real Estate ·
(U) Professional Standards of Conduct
**Clock hours:** 5 · **Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Commission review;
605:10-3-1(a)(1) allocates no hours among its twenty-two areas of study.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Oklahoma pre-license credit is available.

> **The information presented in this course should not be used as a substitute for competent legal
> advice.** — 605:10-5-3(i)(6).

## Overview

The regulatory structure a licensee practises inside — the Commission, the Code, the Rules — and the
standards of conduct enforced through it. The module works through the sources of Oklahoma real estate
law, the licensing path in detail, § 858-312's twenty-eight grounds for discipline, the complaint and
investigation process, and the federal regimes that overlay all of it.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: Timed sequence
chunks.excerpt:
1. Name the four layers of Oklahoma real estate law and say which controls.
2. Describe the Commission and the licence categories.
3. State the licensing requirements of § 858-302 including the three-year education clock.
4. State the state examination passing score and the validity of results and applications.
5. Distinguish the three Oklahoma passing percentages and their examinations.
6. Describe the postlicense requirement and the two-part series.
7. Name the § 858-312 grounds that most commonly arise and explain each.
8. Describe how a complaint proceeds and what a licensee does when one arrives.
9. State the fifteen-day written response requirement and the thirty-day felony notification.
10. State the penalties available under § 858-401.
11. Describe the federal regimes that overlay Oklahoma practice.
12. Describe antitrust exposure and the practical rule that prevents it.
13. Describe the do-not-call and email marketing regimes at the level of principle.

## Timed sequence

| Hour | Content | Instruction |
|---|---|---:|
| 78 | The sources of Oklahoma real estate law; the Commission | ≥50 min |
| 79 | Licensing: qualification, education, examination, application | ≥50 min |
| 80 | § 858-312: the grounds for discipline | ≥50 min |
| 81 | Complaints, investigation, penalties | ≥50 min |
| 82 | Federal overlays: antitrust, marketing, and the rest | ≥50 min |

---

## Hour 78 — The sources of Oklahoma law, and the Commission

### 78.1 Four layers, and which controls

**Statute** — **Title 59 of the Oklahoma Statutes, the Oklahoma Real Estate License Code**, enacted by the
Legislature. The top of the hierarchy.

chunks.heading: 78.2 The Commission
chunks.excerpt:
**Rule** — **Oklahoma Administrative Code Title 605**, promulgated by the Oklahoma Real Estate Commission.
**A rule cannot exceed the statute that authorises it.**

**Commission forms, orders and determinations** — course approval letters, prescribed forms, the deed
theft notification form once its rules issue. **These are operative documents**, and using a superseded
version of a prescribed form is a real problem.

**Case law** — the courts' interpretation of all of the above.

**Where to find them:** the Commission publishes the *Oklahoma Real Estate License Code and Rules* as a
single volume, which is what this course was built from. **Read the section, not a summary of it.** A
summary — including this course — is a navigation aid; the operative text is the operative text.

### 78.2 The Commission

The **Oklahoma Real Estate Commission** consists of **seven members**. It is, by statute, **the sole
governmental entity — state, county or municipal — with authority to regulate and issue real estate
licences in Oklahoma.**

Composition, as read: **five** members licensed real estate brokers with at least **five years' active
experience** as brokers before appointment and engaged full time in the brokerage business; **one** lay
person not in the real estate business; and **one** active representative of a school of real estate
located within Oklahoma. Members must be U.S. citizens and Oklahoma residents for at least **three years**
before appointment.

The Commission licenses, approves education providers, courses and instructors, investigates complaints
and imposes sanctions.

### 78.3 The licence categories

chunks.heading: Hour 79 — Licensing
chunks.excerpt:
**Provisional sales associate** — the entry licence, obtained after the 90-hour Basic Course and the
examination. **Sales associate** — obtained after the provisional licence and the postlicense education
§ 858-302 requires. **Broker associate** and **broker** — requiring the 90-hour **Advanced Course**, active
licensure experience, and for a broker, documentation of transactions and the Broker in Charge course.

---

## Hour 79 — Licensing

### 79.1 The requirements — 59 O.S. § 858-302

- **Eighteen years of age or older.**
- **Evidence of successful completion of ninety (90) clock hours** of basic real estate instruction in a
  Commission-approved course of study.
- **Application** on Commission forms with the fee and all required information and documents.
- **Appear in person for an examination** in the form and on the subjects the Commission prescribes.
- On passing, final approval and payment of the licence fee **plus the Oklahoma Real Estate Education and
  Recovery Fund fee**, the licence issues.

**605:10-3-2** adds what the application contains, including **evidence of successful completion of the
course requirement**, a **sworn statement** as to accuracy, documentation verifying citizenship or
qualified alien status, and **submission to a national criminal history record check** — which is valid
for **six months** from issuance.

### 79.2 The three-year education clock

**§ 858-302(A):**

> The education required in this subsection **shall only be valid for a period of three (3) years from
> the date the school certified successful completion of the course**; thereafter, the applicant shall be
> required to successfully complete an additional ninety (90) clock hours or its equivalent in basic real
> estate instruction.

chunks.heading: 79.3 The examination, and three percentages
chunks.excerpt:
**Three years, from the date the SCHOOL CERTIFIED completion.** Not from the day you finished the last
module; not from your application date. **Plan around it from the day you enrol.**

### 79.3 The examination, and three percentages

**605:10-3-5(f):**

> A score of **seventy-five percent (75%)** or more shall be considered a passing grade on the **broker**
> examination. A score of **seventy percent (70%)** or more shall be considered a passing grade on the
> **provisional sales associate/sales associate** examination.

**605:10-3-5(g)** — passing examination results are **valid for one (1) year.**
**605:10-3-5(e)** — the original examination application is **valid for one (1) year** from filing.
**605:10-3-3(a)(1)** — an approved licence application is **valid for one (1) year.**

**And the three percentages, one final time:**

| Percentage | Examination | Rule |
|---:|---|---|
| **75%** | **this course's** end-of-course final examination | 605:10-5-3(f) |
| **70%** | the **state licensing** examination for provisional sales associate / sales associate | 605:10-3-5(f) |
| **80%** | an **instructor** applicant's qualifying examination | 605:10-5-1(f) |

**A document that names a percentage without naming its examination has misstated the regulator.**

**605:10-3-5(d)** — an applicant who fails may **review their missed questions at the end of the
examination** and may challenge the validity of a question. **No notes, pencils or electronic devices**
during the review, and nothing leaves the examination area.

### 79.4 Part I of II

chunks.heading: 79.5 What the school must tell you before you enrol
chunks.excerpt:
**605:10-5-3(j)** requires each entity to promote the Basic Course as **Part I of a two part series**, with
the **Provisional Postlicense Course of Real Estate as Part II.** Section 858-302 requires that
postlicense education **after the provisional licence issues**, before a full sales associate licence.

**Ninety hours is not the whole of your education**, and any provider that lets you think otherwise has
misled you.

### 79.5 What the school must tell you before you enrol

**605:10-5-1(m)** requires the notice about **felony crimes referenced in 59 O.S. §§ 858-301.1 and
858-4000.1**, including that **the Commission will allow the applicant to seek preapproval prior to
enrolling in a pre-license course** — and the notice about eligibility for applicants who are not
permanent U.S. citizens.

**Use the preapproval route if it may apply to you**, before you pay for ninety hours. **This course states
no offence, period or eligibility rule from those sections**, because they were not read from primary
text for this project.

---

## Hour 80 — § 858-312: the grounds for discipline

### 80.1 The provision

The Commission **may upon its own motion, and SHALL upon written complaint filed by any person**,
investigate the business transactions of any licensee, and may impose sanctions as provided in § 858-208
on a showing of cause. **Twenty-eight grounds are listed.**

### 80.2 The ones that arise most, grouped

**Honesty and representations**

chunks.heading: 80.2 The ones that arise most, grouped
chunks.excerpt:
- **(2)** substantial misrepresentations or false promises in the conduct of business, or through
  licensees, or **advertising**, intended to influence, persuade or induce.
- **(8)** **any other conduct which constitutes untrustworthy, improper, fraudulent, or dishonest
  dealings** — the catch-all, and it is broad.
- **(10)** **guaranteeing future profits** which may result from the resale of real estate.
- **(28)** soliciting, selling or offering real property **by means of a deceptive practice.**
- **(25)** being **unworthy or incompetent** to act as a broker in a manner as to endanger the public.

**Money**

- **(6)** failing within a reasonable time to **account for or remit** monies, documents or other property
  belonging to others.
- **(16)** **commingling** the money or property of others with the licensee's own, unless held in an
  escrow account containing **only** the money or property of others.
- **(22)** offering, loaning, paying, **or making to appear to have been paid**, a down payment or earnest
  money deposit for a purchaser or seller.
- **(4)** an associate accepting compensation **except from the broker with whom the associate is
  associated.**
- **(21)** paying any part of a fee or commission **to any person not licensed**; and **(14)** paying
  compensation to a person performing licensee services without a licence.
- **(18)** a broker's **failure, after receipt of a commission, to account to and pay a licensee their
  earned share.**

**Advertising and property**

chunks.heading: 80.2 The ones that arise most, grouped
chunks.excerpt:
- **(20)** advertising to buy, sell, rent or exchange real estate **without disclosing in writing that the
  licensee is a real estate licensee.**
- **(11)** advertising, offering, **or placing a sign** on real estate **without the owner's consent.**
- **(12)** using prizes, money, gifts or other valuable consideration **as an inducement to secure
  customers or clients to purchase specific property** — with general marketing use permitted **provided
  it is not contingent or limited to individuals making an offer or purchasing a specific property.**
- **(24)** **recording a contract, assignment, affidavit or other writing purporting to affect title or
  encumber property for the purpose of collecting a commission or coercing payment.** Recording a judgment
  is not prohibited.

**Compliance and statute**

- **(3)** **failing to comply with §§ 858-351 through 858-363** — the broker-relationships duties.
- **(23)** **violation of the Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act.**
- **(17)** conviction of violating **the federal fair housing laws, 42 U.S.C. § 3601 et seq.**
- **(13)** appraisal compensation **contingent on a predetermined value**, or an appraisal report on
  property in which the licensee has an **undisclosed interest**; compliance with the Oklahoma real estate
  appraisal law; and **written disclosure to the employer of whether the person is licensed or certified
  by the Oklahoma Real Estate Appraiser Board.**
- **(9)** disregarding or violating **any provision** of the Code or the Commission's rules.

**Character and reporting**

chunks.heading: 80.3 What the list is actually telling you
chunks.excerpt:
- **(1)** a materially false or fraudulent statement in a **licence application.**
- **(15)** unworthiness, or conviction of or plea to **a crime involving moral turpitude.**
- **(19)** conviction of or plea to **forgery, embezzlement, obtaining money under false pretenses,
  extortion, conspiracy to defraud, fraud**, or similar offences.
- **(5)** representing a broker **other than the one you are associated with**, without that broker's
  express knowledge and consent.
- **(26)** **failure to provide an adequate written response to the Commission within fifteen (15) days**
  after receiving written notice of a complaint or investigation.
- **(27)** **failure to notify the Commission** of a felony conviction or plea **within thirty (30) days**
  of the plea and again within thirty days of judgment and sentencing — § 858-301.2.

### 80.3 What the list is actually telling you

Read the twenty-eight together and a pattern appears. **Almost none of them require dishonest intent.**
Failing to account in a reasonable time. Commingling. Advertising without disclosing licensee status.
Recording something to collect a fee. Not responding to the Commission in fifteen days.

**These are process failures, and process failures are what discipline is mostly made of.** The
professional habits that prevent them are the ones this course has repeated: write it down, deliver it to
the broker, disclose in writing, calendar the deadline, respond to the regulator on time.

---

## Hour 81 — Complaints, investigation, and penalties

### 81.1 How a matter starts

chunks.heading: 81.2 What a licensee does when a complaint arrives
chunks.excerpt:
The Commission **may on its own motion**, and **SHALL upon written complaint filed by any person**,
investigate the business transactions of a licensee. It may hold hearings; a hearing examiner may be
appointed; and appeal procedures are set out in 605:10-1-3.

**"Shall upon written complaint" means any person can start one and the Commission must look.**

### 81.2 What a licensee does when a complaint arrives

1. **Tell your broker immediately.** Not eventually.
2. **Preserve everything.** Every file, email, text and note. **Altering or destroying a record after a
   complaint converts a defensible matter into an indefensible one** — and § 858-312(8), untrustworthy or
   dishonest dealings, is broad enough to reach it.
3. **Get counsel** before responding.
4. **Respond within fifteen days.** § 858-312(26) makes **failure to provide an adequate written response
   to the Commission within fifteen (15) days** a ground in itself. **You can be disciplined for ignoring
   the letter even if the underlying complaint was groundless.**

### 81.3 The penalties — § 858-401

**Unlicensed activity.** Any **unlicensed** person who willingly, knowingly or negligently violates the
Code is, on conviction, guilty of a **misdemeanour**, punishable by a fine of **not more than $5,000**,
imprisonment in the county jail for **not more than six (6) months**, or both.

**Administrative.** The Commission may, after notice and hearing and on finding a violation, **impose a
fine of not more than $5,000 or the amount of the commission earned, whichever is greater, for each
violation** involving unlicensed activity; may seek an **injunction**; and may impose administrative fines
**enforceable in the district courts.**

chunks.heading: 81.4 Errors, and the honest response
chunks.excerpt:
**§ 858-307.3** — a person whose licence is revoked **shall not file an application for reissuance within
five (5) years** of the effective date of revocation.

### 81.4 Errors, and the honest response

Every licensee will eventually make a mistake — a missed deadline, a transposed figure, a disclosure sent
late.

**The professional response is the same every time: tell your broker, tell the affected party, correct it
in writing, and document what happened.**

The alternative — quietly fixing it and hoping — converts an error into a concealment, and concealment is
what turns a survivable problem into a licence problem under § 858-312(8).

---

## Hour 82 — Federal overlays

### 82.1 Antitrust

Four practices, and each is criminal exposure rather than merely a licence problem:

**Price fixing** — any agreement or understanding among competing firms about **compensation rates or
fees**. Compensation is negotiable between the broker and the party, and **any** conversation with a
competitor about what "we" charge is a conversation to leave.

**Market allocation** — agreeing with competitors to divide territories, property types or customer
groups.

**Group boycott** — agreeing with competitors to refuse to deal with a particular broker or business
model.

**Tying** — conditioning the sale of one product or service on the purchase of another.

**The practical rule: never discuss your firm's compensation structure with a competitor, in any setting,
however casual. Leave the conversation, and be seen to leave it.**

### 82.2 Fair housing, ECOA, ADA

Module OK-13 in full, and the Oklahoma consequence at § 858-312(17) and § 858-353(A)(6).

### 82.3 RESPA and TRID

chunks.heading: 82.4 Telephone, text and email marketing
chunks.excerpt:
Module OK-12 Hour 71. **Section 8 kickbacks** and **section 9's title-company prohibition**, the
**affiliated business arrangement** disclosure, and the **three-business-day** Closing Disclosure rule.

Note again the overlap with § 858-312(21) and (14): **a referral arrangement can breach federal law and
Oklahoma licence law with the same act.**

### 82.4 Telephone, text and email marketing

The **Telephone Consumer Protection Act** and the **National Do Not Call Registry** govern telemarketing
calls, and the rules on **autodialled calls and text messages are stricter than most licensees assume.**
Firms must maintain an **internal do-not-call list** and honour requests.

**CAN-SPAM** governs commercial email: accurate headers and subject lines, a physical postal address, and
a **working opt-out that is honoured promptly.**

**This course states no registration period, exemption or penalty amount**, because neither the TCPA nor
the FCC rules nor CAN-SPAM was read from primary text for this project. **Prospecting practice is set by
your firm's written policy, drafted with counsel, and followed.**

### 82.5 Environmental and disclosure regimes

Module OK-15 in full — including the federal **lead-based paint** regime for **target housing built before
1978**, which is one of the very few places a licensee is a **participant** in a disclosure rather than a
bystander to it.

### 82.6 The professional standard, in one paragraph

chunks.heading: Module OK-14 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**Be honest with everyone, competent in what you take on, and prompt in writing.** Disclose what the
statute requires, to everyone entitled to it. Account for other people's money the day it reaches you.
Route what is not yours — legal, tax, appraisal, engineering, environmental, zoning, boundary. Calendar
every deadline the day it is created. And when you get something wrong, say so, in writing, immediately.

**Every one of the twenty-eight grounds is a failure of one of those six habits.**

### Module OK-14 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module OK-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, from 605:10-5-3(f).

---

## Instructor source note for Module OK-14

Oklahoma citations in this module — 59 O.S. §§ 858-301.2, 858-302, 858-303, 858-307.3, 858-312, 858-351 to
858-364 and 858-401, and 605:10-1-3, 605:10-3-1, 605:10-3-2, 605:10-3-3, 605:10-3-5, 605:10-5-1 and
605:10-5-3 — were read on 2026-08-20 from the Commission's Code and Rules effective 1 November 2025 and are
recorded in `oklahoma/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this module:** **59 O.S. § 858-208**, the sanctions section
§ 858-312 cross-refers to, so no sanction available under it is named beyond the § 858-401 penalties that
were read; **§§ 858-301.1 and 858-4000.1**; **the Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act**; the
Oklahoma real estate appraisal law; the Sherman Act, RESPA, TILA, the TCPA and CAN-SPAM in their own text;
and Oklahoma's trust and escrow account provisions. The federal material is stated at the level of
principle from the general body of pre-license knowledge.

chunks.heading: Supplemental source review — 2026-09-06
chunks.excerpt:
<!-- OK-SOURCE-SUPPLEMENT:START -->

## Supplemental source review — 2026-09-06

This required reading clarifies the existing topics; no additional clock-hour credit or regulator approval is claimed.

### authority

Related module 14, §78.2. OREC's authority under 59 O.S. 858-208 includes licensing discipline and
approval of qualifying educational entities, courses and instructors. Its availability of application
forms is not an approval decision. A provisional sales associate must satisfy the specified post-license
requirement; the category is not an independent broker license. Under 858-363, associates perform acts
through the broker's name and supervision. Inactive status is not authority to continue licensed acts.
Apply the statutory categories rather than assuming that payment or finishing a course confers a
license. Required pre-enrollment notices in OAC 605:10-5-1(m) concern specified criminal-history and
immigration-status eligibility review; do not promise eligibility or ask students to conceal issues.

Sources: [OREC License Code and Rules, as of November 1, 2025](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/orec/documents/meetings/Nov%201%202025%20Oklahoma%20Real%20Estate%20Commission%20Code%20and%20Rules%20Book.pdf).

### wholesaling

chunks.heading: conflicts
chunks.excerpt:
Related module 14 and the license-code study area. Under 59 O.S. 858-301, public marketing and
advertising of an equitable interest in a contract to purchase real property fall within the license
requirement. Relabeling the activity does not remove that statutory language. Section **858-314(C)**
gives the homeowner a two-business-day cancellation right without penalty for a covered wholesaler
contract. Related written disclosures and prohibited conduct in that section must also be considered.
Do not cite 858-312.1 for this cancellation right: that is a different provision concerning suspended
or revoked licensees. The assessment tests the specified public-marketing activity and covered
contract, not a claim that every private contractual assignment is identical.

Sources: [OREC License Code and Rules, as of November 1, 2025](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/orec/documents/meetings/Nov%201%202025%20Oklahoma%20Real%20Estate%20Commission%20Code%20and%20Rules%20Book.pdf).

### conflicts

Related module 14, §80.2 and module 03. A broker serving both parties must provide the written notice
required by 59 O.S. 858-355.1(D). Section 858-312(3), not (6), makes failure to comply with the Broker
Relationships Act a disciplinary ground. Section (6) concerns accounting and remittance. Payment alone
does not establish a brokerage relationship under 858-359(A). The Oklahoma Broker Relationships Act
abrogates common-law agency duties within its scope (858-360), but permits additional agreed services
that do not displace statutory duties. The word "agent" as a trade description does not recreate a
different common-law regime (858-361).

chunks.heading: conflicts
chunks.excerpt:
Confidential information under 858-353(A)(4) includes specified price/financing flexibility, motivation
and designated information; the statutory exceptions include written consent, legal requirement and
information becoming public from a source other than the firm. Do not call every physical defect
confidential or disclose negotiations just because a transaction ended. Both-side service does not
permit a broker to sacrifice honesty, accounting or timely communication. Fees can be separately
negotiated under 858-359(D); competing firms cannot agree on a common fee floor. An independent firm's
own fee policy is not, by itself, an agreement among competitors. Sources include the current OREC
Code and the DOJ's primary horizontal-price-fixing enforcement record.

Sources: [OREC License Code and Rules, as of November 1, 2025](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/orec/documents/meetings/Nov%201%202025%20Oklahoma%20Real%20Estate%20Commission%20Code%20and%20Rules%20Book.pdf); [DOJ — United States v. Atlanta Real Estate Board, horizontal price fixing](https://www.justice.gov/atr/case/us-v-atlanta-real-estate-board).

<!-- OK-SOURCE-SUPPLEMENT:END -->
