chunks.heading: Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-15
chunks.excerpt:
# Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-15

## Hours 83–87 · Disclosures, environmental issues, and risk management

**Commission areas of study covered:** 605:10-3-1(a)(1)(R) Disclosures and Environmental Issues ·
(T) Risk Management
**Clock hours:** 5 · **Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Commission review;
605:10-3-1(a)(1) allocates no hours among its twenty-two areas of study.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Oklahoma pre-license credit is available.

> **The information presented in this course should not be used as a substitute for competent legal
> advice.** — 605:10-5-3(i)(6).

## Overview

What must be disclosed, what must be recognised and routed, and how a licensee manages the risk that runs
through everything else in this course. Oklahoma makes disclosure a **statutory duty to all parties** —
§ 858-353(A)(5) — and an independent **ground for discipline** — § 858-312(23) — through the Residential
Property Condition Disclosure Act, whose own text this project has not read and whose content is
therefore stated nowhere here.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: Timed sequence
chunks.excerpt:
1. State the § 858-353(A)(5) disclosure duty and to whom it is owed.
2. State the § 858-312(23) licence consequence and route the Act itself.
3. Explain why confidentiality does not override a disclosure required by law.
4. Recognise the common environmental concerns and route each correctly.
5. State the federal lead-based paint obligations and the licensee's own part in them.
6. Identify Oklahoma-specific property conditions that must be recognised and routed.
7. Explain what a licensee may and may not say about condition.
8. Define risk management and name the four responses to a risk.
9. Identify the recurring risk areas in a residential practice.
10. Describe the documentation discipline that manages most of them.
11. Describe errors and omissions coverage at the level of principle.
12. State what a licensee does on discovering their own error.

## Timed sequence

| Hour | Content | Instruction |
|---|---|---:|
| 83 | The Oklahoma disclosure duty and its licence consequence | ≥50 min |
| 84 | Environmental concerns: recognise, disclose, route | ≥50 min |
| 85 | Lead-based paint, and Oklahoma-specific conditions | ≥50 min |
| 86 | Risk management: identifying and responding to risk | ≥50 min |
| 87 | Documentation, insurance, and the honest correction | ≥50 min |

---

## Hour 83 — The Oklahoma disclosure duty

### 83.1 The duty — § 858-353(A)(5)

Among the seven duties owed to **all parties in a transaction**, **mandatory and unwaivable**:

> **Disclose information pertaining to the property as required by the Residential Property Condition
> Disclosure Act.**

**To all parties.** Not to a client. The other side of your transaction is owed this by you, personally, as
a matter of statute.

### 83.2 The licence consequence — § 858-312(23)

chunks.heading: 83.3 And what this course does not tell you
chunks.excerpt:
**Violation of the Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act** is an independent ground for the
Commission to impose sanctions.

**So an Oklahoma disclosure failure runs on two tracks at once:** it is a breach of the
broker-relationships duties under § 858-353(A)(5), reachable through § 858-312(3); **and** it is a
freestanding ground under § 858-312(23).

### 83.3 And what this course does not tell you

**The Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act's own text was not read from primary text for this
project.** So **this course states no form, no deadline, no exemption, no delivery requirement and no
content requirement from it.**

**That is a real gap and it is named rather than filled.**

**What you must do:** **read the Act.** It is the operative source for the single most common disclosure
question an Oklahoma residential licensee will face — which properties it covers, which transactions are
exempt, what form is used, who completes it, when it must be delivered, and what happens if it is
delivered late or not at all. Get the current form from the Commission and read the Act alongside it,
before your first listing.

### 83.4 Confidentiality does not override it

Module OK-03 Hour 14 established that **§ 858-353(A)(4)** names **four items and only four** as
confidential — willingness to pay more or accept less, willingness to accept different financing terms,
motivating factors, and anything a party **specifically designates** as confidential.

**And the same paragraph provides that confidential information may be disclosed where "the disclosure is
required by law."**

chunks.heading: Hour 84 — Environmental concerns
chunks.excerpt:
**So a seller cannot designate a defect as confidential and thereby suppress it.** If § 858-353(A)(5) and
the Act require it disclosed, it is disclosed — and the statute says so in the same paragraph that creates
the confidentiality duty.

**Say it at the time**, when the seller tells you: *"I have to tell you this is something I'll need to
disclose. Let's talk about how we handle it."* Sellers accept that far better than they accept finding out
afterwards.

---

## Hour 84 — Environmental concerns

### 84.1 One rule governs the whole hour

**Recognise. Disclose. Route.**

**Recognise** the issue. **Disclose** what you know or should know, under § 858-353(A)(1) honesty and
reasonable skill and care and § 858-353(A)(5). **Route** the determination to a qualified professional or
the responsible agency.

**A licensee assesses no environmental condition.** Not radon, not mould, not soil, not asbestos, not
water. Not ever.

### 84.2 The concerns a residential licensee will meet

**Radon.** Testing is by a qualified tester and mitigation by a qualified contractor. A licensee neither
tests nor interprets a result.

**Asbestos.** Common in pre-1980 construction — insulation, floor tile, siding, pipe wrap, popcorn
ceilings. **Intact material is often best left undisturbed; disturbance is the risk.** Renovation plans on
an older house are a routing trigger.

**Mould.** Route to a qualified professional. The underlying question is almost always a **moisture
source**, and a licensee who opines on health effects has strayed a long way outside the licence.

**Underground storage tanks.** Heating oil tanks on older properties; agricultural and fuel tanks on rural
land. Route to a qualified consultant and the responsible state agency.

chunks.heading: 84.3 Oklahoma-specific conditions to recognise
chunks.excerpt:
**Methamphetamine contamination.** A serious and specific issue. A known history is disclosed, and
remediation is routed to the responsible agency and a qualified professional.

**Water supply and waste.** **Private wells and septic systems**, which on rural Oklahoma property decide
habitability and financeability. Route to the county health authority and a qualified inspector — **early,
because a failed septic can stop a loan.**

**Wetlands, floodplain and flood insurance.** **An inventory map is an inventory, not a determination.**
Route to the responsible agency and a consultant. And note that **the standard homeowners policy excludes
flood** — a buyer in or near a mapped zone needs a quote **early**, because it can change what they can
afford.

**Formaldehyde, groundwater and soil contamination.** Routed, always.

### 84.3 Oklahoma-specific conditions to recognise

**Oil and gas activity.** Producing wells, plugged and abandoned wells, gathering lines, tank batteries,
saltwater disposal, and surface use rights held by a severed mineral owner. **A licensee recognises that a
severed mineral estate may carry surface access rights, discloses what is known, and routes every question
to counsel and the title company.** This course states no rule of Oklahoma oil and gas law, because those
provisions were not read from primary text for this project.

**Seismicity.** Oklahoma has experienced induced seismic activity. **A licensee does not assess it, does
not predict it, and does not characterise a property's exposure.** What a licensee does is disclose known
damage, route structural questions to a qualified engineer, and tell a buyer to ask their insurer about
earthquake coverage — which is generally a separate policy or endorsement.

chunks.heading: 84.4 What a licensee may say about condition
chunks.excerpt:
**Severe weather and storm shelters.** Storm shelters and engineered safe rooms are a recognised feature of
this market. **A licensee describes what is there and does not certify it** — whether a shelter meets any
standard is a question for the manufacturer's documentation and a qualified inspector. Registration
practices with local emergency management vary and are routed to the municipality.

**Expansive soils and foundation movement.** Present in parts of the state. **Recognise, disclose, route
to a qualified engineer.** Never characterise a crack.

### 84.4 What a licensee may say about condition

**May:** describe what is visible; report what the seller has disclosed, attributed to the seller; report
what an inspection found, attributed to the inspector; say that a question exists and who answers it.

**May not:** assess; opine on cause, severity, cost or health effect; predict; or reassure. *"That's
nothing to worry about"* is the single most dangerous sentence available to a licensee.

---

## Hour 85 — Lead-based paint, and the licensee as participant

### 85.1 The federal regime

For **target housing built before 1978**, the federal Residential Lead-Based Paint Hazard Reduction Act and
its implementing rule require, in a sale:

- delivery of the **EPA-approved pamphlet**;
- **disclosure** of any known lead-based paint and lead-based paint hazards, and delivery of any
  **available records and reports**;
- a **ten-day opportunity** for the purchaser to conduct a risk assessment or inspection, which the parties
  may agree in writing to change;
- a **disclosure form signed by the parties AND by the agent**; and
- **record retention** of the completed disclosure.

### 85.2 Why this one is different

**The agent's signature is on that form.**

chunks.heading: 85.3 What a licensee actually does
chunks.excerpt:
This is one of the very few places where a licensee is **not a bystander to someone else's disclosure
obligation but a participant with an obligation of their own** — including an affirmative duty to ensure
compliance.

**1978 is a line about the housing, not about the paint.** A pre-1978 house triggers the requirement
whether or not anyone believes there is lead in it, and whether or not the house has been repainted.

### 85.3 What a licensee actually does

Identify the year built from the record. If it is **before 1978**, the regime applies: pamphlet,
disclosure, records, the ten-day opportunity, the signed form, retention. **Do not wait to be asked.**

**This course states no penalty amount or enforcement provision**, because the federal Act and its rule
were not read from primary text for this project. The obligations above are stated at the level of
principle from the general body of pre-license knowledge, and the operative text is read directly.

---

## Hour 86 — Risk management

### 86.1 What it is

**Identifying what can go wrong, and deciding in advance what to do about it.** Four classical responses:

- **Avoid** — do not take on the risk at all. Declining a property type you do not understand; declining
  an instruction you cannot lawfully follow.
- **Reduce or control** — practices that lower the chance or the consequence. Every documentation
  discipline in this course.
- **Transfer** — insurance, and contractual allocation.
- **Retain** — accept it knowingly, having priced it.

### 86.2 The recurring risk areas in a residential practice

**Misrepresentation** — Module OK-09 Hour 50. Almost always by **repeating without checking**. Prevented
by **attribute or verify, never assert.** Grounds: § 858-312(2), and § 858-353(A)(1).

chunks.heading: 86.3 Agency risk — or in Oklahoma, its absence
chunks.excerpt:
**Disclosure failure** — this module Hours 83 and 84. Grounds: § 858-312(23) and § 858-353(A)(5).

**Deadline failure** — Modules OK-09 and OK-10. Prevented by calendar work done the day the contract is
accepted. Ground: § 858-353(A)(1), reasonable skill and care.

**Money handling** — Modules OK-10 Hour 59 and OK-12 Hour 72. Grounds: § 858-312(6), (16) and (22), and
§ 858-353(A)(3).

**Fair housing** — Module OK-13. Grounds: § 858-312(17) and § 858-353(A)(6), plus federal exposure.

**Practising law** — Modules OK-05, OK-09 and throughout. Prevented by routing.

**Confidentiality** — Module OK-03 Hour 14, and § 858-358 after termination.

**Advertising** — Module OK-06 Hour 35. Grounds: § 858-312(20), (11), (12), (10) and (2).

**Failure to communicate** — § 858-353(B)(2). **Most complaints are about silence, not fraud.**

**Regulator response** — § 858-312(26)'s **fifteen days.**

### 86.3 Agency risk — or in Oklahoma, its absence

A licensee elsewhere carries risk from the fiduciary duties. **In Oklahoma § 858-360(A) abrogated them**,
and the risk instead attaches to **the statutory list**: the seven duties to all parties, the two to the
party served, and the written disclosure and confirmation requirements of §§ 858-355.1 and 858-356.

**The risk is not smaller. It is more precisely defined**, which means it is more precisely auditable — and
§ 858-312(3) makes any failure to comply with §§ 858-351 through 858-363 a ground.

**Which is good news, if you take it seriously:** a closed statutory list is a checklist, and a checklist
can be worked.

---

## Hour 87 — Documentation, insurance, and the honest correction

### 87.1 The documentation discipline

**Write it down. Put it in writing. Keep it.**

chunks.heading: 87.2 Errors and omissions coverage
chunks.excerpt:
- **Every disclosure**, with the date it was given.
- **Every material conversation**, confirmed by email the same day.
- **Every figure**, with its source.
- **Every offer received and presented**, with dates and times — § 858-353(A)(2).
- **Every deadline**, computed the day the contract is accepted.
- **Every instruction from a party**, and every refusal of an unlawful one.
- **Every accounting** for money and property — § 858-353(A)(3).

**Write every file as though someone else will read it, because someone may.** The Commission **shall**
investigate upon written complaint by any person, and **§ 858-312(26) gives you fifteen days to respond
adequately in writing.** You cannot do that from memory.

### 87.2 Errors and omissions coverage

**Professional liability insurance** covering claims of negligent acts, errors or omissions in professional
services.

Three things every licensee should know about their own coverage: **what it covers**; **what it excludes**
— fraud, intentional acts, and often fair housing and antitrust; and **that it is usually claims-made**,
meaning the policy in force when the **claim** is made responds, not the one in force when the work was
done. **Coverage is a question for your broker and the carrier**, and it is asked before it is needed.

**This course states no Oklahoma insurance requirement for licensees**, because no such provision was read
from primary text for this project.

### 87.3 The honest correction

**Every licensee will eventually make a mistake.** A deadline missed, a figure transposed, a disclosure
sent late, a statement made that turns out to be wrong.

**The professional response, every time:**

chunks.heading: 87.4 The whole module in one page
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Correct it in writing, immediately**, to everyone who received the wrong information.
2. **Tell your broker.**
3. **Document what happened**, when you learned it, and what you did.
4. **Do not alter the earlier record.** Add to it.

**The alternative — quietly fixing it and hoping — converts an error into a concealment.** And under
§ 858-312(8), **any other conduct which constitutes untrustworthy, improper, fraudulent, or dishonest
dealings**, concealment is what turns a survivable problem into a licence problem.

### 87.4 The whole module in one page

**Disclose** what § 858-353(A)(5) and the Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act require — **to all
parties**, and read the Act because this course could not. **Confidentiality does not override a disclosure
required by law.** **Recognise, disclose, route** every environmental question, and **assess none of them.**
**Pre-1978 housing** triggers the federal lead regime, and **your signature is on that form.** **Manage risk
by documenting**, calendaring, routing and communicating. **And when you get it wrong, correct it in
writing immediately.**

### Module OK-15 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module OK-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, from 605:10-5-3(f).

---

## Instructor source note for Module OK-15

Oklahoma citations in this module — 59 O.S. §§ 858-312, 858-353, 858-358 and 858-360, and 605:10-3-1 and
605:10-5-3 — were read on 2026-08-20 and are recorded in
`oklahoma/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

chunks.heading: Supplemental source review — 2026-09-06
chunks.excerpt:
**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this module:** **the Residential Property Condition Disclosure
Act**, whose existence, whose status as a § 858-353(A)(5) duty and whose status as a § 858-312(23) ground
ARE stated because those provisions were read, but none of whose content, form, deadline or exemption is;
the federal Residential Lead-Based Paint Hazard Reduction Act and its rule in their own text; Oklahoma's
oil and gas, seismicity, floodplain and environmental provisions; and any insurance requirement. **No
Oklahoma environmental standard, threshold, testing requirement or remediation standard appears anywhere
in this module.**

<!-- OK-SOURCE-SUPPLEMENT:START -->

## Supplemental source review — 2026-09-06

This required reading clarifies the existing topics; no additional clock-hour credit or regulator approval is claimed.

### disclosure

Related module 15, §§83.1 and 83.4. Oklahoma's Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act distinguishes
a disclosure statement from a disclaimer. Under 60 O.S. 833(A)(1), a disclaimer route requires both
that the seller has never occupied the property and that the seller has no actual knowledge of a
defect. "I did not live there" alone does not erase known defects. Under 832(10), the disclosure is
based on actual knowledge and is not a warranty. The broker's own actual knowledge of an omitted
defect requires disclosure under 836(C). Section 836(E) does not impose an independent property
inspection or independent verification duty on the licensee; referral to an inspector is not a reason
to conceal known facts.

chunks.heading: lead
chunks.excerpt:
Timing is part of the duty. Under 834(B), if the buyer receives the disclosure or disclaimer after
making the offer, acknowledgment and confirmation are required before acceptance. Under 834(C), a
newly discovered defect before acceptance requires prompt written, signed and dated information;
paragraph (D) requires buyer acknowledgment. Retain the delivered version, update and receipt, not
just a note saying "disclosures done." An out-of-date assertion cannot be treated as current merely
because it once appeared in the file.

Sources: [Oklahoma Legislature, Title 60 — Property](https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os60.pdf); [OREC License Code and Rules, as of November 1, 2025](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/orec/documents/meetings/Nov%201%202025%20Oklahoma%20Real%20Estate%20Commission%20Code%20and%20Rules%20Book.pdf).

### lead

Related module 15, §85.1. For covered pre-1978 housing, federal lead disclosure requires the applicable
pamphlet, known information, available records/reports and contractual warning/acknowledgments before
the buyer or tenant becomes obligated. Relevant common-area reports can matter in multifamily
housing. A purchaser generally receives a ten-day opportunity for a lead inspection or risk assessment;
the parties can change that period by written agreement and a buyer may waive the opportunity. The
rule does not itself require the seller to test or guarantee absence of lead. Do not treat a seller's
lack of knowledge as permission to omit the required paperwork. Source: EPA real-estate lead disclosure
guidance and its linked federal disclosure rule.

Sources: [EPA — Real Estate Disclosures About Potential Lead Hazards](https://www.epa.gov/lead/real-estate-disclosures-about-potential-lead-hazards).

### environment

chunks.heading: wire
chunks.excerpt:
Related module 15, §§84.1–84.3. Radon cannot be reliably detected by ordinary senses; testing is the
way to determine its level (EPA Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon). A seller's inability to
smell it is not evidence of absence. Do not disturb suspect asbestos material to make a showing look
better; professional evaluation is appropriate because disturbance can release fibers (EPA asbestos
guidance). Flood risk is not zero outside a mapped high-risk zone; FEMA explains that maps, insurance
requirements and actual exposure are related but different questions. Refer detailed determinations
to qualified sources and disclose known facts. Do not guarantee environmental safety from appearance.

Sources: [EPA — Home Buyer’s and Seller’s Guide to Radon](https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2015-05/documents/hmbuygud.pdf); [EPA — Protect Your Family from Exposures to Asbestos](https://www.epa.gov/asbestos/protect-your-family-exposures-asbestos); [FEMA NFIP — Flood Zones and Maps](https://www.floodsmart.gov/flood-zones-and-maps/what-is-my-flood-zone).

### wire

Related module 15, §86.2. A changed wire instruction received by email may be business-email compromise.
Verify independently using a previously established number or other trusted channel, not the contact
details in the suspect message. A convincing sender name or logo does not establish authenticity. If
funds have been sent, immediately contact the financial institution and follow its fraud-response
instructions, preserve evidence and report through the appropriate law-enforcement channels. The FBI
recommends immediate bank contact; neither investigation nor recovery is guaranteed. Never ask a
customer to post account numbers publicly to prove a transfer.

chunks.heading: wire
chunks.excerpt:
Sources: [FBI — Business Email Compromise](https://www.fbi.gov/how-we-can-help-you/common-frauds-and-scams/business-email-compromise).

<!-- OK-SOURCE-SUPPLEMENT:END -->

lessons.title: Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-16

chunks.heading: Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-16
chunks.excerpt:
# Oklahoma Basic Course of Real Estate, Part I of II — Module OK-16

## Hours 88–90 · Property management and leasing

**Commission area of study covered:** 605:10-3-1(a)(1)(S) Property Management and Leasing
**Clock hours:** 3 · **Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Commission review;
605:10-3-1(a)(1) allocates no hours among its twenty-two areas of study.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Oklahoma pre-license credit is available.

> **The information presented in this course should not be used as a substitute for competent legal
> advice.** — 605:10-5-3(i)(6).

## Overview

The final module. Leasehold estates and lease documents; the property manager's functions and the
management agreement; the operating statement; and the trust-fund discipline that is where property
managers most often lose licences. It closes with what a student carries out of ninety hours — and what
they do not.

## Learning objectives

1. Classify the four leasehold estates and state what ends each.
2. Explain that a lease is both a conveyance and a contract.
3. Distinguish assignment from sublease and state who remains liable.
4. Distinguish gross, net, percentage and ground leases.
5. Describe a property manager's functions.
6. Name what a management agreement must settle.
7. Compute effective gross income, net operating income and before-tax cash flow.
8. State the trust-fund rule and the Oklahoma grounds that enforce it.
9. Apply the § 858-353 duties in a management context.
10. Apply fair housing to tenant screening.
11. State what a licensee carries out of ninety hours, and what they do not.
12. State the course's regulatory status and the education validity clock.

## Timed sequence

chunks.heading: Hour 88 — Leasehold estates and leases
chunks.excerpt:
| Hour | Content | Instruction |
|---|---|---:|
| 88 | Leasehold estates and lease documents | ≥50 min |
| 89 | Property management: functions, agreement, operating statement | ≥50 min |
| 90 | Trust funds, duties, and what you carry forward | ≥50 min |

---

## Hour 88 — Leasehold estates and leases

### 88.1 The four leasehold estates

**Estate for years.** A definite beginning and a definite end. **It terminates on its own terms and
requires no notice.**

**Periodic tenancy, or estate from period to period.** Renews automatically — month to month, year to year
— until proper notice by either party.

**Tenancy at will.** Possession with the landlord's consent for an indefinite period, terminable by either
party.

**Tenancy at sufferance.** A **holdover** — the tenant remains after the right to possess has ended. Not a
tenancy the landlord agreed to.

**This course states no Oklahoma notice period, security deposit rule, remedy or eviction procedure**,
because Oklahoma's landlord-tenant provisions were not read from primary text for this project. **Which
estate exists** is what a licensee must be able to identify; **what notice ends it, and every remedy, is
routed to counsel and to the lease.**

### 88.2 A lease is two things at once

A **conveyance** of a possessory interest for a term, and a **contract** of covenants between the parties.

That dual nature is why a lease dispute can be framed either as a breach of contract or as an interference
with possession, and why the **covenant of quiet enjoyment** matters as much as any written clause.

### 88.3 Standard provisions

chunks.heading: 88.4 Assignment and sublease
chunks.excerpt:
Parties; premises; term; rent and when and where it is paid; **security deposit** and its handling; use
and occupancy; maintenance and repair, and which side does what; utilities; alterations; **assignment and
subletting**; access by the landlord; insurance; default and remedies; and the condition of the premises
at surrender.

**Trade fixtures**, from Module OK-01 Hour 2: a tenant's business installations remain the tenant's and
**must be removed before the term ends**, after which they generally pass to the landlord by **accession.**

### 88.4 Assignment and sublease

**Assignment** transfers the tenant's **entire** remaining interest. **Sublease** transfers **less than
all** of it, leaving the original tenant as a landlord to the subtenant.

**In both cases the original tenant generally remains liable unless expressly released** — which tenants
routinely assume they are not. Whether either is permitted at all is a question for the lease's own terms.

### 88.5 Lease types by rent structure

**Gross** — the landlord pays operating expenses. **Net**, in its several degrees — the tenant pays some or
all of them. **Percentage** — common in retail; rent includes a share of sales. **Ground** — a long-term
lease of land on which the tenant builds.

---

## Hour 89 — Property management

### 89.1 The manager's position

The manager provides **brokerage services** to the owner as a **party** under §§ 858-351 to 858-363. **All
seven § 858-353(A) duties apply**, and the two § 858-353(B) duties apply to the owner as the party served.

**And every fair housing obligation runs to applicants and tenants at the same time** — Module OK-13, and
§ 858-353(A)(6), and § 858-312(17).

### 89.2 Functions

Producing the owner's intended return while preserving the asset:

chunks.heading: 89.3 The management agreement
chunks.excerpt:
- **Marketing and leasing.**
- **Tenant screening**, applied **identically to every applicant** — written criteria, applied uniformly,
  documented. Fair housing exposure in management is concentrated here.
- **Rent collection**, and enforcement under the lease.
- **Maintenance**, routine and capital.
- **Budgeting and reporting** to the owner.
- **Regulatory compliance.**
- **Risk management** — insurance, habitability, security, documentation.

### 89.3 The management agreement

It is a **brokerage agreement**, so **§ 858-355.1(A)** applies: it **shall incorporate as material terms
the § 858-353 duties.** And **§ 858-363**: it is entered **in the broker's name**, not the associate's.

It must settle: the **scope of authority**; the **compensation** — and **§ 858-353(A)(7)**'s disclosure in
writing, with a term **not exceeding one year** and **defaulting to sixty days** if unstated; the
**term**; **reporting and accounting** obligations; the owner's **approval thresholds for expenditure**;
and the **handling of trust funds.**

**An unwritten scope of authority is how a manager ends up having spent an owner's money on something the
owner did not authorise.**

### 89.4 The operating statement

**Potential gross income**, less **vacancy and collection loss** → **effective gross income**, less
**operating expenses** → **net operating income.**

*Worked.* Potential gross income $184,000. Vacancy and collection loss 6% = $11,040. **Effective gross
income $172,960.** Operating expenses $71,000. **NOI = $101,960.**

**Debt service is NOT an operating expense.** With annual debt service of $76,400: 101,960 − 76,400 =
**$25,560 before-tax cash flow** — a different figure answering a different question.

chunks.heading: Hour 90 — Trust funds, duties, and what you carry forward
chunks.excerpt:
**And check for a replacement reserve line.** No reserve understates expenses, overstates NOI, and — since
NOI ÷ cap rate produces value — overstates value directly.

---

## Hour 90 — Trust funds, duties, and what you carry forward

### 90.1 Trust funds — where managers lose licences

**Security deposits and prepaid rent are other people's money from the moment they arrive.**

Three Oklahoma provisions:

**§ 858-353(A)(3)** — a duty to **all parties**, mandatory and unwaivable: **timely account for all money
and property received.**

**§ 858-312(6)** — **failing, within a reasonable time, to account for or to remit any monies, documents,
or other property coming into possession of the licensee which belong to others.**

**§ 858-312(16)** — **commingling** the money or property of others with the licensee's own, **unless the
money or property of others is received by the licensee and held in an escrow account that contains only
money or property of others.**

Read the Code with **OAC 605:10-13-1(b)**: the rule permits personal funds sufficient to maintain the
account's integrity and cover the financial institution's servicing charges. This narrow exception is
not permission to pay operating expenses or store arbitrary company reserves in trust. An operating
account with careful internal bookkeeping does not become a compliant trust account.

**An owner who says "just put the deposits in the operating account, it's simpler" is asking you to commit
the conduct § 858-312(16) names.** The answer is no, and it does not become yes because the owner is the
client or because a spreadsheet tracks each balance.

chunks.heading: 90.2 A discriminatory instruction from an owner
chunks.excerpt:
**Original review limitation, superseded in part by the 2026-09-06 assessment-source supplement:** those
provisions were not read from primary text for this project. **Read them and your broker's written
procedures before you touch a deposit.**

**Trust account failures are the fastest route out of this profession, and they are almost never theft.
They are convenience, helpfulness and sloppiness — which look identical on an audit.**

### 90.2 A discriminatory instruction from an owner

*No children on the upper floor. Don't rent to anyone from that neighbourhood.*

**Refuse. Say plainly that you cannot follow it. Withdraw from the engagement if it stands.**

Not compliance: following it while noting an objection; applying it informally; asking the owner to put it
in writing. **A written discriminatory instruction is evidence against you.**

Same answer as Module OK-13 Hour 74.5, and the same every time it appears.

### 90.3 What you carry out of ninety hours

**A working knowledge of the transaction** — property and the interests in it, title and its defects,
contracts and their performance, financing and its arithmetic, valuation, closing, leasing.

**The Oklahoma statutory framework**, and specifically:

chunks.heading: 90.4 What you do not carry
chunks.excerpt:
- **There is no agency.** § 858-360(A) abrogated the fiduciary duties; § 858-360(B) forbids agency,
  subagency and dual agency.
- **Seven duties to all parties**, mandatory and unwaivable — § 858-353(A).
- **Two more to the party you serve** — § 858-353(B).
- **Four confidential items, and only four** — § 858-353(A)(4).
- **Written disclosure before signing, confirmed in or attached to the contract** — §§ 858-355.1(C) and
  858-356.
- **Compensation in writing before the contract's effective date**, capped at one year, defaulting to
  sixty days — § 858-353(A)(7).
- **Twenty-eight grounds** for discipline — § 858-312 — of which most are process failures.

**The federal fair housing framework**, and the practices it forbids including the ones nobody intends.

**The arithmetic.**

**And most durably: a reliable sense of which questions are yours and which are routed** — to your broker,
to counsel, to the lender, to the title company, to the municipality, to a qualified professional, to the
Commission.

### 90.4 What you do not carry

**The right to give legal, tax, engineering, environmental or appraisal advice.**

**The specifics of everything this course could not read from primary text.** Each is named in
`oklahoma/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`, and the list is not short: **the Residential Property
Condition Disclosure Act**; **the Oklahoma Real Estate Contract Form Committee's promulgated forms**;
59 O.S. §§ 858-208, 858-301.1 and 858-4000.1; the Commission's rules implementing the **deed theft
notification** and its form; the **OREC syllabus**; and Oklahoma's trust account, foreclosure,
landlord-tenant, probate, lien, tax, subdivision, mineral and environmental provisions.

chunks.heading: 90.5 What comes next
chunks.excerpt:
**Each must be read in current text before it is relied on.** 605:10-5-3(k) makes the same point from the
school's side: all materials distributed to students **must be current and up-to-date with the License Code
and Rules and state or federal laws.**

**And a licence.** This course is one requirement among several.

### 90.5 What comes next

**The end-of-course examination.** Under 605:10-5-3(e) it consists of **no less than 150 questions**, and
**"End-of-course examination questions may not be the same as any previously used questions covering the
respective course content."** Under 605:10-5-3(f) you pass at **at least 75 percent**, and an entity **may
allow a student who fails to take another examination without repeating instruction.** Under
605:10-5-3(g) this school **publishes its grading standards and gives them to you in writing at the
beginning of the course.**

**Then the state examination**, passed at **70 percent** for the provisional sales associate — 605:10-3-5(f)
— with results valid **one year.**

**Then your application**, within **three years of the date this school certifies your completion** —
59 O.S. § 858-302(A).

**Then Part II.** 605:10-5-3(j) requires this course to be promoted as **Part I of a two part series**, and
§ 858-302 requires the **Provisional Postlicense Course** after your provisional licence issues, before a
full sales associate licence. **Ninety hours was never the whole of it.**

### 90.6 The status of this course

**Version 1.0 submission draft. Not approved. No Oklahoma pre-license credit is available for it.**

Under 605:10-5-1(d) no person or entity may advertise a course as approved before the Commission approves
it, and may not advertise that it is endorsed, recommended or accredited by the Commission.

chunks.heading: Module OK-16 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**A school that would not tell you that, and would not give you the list in 90.4, is not a school to buy
education from.**

### Module OK-16 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module OK-01. The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **75 percent** end-of-course standard is the
Commission's, from 605:10-5-3(f).

---

## Instructor source note for Module OK-16

Oklahoma citations in this module — 59 O.S. §§ 858-302, 858-312, 858-351 to 858-363, and 605:10-3-1,
605:10-3-5, 605:10-5-1 and 605:10-5-3 — were read on 2026-08-20 and are recorded in
`oklahoma/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this module:** Oklahoma's landlord-tenant provisions and every
notice period, security deposit rule, remedy and eviction procedure in them; Oklahoma's trust and escrow
account provisions; and the Oklahoma Real Estate Contract Form Committee's promulgated forms. **Every
dollar figure is an invented arithmetic illustration and is not Oklahoma market data.**

<!-- OK-SOURCE-SUPPLEMENT:START -->

## Supplemental source review — 2026-09-06

This required reading clarifies the existing topics; no additional clock-hour credit or regulator approval is claimed.

### trust

chunks.heading: tenancy
chunks.excerpt:
Related modules 10, §59.2 and 16, §90.1. Trust money belongs to the entitled party, not to the firm.
Commingling and failure to account/remit are distinct concerns under 59 O.S. 858-312(16) and (6).
OAC 605:10-13-1 requires bookkeeping that identifies ownership, receipts, disbursements and balances.
If three separate ledgers hold $3,100, $2,400 and $1,200, their liability total is $6,700; an unrelated
firm expense cannot properly reduce a client's balance. This arithmetic example prescribes no
deadline or deposit rule. Reconcile the bank and transaction ledgers, investigate discrepancies and
preserve records. For a disputed deposit, preserve funds and use authorized disposition procedures,
including the applicable rule or interpleader route; do not decide a party's legal entitlement by
preference or pay office expenses while waiting.

Sources: [OREC License Code and Rules, as of November 1, 2025](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/orec/documents/meetings/Nov%201%202025%20Oklahoma%20Real%20Estate%20Commission%20Code%20and%20Rules%20Book.pdf).

### tenancy

chunks.heading: tenancy
chunks.excerpt:
Related module 16, §§89.2 and 90.1. Read the Oklahoma Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, not only the
management contract. Under 41 O.S. 118(A), landlord obligations include specified habitability and
maintenance duties; supplied plumbing and common areas in covered multifamily premises cannot simply
be ignored. The section has qualifications and limited written-agreement provisions, not a blanket
rule that every conceivable repair is always landlord-paid. Under 41 O.S. 127, the tenant has duties
concerning cleanliness, proper use, damage and peaceful enjoyment. A complaint is evaluated under the
applicable duty and facts, without retaliatory or discriminatory treatment. Security deposits are
handled under 41 O.S. 115; where an assessment expressly supplies lawful deductions, subtract those
amounts without inventing another fee. This example does not establish deduction eligibility or a
return deadline. Federal fair-housing accommodation obligations can apply during an existing tenancy,
not just at application. Evaluate a disability-related request individually rather than imposing an
automatic no-exceptions rule; a request is not automatically granted regardless of reasonableness.

Sources: [Oklahoma Legislature, Title 41 — Landlord and Tenant](https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os41.pdf); [U.S. Code (2024), Title 42, Chapter 45 — Fair Housing](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title42/pdf/USCODE-2024-title42-chap45.pdf); [HUD/DOJ — Reasonable Accommodations](https://www.hud.gov/sites/documents/huddojstatement.pdf).

lessons.title: Pennsylvania Real Estate Fundamentals — Module PA-F-01

chunks.heading: Pennsylvania Real Estate Fundamentals — Module PA-F-01
chunks.excerpt:
# Pennsylvania Real Estate Fundamentals — Module PA-F-01

## Pennsylvania licensure and the regulatory framework

**Course:** Real Estate Fundamentals — one of the two courses **49 Pa. Code § 35.272(b)(2)** names by
title for the salesperson's education requirement.
**Instructional hours:** **5.0** of the course's 30.0
**Credits:** this module sits within the course's **2 credits**, at the rate § 35.358(b)(1) fixes —
*"one credit for every 15 clock hours of instruction."*
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Pennsylvania prelicensing credit is available.

> ### Three things about this course, stated before anything else
>
> **1. The regulation's minimum is 60 hours, not 75.** **§ 35.272(a)(2)** requires an examination
> candidate to have *"successfully completed **four credits, or 60 hours of instruction**, in basic real
> estate courses."* **§ 35.201** defines a credit: *"**A period of 15 hours of instruction.**"* Four
> credits is sixty hours. That is the floor the Commission set.
>
> **2. This course and its companion together run 75 hours, which exceeds that floor.** *Real Estate
> Fundamentals* here is **30 hours / 2 credits**; *Real Estate Practice* is **45 hours / 3 credits**;
> together **5 credits / 75 hours.** **The regulation names both courses by title and assigns hours to
> neither.** The 30/45 split is a **StateCourse decision requiring Commission confirmation**, not a
> regulatory requirement, and it is recorded as such in
> `pennsylvania/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`.
>
> **3. This course has not yet been conformed to the Commission's own outline.** **§ 35.358(a)(2)**
> provides: *"**Instruction in a Commission required course shall conform to the content or the outline
> developed by the Co

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
mmission for the course.**"* **This project has NOT obtained the Commission's
> content outline for either named course.** Everything here is written from **49 Pa. Code Chapter 35
> itself**, read on 2026-08-20. **Conforming it to the Commission's outline is a submission gate.**

## Learning objectives

1. State the education, age and timing requirements for the salesperson's examination.
2. Explain what a *credit* is and how a course's hours convert to credits.
3. State the standards a real estate education provider must observe in delivering this course.
4. Identify the licence categories 49 Pa. Code Chapter 35 recognises.
5. State the reporting obligations a licensee carries to the Commission.
6. State what the Real Estate Recovery Fund is, and what it is not.
7. Distinguish a **standard** licence from a **reciprocal** licence.

---

## A. What the Commission requires before you may sit the examination

### A.1 § 35.272(a) — the three conditions

> **(1)** *"Be **18 years of age or older**."*
> **(2)** *"Have successfully completed **four credits, or 60 hours of instruction, in basic real estate
> courses** as determined by the Commission under subsection (b)."*
> **(3)** *"Submit a completed examination application to the Commission or its designee with the
> examination fee."*

**This course states no examination fee**, because the fee schedule in § 35.203 was read only as a list
of headings and fees change; the current fee comes from the Commission.

### A.2 § 35.272(b) — how the education requirement is satisfied

**Three degrees deem it satisfied outright**, with no showing of coursework in specific areas:

chunks.heading: A.3 The ten-year clock — § 35.272(b)(3)
chunks.excerpt:
- **a bachelor's degree with a major in real estate** from an accredited college as § 35.201 defines it;
- **a bachelor's degree** from such a college **having completed coursework equivalent to a major in real
  estate**;
- **a juris doctor degree from an accredited law school.**

Otherwise, **credits will be allowed for *Real Estate Fundamentals* and *Real Estate Practice* and all
acceptable basic real estate courses** when offered by:

- **an accredited college** as defined in § 35.201;
- **a real estate education provider who has met the approval requirements in § 35.341**; or
- **a real estate education provider outside Pennsylvania approved by the licensing authority of its own
  jurisdiction** — and in that case *"**the course transcript or certificate of completion must state
  that the course is approved by the licensing authority of the jurisdiction where the real estate
  education provider is located**."*

### A.3 The ten-year clock — § 35.272(b)(3)

> ***"Courses shall have been completed within 10 years prior to the date of successful completion of
> the licensing examination."***

Read the anchor carefully, because it is unusual. The ten years does **not** run to the application, and
does **not** run to the day the licence issues. **It runs to the date the candidate successfully
completes the licensing examination.** A candidate who took this course eleven years ago and passes the
examination today has education the rule does not count — even if everything else is in order.

### A.4 Reciprocal conversion — § 35.272(c)

> *"A licensee who is **converting a reciprocal license to a standard salesperson's license is exempt
> from the requirements in subsections (a) and (b)** and is **only required to pass the state portion of
> the examination**."*

chunks.heading: B. What the provider delivering this course must do
chunks.excerpt:
**Standard** and **reciprocal** are the two licence types § 35.201 distinguishes: a **standard licence**
is *"a license, other than a reciprocal license, issued to an individual or entity who has fulfilled the
education/experience and examination requirements of the act."*

**This course states no Pennsylvania licensing examination passing score, item count or time limit**,
because **no Commission examination content outline or candidate handbook was obtained by this
project.** Those figures come from the Commission and its examination vendor.

---

## B. What the provider delivering this course must do

You are entitled to know the standards your provider is held to, because several of them determine
whether your hours count.

### B.1 The clock hour — § 35.358(a)(1)

> *"Instructor-led learning **may not exceed 7 1/2 clock hours of instruction per day**. For purposes of
> this section, a **clock hour is defined as a 60-minute period comprising 50 minutes of instruction and
> a 10-minute break**. **A student may not be required to attend class for more than 90 consecutive
> minutes without a break.**"*

Three separate limits, and they are limits on the **provider**, not on the student. A Pennsylvania clock
hour is **fifty minutes of instruction inside a sixty-minute period** — so this 30-hour course is
**1,500 minutes of instruction** within 1,800 minutes of clock time.

### B.2 Content — § 35.358(a)(2)

chunks.heading: B.3 Attendance — § 35.358(a)(3)
chunks.excerpt:
> *"The substantive content of the course, as evidenced by the **course outline, text and other
> instructional materials**, shall adequately reflect the **stated purpose of the course**, as evidenced
> by the **course title and course description**. **Instruction in a Commission required course shall
> conform to the content or the outline developed by the Commission for the course.**"*

This is the sentence behind the submission gate at the head of this module. The Commission develops
outlines; instruction **shall conform** to them; **this project does not have the outline.**

### B.3 Attendance — § 35.358(a)(3)

> *"**Unless the course is taught by means of distance education**, a student shall be **physically
> present during at least 80% of the classroom instruction for a prelicensure course** ... **to receive
> credit**. **The real estate education provider shall be responsible for verifying student
> attendance.**"*

Note the carve-out for distance education, and note what the regulation does **not** then say: the text
read for this project **states no equivalent attendance standard for a distance course.** This build
therefore **asserts none**, and treats the attendance condition as a value the provider sets under
whatever standard the Commission approves.

### B.4 Distance delivery — § 35.358(a)(4)

> *"**Courses delivered by distance education**, in addition to meeting the content requirements in
> § 35.384, **must have the delivery method approved by the Association of Real Estate License Law
> Officials or another certifying body with similar approval standards approved by the Commission.**"*

**No such approval is held for this build.** That is the second submission gate, and it is not a
formality — it is a precondition to the course counting at all.

chunks.heading: B.5 Grading — § 35.358(b)(2)
chunks.excerpt:
### B.5 Grading — § 35.358(b)(2)

> ***"A prelicensure course must be graded by proctored examination"*** — except where a student's
> handicap or disability would make grading by examination impractical.

**Proctored.** The in-module checks you will meet throughout this course are **not** that examination.
They exist to keep you honest with yourself as you go; the graded event is separate and is watched.

### B.6 Your transcript — §§ 35.359 and 35.360

> § 35.359(a): *"**Within 30 days after a course has been taught**, a real estate education provider
> shall provide each student in the course with an **official course transcript** ... **signed by the
> director**."*

The transcript must carry — among other things — the provider's **Commission approval number**, the
**date you completed the course**, the **number of hours of the course**, your **final grade**, and *"the
fact that the course **will be accepted by the Commission** towards fulfillment of the education
requirement."*

**Keep it.** § 35.272(b)(3)'s ten-year clock is measured against a date that appears on that document.

> § 35.360(e): *"Continuing education records must be maintained for **4 years**. **All other records
> must be retained for 10 years.**"*

Ten years for prelicensure records, which matches the ten-year education window exactly. That is not a
coincidence.

### B.7 Your enrolment agreement — § 35.357

Every student must enter into one, and it must **itemise the tuition and other fees**, state the
provider's **refund policy** on withdrawal, dismissal or the provider's termination of operations, and
**contain the Bureau's toll-free telephone number, (800) 822-2113**, which you may call *"to obtain
information about **filing a complaint against the real estate education provider**."*

chunks.heading: C. The licence categories Chapter 35 recognises
chunks.excerpt:
That number is in the rule so that a student who is being mistreated by a school has somewhere to go
that is not the school.

---

## C. The licence categories Chapter 35 recognises

The chapter's licensure subchapter addresses, among others: **broker**; **associate broker**;
**salesperson**; **cemetery broker**; **cemetery salesperson**; **builder-owner salesperson**; **rental
listing referral agent**; **campground membership salesperson**; and **time-share salesperson.**

Three of these carry education requirements the regulation states in its own numbers, and they are worth
knowing because they show what a *credit* buys:

- **Campground Membership Sales** — *"the **one-credit (15 hours)**, Commission-developed course."*
- **Time Share Sales** — *"the **two-credit (30 hours)**, Commission-developed course."*
- **Salesperson, cemetery broker and rental listing referral agent** — **four credits, or 60 hours**, in
  basic real estate courses.

Note the phrase that recurs: **Commission-developed course.** The Commission writes courses itself. That
is the same fact § 35.358(a)(2) states from the provider's side.

### C.1 Where a salesperson must practise — § 35.243 area

> *"An **associate broker, salesperson**, cemetery salesperson, campground membership salesperson or
> time-share salesperson **shall practise in affiliation with a broker** holding either a reciprocal or
> standard license issued by the Commission."*

A salesperson's licence does not stand on its own. It operates **through** an employing broker, and that
relationship shapes almost everything in the companion course — escrow, advertising, agency, and
supervision all run through the broker.

---

## D. What you must tell the Commission — § 35.290

chunks.heading: D.1 § 35.291 — Posting of suspension notice
chunks.excerpt:
> **(a)** *"A licensee shall notify the Commission of being **convicted of, or pleading guilty or nolo
> contendere to, a felony or misdemeanor, within 30 days of the verdict or plea**."*
> **(b)** *"A licensee shall notify the Commission of **disciplinary action taken against him by the real
> estate licensing authority of another jurisdiction within 30 days of receiving notice** of the
> disciplinary action."*

Two obligations, both **30 days**, both self-reporting. Note the trigger in (a): **the verdict or the
plea**, not the sentence and not the exhaustion of appeals. And note that a **nolo contendere** plea
counts — a licensee who pleads no contest precisely to avoid admitting anything has still triggered the
reporting duty.

### D.1 § 35.291 — Posting of suspension notice

A **broker** whose licence is suspended **shall return the licence to the Commission** and **post a
notice of the Commission's action**, provided by the Commission, **prominently on or near the public
entrance to each office**, main and branch. *"Failure to post the notice constitutes grounds for further
disciplinary action."*

---

## E. The Real Estate Recovery Fund — what it is, and what it is not

The Fund is described in the words **§ 35.331(a)(1)** requires to appear in every written agreement
between a broker and a consumer who may owe compensation:

> *"Notification that a **Real Estate Recovery Fund** exists to **reimburse a person who has obtained a
> final civil judgment against a Commonwealth real estate licensee owing to fraud, misrepresentation or
> deceit in a real estate transaction and who has been unable to collect the judgment after exhausting
> legal and equitable remedies**. Details about the Fund may be obtained by calling the Commission at
> **(717) 783-3658**."*

chunks.heading: F. How to read a rule — a working habit for this course
chunks.excerpt:
Read the conditions in order, because every one of them is a hurdle:

1. **A final civil judgment** — not a complaint, not a Commission disciplinary finding, not a settlement.
2. **Against a Pennsylvania real estate licensee.**
3. **Owing to fraud, misrepresentation or deceit** — not to negligence, not to a bad outcome.
4. **In a real estate transaction.**
5. **Unable to collect after exhausting legal and equitable remedies.**

**The Fund is not insurance and it is not a complaint remedy.** It is a payer of last resort behind an
uncollectable judgment.

**This course states no Recovery Fund payment limit, per-licensee cap or aggregate cap**, because those
are in the **Real Estate Licensing and Registration Act, which this project has not read.**

**§ 35.333(a)(9)** requires substantially the same statement, **in the words the rule prints**, in every
agreement of sale. You will meet it again in the companion course.

---

## F. How to read a rule — a working habit for this course

Chapter 35 is written in a particular way, and noticing the pattern will make the rest of both courses
easier.

**Rules state who the duty falls on.** § 35.321(a) makes the *broker* deposit escrow money and makes the
*broker of record* responsible for ensuring it happens. § 35.358(a)(3) makes the *provider* responsible
for verifying attendance. When you read a rule, find the actor first.

**Exceptions are stated in their own subsections, and they are narrow.** § 35.324(a) gives a deadline;
§ 35.324(b) gives the only exception, and it requires the **written permission of both parties**.
§ 35.326(a) prohibits commingling; § 35.326(b) permits exactly two deposits of the broker's own money,
for bank service charges and minimum balances. When you find a prohibition, check the next subsection.

chunks.heading: Module PA-F-01 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**Where the Commission wants exact words, it prints them.** § 35.340 prints the CMA disclaimer and says
*"printed conspicuously and **without change**."* § 35.333(a)(9) prints the Recovery Fund statement.
§ 35.333(a)(11) prints the time-share cancellation notice and specifies **bold face type of at least 10
point size immediately above the signature line.** Where the rule prints words, they are not a model —
they are the requirement.

**Where the Commission does not state a figure, this course does not invent one.** You will see routing
language throughout both courses — *"this project did not read that source; the answer comes from
there."* That is deliberate. A course that guesses a deadline teaches a licensee to guess deadlines.

---

## Module PA-F-01 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied scenario, five engagement items and five remediation items — delivered as in
every module of both Pennsylvania courses. **The 80 percent engagement threshold and the 100 percent
applied threshold are StateCourse standards.** **49 Pa. Code Chapter 35 prescribes no in-module
assessment and no in-module score**; what it prescribes, in § 35.358(b)(2), is that the **course** be
**graded by proctored examination.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module PA-F-01

Drawn from **49 Pa. Code Chapter 35**, read on 2026-08-20 from the official Pennsylvania Code full-text
database, **current through 56 Pa.B. 3438 (June 6, 2026)** — specifically **§§ 35.201, 35.203, 35.223,
35.243, 35.272, 35.290, 35.291, 35.331, 35.333, 35.341, 35.356, 35.357, 35.358, 35.359 and 35.360.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module PA-F-01
chunks.excerpt:
**Not read in its own text, and therefore the source of nothing here:** the **Real Estate Licensing and
Registration Act, 63 P.S. §§ 455.101—455.902**, including the Real Estate Recovery Fund provisions; the
**Commission's content outlines** for *Real Estate Fundamentals* and *Real Estate Practice*; any
**Commission examination content outline or candidate handbook**; and **ARELLO's distance education
certification standards.**

**No examination passing score, examination item count, application fee, examination fee, Recovery Fund
limit or distance-education attendance standard is stated in this module**, because the sources setting
them were not obtained. The **60-hour / four-credit minimum**, the **10-year education window**, the
**15-hour credit**, the **50-minute clock hour**, the **7½-hour daily cap**, the **90-minute break
rule**, the **80 percent classroom attendance standard**, the **30-day transcript deadline**, the
**10-year and 4-year retention periods**, the **30-day reporting deadlines**, and both telephone numbers
are **transcribed from 49 Pa. Code Chapter 35 itself.**

chunks.heading: Pennsylvania Real Estate Fundamentals — Module PA-F-02
chunks.excerpt:
# Pennsylvania Real Estate Fundamentals — Module PA-F-02

## Real property, estates and interests

**Course:** Real Estate Fundamentals · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 30.0
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Pennsylvania prelicensing credit is available.

> **Source note before you begin.** This module teaches **general real property concepts** — the
> vocabulary a licensee needs before any Pennsylvania rule can be applied. **49 Pa. Code Chapter 35 does
> not define most of these terms**, because it is a rule about licensees rather than a codification of
> property law. Where Pennsylvania's own statutes govern — the Landlord and Tenant Act, the
> Municipalities Planning Code, the realty transfer tax statutes — **this project did not read them**,
> and this module states no provision from any of them. Their names appear so that you know where the
> answer lives.

## Learning objectives

1. Distinguish real property from personal property, and apply the fixture tests.
2. Identify the bundle of rights and what each right permits.
3. Distinguish freehold estates from leasehold estates.
4. Distinguish the forms of concurrent ownership.
5. Identify encumbrances and distinguish liens from non-lien encumbrances.
6. Explain why a salesperson's judgement on any of these routes to counsel — and connect that to
   § 35.292(a)(8) and (12).

---

## A. Real property and personal property

**Land** is the surface, what lies beneath it, and the airspace above it. **Real property** is the land
plus everything permanently attached to it plus the rights that run with it. **Personal property** —
sometimes called *chattels* or *personalty* — is everything else, and it moves.

chunks.heading: A.1 Fixtures
chunks.excerpt:
The distinction decides what conveys. A deed carries the real property. It does not carry the
refrigerator unless the agreement says so.

### A.1 Fixtures

A **fixture** is personal property that has become real property by being attached. The tests, in the
order they are usually applied:

1. **Method of annexation** — how firmly is it attached, and what damage would removal cause?
2. **Adaptation** — was it made or fitted specifically for this property? Custom shutters cut to these
   windows are adapted; a standing lamp is not.
3. **Relationship of the parties** — a tenant's attachment is read differently from an owner's.
4. **Intention** — usually controlling, and read from the objective circumstances rather than from what
   somebody now says they meant.

**The practical answer is not the doctrine.** The reliable practice is to **name in writing what stays
and what goes**, item by item, before anyone signs. Every fixture dispute a licensee ever sees could
have been prevented by a sentence in the agreement.

### A.2 Trade fixtures

Articles a **tenant** attaches for the conduct of a **business** — shelving, display counters, a walk-in
cooler. They remain the **tenant's**, and are removable **before the term ends**, after which they
generally pass to the landlord by **accession**. The lease can change that default and often does.

### A.3 Emblements

Annual crops produced by cultivation. A tenant farmer generally retains the right to harvest the crop
planted before the tenancy ended.

---

## B. The bundle of rights

Ownership is best understood as a **bundle** rather than a single thing, because the rights can be
separated and sold apart:

chunks.heading: B.1 Appurtenant rights
chunks.excerpt:
- **Possession** — to occupy and hold.
- **Use (enjoyment)** — to use it in lawful ways.
- **Exclusion** — to keep others out.
- **Disposition** — to sell, give, lease, mortgage or devise.
- **Encumbrance** — to pledge it as security or grant lesser interests in it.

A landowner who grants a utility easement has sold a stick from the bundle. A landowner who leases has
transferred possession while keeping the rest. A landowner who grants a mortgage has pledged, not
conveyed.

### B.1 Appurtenant rights

Rights that **run with the land**: **air rights**, **subsurface and mineral rights**, **water rights**,
and **appurtenant easements**. They pass with the parcel unless severed.

**Severance** is the key idea. Mineral rights and surface rights can be owned by different people, and a
buyer who assumes otherwise has assumed something no deed said. **This module states no Pennsylvania
rule on subsurface support, coal, oil or gas rights**, because the Pennsylvania statutes governing them
were **not read for this project**. In a Commonwealth with Pennsylvania's mining and drilling history, a
licensee who guesses here will be wrong expensively — the question goes to counsel and to a title
examination.

---

## C. Estates in land

### C.1 Freehold estates — of indefinite duration

**Fee simple absolute.** The largest estate: perpetual, inheritable, freely transferable, subject only to
government powers and to whatever encumbrances burden it.

**Fee simple defeasible.** A fee that can end on a stated condition. Two branches:

chunks.heading: C.2 Leasehold estates — of limited duration
chunks.excerpt:
- **Fee simple determinable** — ends **automatically** on the event, with a possibility of reverter in
  the grantor. Language of duration: *so long as*, *while*, *during*.
- **Fee simple subject to a condition subsequent** — the grantor holds a **right of re-entry** and must
  act. Language of condition: *but if*, *provided that*, *on condition that*.

The difference is whether title snaps back by itself or must be taken back, and it turns on words in a
deed drafted by a lawyer. A licensee's job is to **notice** the language and **route it**, not to
construe it.

**Life estate.** Measured by a life. The **life tenant** may possess and use, and must avoid **waste** —
permanent injury to the property that damages the remainderman's future interest. When the measuring
life ends the estate passes to the **remainderman**, or **reverts** to the grantor.

A **life estate pur autre vie** is measured by the life of someone other than the holder.

### C.2 Leasehold estates — of limited duration

| Estate | How it ends |
|---|---|
| **Estate for years** | A definite beginning and a definite end. **Terminates on its own terms; no notice required.** |
| **Periodic tenancy** | Renews automatically period to period **until proper notice** is given. |
| **Tenancy at will** | Continues at the pleasure of both parties; either may end it. |
| **Tenancy at sufferance** | A holdover the landlord never agreed to — possession without right. |

**Notice periods for a Pennsylvania periodic tenancy are set by the Pennsylvania Landlord and Tenant
Act, which this project did not read. No notice period is stated in this course.**

### C.3 A lease is two things at once

chunks.heading: D. Concurrent ownership
chunks.excerpt:
A lease is **a conveyance** of a possessory interest for a term **and a contract** of covenants between
the parties. That dual nature is why a lease dispute can be framed either as a breach of contract or as
an interference with possession, and why the **covenant of quiet enjoyment** matters as much as any
written clause.

**Assignment** transfers the tenant's **entire** remaining interest. A **sublease** transfers **less than
all** of it, leaving the original tenant as a landlord to the subtenant. **In both cases the original
tenant generally remains liable unless expressly released** — and tenants routinely assume otherwise.
Whether either is permitted at all is a question for the lease's own terms.

---

## D. Concurrent ownership

**Tenancy in common.** Two or more owners, **undivided** interests that may be **unequal**, **no right of
survivorship** — an interest passes by will or intestacy — and each co-tenant may generally transfer or
encumber their own interest and may seek **partition**.

**Joint tenancy.** Requires the four unities — **possession, interest, time, title** — and carries a
**right of survivorship**. Severing a unity converts the severed share to a tenancy in common.

**Tenancy by the entirety.** Available only to **legally married couples**, with survivorship. Its
availability, its incidents and how it is created and severed are matters of **Pennsylvania law this
project did not read**, and **this module states no Pennsylvania rule on it.**

**Ownership in trust, by entity, and in common-interest communities** — condominium and planned
community forms — are additional structures. **Pennsylvania's Uniform Condominium Act and Uniform Planned
Community Act were not obtained by this project**, and no provision of either is stated here.

chunks.heading: D.1 Why this matters at a listing appointment
chunks.excerpt:
### D.1 Why this matters at a listing appointment

The names on a deed determine **who must sign**. A licensee who takes a listing signed by one of two
owners has a listing that may not bind the property. Read the deed, ask who is on title, and where the
answer is not obvious, **route it** — which is exactly what § 35.292(a)(8) requires: *"**Advise the
consumer to seek expert advice on matters about the transaction that are beyond the licensee's
expertise.**"*

---

## E. Encumbrances

An **encumbrance** is any claim, right or interest held by someone other than the owner that burdens the
title or limits the use.

### E.1 Liens — money claims

- **Mortgage lien** — voluntary, given as security for a loan.
- **Property tax lien** — involuntary, statutory, and generally superior in priority.
- **Mechanic's lien** — a contractor's or supplier's claim for work or materials. **Pennsylvania's
  Mechanics' Lien Law was not read for this project; no filing deadline, threshold or priority rule is
  stated here.**
- **Judgment lien** — attaching by operation of law to property of a judgment debtor.
- **Special assessment** — for a public improvement benefiting the property.

**General liens** attach to all of a debtor's property; **specific liens** attach to identified property.
**Voluntary liens** are granted; **involuntary liens** arise by law.

### E.2 Non-lien encumbrances — use claims

chunks.heading: F. Where this module stops, and why
chunks.excerpt:
- **Easement** — a right to use another's land. **Appurtenant** easements benefit a dominant parcel and
  run with the land; easements **in gross** benefit a person or entity.
- **Licence** — permission to use, **revocable**, personal, and not an interest in land.
- **Encroachment** — a physical intrusion across a boundary. Found by a **survey**, not by a fence.
- **Deed restriction / restrictive covenant** — a private limitation running with the land.

**A restrictive covenant is private and is enforced privately; zoning is public and is enforced by the
municipality. Where the two differ, the more restrictive controls the owner's actual freedom of
action** — and a licensee who checks only the zoning has checked half of it.

---

## F. Where this module stops, and why

Everything above is vocabulary. **None of it authorises a licensee to give an opinion.** § 35.292(a)(12)
draws the line precisely, and it is worth reading twice:

> *"**Advise the consumer about compliance with laws pertaining to real estate transactions without
> rendering legal advice.**"*

Both halves are in one sentence. You are expected to **advise about compliance** — to tell a seller a
disclosure statement is required, to tell a buyer an agreement must contain the zoning classification, to
tell either that a question needs a lawyer. You may not **render legal advice** — construe a defeasible
fee, opine on whether an easement was extinguished, or tell a co-tenant what their interest is worth in
a partition.

The vocabulary in this module is what lets you tell the two apart.

---

## Module PA-F-02 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module PA-F-02
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items, delivered as in Module PA-F-01. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100
percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; § 35.358(b)(2)'s requirement is that the
**course** be **graded by proctored examination.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module PA-F-02

**49 Pa. Code Chapter 35 was read** on 2026-08-20 and is the source of **§ 35.292(a)(8) and (12)**,
quoted above. **Every other concept in this module is general real property law**, taught as vocabulary,
and **is not drawn from any Pennsylvania statute**, because the Pennsylvania statutes governing property
were **not obtained by this project.**

**Named but not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this build:** the **Pennsylvania Landlord and
Tenant Act (68 P.S. § 250.101 et seq.)**; the **Pennsylvania Uniform Condominium Act** and **Uniform
Planned Community Act**; the **Mechanics' Lien Law**; the **Municipalities Planning Code**; Pennsylvania's
**subsurface, mineral, oil and gas** statutes; and the **Real Estate Licensing and Registration Act**.

**No notice period, filing deadline, lien threshold, priority rule, condominium rescission period or
tenancy-by-the-entirety rule is stated in this module.**
