chunks.heading: Pennsylvania Real Estate Practice — Module PA-P-03
chunks.excerpt:
# Pennsylvania Real Estate Practice — Module PA-P-03

## Disclosure of business relationships — §§ 35.284, 35.336 to 35.339

**Course:** Real Estate Practice · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 45.0
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Pennsylvania prelicensing credit is available.

> ### A submission gate stated at the top of this module
>
> **§§ 35.336, 35.337 and 35.338 set out four consumer disclosure summaries in full, verbatim, inside the
> regulation**, and **§ 35.339** sets out the **oral disclosure** for a non-in-person initial interview.
>
> **This project read that those sections exist and print those summaries. It did NOT transcribe their text
> into this build, and no document here reproduces, describes or paraphrases the wording of any of them.**
>
> What this module teaches is **which summary applies, when it must be given, in what form, and what
> happens to the acknowledgement afterwards** — all of which § 35.284 and § 35.286 state, and all of which
> was read. **Obtaining and delivering the summaries in the Commission's own words is a submission gate.**

## Learning objectives

1. Identify which of the four disclosure summaries applies to a given consumer.
2. State when the summary must be provided in an in-person initial interview.
3. State what must happen when the initial interview is not in person.
4. State what the licensee must do with the signed acknowledgement — and what to do when a consumer refuses
   to sign.
5. State the retention period for each acknowledgement, and why one of them is different.
6. Connect this obligation to § 35.292(a)(6).

---

## A. Which summary, and to whom — § 35.284

chunks.heading: B. When — the initial interview
chunks.excerpt:
The rule allocates four summaries across four situations. Read the allocation carefully, because the lease
case splits and students routinely miss the split.

| The consumer is | The summary is | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Seeking to **purchase or sell** real estate | **§ 35.336** | § 35.284(a)(1) |
| Seeking to **lease**, and the licensee is working **on behalf of the tenant** | **§ 35.336** | § 35.284(b)(1) |
| Seeking to **lease**, and the licensee is working **on behalf of the owner** | **§ 35.337** | § 35.284(b)(2) |
| Seeking to purchase a **time-share estate** | **§ 35.338** | § 35.284(c) |

**The two lease rows are the point.** The same transaction type produces **two different summaries**
depending on **whose side the licensee is on.** A licensee who keeps one lease form in the drawer and uses
it for every rental will be handing the wrong document to half of them.

Note also the title of § 35.336 as the rule prints it — *"disclosure summary for the purchase or sale of
residential or commercial real estate **or for the lease of residential or commercial real estate when the
licensee is working on behalf of the tenant**."* The tenant-side lease case is folded into the sale
summary; the owner-side lease case gets its own.

---

## B. When — the initial interview

### B.1 In person

> **§ 35.284(a)(1):** *"a licensee shall provide the disclosure summary in § 35.336 to consumers seeking to
> purchase or sell real estate **at the initial interview if the interview occurs in person**."*

**At the initial interview.** Not before showing property, not when an offer is written, not when the
consumer asks. At the **first** substantive contact.

chunks.heading: B.2 Not in person
chunks.excerpt:
The reason is the whole purpose of the disclosure: a consumer is about to start telling a licensee things —
what they can afford, what they will take, why they are moving — and the consumer is entitled to know, before
they say any of it, **whose side the licensee is on.** A disclosure delivered after the consumer has already
talked has protected nobody.

### B.2 Not in person

> **§ 35.284(a)(2):** *"If the initial interview **does not occur in person**, the licensee shall provide the
> **oral disclosure in § 35.339 at the initial interview** and the **written disclosure statement in § 35.336
> no later than the earlier of**"* the points the rule then states.

**Two obligations, not one.** A telephone or online first contact does **not** postpone the disclosure — it
**converts** it into an oral disclosure **now** plus the written statement **shortly after**. The licensee who
says "I'll email you the form" has done half the rule.

**The text of the § 35.339 oral disclosure was not obtained by this project and appears nowhere in this
build.** Nor are the two alternative outer limits in § 35.284(a)(2) stated here as specific events, because
reproducing them accurately requires the section's own words, which this project did not transcribe.
**Delivering the oral disclosure in the Commission's words, and meeting the correct outer limit, is part of
this module's submission gate.**

---

## C. The acknowledgement — § 35.284(d)

> *"A licensee shall **provide a copy of the signed disclosure** to the consumers referenced in subsections
> (a)—(c) and **retain the signed acknowledgment** under § 35.286. **If a consumer refuses to sign the
> acknowledgment, the refusal shall be noted on the acknowledgment.**"*

chunks.heading: D. Retention — § 35.286, and the one that is only six months
chunks.excerpt:
Three obligations in one subsection, and the third is the one that saves licensees.

**Give the consumer a copy of the signed disclosure.**

**Retain the signed acknowledgement** under the retention rule below.

**If the consumer refuses to sign, note the refusal on the acknowledgement.** The rule does not treat a
refusal as a failure — it treats it as an **event to be recorded.** A consumer is entitled to decline to
sign; a licensee is not entitled to have no record of what happened. **The noted refusal is the licensee's
evidence that the disclosure was made**, and it is the difference between a documented compliance and a
disputed memory two years later.

---

## D. Retention — § 35.286, and the one that is only six months

> **§ 35.286(a):** *"A broker or cemetery broker shall **retain records pertaining to a real estate
> transaction for at least 3 years following consummation** — **except for the following which shall be
> retained for 6 months**:*
>
> **(1)** *"The **acknowledgement portion of the consumer notice** applicable to the sale or purchase of
> real estate **in § 35.336 ... when there is not a real estate transaction**."*
> **(2)** *"The acknowledgement portion of the consumer notice applicable to **time shares in § 35.338**."*
> **(3)** *"The acknowledgement portion of the consumer notice applicable to **leases in § 35.336 and
> § 35.337**."*
> **(4)** *"The **written disclosure statement establishing a subagent or transaction licensee relationship**
> required by § 35.281(b)(3)."*

### D.1 Read the qualifier in (1)

> *"... **when there is not a real estate transaction**."*

chunks.heading: D.2 The other three six-month categories
chunks.excerpt:
**That is the whole distinction.** If the consumer you disclosed to went on to buy or sell, the
acknowledgement is a **record pertaining to a real estate transaction** and is kept for **3 years following
consummation** under the general rule. If nothing came of it — the consumer walked into an open house,
signed the acknowledgement and was never heard from again — it is kept for **6 months.**

The rule is proportionate: records of transactions live with the transaction; records of contacts that never
became transactions do not need to be kept for years.

### D.2 The other three six-month categories

**Time-share** acknowledgements and **lease** acknowledgements are six months **without** the
"no-transaction" qualifier, and so is the **written disclosure statement establishing a subagent or
transaction licensee relationship** under § 35.281(b)(3).

**Everything else pertaining to a real estate transaction: three years following consummation.**

### D.3 Production — § 35.286(b)

The broker **shall produce** these records for examination by the Commission or its authorized
representatives **upon written request** or **pursuant to an office inspection under § 35.246** — and an
entity holding a broker's licence must produce its **corporate, partnership or association records** the
same way.

---

## E. Where this obligation comes from — § 35.292(a)(6)

Duty (6) of the twelve owed to **all consumers** and **not waivable**:

> *"**Provide consumers with the information in section 608 of the act at the initial interview.**"*

So the disclosure is not merely a form to hand over. It is one of the **twelve unwaivable duties**, and a
failure to make it is a failure of § 35.292 as much as of § 35.284.

chunks.heading: F. What the disclosure does not do
chunks.excerpt:
**Section 608 of the Real Estate Licensing and Registration Act was not read for this project**, and this
module states none of its content. The citation is § 35.292's own, reproduced so a reader knows where to
go.

---

## F. What the disclosure does not do

Three things worth stating plainly, because consumers and new licensees both assume otherwise.

**It does not create a relationship.** Handing a consumer a disclosure summary makes nobody anybody's
client. **§ 35.281(a)** requires the agreement itself — *"all contracts, commitments and agreements ...
shall be in writing"* — and Module PA-P-04 covers what that agreement must contain.

**It does not fix the relationship for the transaction.** Relationships can change: designation may take
place **at any time** under § 35.315(b), and a licensee who moves from one relationship to another has
obligations under the rule governing the new one.

**It does not substitute for the § 35.292 duties.** Nothing on any form reduces the twelve. A consumer who
receives, reads and signs every disclosure Pennsylvania requires is still owed honesty, good faith,
presentation of all offers, and the duty to be told when a question is beyond the licensee's expertise.

---

## G. The practical sequence, in order

chunks.heading: Module PA-P-03 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
1. **First substantive contact.** Stop before the consumer starts telling you things.
2. **In person?** Provide the correct summary — § 35.336, § 35.337 or § 35.338 — and go through it.
3. **Not in person?** Make the § 35.339 **oral disclosure now**, and get the **written summary out** within
   the rule's outer limit.
4. **Get it signed.** If the consumer declines, **note the refusal on the acknowledgement.**
5. **Give the consumer a copy** of the signed disclosure.
6. **File the acknowledgement** — 3 years after consummation if a transaction followed, 6 months if not, and
   6 months for time-share and lease acknowledgements.
7. **Only then**, if a relationship is to be formed, put the **written agreement** in place under § 35.281 and
   § 35.331.

---

## Module PA-P-03 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module PA-P-01. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100 percent**
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**.

**No item in this module asks a student to recall or reproduce any wording from § 35.336, § 35.337, § 35.338
or § 35.339**, because this project did not obtain their text. Items test which summary applies, when it must
be given, the oral-plus-written rule for a non-in-person interview, the refusal-noting rule, and the
retention periods — all of which are stated in § 35.284 and § 35.286, which were read.

---

## Instructor source note for Module PA-P-03

Drawn from **49 Pa. Code §§ 35.246, 35.281, 35.284, 35.286, 35.292, 35.315, 35.336, 35.337, 35.338 and
35.339**, read on 2026-08-20, current through **56 Pa.B. 3438 (June 6, 2026)**. **The existence, allocation,
timing and retention of the four disclosure summaries are transcribed from §§ 35.284 and 35.286.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module PA-P-03
chunks.excerpt:
**Not obtained, and therefore reproduced, described or paraphrased NOWHERE in this build:** the **verbatim
text of the disclosure summaries in §§ 35.336, 35.337 and 35.338**, and the **oral disclosure in § 35.339**;
the two outer limits stated in **§ 35.284(a)(2)**; and **section 608 of the Real Estate Licensing and
Registration Act.**

**No wording from any consumer notice, and no § 35.284(a)(2) outer-limit event, is stated in this module.**
The **3-year** and **6-month** retention periods and the **refusal-noting** rule are transcribed from
§§ 35.286 and 35.284(d).

lessons.title: Pennsylvania Real Estate Practice — Module PA-P-04

chunks.heading: Pennsylvania Real Estate Practice — Module PA-P-04
chunks.excerpt:
# Pennsylvania Real Estate Practice — Module PA-P-04

## Written agreements and listing agreements — §§ 35.281, 35.331, 35.332

**Course:** Real Estate Practice · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 45.0
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Pennsylvania prelicensing credit is available.

## Learning objectives

1. State what § 35.281 requires to be in writing, and note that it is broader than the Statute of Frauds.
2. Recite the eight contents § 35.331(a) requires in every such agreement.
3. State the Real Estate Recovery Fund notification and what the Fund actually covers.
4. Distinguish the two forms of exclusive listing agreement.
5. Recite the six provisions § 35.332(c) prohibits in an exclusive listing agreement.
6. State the bold-face requirement for an exclusive right-to-sell or right-to-lease.
7. Explain why compensation is a negotiated term and what the rule requires be said about it.

---

## A. § 35.281 — what must be in writing

> **(a)** *"**All contracts, commitments and agreements** between a broker, or a licensee employed by the
> broker, and a **principal or a consumer who is required to pay a fee, commission or other valuable
> consideration shall be in writing** and contain the information specified in § 35.331."*

Three features of that sentence matter.

**"All contracts, commitments and agreements."** Not just listings. Not just formal agreements. A
**commitment** counts.

**The trigger is compensation.** The rule reaches any principal **or consumer** *"who is **required to pay** a
fee, commission or other valuable consideration."* If money may be owed to the broker, the arrangement is in
writing.

chunks.heading: B. § 35.331(a) — the eight required contents
chunks.excerpt:
**It is broader than the Statute of Frauds.** A listing agreement or a buyer agency agreement is an
**employment agreement**, not a contract to convey an interest in land — so the Statute of Frauds may or may
not reach it. **§ 35.281 reaches it regardless, as a condition of the licence.** A licensee who asks
"does the Statute of Frauds require this in writing?" has asked a question that does not matter here.

*(§ 35.281(b)(3) separately requires a **written disclosure statement establishing a subagent or transaction
licensee relationship**, which § 35.286(a)(4) then requires be retained for **6 months**.)*

---

## B. § 35.331(a) — the eight required contents

Every written agreement caught by § 35.281 must contain all eight.

### B.1 (1) The Real Estate Recovery Fund notification

> *"Notification that a **Real Estate Recovery Fund** exists to reimburse a person who has **obtained a final
> civil judgment against a Commonwealth real estate licensee owing to fraud, misrepresentation or deceit in a
> real estate transaction** and who has been **unable to collect the judgment after exhausting legal and
> equitable remedies**. Details about the Fund may be obtained by calling the Commission at **(717)
> 783-3658**."*

**Every condition is a hurdle**, and a licensee should be able to explain them:

1. **A final civil judgment** — not a complaint, not a Commission disciplinary finding, not a settlement.
2. **Against a Pennsylvania real estate licensee.**
3. **Owing to fraud, misrepresentation or deceit** — not negligence, not a bad outcome.
4. **In a real estate transaction.**
5. **Unable to collect after exhausting legal and equitable remedies.**

chunks.heading: B.2 (2) The escrow notification
chunks.excerpt:
**The Fund is not insurance and it is not a complaint remedy.** It is a payer of last resort standing behind
an uncollectable judgment. **This course states no payment limit, per-licensee cap or aggregate cap**,
because the Real Estate Licensing and Registration Act was not read for this project.

### B.2 (2) The escrow notification

> *"Notification that **payments of money received by the broker on account of a sale** — regardless of the
> form of payment and the person designated as payee — **shall be held by the broker in an escrow account
> pending consummation of the sale or a prior termination thereof**."*

Note *"regardless of the form of payment and the person designated as payee."* A cheque made out to someone
else does not escape the escrow duty. Module PA-P-06 develops this.

### B.3 (3) The negotiation notification — read it twice

> *"Notification that **the broker's commission AND the duration of the agreement have been determined as a
> result of negotiations** between the broker, or a licensee employed by the broker, and the seller/landlord
> or buyer/tenant."*

**Two things are declared negotiated, not one.** The **commission** and the **duration**.

Compensation in Pennsylvania is **not** set by the Commission, by any trade association, by any multiple
listing service, or by any course — and the rule requires the agreement to **say so on its face.** **No
commission rate, split, or minimum appears anywhere in this build**, and every practice problem supplies its
rate as a given inside the problem.

The duration half is equally deliberate, and it connects to § 35.332(c)(1) and (2) below: a listing period is
negotiated, capped at one year, and cannot renew itself.

### B.4 (4) through (6)

chunks.heading: B.5 (7) and (8) — the mirrored disclosures
chunks.excerpt:
> **(4)** *"A **description of the services to be provided and the fees to be charged**."*
> **(5)** *"Notification about the **possibility that the broker or any licensee employed by the broker may
> provide services to more than one party in a single transaction**, and an explanation of **the duties owed
> to the other party** and **the fees which the broker may receive** for those services."*
> **(6)** *"Notification of the licensee's **continuing duty to disclose in a reasonably practicable period of
> time any conflict of interest**."*

**(5) is the dual agency warning, given at the front end.** Before anyone is in a transaction, the consumer is
told the firm may end up serving both sides, what the other party would be owed, and what the broker would be
paid. It is the same information § 35.314 and § 35.315 govern later, disclosed before the situation arises.

**(6) says the conflict duty is continuing.** It does not discharge at signing. § 35.283 governs disclosure of
interest, and § 35.292(a)(7) makes it one of the twelve unwaivable duties.

### B.5 (7) and (8) — the mirrored disclosures

chunks.heading: B.6 § 35.331(b) — incorporation by reference
chunks.excerpt:
> **(7)** *In an agreement between a **broker and a seller/landlord**: a statement regarding **cooperation with
> subagents and buyer agents**; a disclosure that **a buyer agent, even if compensated by the listing broker or
> seller/landlord, will represent the interests of the buyer/tenant**; and a disclosure of **any potential for
> the broker to act as a dual agent.***
>
> **(8)** *In an agreement between a **broker and a buyer/tenant**: an explanation that **the broker may be
> compensated based upon a percentage of the purchase price**; **the broker's policies regarding cooperation
> with listing brokers willing to pay buyer's brokers**; a disclosure that **the broker, even if compensated by
> the listing broker or seller/landlord, will represent the interests of the buyer/tenant**; and a disclosure of
> **any potential for the broker to act as a dual agent.***

**The same sentence appears on both sides**: a buyer agent represents the buyer **even if paid by the seller.**
The seller is told it in (7); the buyer is told it in (8). That is § 35.311(c) and § 35.313(c) written into
the paperwork so that neither party can later claim surprise.

**(8) also requires the buyer to be told something about the broker's own incentives** — that the fee may be a
**percentage of the purchase price**. A buyer's agent paid on percentage is paid more when the buyer pays
more, and Pennsylvania requires the buyer be told.

### B.6 § 35.331(b) — incorporation by reference

> *"To the extent that any of the information required in subsection (a) is set forth in the **disclosure
> summaries in §§ 35.336—35.338**, those provisions **need not be repeated, but may be incorporated by
> reference**."*

chunks.heading: C. § 35.332 — Exclusive listing agreements
chunks.excerpt:
A drafting convenience, and it has a practical consequence: the consumer notice and the written agreement are
**designed to work together**, which is another reason the notice must actually be delivered.

---

## C. § 35.332 — Exclusive listing agreements

### C.1 The two forms

> **(a)** *"An exclusive listing agreement may comprise one of the following:*
> **(1)** *"**The exclusive agency of the broker.**"*
> **(2)** *"**The exclusive right-to-sell or exclusive right-to-lease.**"*

The difference is **whether the owner can sell it themselves and owe nothing.** Under an **exclusive agency**,
the broker is the only broker — but an owner who finds their own buyer may owe no commission. Under an
**exclusive right-to-sell**, the broker earns on a sale during the listing period **by whomever made**.

### C.2 What must be in it — § 35.332(b)

**In addition to everything § 35.331 requires**:

> **(1)** *"The **sale or lease price**."*
> **(2)** *"The **commission, fees or other compensation** expected on the sale or lease price."*
> **(3)** *"The **duration of the agreement**."*
> **(4)** *In an **exclusive right-to-sell** agreement, ***"a statement in bold face type that the broker earns
> a commission on the sale of the property during the listing period by whomever made, including the
> owner."****
> **(5)** *In an **exclusive right-to-lease** agreement, **"a statement in bold print"** to the same effect for
> a lease **"by whomever made, including the lessor."***

chunks.heading: C.3 What it may NOT contain — § 35.332(c), all six
chunks.excerpt:
**The bold-face requirement exists because of what it says.** The single most common listing dispute is an
owner who sold to their own cousin and is astonished to owe a commission. Pennsylvania requires that
consequence be printed **in bold face**, in the agreement the owner signs, in the rule's own words: **"by
whomever made, including the owner."**

### C.3 What it may NOT contain — § 35.332(c), all six

> **(1)** ***"A listing period exceeding 1 year."***
> **(2)** ***"An automatic renewal clause."***
> **(3)** *"A **cancellation notice** to terminate the agreement at the end of the listing period set forth in
> the agreement."*
> **(4)** *"**Authority of the broker to execute a signed agreement of sale or lease for the owner** or
> lessor."*
> **(5)** *"**An option by the broker to purchase** the listed property."*
> **(6)** *"**Authority of the broker to confess judgment** against the owner or lessor for the Commission in
> the event of a sale or lease."*

Take them in pairs, because they group naturally.

**(1) and (2) — the listing must end, and it must end by itself.** Maximum **one year**, and **no automatic
renewal**. A listing that rolls over until cancelled is prohibited twice over.

**(3) removes the trap that would defeat (1) and (2).** An agreement cannot require the owner to give notice
in order to stop the listing **at its own stated end.** Without (3), a listing could technically expire while
practically continuing for anyone who forgot to send a letter.

chunks.heading: D. Two practical sequences
chunks.excerpt:
**(4) and (6) — the broker does not get to act for the owner or against them.** No **authority to sign an
agreement of sale for the owner**; no **confession of judgment** for the commission. A confession of judgment
lets a creditor take judgment without the debtor's day in court, and Pennsylvania forecloses it in a listing
agreement outright.

**(5) — no option to purchase.** A broker holding an option to buy the property they are engaged to sell has
an interest directly opposed to the client's, and no amount of disclosure cures it in a listing agreement.

---

## D. Two practical sequences

### D.1 Taking a listing

1. **Consumer notice first** — the correct summary under § 35.284, signed, refusal noted if refused, copy
   given, acknowledgement filed.
2. **Confirm who is on title**, because the agreement must be signed by the owners — Module PA-F-04.
3. **Written agreement** under § 35.281, containing **all eight § 35.331 contents** plus the **three
   § 35.332(b) additions**, with the **bold-face by-whomever-made statement** if it is an exclusive
   right-to-sell.
4. **Check the six prohibitions in § 35.332(c)** before it is signed, not after.
5. **Duration and commission** stated as negotiated — § 35.331(a)(3).

### D.2 Taking on a buyer

Everything above, plus the § 35.331(a)(8) disclosures: **percentage compensation explained**, **cooperation
policy stated**, **representation notwithstanding who pays**, and **dual agency potential disclosed.**

---

## Module PA-P-04 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module PA-P-01. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100 percent**
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**.

**No item states a commission rate, split or minimum**, because compensation is negotiated and no course sets
it.

---

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module PA-P-04
chunks.excerpt:
## Instructor source note for Module PA-P-04

Drawn from **49 Pa. Code §§ 35.281, 35.283, 35.284, 35.286, 35.292, 35.311, 35.313, 35.314, 35.315, 35.331,
35.332 and 35.336—35.338**, read on 2026-08-20, current through **56 Pa.B. 3438 (June 6, 2026)**. Every
required content, prohibition, cap and quoted phrase above is **transcribed from that text.**

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** the **Real Estate Licensing and Registration Act**,
including the **Real Estate Recovery Fund** provisions; **Pennsylvania's Statute of Frauds**; and the
**verbatim text of the §§ 35.336—35.338 disclosure summaries.**

**No Recovery Fund payment limit, commission rate, or Statute of Frauds provision is stated in this module.**
The **one-year maximum listing period**, the **six prohibited provisions**, the **bold-face requirement** and
the **Commission telephone number** are transcribed from § 35.331 and § 35.332.

lessons.title: Pennsylvania Real Estate Practice — Module PA-P-05

chunks.heading: Pennsylvania Real Estate Practice — Module PA-P-05
chunks.excerpt:
# Pennsylvania Real Estate Practice — Module PA-P-05

## Agreements of sale and statements of estimated cost — §§ 35.333, 35.334

**Course:** Real Estate Practice · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 45.0
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Pennsylvania prelicensing credit is available.

## Learning objectives

1. Recite the eleven contents § 35.333(a) requires in an agreement of sale.
2. State the zoning-classification requirement, its exception, and the consequence of omitting it.
3. State the six additional contents required where the agreement is mortgage-contingent.
4. State the two provisions that must be printed in bold face if used.
5. State the time-share and campground cancellation statement and its formatting requirement.
6. Apply § 35.334 — when the estimate is due, to whom, and to what standard of accuracy.

---

## A. § 35.333(a) — the eleven required contents

An agreement of sale, other than for a cemetery lot, mausoleum or cremation space, **shall contain**:

chunks.heading: A.1 Item (7) is the agency disclosure, restated in the contract
chunks.excerpt:
> **(1)** *"The **date of the agreement**."*
> **(2)** *"The **names of the buyer and seller**."*
> **(3)** *"A **description of the property and the interest to be conveyed**."*
> **(4)** *"The **sale price**."*
> **(5)** *"The **dates for payment and conveyance**."*
> **(6)** The **zoning classification** — see Part B.
> **(7)** *"A statement **identifying the capacity in which the broker, or a licensee employed by the broker
> is involved in the transaction and whether services have been provided to another party in the
> transaction**."*
> **(8)** The **escrow provision** — *"payments of money received by the broker on account of the sale —
> regardless of the form of payment and the person designated as payee — shall be held by the broker in an
> escrow account pending consummation of the sale or a prior termination thereof."*
> **(9)** The **Real Estate Recovery Fund statement**, in the words the rule prints — see Part C.
> **(10)** *"A statement that **access to a public road may require issuance of a highway occupancy permit
> from the Department of Transportation**."*
> **(11)** For a **time share or campground membership**, the **cancellation statement** — see Part E.

**A cemetery agreement** must contain **(1) through (5) and (9)** only — § 35.333(d).

### A.1 Item (7) is the agency disclosure, restated in the contract

> *"A statement identifying **the capacity in which the broker ... is involved** ... and **whether services
> have been provided to another party** in the transaction."*

chunks.heading: B. § 35.333(a)(6) — the zoning classification, and the consequence Pennsylvania attaches to omitting it
chunks.excerpt:
Whatever relationship was disclosed at the initial interview under § 35.284, and whatever agreement was
signed under § 35.281, the **agreement of sale itself must say what the licensee is.** Consumer notice,
written agreement, and contract all carry it. A licensee who is a **transaction licensee**, a **dual agent**,
or a **designated agent** says so here.

---

## B. § 35.333(a)(6) — the zoning classification, and the consequence Pennsylvania attaches to omitting it

> *"The **zoning classification of the property**, except if the property (or **each parcel thereof, if
> subdividable**) is **zoned solely or primarily to permit single-family dwellings**, together with a
> statement that **the failure of the agreement of sale to contain the zoning classification of the property
> shall render the agreement voidable at the option of the buyer** and, **if voided, deposits tendered by the
> buyer shall be returned to the buyer without a requirement of court action**."*

Four points, and every one is examinable.

**The exception is narrow.** It applies where the property is zoned **solely or primarily** for
**single-family dwellings** — and where a tract is **subdividable**, the test applies to **each parcel
thereof.** A duplex, a mixed-use building, a commercial parcel, farmland and a subdividable tract all need
the classification stated.

**The classification alone is not enough.** The rule requires the classification **"together with a
statement"** of the consequence. Two things go in, not one.

**The consequence runs one way.** The agreement is **voidable at the option of the buyer.** A seller cannot
use the omission to escape a deal they regret; only the buyer may void.

chunks.heading: C. § 35.333(a)(9) — the Recovery Fund statement, in the rule's own words
chunks.excerpt:
**The deposit comes back without litigation.** *"**Without a requirement of court action**."* This is a
genuine exception to the ordinary escrow-dispute machinery in § 35.327, where a broker holds until the
dispute resolves and may need to interplead. Where an agreement is voided under (a)(6), the rule itself
directs the return.

**This course states no zoning classification, district name, setback or use category**, because
Pennsylvania's Municipalities Planning Code and every local ordinance were **not read for this project.** The
classification comes from the **municipality**, and a licensee obtains it rather than guessing at it.

---

## C. § 35.333(a)(9) — the Recovery Fund statement, in the rule's own words

> *"A Real Estate Recovery Fund exists to reimburse any person who has obtained a final civil judgment
> against a Pennsylvania real estate licensee owing to fraud, misrepresentation, or deceit in a real estate
> transaction and who has been unable to collect the judgment after exhausting all legal and equitable
> remedies. For complete details about the Fund, call (717) 783-3658."*

**The rule prints this statement.** It also appears, in slightly different words, in **§ 35.331(a)(1)** for
written agreements between a broker and a consumer. A licensee meets it twice in every listed transaction.

**What it covers, and does not:** a **final civil judgment**, against a **licensee**, for **fraud,
misrepresentation or deceit**, in a **real estate transaction**, that the claimant **could not collect after
exhausting legal and equitable remedies.** Not negligence. Not a bad outcome. Not a Commission disciplinary
finding. **No payment limit is stated in this build**, because RELRA was not read.

---

## D. § 35.333(b) — the mortgage-contingent agreement

chunks.heading: E. § 35.333(a)(11) — the time-share and campground cancellation statement
chunks.excerpt:
> *"An agreement of sale that is **conditioned upon the ability of the buyer to obtain a mortgage** shall
> contain:*
> **(1)** *"The **type of mortgage**."*
> **(2)** *"The **mortgage principal**."*
> **(3)** *"The **maximum interest rate** of the mortgage."*
> **(4)** *"The **minimum term** of the mortgage."*
> **(5)** *"The **deadline for the buyer to obtain the mortgage**."*
> **(6)** *"The **nature and extent of assistance that the broker will render to the buyer in obtaining the
> mortgage**."*

Six items, and notice which way three of them point.

**"Maximum interest rate" and "minimum term" define the financing the buyer must accept.** If a lender offers
a loan **within** those limits, the buyer has obtained the financing the contract described — the contingency
is satisfied and the buyer is bound. If the only available loan exceeds the maximum rate or falls short of
the minimum term, it is not the loan the contract described. **Leaving these blank, or filling them in
carelessly, is how a buyer ends up committed to financing they never intended to accept.**

**(5) is a deadline, and deadlines in a contract are the licensee's business to track.**

**(6) is unusual and worth noting:** the agreement must state **what the broker will actually do** to help the
buyer get the mortgage. Pennsylvania requires the broker's own role to be written down.

**This course states no interest rate, term, qualifying ratio or lender requirement.** Those come from the
lender, and Module PA-F-06 records that the federal lending regulations were not read for this project.

---

## E. § 35.333(a)(11) — the time-share and campground cancellation statement

chunks.heading: F. § 35.333(c) — the two provisions that must be bold if used
chunks.excerpt:
> *"a statement regarding the purchaser's right of cancellation that is set forth **conspicuously in bold
> face type of at least 10 point size immediately above the signature line for the purchaser** and that is in
> substantially the following form:*
>
> *"**You, the purchaser, may cancel this purchase at any time prior to midnight of the fifth day following
> the date of this transaction.** If you desire to cancel, you are required to **notify the seller, in
> writing**, at (insert address). Such notice shall be given by **certified return receipt mail or by any
> other bona fide means of delivery which provides you with a receipt.** Such notice shall be effective **upon
> being postmarked** by the United States Postal Service or **upon deposit of the notice with any bona fide
> means of delivery which provides you with a receipt.**"*

Five requirements packed into one paragraph:

1. **Bold face type of at least 10 point size.**
2. **Immediately above the purchaser's signature line** — not elsewhere in the document.
3. **Midnight of the fifth day** following the date of the transaction.
4. **Written notice**, by **certified return receipt mail** or another **bona fide means of delivery providing
   a receipt.**
5. **Effective on postmark or deposit** — not on the seller's receipt of it.

Point 5 is the one that protects the purchaser: a cancellation posted on the fifth day is effective, whatever
happens to it afterwards.

---

## F. § 35.333(c) — the two provisions that must be bold if used

chunks.heading: G. § 35.334 — Statements of estimated cost and return
chunks.excerpt:
> *"The following terms **shall be printed in bold face if made part of an agreement of sale**:*
> **(1)** *"A provision **relieving the seller from responsibility for defects** involving the sale property,
> or a provision **requiring the buyer to execute a release to that effect at the time of settlement**, or a
> provision of **similar import**."*
> **(2)** *"A provision **reserving to the builder-seller the right to change, or depart from, the building
> specifications** for the sale property."*

Both are provisions a buyer would very much want to notice, and both are the kind a buyer would very easily
miss. Pennsylvania's answer is not to prohibit them but to require they be **conspicuous.**

**Note "or a provision of similar import" in (1).** The rule reaches the substance, not the label. A clause
that achieves the same effect by different words is caught.

**And note that (1) reaches a release signed later.** A provision requiring the buyer to sign a release **at
settlement** must be bold **in the agreement of sale** — so that the buyer knows at signing what they will be
asked to sign at the table.

---

## G. § 35.334 — Statements of estimated cost and return

chunks.heading: G.1 Four features of this rule
chunks.excerpt:
> **(a)** *"**Before an agreement of sale is executed**, the brokers involved in the transaction shall provide
> **each party** with a **written estimate of reasonably foreseeable expenses** associated with the sale that
> the party may be expected to pay, including, **but not limited to**:*
> **(1)** *"The **broker's commission**."*
> **(2)** *"The **mortgage payments and financing costs**."*
> **(3)** *"**Taxes and assessments**."*
> **(4)** *"**Settlement expenses**."*
>
> **(b)** *"The estimates of costs required under subsection (a) shall be **as accurate as may be reasonably
> expected of a person having knowledge of, and experience in, real estate sales**."*

### G.1 Four features of this rule

**The timing is "before an agreement of sale is executed."** Not before settlement, when the numbers are
known and it is too late to reconsider. Before signing.

**"The brokers involved" — plural — and "each party."** Both sides' brokers, both parties. A buyer's agent
does not rely on the listing broker having done it.

**"Including, but not limited to."** The four items are a floor. A transaction with an assessment pending, a
transfer tax split, a homeowner association capital contribution or a fuel adjustment includes those too.

**The standard in (b) is competence, not effort.** *"As accurate as may be reasonably expected of a person
having **knowledge of, and experience in, real estate sales**."* Not best efforts, not good faith — the
accuracy a professional in this business ought to achieve.

### G.2 The rule prints an exemplary statement

**§ 35.334(c)** sets out a **Statement of Estimated Costs to Buyer at Settlement** as exemplary of the
requirement. Its line items are the map of a Pennsylvania closing:

chunks.heading: G.3 A worked estimate, all rates given
chunks.excerpt:
**Purchase price · payment on account · balance at settlement.** Then estimated closing expenses — **title
search and insurance; conveyancing or preparation of papers; recording fees for the deed and the mortgage;
the mortgagee's charges — appraisal fee, credit report, origination and placement fees; mortgage service
charge; fire insurance.** Then miscellaneous charges — **local realty transfer tax** and **Pennsylvania realty
transfer tax.**

**Two transfer taxes, local and state.** A licensee estimating costs on a Pennsylvania sale computes both, or
computes neither correctly.

**This course states no realty transfer tax rate, state or local**, because Pennsylvania's transfer tax
statutes and every local ordinance were **not read for this project.** Every practice problem supplies both
rates as givens inside the problem.

### G.3 A worked estimate, all rates given

*Purchase price $315,000; deposit $10,000; state realty transfer tax 1 percent and local realty transfer tax
1 percent, split evenly between buyer and seller by the agreement; title search and insurance $2,150;
conveyancing $350; recording fees $195; mortgagee's charges $1,780; first-year fire insurance $1,020.*

Transfer tax total = 315,000 × 0.02 = **$6,300**; the buyer's half = **$3,150.**
Balance at settlement before expenses = 315,000 − 10,000 = **$305,000.**
Estimated closing expenses = 2,150 + 350 + 195 + 1,780 + 1,020 + 3,150 = **$8,645.**
**Estimated cash the buyer brings, before any mortgage proceeds, = $313,645.**

*(Rates are given inside the problem. Substitute the current statutory and local rates before delivery.)*

---

## Module PA-P-05 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module PA-P-05
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items, delivered as in Module PA-P-01. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100 percent**
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**.

**Every rate in every item is supplied inside the item as a given.**

## Instructor source note for Module PA-P-05

Drawn from **49 Pa. Code §§ 35.281, 35.284, 35.327, 35.331, 35.333 and 35.334**, read on 2026-08-20, current
through **56 Pa.B. 3438 (June 6, 2026)**. Every required content, quoted statement and formatting requirement
above is **transcribed from that text**, including the **Recovery Fund statement** and the **time-share

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** the **Real Estate Licensing and Registration Act**,

transfer tax ordinance**; the **Municipalities Planning Code** and every local zoning ordinance; **PennDOT's

**No transfer tax rate, Recovery Fund limit, zoning classification, permit requirement, interest rate or

lessons.title: Pennsylvania Real Estate Practice — Module PA-P-06

chunks.heading: Pennsylvania Real Estate Practice — Module PA-P-06
chunks.excerpt:
# Pennsylvania Real Estate Practice — Module PA-P-06

## Escrow — §§ 35.321 to 35.328

**Course:** Real Estate Practice · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 45.0
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Pennsylvania prelicensing credit is available.

> **Escrow is where licences are lost.** Every other rule in this course can be broken by carelessness;
> these can be broken by carelessness **and** they involve other people's money. Eight sections, and a
> licensee should be able to state each of them from memory.

## Learning objectives

1. State the escrow duty, who it falls on, and the one category of money it does not reach.
2. State that the duty cannot be waived, and by whom it cannot be waived.
3. Allocate the escrow duty in a cobrokerage transaction under the three § 35.323 cases.
4. State the deposit deadline and the single exception with both of its conditions.
5. State the four characteristics an escrow account must have.
6. State the commingling prohibition and the two permitted deposits of the broker's own money.
7. Apply § 35.327 when entitlement is disputed.
8. Recite the six escrow records § 35.328 requires.

---

## A. § 35.321 — the duty to deposit

chunks.heading: A.1 The one carve-out — rents
chunks.excerpt:
> **(a)** *"a broker shall **deposit money that the broker receives belonging to another into an escrow
> account in a Federally or State-insured bank or depository** to be **held pending consummation of the
> transaction or a prior termination thereof that does not involve a dispute** between the parties, at which
> time the broker shall **pay over the full amount to the party entitled to receive it**. **If a broker is a
> partnership, association or corporation, its broker of record shall be responsible for ensuring that the
> escrow duty is performed.**"*

Four things in one subsection.

**The duty is the broker's**, and in an entity it is the **broker of record** who must ensure it happens. A
salesperson who receives a deposit is handling the broker's obligation.

**"Money ... belonging to another."** That is the test. Not "earnest money," not "deposits" — **money
belonging to somebody else.**

**Held pending consummation or a prior termination "that does not involve a dispute."** Where there **is** a
dispute, § 35.327 takes over and the money stays put.

**Pay over the FULL amount to the party entitled.** Not net of anything.

### A.1 The one carve-out — rents

> **(b)** *"A broker is **not required to hold in escrow rents** that he receives as a property manager for a
> lessor. A broker shall **deposit rents received into a rental management account that is separate from the
> broker's escrow and general business accounts**."*

**Rents are not escrow — but they are not the broker's money either.** They go into a **third** account, a
**rental management account**, separate from **both** the escrow account and the general business account.

chunks.heading: A.2 Security deposits — when the duty to pay over arises
chunks.excerpt:
**Three accounts, three purposes.** A broker who runs rents through the general business account has
commingled, whatever they call it.

### A.2 Security deposits — when the duty to pay over arises

> **(e)** *"If a broker receives a **security deposit** belonging to another under a lease agreement, the
> broker's **duty to pay over the deposit ... shall arise when the tenancy ends**."*

And on a mid-tenancy change of ownership or management, the broker **may transfer the security deposit** to
the escrow account of the lessor or the lessor's broker — but only **upon notification in writing to each
tenant** from whom a deposit was received, stating **the name and address of the banking institution** where
the deposits will be held and **the amount of the deposits.**

**A security deposit is not a rent.** It is money belonging to another, held in escrow, and it moves only with
written notice to the tenant.

### A.3 Two special consummation rules

> **(c)** Under an **installment land purchase agreement**, the transaction is consummated for escrow purposes
> *"when the buyer has been afforded the opportunity, by means of the **seller's written acknowledgement on or
> affixed to the agreement, to record the agreement**, unless the agreement specifies otherwise."*
>
> **(d)** Under an agreement of sale involving **cemetery property**, consummated *"when the **buyer receives a
> copy of the agreement of sale**."*

---

## B. § 35.322 — the duty cannot be waived

> *"A broker's escrow duty **may not be waived or altered by an agreement** between **the parties to the
> transaction**, between **the broker and the parties**, or between **the broker and other brokers** who may
> be involved in the transaction."*

chunks.heading: C. § 35.323 — cobrokerage: who holds it
chunks.excerpt:
**Three groupings, all of them closed.** Buyer and seller cannot agree it away between themselves. The broker
cannot get the parties to sign it away. Brokers cannot arrange it among themselves.

There is exactly **one** place in these sections where the parties' written permission changes anything, and
it is § 35.324(b)'s narrow timing exception — which delays a deposit, not the duty.

---

## C. § 35.323 — cobrokerage: who holds it

Three cases, and the difference between the second and third is **prior notice.**

| Case | Deposit tendered to | Who holds it |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | the **listing broker** | **The listing broker.** |
| **(b)** | the **selling broker**, buyer having **prior notice** it goes to the listing broker | **The listing broker.** |
| **(c)** | the **selling broker**, **without** that prior notice | **The selling broker.** |

### C.1 What "prior notice" requires — and it is not casual

Under **(b)** the selling broker *"shall require the buyer to **acknowledge in writing, prior to his signing
the agreement of sale**, that the prior notice contained the following information":*

> **(1)** *"The **name of the listing broker**."*
> **(2)** *"That the **selling broker's acceptance of the buyer's deposit is on behalf of the listing broker as
> subagent for the listing broker**."*
> **(3)** *"That the **listing broker is a licensed real estate broker who is required to hold the deposit in
> escrow**."*
> **(4)** *"That the **listing broker be designated as payee**, if the buyer's deposit is in the form of a
> check."*

**Four items, acknowledged in writing, before the buyer signs the agreement of sale.** Miss any of it and
subsection (c) applies: **the selling broker holds the money**, and holds the duty with it.

chunks.heading: D. § 35.324 — the deadline
chunks.excerpt:
**Note item (4).** The cheque should be made payable to the **listing broker**. And note § 35.331(a)(2) and
§ 35.333(a)(8), which both say the escrow duty applies *"regardless of the form of payment and the person
designated as payee"* — so a cheque made out to the wrong party does not defeat the duty; it just makes a
mess.

---

## D. § 35.324 — the deadline

> **(a)** *"a broker shall deposit money belonging to another into an escrow account **by the end of the next
> business day following its receipt in the real estate office where the escrow records are maintained**."*

**Next business day.** And note the clock's starting point: **receipt in the office where the escrow records
are maintained** — not receipt by the salesperson in a car park.

### D.1 The single exception, with both conditions

> **(b)** *"If the money ... has been tendered to the broker **in the form of a check under an offer to
> purchase or lease** real estate, the broker **may, with the written permission of both the buyer and the
> seller or the lessee and the lessor**, refrain from depositing the money ... by the deadline in subsection
> (a) **pending the seller's or lessor's acceptance of the offer**. The broker shall **deposit the check into
> an escrow account within 1 business day of the seller's or lessor's acceptance of the offer**."*

**Three conditions together:**

1. The money is **a check** — not cash, not a wire.
2. Tendered **under an offer** to purchase or lease.
3. **Written permission of BOTH sides.**

**And the exception buys a delay, not a discharge.** Once the offer is accepted, the check goes in **within 1
business day.**

chunks.heading: E. § 35.325 — what the account must be
chunks.excerpt:
**This is the only place the parties' agreement affects the escrow duty at all** — which is exactly consistent
with § 35.322, because it alters **timing**, not the duty.

---

## E. § 35.325 — what the account must be

> **(a)** *"An escrow account shall:*
> **(1)** *"Be maintained in a **Federally- or State-insured bank or recognized depository**."*
> **(2)** *"**Designate the broker as trustee.**"*
> **(3)** *"**Provide for the withdrawal of funds without prior notice.**"*
> **(4)** *"**Be used exclusively for escrow purposes.**"*

**(3) is easily overlooked and it has a reason.** A certificate of deposit or a notice account, however
sensible as an investment, would delay a payout the broker may be obliged to make at once.

### E.1 Authority to move money — § 35.325(b)

A broker who is a **sole proprietor or broker of record** may give **an employee** written authority to
**deposit** into the account, and may give a **licensed** employee written authority to **withdraw** for
payments properly chargeable to the account.

**Read the asymmetry.** Any employee may be authorised to **put money in**. Only a **licensed** employee may
be authorised to **take money out** — and only in writing, and only for proper charges.

### E.2 Interest — § 35.325(c)

> *"If money is expected to be held in escrow for **more than 6 months**, the broker is **encouraged** to
> deposit the money into an **interest-bearing** escrow account. **Interest earned on an escrow account shall
> be held and disbursed, pro rata, in the same manner as the principal amount**, unless the parties direct
> otherwise by agreement. **A broker may not claim the interest earned on an escrow account**, unless the
> broker is a lessor as provided in section 511.2 of the Landlord and Tenant Act."*

chunks.heading: E.3 § 35.325(d) — the authorisation letter
chunks.excerpt:
**"Encouraged," not required** — the six-month interest-bearing provision is a recommendation. **But the
interest rule is mandatory:** interest follows the principal, **pro rata**, and **the broker may not claim
it.**

**Section 511.2 of the Landlord and Tenant Act was not read for this project**, and no rule about a lessor's
entitlement to escrow interest is stated in this build.

### E.3 § 35.325(d) — the authorisation letter

On written request, or under an office inspection under § 35.246, the broker shall provide the Commission
**a letter addressed to the bank authorising the release of records** pertaining to the account. The broker
cannot decline to let the Commission see the account.

---

## F. § 35.326 — commingling and misappropriation

> **(a)** *"a broker **may not commingle money that is required to be held in escrow — or interest earned on an
> escrow account — with business, personal or other funds**."*
> **(b)** *"A broker **may** deposit business or personal funds into an escrow account **to cover service
> charges assessed to the account by the bank** or **to maintain a minimum balance in the account as required
> by the regulations of the bank**."*
> **(c)** *"A broker **may not misappropriate** money that is required to be held in escrow — or interest
> earned — **for business, personal or other purposes**."*

**Commingling and misappropriation are two different violations.** **Commingling** is **mixing**;
**misappropriation** is **using**. A broker who parks escrow money in the business account for a week and
touches none of it has commingled without misappropriating — and has still violated (a).

chunks.heading: G. § 35.327 — when entitlement is disputed
chunks.excerpt:
**The two permitted deposits in (b) are exhaustive and tiny.** **Bank service charges** and a **required
minimum balance.** Nothing else the broker's own money may do inside that account.

**And note that (a) and (c) both reach the interest.** Interest earned on escrow is escrow money.

---

## G. § 35.327 — when entitlement is disputed

> *"If a dispute arises between the parties to a real estate transaction over entitlement to money that is
> being held in escrow by a broker, **the broker shall retain the money in escrow until the dispute is
> resolved**. If resolution of the dispute appears remote without legal action, the broker **may, following 30
> days' notice to the parties, petition the county court having jurisdiction in the matter to interplead the
> rival claimants**."*

### G.1 The rule in three sentences a licensee can actually use

**The broker does not decide who wins.** Not the seller because the seller is the client. Not the buyer
because the buyer is sympathetic. Not whoever complains loudest.

**The broker holds.** Until the dispute is resolved — by the parties' agreement, or by a court.

**If it will not resolve, the broker may go to court**, after **30 days' notice to the parties**, and ask the
court to make the claimants fight each other. **"May," not "shall"** — interpleader is an option, not an
obligation.

### G.2 The one place a deposit comes back without any of this

**§ 35.333(a)(6)**, from Module PA-P-05: where an agreement of sale omitted the required zoning classification
and the buyer voids it, *"deposits tendered by the buyer **shall be returned to the buyer without a
requirement of court action**."* That is a direction in the rule itself, not a broker's judgement call.

---

## H. § 35.328 — the six records

chunks.heading: I. The eight sections in one sequence
chunks.excerpt:
> *"A broker shall **keep records of monies received by him that are required to be held in escrow** and shall
> **produce the records for examination by the Commission** ... upon written request or pursuant to an office
> inspection under § 35.246. The records shall contain:*
>
> **(1)** *"The **name of the party from whom the broker received the money**."*
> **(2)** *"The **name of the party to whom the money belongs**."*
> **(3)** *"The **name of the party for whose account the money is deposited**."*
> **(4)** *"The **date the broker received the money**."*
> **(5)** *"The **date the broker deposited the money into the escrow account**."*
> **(6)** *"The **date the broker withdrew the money from the escrow account**."*

**Three names and three dates**, and they are chosen so that a reader can audit compliance from the record
alone.

**(1), (2) and (3) can all be different people** — the buyer hands it over, it belongs to the buyer until
consummation, and it is deposited for the account of the transaction. The rule wants all three because
assuming they are the same is how money ends up with the wrong person.

**(4) and (5) together prove the § 35.324 deadline was met.** Received Tuesday, deposited Wednesday: compliant
on the face of the record. Received Tuesday, deposited the following Monday: the record convicts.

**(6) proves the money left when it should have, and to nobody's account before then.**

**And this is separate from § 35.286's general retention rule** — three years following consummation for
records pertaining to a transaction.

---

## I. The eight sections in one sequence

chunks.heading: Module PA-P-06 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Receive** money belonging to another. *(§ 35.321)*
2. **Determine who holds it** if two brokers are involved — and whether the four-item written prior notice was
   given before the buyer signed. *(§ 35.323)*
3. **Deposit by the end of the next business day** — unless it is a check under an offer and **both** parties
   gave **written permission**, in which case within **1 business day of acceptance.** *(§ 35.324)*
4. **Into an account** that is insured, names the broker **as trustee**, allows withdrawal **without prior
   notice**, and is used **exclusively** for escrow. *(§ 35.325)*
5. **Do not mix and do not use** — except bank charges and a required minimum balance. *(§ 35.326)*
6. **Record** three names and three dates. *(§ 35.328)*
7. On consummation or an undisputed termination, **pay over the full amount to the party entitled.**
   *(§ 35.321)*
8. On a **dispute**, **hold** — and, if it will not resolve, **30 days' notice** and **interplead.**
   *(§ 35.327)*

**And none of it can be waived by anyone.** *(§ 35.322)*

---

## Module PA-P-06 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module PA-P-01. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100 percent**
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**.

---

## Instructor source note for Module PA-P-06

Drawn from **49 Pa. Code §§ 35.246, 35.286, 35.321 to 35.328, 35.331 and 35.333**, read on 2026-08-20, current
through **56 Pa.B. 3438 (June 6, 2026)**. Every deadline, prohibition, required record and quoted phrase above
is **transcribed from that text.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module PA-P-06
chunks.excerpt:
**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** the **Real Estate Licensing and Registration Act**,
including **§ 455.604(a)(5)**, which § 35.292(a)(5) cites; and the **Pennsylvania Landlord and Tenant Act**,
including **section 511.2 (68 P.S. § 250.511b)**, which § 35.325(c) cites.

**No statutory penalty, security deposit limit, lessor interest entitlement or Landlord and Tenant Act
provision is stated in this module.** The **next-business-day** deadline, the **1 business day** post-acceptance
deadline, the **6-month** interest recommendation and the **30 days' notice** before interpleader are all

# Pennsylvania Real Estate Practice — Module PA-P-07

## Seller disclosure and material defects — §§ 35.284a, 35.335a

**Course:** Real Estate Practice · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 45.0
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Pennsylvania prelicensing credit is available.

> ### A submission gate stated at the top of this module
>
> **§ 35.335a sets out, in full inside the regulation, the minimum disclosures a seller's property disclosure
> statement must contain** — an itemised list running through the roof, the structure, the systems, water and
> sewer, hazardous substances and much else.
>
> **This project read § 35.335a's opening statements and its definition of a material defect, both transcribed
> below. It did NOT transcribe the itemised disclosures, and no document in this build reproduces, describes
> or paraphrases any of them.**
>
> **68 Pa.C.S. Chapter 73, the Real Estate Seller Disclosure Law itself, was NOT obtained.** Every statement
> below about what the Law requires is drawn from **§ 35.284a and § 35.292(a)(4)**, which cite it. **Obtaining
> Chapter 73 and the full § 35.335a itemisation is a submission gate.**

## Learning objectives

1. State the two things § 35.284a requires a licensee to do.
2. State the seller's disclosure obligation in the words § 35.335a uses.
3. Apply the definition of a material defect — including the sentence about useful life.
4. Explain what the disclosure statement is not.
5. Connect the seller's obligation to the licensee's own duties under § 35.292 and § 35.312(a)(2).
6. Identify what a licensee does when a seller declines to disclose something the licensee knows.

---

## A. § 35.284a — what the licensee must do

chunks.heading: B. § 35.335a — the seller's obligation, in the rule's own words
chunks.excerpt:
> *"Disclosures required by the Real Estate Seller Disclosure Law"* — the licensee shall, among the
> obligations the section states:
>
> **(2)** *"**Provide sellers with a property disclosure statement that meets or exceeds the disclosures set
> forth in § 35.335a** (relating to seller property disclosure statement)."*

**"Meets or exceeds."** § 35.335a is a **floor**, not a ceiling. A form that asks more is compliant; a form
that asks less is not.

**And note whose obligation is whose.** The **seller** discloses. The **licensee** provides the seller with a
conforming statement. Those are two different acts by two different people, and confusing them is the source
of the most serious error in this area — a licensee filling in the seller's form.

**§ 35.292(a)(4)** puts the same obligation among the twelve duties owed to **all consumers** and **not
waivable**:

> *"**Comply with 68 Pa.C.S. Chapter 73** (relating to Real Estate Seller Disclosure Law)."*

So a failure here is a failure of § 35.292 as well as of § 35.284a.

---

## B. § 35.335a — the seller's obligation, in the rule's own words

The rule opens the disclosure statement with these paragraphs, transcribed:

chunks.heading: B.1 The seller's obligation has three limits built into one sentence
chunks.excerpt:
> ***"A seller must disclose to a buyer all known material defects about property being sold that are not
> readily observable.*** *This disclosure statement is designed to **assist the seller in complying with
> disclosure requirements** and to **assist the buyer in evaluating the property being considered**."*
>
> *"This statement **discloses the seller's knowledge of the condition of the property as of the date signed
> by the seller** and is **not a substitute for any inspections or warranties that the buyer may wish to
> obtain**. This statement is **not a warranty of any kind by the seller** or **a warranty or representation
> by any listing real estate broker, any selling real estate broker or their agents**. **The buyer is
> encouraged to address concerns about the condition of the property that may not be included in this
> statement.** **This statement does not relieve the seller of the obligation to disclose a material defect
> that may not be addressed on this form.**"*

### B.1 The seller's obligation has three limits built into one sentence

> *"A seller must disclose to a buyer **all known material defects** about property being sold **that are not
> readily observable**."*

**Known.** The seller discloses what the seller knows. The Law does not, on this text, require the seller to
investigate.

**Material defects.** Not every imperfection — the defined term in B.2 below.

**Not readily observable.** A condition a buyer can plainly see is not the target of the rule. The purpose is
to surface what a buyer **cannot** see.

### B.2 The definition — and the last sentence, which is the examinable one

chunks.heading: C. What the statement is not — four denials in one paragraph
chunks.excerpt:
> ***"A material defect is a problem with the property or any portion of it that would have a significant
> adverse impact on the value of the residential real property or that involves an unreasonable risk to people
> on the land. The fact that a structural element, system or subsystem is near, at or beyond the end of its
> normal useful life is not by itself a material defect."***

**Two alternative branches, and either one suffices:**

1. A problem with **significant adverse impact on value**, **or**
2. A problem involving an **unreasonable risk to people on the land.**

A condition that endangers people qualifies **even if it costs little to fix.** A condition that guts the
value qualifies **even if nobody is at risk.**

**And then the sentence that decides most real questions:**

> *"**The fact that a structural element, system or subsystem is near, at or beyond the end of its normal
> useful life is not by itself a material defect.**"*

**A twenty-eight-year-old roof is old. Old is not, by itself, a defect.** A twenty-eight-year-old roof that
**leaks** is a defect. The Law distinguishes **age** from **condition**, and the words *"by itself"* are doing
the work — age is not disqualifying evidence either, it is simply not sufficient on its own.

This is the single most useful thing a licensee can explain to an anxious seller, and it takes one sentence:
**you are not being asked to certify that everything is new; you are being asked to disclose what you know is
wrong.**

---

## C. What the statement is not — four denials in one paragraph

The rule's own second paragraph disclaims four things, and a licensee should be able to state all four:

chunks.heading: C.1 Denial 3 protects the licensee — and denial 4 removes the seller's escape
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Not a substitute for inspections or warranties the buyer may wish to obtain.**
2. **Not a warranty of any kind by the seller.**
3. **Not a warranty or representation by any listing broker, selling broker, or their agents.**
4. **Not a release** — *"does not relieve the seller of the obligation to disclose a material defect that may
   not be addressed on this form."*

### C.1 Denial 3 protects the licensee — and denial 4 removes the seller's escape

**Denial 3** is why a licensee must never adopt the seller's answers as their own. The statement is the
**seller's** knowledge as of the **date the seller signed it.** A licensee who says "the disclosure says the
basement is dry" has repeated the seller's statement; a licensee who says "the basement is dry" has made a
representation the rule expressly says the form is not.

**Denial 4 is the answer to the most common seller question:** *"It's not on the form — do I have to say
anything?"* **Yes.** The form is a **prompt**, not the boundary of the duty. A material defect the form does
not ask about is still a material defect the seller must disclose.

---

## D. Where the licensee's own duties come in

The seller's obligation and the licensee's are **separate**, and a licensee who conflates them will get the
answer wrong in the direction that produces liability.

chunks.heading: D.1 The seller who instructs you to stay quiet
chunks.excerpt:
| | The seller | The licensee |
|---|---|---|
| Source | **68 Pa.C.S. Chapter 73**, via **§ 35.335a** | **§ 35.292(a)** and the relationship rules |
| Scope | **Known material defects not readily observable** | **The twelve unwaivable duties**, plus relationship duties |
| Honesty | Must not misstate what they know | **§ 35.292(a)(2)** — *"deal honestly and in good faith"* — to **all consumers** |
| Confidentiality | — | **§ 35.312(a)(2)**: a seller's agent owes confidentiality ***"except that a licensee has a duty to reveal known material defects about the property"*** |

### D.1 The seller who instructs you to stay quiet

**§ 35.312(a)(2)** answers it before the question arises. The seller's agent's confidentiality duty is written
with the exception **inside it**:

> *"**Confidentiality, except that a licensee has a duty to reveal known material defects about the
> property.**"*

There is no conflict to resolve, because **confidentiality never covered it.** § 35.314(b)(3) states the same
exception for a **dual agent.**

And even if it did not, **§ 35.292(a)(2)** — deal honestly and in good faith — is owed to **all consumers**,
including the buyer on the other side, and **may not be waived.**

So the instruction is refused. Not negotiated, not documented and quietly ignored — **refused**, and the
reason given.

### D.2 What a licensee is not required to do

**§ 35.292(b):** *"A licensee is **not required to conduct an independent inspection of the property**."*

**§ 35.292(c):** *"A licensee is **not required to independently verify the accuracy or completeness of any
representation made by the consumer** ... **which the licensee reasonably believes to be accurate and
reliable**."*

chunks.heading: E. What the licensee actually does, in order
chunks.excerpt:
**Both shelters have a limit and it is the same limit: what you actually know or reasonably believe.** (b)
excuses you from inspecting; it does not excuse you from what you saw. (c) excuses you from verifying; it does
not excuse reliance on a statement you had reason to doubt. A seller who writes "no water infiltration" on a
form, in a basement with a visible tide line and a running dehumidifier, has made a statement the licensee no
longer reasonably believes.

---

## E. What the licensee actually does, in order

1. **Provide the seller with a conforming statement** — one that **meets or exceeds** § 35.335a. § 35.284a(2).
2. **Explain the obligation**, in the rule's own terms: **known**, **material**, **not readily observable** —
   and that **age alone is not a defect.** That is compliance advice, which § 35.292(a)(12) requires; it is not
   legal advice.
3. **Do not complete it for the seller.** It is the seller's statement of the seller's knowledge, signed on a
   date.
4. **Do not adopt the seller's answers as your own.** Attribute them.
5. **Disclose what you know**, whatever the seller wrote — § 35.312(a)(2) and § 35.292(a)(2).
6. **Route the rest.** Where a condition needs a professional, § 35.292(a)(8) makes the referral a **duty**.
7. **Retain the records** — § 35.286: **3 years following consummation** for records pertaining to a
   transaction.

---

## F. Conditions a licensee routes rather than opines on

Module PA-F-03 introduced these; here is the practice consequence. **On every one of them, a licensee's job is
to identify the question and name who answers it:**

chunks.heading: Module PA-P-07 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**Lead-based paint** in pre-1978 target housing — the federal disclosure obligation, whose regulation this
project did not read. **Radon** — a current test, not an old result, and not a licensee's reassurance.
**Asbestos, mould, underground storage tanks, wetlands, on-lot septic suitability, well water quality.**
**Mine subsidence**, in a Commonwealth with Pennsylvania's mining history — a question for the Commonwealth's
own programme and an insurer, and **this project read no Pennsylvania mining or subsidence statute or
programme document.**

**A licensee who opines on any of these has stepped outside § 35.292(a)(8) and (12) simultaneously** — giving
advice beyond their expertise, and giving it as though it settled a legal or technical question.

---

## Module PA-P-07 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module PA-P-01. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100 percent**
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**.

**No item asks a student to recall or reproduce any itemised disclosure from § 35.335a, or any provision of
68 Pa.C.S. Chapter 73**, because this project obtained neither. Items test the **definition of a material
defect**, the **useful-life sentence**, the **four denials**, the **meets-or-exceeds standard**, the **separation
of the seller's obligation from the licensee's**, and the **material defect exception to confidentiality** — all
of which were read.

---

## Instructor source note for Module PA-P-07

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module PA-P-07
chunks.excerpt:
Drawn from **49 Pa. Code §§ 35.284a, 35.286, 35.292, 35.312, 35.314 and 35.335a**, read on 2026-08-20, current
through **56 Pa.B. 3438 (June 6, 2026)**. The **seller's disclosure obligation**, the **definition of a material
defect**, the **useful-life sentence** and the **four denials** are **transcribed verbatim from § 35.335a.**

**Not obtained, and therefore reproduced, described or paraphrased NOWHERE in this build:** **68 Pa.C.S.
Chapter 73, the Real Estate Seller Disclosure Law**; the **itemised disclosures in § 35.335a**; the **federal
lead-based paint regulations**; and Pennsylvania's **mining, subsidence, wetlands, septic and well** statutes
and programmes.

**No exemption from the Seller Disclosure Law, no itemised disclosure, no notice period, no radon action level,
no testing protocol and no remediation standard is stated in this module.**
