## Hour 53 — Virginia agency and license-law case lab

chunks.heading: 53.1 The method
chunks.excerpt:
## 53.1 The method

Every Virginia relationship problem is solved the same way, and the method is worth more than any
individual answer:

**One — who is engaged by whom?** That selects the duty section: § 54.1-2131 seller, § 54.1-2132
buyer, § 54.1-2133 landlord, § 54.1-2134 tenant, § 54.1-2135 management.

**Two — does a written brokerage agreement exist, and does it satisfy § 54.1-2137 C?** Definite
termination date or 90 days; fee and how and when paid; services; the supervising broker's name and
contact information under § 54.1-2110.1 B 6. On the buyer side, § 54.1-2132 A 1 requires it **before
showing property**.

**Three — were the § 54.1-2136 preconditions given?** The type of relationship proposed, and the
compensation and whether it is shared.

**Four — is anyone in the conversation neither a client nor represented?** If so, § 54.1-2138 A
requires written disclosure of any relationship with another party on a substantive discussion about
a specific property, no later than when specific real estate assistance is first provided,
conspicuously.

**Five — is the firm on both sides?** Then it is dual under § 54.1-2139, or designated under
§ 54.1-2139.1 with the supervising broker as dual — and written consent from **all** clients is
required, timed by 18VAC135-20-220 A 3, failing which 18VAC135-20-270 2 makes it a conflict of
interest.

**Six — what is the standard for the duty in question?** Ordinary care; actual knowledge; timely; in
writing.

**Seven — what must be retained, and for how long?** Three years, under 18VAC135-20-185 C 1,
§ 54.1-2138 D, and § 54.1-2110.1 B 7.

**Eight — remember § 54.1-2144.** The common law of agency is abrogated to the extent inconsistent.
Do not answer from national doctrine.

chunks.heading: 53.2 Case A — the buyer who was shown a house first
chunks.excerpt:
## 53.2 Case A — the buyer who was shown a house first

*Facts.* At an open house on Saturday, Licensee M meets a couple, talks with them about the property
for twenty minutes, and then drives them to two other listings that afternoon. On Sunday they sign a
buyer brokerage agreement dated Sunday, with no termination date. On Monday they offer on one of
Saturday's houses, which is listed by Licensee M's own firm.

*Resolution.*

**§ 54.1-2132 A 1 was breached on Saturday.** A licensee engaged by a buyer shall enter into a
brokerage agreement with the prospective buyer **prior to showing property**. Signing on Sunday does
not cure Saturday.

**§ 54.1-2136 must have preceded the relationship** — the type of relationship proposed and the
compensation and whether shared. Nothing in the facts shows it was given.

**§ 54.1-2138 A applied at the open house.** The couple were neither M's clients nor represented, and
M had a substantive discussion about a specific property; if M's firm had a relationship with the
seller, written disclosure was required no later than when specific real estate assistance was first
provided — which was, at the latest, when M drove them to other properties.

**The Sunday agreement terminates 90 days from its date** under § 54.1-2137 C 1, since it states none.

**Monday makes the firm dual or designated.** Written consent from all clients under § 54.1-2139 or
§ 54.1-2139.1, timed by 18VAC135-20-220 A 3, or it is a conflict of interest under 18VAC135-20-270 2.

## 53.3 Case B — the offer that was not presented

chunks.heading: 53.4 Case C — the confidence after closing
chunks.excerpt:
*Facts.* A listing licensee receives a written offer $40,000 below list from a buyer whose lender
letter is a pre-qualification. Believing it a waste of the seller's time, the licensee emails the
buyer's agent "seller isn't entertaining anything under list" and does not tell the seller. Three
weeks later the seller learns of it.

*Resolution.*

**18VAC135-20-300 3** — failure to tender promptly to the client every written offer, counteroffer and
rejection — is a misrepresentation or omission. **§ 54.1-2131 A 2 c** requires receiving and presenting
written offers in a timely manner, and it does so even when the property is already under contract,
which is a fortiori here.

**§ 54.1-2131 A 4**, ordinary care, and **A 1**, performance in accordance with the brokerage
agreement, are also engaged.

**The pre-qualification is not a ground for withholding.** It is a fact to present **with** the offer,
so the seller can weigh it. The licensee substituted their judgment for the client's, which is the
error the rule exists to prevent.

**Broker exposure** is decided by **18VAC135-20-330** — knew or should have known, and failed to take
reasonable action to remedy. A firm whose written policies under § 54.1-2110.1 B 2 d and whose
document review under B 1 would have caught it is in a very different position from one with neither.

## 53.4 Case C — the confidence after closing

*Facts.* Eighteen months after a sale closes, the former seller's licensee is representing a buyer.
The buyer is considering a property whose owner is that former seller. The licensee knows, from the
earlier engagement, the former seller's financial circumstances and the lowest figure they said they
would take.

*Resolution.*

chunks.heading: 53.5 Case D — the licensee's own purchase
chunks.excerpt:
**§ 54.1-2137 D.** After termination, expiration or completion of performance, the licensee owes no
further duties **except** to account and to **keep confidential** the client's personal and financial
information and anything the client asked be kept confidential — unless the law provides otherwise or
the client consents **in writing**.

So the confidentiality duty **survives**, and the licensee may not use or disclose the information for
the new client's benefit. This creates a genuine conflict with the duty owed to the current buyer
under § 54.1-2132 A 3 to promote their interests, and the resolution is not to split the difference:
it is to escalate to the principal broker and, if the conflict cannot be managed, to decline the
engagement as to this property. **§ 54.1-2138 C** requires written disclosure to all clients and
customers already involved if the licensee's relationship changes.

## 53.5 Case D — the licensee's own purchase

*Facts.* A licensee, personally, offers to buy a listed property from an elderly seller represented by
another firm, without mentioning their licence, and later resells it.

*Resolution.*

**§ 54.1-2138.2** requires a licensee to disclose an ownership interest in specific real property.
**18VAC135-20-155 B** makes clear the Board reaches conduct in a **personal capacity**: a licensee
failing to comply with Chapter 21 or the regulations in performing acts covered by § 54.1-2100 may be
charged **regardless of whether the acts are in a personal or professional capacity**. And
**§ 36-96.2 A**'s owner exemption from fair housing **does not inure to the benefit of any Real Estate
Board licensee, regardless of capacity** — so buying and selling personally does not step outside
either regime.

### Hour 53 engagement check

chunks.heading: Hour 54 — Fair housing and marketing case lab
chunks.excerpt:
**Question.** Resolve, with citations: a firm's Licensee P lists a house on 2 February with a written
agreement stating no termination date. On 20 May Licensee Q of the same firm brings a buyer with whom
Q signed a buyer agreement before showing anything. The seller accepts. No consent forms were signed
by anyone.

**Expected answer.** **The listing expired.** § 54.1-2137 C 1 — no definite termination date means the
agreement terminated **90 days after 2 February**, in early May, before 20 May. Unless it was extended
in writing, P had no brokerage agreement on 20 May, and § 54.1-2137 B requires an agreement before
providing brokerage services. **Q's side is compliant** as to timing — § 54.1-2132 A 1 requires the
agreement before showing property, and Q did that — though Q's agreement is subject to the same
§ 54.1-2137 C requirements. **The firm is on both sides**, so this is designated agency under
§ 54.1-2139.1 with the **supervising broker as dual agent**, or dual agency under § 54.1-2139;
**written consent from all clients was required**, timed under **18VAC135-20-220 A 3**, and its
absence makes this a **conflict of interest under 18VAC135-20-270 2**. Retention of any consents, once
obtained, is three years from execution under **18VAC135-20-185 C 1**.

## Hour 54 — Fair housing and marketing case lab

## 54.1 The audit method

**One — is any statement about people rather than property?** Advertising, conversation, screening
notes, or an internal email.

**Two — does it touch a protected basis?** Virginia's list from § 36-96.3: race, colour, religion,
national origin, sex, elderliness, source of funds, familial status, sexual orientation, gender
identity, military status, and disability. **Five of those are not federal.**

chunks.heading: 54.2 Case A — the neighbourhood question
chunks.excerpt:
**Three — which subdivision does the conduct fall under?** Refusal (A 1); terms and conditions (A 2);
advertising (A 3); representing unavailability (A 4); access to services (A 5); covenants (A 6);
blockbusting (A 7); disability refusal (A 8); disability terms (A 9).

**Four — is a disability accommodation or modification in play?** § 36-96.3 B (i) and (ii).

**Five — does the advertising comply with 18VAC135-20-190?**

**Six — what is the correction, and who has to be told?**

## 54.2 Case A — the neighbourhood question

*Facts.* A relocating buyer asks, "What are the families like in Ashford Green? Is it a good area for
someone like us?"

*Resolution.* Answering with any description of who lives there — by race, national origin, religion,
family composition, age — is **steering**, and a statement about the composition of an area falls
within § 36-96.3 A 1 and A 2 if it influences availability or terms, and A 4 if it makes a property
seem unavailable.

The compliant answer names **objective sources the buyer consults for themselves**: school division
data and attendance zones, crime statistics published by the locality's police department, census
data, tax rates, commute times, and the association's documents. And it offers to show every property
that meets the buyer's stated criteria.

Record the buyer's criteria **in the buyer's own words**. It is the record that shows the search was
driven by the buyer.

## 54.3 Case B — the screening exception

chunks.heading: 54.4 Case C — the accommodation refused by policy
chunks.excerpt:
*Facts.* A landlord's published criteria require income of three times the rent and no evictions in
five years. An applicant with a housing choice voucher has income of 1.6 times the rent; the voucher
pays the balance. The manager rejects them on income. Separately, the manager waives the income
criterion for a different applicant "who seemed like a good fit".

*Resolution.* Two violations.

**Source of funds.** Applying a whole-rent income multiple to an applicant whose subsidy pays most of
the rent screens out voucher holders as a class. The criterion must be applied to the **tenant's
portion**, and the Virginia protected class is **source of funds** under § 36-96.3 A 1 and A 2.

**Inconsistent application.** Waiving a published criterion for one applicant and not another is the
classic evidentiary pattern in a disparate-treatment case, whatever the reason given. Published
criteria are a defence only while they are applied uniformly.

The correction: rewrite the criterion to apply to the tenant's portion where a subsidy exists; apply
published criteria to every applicant identically; document each application; and remove the
discretion that produced the "good fit" waiver. The firm's written fair housing policy under
**§ 54.1-2110.1 B 2 b** is where the corrected criterion belongs.

## 54.4 Case C — the accommodation refused by policy

*Facts.* An applicant with a disability requests an exception to a no-pets policy for an assistance
animal and asks for a reserved parking space near the entrance. The manager replies that the building
has a no-pets policy, that pet rent is $45 a month if an exception is made, and that parking is
first-come.

chunks.heading: 54.5 Case D — the advertisement, audited line by line
chunks.excerpt:
*Resolution.* Both requests are **reasonable accommodations** under **§ 36-96.3 B (ii)** — changes to
rules, practices, policies or services necessary to afford equal opportunity to use and enjoy a
dwelling.

**A no-pets policy is not an answer**, because an assistance animal is not a pet. **Pet rent and pet
deposits may not be charged** for it, for the same reason — though the tenant remains responsible for
damage the animal causes and for its behaviour. **The parking request is an accommodation to a
first-come practice**, and the ordinary cost of making it falls on the provider.

Where the disability or the need is not readily apparent, a provider may seek reliable information
confirming the disability-related need, without demanding details of the diagnosis. **Virginia has
enacted specific provisions on assistance animals in rental housing and on the verification a provider
may request; this course does not state that procedure**, because those provisions have not been read
from primary text for this project. Read them, or refer — and do **not** refuse the request while the
question is open.

## 54.5 Case D — the advertisement, audited line by line

*Facts.* A post reads: *"Rare find in the Hollow! Charming 2BR cottage, walk to First Baptist, quiet
street — ideal for a mature couple or single professional. Owner prefers no children. Recently
renovated. Text Dana 555-0100. #JustListed"* — and the property has been under contract for six days.

*Audit.*

**"walk to First Baptist"** — under § 36-96.3 A 3, **reference alone to a place of worship is not
prima facie evidence** of an illegal preference. This line, on its own, is permissible. It is included
in the exercise precisely because students over-correct here.

chunks.heading: Hour 54 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**"ideal for a mature couple or single professional"** — preference on **elderliness** and **familial
status**, § 36-96.3 A 3.

**"Owner prefers no children"** — an express statement of preference on **familial status**, and a
statement of an intention to discriminate. This is the plainest violation on the page, and note that
even an exempt owner may not advertise this way: every § 36-96.2 exemption is expressed "except for
subdivision A 3 of § 36-96.3".

**"#JustListed" on a property under contract for six days** — property information inconsistent with
the property's current contract status, **18VAC135-20-190 B 3**, and a failure to update in a timely
manner after a material change to listing status, **B 4**. If the intent is to harvest buyer leads
rather than sell at those terms, **18VAC135-20-300 1**, bait and switch.

**No firm name, no advertising disclosure** — **18VAC135-20-190 A** requires advertising in the name
of the firm with the firm's licensed name clearly and legibly displayed, and **B 1** requires a clear,
legible and conspicuous advertising disclosure with the firm's name and office contact information as
the firm's written policy specifies.

**Compliant rewrite.** *"Two-bedroom cottage in the Hollow, recently renovated, on a quiet street.
[Firm's licensed name], [office contact information per firm policy]. Contact Dana, 555-0100."* —
posted only while the listing status is accurately represented.

### Hour 54 engagement check

**Question.** A licensee's internal note on a rental applicant reads: "Nice guy, National Guard, gets
deployed — probably won't be around, look for someone more stable." The applicant is rejected. What is
wrong, and what does the firm need to change?

chunks.heading: Hour 55 — Leasing and property management case lab
chunks.excerpt:
**Expected answer.** **Military status is a Virginia protected class** under **§ 36-96.3**, and
rejecting an applicant on the basis of it violates **A 1** (refusal to rent) and **A 2** (terms and
conditions). The written note is direct evidence of the reason, which is what makes this case simple
and dangerous. The firm needs published, objective, written screening criteria applied uniformly and
documented for every applicant, with the deployment-related speculation removed entirely from the
process — and that criterion belongs in the firm's written fair housing policy, which
**§ 54.1-2110.1 B 2 b** requires a firm doing residential leasing to have. Note also that a fair
housing violation by an affiliated licensee can reach the supervising broker under
**18VAC135-20-330**, which names Chapter 5.1 of Title 36 expressly.

## Hour 55 — Leasing and property management case lab

## 55.1 The method

**One — which chapter of Title 55.1 governs?** Chapter 12 VRLTA for residential; Chapter 13
manufactured home lots; Chapter 14 nonresidential; Chapter 16 leases generally.

**Two — read the operative section and the sections around it**, at law.lis.virginia.gov, in its
current text. Do not answer from memory, and do not answer from a summary.

**Three — read the rental agreement**, which may give the tenant more than the statute requires but
not less where the Act sets a floor.

**Four — apply the licensing duties.** § 54.1-2133 landlord, § 54.1-2134 tenant, § 54.1-2135
management; § 54.1-2138 B disclosure in the lease application or the lease, whichever comes first, and
not applicable to terms under two months.

**Five — apply fair housing**, § 36-96.3, with source of funds and accommodation requests the two most
common.

chunks.heading: 55.2 Case A — the maintenance request that became a habitability dispute
chunks.excerpt:
**Six — apply the trust accounting rules.** 18VAC135-20-181 A 1 and A 2; 18VAC135-20-185 A.

**Seven — refer the legal conclusions.** Whether a notice was valid, whether a breach is material, and
what remedy is available are counsel's.

## 55.2 Case A — the maintenance request that became a habitability dispute

*Facts.* A tenant reports a failing heating system by text on 4 January. The manager sees the text,
schedules a vendor for 11 January, the vendor does not attend, and nothing further happens. On 22
January the tenant emails saying they will withhold rent and are consulting a lawyer.

*Resolution.*

**The record is the case.** What was reported, when, how, what was done, and when. A text seen and not
logged is the failure that decides this dispute, and it is a **§ 54.1-2135** timely-performance and
ordinary-care problem before it is anything else.

**Which chapter:** Chapter 12 of Title 55.1, the VRLTA, governs the landlord's obligation to maintain
fit premises and the tenant's remedies, including whether and how rent may be withheld or escrowed.
**This course states none of those provisions**, because Chapter 12 has not been read from primary
text for this project. They must be read now, in current text, before any position is taken.

**What the manager does immediately:** get the heat working; log everything retrospectively with
dates and sources; write to the owner; escalate to the principal broker; and route the withholding
question to counsel. **What the manager must not do** is tell the tenant whether they may lawfully
withhold, or tell the owner to treat non-payment as a default.

chunks.heading: 55.3 Case B — the deposit at move-out
chunks.excerpt:
**What should have existed:** a request-to-completion tracking system with defined response times for
emergency and routine work, vendor accountability, and an escalation trigger when a scheduled visit
does not occur.

## 55.3 Case B — the deposit at move-out

*Facts.* A tenant vacates 30 April. The manager deducts carpet replacement in full for carpet
installed six years earlier, plus a $150 "administrative fee" not mentioned in the lease, and returns
the balance on 20 June with a one-line note.

*Resolution.*

**Three separate problems.**

**The carpet.** Ordinary wear and tear is not chargeable, and a six-year-old carpet has consumed most
of its useful life; charging full replacement transfers the landlord's capital cost to the tenant. The
defensible approach is depreciation over useful life, supported by the move-in and move-out condition
record — which is why that record is taken.

**The administrative fee.** A charge not provided for in the rental agreement has no basis. Whether it
is also prohibited is a Chapter 12 question.

**The timing and the itemisation.** Both the deadline for returning a deposit and the itemisation
required are set by the VRLTA. **This course states no deadline**, for the reason given above. Read
Chapter 12.

**The trust dimension.** The deposit is escrow money under **18VAC135-20-181 A 2**, its receipt and
disposition must appear in the records **18VAC135-20-185 A** requires, and the accounting duty is
**§ 54.1-2135**. A deposit that was never in escrow is a violation independent of everything above.

## 55.4 Case C — the accommodation, the vendor, and the money

chunks.heading: 55.5 The decision log
chunks.excerpt:
*Facts.* A tenant with a disability requests a grab bar in the bathroom and asks the manager to
arrange it. The manager has it installed, pays the vendor $380 from the escrow account, and charges it
to the owner's ledger.

*Resolution.*

**Classification first.** A grab bar is a physical change to the premises, so it is a **reasonable
modification** under **§ 36-96.3 B (i)** — permission may not be refused, and it is **at the disabled
person's expense**. It is **not** an accommodation, which is a change to a rule. Getting this wrong in
either direction causes a problem: refusing it is a violation, and paying for it charges the owner for
something the statute places on the tenant.

**The restoration condition.** In a rental the landlord may, **where reasonable**, condition permission
on the tenant agreeing to restore the interior to its prior condition, reasonable wear and tear
excepted.

**The money.** Paying a vendor from escrow against an owner's ledger is permissible only within the
authority the management agreement gives and only if the owner's ledger carries the funds. If it does
not, this is the Hour 33 conversion problem: **18VAC135-20-181 A 1 e** requires the balance to be
sufficient **at all times** to account for all funds held.

**What the manager should have done:** classify the request correctly; confirm in writing who bears
the cost and on what statutory basis; obtain the owner's authority for any expenditure above the
management agreement's threshold; and record the whole exchange.

## 55.5 The decision log

chunks.heading: Hour 55 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
Every case above is won or lost on documentation. A decision log entry records: **date and time; who
said what, by what channel; what was decided; on what authority — the statute, the lease, the
management agreement, or the owner's written instruction; who was notified; and what the next step and
its date are.**

A log kept contemporaneously is evidence. A log reconstructed after a complaint is an admission that
none was kept.

### Hour 55 engagement check

**Question.** A landlord client instructs you: "Change the locks Friday — they're two months behind
and I want them out." Write your response and identify every issue.

**Expected answer.** I decline the instruction, in writing. **Self-help eviction — changing locks,
removing possessions, or shutting off utilities — is unlawful**, and possession is recovered through
the statutory judicial process. Under **§ 54.1-2133** my duties include compliance with the article
and all applicable law, and a client's instruction cannot authorise a violation; carrying it out would
expose the owner to liability and me to Board discipline. What I will do is: confirm the ledger and
the exact arrears; identify the notice the **VRLTA, Chapter 12 of Title 55.1**, requires and its
period — read from the current text rather than recalled, because that is where landlords lose cases —
confirm what notice has actually been given and how; refer the owner to counsel to commence the
process; and log the instruction, my refusal, and the referral. I also notify my **principal broker**.

## Hour 56 — Real estate mathematics mastery

## 56.1 How to correct an error by method

A wrong answer has a cause, and there are only a handful. Before re-attempting, classify:

chunks.heading: 56.2 Area and volume
chunks.excerpt:
**Direction error** — adjusting the subject instead of the comparable, or adjusting up when the
comparable is superior. Fix: restate the rule aloud — adjust the comparable; comparable better,
subtract.

**Base error** — taking a percentage of the wrong number. LTV on the price when the appraisal is
lower; cash-on-cash on the down payment when closing costs were also invested; commission on the list
price rather than the sale price.

**Period error** — annual when the question wants monthly, or a 360-day year when the contract says
365.

**Inclusion error** — putting debt service or a capital expenditure into operating expenses; leaving
the replacement reserve out; prorating a security deposit.

**Side error** — debiting the party who should be credited.

**Rounding error** — rounding a daily rate before multiplying rather than after.

## 56.2 Area and volume

Rectangle: length × width. Triangle: ½ × base × height. Irregular shape: divide into rectangles and
triangles and sum.

**1 acre = 43,560 square feet.** A commercial square foot is measured differently from a residential
one, and land is frequently priced per acre or per square foot.

*A lot measures 210 ft by 290 ft. Acres?* 210 × 290 = 60,900 sq ft; ÷ 43,560 = **1.398 acres**.
*At $78,000 per acre:* 1.398 × 78,000 = **$109,044**.

## 56.3 Commission

*Sale $624,000; total fee 5.5%; split 50/50 between firms; listing salesperson on a 70/30 split with
their firm.*
Total: 624,000 × 0.055 = **$34,320**. Listing firm: **$17,160**. Salesperson: 17,160 × 0.70 =
**$12,012**.
*Reverse:* a salesperson netted $12,012 on a 70% split of half a 5.5% fee → firm half 12,012 ÷ 0.70 =
17,160 → total 34,320 → price 34,320 ÷ 0.055 = **$624,000**.

chunks.heading: 56.4 Taxes and prorations
chunks.excerpt:
Fees are negotiable between client and broker, and **§ 54.1-2136 (ii)** requires the compensation and
whether it will be shared to be disclosed **before the relationship begins**.

## 56.4 Taxes and prorations

*Assessed $476,000; rate $1.14 per $100.* 476,000 ÷ 100 = 4,760; × 1.14 = **$5,426.40**.

*Prorate at settlement 8 August, paid in arrears, 365-day year, settlement day to the buyer.*
Daily: 5,426.40 ÷ 365 = **$14.8668**. Seller's days 1 Jan–7 Aug = 31+28+31+30+31+30+31+7 = **219**.
219 × 14.8668 = **$3,255.83 — debit seller, credit buyer.**

## 56.5 Finance

*Price $580,000; 15% down.* Down payment **$87,000**; loan **$493,000**; LTV **85%**.
*Two discount points:* 493,000 × 0.02 = **$9,860**.
*First month's interest at 6.5%:* 493,000 × 0.065 ÷ 12 = **$2,670.42**.
*Payment factor 6.32 per $1,000:* 493 × 6.32 = **$3,115.76** P&I; principal in month one =
3,115.76 − 2,670.42 = **$445.34**.
*Ratios with gross monthly income $12,500, PITI $3,940, other debts $780:* front-end 3,940 ÷ 12,500 =
**31.5%**; back-end 4,720 ÷ 12,500 = **37.8%**. Thresholds are the lender's and are not stated here.

## 56.6 Appraisal and adjustment

*Comparable sold at $455,000. It has a 3-car garage; the subject has 2. Garage bay contributes
$9,000. It has 1,850 sq ft; the subject has 1,975, at $70 per sq ft. It sold 4 months ago in a market
rising 0.3% per month.*

Garage: comparable **superior** by one bay → **−$9,000**.
Area: comparable **inferior** by 125 sq ft → 125 × 70 = **+$8,750**.
Market conditions: 4 × 0.3% = 1.2% → 455,000 × 0.012 = **+$5,460**.
Adjusted: 455,000 − 9,000 + 8,750 + 5,460 = **$460,210**.

## 56.7 Income property

chunks.heading: 56.8 The mixed set
chunks.excerpt:
*18 units at $1,540; other income $6,200; vacancy 6.5%; operating expenses $153,400 including a
$9,000 reserve; cap rate 6.25%; monthly gross rent for GRM $27,720.*

PGI = 18 × 1,540 × 12 + 6,200 = 332,640 + 6,200 = **$338,840**.
Vacancy 6.5% = 22,024.60. **EGI = $316,815.40.**
**NOI = 316,815.40 − 153,400 = $163,415.40.**
**Value = 163,415.40 ÷ 0.0625 = $2,614,646.40.**
*GRM at 13.9:* 13.9 × 27,720 = **$385,308** — a figure for a small residential income property, and
note that it uses gross rent and therefore ignores vacancy and every operating expense.

## 56.8 The mixed set

Complete these and classify any error by the categories in 56.1.

1. A lot is 0.62 acres. How many square feet? **27,007.2**
2. Sale price $389,500 at a 6% total fee, split 50/50, salesperson at 60%. Salesperson's share?
   **$7,011**
3. Assessed $318,000 at $0.96 per $100. Annual tax? **$3,052.80**
4. Loan $342,000 at 7.125%. First month's interest? **$2,030.63**
5. Purchase $455,000, appraisal $441,000, lender lends 85% LTV. Loan amount and buyer's required cash
   for the down payment? **$374,850 and $80,150**
6. NOI $148,000 at a 6.8% cap rate. Value? **$2,176,470.59**
7. A comparable superior to the subject by a $14,000 feature sold for $506,000. Adjusted price?
   **$492,000**
8. Annual tax $4,015, paid in arrears, settlement 17 March, 365-day year, settlement day to the buyer.
   Seller's share? **$824.79** *(daily $11.0000; 75 days, 1 January–16 March)*
9. A tenant paid $2,400 rent on 1 October; settlement 14 October; 31 days; settlement day to the
   buyer. Rent proration and its side? **$1,393.55, debit seller, credit buyer** *(18 days)*
10. A property produces $52,000 NOI, costs $700,000, with $175,000 down and $525,000 borrowed at 6.5%
    interest-only. Cash-on-cash, and is the leve

chunks.heading: Hour 56 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
rage positive? **$52,000 − $34,125 = $17,875; ÷
    175,000 = 10.21%; unleveraged 7.43%; positive.**

### Hour 56 engagement check

**Question.** A student computes a tax proration as follows: annual tax $4,380, settlement 12
September, "so nine months have passed, 9 ÷ 12 × 4,380 = $3,285, debit buyer." Identify every error by
category and give the correct entry using a 365-day year with the settlement day charged to the buyer.

**Expected answer.** Three errors. A **period error** — nine full months have not passed on 12
September; the seller's period is 1 January to 11 September, which is **254 days**, not 9/12 of a
year. A **rounding or method error** — using whole months rather than the 365-day daily rate the
convention requires. And a **side error** — taxes paid in arrears mean the **buyer** will pay the
whole bill, so the seller owes the buyer: it is a **debit to the seller and a credit to the buyer**,
not a debit to the buyer. Correct: 4,380 ÷ 365 = $12.00 daily; 254 × 12.00 = **$3,048.00, debit
seller, credit buyer.**

lessons.title: Virginia Principles and Practices of Real Estate — Module 15

chunks.heading: Virginia Principles and Practices of Real Estate — Module 15
chunks.excerpt:
# Virginia Principles and Practices of Real Estate — Module 15

## Course Day 15 · Hours 57–60 · Cumulative review, simulation, and readiness

**Required subjects covered:** 18VAC135-20-400(1) through (25) — every required subject, integrated
**Class hours:** 4 (200 instructional minutes)
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Not approved. No Virginia pre-license credit is available for this course.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this module the student will be able to:

- Retrieve and apply the national principles of property, transfer, contracts, title, liens, finance,
  settlement and appraisal without prompting.
- Resolve a Virginia compliance sequence with the governing section cited at each step.
- Complete an integrated transaction from intake to settlement and identify every required document.
- Identify their own remaining gaps and state the final examination's conditions.

## Timed sequence

| Hour | Content | Class hours | Evidence of participation |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 57 | National principles cumulative review | 1 | Section completed; retrieval grid completed |
| 58 | Virginia law and regulations cumulative review | 1 | Section completed; compliance circuit resolved with citations |
| 59 | Comprehensive transaction simulation and remediation | 1 | Section completed; capstone file completed |
| 60 | Final instructional review and readiness verification | 1 | Readiness check passed; individual study plan completed |
| **Total** | | **4** | Monitored final assessment follows, outside instructional time |

---

## Hour 57 — National principles cumulative review

## 57.1 Property and rights

chunks.heading: 57.1 Property and rights
chunks.excerpt:
**Land, real estate, real property** — the third adds the legal interests, and it is what is actually
sold. The **bundle of rights** is separable; a seller may convey some sticks and keep others.

**Physical characteristics** — immobility, durability, uniqueness, scarcity. **Economic** —
improvements, permanence of investment, area preference.

**Fixtures** — MARIA: method of annexation, adaptation, relationship of the parties, intention,
agreement. **Intention governs**, judged objectively; the others are evidence of it. **Trade
fixtures** stay the tenant's and must be removed before the term ends or pass by **accession**.
**Severance** runs the other way; **emblements** protect the tenant's annual crop.

**Estates** — freehold and leasehold. **Fee simple absolute**; **defeasible fees** with a
**possibility of reverter** (determinable, automatic, "so long as") or a **right of re-entry**
(condition subsequent, must be exercised, "but if"). **Life estate** with a **reversion** to the
grantor or a **remainder** to a third party; **pur autre vie** is the inheritable one; the life tenant
may not commit **waste**.

**Concurrent ownership** — **severalty** (one owner); **tenancy in common** (undivided fractional
shares, no survivorship, freely transferable, partition available); **joint tenancy** (four unities:
time, title, interest, possession — with **survivorship**, destroyed as to a share that is conveyed);
**tenancy by the entirety** (spouses, survivorship, neither may convey alone). **Virginia is not a
community property state.**

chunks.heading: 57.2 Description and transfer
chunks.excerpt:
**Encumbrances** — **easements** appurtenant (dominant and servient tenements, runs with the land) and
in gross (benefits a person or entity); created by grant, reservation, implication, necessity,
prescription, or condemnation; terminated by merger, release, abandonment, end of necessity, or
express terms. A **licence** is personal and revocable. An **encroachment** is found by survey.
**Restrictive covenants** are private, can be stricter than zoning, and are privately enforced.

**Government powers — PETE**: police power (zoning, codes, no compensation), eminent domain (taking,
just compensation, executed by condemnation), taxation, escheat. **Variance** relieves a dimensional
requirement for a hardship from the property; **special use permit** authorises a listed conditional
use; **nonconforming use** was lawful when established; **rezoning** amends the ordinance.

## 57.2 Description and transfer

**Metes and bounds** — point of beginning, calls of bearing and distance, closes; **monuments control
over courses and distances**. **Lot and block** references a recorded plat. **Rectangular survey** is
not used in Virginia; a section is 640 acres.

**Deed elements** — competent grantor, identifiable grantee, recital of consideration, granting
clause, adequate legal description, grantor's signature, **delivery and acceptance**. Acknowledgment
is generally needed to **record**, not to be valid between the parties. **The grantee does not sign.**

**Deed types** — general warranty (warrants against all defects, whenever arising), special warranty
(only during the grantor's ownership), quitclaim (conveys whatever the grantor has, warrants
nothing — a **curative** instrument).

chunks.heading: 57.3 Contracts
chunks.excerpt:
**Notice** — **actual** (what is known), **constructive** (what is recorded, charged to everyone),
**inquiry** (what visible facts required one to investigate; **possession is notice**). Recording
gives constructive notice; **title passes on delivery**, not on recording.

**Chain of title**; **gap**; **cloud**; **marketable title**; **quiet title** action.

**Title insurance** — backward-looking indemnity for defects existing at policy date and not
excepted; **owner's** and **lender's** policies are different, and the lender's protects the lender
only. **Schedule B-I requirements** are actions; **B-II exceptions** are risks the insurer declines;
**exclusions** are printed categories. **No physical condition is covered.**

## 57.3 Contracts

Four elements: **mutual assent, competent parties, lawful objective, consideration** — plus the
**statute of frauds** writing for an interest in land.

**Valid, void, voidable, unenforceable.** **Bilateral or unilateral.** **Executory or executed** — and
the legal meaning of executed is **performed**, not signed.

**Offer** ends by acceptance, rejection, **counteroffer** (a rejection plus a new offer — the original
is dead), revocation before acceptance, lapse, death or incapacity, or destruction of the property.
Acceptance must be **unqualified and communicated**; modern forms require **delivery**.

**Remedies** — damages, liquidated damages, rescission, **specific performance** (available because
land is unique). **Assignment** transfers rights; **novation** substitutes a party and **releases**
the original.

**Contingencies** are **satisfied, waived, or failed with a stated consequence** — and a period
allowed to lapse without notice may be deemed satisfied or waived.

## 57.4 Liens and finance

chunks.heading: 57.5 Settlement, appraisal, and the numbers
chunks.excerpt:
**Voluntary or involuntary; statutory or equitable; general or specific.** **Tax liens hold statutory
priority regardless of recording date.** **Mechanics' liens relate back.** **Subordination** changes
position by agreement. Otherwise: **first to record, first in right.** On foreclosure, **junior liens
are extinguished as to the property; senior liens survive.**

**Note** is the debt and is not recorded; **security instrument** is the collateral and is recorded.
**Virginia uses the deed of trust** — grantor, trustee, beneficiary — not the two-party mortgage.
Clauses: **acceleration, alienation (due-on-sale), prepayment, defeasance, subordination, escrow.**

**Assumption** — buyer becomes liable; the seller is released only in writing. **Subject to** — buyer
does not assume; the seller stays liable.

**Programme categories** — conventional (conforming or not; **PMI protects the lender**), FHA
(**insured**, owner-occupant, MIP, minimum property standards), VA (**guaranteed**, eligible veteran,
funding fee, certificate of eligibility), USDA (rural area and income limits). **Eligibility is the
lender's determination, never the licensee's.**

## 57.5 Settlement, appraisal, and the numbers

**Debit** is a charge; **credit** is in a party's favour. **Arrears → debit seller, credit buyer.**
**Advance → debit buyer, credit seller.** **Rent → debit seller, credit buyer** for the unearned
portion. **Security deposits transfer in full and are never prorated.**

**Value, price, cost** are three different things. **Market value** requires an open market, prudent
and knowledgeable parties, **no duress**, reasonable exposure, and typical terms.

chunks.heading: Hour 57 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**Principles** — substitution, highest and best use (**legally permissible, physically possible,
financially feasible, maximally productive**), anticipation, contribution, conformity, progression and
regression, increasing and diminishing returns, competition, change, plottage.

**Sales comparison** — **adjust the comparable, never the subject; comparable better, subtract.**
**Cost** — land + cost new − depreciation, where depreciation is **physical**, **functional**, or
**external** (always incurable).
**Income** — **V = I ÷ R**; NOI **excludes debt service, depreciation, and capital expenditures** but
**includes replacement reserves**; **GRM uses gross rent and therefore ignores vacancy and every
expense.**

### Hour 57 engagement check

**Question.** Answer without looking back. (a) A deed is signed, acknowledged, and locked in a drawer.
Did title pass? (b) A comparable is superior to the subject — adjust which, and in which direction?
(c) Which liens survive a foreclosure sale? (d) What does NOI exclude and what does it include?

**Expected answer.** (a) **No** — **delivery** with present intent to pass title is missing;
acknowledgment makes the deed recordable but transfers nothing. (b) **Adjust the comparable, downward**
— comparable better, subtract. (c) **Senior liens survive**, and the purchaser takes subject to them;
**junior liens are extinguished as to the property**; **real property tax liens hold statutory
priority** and survive regardless of date. (d) NOI **excludes** debt service, depreciation, and capital
expenditures, and **includes** replacement reserves.

---

## Hour 58 — Virginia law and regulations cumulative review

## 58.1 The article, in the order it operates

chunks.heading: 58.1 The article, in the order it operates
chunks.excerpt:
**§ 54.1-2144 — common law abrogated.** Answer from the article, not from national agency doctrine.

**§ 54.1-2136 — preconditions.** Before any relationship: **(i)** the type proposed and **(ii)** the
compensation and whether shared.

**§ 54.1-2137 — the agreement.** In writing, before providing services. **Definite termination date or
90 days.** Fee and how and when paid. Services. Other agreed terms. Dual-representation disclosures
where applicable. After it ends, **only two duties survive: account, and keep confidential.**

**§ 54.1-2132 A 1 — brokerage agreement with a buyer *before showing property*.**

**§ 54.1-2131 A / § 54.1-2132 A — the duties.** Perform per the agreement; promote the client's
interests; **confidentiality**; **ordinary care**; **timely accounting**; disclose material facts of
**actual knowledge**; comply with the article and fair housing.

**§ 54.1-2131 B — toward the other side.** Honesty; no knowingly false information; **written**
disclosure of material adverse facts about the **physical condition** actually known; **defective
drywall** under § 36-156.1. And the statutory exclusions: **not** matters outside the boundaries or as
to adjacent properties, **not** governmental land use regulations, **not** highways or public streets.

**§ 54.1-2132 B — the buyer's licensee** discloses to the seller whether the buyer intends to occupy
as a **principal residence**.

**§§ 54.1-2131 C, 54.1-2132 C — ministerial acts** neither breach the agreement nor create a
relationship.

chunks.heading: 58.2 Licensing, supervision, and records
chunks.excerpt:
**§ 54.1-2138 — disclosure of relationship.** Trigger: a **substantive discussion about a specific
property** with someone neither client nor represented. Timing: **in writing, earliest practical time,
no later than when specific real estate assistance is first provided.** Form: **conspicuous — bold,
all capitals, underlined, or boxed.** Leasing: in the **application or the lease, whichever first**;
**not for terms under two months.** Change of relationship: written, to everyone already involved.
Retention: **three years** for disclosures relating to fully executed purchase contracts.

**§ 54.1-2138.1 — limited service agent.** Written agreement; disclose the status; **list services
provided**; **list standard-agent duties not provided**; conspicuous; statutory consent language. A
licensee helping the other side **without additional compensation** is liable only for **gross
negligence or wilful misconduct** and creates no relationship; **for a fee**, still no relationship,
but the **ordinary standard of care** applies.

**§ 54.1-2138.2 — disclose an ownership interest** in specific real property.

**§ 54.1-2139 / § 54.1-2139.01 / § 54.1-2139.1 — dual, commercial dual, designated.** Designated is
**not** dual **provided no designated agent represents more than one client** — but the **supervising
broker is dual**. Designated agents disclose confidences **only to their own broker**.

**§ 54.1-2140 / § 54.1-2141 — compensation and common source information companies create no
relationship.**

## 58.2 Licensing, supervision, and records

chunks.heading: 58.2 Licensing, supervision, and records
chunks.excerpt:
**§ 54.1-2104 / -2105 / -2105.1 / -2105.2** — the Board, its powers, and cease and desist orders for
unlicensed activity. **§ 54.1-2103** exemptions. **§ 54.1-2106.1** licences required.
**§ 54.1-2110** resident broker's place of business.

**§ 54.1-2110.1 — supervision.** Every place of business, branch office, **and team**. Availability to
review and approve documents. **Written policies in eight areas** — escrow, fair housing, advertising
and marketing, negotiating and drafting, unlicensed assistants, agency and independent-contractor
relationships, distributing new or amended law, and disclosing physical-condition information.
Competent services. Current licences. Teams and entities. **Supervising broker named in brokerage
agreements.** **Records three years.** **Over 50 miles → quarterly written certification.**

**18VAC135-20-165** — timely supervision; only licensees do licensed activity (with -335 A); adequate
supervision of unlicensed persons (with -335 B); diligence in responding to cooperating brokers.

**18VAC135-20-181** — federally insured escrow accounts, in the firm's licensed name, **labelled
escrow**, **principal broker responsible with signatory authority**, others with authority may be,
**balance sufficient at all times**; all transaction funds in, **including rents and rental security
deposits**.

**18VAC135-20-185** — financial records readily accessible; **brokerage agreements and dual and
designated consents three years from execution**.

chunks.heading: 58.3 Conduct and discipline
chunks.excerpt:
**18VAC135-20-190** — **in the firm's name**, under the broker's direct supervision, firm's licensed
name clearly and legibly displayed; **advertising disclosure with the firm's name and office contact
information as the firm's written policy specifies**; property information **consistent with condition
and current contract status**; **updated in a timely manner**; **timely written request** where a third
party controls it.

**18VAC135-20-220 A** — disclosure of relationship, and dual and designated **written consent from all
clients**, timed to the presentation of the offer.

## 58.3 Conduct and discipline

**18VAC135-20-155** — the Board's disciplinary power, including for violations of **Chapter 10 of
Title 55.1**, and **B**: conduct in a **personal capacity** is reachable.

**18VAC135-20-260** — prohibited acts, including **two 30-day self-reporting clocks**: convictions and
out-of-state disciplinary action.

**18VAC135-20-270** — conflict of interest: active with another broker without written consent; acting
for more than one client under §§ 54.1-2139, 54.1-2139.01 or 54.1-2139.1 **without first obtaining
written consent of all clients**.

**18VAC135-20-300** — misrepresentation or omission: **bait and switch**; failure by a standard agent
to disclose known material adverse physical-condition facts; **failure to tender promptly every
written offer, counteroffer and rejection**; failure to disclose material facts to the client where
that is a failure of ordinary care; failure to give required written notices.

**18VAC135-20-330** — the broker is disciplined for a salesperson's violation **only** if the broker
**knew or should have known** and **failed to take reasonable action to remedy**. Not vicarious
liability.

chunks.heading: 58.4 Disclosure, fair housing, and common interest communities
chunks.excerpt:
**§§ 54.1-2112–54.1-2120** — the **Transaction Recovery Fund**; **§ 54.1-2119** revokes the licence on
payment from the fund.

## 58.4 Disclosure, fair housing, and common interest communities

**§ 55.1-703 — buyer beware.** The owner furnishes the **Real Estate Board's** statement, whose content
is that the **owner makes no representations**, and which advises the purchaser to exercise whatever
due diligence they deem necessary — naming home inspection (§ 54.1-500), mould assessment following
EPA guidance, energy analysis (§ 54.1-1144), survey, and contacting the locality.

**§ 36-96.3 — Virginia's protected classes:** race, colour, religion, national origin, sex,
**elderliness**, **source of funds**, familial status, **sexual orientation**, **gender identity**,
**military status**, and disability. Words or symbols associated with a religion, national origin, sex
or race are **prima facie evidence** and a disclaimer does not cure it; **reference alone to a place of
worship is not**. **B (i)** modification — tenant pays, restoration may be required where reasonable.
**B (ii)** accommodation — a change to a rule.

**§ 36-96.2 A — the owner exemption does not inure to the benefit of any Real Estate Board licensee,
regardless of capacity.** Every exemption is expressed "except for subdivision A 3", so **advertising
is never exempt**.

chunks.heading: Hour 58 engagement check — the compliance circuit
chunks.excerpt:
**§ 55.1-2308** — five contract disclosures for a resale in a common interest community; omission
makes cancellation before settlement the purchaser's **sole remedy**.
**§ 55.1-2309** — the **seller or seller's agent** obtains and provides the resale certificate; **not
waivable by agreement**; **14 days** from written request, then **deemed unavailable**.
**§ 55.1-2312** — cancel within the agreed period, or **three days from ratification** if delivery
preceded it, **three days from receipt** if it followed, and **any time before settlement** if nothing
was delivered; **written notice**, **purchaser bears the burden of proving delivery**; **without
penalty**, deposit returned promptly.
**§ 55.1-2314** — a non-compliant certificate relieves the purchaser of delinquent assessments and
prior violations; preparer liable to the seller up to **$1,000**.

### Hour 58 engagement check — the compliance circuit

**Question.** For each, name the governing section and the answer. (a) A listing agreement states no
end date; when does it end? (b) When must a buyer brokerage agreement be signed? (c) A licensee has a
substantive discussion about a specific property with an unrepresented buyer; when is written
disclosure due? (d) The firm has both sides through two licensees; what is the supervising broker's
status and what is required? (e) A salesperson is convicted of a felony; what must happen and when?
(f) A licensee sells their own house; can they use the owner exemption from fair housing?

chunks.heading: Hour 59 — Comprehensive transaction simulation and remediation
chunks.excerpt:
**Expected answer.** (a) **§ 54.1-2137 C 1** — **90 days after its date.** (b) **§ 54.1-2132 A 1** —
**before showing property** to the prospective buyer. (c) **§ 54.1-2138 A** — in writing at the
earliest practical time and **no later than when specific real estate assistance is first provided**,
conspicuously; and **18VAC135-20-220 A 2** restates it. (d) **§ 54.1-2139.1** — designated agency, and
the **supervising broker is a dual agent or representative**; **written consent from all clients** is
required, timed by **18VAC135-20-220 A 3**, and its absence is a **conflict of interest under
18VAC135-20-270 2**. (e) **18VAC135-20-260 4 and 5** — the conviction is a prohibited act, and the
licensee must **inform the Board in writing within 30 days**. (f) **No** — **§ 36-96.2 A** provides
that the exemption does not apply to or inure to the benefit of any Real Estate Board licensee,
**regardless of whether the licensee is acting in a personal or professional capacity**.

---

## Hour 59 — Comprehensive transaction simulation and remediation

## 59.1 The capstone

*Facts.* Marguerite owns a 1971 townhouse in a property owners' association in a Virginia locality.
She is selling and buying a condominium in the same locality. Both firms in the purchase are the same
firm. Marguerite's townhouse has an active roof leak she has mentioned to her licensee, and a
neighbour's shed encroaches about two feet across the rear line. Her buyer, Terrence, is a veteran
using VA financing with a voucher-holding co-applicant relative; he intends to occupy. The
condominium Marguerite is buying has a special assessment discussed in the association's March
minutes.

chunks.heading: 59.2 The listing side
chunks.excerpt:
The capstone requires the student to produce a complete transaction file and a compliance narrative.
The grid below is the marking scheme.

## 59.2 The listing side

| Step | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Before the relationship | Advise of the type of relationship proposed and the compensation and whether shared | § 54.1-2136 |
| Intake | Verify ownership, every person on title, authority to sign, and identity | Land records; Hour 50.5 |
| Agreement | Written; **definite termination date or 90 days**; fee and how and when paid; services; supervising broker's name and contact information | § 54.1-2137 B and C; § 54.1-2110.1 B 6 |
| Owner's disclosure | Furnish the Real Estate Board's residential property disclosure statement | § 55.1-703 |
| Licensee's disclosure | **The roof leak** — a material adverse fact about the **physical condition**, actually known — disclosed **in writing** to prospective buyers | § 54.1-2131 B |
| The encroachment | **Outside** the physical-condition duty as a matter relating to adjacent property — but a **material fact concerning the property or the transaction** actually known, disclosed to the **client**, and routed to a **surveyor** and counsel | § 54.1-2131 A 6 and B |
| Lead-based paint | 1971 construction is **target housing**: disclosure, records, pamphlet, contract warning, **ten-day** assessment opportunity | Federal |
| Association | Contract carries the **five § 55.1-2308 disclosures**; **written** resale certificate request at listing | §§ 55.1-2308, 55.1-2309 B |
| Marketing | Firm's name, broker supervision, firm's licensed name displayed, advertising disclosure per firm policy, information consistent with condition and status, updated timely | 18VAC135-20-190 |
| Offers | **Every** written offer presented promptly | §

chunks.heading: 59.3 The purchase side
chunks.excerpt:
54.1-2131 A 2 c; 18VAC135-20-300 3 |
| Deposit | Into the firm's escrow account | 18VAC135-20-181 A 1 and A 2 |

## 59.3 The purchase side

| Step | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Before showing | Preconditions, then a **written brokerage agreement before showing property** | §§ 54.1-2136, 54.1-2132 A 1 |
| Occupancy | Disclose to the seller whether the buyer intends to occupy as a **principal residence** | § 54.1-2132 B |
| Financing | Describe VA as a **category**; state **no** eligibility, entitlement, funding fee or rate; refer to a lender | § 54.1-2132 A 5; 18VAC135-20-300 |
| Fair housing | **Military status** and **source of funds** are both Virginia protected classes; no screening, steering, or offer-evaluation practice may turn on either | § 36-96.3 A 1–3 |
| Association | Confirm the § 55.1-2308 disclosures; request the certificate **in writing**; diary the **§ 55.1-2312** cancellation period; **read the March minutes** and the reserve study for the special assessment | §§ 55.1-2308, 55.1-2309, 55.1-2312 |
| Milestones | Deposit, application, inspections, lead-based paint ten days, appraisal, title, conditions, commitment, Closing Disclosure, walk-through, settlement | Hour 52.3 |
| Wire fraud | Written warning at ratification and before settlement; **any change verified by telephone to an independently obtained number** | Hour 50.1 |

## 59.4 Both sides in one firm

chunks.heading: 59.5 The five deliberate traps
chunks.excerpt:
Two licensees of the same firm on the two sides of Marguerite's **purchase** makes it **designated
agency under § 54.1-2139.1**, in which the **supervising broker is a dual agent or representative**.
**Written consent from all clients** is required, timed by **18VAC135-20-220 A 3** — from the buyer no
later than when the offer is presented to the licensee who will present it, from the seller no later
than when it is presented to the seller. Without it, **18VAC135-20-270 2** makes it a conflict of
interest. Designated agents may disclose client confidences **only to their own broker**. Consents are
retained **three years from execution** under **18VAC135-20-185 C 1**.

## 59.5 The five deliberate traps

**One — the encroachment.** Students disclose it as a physical-condition fact. § 54.1-2131 B expressly
excludes **matters outside the boundaries of the land or relating to adjacent properties** from the
physical-condition duty. It is still a **material fact** owed to the **client** under A 6, and the
correct handling is a survey, counsel, and honesty — not silence and not a licensee's opinion about the
boundary.

**Two — the roof leak.** Squarely inside § 54.1-2131 B: material, adverse, physical condition, actually
known. **In writing.** A student who relies on § 55.1-703 to carry it has confused the **owner's**
buyer-beware statement with the **licensee's** duty.

**Three — the voucher and the veteran.** **Source of funds** and **military status** are Virginia
protected classes. Any suggestion that a VA offer is "harder" or that a voucher co-applicant is a
problem is where this file goes wrong.

chunks.heading: 59.6 Remediation
chunks.excerpt:
**Four — the special assessment in the March minutes.** Nothing requires the buyer to be given the
minutes automatically; the buyer must **obtain and read them**, and the resale certificate and the
cancellation window in § 55.1-2312 are the mechanism. A licensee who does not diary that window has
lost the buyer's protection.

**Five — 1971.** Pre-1978, so **target housing**, so the federal lead-based paint package. Students
forget it on resale transactions constantly.

## 59.6 Remediation

Any capstone element missed opens targeted remediation: the governing section, a short alternate
explanation, and a **new fact pattern** on the same rule. The student must identify the rule, apply it
to the new facts, and answer an alternate item correctly before the element is marked complete.
Elements missed twice are added to the instructor remediation queue and are addressed in a
conference before Hour 60 is marked complete.

### Hour 59 engagement check

**Question.** Marguerite tells her licensee, "don't put the roof in writing — the buyer's inspection
will find it, and § 55.1-703 says I make no representations anyway." Respond.

chunks.heading: Hour 60 — Final instructional review and readiness verification
chunks.excerpt:
**Expected answer.** The instruction cannot be followed. **§ 55.1-703 governs the owner**, and it is
correct that the owner's statutory statement makes no representations. **It does not govern the
licensee.** **§ 54.1-2131 B** requires a licensee engaged by a seller to disclose to prospective
buyers **all material adverse facts pertaining to the physical condition of the property that are
actually known by the licensee**, **in writing** — and an active roof leak the licensee has been told
about is exactly that. Failing to do so is also **misrepresentation or omission under
18VAC135-20-300 2**. A client's instruction cannot authorise a violation, the statute provides that
**no cause of action arises against a licensee for revealing information as required**, and I would
confirm the position to Marguerite in writing and notify my principal broker.

---

## Hour 60 — Final instructional review and readiness verification

## 60.1 The distinctions most often missed

A last pass over the pairs that produce wrong answers:

chunks.heading: 60.2 Where to look it up
chunks.excerpt:
**Delivery vs. recording** — title passes on delivery; recording gives notice.
**Adjust comparable, not subject** — comparable better, subtract.
**Arrears vs. advance** — arrears: debit seller, credit buyer. Advance: the reverse. **Deposits never
prorate.**
**NOI excludes** debt service, depreciation and capital expenditures; **includes** reserves.
**Assessed value is not market value.**
**Variance is dimensional; special use permit is a listed conditional use; rezoning is legislative.**
**Fee determinable is automatic; condition subsequent must be exercised.**
**Joint tenancy conveyance destroys survivorship as to that share.**
**Counteroffer kills the original offer.**
**Executed means performed**, not signed.
**Lender's title policy protects the lender.** **PMI protects the lender.**
**Junior liens die at foreclosure; senior liens and tax liens survive.**
**Ordinary care, not fiduciary** — § 54.1-2144 abrogated the common law.
**Actual knowledge, not a duty to investigate** — §§ 54.1-2131 A 6 and B, 54.1-2132 A 7.
**Buyer agreement before showing** — § 54.1-2132 A 1.
**90 days if no termination date** — § 54.1-2137 C 1.
**Virginia's disclosure statute is buyer-beware** — § 55.1-703.
**The owner exemption never helps a licensee** — § 36-96.2 A.
**Designated agency: the supervising broker is the dual agent** — § 54.1-2139.1.
**The broker is liable only on knew-or-should-have-known plus failure to remedy** — 18VAC135-20-330.
**Every written offer is presented** — 18VAC135-20-300 3.

## 60.2 Where to look it up

A licensee's most valuable long-term skill is not recall; it is **knowing where the answer lives**.

chunks.heading: 60.3 Academic integrity and the final examination
chunks.excerpt:
**Code of Virginia** and the **Virginia Administrative Code**, both current and free at
law.lis.virginia.gov. **Title 54.1 Chapter 21** for licensing and brokerage relationships;
**18VAC135-20** for the Board's regulations; **Title 55.1** for property, disclosure, settlement,
tenancies, and common interest communities; **Title 36 Chapter 5.1** for fair housing.

**DPOR and the Real Estate Board** for licensing procedure, forms, fees, and the residential property
disclosure statement itself, which § 55.1-703 says the Board provides on its website.

And the rule this whole course has followed: **read the section, not a summary of it.** Four times in
this project a secondary description diverged from the primary text, once by thirty hours.

## 60.3 Academic integrity and the final examination

**The final assessment is monitored, is administered after the sixtieth instructional hour, and its
time is not counted in the 3,000 instructional minutes.** Its conditions — permitted materials, time
limit, passing standard, retake policy, and identity verification — are set out in
`virginia/compliance/monitored-final-exam-sop.md` and are given to the student before the
examination.

Integrity rules: the work must be the enrolled student's own; the identity verification exists to
protect every honest student's certificate; and any assistance, sharing of items, or substitution
invalidates the attempt and is reportable. A certificate of completion attests to instruction the
student actually received.

chunks.heading: 60.4 The individual study plan
chunks.excerpt:
**Two things this course must never be misunderstood as saying.** The course carries **no Virginia
pre-license credit** and is **not approved**; approval is a decision of the Real Estate Board and, until
it is recorded, no completion of this course qualifies anyone for anything. And the course does not
license anyone: licensure requires application to the Board, examination, and the Board's action.

## 60.4 The individual study plan

Each student leaves Hour 60 with a written plan built from their own record: every engagement check
missed and the hour it came from; every unit quiz item missed, grouped by required subject; every
mathematics error classified by **method** — direction, base, period, inclusion, side, rounding — and
every capstone element that required remediation.

Against each, the plan names the hour to revisit, the primary source to read, and the practice to
repeat. A plan that names topics without naming sources is a list of worries, not a plan.

## 60.5 Readiness check

The student demonstrates, without notes:

1. The seven duties under § 54.1-2131 A and the standard attached to each.
2. When a buyer brokerage agreement must be signed, and what happens if no termination date is stated.
3. The trigger, timing, and form of the § 54.1-2138 A disclosure.
4. What § 55.1-703 actually requires of an owner, in one sentence.
5. Virginia's protected classes, including the five that are not federal.
6. The § 55.1-2312 cancellation periods, all three.
7. Adjust which, in which direction, and why.
8. What NOI excludes and includes.
9. Which liens survive a foreclosure sale.
10. The standard by which a broker is disciplined for a salesperson's act.

### Hour 60 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 15
chunks.excerpt:
**Question.** State, in one sentence each and without notes: (a) the standard of care a Virginia
licensee owes a client; (b) the knowledge standard for disclosing material facts; (c) when a brokerage
agreement with no termination date ends; (d) whether Virginia's residential property disclosure statute
requires the owner to describe the property's condition; (e) whether a licensee selling their own home
may rely on the fair housing owner exemption.

**Expected answer.** (a) **Ordinary care** — § 54.1-2131 A 4 and § 54.1-2132 A 5; the common law of
agency is abrogated to the extent inconsistent under § 54.1-2144, so it is not a fiduciary standard.
(b) **Actual knowledge** — §§ 54.1-2131 A 6 and B and 54.1-2132 A 7; there is no duty to investigate.
(c) **90 days after the date of the agreement** — § 54.1-2137 C 1. (d) **No** — § 55.1-703 is a
buyer-beware statute under which the owner furnishes a Real Estate Board statement saying the owner
makes **no representations** and advising the purchaser to exercise due diligence. (e) **No** —
§ 36-96.2 A provides the exemption does not apply to or inure to the benefit of any Real Estate Board
licensee, **regardless of whether the licensee is acting in a personal or professional capacity**.

---

## Instructor source note for Module 15

Every Virginia citation in this module restates text read directly from law.lis.virginia.gov on
2026-08-20 and recorded in `virginia/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`. No new authority is
introduced in Hours 57 through 60; the module is review, and a review hour that introduces an unread
rule is a defect.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module 15
chunks.excerpt:
**Hours 57 and 58 are deliberately dense and are written as retrieval material**, not as first
instruction. Every proposition in them appears in an earlier hour with its explanation, and the
cross-references are exact so a student can return to the source hour rather than re-reading the
summary.

**The capstone in Hour 59 contains five deliberate traps**, listed at 59.5, and the marking scheme in
59.2 and 59.3 is the assessment instrument. The encroachment trap in particular tests the statutory
boundary in § 54.1-2131 B — that matters relating to adjacent properties sit **outside** the
physical-condition duty while remaining material facts owed to the client under A 6 — which is the
distinction this course has taught most carefully and which national material does not draw.

**Hour 60.3 states the course's regulatory status in the terms every document in this package uses.**
The final assessment's conditions, permitted materials, time limit, passing standard, retake policy and
identity verification are held in `virginia/compliance/monitored-final-exam-sop.md` and are **not**
restated here, so that there is one controlling statement of them rather than two that can drift apart.

lessons.title: Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-01

chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-01
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-01

## The Washington licensing framework, and the rules governing this course

**Course:** Real Estate Fundamentals — one of the two courses **RCW 18.85.101(1)(c)** names.
**Instructional hours:** **5.0** of 60.0
**Clock hours:** a Washington clock hour is **50 minutes of actual instruction** — WAC 308-124H-820(4).
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

> ### Four things about this course, stated before anything else
>
> **1. Washington licenses a BROKER, not a salesperson.** The entry-level licence is a **broker**,
> supervised by a **designated broker** or **managing broker** within a **real estate firm**. RCW
> 18.86.010(3): *"'Broker' means broker, managing broker, and designated broker, collectively."* This
> course uses Washington's words throughout, and a student who mentally substitutes "salesperson" will
> misread half the statute.
>
> **2. The statute fixes 90 hours and two courses; current DOL curricula fix 60/30.** RCW 18.85.101(1)(c)
> requires *"90 hours of instruction in real estate,"* and provides that instruction *"must include
> courses **as prescribed by the director** including **fundamentals**, which shall include **three hours
> of instruction on fair housing and consumer protection issues**, and **practices**."* DOL's current
> prescribed documents require **60 hours of Fundamentals** (Rev. 5/2022) and **30 hours of Practices**
> (effective 03-18-2009). StateCourse decides only the module-level allocation within those totals.
>
> **3. The Department prescribes the curriculum, and both current documents are now controlled.** WAC
> 308-124H-810 requires an approved school to *"**utilize the most recent co

chunks.heading: Learning objectives
chunks.excerpt:
urse curriculum prescribed by
> the department**."* Both DOL PDFs were obtained and byte-locked on 2026-09-04. The inherited modules were
> originally written from **RCW 18.85, RCW 18.86 and WAC 308-124H** and have not yet passed objective-level
> mapping to those DOL documents. **Conforming them remains a submission gate.**
>
> **4. This course will carry a large examination, and the size is set by rule.** WAC
> 308-124H-820(8): courses of 30 clock hours or more must include a comprehensive examination of **no
> fewer than three questions per clock hour with a minimum of 90 questions**, and a **passing course grade
> of at least 70 percent.** At 60 clock hours, this course's examination must contain **at least 180
> questions.**

## Learning objectives

1. State the five statutory requirements for a Washington broker's licence.
2. State what a Washington clock hour is and how the two-year completion window runs.
3. State the examination requirements a course of 30 clock hours or more must satisfy.
4. Identify what a course may not be approved to teach for clock hours.
5. State what an approved school's certificate of course completion must contain.
6. Explain what a distance education course must demonstrate to be approved.
7. State the relationship between a broker, a firm, a designated broker and a managing broker.

---

## A. What RCW 18.85.101(1) requires of you

chunks.heading: A.1 The two-year window, and where it is measured to
chunks.excerpt:
> **(a)** *"Is **18 years of age or older**";*
> **(b)** *"Has a **high school diploma or its equivalent**";*
> **(c)** *"has furnished proof ... that the applicant has **successfully completed 90 hours of instruction
> in real estate**. Instruction must include courses as prescribed by the director including
> **fundamentals**, which shall include **three hours of instruction on fair housing and consumer
> protection issues**, and **practices**. **Each course must be completed within two years before applying
> for the broker's license examination** and be **approved by the director**. The applicant must **pass a
> course examination, approved by the director, for each course** used to satisfy the requirement";*
> **(d)** *"Has **passed the broker's license examination**."*

### A.1 The two-year window, and where it is measured to

> *"Each course must be completed **within two years before applying for the broker's license
> examination**."*

**Two years, and the anchor is the application to sit the examination** — not the licence application and
not the date the licence issues. A course finished twenty-six months before you apply to test is a course
the statute does not count, however good it was.

This is a **short** window by national standards. Pennsylvania allows ten years; Washington allows two.
The practical consequence is that a Washington student should finish both courses and test promptly.

### A.2 A course examination for EACH course

> *"The applicant must **pass a course examination, approved by the director, for each course** used to
> satisfy the broker's license requirement."*

chunks.heading: A.3 What comes after — recorded so you are not surprised
chunks.excerpt:
**Two courses, two course examinations** — and they are separate from **the broker's license examination**
in (d), which is the state test. Three examinations in total before licensure, and this course is
responsible for one of them.

### A.3 What comes after — recorded so you are not surprised

**RCW 18.85.101(2):** *"The education requirements for the **first renewal** of the broker's license must
include **90 hours** of courses as prescribed by the director, including **real estate law**, which shall
include **three hours of instruction on fair housing and consumer protection issues**, **advance
practices**, and **continuing education**."*

**Another 90 hours before your first renewal.** This course does not deliver them. It names them.

**RCW 18.85.101(3):** *"The broker is **licensed to one firm at a time** and is **supervised by a
designated or managing broker**."*

---

## B. What a Washington clock hour is — WAC 308-124H-820(4)

> *"Have a minimum of three hours of course work or instruction for the student. **A clock hour is a period
> of 50 minutes of actual instruction.**"*

**Fifty minutes of actual instruction.** So this 60-hour course is **3,000 minutes of instruction**, and the
90-hour programme is **4,500 minutes.**

And **WAC 308-124H-820(7)(h)**: *"**Clock hours shall not be awarded for any course time devoted to meals or
transportation.**"*

---

## C. The examination this course must carry — WAC 308-124H-820(8)

chunks.heading: D. What a course may NOT be approved to teach — WAC 308-124H-820(7)
chunks.excerpt:
> *"**Courses of 30 clock hours or more which are submitted for approval must include a comprehensive
> examination(s) and answer key(s) of no fewer than three questions per clock hour with a minimum of 90
> questions, and a requirement of passing course grade of at least 70 percent**; essay question examination
> keys must identify the material to be tested and the points assigned for each question."*

Work the arithmetic, because it scales:

| Course | Clock hours | Minimum items | Passing grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Real Estate Fundamentals** | **60** | **180** | **70%** |
| **Real Estate Practices** | **30** | **90** | **70%** |

**Three questions per clock hour, with a floor of 90.** This is the strictest examination-size rule in this
project, because it is proportional: a longer course cannot carry a shorter test.

**The 70 percent is the director's figure**, not this school's. The in-module checks you will meet
throughout this course are **not** that examination — they gate progression, and their thresholds are
StateCourse standards.

---

## D. What a course may NOT be approved to teach — WAC 308-124H-820(7)

Eight exclusions, and the reasoning behind them is one test applied eight ways.

chunks.heading: D.1 The rule's own example is the clearest statement of the test
chunks.excerpt:
> **(a)** *"**Mechanical office and business skills**, such as, keyboarding, speed-reading, memory
> improvement, grammar, and report writing";*
> **(b)** *"**Standardized software programs** such as word processing, email, spreadsheets or databases";*
> **(c)** *"**Orientation courses for licensees**, such as those offered by trade associations";*
> **(d)** *"**Personal and sales motivation courses** or sales meetings held in conjunction with a
> licensee's general business";*
> **(e)** *"Courses ... designed or developed to **serve other professions**, unless each component of the
> curriculum and content **specifically shows how a real estate licensee can utilize the information in the
> practice of real estate**";*
> **(f)** *"**Personal finance, etiquette, or motivational type courses**";*
> **(g)** *"Courses ... designed to **promote or offer to sell specific products or services to real estate
> licensees** such as warranty programs, client/customer database systems, software programs or other
> devices";*
> **(h)** *"Clock hours shall not be awarded for any course time devoted to **meals or transportation**."*

### D.1 The rule's own example is the clearest statement of the test

> *"an example: **A course using spreadsheet program to demonstrate investment analysis would be
> acceptable, but a course teaching how to use a spreadsheet would not be acceptable**."*

**The subject must be real estate.** A tool is in scope only when it is being used on a real estate problem.
That single sentence resolves nearly every borderline case under (a), (b) and (g).

### D.2 And (g) contains a line worth noticing

chunks.heading: E. What else a course must satisfy — WAC 308-124H-820
chunks.excerpt:
> *"**Services or products can be offered during nonclock hour time, such as breaks or lunchtime.**
> **Letterhead, logos, company names or other similar markings by itself, on course material are not
> considered promotional.**"*

The rule is not squeamish about a provider having a name. What it prohibits is **spending clock hours
selling.**

---

## E. What else a course must satisfy — WAC 308-124H-820

> **(6)** *"Be under the supervision of an **instructor approved to teach the topic area**, who must, at a
> minimum, be **available to respond to specific questions from students on an immediate or reasonably
> delayed basis**";*
> **(9)** *"Include **textbook or instructional materials approved by the director**, which must be **kept
> accurate and current**";*
> **(10)** *"**Not have a title which misleads the public** as to the subject matter of the course";*
> **(11)** *"The provider's course application must **identify learning objectives and demonstrate how these
> are related to the practice of real estate**."*

**(9) is why a course cannot be written once and left alone.** Materials must be **kept accurate and
current** — an obligation that runs continuously, not at approval.

**And WAC 308-124H-810** adds a title rule with teeth: an approved school offering mandated training must
have **"real estate" in the course title** (except business management), and **may not use** the eight
prescribed core curricula phrases in other course titles — *real estate fundamentals; real estate brokerage
management; real estate law; advanced real estate law; business management; real estate practices; advanced
real estate practices; and Washington real estate fair housing.*

---

## F. Distance education — what this delivery method must prove

chunks.heading: F. Distance education — what this delivery method must prove
chunks.excerpt:
If you are taking this course at a distance, the rules below govern how it had to be built.
