**WAC 308-124H-830** defines a distance delivery method as one where *"instruction takes place in **other
than a live classroom setting**, the instructor and the student are in **physically separate locations**,
and **interactive** instructional methods ... are used."*

**WAC 308-124H-835** then defines **interactive**, and the definition is a design requirement:

> *"**interactive** means the course structure and technologies promote **active student involvement** with
> the course content, including the ability to: **(a) access or bypass optional content**, if applicable;
> **(b) submit questions or answer test items, and receive direct feedback**; and **(c) communicate with the
> instructor and/or other students on an immediate or reasonably delayed basis.**"*
>
> *"**Interactive instruction specifically excludes courses that only provide passive delivery of
> instructional content.**"*

**WAC 308-124H-840** requires an application for **each separate delivery method**, demonstrating —
among other things — **learning units divided into modules**, **learning objectives for each**, **an
objective, quantitative criterion for mastery**, **a mechanism of individual remediation**, **measurement of
progress at regular intervals**, and, for computer-based instruction, *"the course software **must include
automatic shutdown after a period of inactivity**."* It also requires **reasonable security** so that the
student who receives credit is the student who enrolled — and *"**Both the approved school and the student
must certify in writing that the student has completed the course, and the required number of clock
hours.**"*

chunks.heading: G. Your certificate — WAC 308-124H-855
chunks.excerpt:
**WAC 308-124H-845** provides one shortcut: an applicant with **ARELLO certification** of the delivery
method need not apply separately, *"**provided a clock hour enforcement mechanism is in place**."*

**No ARELLO certification and no delivery-method approval is held for this build. Submission gate.**

---

## G. Your certificate — WAC 308-124H-855

An approved school **shall issue a certificate of course completion** to students who have satisfactorily
completed the course requirements, containing **nine** items:

1. **Student's name**
2. **School's name and identification number issued by the department**
3. **The course commencement date and completion date**
4. **Course title**
5. **Clock hours for the course**
6. **School administrator's signature**
7. **Course identification number issued by the department**
8. **Instructor name and number**
9. **Completion of a required examination, if applicable**

**Two department-issued numbers appear on it** — the school's and the course's. **Without approval there are
no such numbers**, and so no conforming certificate can issue. That is why this build cannot yet award
clock hours, and says so on every page.

**Keep the certificate.** RCW 18.85.101(1)(c)'s two-year window is measured against the **completion date**
printed on it.

---

## H. How Washington structures a brokerage — the vocabulary you will need throughout

- **Real estate firm** — the licensed entity. Brokers are licensed **with** a firm.
- **Designated broker** — the person responsible for the firm and for supervising the brokers licensed with
  it.
- **Managing broker** — a broker to whom supervisory duties may be delegated.
- **Broker** — the entry-level licence, and the person doing most of the work in most transactions.

chunks.heading: I. And the sentence that will govern everything in the companion course
chunks.excerpt:
**RCW 18.85.101(3)** puts it plainly: *"The broker is **licensed to one firm at a time** and is **supervised
by a designated or managing broker**."*

This matters more in Washington than the equivalent structure does elsewhere, because **RCW 18.86 assigns
duties to the FIRM and to the individual broker differently.** The companion course develops it. Two
previews:

- **RCW 18.86.020(2)(a):** *"**A firm must enter into a services agreement with the principal**"* — the
  agreement is between the **firm** and the principal, and the firm **appoints** a broker as agent.
- **RCW 18.86.060(5):** where different brokers **in the same firm** represent different parties, *"the
  firm's **designated broker, and any managing broker responsible for the supervision of both brokers, is a
  limited dual agent**"* — while *"each appointed broker shall **solely represent** the party with whom the
  appointed broker has an agency relationship."*

**Supervision has legal consequences in Washington, not merely administrative ones.**

---

## I. And the sentence that will govern everything in the companion course

**RCW 18.86.110:**

> *"**The duties under this chapter are statutory duties and not fiduciary duties. This chapter supersedes
> the fiduciary duties of an agent to a principal under the common law.** The common law continues to apply
> to the parties in all other respects. ... **This chapter shall be construed broadly.**"*

Washington kept the word **agent** and replaced what stands behind it. A student who arrives with a national
textbook's account of fiduciary duty — loyalty, obedience, disclosure, confidentiality, accounting,
reasonable care as **common-law fiduciary** obligations — has an account **Washington superseded by
statute.**

chunks.heading: Module WA-F-01 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
What remains is **the list in RCW 18.86.030**, owed to **all parties**, plus the relationship-specific lists
in **.040, .050 and .060** — and nothing else. Module WA-P-01 takes it up.

---

## Module WA-F-01 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied scenario, five engagement items and five remediation items. The **80 percent**
engagement threshold and the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**. **The 70
percent that IS a regulator figure** applies to the **comprehensive course examination** WAC
308-124H-820(8) requires, which is a separate event carrying **at least 180 items** for this course.

---

## Instructor source note for Module WA-F-01

Drawn from **RCW 18.85.101** and **WAC 308-124H-810, -820, -830, -835, -840, -845 and -855**, read on
2026-08-20 from the Washington State Legislature's official sites, together with **RCW 18.86.010, 18.86.020,
18.86.060 and 18.86.110.**

**Not obtained, and therefore the source of nothing here:** the **Department of Licensing's prescribed course
curriculum**; **WAC 308-124A-800** and **WAC 308-124A-802**; the remainder of **RCW 18.85** in its own text,
including **RCW 18.85.011**, **18.85.041**, **18.85.141** and **18.85.361**; **WAC 308-124, 308-124A,
308-124B, 308-124C, 308-124D and 308-124E**; **ARELLO's certification standards**; and any **Department
examination content outline or candidate handbook.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WA-F-01
chunks.excerpt:
**No licensing examination item count, passing score, time limit, application fee, course fee or penalty is
stated in this module.** The **90 hours**, the **three-hour fair housing and consumer protection block**, the
**two-year window**, the **50-minute clock hour**, the **three-questions-per-clock-hour** examination rule,
the **90-question floor**, the **70 percent** passing grade and the **nine certificate items** are all
**transcribed from RCW 18.85.101 and WAC 308-124H.**

lessons.title: Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-02

chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-02
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-02

## Real property, estates and interests

**Course:** Real Estate Fundamentals · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 60.0 · **Clock hour = 50 minutes**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

> **Source note.** This module teaches **general real property concepts** — the vocabulary needed before
> any Washington rule can be applied. **RCW 18.85, RCW 18.86 and WAC 308-124H do not define most of these
> terms**, because they regulate licensees rather than codify property law. Washington's own property
> statutes — the **Residential Landlord-Tenant Act (RCW 59.18)**, the **condominium and common interest
> community acts (RCW 64.34, RCW 64.90)**, and the **deed of trust act (RCW 61.24)** — were **not read for
> this project**, and this module states no provision of any of them.

## Learning objectives

1. Distinguish real from personal property and apply the fixture tests.
2. Identify the bundle of rights and the government powers that limit it.
3. Distinguish freehold from leasehold estates.
4. Distinguish the forms of concurrent ownership, including Washington's community property character.
5. Distinguish liens from non-lien encumbrances.
6. Connect each of these to the broker's statutory duty to route — RCW 18.86.040(1)(c).

---

## A. Real and personal property

**Land** is the surface, what lies beneath, and the airspace above. **Real property** is land plus what is
permanently attached plus the rights running with it. **Personal property** is everything else.

The distinction decides what conveys. A deed carries the real property. It does not carry the washing
machine unless the agreement says so.

### A.1 Fixtures

chunks.heading: A.2 Trade fixtures and emblements
chunks.excerpt:
An article of personal property that has become real property by attachment. The tests, in order:

1. **Method of annexation** — how firmly attached, and what damage removal would cause.
2. **Adaptation** — was it made or fitted for this property specifically.
3. **Relationship of the parties** — a tenant's attachment reads differently from an owner's.
4. **Intention** — usually controlling, read from the objective circumstances rather than from what
   somebody now says they meant.

**The practical answer is not the doctrine.** Name in writing what stays and what goes, item by item,
before anyone signs. Every fixture dispute a broker ever sees was preventable by a sentence.

### A.2 Trade fixtures and emblements

**Trade fixtures** are articles a **tenant** attaches for a **business** — shelving, coolers, display
counters. They remain the tenant's and are removable **before the term ends**, after which they generally
pass to the landlord by **accession**. The lease can change the default.

**Emblements** are annual crops produced by cultivation; a tenant farmer generally retains the right to
harvest what was planted before the tenancy ended.

---

## B. The bundle of rights, and what limits it

Ownership is a **bundle** because the sticks can be sold separately: **possession**, **use**,
**exclusion**, **disposition**, and **encumbrance**.

A landowner who grants a utility easement has sold a stick. One who leases has transferred possession and
kept the rest. One who grants a deed of trust has pledged, not conveyed.

### B.1 The four government powers

chunks.heading: B.2 Appurtenant rights, and a Washington-specific caution
chunks.excerpt:
- **Police power** — regulation for public health, safety and welfare: zoning, building codes, subdivision
  regulation, environmental rules. **No compensation**, because nothing is taken.
- **Eminent domain** — taking for public use, **with just compensation**, through **condemnation**.
- **Taxation** — levy against real property.
- **Escheat** — property reverts to the state when an owner dies with no heirs and no will.

**The compensation line is the distinction to hold: police power regulates without paying; eminent domain
takes and pays.**

### B.2 Appurtenant rights, and a Washington-specific caution

Rights running with the land: **air rights**, **subsurface and mineral rights**, **water rights**, and
**appurtenant easements**.

**Water rights deserve their own sentence in Washington.** Much of the Commonwealth's agricultural and
rural land turns on water availability and on the right to use it, and the governing law is a body of
Washington statute and administrative practice **this project did not read.** A broker who reassures a
buyer that a rural parcel "has water" has made a representation they cannot support. **The question goes to
the Department of Ecology, to a water rights professional, and to counsel** — which is exactly what RCW
18.86.040(1)(c) and 18.86.050(1)(c) require:

> *"To **advise the [principal] to seek expert advice on matters relating to the transaction that are
> beyond the agent's expertise**."*

**That is a statutory duty in Washington, not a courtesy.**

---

## C. Estates in land

### C.1 Freehold

**Fee simple absolute** — the largest estate: perpetual, inheritable, freely transferable, subject to
government powers and to whatever encumbers it.

**Fee simple defeasible** — a fee that can end on a stated condition:

chunks.heading: C.2 Leasehold
chunks.excerpt:
- **Determinable** — ends **automatically**, with a possibility of reverter. Language of duration: *so long
  as*, *while*, *during*.
- **Subject to a condition subsequent** — the grantor holds a **right of re-entry** and must act. Language
  of condition: *but if*, *provided that*, *on condition that*.

The difference is whether title returns by itself or must be taken back, and it turns on words in a deed a
lawyer drafted. **A broker's job is to notice the language and route it**, not to construe it.

**Life estate** — measured by a life. The **life tenant** may possess and use and must avoid **waste**.
When the measuring life ends the estate passes to the **remainderman** or **reverts**. A life estate **pur
autre vie** is measured by a life other than the holder's.

### C.2 Leasehold

| Estate | How it ends |
|---|---|
| **Estate for years** | Definite beginning, definite end. **Terminates on its own terms; no notice required.** |
| **Periodic tenancy** | Renews period to period **until proper notice**. |
| **Tenancy at will** | Continues at the pleasure of both parties. |
| **Tenancy at sufferance** | A holdover the landlord never agreed to. |

**Notice periods for a Washington periodic tenancy are set by the Residential Landlord-Tenant Act, RCW
59.18, which this project did not read. No notice period is stated in this course.**

### C.3 A lease is two things at once

A **conveyance** of a possessory interest for a term, **and a contract** of covenants. That dual nature is
why a lease dispute can be framed as a breach of contract or as an interference with possession, and why
the **covenant of quiet enjoyment** matters as much as any written clause.

chunks.heading: D. Concurrent ownership — and Washington's own character
chunks.excerpt:
**Assignment** transfers the tenant's **entire** remaining interest; a **sublease** transfers **less than
all** of it. **In both cases the original tenant generally remains liable unless expressly released** — and
tenants routinely assume otherwise.

---

## D. Concurrent ownership — and Washington's own character

**Tenancy in common.** Undivided interests that may be **unequal**, **no survivorship**, each co-tenant may
generally transfer or encumber their own interest and seek **partition**.

**Joint tenancy.** Requires the four unities — **possession, interest, time, title** — with a **right of
survivorship**. Severing a unity converts the severed share to a tenancy in common.

### D.1 Washington is a community property state

**Washington is one of a minority of states in which property acquired during marriage is presumptively
community property.** That single fact changes several practical questions a broker meets weekly:

- **Who must sign.** A listing or a deed signed by one spouse may not convey or bind what both own.
- **What the title report shows**, and whether a separate-property characterisation is documented.
- **How the estate passes** on death, and what a will can and cannot do with it.

chunks.heading: D.2 Why the deed matters at a listing appointment
chunks.excerpt:
> **What this course does NOT state.** **Washington's community property statutes were not read for this
> project.** This module therefore states **no rule about what is community property, what is separate
> property, how either is characterised, how it may be conveyed, or how it passes at death.** It states
> **that Washington is a community property state**, which is the fact a broker must know in order to ask
> the right question — and it routes the answer to **the title company and to counsel.**
>
> This is not evasion. A broker who guesses at community property characterisation has guessed at whether
> the seller can convey.

**Ownership in trust, by entity, and in common-interest communities** — condominium and planned community
forms — are further structures. **RCW 64.34 and RCW 64.90 were not obtained by this project**, and no
provision of either is stated here.

### D.2 Why the deed matters at a listing appointment

The names on a deed determine **who must sign**. Read the deed. Ask who is on title. Ask whether the
sellers are married and when the property was acquired. Where the answer is not obvious, **route it** —
RCW 18.86.040(1)(c).

---

## E. Encumbrances

### E.1 Liens — money claims

chunks.heading: E.2 Non-lien encumbrances — use claims
chunks.excerpt:
- **Deed of trust** — Washington's dominant security instrument, and a **three-party** arrangement
  (grantor, trustee, beneficiary) rather than a two-party mortgage. **RCW 61.24, the Deeds of Trust Act,
  was not read for this project**, and no foreclosure procedure, notice period or timeline is stated in
  this course.
- **Property tax lien** — statutory, involuntary, and generally superior in priority.
- **Mechanics' and materialmen's lien** — for work or materials. **Washington's lien statute was not read;
  no filing deadline, threshold or priority rule is stated.**
- **Judgment lien**, and **special assessments** for public improvements.

**General liens** attach to all a debtor's property; **specific liens** to identified property.
**Voluntary** liens are granted; **involuntary** liens arise by law.

### E.2 Non-lien encumbrances — use claims

- **Easement** — an interest in land. **Appurtenant** easements benefit a dominant parcel and run with the
  land; easements **in gross** benefit a person or entity.
- **Licence** — revocable permission, personal, **not** an interest in land.
- **Encroachment** — a physical intrusion across a boundary. Found by a **survey**, not by a fence.
- **Restrictive covenant** — a private limitation running with the land.

**A restrictive covenant is private and enforced privately; zoning is public and enforced by the
municipality.** Where the two differ, **the more restrictive controls what the owner may actually do** — and
a broker who checked only the zoning has checked half of it.

---

## F. Where this module stops

Everything above is vocabulary, and **none of it authorises a broker to give an opinion.**

**RCW 18.86.030(2)** states the limit from one side:

chunks.heading: Module WA-F-02 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
> *"Unless otherwise agreed, a broker **owes no duty to conduct an independent inspection** of the property
> or to conduct an independent investigation of either party's financial condition, and owes **no duty to
> independently verify the accuracy or completeness of any statement** made by either party or by any
> source reasonably believed by the broker to be reliable."*

**RCW 18.86.040(1)(c) and 18.86.050(1)(c)** state the duty from the other:

> *"To **advise ... to seek expert advice on matters relating to the transaction that are beyond the agent's
> expertise**."*

**Together they define the job.** You need not investigate. You must recognise the question and send it
where it is answered. The vocabulary in this module is what lets you recognise it.

---

## Module WA-F-02 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module WA-F-01. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100
percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**; the **70 percent** that is the director's applies
to the comprehensive course examination WAC 308-124H-820(8) requires.

---

## Instructor source note for Module WA-F-02

**RCW 18.86** was read on 2026-08-20 and is the source of **§ 18.86.030(2)** and **§§ 18.86.040(1)(c) and
18.86.050(1)(c)**, transcribed above. **Every other concept in this module is general real property law**,
taught as vocabulary.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WA-F-02
chunks.excerpt:
**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this build:** **Washington's community property statutes**; the
**Residential Landlord-Tenant Act (RCW 59.18)**; the **Deeds of Trust Act (RCW 61.24)**; the **condominium
and common interest community acts (RCW 64.34, RCW 64.90)**; Washington's **mechanics' lien**, **adverse
possession**, **water rights** and **subsurface rights** statutes; and the remainder of **RCW 18.85**.

**No notice period, filing deadline, lien threshold, priority rule, foreclosure timeline, community property
rule or condominium rescission period is stated in this module.**

lessons.title: Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-03

chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-03
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-03

## Legal descriptions, encumbrances of record and land use control

**Course:** Real Estate Fundamentals · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 60.0 · **Clock hour = 50 minutes**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

## Learning objectives

1. Read the three legal description methods and identify which Washington uses.
2. Compute area and acreage from a description.
3. Distinguish a legal description from an address, a tax parcel number and a plat reference.
4. Distinguish zoning, variances, conditional uses and nonconforming uses.
5. Identify the land use questions a broker routes rather than answers.
6. Apply the material fact definition in RCW 18.86.010(11) to a land use problem.

---

## A. Legal descriptions

An **address** identifies a mailbox. A **tax parcel number** identifies an assessment record. **Neither
describes land.**

### A.1 The rectangular (government) survey — Washington's primary system

Washington is a **public land survey state**, and most of its land is described by **township, range and
section** referenced to the **Willamette Meridian**.

- A **township** is six miles square and contains **36 sections**.
- A **section** is **one square mile** and contains **640 acres**.
- Sections are numbered **1 through 36**, beginning in the **north-east** corner and running **boustrophedon**
  — west across the top row, east across the second, and so on.

**Worked example.** *The NW ¼ of the SE ¼ of Section 14* contains 640 × ¼ × ¼ = **40 acres.** Read the
description **backwards** — start at the section, take the SE quarter, then the NW quarter of that. Each
"of" divides.

chunks.heading: A.2 Metes and bounds
chunks.excerpt:
*The E ½ of the NW ¼ of the SW ¼* contains 640 × ¼ × ¼ × ½ = **20 acres.**

### A.2 Metes and bounds

Used in Washington for parcels the rectangular system does not neatly describe — irregular tracts, water
boundaries, and older conveyances. A metes and bounds description begins at a **point of beginning**, runs
**courses** and **distances**, calls **monuments**, and **returns to the point of beginning**.

**A description that does not close describes no parcel**, and that is a surveyor's problem, not a broker's.
**Monuments generally control over distances** where they conflict, because a called monument is physical
evidence of what the parties meant.

**A fence is not a boundary.** It is evidence of where somebody once thought the boundary was. Where a
fence, hedge, driveway or outbuilding sits near a line, the answer is a **current survey**.

### A.3 Reference to a recorded plat

*Lot 7, Block 3, [named] Addition, according to the plat recorded in Volume __ of Plats, page __, records of
__ County, Washington.* The recorded plat supplies the description by reference, and **the plat is only as
good as its recording.**

### A.4 What a broker actually does

Read the description in the listing **against the seller's own deed** and against a **survey**. If the seller
says the property "includes the strip down to the creek" and the deed does not describe it, you have found a
question — and RCW 18.86.040(1)(c) tells you what to do with it.

**Area conversions worth memorising:** **1 acre = 43,560 square feet.** **1 section = 640 acres = 1 square
mile.** **1 township = 36 sections.**

---

## B. Encumbrances of record, and how they are found

chunks.heading: C. Land use control
chunks.excerpt:
A **title search** discloses what the public record holds against the parcel: **deeds of trust and other
liens**, **easements**, **restrictive covenants**, **plat notes and dedications**, **judgments**, and
**assessments**.

**A preliminary commitment for title insurance lists exceptions** — the matters the policy will **not**
cover. **Reading the exceptions is the point of receiving it**, and a broker who hands a buyer a commitment
without saying so has handed over a document the buyer will not open.

**No Washington title policy form, exception schedule or rate manual was read for this project.** This course
states no policy term, exception or premium. **Coverage questions go to the title company and to counsel.**

---

## C. Land use control

### C.1 The instruments

- **Comprehensive plan** — the jurisdiction's long-range policy. In Washington this sits inside a statutory
  planning framework; **the Growth Management Act and Washington's planning statutes were not read for this
  project**, and this course states no requirement of any of them.
- **Zoning ordinance** — the enforceable rule: **use districts**, plus **bulk and dimensional controls** —
  setbacks, height, lot coverage, minimum lot area, frontage.
- **Subdivision ordinance** — governs dividing land, short plats and full plats.
- **Building codes** — with permits and a **certificate of occupancy**.
- **Critical areas and shoreline regulation** — a genuinely Washington-specific layer. Wetlands, steep
  slopes, fish and wildlife habitat, aquifer recharge areas and marine and freshwater shorelines carry
  regulation that can materially limit what may be built. **The governing statutes and every local ordinance
  were not read for this project. No buffer width, slope threshold, shoreline designation or permit

chunks.heading: C.2 The four relief mechanisms
chunks.excerpt:
requirement is stated in this course.**

### C.2 The four relief mechanisms

| Mechanism | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Variance** | Permission to depart from a dimensional or use requirement, generally on a hardship showing not created by the owner. |
| **Conditional use permit** | A use the ordinance **already contemplates** in that district, allowed once stated conditions are met. |
| **Nonconforming use** | A use that **lawfully predates** the ordinance. Its permitted scope, expansion limits and continuation conditions are set by the ordinance. |
| **Rezone** | Amendment of the ordinance itself — a legislative act. |

**Students merge the first three constantly.** A **variance** asks for an exception; a **conditional use**
asks for something the rule already allows on conditions; a **nonconforming use** asks for nothing, because
it was there first.

**"Grandfathered" is not a legal term and it is not a broker's conclusion.** When an owner uses it, what they
mean is a legal nonconforming use whose scope is defined by an ordinance the broker has not read. **Say what
is known — the owner states the use predates the current zoning — and route the rest.**

---

## D. Where land use meets the material fact duty

**RCW 18.86.010(11)** defines a material fact:

> *"information that **substantially adversely affects the value of the property or a party's ability to
> perform its obligations** in a real estate transaction, or **operates to materially impair or defeat the
> purpose of the transaction**."*

**RCW 18.86.030(1)(d)** makes disclosing them a duty owed to **all parties**, unwaivable:

chunks.heading: Module WA-F-03 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
> *"To **disclose all existing material facts known by the broker and not apparent or readily ascertainable
> to a party**; **provided that this subsection shall not be construed to imply any duty to investigate
> matters that the broker has not agreed to investigate**."*

Apply the two together to land use, because the analysis is not obvious.

**A known critical-area designation that prevents building on the buildable portion of a lot** substantially
adversely affects value and may defeat the purpose of the transaction. If the broker **knows** it and it is
**not apparent or readily ascertainable**, it is disclosed.

**But the proviso is real.** *"This subsection shall not be construed to imply any duty to investigate
matters that the broker has not agreed to investigate."* A broker is not required to research the wetland
inventory. The duty attaches to **what the broker knows.**

**And RCW 18.86.030(2)** removes any duty *"to conduct an independent inspection"* or *"to independently
verify the accuracy or completeness of any statement made by either party or by any source reasonably
believed by the broker to be reliable."*

**So the shape is: no duty to dig, an absolute duty to disclose what you know, and a statutory duty to tell
the party to get expert advice.** Those three sentences answer most Washington land use questions a broker
faces.

---

## Module WA-F-03 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module WA-F-01. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100 percent**
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**.

---

## Instructor source note for Module WA-F-03

**RCW 18.86** was read on 2026-08-20 and is the source of **§§ 18.86.010(11), 18.86.030(1)(d), 18.86.030(2)
and 18.86.040(1)(c)**, transcribed above.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WA-F-03
chunks.excerpt:
**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this build:** **Washington's Growth Management Act** and every
planning, zoning, subdivision, **critical areas** and **shoreline** statute or local ordinance; **Washington's
recording statutes**; any **title insurance policy form or rate manual**; and the remainder of **RCW 18.85**
and **WAC 308-124**.

**No setback, height limit, lot size, buffer width, slope threshold, shoreline designation, permit fee,
approval deadline, title policy exception or premium is stated in this module.** The **640-acre section**,
the **36-section township** and the **43,560-square-foot acre** are universal survey constants.

lessons.title: Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-04

chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-04
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-04

## Transfer of title, deeds, recording and title assurance

**Course:** Real Estate Fundamentals · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 60.0 · **Clock hour = 50 minutes**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

## Learning objectives

1. Distinguish voluntary from involuntary transfer.
2. State the essential elements of a valid deed.
3. Distinguish deed types by the covenants each carries — including Washington's statutory warranty deed.
4. Explain what recording accomplishes and what it does not.
5. Distinguish owner's from lender's title insurance.
6. Describe a Washington closing and the broker's role in it.

---

## A. Voluntary transfer

**By deed** during life; **by will** at death — the maker a **testator**, the gift of real property a
**devise**; and **by dedication**, where an owner gives land to public use.

## B. Involuntary transfer

chunks.heading: C. The deed
chunks.excerpt:
- **Intestate succession** — no will. **Washington's intestacy statute was not read for this project**, and
  no share, priority or spousal provision is stated. Note that Washington's **community property**
  character bears directly on this, which is a further reason it goes to counsel.
- **Escheat** — no heirs and no will.
- **Eminent domain** — condemnation with just compensation.
- **Non-judicial foreclosure under a deed of trust** — Washington's dominant remedy. **RCW 61.24, the Deeds
  of Trust Act, was not read for this project**, and **no notice period, timeline, reinstatement right,
  redemption right or deficiency rule is stated in this course.**
- **Tax foreclosure** for unpaid property taxes.
- **Adverse possession** — title by possession that is, in the usual formulation, **open, notorious,
  continuous, exclusive and hostile under a claim of right for the statutory period.** **Washington's
  statutory period was not read for this project and is not stated here.** What matters to a broker is
  recognising the trigger: a long-standing fence, a neighbour's driveway, an outbuilding across a line —
  all go to a surveyor and counsel.
- **Accretion, erosion, avulsion and reliction** — the work of water on a boundary, which in a state with
  Washington's shoreline and river frontage is not a theoretical topic.

---

## C. The deed

### C.1 Essential elements

**Grantor** with capacity; **grantee** identified with certainty; **words of conveyance**; **consideration**
recited; **legal description**; **grantor's signature**; and **delivery and acceptance.**

**A deed takes effect on delivery, not on signing and not on recording.** The grantee does not sign a deed.
**Acknowledgement before a notary is required for recording.**

### C.2 Deed types

chunks.heading: D. Recording
chunks.excerpt:
| Deed | What it warrants |
|---|---|
| **Statutory warranty deed** | Washington's common conveyance instrument. By statute it carries the full covenants of warranty without their being written out. |
| **Special (limited) warranty deed** | Covenants only against defects arising during the grantor's ownership. |
| **Bargain and sale deed** | Implies the grantor holds title; covenants vary by form. |
| **Quitclaim deed** | Conveys whatever interest the grantor has — **possibly none** — with **no warranty**. |

**A statutory warranty deed is short because the statute supplies the covenants.** That is its point: the
form is compact and the protection is full. **This course states no text of Washington's statutory form**,
because the statute prescribing it was not read for this project.

**A quitclaim deed is not a lesser-quality conveyance of good title. It conveys whatever the grantor
happens to hold, warranting nothing** — which is why it is the right instrument for clearing a cloud and
the wrong one for a purchase. **Recording does not improve it: a recorded quitclaim deed is still a
quitclaim deed.**

**Special-purpose deeds** — personal representative's, trustee's, sheriff's, and a **deed in lieu of
foreclosure** — are named here so a broker recognises them in a chain of title. Each raises questions of
authority belonging to a title examiner and counsel.

---

## D. Recording

### D.1 What recording does

Recording with the **county auditor** in the county where the property lies gives **constructive notice** to
the world. Everyone is treated as knowing what the record contains, whether they looked or not.

chunks.heading: D.2 What recording does not do
chunks.excerpt:
- **Actual notice** — what a person in fact knows.
- **Constructive notice** — what the record imputes.
- **Inquiry notice** — what a person would have learned had they investigated a fact that should have
  prompted investigation. **Someone else in possession** is the classic trigger.

### D.2 What recording does not do

**It does not validate an invalid instrument** — a forged deed is void whether recorded or not. **It does
not improve the estate conveyed.** **It does not establish that the grantor had good title.**

**Washington's recording statute was not read for this project.** This course therefore **states no
Washington recording priority rule and no recording deadline.** The practical consequence is universal: an
unrecorded interest is an exposure, and prompt recording is how a purchaser protects what they bought.

### D.3 A note on notice and RCW 18.86.100

Washington reverses one common-law notice rule by statute, and it belongs here:

> **RCW 18.86.100:** *"Unless otherwise agreed to in writing, **a principal does not have knowledge or
> notice of any facts known by an agent of the principal that are not actually known by the principal**."*

**Under the common law an agent's knowledge is generally imputed to the principal. Washington provides the
opposite by statute.** A seller is not charged with what their broker knew and did not tell them. Module
WA-P-03 develops it; it appears here because it is a **notice** rule and this is the notice module.

---

## E. Evidence of title and title insurance

chunks.heading: E.1 Two policies, two beneficiaries
chunks.excerpt:
**Chain of title** — the successive conveyances. **Title search and examination** — running the chain and
reading what it discloses. **Cloud on title** — an outstanding claim or apparent defect: an unreleased deed
of trust, a gap in the chain, an unsatisfied judgment, an heir who never joined in a deed. **Marketable
title** — title a reasonable buyer would accept, free of reasonable doubt. **Quiet title action** — the
lawsuit to resolve a cloud.

### E.1 Two policies, two beneficiaries

- **Lender's (mortgagee's) policy** — protects the **lender**, in the amount of the loan, decreasing as the
  loan is paid. Almost always required by the lender.
- **Owner's policy** — protects the **owner**, in the amount of the purchase price.

**A buyer who pays for a lender's policy has bought the lender protection, not themselves.** That is the
single most useful sentence a broker can say at a Washington closing table, and it takes five seconds.

**Every policy has exceptions** — matters it does not cover, often including matters a **survey** would
disclose. **No policy form or rate manual was read for this project**, and no term, exception, endorsement
or premium is stated in this course.

---

## F. Closing in Washington

**Closing is conducted by an escrow agent, a title company, or an attorney.** The parties' funds and
documents are delivered into escrow, conditions are satisfied, documents are recorded, and funds are
disbursed.

### F.1 What the broker does, and what the broker does not

**Does:** track deadlines; deliver documents; keep both sides informed; account for money and property
received; recognise questions and route them.

**Does not:** conduct the closing, prepare the deed, opine on title, or advise on the legal effect of an
instrument.

chunks.heading: F.2 Prorations
chunks.excerpt:
**The statutory basis is two sentences in RCW 18.86.030(1):**

> **(e)** *"To **account in a timely manner for all money and property received from or on behalf of either
> party**";*

and, from **RCW 18.86.040(1)(c)** and **18.86.050(1)(c)**:

> *"To **advise ... to seek expert advice on matters relating to the transaction that are beyond the agent's
> expertise**."*

**And RCW 18.86.110 closes the door on the other side:** *"This chapter **does not affect the duties of a
broker while engaging in the authorized or unauthorized practice of law** as determined by the courts of
this state."* Whatever the practice-of-law boundary is, RCW 18.86 does not move it.

### F.2 Prorations

Items paid in advance or in arrears are **prorated** as of closing — real estate taxes, assessments,
homeowner association dues, rents and deposits on tenanted property, and any fuel remaining.

**A proration is always a double entry.** Whatever is credited to one party is debited to the other. A
prorated item appearing once has been done wrong.

**Which party owns the day of closing, and whether a 360-day or 365-day convention applies, are matters of
contract and local practice. This course states neither as a Washington rule**, because the statutes and
rules read for this project state neither. Practice problems specify the convention inside the problem.

### F.3 Excise tax

Washington imposes a **real estate excise tax** on the sale of real property, and it is a line every
Washington closing statement carries.

chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-05
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-05

## Contract law fundamentals

**Course:** Real Estate Fundamentals · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 60.0 · **Clock hour = 50 minutes**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

## Learning objectives

1. State the essential elements of a valid contract.
2. Distinguish void, voidable, unenforceable and valid.
3. Apply offer, acceptance, counteroffer and the mirror image rule.
4. Identify the defects in reality of consent.
5. State what a writing is required for, and what RCW 18.86 separately requires in writing.
6. Distinguish the remedies for breach and explain why specific performance is available.
7. Apply RCW 18.86.010(15) — when a prospective transaction begins.

---

## A. Essential elements

**Competent parties. Mutual assent. Consideration. Lawful object.** And **a writing**, where the Statute of
Frauds requires one — which it does for contracts conveying an interest in real property.

**Recording and notarisation are not elements of a contract.** They belong to the conveyance and the
recording statute. A contract can be valid, fully enforceable and never recorded.

### A.1 Four states a contract can be in

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Valid** | Meets all elements; enforceable by either party. |
| **Void** | Never had legal effect. |
| **Voidable** | Valid **until the party holding the power to avoid it elects to do so**. |
| **Unenforceable** | Valid in substance; a court will not enforce it — commonly for want of a writing. |

chunks.heading: A.2 Classifications
chunks.excerpt:
**The difference between void and voidable is who holds the power.** A contract with a minor is voidable
**at the minor's election** — the adult cannot escape it. A contract induced by fraud is voidable at the
**defrauded** party's election — the party who lied cannot use their own fraud to get out.

### A.2 Classifications

**Bilateral** (promise for promise — most purchase and sale agreements) versus **unilateral** (promise for
an act — most options on their face). **Express** versus **implied**. **Executory** (still being performed)
versus **executed** (fully performed).

**A purchase and sale agreement is executory from mutual acceptance until closing** — and that period, with
deadlines falling and money in escrow, is where a broker does most of the work.

---

## B. Offer and acceptance

An **offer** is a manifestation of willingness to be bound on stated terms. It may be **revoked at any time
before acceptance**, unless consideration was given to hold it open — which is what an **option** is.

An offer **terminates** by **revocation**, **rejection**, **lapse**, **death or incapacity of either party**,
**destruction of the subject matter**, or **counteroffer**.

### B.1 The mirror image rule

Acceptance must be **unqualified** and **mirror** the offer. A purported acceptance that **changes any term
is a counteroffer** — which **rejects and terminates the original offer** and reverses the roles.

Work it through. A buyer offers Monday. The seller signs Tuesday but strikes the closing date and writes a
new one. That is **not an acceptance.** The buyer's offer is **gone**, and cannot be revived by the buyer
signing the original on Wednesday. What exists is the seller's counteroffer.

chunks.heading: B.2 The duty that applies whichever side you are on
chunks.excerpt:
**Acceptance must also be communicated.** A signed agreement sitting in a drawer has accepted nothing.

### B.2 The duty that applies whichever side you are on

**RCW 18.86.030(1)(c)** — owed to the principal **and to all parties**, and **not waivable**:

> *"To **present all written offers, written notices and other written communications to and from either
> party in a timely manner, regardless of whether the property is subject to an existing contract for sale
> or the buyer is already a party to an existing contract to purchase**."*

**Read the "regardless" clause, because it is unusually strong.** In many states a listing broker's duty to
present offers softens once the property is under contract, or requires a seller's waiver. **Washington
states the opposite in the statute itself: the duty continues regardless.**

**Note also what it reaches: WRITTEN offers, notices and communications, in BOTH directions.** The statutory
duty is expressed in terms of writings.

### B.3 When a "transaction" begins

**RCW 18.86.010(15):**

> *"For purposes of this chapter, **a prospective transaction does not exist until a written offer has been
> signed by at least one party**."*

That definition decides when several of RCW 18.86's duties attach, and it is precise: **a signed written
offer by at least one party.** Conversations, showings and verbal indications do not start it.

---

## C. Reality of consent

Assent must be real. It is defective where there is **fraud**, **misrepresentation** (innocent or
negligent), **duress**, **undue influence**, or **mistake** — mutual mistake of material fact may permit
rescission; unilateral mistake usually does not. **In each case the contract is voidable at the election of
the injured party.**

chunks.heading: D. Writings
chunks.excerpt:
**Puffing** is opinion a reasonable person would not rely on as fact — *"a wonderful home."*
**Misrepresentation** is a false statement of fact — *"2,400 square feet," "the roof is five years old,"
"the crawl space has never taken water."* **The line moves toward misrepresentation as the statement becomes
more specific and more verifiable.**

**And RCW 18.86.030(1)(b) is owed to everyone and unwaivable:** *"To **deal honestly and in good faith**."*

---

## D. Writings

Contracts for the sale of an interest in real property must generally be **in writing and signed by the
party to be charged** to be enforceable. **Washington's Statute of Frauds was not read for this project**,
and this course **states no Washington lease-term threshold and no Washington exception.**

**What was read is RCW 18.86, and it requires writings of its own** — which are not Statute of Frauds
requirements but licensing-law requirements, and reach further:

chunks.heading: D.1 The parol evidence rule
chunks.excerpt:
- **RCW 18.86.020(2)(a):** *"A firm **must enter into a services agreement with the principal before, or as
  soon as reasonably practical after**, its appointed broker commences rendering real estate brokerage
  services."*
- **RCW 18.86.030(1)(g):** the agency disclosure must be **in writing**, *"in a **separate paragraph titled
  'Agency Disclosure'**"* in the agreement or in a separate writing so titled.
- **RCW 18.86.060(1):** limited dual agency requires *"the **written consent of both parties** to the
  transaction, **set forth in the services agreement**."*
- **RCW 18.86.080(7):** *"**To receive compensation** for rendering real estate brokerage services from any
  party or firm, a real estate firm **must have a services agreement**"* containing stated terms.
- **RCW 18.86.040(1) and .050(1):** the relationship duties may not be waived *"except as expressly set
  forth in (e),"* and additional duties arise only *"if agreed to **in writing signed by**"* the agent.

**A broker who asks "does the Statute of Frauds require this in writing?" has asked a question that often
does not matter. The operative question in Washington practice is what RCW 18.86 requires**, and the answer
is: **the services agreement, the agency disclosure, the dual agency consent, and the compensation terms.**

### D.1 The parol evidence rule

Where a written contract is a complete expression of the agreement, evidence of **prior or contemporaneous
oral agreements offered to vary its terms** is barred. Combined with the writing requirements above, the
working rule is simple: **every change goes on paper, signed.**

---

## E. Performance, breach and remedies

A contract discharges by **performance**, **mutual agreement**, **operation of law**, or **breach**.

chunks.heading: E.1 Where the money sits while any of this happens
chunks.excerpt:
**Assignment** transfers rights and generally **leaves the assignor liable**. **Novation** substitutes a new
party and **releases** the original — which is why it needs everyone's agreement. Confusing the two is how a
seller discovers, after an assignment they approved, that they are still on the hook.

**Remedies:** **damages**; **liquidated damages** (commonly the earnest money, where the agreement so
provides); **rescission**; and **specific performance**.

**Specific performance is available in real estate because each parcel is unique**, so damages are often
inadequate. That is the legal consequence of a physical characteristic of land.

### E.1 Where the money sits while any of this happens

**RCW 18.86.030(1)(e)** — owed to all parties, unwaivable:

> *"To **account in a timely manner for all money and property received from or on behalf of either
> party**."*

**And RCW 18.86.070(2):** after termination of the agency relationship a broker owes **no further duty**
except two — *"(a) **to account for all moneys and property received during the relationship**; and (b) **to
not disclose confidential information**."*

**Two duties survive termination, and one of them is accounting.** Washington's trust account rules sit in
**WAC 308-124 and the remainder of RCW 18.85, which this project did not read** — so **this course states no
deposit deadline, no account requirement and no reconciliation interval.** The duty to account is stated
because the statute states it; the mechanics are routed.

---

## F. Where a broker stands in relation to a contract

**RCW 18.86.110:** *"This chapter **does not affect the duties of a broker while engaging in the authorized
or unauthorized practice of law as determined by the courts of this state**."*

chunks.heading: Module WA-F-05 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
RCW 18.86 does not move the practice-of-law line, and it does not tell you where the line is. What it does
tell you is what to do when you reach it — **RCW 18.86.040(1)(c) and 18.86.050(1)(c)**:

> *"To **advise ... to seek expert advice on matters relating to the transaction that are beyond the agent's
> expertise**."*

**Completing a form and inventing a term are different acts.** Drafting a clause, construing a provision, or
advising whether a party has a claim or a right to terminate belongs to a lawyer — and sending the party
there is a **statutory duty**, not a courtesy.

---

## Module WA-F-05 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module WA-F-01. The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100 percent**
applied threshold are **StateCourse standards**.

---

## Instructor source note for Module WA-F-05

**RCW 18.86** was read on 2026-08-20 and is the source of **§§ 18.86.010(15), 18.86.020(2)(a), 18.86.030(1)(b),
(c), (e) and (g), 18.86.040(1), 18.86.050(1), 18.86.060(1), 18.86.070(2), 18.86.080(7) and 18.86.110**,
transcribed above. Every other principle in this module is **general contract law**, taught as framework.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this build:** **Washington's Statute of Frauds**; Washington
contract and remedies case law; **WAC 308-124** and the remainder of **RCW 18.85**, including the **trust
account and record-keeping** provisions; and any **standard Washington purchase and sale agreement form or
addendum**.

**No lease-term threshold, limitations period, statutory exception, earnest money deadline, trust account
requirement, liquidated damages cap or form provision is stated in this module.**

chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-06
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-06

## Real estate finance I — instruments, parties and loan types

**Course:** Real Estate Fundamentals · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 60.0 · **Clock hour = 50 minutes**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

## Learning objectives

1. Define the finance vocabulary and compute with it.
2. Distinguish the note from the security instrument.
3. Distinguish a deed of trust from a mortgage, and state which Washington uses.
4. Identify the special provisions of a note and their consequences.
5. Distinguish the loan programmes and repayment types.
6. Distinguish the primary from the secondary mortgage market.

---

## A. Vocabulary, with the arithmetic attached

**Principal and interest. Amortization. Debt service. PITI. Equity. Loan-to-value ratio. Points. Yield.**

**PITI** is the four-part housing payment — principal, interest, taxes, insurance — and it is what
qualifying ratios are computed against, not principal and interest alone.

**Equity** is value less what is owed. **Loan-to-value** is the loan divided by the value the lender
recognises, and lenders customarily recognise **the lower of the contract price and the appraised value.**
That convention is why an appraisal below contract price is a problem for the buyer: **the lender lends
against the lower figure and the difference must come from somewhere.**

**A discount point is one percent of the loan amount**, paid at closing, buying the lender yield. A common
rule of thumb in national content is that a point moves yield by roughly **one-eighth of one percent** — an
approximation, not a formula.

### A.1 Worked examples, all figures given inside the problem

chunks.heading: B. The note and the security instrument — two documents, two jobs
chunks.excerpt:
**Points.** A $415,000 loan with 1.5 points: 415,000 × 0.015 = **$6,225** paid at closing.

**First month's split.** A $415,000 balance at 6.25 percent with a monthly payment of $2,555:
interest = 415,000 × 0.0625 ÷ 12 = **$2,161.46**; principal reduction = 2,555 − 2,161.46 = **$393.54**;
new balance = **$414,606.46.**

**Interest is always computed on the previous balance**, and only the remainder touches principal. That is
why early payments on a thirty-year amortisation barely move the balance.

**Loan-to-value.** Contract price $520,000, appraised value $505,000, loan $404,000. The lender recognises
**$505,000** — the lower — so LTV = 404,000 ÷ 505,000 = **80 percent**, and the buyer covers the $15,000
gap from their own funds.

---

## B. The note and the security instrument — two documents, two jobs

**The promissory note** is the borrower's **promise to repay**. It is a contract, and everything in Module
WA-F-05 applies to it.

**The security instrument** **pledges the property**. **Hypothecation** is the idea that ties them: the
borrower pledges the property **while keeping possession of it.** Nothing about a real estate loan moves the
borrower out.

### B.1 Deed of trust versus mortgage — and which Washington uses

| | **Mortgage** | **Deed of trust — Washington's dominant instrument** |
|---|---|---|
| Parties | **2** | **3** |
| Who they are | Mortgagor, Mortgagee | **Grantor, Trustee, Beneficiary** |
| Foreclosure | **Judicial** | **Non-judicial power of sale**, conducted by the trustee |

**The third party is what makes the shortcut possible.** A **trustee** holds the security for the
beneficiary's benefit and can conduct a sale without a lawsuit.

chunks.heading: B.2 Special note provisions
chunks.excerpt:
**Washington's Deeds of Trust Act is RCW 61.24, and it was not read for this project.** **This course states
no notice period, no timeline, no reinstatement right, no redemption right and no deficiency rule.** A
broker asked about a foreclosure timeline routes the question — to counsel, and to the trustee's own
notices.

**And a caution for a broker working with a distressed seller.** Whether a short sale is possible, what the
lender will accept, and what happens to any deficiency are **legal and lender questions.** A broker who
negotiates a workout with a lender on a borrower's behalf has stepped outside brokerage, and **RCW 18.86.110**
expressly leaves the practice-of-law boundary where the courts put it.

### B.2 Special note provisions

- **Acceleration clause** — on default the **whole balance** becomes due at once.
- **Prepayment penalty clause** — a charge for paying early.
- **Due-on-sale (alienation) clause** — the balance becomes due if the property is sold.

**The due-on-sale clause is why assumption is rare.** Where the lender may call the loan on transfer, a
buyer taking over the seller's existing financing is the exception, not the routine.

### B.3 Subordinate financing and priority

**First**, **second** and further liens rank by **recording**, subject to statutory priorities such as
property tax liens. **Subordination** is the deliberate exception: a lender agreeing to sit behind one who
would otherwise sit behind it.

**And the reconveyance matters.** When a deed of trust is paid, the trustee reconveys, and **a deed of trust
paid off but never reconveyed of record is still a cloud on title.** Module WA-F-04 met the same idea from
the title side.

---

## C. Loan programmes

chunks.heading: D. Repayment types
chunks.excerpt:
- **Conventional** — not government insured or guaranteed. **Conforming** loans meet secondary-market
  standards; **nonconforming** loans do not and are priced accordingly. **Private mortgage insurance (PMI)**
  typically appears at higher loan-to-value.
- **FHA-insured** — FHA **does not build housing and does not lend**; it **insures approved lenders against
  loss.** Borrowers pay a **mortgage insurance premium (MIP)**.
- **VA-guaranteed** — the VA **guarantees** approved lenders against loss for eligible veterans; a **funding
  fee** applies; the defining feature is the possibility of **no down payment.** A **VA release of liability
  does not by itself release the original borrower from liability to the lender** — that takes the lender's
  own release.
- **USDA Rural Development** — direct and guaranteed loans in eligible areas.
- **Washington State Housing Finance Commission programmes** exist for eligible buyers. **No Commission
  programme document was read for this project**, and **no eligibility limit, income cap, purchase price
  limit or assistance amount is stated in this course.** They are named so a broker knows to ask a lender.

**This course states no loan limit, down payment percentage, MIP or funding fee rate, or qualifying ratio**,
because no agency handbook or programme guide was read. Those figures change, and they come from the lender.

---

## D. Repayment types

**Fixed-rate level payment (fully amortized)** — the most common residential plan.

chunks.heading: E. Primary and secondary markets
chunks.excerpt:
**Adjustable rate (ARM)** — with an **index**, a **margin**, a **periodic cap** and a **lifetime cap**. Note
carefully: **a cap on the PAYMENT is not a cap on the INTEREST.** Where a payment cap holds the payment
below the interest accruing, the shortfall is added to principal — **negative amortization** — and the
balance grows.

**Interest-only / term. Balloon (partially amortized). Graduated payment. Growing equity. Buydown**, where a
lump sum at closing reduces the rate temporarily or permanently and may be paid by buyer, seller or third
party.

**By purpose:** **construction**, **blanket** (with a **partial release** clause), **package**, **open-end**,
and **bridge** loans.

**Seller financing** — a **real estate contract** or a **purchase money deed of trust**. Washington has its
own history and its own law here, and **none of it was read for this project.** A broker whose transaction
involves seller financing routes it to counsel, without exception.

---

## E. Primary and secondary markets

The **primary market** is where a loan is **made** — banks, credit unions, savings institutions, mortgage
banking companies and mortgage brokers. The **secondary market** is where a loan already made is **bought**
— **Fannie Mae**, **Freddie Mac** and **Ginnie Mae** — through **loan pooling** and **mortgage-backed
securities.**

**The link is conforming standards.** A lender writes to those standards **so the loan can be sold**, and
selling it returns capital to lend again. That is why a nonconforming loan is priced differently: the lender
may have to keep it.

**The Federal Reserve** affects mortgage rates and the availability of funds through monetary policy. It
does not set mortgage rates directly, and a broker who tells a client otherwise has misstated it.

---

chunks.heading: F. What a broker may and may not say about financing
chunks.excerpt:
## F. What a broker may and may not say about financing

**RCW 18.86.030(2)** removes any duty *"to conduct an independent investigation of either party's financial
condition"* and any duty *"to independently verify the accuracy or completeness of any statement made by
either party or by any source reasonably believed by the broker to be reliable."*

**But no shelter permits an affirmative statement you cannot support.** *"You'll qualify."* *"That'll
appraise."* *"Rates are coming down before your lock expires."* Each is a **representation**, and
**RCW 18.86.030(1)(b)** — deal honestly and in good faith, owed to all parties, unwaivable — is what it will
be measured against.

**The reliable formulation is three words: ask your lender.** And where the question is beyond you,
**RCW 18.86.040(1)(c) and 18.86.050(1)(c)** make sending the client there a duty.

---

## Module WA-F-06 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module WA-F-01. **Every rate, factor and payment used in any item is supplied
inside the item as a given.** The **80 percent** engagement threshold and the **100 percent** applied
threshold are **StateCourse standards**.

---

## Instructor source note for Module WA-F-06

**RCW 18.86** was read on 2026-08-20 and is the source of **§§ 18.86.030(1)(b), 18.86.030(2), 18.86.040(1)(c),
18.86.050(1)(c) and 18.86.110**, transcribed above.

**Not read, and therefore stated nowhere in this build:** the **Deeds of Trust Act (RCW 61.24)**; Washington's
**real estate contract** and **seller financing** statutes; **FHA, VA and USDA** programme handbooks; **Fannie
Mae, Freddie Mac and Ginnie Mae** guides; any **Washington State Housing Finance Commission** programme
document; and **TILA, RESPA and TRID**, which Module WA-F-07 addresses in outline.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WA-F-06
chunks.excerpt:
**No loan limit, insurance premium rate, funding fee, qualifying ratio, index value, foreclosure period,
reinstatement right, redemption right or programme eligibility figure is stated in this module.**

chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-07
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-07

## Real estate finance II — lending practice and federal regulation

**Course:** Real Estate Fundamentals · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 60.0 · **Clock hour = 50 minutes**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

> **Source note stated up front.** **TILA and Regulation Z, RESPA and Regulation X, the TRID rule, ECOA
> and the Fair Credit Reporting Act were NOT read for this project.** This module teaches **what each does
> and what a broker must therefore be careful about.** **It states no disclosure deadline, no tolerance
> category, no trigger term list, no threshold and no penalty**, because the regulations setting them were
> not obtained. Every live deadline goes to the lender.

## Learning objectives

1. Describe the loan application and underwriting sequence.
2. Explain how a borrower and a property are analysed.
3. State what TILA/Regulation Z governs and the safest broker advertising practice.
4. State what RESPA/Regulation X governs, and the referral fee prohibition.
5. Describe what TRID consolidated and why a broker cares about timing.
6. State the broker's own position under RCW 18.86.030(2).

---

## A. The sequence, from application to funding

chunks.heading: B. Underwriting — what is actually being assessed
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Pre-qualification** — an informal assessment on stated figures.
2. **Pre-approval** — a lender's assessment on documented figures, subject to conditions.
3. **Application.**
4. **Disclosure** — the lender issues the initial disclosures the federal rules require.
5. **Processing** — verification of income, assets, employment and credit.
6. **Appraisal** and **title work.**
7. **Underwriting** — the decision, usually with conditions.
8. **Clear to close.**
9. **Closing disclosure and the waiting period the federal rule imposes.**
10. **Signing, funding and recording.**

**A broker's value in that sequence is deadline management and honest expectation-setting**, not lending
advice. **A pre-qualification is not a pre-approval and neither is a commitment**, and a broker who presents
one as another has made a representation the file will not support.

---

## B. Underwriting — what is actually being assessed

### B.1 The borrower

**Credit history and score. Stability and adequacy of income. Assets sufficient to close and to reserve.
Existing recurring obligations. Occupancy intent.**

**Qualifying ratios** compare **housing expense to gross income** and **total recurring debt to gross
income.** **This course states no ratio figures**, because no agency handbook or lender guideline was read
for this project. What a student should carry away is the **structure**: there are generally **two ratios**,
and a buyer must satisfy **both** — passing one and failing the other is not qualifying.

chunks.heading: B.2 The property
chunks.excerpt:
**Worked example with the ratios supplied inside the problem.** *Gross monthly income $8,400; the programme
in this problem uses 28 percent housing and 36 percent total debt.*
Maximum housing expense = 8,400 × 0.28 = **$2,352.**
Maximum total recurring debt = 8,400 × 0.36 = **$3,024.**
If the buyer has $700 of car and student loan payments, the housing expense available under the debt ratio is
3,024 − 700 = **$2,324** — **less than the housing ratio allows.** **The binding constraint is whichever
ratio produces the smaller figure**, and here it is the debt ratio.

*(The 28 and 36 in that example are given inside the problem. They are not stated by this course as
Washington or federal requirements.)*

### B.2 The property

**Appraisal**, **title examination and insurance**, and — for some programmes — **property condition
standards.**

**Loan value is customarily the lower of contract price and appraised value.** Module WA-F-06 worked it.

---

## C. Truth in Lending — TILA and Regulation Z

**What it does:** requires disclosure of the cost of consumer credit and regulates the **advertising** of
consumer credit terms.

**The disclosure a student should recognise:** the **annual percentage rate (APR)**, which folds the cost of
credit — points and certain fees — into a single annualised rate. **The APR is not the interest rate**, and
it is normally higher. Two loans at the same note rate can carry different APRs, which is the entire reason
for requiring it.

**Advertising is where a broker meets Regulation Z**, because it reaches advertisements for consumer credit
**regardless of who places them.** Certain **trigger terms** in an advertisement pull in mandatory
disclosures.

chunks.heading: D. Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act — RESPA and Regulation X
chunks.excerpt:
> **The safest practice, and the one this course recommends: publish no numbers in an advertisement other
> than the price.** A listing that says *"$3,100 a month!"* has entered territory the regulation governs. A
> listing that says *"$589,000"* has not.

**This course states no trigger term list, no required disclosure and no penalty**, because Regulation Z was
not read for this project. A broker planning an advertisement with financing terms in it clears it with the
firm's designated broker and, where appropriate, with the lender.

---

## D. Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act — RESPA and Regulation X

**What it does:** governs settlement services on federally related mortgage loans for residential property,
requires certain disclosures, and **prohibits kickbacks and referral fees among settlement service
providers.**

### D.1 The referral fee prohibition, stated as a working rule

**A broker may not pay or receive a fee, kickback or thing of value for referring settlement service
business.** Escrow agents, title companies, lenders, appraisers, inspectors and home warranty companies are
settlement service providers.

**The practical form the problem takes** is rarely an envelope of cash. It is a marketing agreement priced
above the value of what is delivered, a "co-marketing" arrangement, a desk rental at less than market, or a
gift programme keyed to referral volume. **Every one of them is a question for the firm's designated broker
and for counsel, before it is entered into — not after.**

chunks.heading: D.2 Affiliated business arrangements
chunks.excerpt:
**And there is a Washington overlay that a broker must not lose sight of.** **RCW 18.86.080(2):** *"**An
agreement to pay or payment of compensation does not establish an agency relationship** between the party
who paid the compensation and the broker."* That is a Washington rule about **agency**, not about RESPA, and
the two answer different questions. Module WA-P-04 develops it.

**This course states no RESPA threshold, exemption, disclosure deadline or penalty**, because the statute and
regulation were not read for this project.

### D.2 Affiliated business arrangements

Where a broker refers business to an entity in which the broker or the firm has an interest, federal law
regulates the arrangement and requires disclosure. **The requirements were not read for this project and are
not stated here.** What a student should carry is the trigger: **an ownership or financial interest in a
settlement service provider is a disclosable fact and a compliance question**, and it is also, under **RCW
18.86.040(1)(b) and 18.86.050(1)(b)**, a **conflict of interest the broker must timely disclose to their
principal.**

---

## E. TRID — the consolidated disclosures

The **TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure** rule consolidated the duplicate disclosures the two statutes
required into two forms: the **Loan Estimate**, issued early in the process, and the **Closing Disclosure**,
issued before consummation.

**The rule imposes timing requirements on both**, and changes of certain kinds can restart a waiting period
and delay a closing.

chunks.heading: F. Fair lending — ECOA in outline
chunks.excerpt:
**This course states no TRID deadline, tolerance category or triggering change**, because the rule was not
read for this project. **What a broker must know is that the timing exists and that it is not
negotiable** — so a change requested late in a transaction may move the closing date, and the person who can
say whether it will is **the lender.**

---

## F. Fair lending — ECOA in outline

The **Equal Credit Opportunity Act** prohibits discrimination in credit transactions on prohibited bases.
**ECOA and its implementing regulation were not read for this project**, and **this course states no
prohibited basis list from them.**

**Module WA-F-09 delivers the statutory three-hour fair housing and consumer protection block** required by
RCW 18.85.101(1)(c), and it is the module in which discrimination is addressed in substance. What belongs
here is the **link**: financing is one of the places housing discrimination happens, and a broker who
notices a pattern in how clients are treated by a lender has noticed something that matters.

---

## G. The broker's own position

**RCW 18.86.030(2):**

> *"Unless otherwise agreed, a broker **owes no duty to conduct an independent inspection of the property or
> to conduct an independent investigation of either party's financial condition**, and owes **no duty to
> independently verify the accuracy or completeness of any statement made by either party or by any source
> reasonably believed by the broker to be reliable**."*

**That is a real shelter and it has a real limit.**

chunks.heading: Module WA-F-07 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**No duty to investigate the buyer's finances** — you need not audit a pre-approval letter.
**No duty to verify statements** — including a lender's, where the belief is reasonable.
**But no shelter for an affirmative statement of your own.** Repeating what the lender said, with
attribution, is reporting. Saying *"you're approved"* is a representation, and
**RCW 18.86.030(1)(b)** — deal honestly and in good faith — is owed to **all parties** and **may not be
waived.**

**And the duty to route is statutory: RCW 18.86.040(1)(c) and 18.86.050(1)(c).** Financing questions beyond
your expertise go to the lender. Legal questions go to counsel. Saying so is compliance, not weakness.

---

## Module WA-F-07 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module WA-F-01. **Every ratio, rate and figure used in any item is supplied
inside the item as a given**, and **no item requires a student to recall a federal disclosure deadline,
tolerance or threshold**, because the regulations setting them were not read for this project.

---

## Instructor source note for Module WA-F-07

**RCW 18.86** was read on 2026-08-20 and is the source of **§§ 18.86.030(1)(b), 18.86.030(2), 18.86.040(1)(b)
and (c), 18.86.050(1)(b) and (c) and 18.86.080(2)**, transcribed above.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **TILA and Regulation Z**; **RESPA and Regulation X**;
the **TRID** rule; **ECOA** and its implementing regulation; the **Fair Credit Reporting Act**; the
**Dodd-Frank Act**; **FHA, VA and USDA** handbooks; **Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and Ginnie Mae** guides; and
**WAC 308-124** and the remainder of **RCW 18.85**.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WA-F-07
chunks.excerpt:
**No qualifying ratio, disclosure deadline, tolerance figure, trigger term, threshold, exemption or penalty
is stated in this module as a requirement.** The 28 and 36 percent figures in the worked example are given
inside the example and are not asserted as any regulator's.
