chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-12
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Fundamentals — Module WA-F-12

## Taxes, settlement statements and real estate mathematics

**Course:** Real Estate Fundamentals · **Instructional hours: 7.0** of 60.0 — the largest module in this
course, and the last · **Clock hour = 50 minutes**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

> **Every rate in this module is supplied inside the problem.** **RCW 82.45 (real estate excise tax), every
> local excise tax ordinance, Washington's property tax statutes and the Internal Revenue Code were NOT read
> for this project.** **No tax rate, threshold, bracket, exemption, exclusion or limit is stated anywhere in
> this course.** The method is taught; the rates come from the statute, the county and the client's own tax
> professional.

## Learning objectives

1. Compute area, acreage and cost per unit.
2. Compute commissions, splits and net-to-seller — including the price needed to net a required sum.
3. Compute property tax from a given rate and assessed value.
4. Compute excise tax from a given rate.
5. Compute prorations by both the 360-day and 365-day conventions.
6. Read a settlement statement and place an entry as a debit or a credit to the correct party.
7. Compute the bottom-line figures — cash to close and net to seller.
8. State the boundary between compliance information and tax advice.

---

## A. Area and unit costs

**Constants worth memorising:** **1 acre = 43,560 square feet.** **1 section = 640 acres = 1 square mile.**
**1 township = 36 sections.** **1 square yard = 9 square feet.**

chunks.heading: B. Commissions and net to seller
chunks.excerpt:
**Areas:** rectangle = **base × height**; triangle = **½ × base × height**; trapezoid =
**½ × (base₁ + base₂) × height**. An irregular parcel with straight sides is **decomposed** into those shapes,
each computed and added — not estimated.

**Worked example.** *A lot is a rectangle 120 ft × 210 ft with a right-triangular extension 120 ft × 60 ft.*
Rectangle = 120 × 210 = **25,200 sq ft.** Triangle = ½ × 120 × 60 = **3,600 sq ft.**
Total = **28,800 sq ft** = 28,800 ÷ 43,560 = **0.661 acres.**
At **$14.50 per square foot**, the land is 28,800 × 14.50 = **$417,600.**

---

## B. Commissions and net to seller

**This course states no commission rate, split or minimum.** Compensation is negotiated between a firm and
its principal — and **RCW 18.86.080(7)(a)(i)** requires the services agreement to state **the amount the
principal agrees to compensate the firm.** Every problem below supplies its rate.

### B.1 A straightforward commission

*Sale price $685,000; the seller's services agreement provides 5.5 percent to the listing firm, which shares
half with the selling firm; the listing broker's own split with the firm is 60/40 in the broker's favour.*

Total to listing firm = 685,000 × 0.055 = **$37,675.**
Shared with selling firm = 37,675 ÷ 2 = **$18,837.50** each.
Listing broker's share = 18,837.50 × 0.60 = **$11,302.50.**

### B.2 Net to seller from a known price

*Sale price $685,000; commission 5.5 percent; excise tax at a combined rate of 1.78 percent given in this
problem; payoff $412,000; other closing costs $3,400.*

Commission = **$37,675.** Excise tax = 685,000 × 0.0178 = **$12,193.**
Net = 685,000 − 37,675 − 12,193 − 412,000 − 3,400 = **$219,732.**

### B.3 The price needed to NET a required sum — the one that catches people

chunks.heading: C. Property tax
chunks.excerpt:
This is **algebra, not arithmetic**, because the commission is a percentage **of the unknown price.**

*A seller must net $250,000 after a 5.5 percent commission and $4,900 of other costs, with no loan payoff and
excise tax ignored for this problem.*

Let **P** be the price. Then **P − 0.055P − 4,900 = 250,000**, so **0.945P = 254,900**, and
**P = 254,900 ÷ 0.945 = $269,735.45.**

**Check it:** 269,735.45 × 0.055 = 14,835.45; 269,735.45 − 14,835.45 − 4,900 = **$250,000.** ✓

**The classic error is to add 5.5 percent to $254,900**, which gives $268,919.50 — short by more than $800.
**Adding a percentage to the net is not the same as taking a percentage from the price.**

---

## C. Property tax

Washington property tax is levied by multiple taxing districts against **assessed value**, and rates are
customarily expressed **per $1,000 of assessed value**.

**Worked example, rate given.** *Assessed value $624,000; the combined levy rate in this problem is
$8.9412 per $1,000.*

Annual tax = (624,000 ÷ 1,000) × 8.9412 = 624 × 8.9412 = **$5,579.31.**

**The national section of a licensing examination may use a MILL RATE instead.** **One mill is one-thousandth
of a dollar — $1 per $1,000 of assessed value.** So a rate of **8.9412 mills** is the same figure as **$8.9412
per $1,000.** A student should be able to work either way and to recognise that they are the same thing said
twice.

**This course states no Washington levy rate, assessment ratio, revaluation cycle, exemption or deferral
programme**, because Washington's property tax statutes were not read for this project. **Assessed value and
the levy rate come from the county assessor.**

---

## D. Real estate excise tax

chunks.heading: E. Prorations
chunks.excerpt:
Washington imposes a **real estate excise tax** on the sale of real property. It appears on every Washington
closing statement, and it is customarily the **seller's** charge unless the agreement provides otherwise.

**RCW 82.45 and every local excise tax ordinance were not read for this project.** **This course states no
state rate, no local rate, no bracket, no threshold and no exemption.** Practice problems supply the combined
rate as a given, and **instructors substitute the current statutory and local rates before delivery.**

**Worked example, rate given.** *Sale price $585,000; combined state and local excise tax rate for this
problem 1.78 percent.* Excise tax = 585,000 × 0.0178 = **$10,413.**

> **Instructor note and submission gate.** Washington's excise tax is **graduated** in structure, which means
> a single flat rate is a **simplification used here for teaching arithmetic only.** Before delivery, replace
> these problems with the current statutory brackets and local additions, and add at least one problem that
> requires the student to apply more than one bracket. **Obtaining RCW 82.45 is a submission gate for this
> module.**

---

## E. Prorations

Items paid in advance or in arrears are divided between the parties as of closing: **property taxes**,
**assessments**, **homeowner association dues**, **rents and deposits** on tenanted property, **interest**,
and **fuel** remaining.

**Two conventions, and every problem must say which it uses:**

- **365-day method** — actual days. Most common in practice.
- **360-day / 30-day-month method** — twelve 30-day months. Common on licensing examinations.

**Two rules that never change:**

chunks.heading: E.1 Worked example — taxes paid in advance, 360-day method
chunks.excerpt:
1. **A proration is always a DOUBLE ENTRY.** Whatever is credited to one party is debited to the other. **A
   prorated item appearing once has been done wrong.**
2. **Whichever party "owns" the day of closing must be stated.** **This course states no Washington rule on
   which party owns it**, because none was found in the statutes and rules read; it is a matter of contract
   and local practice, and **every problem here states it inside the problem.**

### E.1 Worked example — taxes paid in advance, 360-day method

*Annual property tax $5,760, paid in full by the seller for the calendar year. Closing 16 September. The
360-day/30-day method applies and the SELLER owns the day of closing.*

Daily rate = 5,760 ÷ 360 = **$16.00.** Monthly rate = **$480.**
Seller's period = 1 January through 16 September = 8 full months + 16 days = (8 × 480) + (16 × 16) =
3,840 + 256 = **$4,096.**
Buyer's share = 5,760 − 4,096 = **$1,664.**

**The seller prepaid the whole year, so the buyer reimburses the seller for the buyer's portion:**
**credit the seller $1,664 and debit the buyer $1,664.** Double entry. ✓

### E.2 Worked example — rent collected in advance, 365-day method

*A tenant paid $2,450 for September on 1 September. Closing 12 September, 30 days in the month. The SELLER
owns the day of closing.*

Daily rate = 2,450 ÷ 30 = **$81.6667.**
Seller's days = 1 through 12 = **12 days** = **$980.00.**
Buyer's days = 13 through 30 = **18 days** = **$1,470.00.**

**The seller holds money belonging to the buyer's period: debit the seller $1,470 and credit the buyer
$1,470.** Double entry. ✓

chunks.heading: F. The settlement statement
chunks.excerpt:
**Notice the direction reverses between the two examples**, and the reason is the same in both: **follow who
paid and who benefits.** Prepaid by the seller for a period the buyer will own → the buyer reimburses.
Collected by the seller for a period the buyer will own → the seller hands it over.

---

## F. The settlement statement

### F.1 Debits and credits, from first principles

A **debit** is an amount a party **owes**. A **credit** is an amount a party **has coming**.

For the **buyer**: the **purchase price is a debit** — it is what they owe. The **earnest money** and the
**loan amount** are **credits** — money already in or arriving on their behalf.

For the **seller**: the **purchase price is a credit** — it is what they have coming. The **loan payoff**,
the **commission** and the **excise tax** are **debits.**

**Cash to close (buyer) = buyer's total debits − buyer's total credits.**
**Net to seller = seller's total credits − seller's total debits.**

### F.2 Worked example — a complete transaction, all figures given

*Sale price $585,000. Earnest money $10,000 held in escrow. New loan $468,000. Buyer's loan origination and
other lender charges $6,240. Buyer's title, escrow and recording charges $2,180. Seller's commission 5.5
percent. Excise tax at 1.78 percent (seller). Seller's loan payoff $301,500. Seller's escrow and other
charges $1,150. Property tax of $6,000 for the year was paid in full by the seller; closing 1 October;
360-day method; the SELLER owns the day of closing.*

**Tax proration.** Daily = 6,000 ÷ 360 = $16.667; monthly = $500.
Seller's period = 1 January through 1 October = 9 months + 1 day = 4,500 + 16.67 = **$4,516.67.**
Buyer's share = 6,000 − 4,516.67 = **$1,483.33** → **credit seller, debit buyer.**

chunks.heading: F.3 What a broker does with a settlement statement
chunks.excerpt:
**Buyer's side.**
Debits: price 585,000 + lender charges 6,240 + title/escrow/recording 2,180 + tax proration 1,483.33 =
**$594,903.33.**
Credits: earnest money 10,000 + loan 468,000 = **$478,000.**
**Cash to close = 594,903.33 − 478,000 = $116,903.33.**

**Seller's side.**
Credits: price 585,000 + tax proration 1,483.33 = **$586,483.33.**
Debits: commission (585,000 × 0.055) 32,175 + excise tax (585,000 × 0.0178) 10,413 + payoff 301,500 +
other 1,150 = **$345,238.**
**Net to seller = 586,483.33 − 345,238 = $241,245.33.**

**Check the double entry:** the tax proration appears **once on each side** — a credit to the seller and a
debit to the buyer, both $1,483.33. ✓

### F.3 What a broker does with a settlement statement

**Review it.** Confirm the price, the deposit, the commission and the prorations match the agreement.
**Ask about anything that does not.** **Do not opine on the legal effect of an entry**, and **do not tell a
client what the tax consequences of the transaction will be.**

**RCW 18.86.030(1)(e)** — owed to all parties, unwaivable:

> *"To **account in a timely manner for all money and property received from or on behalf of either
> party**."*

**And RCW 18.86.040(1)(c) / 18.86.050(1)(c)** make routing the rest a statutory duty.

---

## G. Taxation of ownership — the boundary, stated plainly

A student will be asked about **the exclusion of gain on a principal residence**, the **deductibility of
interest and property taxes**, **depreciation** on investment property, **exchanges of like-kind property**,
and **capital gains treatment.**

**The Internal Revenue Code and Washington's tax statutes were not read for this project.** **This course
states no figure, holding period, limit, exclusion, rate or eligibility requirement for any of them.**

chunks.heading: Module WA-F-12 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**And the reason is not only that they were not read.** **Tax advice is outside brokerage.** A broker may say
that a transaction has tax consequences and that the client should speak to a tax professional **before**
committing — that is compliance information and it is useful. A broker who says *"you won't owe anything,
you've lived there two years"* has given tax advice on figures they did not verify, in an area where the rules
change.

**RCW 18.86.040(1)(c) and 18.86.050(1)(c) make the referral a duty**, and **RCW 18.86.110** leaves the
practice-of-law boundary exactly where the courts put it.

---

## Module WA-F-12 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module WA-F-01, and **every one of them is a calculation or a settlement
statement placement.** **Every rate, levy, multiplier and convention is supplied inside the item as a
given**, and **no item requires a student to recall a Washington or federal tax rate, bracket, threshold or
exemption.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module WA-F-12

**RCW 18.86** was read on 2026-08-20 and is the source of **§§ 18.86.030(1)(e), 18.86.040(1)(c),
18.86.050(1)(c), 18.86.080(7) and 18.86.110**, transcribed above.

**Not read, and therefore the source of no figure in this build:** **RCW 82.45** and every **local real estate
excise tax ordinance**; **Washington's property tax statutes**, including assessment, levy, revaluation,
exemption and deferral provisions; the **Internal Revenue Code**; and **WAC 308-124** and the remainder of
**RCW 18.85**.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WA-F-12
chunks.excerpt:
**No excise tax rate, bracket or threshold; no levy rate, assessment ratio or exemption; no federal exclusion,
holding period, deduction limit or rate; and no proration convention or settlement-date rule is stated as
Washington law anywhere in this module.** Every figure in every worked example is supplied inside the example,
and **replacing the flat excise tax rate with the current statutory brackets is a submission gate.**

lessons.title: Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-01

chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-01
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-01

## Statutory duties under RCW 18.86 — the duties owed to everyone

**Course:** Real Estate Practices — the second of the two courses **RCW 18.85.101(1)(c)** names.
**Instructional hours:** **5.0** of 30.0 · **Clock hour = 50 minutes**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

> ### The sentence this whole course is built on
>
> **RCW 18.86.110:**
>
> *"**The duties under this chapter are statutory duties and not fiduciary duties. This chapter supersedes
> the fiduciary duties of an agent to a principal under the common law.** The common law continues to apply
> to the parties in all other respects. This chapter does not affect the duties of a broker while engaging
> in the authorized or unauthorized practice of law as determined by the courts of this state. **This
> chapter shall be construed broadly.**"*
>
> **Washington kept the word "agent" and replaced what stands behind it.** A student arriving with a
> national textbook's account of fiduciary duty — loyalty, obedience, disclosure, confidentiality,
> accounting and reasonable care as **common-law fiduciary obligations** — has an account **Washington
> superseded by statute.**
>
> **What remains is the list in RCW 18.86.030, owed to ALL PARTIES, plus the relationship-specific lists in
> .040, .050 and .060 — and nothing else.** Learn the lists.

## Learning objectives

chunks.heading: A. RCW 18.86.030(1) — the seven, transcribed
chunks.excerpt:
1. State the seven duties RCW 18.86.030(1) owes to the principal and to all parties, and that they may not
   be waived.
2. Apply the presentation duty, and explain the "regardless" clause.
3. Apply the disclosure duty together with its proviso.
4. State the three limits in RCW 18.86.030(2) and what they do not excuse.
5. Apply the five-part definition of confidential information.
6. Apply the material fact definition and its negative list.
7. State the consequence of a violation under RCW 18.86.031.

---

## A. RCW 18.86.030(1) — the seven, transcribed

> *"A broker owes the following duties **to their principal and to all parties in a transaction, which may
> not be waived**:*
>
> **(a)** *"To exercise **reasonable skill and care**;*
> **(b)** *"To **deal honestly and in good faith**;*
> **(c)** *"To **present all written offers, written notices and other written communications to and from
> either party in a timely manner, regardless of whether the property is subject to an existing contract for
> sale or the buyer is already a party to an existing contract to purchase**;*
> **(d)** *"To **disclose all existing material facts known by the broker and not apparent or readily
> ascertainable to a party**; **provided that this subsection shall not be construed to imply any duty to
> investigate matters that the broker has not agreed to investigate**;*
> **(e)** *"To **account in a timely manner for all money and property received from or on behalf of either
> party**;*
> **(f)** *"To **provide a pamphlet in the form prescribed by RCW 18.86.120 and obtain an acknowledgment of
> receipt by the party** ...;*
> **(g)** *"To **disclose in writing** before the broker's principal signs an offer, or as soon as reasonably
> practical, but before the parties reach mutual agreement

chunks.heading: A.1 Read the opening words before anything else
chunks.excerpt:
..."*

### A.1 Read the opening words before anything else

**"To their principal AND TO ALL PARTIES in a transaction."** Not to the client. To **everyone** — the buyer
your seller-principal is negotiating against, the unrepresented seller across the table, the tenant your
landlord-principal is screening.

**"Which may not be waived."** No agreement, no signature, no disclosure, no instruction from a principal
removes any of the seven. A broker asked to set one aside has been asked to do something the statute
forecloses, and the answer does not depend on how the request is phrased.

---

## B. Duty (c) — the presentation duty, and the clause that makes Washington different

> *"To present **all written offers, written notices and other written communications to and from either
> party in a timely manner, REGARDLESS OF whether the property is subject to an existing contract for sale
> or the buyer is already a party to an existing contract to purchase**."*

**Four things it reaches:** offers, **notices**, and **other written communications** — and it reaches them
**to and from either party**, in **both directions.**

**"All" means the broker does not filter.** An offer the broker thinks is insulting still goes to the
principal. The principal decides what to do with it; the broker decides nothing.

### B.1 The "regardless" clause

**In many states a listing broker's duty to present offers softens once the property is under contract, or
requires the seller's written waiver to stop.** **Washington states the opposite in the statute itself.**

> ***"regardless of whether the property is subject to an existing contract for sale or the buyer is already
> a party to an existing contract to purchase."***

chunks.heading: B.2 Note what it is expressed in terms of
chunks.excerpt:
**A property already under contract still gets every written offer presented.** A buyer already under
contract on another property still gets every written communication presented. **There is no waiver in the
subsection**, and the whole subsection sits inside a paragraph that says these duties **may not be waived.**

### B.2 Note what it is expressed in terms of

**Written** offers, **written** notices and **other written** communications. The statutory duty is stated in
terms of writings. **The practical lesson is the reverse of a loophole: put it in writing, and then it must
be presented.** A verbal indication of interest carries no statutory presentation duty and, under **RCW
18.86.010(15)**, does not even begin a prospective transaction:

> *"a prospective transaction **does not exist until a written offer has been signed by at least one
> party**."*

---

## C. Duty (d) — disclosure, and its proviso

> *"To **disclose all existing material facts known by the broker and not apparent or readily ascertainable
> to a party**; **provided that this subsection shall not be construed to imply any duty to investigate
> matters that the broker has not agreed to investigate**."*

**Three limits on the duty, and one limit on the limits.**

- **Existing** — not speculative or future.
- **Material facts** — the defined term in Part E.
- **Known by the broker** — actual knowledge.
- **Not apparent or readily ascertainable to a party** — a condition a party can plainly see, or find
  easily, is not the target.

**And the proviso: no duty to investigate what the broker has not agreed to investigate.**

### C.1 The words "has not agreed to" are doing work

chunks.heading: D. The limits — RCW 18.86.030(2)
chunks.excerpt:
The proviso does not say there is never a duty to investigate. It says the subsection does not **imply** one
as to matters the broker **has not agreed to investigate.**

**So a broker who agrees to investigate something has taken it on.** *"I'll check with the county on the
septic capacity"* is an agreement. Having made it, the broker either does it or corrects the record — and
duty (a), reasonable skill and care, now attaches to how it is done.

**Say what you will do, and then do it.** Casual promises create duties in Washington.

---

## D. The limits — RCW 18.86.030(2)

> *"Unless otherwise agreed, a broker **owes no duty to conduct an independent inspection of the property**
> or to **conduct an independent investigation of either party's financial condition**, and owes **no duty to
> independently verify the accuracy or completeness of any statement made by either party or by any source
> reasonably believed by the broker to be reliable**."*

**Three shelters:** no duty to **inspect**, no duty to **investigate finances**, no duty to **verify
statements.**

**And "unless otherwise agreed" opens all three** — the same principle as the (1)(d) proviso. A broker who
agrees to do one of these has agreed to do it.

### D.1 What the shelters do not excuse

**They remove duties to look. They do not remove the duty to disclose what you saw, and they do not license a
statement of your own.**

A broker who walks a crawl space and sees water has not inspected — **they have acquired information**, and
(1)(d) governs.

A broker who repeats the lender's assessment with attribution is reporting. A broker who says *"you're
approved"* has made a representation, and **(1)(b) — deal honestly and in good faith, owed to all parties,
unwaivable — is what it will be measured against.**

chunks.heading: E. Two definitions that decide cases
chunks.excerpt:
**And the verification shelter turns on "reasonably believed ... to be reliable."** It protects reliance on a
source the broker had reason to trust. It does not protect reliance on a statement the broker had reason to
doubt.

---

## E. Two definitions that decide cases

### E.1 Confidential information — RCW 18.86.010(9), a five-part test

> *"information from or concerning a principal that:*
> **(a)** *Was **acquired by the broker during the course of an agency relationship** with the principal;*
> **(b)** *The principal **reasonably expects to be kept confidential**;*
> **(c)** *The principal **has not disclosed or authorized to be disclosed** to third parties;*
> **(d)** ***Would, if disclosed, operate to the detriment of the principal**; and*
> **(e)** *The principal **personally would not be obligated to disclose to the other party**."*

**All five parts. Not any one of them.** Work an example: a seller mentions they are relocating for work in
sixty days.

(a) Acquired during the relationship — **yes**. (b) Reasonably expected confidential — **yes**. (c) Not
disclosed by them — **check; if they said it at the open house, no**. (d) Detrimental if disclosed —
**yes, it signals urgency**. (e) Not something the seller would personally be obliged to disclose — **yes,
a relocation is not a material fact about the property.**

**Five out of five: confidential.**

**Now change one fact.** The seller mentions the roof leaks. Part **(e) fails** — a known material defect
affecting the physical condition is something the seller would be obliged to deal with, and duty (1)(d) makes
the broker's own disclosure obligation independent of the principal's wishes. **It is not confidential
information**, because it never satisfied part (e).

chunks.heading: E.2 Material fact — RCW 18.86.010(11), with its negative list
chunks.excerpt:
**Part (e) is the part students miss, and it is the part that resolves the "my client told me not to tell"
question before it arises.**

### E.2 Material fact — RCW 18.86.010(11), with its negative list

> *"'Material fact' means information that **substantially adversely affects the value of the property or a
> party's ability to perform its obligations** in a real estate transaction, or **operates to materially
> impair or defeat the purpose of the transaction**. **The fact or suspicion that the property, or any
> neighboring property, is or was the site of a murder, suicide or other death, rape or other sex crime,
> assault or other violent crime, robbery or burglary, illegal drug activity, gang-related activity,
> political or religious activity, or other act, occurrence, or use NOT ADVERSELY AFFECTING THE PHYSICAL
> CONDITION OF OR TITLE TO THE PROPERTY is not a material fact.**"*

**Two branches in the affirmative definition**, and either suffices: substantial adverse effect on **value or
a party's ability to perform**, **or** operating to **materially impair or defeat the purpose of the
transaction.**

**And a long negative list, governed by one limiting clause: "not adversely affecting the physical condition
of or title to the property."**

**Apply it.** A former methamphetamine laboratory that **contaminated the structure** affected the **physical
condition** — outside the exclusion, inside the duty. Drug activity that left no physical trace and no title
effect — inside the exclusion.

**The test is not how alarming the event was. It is whether it affected the physical condition or the
title.**

chunks.heading: F. Duties (f) and (g), previewed
chunks.excerpt:
**And the exclusion does not authorise a lie.** Duty (1)(b) is owed to all parties and cannot be waived.
**Not being obliged to volunteer something is not permission to misstate it.** A broker asked directly
answers truthfully or declines to answer — and never invents.

---

## F. Duties (f) and (g), previewed

**(f) — the pamphlet.** *"To **provide a pamphlet in the form prescribed by RCW 18.86.120 and obtain an
acknowledgment of receipt** by the party."* **Module WA-P-02** covers the timing, which differs depending on
whether the party is being served or is unrepresented.

**(g) — the agency disclosure.** In writing, **before the broker's principal signs an offer**, in a **separate
paragraph titled "Agency Disclosure"** — plus **any terms of compensation offered by a party or a firm to a
firm representing another party.** **Module WA-P-02** covers it, and **Module WA-P-04** covers the
compensation half.

---

## G. What a violation is — RCW 18.86.031

> *"**A violation of either RCW 18.86.030 or 18.86.130 is a violation of RCW 18.85.361.**"*

**A breach of these duties is a licence-law violation**, not merely a private wrong. **RCW 18.85.361 was NOT
read for this project**, and **this course states no penalty, sanction or procedure from it.** What a student
must carry is the linkage: **RCW 18.86.030 is enforceable through the licence.**

*(RCW 18.86.130 — the 2026 exclusive-marketing statute — is in Module WA-P-05, and it is the other provision
that carries this consequence.)*

---

## H. The seven, as a working checklist

chunks.heading: Module WA-P-01 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Reasonable skill and care** — be competent at what you do.
2. **Honestly and in good faith** — to everyone, always, unwaivable.
3. **Present everything written, both directions, timely — regardless.**
4. **Disclose known material facts** not apparent or readily ascertainable — **and no duty to investigate what
   you did not agree to investigate.**
5. **Account for every dollar and every item of property.**
6. **Give the pamphlet and get the acknowledgment.**
7. **Disclose your role in writing, under that heading, before your principal signs an offer.**

**None of them is waivable. All of them are owed to everyone in the transaction.**

---

## Module WA-P-01 engagement check

Eleven items — one applied scenario, five engagement items and five remediation items. The **80 percent**
engagement threshold and the **100 percent** applied threshold are **StateCourse standards.** **The 70
percent** that is the director's figure applies to the **comprehensive course examination** WAC
308-124H-820(8) requires, which for this 30-hour course must carry **at least 90 items.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module WA-P-01

Drawn from **RCW 18.86**, read in full on 2026-08-20 from the Washington State Legislature's official site —
specifically **§§ 18.86.010(9), (11) and (15), 18.86.030, 18.86.031, 18.86.040, 18.86.050, 18.86.110 and
18.86.120** — together with **RCW 18.85.101** and **WAC 308-124H-820(8)**.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **RCW 18.85.361**, cited by RCW 18.86.031; the
remainder of **RCW 18.85**, including **RCW 18.85.011**; **WAC 308-124**; and the **full text of the RCW
18.86.120 pamphlet.**

**No penalty, sanction, procedure, fine or licence consequence is stated in this module**, because RCW
18.85.361 was not obtained.

lessons.title: Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-02

chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-02
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-02

## Agency relationships, services agreements and the pamphlet

**Course:** Real Estate Practices · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 30.0 · **Clock hour = 50 minutes**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

> ### A submission gate stated at the top of this module
>
> **RCW 18.86.120 prints the pamphlet in full**, titled **"Real Estate Brokerage in Washington,"** and
> requires it to be *"formatted so it can be easily reviewed by a buyer or seller, **including a legible
> font and font size**."*
>
> **This project read that RCW 18.86.120 prints the pamphlet and read its opening sections. It did NOT
> transcribe the pamphlet in full, and no document in this build reproduces it.** Delivering it **in the form
> prescribed** and **obtaining acknowledgment of receipt** is a **submission gate.**

## Learning objectives

1. State how buyer agency and seller agency arise, and why the two arise differently.
2. State when a firm must enter into a services agreement.
3. Recite the five contents RCW 18.86.020(2)(b) requires in a services agreement.
4. State the one situation in which a services agreement is not required.
5. Apply the pamphlet timing rules — both of them.
6. Apply the agency disclosure requirement, including its heading and its timing.
7. State the seller's agent's and buyer's agent's duties and their two safe harbours.

---

## A. How the relationships arise — RCW 18.86.020(1)

chunks.heading: A.1 The asymmetry, and why it matters
chunks.excerpt:
> *"A broker who performs real estate brokerage services for a buyer **is a buyer's agent unless**:*
> **(a)** *the broker's firm has **appointed the broker to represent the seller** pursuant to a services
> agreement between the firm and the seller, in which case the broker is a **seller's agent**;*
> **(b)** *the firm has appointed the broker to represent the seller **and** has also appointed the broker to
> represent the buyer, in which case the appointed broker is a **limited dual agent**; or*
> **(c)** *the **broker is the seller or one of the sellers**."*

### A.1 The asymmetry, and why it matters

**Buyer agency arises by DEFAULT, from performing services.** A broker who works with a buyer **is** the
buyer's agent unless one of the three exceptions applies. **Nothing needs to be signed for the relationship
to exist.**

**Seller agency requires an APPOINTMENT under a services agreement between the firm and the seller.**

**The practical consequence is one a new broker gets wrong constantly.** A broker showing property to a buyer
who has signed nothing **is already that buyer's agent** and already owes the duties in RCW 18.86.050 —
loyalty, timely disclosure of conflicts, the duty to advise seeking expert advice, and the confidentiality
duty. **The signature documents the relationship; it does not create it.**

**And note (c).** A broker selling their own property is not the buyer's agent by default, because they are on
the other side.

### A.2 The firm is the party — RCW 18.86.020(2)(a)

> *"**A firm must enter into a services agreement with the principal before, or as soon as reasonably
> practical after, its appointed broker commences rendering real estate brokerage services** to, or on behalf
> of, the principal."*

chunks.heading: B. What the services agreement must contain — RCW 18.86.020(2)(b)
chunks.excerpt:
**Read who does what.** The **firm** enters the agreement. The **firm appoints** a broker as agent. The
individual broker is the agent by appointment.

**And the timing has two halves:** *"before, **or as soon as reasonably practical after**"* the broker
**commences rendering services.** Washington does not require the paper first — it requires the paper
promptly, and it makes the relationship exist regardless.

---

## B. What the services agreement must contain — RCW 18.86.020(2)(b)

> *"The services agreement **must include** the following:*
>
> **(i)** *"The **term of the agreement**, and **if the principal is a buyer, a default term of 60 days with
> the option of a longer term**;*
> **(ii)** *"The **broker appointed as an agent** for the principal;*
> **(iii)** *"Whether the agency relationship is **exclusive or nonexclusive**, and **if the principal is a
> buyer, checkbox options for the buyer to select either** an exclusive or nonexclusive relationship;*
> **(iv)** *"Whether the principal **consents to the broker appointed as an agent for the principal to act as
> a limited dual agent**, **which consent must be separately initialed by the principal and include an
> acknowledgment from the principal that a limited dual agent may not advocate terms favorable to one
> principal to the detriment of the other principal** and is further limited as set forth in RCW 18.86.060;
> and*
> **(v)** *"Whether the principal **consents to the firm's designated broker and any managing broker
> responsible for the supervision of the broker** appointed as an agent for the principal **to act as a
> limited dual agent** in a transaction in which different brokers affiliated with the same firm represent
> different parties."*

### B.1 Four features worth stopping on

chunks.heading: B.2 The one exception — RCW 18.86.020(3)
chunks.excerpt:
**(i) — the 60-day buyer default.** A buyer's services agreement has a **default term of 60 days**, with the
option of a longer one. **A buyer is not signed to an indefinite arrangement**, and a broker proposing a
longer term is proposing a departure from the statutory default that the buyer should understand.

**(iii) — checkbox options, for buyers.** The statute prescribes the **mechanism**, not merely the
disclosure: the buyer must be able to **select** exclusive or nonexclusive. A form that pre-selects one has
not complied.

**(iv) — separately initialed, with an acknowledgment.** Limited dual agency consent is not covered by the
signature at the end. It must be **separately initialed**, and it must carry the acknowledgment in the
statute's own terms: **a limited dual agent may not advocate terms favorable to one principal to the
detriment of the other.**

**(v) — a second, different consent.** (iv) is about **your** broker acting as a limited dual agent. **(v) is
about the designated broker and managing broker** becoming limited dual agents when **different brokers in the
same firm** represent the two sides. **Two consents, two situations**, and a broker who explains only the
first has explained half.

### B.2 The one exception — RCW 18.86.020(3)

> *"A services agreement is **not required** when a broker performs real estate brokerage services **as a
> buyer's agent solely for commercial real estate**."*

**Commercial buyer's agency only.** Not commercial seller's agency, not residential anything. And note that
**RCW 18.86.080(8)** supplies the substitute in that case — a written **"Compensation Disclosure."** Module
WA-P-04 covers it.

### B.3 Different relationships in different transactions — RCW 18.86.020(4)

chunks.heading: C. The pamphlet — RCW 18.86.030(1)(f)
chunks.excerpt:
> *"A broker **may work with a party in separate transactions pursuant to different relationships** including,
> but not limited to, **representing a party in one transaction and at the same time not representing that
> party in a different transaction** involving that party, if the broker complies with this chapter in
> establishing the relationships for each transaction."*

**Explicitly permitted, and explicitly conditioned:** each relationship must be established in compliance with
the chapter. This is how a broker lawfully represents a client on their purchase while not representing them
on a concurrent sale — but it requires the paperwork for each, separately.

---

## C. The pamphlet — RCW 18.86.030(1)(f)

> *"To **provide a pamphlet in the form prescribed by RCW 18.86.120 and obtain an acknowledgment of receipt by
> the party**. The pamphlet shall be provided to:*
> **(i)** *"**Any party to whom the broker renders real estate brokerage services as soon as reasonably
> practical but BEFORE the party signs a services agreement**; and*
> **(ii)** *"**Any party NOT REPRESENTED by a broker in a transaction BEFORE the party signs an offer or as
> soon as reasonably practical**."*

### C.1 Two triggers, two different moments

| Who | When |
|---|---|
| **A party you are rendering services to** | As soon as reasonably practical, **but BEFORE they sign a services agreement** |
| **A party NOT represented by any broker** | **Before they sign an offer**, or as soon as reasonably practical |

chunks.heading: C.2 And the acknowledgment is not optional
chunks.excerpt:
**The second is the one brokers forget.** An **unrepresented seller** across the table from your buyer, or an
**unrepresented buyer** making an offer on your listing, **must receive the pamphlet from you** — before they
sign an offer. They are not your principal. The duty is owed anyway, because **RCW 18.86.030(1) runs to all
parties.**

### C.2 And the acknowledgment is not optional

> *"and **obtain an acknowledgment of receipt by the party**."*

**Two acts: provide, and obtain the acknowledgment.** The acknowledgment is what proves the first act
happened, and a broker without one has no record.

**The pamphlet's content is prescribed by RCW 18.86.120 and was not transcribed for this build.** It describes
**licensing and supervision of brokers**, **agency relationships**, **for sellers**, **for buyers**, **for both
as a limited dual agent**, and **the duration of the agency relationship**, among other material. **Delivering
it in the prescribed form is a submission gate.**

---

## D. The agency disclosure — RCW 18.86.030(1)(g)

> *"To **disclose in writing BEFORE the broker's principal signs an offer, or as soon as reasonably practical,
> but BEFORE THE PARTIES REACH MUTUAL AGREEMENT**:*
>
> **(i)** *"Whether the broker **represents the buyer as the buyer's agent, the seller as the seller's agent,
> or both parties as a limited dual agent**. **The disclosure shall be set forth in a separate paragraph
> titled 'Agency Disclosure' in the agreement between the buyer and seller or in a separate writing titled
> 'Agency Disclosure'**; and*
>
> **(ii)** *"**Any terms of compensation offered by a party or a real estate firm to a real estate firm
> representing another party.**"*

### D.1 Four requirements in one subsection

chunks.heading: E. Seller's agent and buyer's agent duties — RCW 18.86.040 and .050
chunks.excerpt:
**In writing.** **Before the principal signs an offer**, or as soon as reasonably practical — with an outer
limit of **before the parties reach mutual agreement.**

**In a separate paragraph titled "Agency Disclosure"** — in the purchase and sale agreement **or** in a
separate writing bearing that title. **The heading is prescribed.** A disclosure buried in a paragraph headed
something else has not complied.

**And (ii) is the part students overlook**: the disclosure carries **any terms of compensation offered by a
party or a firm to a firm representing another party.** That is a compensation disclosure sitting inside the
agency disclosure, and **Module WA-P-04** develops what it means in practice.

---

## E. Seller's agent and buyer's agent duties — RCW 18.86.040 and .050

Each provides that, *"**unless additional duties are agreed to in writing signed by**"* the agent, the duties
are **limited to those in RCW 18.86.030 and** the following, ***"which may not be waived except as expressly
set forth in (e)"***:

chunks.heading: E.1 Five features
chunks.excerpt:
> **(a)** *"To be **loyal** to the [principal] by **taking no action that is adverse or detrimental** to the
> [principal]'s interest in a transaction;*
> **(b)** *"To **timely disclose** to the [principal] **any conflicts of interest**;*
> **(c)** *"To **advise** the [principal] **to seek expert advice on matters relating to the transaction that
> are beyond the agent's expertise**;*
> **(d)** *"To **not disclose any confidential information** from or about the [principal], **except under
> subpoena or court order, EVEN AFTER TERMINATION of the agency relationship**; and*
> **(e)** *"Unless otherwise agreed to in writing **after the agent has complied with RCW 18.86.030(1)(f)**,
> to make a **good faith and continuous effort** to find a buyer for the property / a property for the buyer;
> **except that** the agent is **not obligated to seek additional offers while the property is subject to an
> existing contract for sale** / **additional properties while the buyer is a party to an existing contract to
> purchase**."*

### E.1 Five features

**"Limited to."** The duty list is **closed**. RCW 18.86.110 superseded the common-law fiduciary duties, and
these sections state what replaced them. **Additional duties arise only by a writing signed by the agent.**

**Loyalty is defined negatively** — *"taking no action that is adverse or detrimental."* That is a narrower
formulation than a common-law duty of undivided loyalty, and it is the formulation Washington chose.

**(d) has exactly two exceptions and survives termination.** *"Except under **subpoena or court order**, even
after termination."* A broker who learned a seller's bottom line does not become free to mention it when the
listing expires. **Note how narrow the exceptions are compared with other states' lists.**

chunks.heading: E.2 The two safe harbours — subsection (2) of each
chunks.excerpt:
**(e) is the only waivable one**, and even then only *"in writing **after** the agent has complied with RCW
18.86.030(1)(f)"* — **after the pamphlet has been given and acknowledged.** The statute sequences it: the
party must have the pamphlet before they can waive the effort duty.

**(c) is the routing duty, and it is statutory.** *"To advise ... to seek expert advice on matters ... beyond
the agent's expertise."* Not a courtesy. A duty.

### E.2 The two safe harbours — subsection (2) of each

> *"**(a)** The showing of properties not owned by the seller ... or the listing of competing properties ...
> **does not in and of itself breach the duty of loyalty ... or create a conflict of interest.**"*
> *"**(b)** The **representation of more than one seller by different brokers affiliated with the same firm in
> competing transactions involving the same buyer** does not in and of itself breach the duty of loyalty ...
> or create a conflict of interest."*

**RCW 18.86.050(2)** states the mirror rules for a buyer's agent: showing a property the buyer is interested in
to other buyers, and representing more than one buyer through different brokers in the same firm in competing
transactions involving the same property.

**These exist so that ordinary brokerage is possible.** Without them, every multi-agent firm would be in
permanent conflict.

**But read "in and of itself."** The safe harbour covers the **structural** fact. It does not cover **conduct**
— a broker who actually uses one principal's confidential information to advantage another has done something
the safe harbour never reached.

---

## F. The sequence, in order

chunks.heading: Module WA-P-02 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Give the pamphlet and obtain the acknowledgment** — before a services agreement is signed, and to any
   unrepresented party before they sign an offer. *(1)(f)*
2. **Recognise that buyer agency may already exist** by operation of RCW 18.86.020(1).
3. **Enter the services agreement** — the **firm** with the **principal**, before or as soon as reasonably
   practical after services commence, containing **all five** RCW 18.86.020(2)(b) items, with the dual agency
   consent **separately initialed.**
4. **Disclose the role in writing** in a paragraph titled **"Agency Disclosure,"** before the principal signs
   an offer and before mutual agreement — **including any compensation terms offered to a firm representing
   another party.** *(1)(g)*
5. **Perform the duties** in RCW 18.86.030 to everyone, and in .040 or .050 to the principal.

---

## Module WA-P-02 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module WA-P-01. **No item reproduces or requires any wording from the RCW
18.86.120 pamphlet**, because this project did not transcribe it. Items test **how each relationship arises**,
**the five services agreement contents**, **the 60-day buyer default**, **the separately-initialed consent**,
**both pamphlet triggers**, **the Agency Disclosure heading and timing**, and **the duty lists with their two
safe harbours.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module WA-P-02

Drawn from **RCW 18.86**, read in full on 2026-08-20 — specifically **§§ 18.86.020, 18.86.030(1)(f) and (g),
18.86.040, 18.86.050, 18.86.060, 18.86.080(8) and 18.86.120.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WA-P-02
chunks.excerpt:
**Not obtained, and therefore reproduced NOWHERE in this build:** the **full text of the RCW 18.86.120
pamphlet**; **WAC 308-124**; the remainder of **RCW 18.85**; and any **standard Washington services agreement,
agency disclosure or purchase and sale agreement form.**

**No form provision, pamphlet wording, or agreement clause is stated in this module.** The **60-day buyer
default term**, the **checkbox requirement**, the **separately-initialed consent**, the **"Agency Disclosure"
heading**, both **pamphlet timing rules** and the **subpoena-or-court-order confidentiality exception** are all
**transcribed from RCW 18.86.**

chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-03
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-03

## Limited dual agency, duration, imputed knowledge and vicarious liability

**Course:** Real Estate Practices · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 30.0 · **Clock hour = 50 minutes**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

## Learning objectives

1. State the entry condition for limited dual agency and where the consent must appear.
2. State the limited dual agent's duties, and identify what is absent from the list.
3. Apply RCW 18.86.060(5) — what happens when two brokers in one firm represent the two sides.
4. State the four ways an agency relationship ends and the two duties that survive.
5. Apply RCW 18.86.100 — Washington's reversal of imputed knowledge.
6. Apply RCW 18.86.090 — when a principal is liable for an agent's act.

---

## A. Limited dual agency — RCW 18.86.060

### A.1 The entry condition

> **(1)** *"A broker may act as a limited dual agent **only with the written consent of both parties to the
> transaction, SET FORTH IN THE SERVICES AGREEMENT**."*

**Two requirements, and the second is specific.** Written consent from **both** parties, and it must be **set
forth in the services agreement** — not in a separate form produced at the last moment.

**And Module WA-P-02 supplied the mechanics.** **RCW 18.86.020(2)(b)(iv)** requires that consent to be
**separately initialed by the principal** and to include **an acknowledgment** in the statute's own words:

> *"**a limited dual agent may not advocate terms favorable to one principal to the detriment of the other
> principal**."*

**The principal must acknowledge, in writing they separately initial, what they are giving up.**

chunks.heading: A.2 The duties — and the one that is missing
chunks.excerpt:
### A.2 The duties — and the one that is missing

> **(2)** *Unless additional duties are agreed to in writing signed by the limited dual agent, the duties are
> limited to those in RCW 18.86.030 and the following, **which may not be waived except as expressly set forth
> in (e) and (f)**:*
>
> **(a)** *"To take **no action that is adverse or detrimental to EITHER party's interest** in a transaction;*
> **(b)** *"To **timely disclose to BOTH parties any conflicts of interest**;*
> **(c)** *"To **advise BOTH parties to seek expert advice** on matters relating to the transaction that are
> beyond the limited dual agent's expertise;*
> **(d)** *"To **not disclose any confidential information from or about EITHER party, except under subpoena
> or court order, even after termination** of the agency relationship;*
> **(e)** and **(f)** *the good faith and continuous effort duties, **for both sides**, each subject to the
> same existing-contract exception.*

**Compare with RCW 18.86.040(1)(a) and 18.86.050(1)(a).**

| | Seller's agent | Buyer's agent | **Limited dual agent** |
|---|---|---|---|
| First duty | *"To be **loyal** to the seller by taking no action adverse or detrimental..."* | *"To be **loyal** to the buyer by taking no action adverse or detrimental..."* | *"To take **no action that is adverse or detrimental to either party's interest**"* |

**The word "loyal" does not appear in RCW 18.86.060.** In its place stands the neutrality obligation alone.

**That substitution is the entire concept, and it is why the statute makes the principal acknowledge it.** A
limited dual agent **cannot advocate for one side against the other**, so the statute does not ask for a
loyalty it could not deliver. What it asks for is **neutrality that runs both ways.**

chunks.heading: A.3 The safe harbours — subsections (3) and (4)
chunks.excerpt:
**Note also (d).** The confidentiality duty now runs to **either party**, with the same two exceptions —
**subpoena or court order** — and it **survives termination.** A limited dual agent holds two sets of
confidences and may use neither.

### A.3 The safe harbours — subsections (3) and (4)

Showing properties not owned by the seller, listing competing properties, showing the buyer's property of
interest to other buyers, and **presenting additional offers while the property is subject to a transaction**
do **not in and of themselves** constitute action adverse or detrimental. Nor does **representation of more
than one seller, or more than one buyer, by different brokers licensed to the same firm** in competing
transactions.

**"In and of itself" is the operative phrase, as it was in Module WA-P-02.** The structural fact is
protected; **conduct is not.**

---

## B. RCW 18.86.060(5) — the provision that catches every firm

> *"In a transaction in which **different brokers affiliated with the same firm represent different parties**,
> the firm's **designated broker, and any managing broker responsible for the supervision of both brokers, IS
> A LIMITED DUAL AGENT**. In such case, **each appointed broker shall SOLELY REPRESENT the party with whom the
> appointed broker has an agency relationship**."*

### B.1 What it actually does

**Two brokers in the same firm, one on each side. The statute then assigns three positions at once:**

- **The listing broker** — solely represents the seller.
- **The selling broker** — solely represents the buyer.
- **The designated broker, and any managing broker supervising both** — **limited dual agents**, by operation
  of the statute.

chunks.heading: B.2 And "solely represent" is a real instruction
chunks.excerpt:
**Nobody chose that last position; the statute assigns it.** And it is why **RCW 18.86.020(2)(b)(v)** requires
a **second, separate consent** in the services agreement: consent to the **designated broker and managing
broker** acting as limited dual agents in exactly this situation.

**A broker who obtains the (iv) consent and not the (v) consent has obtained consent to the wrong thing** for
an in-house transaction.

### B.2 And "solely represent" is a real instruction

Each appointed broker **solely represents** their own party. The in-house transaction does **not** convert the
two brokers into dual agents. **The dual agency sits above them, at the supervisory level**, and the two
brokers keep their own loyalty obligations under RCW 18.86.040 and .050.

**The practical burden this creates is on the supervisor.** A designated broker who is a limited dual agent
must supervise both sides while **taking no action adverse or detrimental to either.** Discussing one side's
position with the other broker is exactly what that forbids.

---

## C. Duration — RCW 18.86.070

> **(1)** *"The agency relationships established pursuant to this chapter **continue until the earliest of the
> following**:*
> **(a)** *"**Completion of performance** by the broker;*
> **(b)** *"**Expiration of the term** agreed upon by the parties;*
> **(c)** *"**Termination of the relationship by mutual agreement** of the parties; or*
> **(d)** *"**Termination of the relationship by notice from either party to the other**. **However, such a
> termination does not otherwise affect the contractual rights of either party.**"*

### C.1 (d) and its qualifier

**Either party may end the relationship by notice.** The relationship is not a cage.

chunks.heading: C.2 What survives — RCW 18.86.070(2)
chunks.excerpt:
**But: *"such a termination does not otherwise affect the contractual rights of either party."*** Ending the
**agency relationship** does not end the **contract**. A seller who gives notice terminating the relationship
may still owe compensation under the services agreement's own terms — and that is a **contract** question, not
an agency question.

**The distinction between the POWER to terminate and the RIGHT to terminate without consequence is the
distinction that provision draws.**

### C.2 What survives — RCW 18.86.070(2)

> *"Except as otherwise agreed to in writing, a broker **owes no further duty after termination** of the agency
> relationship, **other than the duty**:*
> **(a)** *"To **account for all moneys and property received during the relationship**; and*
> **(b)** *"To **not disclose confidential information**."*

**Exactly two duties survive.** Everything else in RCW 18.86.030, .040, .050 and .060 stops.

**And (b) is consistent with the confidentiality duty's own words** — RCW 18.86.040(1)(d), .050(1)(d) and
.060(2)(d) each say *"**even after termination of the agency relationship**."* The statute says it twice
because it matters: **a former client's confidences are still confidences.**

---

## D. Imputed knowledge — RCW 18.86.100

> *"Unless otherwise agreed to in writing, **a principal does not have knowledge or notice of any facts known
> by an agent of the principal that are not actually known by the principal**."*

### D.1 Washington reversed the common-law rule

**Under the general common law of agency, an agent's knowledge acquired within the scope of the agency is
imputed to the principal.** Washington provides the **opposite** by statute.

chunks.heading: E. Vicarious liability — RCW 18.86.090
chunks.excerpt:
**Work the consequence.** A listing broker learns something material about the property and does not tell the
seller. Later a buyer alleges the seller concealed it.

- **Under the common law**, the seller could be charged with the broker's knowledge.
- **Under RCW 18.86.100**, the seller **does not** have knowledge or notice of a fact the broker knew and the
  seller did not **actually** know.

**The seller is not charged with what their broker knew and did not tell them.**

**This does not help the broker.** **RCW 18.86.030(1)(d)** obliges the **broker** to disclose known material
facts to **all parties**, and **RCW 18.86.031** makes a violation of RCW 18.86.030 a violation of the licence
law. **The statute protects the principal from the broker's silence; it does not protect the broker.**

**And note "unless otherwise agreed to in writing."** The parties can contract into imputation. Almost nobody
does, but the door is open.

---

## E. Vicarious liability — RCW 18.86.090

> *"A principal is **not liable** for an act, error, or omission by an agent of the principal arising out of an
> agency relationship:*
> **(1)** *"**Unless the principal participated in or authorized** the act, error, or omission; or*
> **(2)** *"**Except to the extent that**: **(a)** the principal **benefited** from the act, error, or
> omission; **and (b)** the court determines that it is **highly probable that the claimant would be unable to
> enforce a judgment against the agent**."*

### E.1 The default and its two exits

**The default is no liability.** A principal is **not** answerable for their agent's acts, errors or omissions.

chunks.heading: E.2 Why a broker should understand a rule about the principal's liability
chunks.excerpt:
**Exit one — participation or authorisation.** If the principal **participated in or authorized** it, the
protection is gone. A seller who instructed the broker to conceal a defect participated.

**Exit two has TWO cumulative conditions, and both must be met:**

**(a)** the principal **benefited** from the act, **AND**
**(b)** a court determines it is **highly probable that the claimant would be unable to enforce a judgment
against the agent.**

**"Highly probable" is a demanding standard**, and it makes exit two a genuine last resort — available where
the agent is judgment-proof and the principal kept the benefit. **Benefit alone is not enough.** **Inability
to collect alone is not enough.**

### E.2 Why a broker should understand a rule about the principal's liability

Three reasons.

**It explains the structure of Washington brokerage.** RCW 18.86 makes the **broker** answerable for the
broker's conduct — through RCW 18.86.031 and the licence law — rather than routing liability to the client.

**It is the counterpart to RCW 18.86.100.** Together they say: **the principal is not charged with the
broker's knowledge, and is generally not liable for the broker's acts.** Washington places both the knowledge
and the responsibility where the conduct was.

**It answers a client's question.** A seller who asks *"am I on the hook for what you do?"* is asking about
RCW 18.86.090, and the honest answer is: **generally not, with two narrow exceptions — and you should ask your
attorney about your own situation**, which **RCW 18.86.040(1)(c)** makes a duty.

---

## F. The four provisions, as one picture

chunks.heading: Module WA-P-03 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
| Provision | What it settles |
|---|---|
| **RCW 18.86.060** | A limited dual agent owes **neutrality, not loyalty** — with both parties' **written consent in the services agreement, separately initialed.** |
| **RCW 18.86.060(5)** | Two brokers, one firm, two sides → each **solely represents** their party; the **designated and managing brokers are limited dual agents** by operation of statute. |
| **RCW 18.86.070** | The relationship ends four ways; **termination does not affect contractual rights**; **two duties survive** — accounting and confidentiality. |
| **RCW 18.86.100** | The principal **is not charged with the broker's knowledge.** |
| **RCW 18.86.090** | The principal is **generally not liable** for the broker's acts — unless they participated or authorised, or benefited **and** the agent is effectively judgment-proof. |

---

## Module WA-P-03 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module WA-P-01. Items test the **entry condition and its separately-initialed
acknowledgment**, **what is absent from the limited dual agent's duty list**, **the three positions RCW
18.86.060(5) assigns**, **the four ways a relationship ends and the two duties that survive**, **the reversal
of imputed knowledge**, and **the two cumulative conditions in RCW 18.86.090(2).**

---

## Instructor source note for Module WA-P-03

Drawn from **RCW 18.86**, read in full on 2026-08-20 — specifically **§§ 18.86.020(2)(b)(iv) and (v),
18.86.030(1)(d), 18.86.031, 18.86.040(1), 18.86.050(1), 18.86.060, 18.86.070, 18.86.090 and 18.86.100.**

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **RCW 18.85.361**; the remainder of **RCW 18.85**;
**WAC 308-124**; Washington agency and liability **case law**; and any **standard services agreement form.**
