chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-04
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-04

## Compensation — RCW 18.86.080

**Course:** Real Estate Practices · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 30.0 · **Clock hour = 50 minutes**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

> **No commission rate, split, minimum or customary figure appears anywhere in this course.** Compensation is
> negotiated between a firm and its principal, and **RCW 18.86.080(7)(a)(i)** requires the services agreement
> to state **the amount the principal agrees to compensate the firm.** Every worked figure in this module is
> supplied inside its problem.

## Learning objectives

1. State who may pay a firm's compensation.
2. State the rule that compensation does not create agency, and apply it.
3. Recite what RCW 18.86.080(7) requires in a services agreement before a firm may be compensated.
4. Explain the significance of RCW 18.86.080(7)(b).
5. State the commercial real estate alternative and its heading.
6. State the two things a firm may be compensated for without a services agreement.
7. Compute compensation, splits and net figures from given rates.

---

## A. Who may pay — RCW 18.86.080(1), (3), (4), (5), (6)

chunks.heading: A.1 Four permissions worth naming
chunks.excerpt:
> **(1)** *"In any real estate transaction, a firm's compensation **may be paid by the seller, the buyer, a
> third party, or by sharing the compensation between firms**."*
> **(3)** *"A **seller may agree** that a seller's agent's firm **may share with another firm** the compensation
> paid by the seller."*
> **(4)** *"A **buyer may agree** that a buyer's agent's firm **may share with another firm** the compensation
> paid by the buyer."*
> **(5)** *"A firm **may be compensated by more than one party** for real estate brokerage services in a real
> estate transaction."*
> **(6)** *"A firm **may receive compensation based on the purchase price without breaching any duty** to the
> buyer or seller."*

### A.1 Four permissions worth naming

**Anyone may pay.** Seller, buyer, a third party, or firms sharing. Washington does not prescribe a source.

**Sharing requires the paying principal's agreement** — (3) and (4) both say *"may agree."* And (7)(a)(ii)
below makes that agreement a required **term of the services agreement**, not an informal understanding.

**More than one party may compensate the same firm** — (5). That is permitted, and (7)(a)(iii) requires the
principal's consent to it as a stated term.

**Percentage compensation does not breach a duty** — (6). A buyer's agent paid on a percentage of the purchase
price is paid more when the buyer pays more, and Washington states expressly that this alone is not a breach.
**It is still, however, a fact the buyer is entitled to have in the agreement**, because (7)(a)(i) requires
**the amount.**

---

## B. The rule everyone misremembers — RCW 18.86.080(2)

> *"**An agreement to pay or payment of compensation does not establish an agency relationship between the
> party who paid the compensation and the broker.**"*

chunks.heading: C. The requirement that governs practice — RCW 18.86.080(7)
chunks.excerpt:
**Money moves one way; representation is decided another way.**

**Work the case that arises constantly.** A seller's firm offers to share compensation with the buyer's firm,
and the buyer's firm accepts. Who does the buyer's broker represent?

**The buyer** — under **RCW 18.86.020(1)**, a broker performing services for a buyer **is** the buyer's agent
unless one of three exceptions applies, and "being paid by the seller's firm" is not one of them.
**RCW 18.86.080(2)** says the payment does not change it.

**And this is not merely a technical point.** A buyer who hears "the seller pays my commission" may conclude
their broker works for the seller. **Correct it**, and correct it in the direction the statute states: *"I
represent you. Where my firm's compensation comes from is set out in our services agreement, and it does not
change who I work for."*

*(RESPA's referral fee prohibition is a **different** question, addressed in outline in Module WA-F-07. **RCW
18.86.080(2) is about AGENCY**, not about the lawfulness of a payment.)*

---

## C. The requirement that governs practice — RCW 18.86.080(7)

chunks.heading: C.1 "Must have" is the operative phrase
chunks.excerpt:
> *"**To receive compensation for rendering real estate brokerage services from any party or firm, a real
> estate firm MUST HAVE A SERVICES AGREEMENT** containing the following:*
>
> **(a)** *"The **terms of compensation**, including:*
> **(i)** *"**The amount the principal agrees to compensate the firm**;*
> **(ii)** *"The **principal's consent, if any, and any terms of such consent, to compensation sharing between
> firms and parties**; and*
> **(iii)** *"The **principal's consent, if any, and any terms of such consent, to compensation of the firm by
> more than one party**;*
>
> **(b)** *"**In a services agreement with a buyer, whether the appointed broker agrees to show the buyer
> properties if there is no agreement or offer by any party or firm to pay compensation to the firm**; and*
>
> **(c)** *"**Any other agreements between the parties.**"*

### C.1 "Must have" is the operative phrase

**No services agreement, no compensation.** Not "should have," not "ordinarily has." **A firm that renders
brokerage services without a services agreement containing these terms has no statutory basis to be paid for
them.**

**And it reaches compensation "from ANY PARTY OR FIRM"** — including a share offered by the other side's firm.
A buyer's firm cannot rely on a listing firm's offer of compensation in place of its own services agreement
with the buyer.

### C.2 Subsection (7)(b) — the newest and most practical line in the section

> *"In a services agreement with a buyer, **whether the appointed broker agrees to show the buyer properties if
> there is no agreement or offer by any party or firm to pay compensation to the firm**."*

**Washington requires the buyer's services agreement to answer this question in advance, in writing.**

chunks.heading: C.3 (a)(ii) and (a)(iii) — "if any" is not "optional"
chunks.excerpt:
**Why it exists.** A buyer may want to see a property whose seller is not offering to compensate the buyer's
firm. **Whether the broker will show it, and on what basis, is settled at the front of the relationship rather
than in the middle of a house hunt.**

**What it means for a conversation with a buyer.** The broker explains **before** anything is signed: *"If a
seller isn't offering to pay my firm, here is what happens — either you compensate my firm under our agreement,
or we agree now that I won't show those properties. The agreement has to say which."*

**A broker who leaves that blank has left blank a term the statute requires**, and has also set up the
transaction's most predictable argument.

### C.3 (a)(ii) and (a)(iii) — "if any" is not "optional"

Both subsections read *"the principal's consent, **if any**, and any terms of such consent."*

**The consent is optional; addressing it is not.** If the principal consents to sharing, the agreement states
the consent and its terms. If the principal does **not** consent, **the firm may not share.** Either way the
question is answered in the document.

---

## D. The commercial exception — RCW 18.86.080(8)

> *"**In lieu of obtaining a services agreement**, a broker rendering real estate brokerage services to a buyer
> **solely for commercial real estate** may **disclose in writing to the buyer, before the buyer signs an offer**
> with regard to such commercial real estate, **the sources and amounts of any compensation the broker has or
> expects to receive from any party** in conjunction with such transaction. **The disclosure shall be set forth
> in a separate paragraph titled 'Compensation Disclosure' in the agreement between the buyer and seller or in a
> separate writing titled 'Compensation Disclosure.'**"*

chunks.heading: D.1 Four conditions, all required
chunks.excerpt:
### D.1 Four conditions, all required

1. **A buyer**, not a seller.
2. **Solely for commercial real estate.**
3. **In writing, before the buyer signs an offer.**
4. **Sources AND amounts** of any compensation from any party.
5. **In a separate paragraph titled "Compensation Disclosure,"** or a separate writing so titled.

**The heading is prescribed**, exactly as **RCW 18.86.030(1)(g)** prescribes **"Agency Disclosure."**
Washington names its headings, and a disclosure under a different heading has not complied.

**And note the pairing with RCW 18.86.020(3)**, from Module WA-P-02: a services agreement is **not required**
for a buyer's agent **solely for commercial real estate**. **Subsection (8) is what fills the gap** — the
compensation disclosure replaces the compensation terms the services agreement would have carried.

---

## E. The two things that need no services agreement — RCW 18.86.080(9)

> *"A firm may receive compensation **without a services agreement** for:*
> - *the provision of a **broker's price opinion**, as defined in RCW 18.85.011, **or***
> - *a **referral by one firm to another firm IF the referring firm provided no real estate brokerage services
>   in the transaction**."*

**Two exceptions, and the second has a condition attached.** A referral fee is outside the services agreement
requirement **only if the referring firm did no brokerage services.** A firm that showed property, advised, or
negotiated and then "referred" has rendered services, and (7) applies.

**RCW 18.85.011's definition of a broker's price opinion was NOT read for this project.** **This course states
no requirement about what a BPO must contain, who may prepare one, or what it may be used for.** Those are
questions for RCW 18.85 and WAC 308-124 in their own text.

---

chunks.heading: F. The disclosure that sits inside the agency disclosure
chunks.excerpt:
## F. The disclosure that sits inside the agency disclosure

**RCW 18.86.030(1)(g)(ii)** — owed to **all parties**, **unwaivable**:

> *"To **disclose in writing** before the broker's principal signs an offer ... **any terms of compensation
> offered by a party or a real estate firm to a real estate firm representing another party**."*

**Read it carefully, because it is easy to invert.** The broker discloses, **to their own principal**, the
**compensation terms offered to the OTHER side's firm.**

**Why it matters.** A seller is entitled to know what is being offered to the buyer's firm, because the seller
is usually funding it. A buyer is entitled to know what a listing firm is offering their firm, because it bears
on their own compensation obligation under (7)(b).

**It goes in the "Agency Disclosure" paragraph**, before the principal signs an offer.

---

## G. Working the numbers, every rate given

### G.1 A share between firms

*Sale price $742,000; the seller's services agreement provides 5 percent to the listing firm; the seller has
consented in the agreement to sharing, on terms of 2.25 percent of the price to the buyer's firm.*

Total from seller = 742,000 × 0.05 = **$37,100.**
To the buyer's firm = 742,000 × 0.0225 = **$16,695.**
Retained by the listing firm = 37,100 − 16,695 = **$20,405.**

*(Note the structure: the consent and its terms are in the services agreement, as RCW 18.86.080(7)(a)(ii)
requires.)*

### G.2 Where the seller offers nothing to the buyer's firm

*The same buyer's services agreement provides that the buyer compensates the buyer's firm 2.5 percent of the
purchase price, less any amount received from any other party. The seller offers nothing. The purchase price
is $610,000.*

chunks.heading: G.3 Net to seller
chunks.excerpt:
Owed to the buyer's firm = 610,000 × 0.025 = **$15,250.**
Received from other parties = **$0.**
**Payable by the buyer = $15,250.**

**Now the same agreement with a seller offering 2 percent:**
Received from the seller's firm = 610,000 × 0.02 = **$12,200.**
**Payable by the buyer = 15,250 − 12,200 = $3,050.**

**This is exactly the situation RCW 18.86.080(7)(b) requires the agreement to have addressed in advance** —
and it is why the buyer must understand their own obligation before they start looking, not after they find a
house.

### G.3 Net to seller

*Price $742,000; compensation as in G.1 ($37,100 total); excise tax at a combined 1.78 percent given in this
problem; payoff $388,400; other seller charges $2,650.*

Excise tax = 742,000 × 0.0178 = **$13,207.60.**
Net = 742,000 − 37,100 − 13,207.60 − 388,400 − 2,650 = **$300,642.40.**

---

## H. The section as a checklist

1. **Anyone may pay** — seller, buyer, third party, or shared. *(1)*
2. **Payment never creates agency.** *(2)*
3. **No services agreement, no compensation** — and it must contain **the amount**, **consent to sharing**,
   **consent to compensation by more than one party**, **the buyer's show-without-compensation term**, and
   **any other agreements.** *(7)*
4. **Commercial buyer's agency** may substitute a **"Compensation Disclosure"** before the buyer signs an
   offer. *(8)*
5. **A BPO and a pure referral** need no services agreement. *(9)*
6. **Disclose to your principal what the other side's firm is being offered**, in the **"Agency Disclosure"**
   paragraph, before they sign an offer. *(RCW 18.86.030(1)(g)(ii))*

---

## Module WA-P-04 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WA-P-04
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items, delivered as in Module WA-P-01. **Every rate in every item is supplied inside the item**, and
**no item states a commission rate, split or minimum** as anything other than a given. Items test **who may
pay**, **the compensation-does-not-create-agency rule**, **the five (7) contents**, **the meaning of (7)(b)**,
**the commercial exception and its heading**, **the two (9) exceptions and the referral condition**, and the
**(1)(g)(ii) disclosure's direction.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module WA-P-04

Drawn from **RCW 18.86**, read in full on 2026-08-20 — specifically **§§ 18.86.020(1) and (3), 18.86.030(1)(g),
and 18.86.080** in its entirety.

**Not read, and therefore the source of nothing here:** **RCW 18.85.011**, including its definition of a
**broker's price opinion**; the remainder of **RCW 18.85**; **WAC 308-124**; **RESPA and Regulation X**; **RCW
82.45** and every local **excise tax** ordinance; and any **standard Washington services agreement form.**

**No commission rate, split, minimum, referral fee limit, excise tax rate or BPO requirement is stated in this
module.** Every figure in every worked example is supplied inside the example.

lessons.title: Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-05

chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-05
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-05

## Listing, marketing and advertising — including RCW 18.86.130

**Course:** Real Estate Practices · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 30.0 · **Clock hour = 50 minutes**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

> ### A submission gate stated at the top of this module
>
> **Washington's licensee advertising rules are in WAC 308-124 and the remainder of RCW 18.85, neither of
> which was obtained by this project.** **Accordingly this module states NO advertising rule from them — no
> firm-name requirement, no disclosure format, no sign rule, no internet or social media rule and no
> penalty.**
>
> What it teaches is **RCW 18.86.130**, which was read in full; the **RCW 18.86.030 duties** as they apply to
> marketing; and the **fair housing advertising discipline** from Module WA-F-09. **Obtaining WAC 308-124 and
> completing this module from its own text is a submission gate.**

## Learning objectives

1. State RCW 18.86.130's prohibition, its condition and its exception.
2. State the consequence of violating it under RCW 18.86.031.
3. Apply the good faith and continuous effort duty and its existing-contract exception.
4. Apply the RCW 18.86.030 duties to marketing conduct.
5. Apply the fair housing advertising discipline.
6. Identify what a broker must route rather than assert in marketing.

---

## A. RCW 18.86.130 — Exclusive real estate property marketing

**Enacted in 2026 and current Washington law**, transcribed in full:

chunks.heading: A.1 Take it apart
chunks.excerpt:
> *"**A broker may not market the sale or lease of residential real estate to a limited or exclusive group of
> prospective buyers or brokers, or any combination thereof, unless the real estate is concurrently marketed
> to the general public and all other brokers**, except as reasonably necessary to protect the health or
> safety of the owner or occupant. **Marketing to the general public does not require an owner to allow
> access onto the residential real estate or into the residence.**"*

### A.1 Take it apart

**What is prohibited:** marketing **the sale or lease** of **residential** real estate **to a limited or
exclusive group** of prospective buyers **or brokers, or any combination.**

**The condition that makes it lawful:** the property is **concurrently marketed to the general public AND all
other brokers.** Both. Not one or the other, and **concurrently** — not afterwards.

**The exception:** *"except as **reasonably necessary to protect the health or safety of the owner or
occupant**."* **Health or safety.** Not convenience, not privacy in the ordinary sense, not the seller's
preference for a quiet sale.

**And the final sentence forecloses the obvious objection:** *"**Marketing to the general public does not
require an owner to allow access** onto the residential real estate or into the residence."*

**So an owner who does not want strangers walking through their home can still comply.** Marketing publicly
and controlling access are different things, and the statute says so expressly. A broker who tells a seller
"we can't market it publicly because you don't want showings" has misstated the statute.

### A.2 Scope

**Residential** real estate. The section does not reach commercial marketing.

**Sale OR lease.** It reaches rentals as well as sales.

chunks.heading: A.3 The consequence
chunks.excerpt:
**A limited or exclusive group of prospective buyers OR BROKERS.** Marketing exclusively within a brokerage,
a network, a private group or an invitation-only channel is within the prohibition unless the concurrent
public marketing condition is met.

### A.3 The consequence

**RCW 18.86.031:** *"A violation of either **RCW 18.86.030 or 18.86.130** is a violation of RCW 18.85.361."*

**RCW 18.86.130 is one of only two provisions carrying that consequence** — the other being the core duties in
RCW 18.86.030. **A violation is a licence-law violation.**

**RCW 18.85.361 was not read for this project**, and **no penalty, sanction or procedure is stated in this
build.**

### A.4 What a broker actually does with it

**Have the conversation before the listing, not after.** A seller who wants a "quiet" or "pocket" listing is
asking for something RCW 18.86.130 constrains, and the time to explain that is at the listing appointment.

**Separate the two things the seller usually wants.** They almost always want **controlled access**, not
**concealed marketing** — and the statute's last sentence gives them the first without the second.

**Document the health or safety exception if it applies**, and treat it as narrow. It is written to protect
people, not transactions.

---

## B. Marketing and the duty to make an effort

**RCW 18.86.040(1)(e)** — the seller's agent's duty:

> *"Unless otherwise agreed to in writing **after the seller's agent has complied with RCW 18.86.030(1)(f)**,
> to make a **good faith and continuous effort to find a buyer for the property**; **except that a seller's
> agent is not obligated to seek additional offers to purchase the property while the property is subject to
> an existing contract for sale**."*

### B.1 Three features

chunks.heading: C. The RCW 18.86.030 duties, applied to marketing
chunks.excerpt:
**"Good faith and continuous effort."** Not best efforts, not a specified activity level — but **continuous**,
which means marketing that stops is a problem.

**It is the ONE duty in RCW 18.86.040(1) that may be waived** — and only *"in writing **after** the agent has
complied with RCW 18.86.030(1)(f)."* **After the pamphlet has been provided and acknowledged.** The statute
sequences it deliberately: the seller must have the pamphlet in hand before they can agree to relieve the
broker of the effort duty.

**The existing-contract exception is narrow.** A broker is **not obligated to seek additional offers** while
the property is under contract. **That is a relief from an obligation to SEEK — it is not permission to stop
presenting.** **RCW 18.86.030(1)(c)** requires presentation of all written offers **"regardless of whether the
property is subject to an existing contract for sale."**

**Read the two together and the line is exact: you need not go looking, and you must still present whatever
arrives.**

**RCW 18.86.050(1)(e)** states the mirror rule for a buyer's agent — a continuous effort to find a property,
and no obligation to seek additional properties while the buyer is under contract.

---

## C. The RCW 18.86.030 duties, applied to marketing

Marketing is where several of the seven bite hardest.

**(a) Reasonable skill and care.** Square footage, lot size, bedroom count, year built, school district and
zoning are all **assertions**, and a broker who publishes one carelessly has published a misstatement.
**Verify from a source, or attribute it, or leave it out.**

**(b) Deal honestly and in good faith** — owed to **all parties**, unwaivable. **This reaches every person who
reads the advertisement**, not merely the parties to a transaction.

chunks.heading: D. Fair housing in marketing
chunks.excerpt:
**(d) Disclose known material facts** not apparent or readily ascertainable. **A listing that omits a known
material fact is a communication, and the duty does not switch off because the medium is marketing.** The
proviso still applies: no duty to investigate what the broker did not agree to investigate.

**And the material fact negative list from RCW 18.86.010(11) applies here too.** Deaths, crimes, drug activity
and **political or religious activity** *"not adversely affecting the physical condition of or title to the
property"* are **not material facts.** A broker neither volunteers them **nor lies about them** — duty (b)
being unwaivable.

---

## D. Fair housing in marketing

Module WA-F-09 delivered the substance in the statutory three-hour block. **This is the practice application,
and it is a discipline rather than a rule list.**

### D.1 Describe the property, not the people

| Property | People |
|---|---|
| *"Three bedrooms, level lot, quiet street"* | *"Perfect for a young family"* |
| *"Ground-floor unit, no steps"* | *"Great for seniors"* |
| *"Walking distance to the light rail"* | *"Ideal for professionals"* |
| *"Zoned for the district's published school assignments"* | *"Good schools"* |

**The right column names or implies a characteristic.** Some of the phrases are apparently benign, and that is
precisely why the discipline is a habit rather than a checklist: **describe what is there, not who should
want it.**

### D.2 The advertisement is more than the words

**Photographs. Captions. Hashtags. The audience an advertisement is targeted to. The account it is posted
from. The group it is shared in.** All of it is the advertisement.

chunks.heading: D.3 Route the objective questions
chunks.excerpt:
**Targeting is the modern form of the oldest problem.** An advertisement shown to some people and not others,
on characteristics or on proxies for them, is a distribution decision — and distribution decisions are exactly
what fair housing law has always reached.

### D.3 Route the objective questions

**School performance, crime statistics, demographics, commute times, flood history and walkability are all
published.** **Send the consumer to the source.** A broker who summarises them has (a) risked steering and (b)
made an assertion under duty (a) and duty (b).

*(No protected class list, exemption or advertising rule is stated in this module. RCW 49.60, the federal Fair
Housing Act and WAC 308-124 were not read for this project — Module WA-F-09 records the same gap.)*

---

## E. What a broker routes rather than asserts in marketing

- **Square footage and lot dimensions** → the county assessor's record with attribution, a survey, or an
  appraisal. **Never your own estimate published as fact.**
- **Bedroom count where the septic permit governs it** → the county health department.
- **Zoning and permitted uses** → the jurisdiction.
- **Whether an addition or outbuilding was permitted** → the jurisdiction's permit record.
- **School assignment** → the district, which can change boundaries.
- **Flood, landslide, seismic and shoreline designations** → the published mapping and the jurisdiction.
- **Whether the property will appraise** → nobody. Do not say it.
- **What the market will do** → nobody. Do not say it.

**RCW 18.86.040(1)(c) and 18.86.050(1)(c) make the referral a statutory duty**, and duty (b) is what an
unsupported assertion will be measured against.

---

## F. The listing sequence

chunks.heading: Module WA-P-05 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Pamphlet, and acknowledgment** — RCW 18.86.030(1)(f).
2. **Services agreement between the FIRM and the seller**, containing all five RCW 18.86.020(2)(b) items,
   with dual agency consent **separately initialed**, and the compensation terms RCW 18.86.080(7) requires.
3. **The RCW 18.86.130 conversation** — public and all-broker marketing, concurrently, unless health or
   safety reasonably requires otherwise; and **access control is a separate question.**
4. **Verify what you are about to publish**, or attribute it, or omit it.
5. **Market continuously and in good faith** — RCW 18.86.040(1)(e).
6. **Present every written offer, regardless** — RCW 18.86.030(1)(c).
7. **Disclose your role** in the paragraph titled **"Agency Disclosure,"** with the compensation terms offered
   to the other side's firm — RCW 18.86.030(1)(g).

---

## Module WA-P-05 engagement check

Eleven items, delivered as in Module WA-P-01. **No item states an advertising rule from WAC 308-124 or a
protected class list**, because neither was read for this project. Items test **RCW 18.86.130's prohibition,
condition, exception and final sentence**, its **RCW 18.86.031 consequence**, the **effort duty and its two
qualifications**, the **duties as applied to marketing**, the **describe-property-not-people discipline**, and
**what a broker routes.**

---

## Instructor source note for Module WA-P-05

Drawn from **RCW 18.86**, read in full on 2026-08-20 — specifically **§§ 18.86.010(11), 18.86.020(2)(b),
18.86.030(1)(a), (b), (c), (d), (f) and (g), 18.86.031, 18.86.040(1)(c) and (e), 18.86.050(1)(c) and (e),
18.86.080(7) and 18.86.130.** **RCW 18.86.130 was enacted by 2026 c 57 and is transcribed in full.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WA-P-05
chunks.excerpt:
**NOT obtained, and therefore the source of NOTHING here:** **WAC 308-124**, including every Washington
licensee **advertising** rule; the remainder of **RCW 18.85**, including **RCW 18.85.361**; the **Washington Law
Against Discrimination, RCW 49.60**; the **federal Fair Housing Act**; and any **multiple listing service rule
or policy.**

**No advertising rule, firm-name requirement, disclosure format, sign rule, internet or social media rule,
protected class list, MLS policy or penalty is stated in this module.**

lessons.title: Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-06

chunks.heading: Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-06
chunks.excerpt:
# Washington Real Estate Practices — Module WA-P-06

## Transaction practice, funds, records and risk management

**Course:** Real Estate Practices · **Instructional hours: 5.0** of 30.0 — the final module of the programme
**Clock hour = 50 minutes**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Washington clock hours are available.

> ### A submission gate stated at the top of this module
>
> **Washington's trust account, record-keeping and record-retention rules are in WAC 308-124 and the
> remainder of RCW 18.85, neither of which was obtained by this project.**
>
> **Accordingly this module states NO account requirement, NO deposit deadline, NO reconciliation interval,
> NO record retention period and NO penalty.** It teaches the **statutory accounting duty in RCW 18.86**,
> which was read, and it routes the mechanics. **Obtaining WAC 308-124 and completing this module from its own
> text is a submission gate.**

## Learning objectives

1. Run a transaction from first contact to closing in the order RCW 18.86 requires.
2. State the accounting duty and identify that it survives termination.
3. Identify what a broker must never do with other people's money.
4. Apply the duties to a multiple-offer situation.
5. Apply the duties to an in-house transaction.
6. State the record a broker should be able to produce, and why.
7. State the risk management habits that follow from the statute.

---

## A. The transaction in order

### A.1 First contact

chunks.heading: A.2 Establishing the relationship
chunks.excerpt:
**Recognise that buyer agency may already exist.** **RCW 18.86.020(1):** a broker performing brokerage
services for a buyer **is** the buyer's agent unless the firm has appointed them to the seller, to both, or the
broker is the seller. **No signature is required for the relationship to exist.**

**Give the pamphlet and obtain the acknowledgment** — **RCW 18.86.030(1)(f)** — *"as soon as reasonably
practical but before the party signs a services agreement."*

**And to any party not represented by a broker**, before they sign an offer or as soon as reasonably practical.
**That duty is owed even though they are not your principal**, because RCW 18.86.030(1) runs **to all
parties.**

### A.2 Establishing the relationship

**The FIRM enters a services agreement with the principal**, before or as soon as reasonably practical after
services commence — **RCW 18.86.020(2)(a)** — containing **all five** items in **(2)(b)**: the term (with the
**60-day buyer default**), the appointed broker, **exclusive or nonexclusive with checkbox options for a
buyer**, the **separately initialed** limited dual agency consent with its acknowledgment, and the **second
consent** covering the designated and managing brokers.

**And the compensation terms RCW 18.86.080(7) requires** — the amount, consent to sharing, consent to
compensation by more than one party, and, for a buyer, **whether the broker will show properties where no one
is offering to compensate the firm.**

### A.3 Working the transaction

chunks.heading: A.4 Offer and agreement
chunks.excerpt:
**Present everything written, both directions, timely, regardless.** *(1)(c)*
**Disclose known material facts not apparent or readily ascertainable.** *(1)(d)*
**Keep the principal informed, and do not disclose their confidential information** — the five-part test in
**RCW 18.86.010(9)**.
**Timely disclose any conflicts of interest.** *(RCW 18.86.040(1)(b) / .050(1)(b))*
**Route what is beyond you** — a statutory duty. *(.040(1)(c) / .050(1)(c))*

### A.4 Offer and agreement

**Disclose the role in writing** in a paragraph titled **"Agency Disclosure"** — **before the principal signs
an offer**, and in any event before mutual agreement — **including any compensation terms offered by a party
or firm to a firm representing another party.** *(1)(g)*

**Remember RCW 18.86.010(15):** *"a prospective transaction does not exist until a **written offer has been
signed by at least one party**."*

### A.5 Through closing

**Account in a timely manner for all money and property received.** *(1)(e)*
**Track and deliver.** **Confirm the closing statement against the agreement.** **Do not opine on legal effect
or tax consequences** — **RCW 18.86.110** leaves the practice-of-law boundary where the courts put it.

---

## B. Money — the duty, and where the mechanics live

### B.1 The statutory duty

**RCW 18.86.030(1)(e)** — owed to the principal **and to all parties**, **unwaivable**:

> *"To **account in a timely manner for all money and property received from or on behalf of either
> party**."*

**And RCW 18.86.070(2)** — after the relationship terminates, **two duties survive**, and this is one:

> *"(a) To **account for all moneys and property received during the relationship**; and (b) to **not disclose
> confidential information**."*

chunks.heading: B.2 What the mechanics are, and where they are
chunks.excerpt:
**A broker who cannot produce a clean accounting has breached a statutory duty**, whatever the mechanics turn
out to require — and the duty follows them past the end of the relationship.

### B.2 What the mechanics are, and where they are

**Which account, on what deadline, with what records, reconciled how often, retained how long** — all of it is
in **WAC 308-124 and the remainder of RCW 18.85**, **which this project did not read.**

**This course therefore states no deposit deadline, no account requirement, no reconciliation interval and no
retention period.** A broker learns them from the rule's own text and from the firm's designated broker,
**before** handling money — not after.

### B.3 What is true regardless of the mechanics

**Other people's money is not the firm's money.** Three things follow, and none of them depends on a rule this
project did not read:

- **Never mix it with the firm's or your own funds.**
- **Never use it**, for any purpose, for any period, however briefly and however certain you are of putting it
  back.
- **Never disburse it on your own judgement of who is entitled** where there is a dispute. **The broker holds;
  the parties or a court decide.**

**A broker who is unsure what to do with money in a dispute asks the designated broker and counsel — before
moving it.**

---

## C. Two situations that test the whole chapter

### C.1 Multiple offers

**Present them all.** **RCW 18.86.030(1)(c)**: all written offers, notices and communications, timely, **both
directions**, **regardless of whether the property is already under contract.** **The broker does not filter.**

chunks.heading: C.2 The in-house transaction
chunks.excerpt:
**Do not disclose the terms of one offer to another buyer without the seller's authority** — the seller's
instructions govern, and **RCW 18.86.010(9)**'s five-part test tells you whether the information is
confidential in the first place.

**Treat every buyer the same way.** A process explained to one buyer and not another is a fair housing problem
waiting to be alleged, and it is also a failure of **duty (b) — honestly and in good faith, owed to all
parties.**

**Advise the seller to seek expert advice** where the choice among offers turns on legal or tax questions —
**a statutory duty under RCW 18.86.040(1)(c).**

### C.2 The in-house transaction

**RCW 18.86.060(5)** assigns three positions at once when two brokers in one firm represent the two sides:

- **Each appointed broker SOLELY represents their own party.**
- **The designated broker, and any managing broker supervising both, IS a limited dual agent** — by operation
  of the statute, not by anyone's choice.

**The consent that covers it is RCW 18.86.020(2)(b)(v)** — the **second** consent, distinct from (iv). A firm
that obtained only (iv) has consent to the wrong thing.

**And the supervisor's position is genuinely constrained.** A limited dual agent must **take no action adverse
or detrimental to either party.** Relaying one side's position to the other broker is exactly what that
forbids, and it is the most common way an in-house transaction goes wrong.

---

## D. The record

**Washington's record-keeping and retention rules were not read for this project, and no requirement from them
is stated here.** What follows is what the **statutory duties themselves** imply a broker should be able to
produce.

chunks.heading: E. Risk management — the whole programme in one page
chunks.excerpt:
- **The pamphlet acknowledgment**, for every party it was owed to — including **unrepresented** parties.
  *(1)(f)*
- **The services agreement**, with all five RCW 18.86.020(2)(b) items and the **separately initialed**
  consents.
- **The Agency Disclosure**, in a paragraph bearing that title, dated before the principal signed an offer.
  *(1)(g)*
- **Every written offer, notice and communication**, and evidence of when it was presented. *(1)(c)*
- **What was disclosed, to whom, and when.** *(1)(d)*
- **A complete accounting** of every dollar and item received. *(1)(e)*
- **Conflict disclosures**, dated. *(.040(1)(b) / .050(1)(b))*

**Every one of those corresponds to a statutory duty, and the record is how the duty is shown to have been
performed.** A broker with no record has no answer.

---

## E. Risk management — the whole programme in one page

Ten habits, each traceable to a provision you have now read.

chunks.heading: F. What these courses did not read, restated at the end
chunks.excerpt:
1. **Give the pamphlet and get the acknowledgment** — including to unrepresented parties. *(1)(f)*
2. **Get the services agreement in place**, with all five contents and both consents. *(RCW 18.86.020(2)(b))*
3. **Answer the compensation questions in the agreement**, including whether you will show properties where no
   one is offering to pay the firm. *(RCW 18.86.080(7))*
4. **Present everything written, both directions, timely — regardless.** *(1)(c)*
5. **Disclose what you know** that is material and not apparent — and remember **you have no duty to
   investigate what you did not agree to investigate**, and **an agreement to investigate creates the duty.**
   *(1)(d)*
6. **Account for every dollar**, and know it survives the relationship. *(1)(e), RCW 18.86.070(2))*
7. **Keep confidences** — the five-part test — **except under subpoena or court order, even after
   termination.** *(RCW 18.86.010(9), .040(1)(d), .050(1)(d), .060(2)(d))*
8. **Disclose conflicts timely**, and disclose your role under the prescribed heading before your principal
   signs an offer. *(1)(g))*
9. **Market publicly and concurrently to all brokers** unless health or safety reasonably requires otherwise.
   *(RCW 18.86.130)*
10. **Route what is beyond you** — a statutory duty, not a courtesy. *(.040(1)(c) / .050(1)(c))*

**And the one that holds the rest together — RCW 18.86.030(1)(b): deal honestly and in good faith.** Owed to
everyone. Not waivable. **Every violation in these two courses is, underneath, a failure of that sentence.**

---

## F. What these courses did not read, restated at the end

**Obtained and read in full:** **RCW 18.86**; **RCW 18.85.101**; **WAC 308-124H** §§ 810, 820, 830, 835, 840,
845 and 855.

chunks.heading: Module WA-P-06 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**NOT obtained.** Nothing in this build states a rule, figure, deadline, form provision, fee or penalty from
any of them:

- **The Department of Licensing's prescribed course curriculum** — **WAC 308-124H-810** requires an approved
  school to use it.
- **WAC 308-124A-800** and **WAC 308-124A-802**.
- **The remainder of RCW 18.85**, including **RCW 18.85.011**, **18.85.041**, **18.85.141** and
  **18.85.361**.
- **WAC 308-124, 308-124A, 308-124B, 308-124C, 308-124D and 308-124E** — Washington's **trust account,
  advertising and record-retention** rules.
- **The full text of the RCW 18.86.120 pamphlet.**
- **RCW 64.06** and the **seller disclosure statement**.
- **RCW 59.18**, the Residential Landlord-Tenant Act, and the unlawful detainer statutes.
- **RCW 49.60**, the Washington Law Against Discrimination, and the **federal Fair Housing Act**.
- **RCW 82.45** and every local **excise tax** ordinance; Washington's **property tax** statutes.
- **RCW 61.24**, the Deeds of Trust Act; Washington's **recording**, **intestacy**, **community property**,
  **condominium**, **adverse possession** and **mechanics' lien** statutes.
- **ARELLO's** certification standards; any **Department examination content outline or candidate handbook**;
  **USPAP**; and **TILA, RESPA, TRID and ECOA**.

**A course that names its gaps has told you something useful, not withheld something.** That list is your map
to where the answers live — and the first thing a new Washington broker should do is read the ones that govern
their own daily work.

---

## Module WA-P-06 engagement check

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WA-P-06
chunks.excerpt:
Eleven items, delivered as in Module WA-P-01. **No item states a trust account requirement, deposit deadline,
reconciliation interval, retention period or penalty**, because the rules setting them were not read for this
project. Items test **the transaction sequence**, **the accounting duty and its survival**, **what is true
about other people's money regardless of the mechanics**, **multiple offers**, **the in-house transaction and
the second consent**, **the record**, and the **risk management habits.**

**This is the final module of the 90-hour programme.** Under **WAC 308-124H-820(8)** the comprehensive
examination for this 30-hour course must carry **at least 90 questions** with a passing grade of **at least 70
percent**, and the 60-hour Fundamentals course must carry **at least 180.** Those are the director's figures.
The **80 percent** in-module engagement threshold is this school's.

---

## Instructor source note for Module WA-P-06

Drawn from **RCW 18.86**, read in full on 2026-08-20 — specifically **§§ 18.86.010(9) and (15), 18.86.020,
18.86.030, 18.86.031, 18.86.040, 18.86.050, 18.86.060(5), 18.86.070(2), 18.86.080(7), 18.86.110 and
18.86.130** — together with **RCW 18.85.101** and **WAC 308-124H-820(8).**

**Not obtained, and therefore the source of nothing here:** the sources listed in Part F.

**No trust account requirement, deposit deadline, reconciliation interval, record retention period, penalty,
sanction or procedure is stated in this module.**

lessons.title: Wisconsin Salesperson Pre-License — Module WI-01

chunks.heading: Wisconsin Salesperson Pre-License — Module WI-01
chunks.excerpt:
# Wisconsin Salesperson Pre-License — Module WI-01

## Hours 1–5 · Real property and the real estate business

**Board topics covered:** REEB 25.033(1) Real property · REEB 25.033(2) The real estate business
**Clock hours:** 5. A Wisconsin clock hour is 60 minutes.
**Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Board review. **REEB 25.033 fixes the total at 72
hours and lists nineteen topics; it allocates no hours among them.**
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Wisconsin pre-license credit is available.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this module the student will be able to:

- Distinguish land, real estate and real property, and real from personal property.
- Classify a fixture and state which factor controls.
- Name the physical and economic characteristics of real estate and explain what each causes.
- Describe the forms of home ownership a Wisconsin buyer will meet, including condominium and
  cooperative, and state what a manufactured home's treatment turns on.
- List the recurring costs of ownership and the tax and insurance questions that go to a specialist.
- Explain supply, demand and the business cycle, and read the indicators honestly.
- Name the specialties within the real estate business and say where a salesperson sits under ch. 452.

## Timed sequence

chunks.heading: Hour 1 — Land, real estate, real property
chunks.excerpt:
| Hour | Content | Evidence |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Land, real estate, real property; real versus personal property | Section completed |
| 2 | Fixtures, characteristics of real estate | Section completed |
| 3 | Types of home ownership; property features; ownership expenses | Section completed |
| 4 | Investment considerations; tax benefits; homeowner's insurance | Section completed |
| 5 | The real estate business: specialties, market, supply and demand, cycles, ch. 452 | Module engagement check |
| **Total** | **5 clock hours** | |

---

## Hour 1 — Land, real estate, real property

### 1.1 The three words — REEB 25.033(1)(a) and (b)

The rule requires instruction on "land, real estate and real property" and on "the difference between
real property and personal property." They are three ideas and a boundary, and the whole of the first
week depends on keeping them apart.

**Land** is the surface of the earth, the space above it, and the ground beneath it, to the extent
the law recognises rights in each. Land has a vertical dimension: air rights above and subsurface
rights below, each of which can be owned and conveyed separately.

**Real estate** is land plus everything permanently attached to it, by nature or by people. A stand
of timber, a barn, a well, a fence, a driveway — attach them and they stop being separate objects.

**Real property** is real estate plus **the legal interests** a person may hold in it. This is what
is actually bought and sold. When a licensee lists "a house", what is being marketed is a set of
rights: to possess, to use, to exclude, to encumber, to transfer, and to do nothing at all.

chunks.heading: 1.2 Personal property, and why the line matters
chunks.excerpt:
The teaching image is the **bundle of rights**, and its value is that it makes visible the fact that
rights separate. A Wisconsin seller who conveys the surface and reserves the mineral or timber rights
has sold real property and kept real property.

### 1.2 Personal property, and why the line matters

**Personal property** — chattels, personalty — is everything that is not real property: movable
things, and intangible rights not attached to land.

The distinction decides the **instrument**. Real property is conveyed by **deed**. Personal property
transfers by **bill of sale** or by delivery. REEB 25.033(8)(f)13 requires instruction on **bills of
sale** precisely because a Wisconsin transaction routinely conveys both, and the offer to purchase is
where the parties say which is which.

Note also **§ 452.133(3)(d)**, which prohibits a licensee from negotiating the sale, exchange,
purchase or rental of **personal property unless related to the transaction** — with the licensee
permitted to use a Board-approved form under s. 452.05(1)(b) for the conveyance of the seller's
interest in personal property. So the line is not merely academic; it bounds what a licensee may do.

### 1.3 Water rights — REEB 25.033(5)(d), introduced here

Wisconsin has more shoreline and more inland water than most states, and **water rights** are a
listed topic in their own right at REEB 25.033(5)(d). Module WI-04 develops them. What belongs in
Hour 1 is the vocabulary:

**Riparian rights** attach to land abutting a flowing watercourse — a river or stream. **Littoral
rights** attach to land abutting a lake or other still water. Both are **appurtenant**: they run with
the land and are not separately owned by a person.

chunks.heading: 1.4 The licensee's boundary, stated at Hour 1
chunks.excerpt:
The **public trust doctrine** in Wisconsin holds navigable waters in trust for the public, and it is
the constitutional foundation of the state's shoreland and navigable-waters regulation. What a
riparian owner may do at the water's edge — a pier, a dredging, a bank alteration, a boathouse — is
regulated, and it is regulated by the Department of Natural Resources and the county rather than
answered by a licensee.

**Ordinary high water mark** is the boundary concept that decides where public rights begin and
private rights end on a navigable water. It is determined by evidence on the ground, not by a
map, and a licensee who tells a buyer where it is has answered a question belonging to the DNR and a
surveyor.

### 1.4 The licensee's boundary, stated at Hour 1

The licence permits a person to provide **real estate brokerage services**. It does not make them a
lawyer, an appraiser, an inspector, a surveyor, a lender, or an accountant.

**REEB 24.03** — competence in area of service — is a listed topic at REEB 25.033(13)(b)1.a, and it
is the rule that says so. Module WI-10 takes it in full. From Hour 1 the habit is: when a question
belongs to another profession, say so, name the profession, and put it in writing.

---

## Hour 2 — Fixtures and the characteristics of real estate

### 2.1 Classification of fixtures — REEB 25.033(1)(c)

A **fixture** is an item that was personal property and became real property by attachment. Once a
fixture, it passes with the deed unless the contract says otherwise.

The test has three principal factors and two supporting ones, commonly given as **MARIA**:

chunks.heading: 2.2 How Wisconsin prevents the dispute
chunks.excerpt:
**Method of annexation.** How is it attached, and what happens on removal? Bolted, wired, plumbed or
built in points to a fixture, and so does damage or a non-functioning system on removal.

**Adaptation to the real estate.** Has it been fitted to this particular property? Custom storm
windows, a built-in cabinet cut to an alcove, and the key to the front door are adapted — and
adaptation makes a fixture even where the physical attachment is slight.

**Intention** of the party who attached it, judged **objectively** by what a reasonable person would
infer from the circumstances. Courts treat intention as controlling and the first two factors as
evidence of it.

**Relationship of the parties.** The same item is treated differently between landlord and tenant
than between seller and buyer, and doubt is generally resolved in favour of the weaker position.

**Agreement**, which is decisive where it exists.

**Trade fixtures** are installed by a *tenant* for the tenant's trade or business, remain the
tenant's personal property, and must be removed before the term ends — after which they generally
pass to the landlord by **accession**. **Severance** runs the other way: standing timber is real
estate, and cut timber is personal property.

### 2.2 How Wisconsin prevents the dispute

Most fixture disputes are contracts that failed to say. Wisconsin's answer is structural: the
**Board-approved offer to purchase** under **ch. REEB 16** carries defined lists of **included items**
and **excluded items**, and the licensee's job at listing is to walk the property and fill them in
correctly.

chunks.heading: 2.3 Characteristics of real estate — REEB 25.033(1)(d)
chunks.excerpt:
Items to resolve before the first photograph: light fittings and chandeliers; mounted televisions and
their brackets; mirrors; appliances; window treatments and their hardware; shelving; workshop
equipment; **fuel tanks** and whether they are owned or leased; **water softeners and iron filters**,
which on a private well are frequently rented; generators; playground equipment; above-ground pools;
sheds on skids as against sheds on foundations; and anything the seller intends to take.

A leased water softener is not the seller's to convey. Discovering that at the walk-through is a
failure of the listing conversation, not of the contract.

### 2.3 Characteristics of real estate — REEB 25.033(1)(d)

**Physical characteristics**, and what each causes:

**Immobility.** A parcel cannot be moved. Demand in Madison cannot be met by shipping in surplus
houses from Green Bay. This is why real estate markets are local, why location dominates value, and
why a national statistic is a poor description of any particular market.

**Indestructibility**, or more precisely durability. The land survives; improvements decay slowly and
are expensive to remove. So the housing stock at any moment is overwhelmingly made of buildings
built in the past, under past codes, for past tastes.

**Uniqueness**, also called heterogeneity or non-homogeneity. No two parcels occupy the same space.
This is why every valuation is an estimate rather than a lookup, and why **specific performance** is
available on a land contract in a way it is not for ordinary goods.

**Economic characteristics:**

chunks.heading: Hour 3 — Home ownership, property features, and the cost of owning
chunks.excerpt:
**Scarcity** — not that land has run out, but that land in a particular useful location is finite.
**Improvements** — a change to one parcel affects the value of its neighbours.
**Permanence of investment** — capital sunk into land as sewers, roads and foundations is not
recoverable.
**Area preference**, or *situs* — the observed human preference for a particular location, which is
what people actually pay for.

---

## Hour 3 — Home ownership, property features, and the cost of owning

### 3.1 Types of home ownership — REEB 25.033(1)(e)

**Fee simple ownership of a lot and house.** The ordinary case: the owner holds the land and the
improvements.

**Condominium.** REEB 25.033(5)(j) requires instruction on condominiums **under ss. 703.08, 703.21
and 703.33**. A condominium divides a project into individually owned **units** and **common
elements** owned in undivided shares, with **limited common elements** serving fewer than all units.
The governing instruments are the declaration, the bylaws, the recorded plat and plans, and the
rules. Wisconsin's condominium law is **ch. 703**, and this course states no requirement from it,
because the chapter has not been read from primary text for this project. What a licensee must do is
obtain the documents, the budget, the reserve position, two years of minutes, the assessment history
and any discussed special assessment — before the offer.

**Cooperative.** REEB 25.033(5)(h). A corporation owns the real property; the resident owns **shares**
and holds a **proprietary lease**. The resident therefore owns **personal property**, not real
property — no deed, financing by share loan rather than mortgage, and a board that typically has
approval rights over a transfer, subject always to fair housing law.

chunks.heading: 3.2 Property features — REEB 25.033(1)(h)
chunks.excerpt:
**Time-share.** REEB 25.033(5)(i) requires instruction on time-shares under **ss. 70.095, 707.02,
707.05, 707.40, 707.47 and 707.49**. Wisconsin regulates time-share sales and disclosure in **ch.
707**, unread here, and a licensee working in time-share must read the chapter.

**Planned communities and homeowners associations**, governed by their recorded declarations.

**Manufactured and mobile homes.** REEB 25.033(1)(f) lists "mobile homes under s. 70.043, Stats." and
**the rule itself carries a Note that s. 70.043 was repealed by 2023 Wisconsin Act 12**. A course
must therefore teach the substance without citing a repealed section as operative.

The substance is a classification question with real consequences: a manufactured home may be
**personal property**, titled and taxed as such, or it may have become **real property** where it is
placed on a permanent foundation on land the owner holds and the appropriate steps have been taken.
Which it is decides whether it conveys by deed or by title transfer, whether it can be mortgaged as
real estate, and how it is taxed. **The current Wisconsin treatment must be read from the statutes as
they now stand**, and a transaction involving a manufactured home goes to the closing agent and to
counsel early.

### 3.2 Property features — REEB 25.033(1)(h)

chunks.heading: 3.3 Ownership expenses — REEB 25.033(1)(g)
chunks.excerpt:
What a buyer is actually evaluating: site characteristics — lot size, frontage, topography, drainage,
soils, exposure, trees; the structure — style, age, size, layout, condition, materials; systems —
heating, cooling, electrical service, plumbing, water supply and wastewater; **energy performance**,
which in a Wisconsin climate is a running cost rather than a preference; outbuildings; and location
attributes — schools, employment, services, and what is next door and might change.

A licensee describes these accurately and does not characterise them. Hour 2 of Module WI-10 takes
the rule that makes this a legal obligation rather than a habit.

### 3.3 Ownership expenses — REEB 25.033(1)(g)

The recurring costs a buyer must plan for, and which a licensee should be able to list without
prompting:

**Property taxes**, which in Wisconsin are levied by the municipality and are billed in December for
the year just assessed, payable in instalments — Module WI-05 takes ss. 74.15 and 74.47.
**Homeowner's insurance**, and separately **flood insurance** where required.
**Mortgage principal and interest**, and any **mortgage insurance**.
**Utilities**, with a Wisconsin heating season that makes fuel a material line.
**Maintenance**, conventionally estimated as a percentage of value annually, and **capital
replacement** — roof, furnace, water heater, windows, well pump, septic — which does not stop.
**Association assessments**, where applicable, and the special assessment risk.
**Snow removal, lawn care, and seasonal costs.**

The professional point: the payment a lender qualifies a buyer on is not the cost of ownership, and a
licensee who lets a buyer conflate the two has not served them.

---

## Hour 4 — Investment, tax, and insurance

chunks.heading: 4.1 Investment considerations — REEB 25.033(1)(i)
chunks.excerpt:
### 4.1 Investment considerations — REEB 25.033(1)(i)

Four sources of return from owning: **cash flow** where the property produces income;
**appreciation**, which is expected rather than promised; **equity buildup** as amortisation retires
principal; and **tax treatment**, which depends entirely on the owner's circumstances.

Against them: **illiquidity** — selling takes months and costs a substantial share of the price;
**indivisibility**; **concentration** of household wealth in one undiversified asset; **management
burden**; **physical risk**; **market risk**; and **regulatory risk**.

**Leverage** is the use of borrowed money to control an asset larger than the buyer's own capital.
It **amplifies whatever is happening**, in both directions. Where the return on the asset exceeds the
cost of debt, borrowing raises the return on equity; where it does not, borrowing lowers it and
magnifies loss.

**Appreciation is not guaranteed**, and a licensee who tells a client a house is a sure investment
has made a representation about future value that nobody can support — which is a **misleading
statement of market value** problem under **REEB 24.09** and a reasonable-skill-and-care problem
under **§ 452.133(1)(b)**.

### 4.2 Tax benefits for home ownership — REEB 25.033(1)(j)

The rule requires the topic to be taught. It does not make a licensee a tax adviser, and the
professional treatment is to name the concepts so a client knows what to ask.

chunks.heading: 4.3 Homeowner's insurance — REEB 25.033(1)(k)
chunks.excerpt:
**Mortgage interest** and **property tax** deductions, both subject to federal limitations that
change and both dependent on whether the taxpayer itemises.
**Exclusion of gain on the sale of a principal residence**, subject to ownership and use requirements
and dollar limits set by federal law.
**Basis** — broadly purchase price plus capital improvements — and **gain** on sale.
**Depreciation** on income-producing property, on which **land is not depreciable**.
**Deferred exchanges** under section 1031, with their identification and completion periods.
**Wisconsin's own credits and relief programmes**, including the school levy and first dollar credits
that appear on a Wisconsin tax bill, and the **lottery and gaming credit**, which is claimed by an
owner who uses the property as a primary residence and which appears on the bill only if claimed.

**This course states no figure, limit, rate or threshold for any of them.** Every one depends on the
taxpayer's circumstances and on law that changes.

**§ 452.133(2)(am)** is the section that makes the boundary a statutory one: a firm owes a client, on
request, information and advice on matters material to the transaction **and within the scope of the
knowledge, skills and training required under ch. 452**. Tax advice is outside that scope. The
professional sentence is: *here is the concept and here is who answers it, and I am putting that in
writing.*

### 4.3 Homeowner's insurance — REEB 25.033(1)(k)

A homeowners policy is conventionally organised as **Coverage A** dwelling, **B** other structures,
**C** personal property, **D** loss of use, **E** personal liability, and **F** medical payments to
others.

chunks.heading: Hour 5 — The real estate business
chunks.excerpt:
**Named peril** forms cover only what they list; **open peril** or all-risk forms cover everything
except what they exclude — so reading the exclusions is how one reads an open-peril policy.

**Replacement cost** pays to replace without deduction for depreciation; **actual cash value**
deducts it, and the difference on a fifteen-year-old roof is large. **Extended** or **guaranteed
replacement cost** endorsements address rebuilding costs above the policy limit.

**Coinsurance** reduces a partial-loss recovery proportionally where the insured carries less than a
stated percentage of replacement value.

**Common exclusions**: **flood**, earth movement, ordinary wear and neglect, mould in many forms,
intentional acts, and business use. **Ordinance or law** coverage — the cost of rebuilding to current
code — is a common endorsement rather than a standard inclusion.

**Flood is excluded and requires a separate policy**, from the National Flood Insurance Program or
the private market. REEB 25.033(18)(g) lists **flood insurance** as a required topic in its own right
and REEB 25.033(18)(f) lists **floodplains under s. 87.30 Stats. and ss. NR 116.01 and 116.06**.
Module WI-12 takes them.

**Condominium unit owners** need a unit-owner policy whose scope depends entirely on where the
association's master policy stops — a boundary set by the declaration.

**Landlords** need a landlord or dwelling-fire policy, and **tenants** need renters coverage, because
the landlord's policy covers the building and not the tenant's belongings or liability.

A licensee identifies the questions and refers them to an insurance professional. Telling a buyer
what a policy will cover is not brokerage.

---

## Hour 5 — The real estate business

### 5.1 Real estate specialties — REEB 25.033(2)(a)

chunks.heading: 5.2 The real estate market and what moves it — REEB 25.033(2)(b) and (c)
chunks.excerpt:
**Residential brokerage**; **commercial and industrial brokerage**; **farm and land brokerage**,
which in Wisconsin is a substantial specialty of its own and carries farmland preservation, drainage,
and current-use questions; **property management**; **appraisal**, separately licensed;
**mortgage banking**, which REEB 25.033(19)(g) reaches through **s. 224.71**; **title and closing
services**; **development and construction**; **counselling and consulting**; and **auction**.

A salesperson should be able to say which specialty a question belongs to, because most of what goes
wrong is a licensee answering a question from a specialty they do not practise.

### 5.2 The real estate market and what moves it — REEB 25.033(2)(b) and (c)

**Demand** is driven by population and household formation, employment and wages, the cost and
availability of credit, expectations, and the price of substitutes such as rentals. It changes in
weeks.

**Supply** is the existing stock plus what new construction can deliver — and new construction takes
land assembly, entitlement, financing, permitting, and building, which in Wisconsin is further
compressed by a construction season that closes in winter. It changes in years.

So the central prediction: **in the short run supply is close to fixed, and a demand increase shows
up almost entirely as price.** Days on market fall, inventory falls, and multiple offers appear. New
supply arrives later, sometimes after demand has moved again — and that mismatch is the structural
reason real estate cycles.

### 5.3 Business cycles — REEB 25.033(2)(d)

chunks.heading: 5.4 Reading the indicators honestly
chunks.excerpt:
**Expansion** — demand growing faster than supply; vacancy below its long-run average; rents and
prices rising; construction beginning to respond.
**Oversupply or contraction** — construction started during expansion completes; supply catches up
and passes demand; vacancy rises; price growth decelerates; concessions appear.
**Recession** — demand below supply; vacancy above average; prices falling; construction stopped;
distressed sales entering.
**Recovery** — the surplus absorbing; vacancy falling toward average; prices lagging; construction
not yet resumed.

The most common student error is to equate the cycle with interest rates. Rates are one input to
demand. **Local employment is usually the stronger driver**, and in Wisconsin's manufacturing and
agricultural markets a single employer or a commodity price can move a local market on its own.

### 5.4 Reading the indicators honestly

**Months of inventory** — active listings divided by average monthly closed sales. **Absorption rate**
— the pace of take-up. **Days on market**, median rather than mean. **List-to-sale price ratio**.
**New listings against closed sales**, which turns before the stock does. **Vacancy rate** for rental
property.

Two constraints belong with them.

**The data is historical.** Closed sales report decisions made weeks earlier, and nothing in the set
describes the future. **§ 452.133(1)(e)** requires a firm to provide **accurate information about
market conditions** on request — accurate, which means what the evidence shows, not an extrapolation
presented as a forecast.

**Aggregates hide the property.** A change in a median can be entirely a change in what sold.

### 5.5 Real estate practice under ch. 452 — REEB 25.033(2)(e)

chunks.heading: Module WI-01 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**Chapter 452** is the Real Estate Practice chapter, and it is where the licence, the duties, the
prohibitions and the discipline live. The sections a salesperson meets constantly, each of which a
later module develops:

**§ 452.133** — duties of licensees and prohibitions. Module WI-02.
**§ 452.135** — the requirement for an agency agreement and disclosure of agency. Module WI-02.
**§ 452.139** — revisions to common law duties and responsibilities. Module WI-02.
**§ 452.136** — advertising. Module WI-10.
**§ 452.13** — trust accounts, and the rules promulgated under § 452.13(5). Module WI-13.
**§ 452.23** — disclosures and inspections by brokers and salespersons, including particular disclosure limits, third-party-report conditions, contradictory facts, and the prudent-licensee standard of care. This is not the Department's investigation-power statute. Module WI-10, section 62.1.
**§ 452.05(1)(b)** — the Board's power to approve forms, which is why Wisconsin brokerage runs on
approved forms at all. Module WI-06.

And the structural fact a Wisconsin salesperson must absorb early: **the duties in § 452.133(1) are
owed to every party to a transaction, not only to clients.** Seven of them, including a **written**
material-adverse-facts disclosure duty and a confidentiality duty that **continues after the
transaction is complete**. Module WI-02 is built on it.

### Module WI-01 engagement check

**Question.** At a listing appointment the seller shows you a water softener and an iron filter in
the basement, a propane tank behind the garage, and a chandelier in the dining room that belonged to
her mother. She says "obviously the chandelier is coming with me". What do you do, and what rule are
you working under?

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WI-01
chunks.excerpt:
**Expected answer.** All four items are resolved **in writing, at listing, before any photograph is
taken**, and recorded in the included and excluded items of the **Board-approved offer to purchase
under ch. REEB 16**.

The **chandelier** is a fixture on the ordinary test — attached, adapted, and objectively intended to
be permanent — so the seller's wish is not the test and it will convey unless it is expressly
excluded. The professional answer is to have it removed and replaced **before marketing**, not after
a buyer has seen it.

The **water softener and iron filter** and the **propane tank** raise a different question:
**ownership**. Each is frequently **leased or rented** rather than owned, and a leased item is not
the seller's to convey. The lease must be produced and the arrangement — assignment, termination, or
exclusion — written into the offer.

The rule I am working under is **§ 452.133(1)(c)**: the firm owes **every party** the duty to timely
disclose **in writing** all material adverse facts the firm knows and the party does not know or
cannot discover through reasonably vigilant observation. A buyer cannot discover by looking that the
softener is rented. And **§ 452.133(1)(b)** — reasonable skill and care — is what makes doing this at
listing rather than at the walk-through part of the job.

---

## Instructor source note for Module WI-01

Wisconsin statements rest on text read directly from `docs.legis.wisconsin.gov` on 2026-08-20 and
recorded in `wisconsin/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`: **REEB 25.033** in full, including its

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WI-01

**REEB 25.033(1)(f) lists "mobile homes under s. 70.043, Stats." and the rule itself carries a Note

**Deliberately not stated, for want of a primary reading:** any requirement of **ch. 703**

**Water rights vocabulary in Hour 1.3 — riparian, littoral, the public trust doctrine, and the
