chunks.excerpt:
# Wisconsin Salesperson Pre-License — Module WI-10

## Hours 56–62 · Fair housing, ethics, and consumer protection

**Board topics covered:** REEB 25.033(12) Fair housing laws · (13) Ethical real estate practices ·
(14) Consumer protection
**Clock hours:** 7 · **Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Board review.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Wisconsin pre-license credit is available.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this module the student will be able to:

- State the federal protected classes and say where Wisconsin's own list is found.
- Identify blockbusting, steering and redlining in a fact pattern and name the practice.
- Distinguish a reasonable accommodation from a reasonable modification.
- Name every REEB 24 section REEB 25.033(13) and (14) cite and say what each is about.
- Apply § 452.136 to an advertisement, including the technology-modification rule.
- Apply the REEB 24.07 consumer-protection provisions to a property condition.
- Explain civil liability for misrepresentation and where it comes from.

## Timed sequence

chunks.heading: Hour 56 — Equal opportunity in housing — REEB 25.033(12)(a) and (b)
chunks.excerpt:
| Hour | Content | Evidence |
|---:|---|---|
| 56 | Equal opportunity in housing; federal fair housing law | Section completed |
| 57 | Blockbusting, steering, redlining; disability; s. 106.50; organizations | Section completed |
| 58 | Ch. REEB 24; competence, tie-in arrangements, written agreements | Section completed |
| 59 | Advertising: REEB 24.04 and § 452.136 | Section completed |
| 60 | Written proposals: REEB 24.12 and 24.13; disclosure of compensation and interest | Section completed |
| 61 | Consumer protection: REEB 24.07 in its five parts | Section completed |
| 62 | § 452.23 licensee disclosures and inspections; civil liability; ch. 709 seller disclosure | Module engagement check |
| **Total** | **7 clock hours** | |

---

## Hour 56 — Equal opportunity in housing — REEB 25.033(12)(a) and (b)

### 56.1 The federal floor

The **federal Fair Housing Act** — Title VIII of the Civil Rights Act of 1968, amended in 1974 and 1988
— prohibits discrimination in the sale, rental and financing of dwellings on the basis of **race,
colour, religion, national origin, sex, familial status, and disability**. Seven classes.

The **Civil Rights Act of 1866** is older, narrower and in one respect stronger: it prohibits **racial**
discrimination in the sale or lease of all property and, as the Supreme Court held in *Jones v. Alfred
H. Mayer Co.* (1968), **carries no exemptions**. A transaction exempt from the Fair Housing Act is not
exempt from the 1866 Act where the discrimination is racial.

chunks.heading: 56.2 Why a licensee's exposure is doubled in Wisconsin
chunks.excerpt:
**Prohibited practices** under federal law: refusing to sell or rent after a bona fide offer, or refusing
to negotiate; discriminating in terms, conditions or privileges, or in services and facilities;
discriminatory advertising; representing that a dwelling is unavailable when it is not; **blockbusting**;
**steering**; and **redlining**.

**Enforcement** runs through HUD complaint and administrative proceedings, federal civil actions, and
Department of Justice pattern-or-practice cases.

### 56.2 Why a licensee's exposure is doubled in Wisconsin

**§ 452.133(1)(a)** requires brokerage services to be provided **honestly and fairly** to every party,
and **§ 452.133(1)(b)** requires **reasonable skill and care**. A fair housing violation by a Wisconsin
licensee is therefore both a fair housing matter and a matter under **ch. 452** — two forums, two
consequences.

---

## Hour 57 — The practices, disability, and s. 106.50

### 57.1 Blockbusting, steering, redlining — REEB 25.033(12)(c)

**Blockbusting** — inducing or attempting to induce a person to sell or rent by representations
regarding the entry or prospective entry into the neighbourhood of persons of a protected class. It is
prohibited whether or not the representation is true, and whether or not anyone sells.

**Steering** — directing prospects toward or away from particular areas, buildings or neighbourhoods on
a protected basis. It is the practice a licensee is most likely to commit **without intending to**,
because it usually arrives as a helpful answer to a friendly question.

chunks.heading: 57.2 Disability: accommodation and modification
chunks.excerpt:
The compliant answer to "what kind of neighbourhood is it?" names **objective sources the buyer consults
for themselves**: school district data and attendance boundaries, crime statistics published by the
municipality, census data, tax rates, commute times. And it offers to **show every property meeting the
buyer's stated criteria**, with the criteria recorded **in the buyer's own words**.

**Redlining** — denying loans, insurance or services, or varying their terms, based on the composition of
an area rather than on the applicant or the property.

### 57.2 Disability: accommodation and modification

**A reasonable accommodation** is a change to a **rule, practice, policy or service** necessary to afford
a person with a disability equal opportunity to use and enjoy a dwelling — waiving a no-pets policy for
an **assistance animal**, assigning a parking space nearer the door, permitting a payment date matching a
benefit date. **The housing provider bears the ordinary cost of making it.**

**A reasonable modification** is a **physical change** to the premises necessary to afford full
enjoyment — a ramp, grab bars, a widened doorway. **It is at the disabled person's expense**, and in a
rental the landlord may, where reasonable, condition permission on the tenant agreeing to restore the
interior.

Two rules follow: **a no-pets policy is not an answer to an assistance-animal request**, because an
assistance animal is not a pet; and **pet fees and pet deposits may not be charged for one** — though the
tenant remains responsible for damage and behaviour.

**Design and construction.** Covered multi-family dwellings built for first occupancy after **13 March
1991** must meet federal accessible design and construction requirements.

chunks.heading: 57.3 Equal rights under s. 106.50 — REEB 25.033(12)(d)
chunks.excerpt:
**The ADA is a different regime.** It governs **places of public accommodation** and commercial
facilities — a real estate office or leasing office open to the public is one. **Housing is governed by
fair housing law**, and ADA service-animal rules must not be imported into a housing accommodation
analysis.

### 57.3 Equal rights under s. 106.50 — REEB 25.033(12)(d)

**Wisconsin's open housing law is s. 106.50**, and **it protects more classes than federal law.**

**This course does not print the Wisconsin list**, because **s. 106.50 has not been read from primary
text for this project** and a protected-class list is the single worst thing for a course to approximate.
Legislatures amend them, and a licensee relying on a remembered version is relying on a list that may
have changed.

What a licensee must carry: **s. 106.50 is the section**; **Wisconsin's list is broader than the federal
seven**; the **Department of Workforce Development's Equal Rights Division** administers it; and **the
current list must be read from s. 106.50 directly** before any licensee relies on a remembered version.

That instruction is not a hedge. It is the only responsible way to teach a list this course has not read.

### 57.4 Organizations — REEB 25.033(12)(e)

The rule requires instruction on the organisations involved in equal opportunity in housing. A licensee
should know where a complaint goes and where guidance comes from: **HUD** and its Office of Fair Housing
and Equal Opportunity federally; the **Wisconsin Equal Rights Division** under s. 106.50; local fair
housing councils and municipal equal opportunity commissions, several of which in Wisconsin administer
local ordinances of their own; and the **Department of Justice** for pattern-or-practice enforcement.

chunks.heading: 57.5 Practice rules
chunks.excerpt:
**Local ordinances may protect classes the state list does not**, which is one more reason a licensee
reads rather than recalls.

### 57.5 Practice rules

**Describe the property, never the occupants or the desired occupants.** "Four bedrooms, fenced yard,
walk to the elementary school" describes the property. "Perfect for a young family" expresses a
familial-status preference; "quiet building, ideal for mature professionals" expresses preferences on
age and family status.

**Use written, objective, uniform criteria** in leasing and apply them identically to every applicant.
Deviating for one applicant is the fact pattern that produces liability, whatever the reason.

**Do not honour a discriminatory covenant.** Historic racial covenants remain in Wisconsin chains of
title; they are void, and repeating one as though it operated is itself a problem.

## Hour 58 — Ch. REEB 24 and the conduct rules

### 58.1 What ch. REEB 24 is — REEB 25.033(13)(a)

**Ch. REEB 24** is the Board's chapter on **ethical real estate practices**, and REEB 25.033(13) requires
instruction on it. It is a **rule**, not a trade association's code: it is Wisconsin law, and violating it
is a disciplinary matter before the Board.

**This course names each cited section and states its subject. It does not quote or paraphrase the text
of any of them**, because ch. REEB 24 has not been read from primary text for this project. A student
must read the chapter itself, and an instructor supplementing this module must obtain and date the
reading.

### 58.2 Competence in area of service — REEB 24.03

REEB 25.033(13)(b)1.a. The rule addresses a licensee's **competence in the area of service** they hold
themselves out to provide.

chunks.heading: 58.3 Tie-in arrangements — REEB 24.075
chunks.excerpt:
It aligns exactly with **§ 452.133(2)(am)**, which limits the duty to advise a client to matters **within
the scope of the knowledge, skills and training required under ch. 452**, and with the plain-language
statement in the **§ 452.135** disclosure: *if you need legal advice, tax advice, or a professional home
inspection, contact an attorney, tax advisor, or home inspector.*

Three practical consequences: a residential licensee who takes a commercial, farm or time-share
transaction outside their competence has a rule problem as well as a service problem; the answer to a
question outside one's competence is a **referral**, not an attempt; and the referral is put **in
writing**.

### 58.3 Tie-in arrangements — REEB 24.075

**REEB 24.075** prohibits a licensee from conditioning the sale of real estate owned by the licensee or controlled by an option, as described in the rule, on the buyer purchasing other real estate or listing the buyer's real estate with the licensee. The rule has specific builder-related provisions; read them before applying an exception.

Do not describe every commercial tie or package as automatically prohibited by this particular rule. Federal antitrust tying analysis and this Wisconsin real-estate conduct rule are related subjects with different elements.

### 58.4 Agreements in writing — REEB 24.08

REEB 25.033(13)(b)1.c. The rule addresses **agreements in writing**.

It sits alongside the statutory requirements a student has already met: **§ 240.10**, requiring a broker's
contract to be in writing; **§ 706.02**, requiring a conveyance to be in writing; **§ 452.135(2)(a)**,
requiring the client disclosure not later than the agency agreement; and the approved-form regime under
**ch. REEB 16**.

chunks.heading: 58.5 Misleading market values — REEB 24.09
chunks.excerpt:
The habit it produces: **if it matters, it is written, signed, delivered and kept.**

### 58.5 Misleading market values — REEB 24.09

REEB 25.033(13)(b)1.d. The rule addresses **misleading market values**, and Module WI-09 Hour 55.3 set
out why it bites: a price presented to win a listing rather than to describe the evidence is the conduct
the rule addresses, and **§ 452.133(1)(e)** independently requires **accurate** information about market
conditions.

### 58.6 Net listings — REEB 24.10

A **net listing** is an arrangement in which the seller receives a fixed sum and the firm keeps the excess as its compensation. **REEB 24.10 strictly prohibits net listings.** It is not merely a matter to take to the supervising broker for consent, and the seller's proposal or informed agreement does not remove the prohibition. Use a lawful negotiated compensation arrangement instead.

## Hour 59 — Advertising

### 59.1 REEB 24.04 and § 452.136 — REEB 25.033(13)(b)2

The paragraph requires instruction on **advertising under s. REEB 24.04 and s. 452.136**, and **it was
amended by CR 23-075**, effective 9-1-24.

**REEB 24.04** is the Board's advertising rule; **this course names it and does not state its text**, for
the reason given at 58.1.

**§ 452.136 has been read**, and it is stated here in full.

### 59.2 § 452.136, applied

**(1) False advertising.** *A licensee may not advertise in a manner that is false, deceptive, or
misleading.*

**(1m) Advertising enhanced by technology.** *A licensee shall in all advertising disclose if the
advertising has been altered or modified using technology, **including artificial intelligence**, to
add, remove, or change elements of the property, that creates a false or misleading impression of the
property.*

chunks.heading: 59.2 § 452.136, applied
chunks.excerpt:
**This subsection is created effective 1 January 2027 by 2025 Wis. Act 69.** It is stated here because
it is on the books and dated, and because it will govern practice within the working life of anyone
completing this course. Virtual staging, sky replacement, removing a neighbouring structure, and
generative editing of a listing photograph all fall within it where the result creates a false or
misleading impression. **Until the effective date, subsection (1) governs the same conduct** — an
altered photograph creating a false impression is misleading advertising whether or not (1m) is yet in
force.

**(2) Disclosure of name.**
**(a)** Except for advertisements for the rental of real estate owned by the licensee, a licensee shall
in all advertising disclose **the firm's name exactly as printed on the licence**, or a **trade name
previously filed** with the department, and shall **clearly indicate that the firm is a business
enterprise and not a private party.**
**(b)** Except for the same rental advertisements, a licensee associated with a firm shall advertise
**under the supervision of and in the name of the firm**, and **the firm's name as used in advertising
shall be clear and conspicuous.** The paragraph does not apply to a licensee engaged in independent
practice under s. 452.30(6).
**(c)** A licensee may advertise the **occasional sale of real estate owned by the licensee**, or engage
in the occasional solicitation of real estate for purchase by the licensee, without complying with (a)
and (b) — **provided the licensee clearly identifies themselves as a real estate licensee in the
advertisement.**

chunks.heading: 59.3 Auditing an advertisement
chunks.excerpt:
**(3) Advertising without an agency agreement prohibited.** A firm and its licensees **may not advertise
a property unless** the firm is the **listing firm**, or has **obtained consent to advertise from the
listing firm.**

**(4) Advertised price.** A licensee **may not advertise property at a price other than that agreed upon
with the owner** — except that the price may be stated as a **range or in general terms if it reflects
the agreed upon price.**

### 59.3 Auditing an advertisement

Six questions, in order:

**Is it false, deceptive or misleading?** (1)
**Has it been altered or modified using technology in a way that creates a false or misleading
impression, and is that disclosed?** (1m) from 1-1-27, and (1) before then.
**Does it disclose the firm's name exactly as licensed, or a filed trade name, and indicate the firm is
a business rather than a private party?** (2)(a)
**Is it under the firm's supervision and in the firm's name, clear and conspicuous?** (2)(b)
**Is the firm the listing firm, or does it have the listing firm's consent?** (3)
**Is the price the price agreed with the owner, or a range or general terms reflecting it?** (4)

And then the fair housing question from Hour 57.5: **does anything in it describe the occupants rather
than the property?**

### 59.4 Other marketing controls

**Do Not Call**, the **TCPA** for automated calls and texts, and **CAN-SPAM** govern solicitation.
**Copyright** — photographs, floor plans, drone footage and video are copyrighted works, usually owned by
the photographer unless the agreement says otherwise; reusing another firm's listing photographs after a
listing changes hands is infringement, not economy. And **§ 452.136(3)** independently bars advertising
another firm's listing without consent.

chunks.heading: Hour 60 — Written proposals, compensation, and interest
chunks.excerpt:
## Hour 60 — Written proposals, compensation, and interest

### 60.1 Completing and presenting written proposals — REEB 24.12 and 24.13

REEB 25.033(13)(b)3 requires instruction on **completing and presenting written proposals under ss. REEB
24.12 and 24.13**, and names five elements:

**a. Confidentiality.** Which aligns with **§ 452.133(1)(d)** — owed to every party, covering information
the firm obtains that it knows a reasonable person would want kept confidential, and **continuing after
the transaction is complete**.

**b. Drafting and submitting offers.** On the **Board-approved forms** under ch. REEB 16, completed
rather than drafted — Module WI-06 Hour 32.

**c. Prompt delivery to buyer.** A signed acceptance, counter-offer or notice reaching the buyer promptly.

**d. Fair presentation of offers.** Which aligns with **§ 452.133(1)(g)** — presenting proposals
**objectively and without bias**, disclosing their **advantages and disadvantages**.

**e. Prompt notification.** Telling a party promptly what has happened to their proposal — particularly
where a **multiple counter-proposal** has been used and buyers are waiting on a seller's selection.

**The REEB 24 text is not stated here**, for the reason at 58.1. What is stated is that each element has
a statutory partner in § 452.133, so a licensee who satisfies the statute is most of the way to
satisfying the rule — and must still read the rule.

### 60.2 Disclosure of compensation and interest — REEB 24.05 and § 452.133

REEB 25.033(13)(b)4 requires instruction on **disclosure of compensation and interest under s. REEB 24.05
and s. 452.133**, and **the introduction was amended by CR 23-075.** Four elements:

chunks.heading: Hour 61 — Consumer protection: REEB 24.07
chunks.excerpt:
**a. Disclosing of interest.** **§ 452.133(3)(b)**: a licensee may not act in a transaction on their own
behalf, on behalf of immediate family where the firm is an individual, on behalf of their firm, or on
behalf of any organisation or entity **in which the licensee has an interest**, **without the prior
written consent of all parties** — and the consent must be obtained **in the offer to purchase, option,
lease, or other transaction contract.**

**b. Referral services.** **§ 452.133(3)(c)**: no referring, recommending or suggesting the services of a
person or entity **from which the licensee may receive compensation for a referral**, or **in which the
licensee has an interest**, unless the licensee **has disclosed that in writing.** The trigger is "may
receive", not "will receive".

**c. Disclosing of profits.** Where a licensee stands to profit from the transaction beyond the agreed
brokerage fee, the profit is disclosed.

**d. Disclosing of licensure.** A licensee dealing in their own account must **identify themselves as a
licensee** — which **§ 452.136(2)(c)** requires expressly in an advertisement for the occasional sale or
purchase of the licensee's own real estate.

And **§ 452.133(3)(a)** underlies all of it: no fee or compensation related to the transaction from
anyone other than the licensee's client or firm **without the prior written consent of all parties**.

## Hour 61 — Consumer protection: REEB 24.07

### 61.1 The structure — REEB 25.033(14)(a) to (f)

REEB 25.033(14) requires instruction on six provisions of **REEB 24.07**, and the structure of the rule
is worth learning even where its text is not quoted here:

chunks.heading: 61.2 What the six provisions do, and how they relate to the statute
chunks.excerpt:
**(1)(a) Property inspections.** REEB 25.033(14)(a).
**(1)(b) Inquiry by the listing firm.** REEB 25.033(14)(b).
**(2) Disclosure of material adverse facts.** REEB 25.033(14)(c).
**(3) Disclosure of material suggesting adverse material facts.** REEB 25.033(14)(d).
**(4) Disclosure of side agreements.** REEB 25.033(14)(e).
**(5) Reliance upon third parties.** REEB 25.033(14)(f).

**This course does not state the text of any of them**, because ch. REEB 24 has not been read from
primary text for this project. What it teaches is **what each provision is about, how it relates to
§ 452.133(1)(c), and what a licensee does** — and it instructs the student to read the rule.

### 61.2 What the six provisions do, and how they relate to the statute

**Wis. Stat. 452.133(1)(c)** and **REEB 24.07(2)** require timely written disclosure of known material adverse facts to parties who do not know or cannot discover them through reasonably vigilant observation, unless disclosure is prohibited by law. Apply the actual statutory wording rather than replacing it with a narrower “both conditions” test.

chunks.heading: 61.3 The practical method
chunks.excerpt:
**REEB 24.07(1)(a)–(d)** supplies the licensee-inspection framework: a reasonably competent and diligent inspection of accessible structures and immediate surroundings; before listing execution, inspection plus seller inquiry with a written response requested; and the other licensee's inspection before making a written proposal, subject to access and the party's instruction to submit before access. In that last case inspect promptly afterward if access is provided. The rule excludes specified invasive, obstructed, or hazardous activity, including moving furniture, opening panels, operating equipment, and entering hazardous areas. It does not turn a licensee into an engineer or home inspector.

**REEB 24.07(3) was repealed effective March 1, 2026 by CR 25-077.** Its former stand-alone “material suggesting adverse material facts” rule must not be taught as operative law. REEB 25.033(14)(d) still contains a reference to that repealed paragraph: preserve the curricular topic and explain this stale cross-reference, but use current operative duties for conduct.

**REEB 24.07(4)** requires timely written disclosure to the financing institution or other secured lender if the licensee knows the parties have not disclosed their entire agreement to that lender. It is not a blanket statement that every side agreement is forbidden.

**REEB 24.07(5)** allows reliance on a qualified third party's written property-condition report if copies are given timely to all parties. **(6)** separately requires timely written disclosure of a material inconsistency between the licensee's inspection and the seller's or third party's information. **(7)** prohibits knowingly giving false property information to parties or another licensee.

### 61.3 The practical method

chunks.heading: Hour 62 — Investigations, liability, and the seller's disclosure
chunks.excerpt:
Distinguish observed information from an unsupported diagnosis. If the firm knows a material adverse fact, apply 452.133(1)(c) and 24.07(2). If an inspection reveals a material inconsistency with a seller's or qualified third party's statement, apply 24.07(6). If the cause or significance is uncertain, apply reasonable skill and care and the competence rules, describe observations accurately, and obtain appropriate inspection or assistance rather than certifying a technical conclusion.

**The repeal of 24.07(3) does not repeal the other inspection, honesty, care, competence, and disclosure duties.** A stain alone does not automatically prove a structural defect; uncertainty is also not permission to ignore a known fact or materially contradictory evidence. Track the agreed investigation and notice deadlines without inventing an additional statutory deadline.

For a lender side-agreement issue, disclose the known omission timely in writing as required by 24.07(4). For reliance under (5), obtain the qualified third party's written report and give copies to all parties in a timely manner.

## Hour 62 — Investigations, liability, and the seller's disclosure

### 62.1 Disclosures and inspections by licensees under § 452.23 — REEB 25.033(14)(g)

**Wis. Stat. 452.23 is “Disclosures and inspections by brokers and salespersons.”** It is not a grant of the Department's power to investigate licensees. It prohibits disclosures that constitute the specified unlawful discrimination, addresses information a licensee need not disclose under its stated conditions, and addresses qualified third-party reports.

chunks.heading: 62.2 Civil liability for misrepresentation — REEB 25.033(14)(h)
chunks.excerpt:
Under **452.23(2)(b)**, a qualifying written third-party report provided to the person can remove the need for duplicate disclosure of information already disclosed there. Under **(3)** the licensee must disclose known facts that contradict such a report. Under **(4)** the licensee must exercise the care expected of a reasonably prudent person with the knowledge, skills, and training required for licensure. The statute's other exceptions and conditions must be checked in current text before being applied.

Board investigation and discipline are separate matters, including the applicable provisions of **452.14**. Preserve records and obtain appropriate advice for a real complaint; do not misidentify 452.23 as the disciplinary-investigation authority.

### 62.2 Civil liability for misrepresentation — REEB 25.033(14)(h)

Separate from Board discipline, a licensee and a firm can be **sued**.

**§ 452.139(2)** allocates responsibility: a **client is not liable** for a misrepresentation made by the
firm or its licensees **unless the client knew or should have known, or the firm or licensee is
repeating a misrepresentation made by the client**; and a firm is not liable for a **subagent's**
misrepresentation on the same conditions. **§ 452.139(2)(c)** preserves the firm's responsibility under
**s. 452.12(3)** for misrepresentations by its own associated licensees, and preserves a client's
liability for their own.

The exposure a licensee actually creates: **repeating the seller's statement as fact**. The moment a
licensee passes on "the roof is five years old" without attributing it and without qualification, the
statement becomes the firm's — and § 452.139(2)(a)'s protection for the client falls away precisely
because the licensee is repeating the client's misrepresentation.

chunks.heading: 62.3 Seller's disclosure duties under ch. 709 — REEB 25.033(14)(i)
chunks.excerpt:
The habit that prevents it: **attribute, qualify, and route.** *The seller states the roof was replaced
in 2019; I have not verified that; here is the permit record if one exists, and your inspector can
assess it.*

### 62.3 Seller's disclosure duties under ch. 709 — REEB 25.033(14)(i)

Wisconsin requires a seller of residential property, subject to the chapter's exemptions, to furnish a
**Real Estate Condition Report** — the form REEB 25.033(8)(f)10.a names.

**This course states no ch. 709 requirement, deadline, exemption or report item**, because the chapter
has not been read from primary text for this project.

What a licensee does, from Module WI-06 Hour 36.1: **give it to the seller and let the seller complete
it; do not coach toward "not aware"; read it as an investigation prompt list; deliver it as the
transaction requires; and update it when things change.**

**And the point that must not be missed: the seller's report does not discharge the firm's duty.**
**§ 452.133(1)(c)** requires the **firm** to disclose in writing material adverse facts **the firm**
knows. A seller's "not aware" is irrelevant to what the firm knows.

### Module WI-10 engagement check

**Question.** You list a house. The seller's condition report says "not aware" of any basement water. At
the first showing you notice efflorescence on the basement wall and a dehumidifier running, and the
seller mentions "the sump only runs in spring". A buyer's agent later asks you directly whether the
basement has ever taken water. Separately, your firm's marketing company has virtually removed the
neighbouring garage from the listing photographs. Work through everything.

**Expected answer.**

chunks.heading: Extended treatment — the conduct rules applied
chunks.excerpt:
**The observations call for careful inquiry, not a fabricated diagnosis.** Efflorescence, a running dehumidifier, and a statement that a sump operates in spring do not by themselves prove that the basement floods or establish the cause. Record the actual observations and seller statements, seek competent inspection, and avoid saying either that flooding is proved or that the property is defect-free. Disclose known material adverse facts under 452.133(1)(c) and 24.07(2), and materially inconsistent information under 24.07(6), where their conditions are met. The former 24.07(3) provision is repealed; it is not a current independent basis for the answer.

**When the buyer's agent asks me directly**, I answer honestly — **§ 452.133(1)(a)** — and in writing,
and I do not soften it. If the seller instructs me not to, that instruction is not one I may follow:
**§ 452.133(2)(c)** limits a client's orders to those **not inconsistent with another duty under ch.
452**, and (1)(c) is such a duty.

**The photographs are advertising that has been altered using technology to remove an element of the
property in a way that creates a false impression.** **§ 452.136(1)** already makes misleading
advertising a violation, and **§ 452.136(1m)** — created effective **1 January 2027 by 2025 Wis. Act
69** — will require the alteration to be **disclosed**. Either way the images come down or are disclosed,
and I take it to my **supervising broker**, who is responsible for advertising under
**§ 452.136(2)(b)**.

## Extended treatment — the conduct rules applied

### E10.1 An advertisement, audited line by line

chunks.heading: E10.1 An advertisement, audited line by line
chunks.excerpt:
*"JUST LISTED — stunning lakefront retreat, 150 ft of pristine frontage, priced to sell at $549,000 (or
best offer)! Perfect for empty nesters or a quiet couple. Walk to St. Mary's. Call Dana 555-0100.
#LakeLife"* — the property is listed by another firm, the frontage is 120 feet on the plat, the seller
agreed a price of $575,000, and the photograph has had a neighbouring shed removed digitally.

**"150 ft of pristine frontage" against 120 feet on the plat** — **§ 452.136(1)**, false or misleading
advertising, and a **§ 452.133(1)(a)** honesty problem toward every party.

**"$549,000 (or best offer)" against an agreed $575,000** — **§ 452.136(4)**: a licensee may not
advertise property at a price other than that agreed with the owner. A range or general terms are
permitted **only if they reflect the agreed price**.

**The property is another firm's listing** — **§ 452.136(3)**: a firm may not advertise a property
unless it is the listing firm or has the listing firm's consent.

**No firm name** — **§ 452.136(2)(a)**: the firm's name exactly as licensed, or a filed trade name, and
a clear indication that the firm is a business enterprise rather than a private party. **(2)(b)**: under
the firm's supervision and in the firm's name, **clear and conspicuous**.

**The digitally removed shed** — **§ 452.136(1)** now, because an altered image creating a false
impression is misleading advertising; and **§ 452.136(1m)** from **1 January 2027**, which will require
the alteration to be **disclosed**.

**"Perfect for empty nesters or a quiet couple"** — a preference on **familial status** and, depending on
the reading, age. Describe the property, never the occupants.

chunks.heading: E10.2 Steering, recognised in ordinary conversation
chunks.excerpt:
**"Walk to St. Mary's"** — a reference to a place of worship. Wisconsin's own list under **s. 106.50** has
not been read for this course and no state rule is stated; the practice answer is that describing
proximity to a landmark is different from describing the community, and the safe formulation names
distance rather than affinity.

**A compliant rewrite:** *"Lakefront home, 120 feet of frontage, offered at $575,000. [Firm's licensed
name], [office contact information]. Contact Dana, 555-0100."* — posted only if the firm is the listing
firm or has the listing firm's written consent, and with any digital alteration disclosed.

### E10.2 Steering, recognised in ordinary conversation

Steering rarely arrives as a decision. It arrives as an answer.

*"Which schools are better?"* → Name the source — the district's own published data — and offer to show
everything meeting the buyer's criteria. Do not rank neighbourhoods.

*"Would we fit in there?"* → Ask what matters to them about a neighbourhood — commute, lot size, price,
walkability — and answer on those. Do not answer on who lives there.

*"Is it safe?"* → Name the municipality's published crime statistics. Do not characterise.

*"We'd like to be near people like us."* → Record the objective criteria they actually name and search on
those. Do not infer a protected characteristic and do not act on one.

*A licensee's own convenience* — showing only properties in areas they know well — becomes steering the
moment it correlates with a protected characteristic. **Record the buyer's criteria in the buyer's own
words** and show against them.

### E10.3 Material adverse facts: a working method

chunks.heading: E10.4 What a complaint file looks like
chunks.excerpt:
The current statutory test in 452.133(1)(c) concerns a material adverse fact the firm knows and that the party does not know **or** cannot discover through reasonably vigilant observation, unless disclosure is prohibited by law. Do not silently rewrite the statute's connector or assume that any visible clue resolves all hidden aspects of a known condition.

Classify the actual fact, the firm's knowledge, the recipient's information, and the required form and timing of disclosure. Distinguish that analysis from an uncertain observation that requires reasonable care and competent follow-up. REEB 24.07(3) was repealed on March 1, 2026; current 24.07(1), (2), (5), and (6), and 24.03 continue to govern their respective issues.

### E10.4 What a complaint file looks like

When a Board complaint arrives, the licensee's file either answers it or does not. What answers it:

**Contemporaneous notes** with dates, times and channels. **Every written disclosure**, with the date
given. **Every § 452.135 disclosure**, delivered and evidenced. **The referral record** — who was named,
when, in what form. **The advertising record**, including any timely written request to a third party who
controls a platform. **Every offer and its presentation**, with dates. **The trust account ledger** for
the transaction. And **the correspondence.**

What does not answer it: a reconstruction, a recollection, or an assertion that the licensee "always"
does something.

**And the response itself:** notify the supervising broker immediately; preserve everything and change
nothing; do not contact the complainant to argue; respond within the time given; obtain counsel.

notes that local ordinances may protect further classes, and instructs the licensee to read the current
list directly. Sections 106.50(1m)(h), (2), (2m), and the displayed (2r) text were read on 2026-09-06; no claim is made that every exemption or enforcement provision was exhaustively reviewed.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WI-10
chunks.excerpt:
**Deliberately not stated, for want of a primary reading:** any requirement, deadline, exemption or item
from **ch. 709**; the procedures, sanctions and penalties in **§§ 452.14 and 452.23**; **s. 452.12(3)**,
**s. 452.30(6)**; and the federal accessible design and construction technical standards.

Federal statements — the Fair Housing Act's seven classes, the Civil Rights Act of 1866 and *Jones v.
Alfred H. Mayer Co.*, the accommodation and modification framework, the ADA's scope, Do Not Call,

lessons.title: Wisconsin Salesperson Pre-License — Module WI-11

chunks.heading: Wisconsin Salesperson Pre-License — Module WI-11
chunks.excerpt:
# Wisconsin Salesperson Pre-License — Module WI-11

## Hours 63–66 · Leases and property management

**Board topics covered:** REEB 25.033(15) Leases · REEB 25.033(16) Property Management
**Clock hours:** 4 · **Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Board review.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Wisconsin pre-license credit is available.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this module the student will be able to:

- Classify a leasehold estate and name the standard provisions a lease settles.
- Distinguish assignment from sublease and say who remains liable.
- Name the ATCP 134 sections REEB 25.033(15)(h) requires and say what each governs.
- Describe a property manager's functions and the management agreement's essential terms.
- Explain trust accounting for rents and security deposits in a Wisconsin managed portfolio.
- Identify the risk-management controls a managed property requires.

## Timed sequence

| Hour | Content | Evidence |
|---:|---|---|
| 63 | Leasehold estates; standard provisions; lease documents | Section completed |
| 64 | Legal principles; improvements; maintenance; breach | Section completed |
| 65 | Residential rental practices under ATCP 134 | Section completed |
| 66 | Property management: functions, agreement, considerations, risk | Module engagement check |
| **Total** | **4 clock hours** | |

---

## Hour 63 — Leasehold estates and lease documents

### 63.1 The four leasehold estates — REEB 25.033(15)(a)

**Estate for years** — a fixed term with a definite beginning and end. It **expires without notice**, and
its length is irrelevant to the name: a two-week lease is an estate for years.

chunks.heading: 63.2 A lease is two things at once — REEB 25.033(15)(d)
chunks.excerpt:
**Periodic estate** — renews automatically for successive periods until one party gives notice.
Month-to-month tenancies are the common case.

**Estate at will** — possession with consent, no fixed period, terminable by either party subject to
statutory notice.

**Estate at sufferance** — a tenant who entered lawfully and stayed past the term without consent.
Distinguished from trespass only by the lawful entry, and removing such a tenant is a **legal process**,
not a self-help matter.

### 63.2 A lease is two things at once — REEB 25.033(15)(d)

A lease is a **conveyance** — it transfers a leasehold estate and the right of exclusive possession —
and a **contract** — it creates mutual promises. The first explains why a tenant may exclude even the
landlord except as the lease and the law allow; the second explains how breach is analysed.

A lease of stated length is a **conveyance** for the purposes of **ch. 706**, which is why the writing
and signature requirements Module WI-07 named reach leases as well as deeds.

### 63.3 Standard provisions — REEB 25.033(15)(b) and lease documents (15)(c)

chunks.heading: Hour 64 — Legal principles, improvements, maintenance, breach
chunks.excerpt:
A Wisconsin residential lease settles: the **parties**; the **premises**, including any storage, parking
or garage; the **term**; the **rent**, its amount, due date, place and method, and any late fee; the
**security deposit** and its treatment; **utilities**, and in a Wisconsin climate specifically **who pays
for heat**; **permitted use and occupancy limits**; **maintenance** responsibilities on each side; the
**landlord's right of entry** and the notice required; rules on **pets** — and separately the treatment
of **assistance animals**, which are not pets; **snow removal and lawn care**, allocated expressly;
**alterations**; **assignment and subletting**; **default and remedies**; **renewal or termination**; and
the **required disclosures**.

**Two Wisconsin documents belong with the lease** and are governed by ATCP 134, which Hour 65 takes:
the **check-in and check-out condition report** the tenant is entitled to complete, and the
**nonstandard rental provisions** document by which certain terms must be separately identified and
agreed rather than buried in the lease.

---

## Hour 64 — Legal principles, improvements, maintenance, breach

### 64.1 Assignment and sublease

**Assignment** transfers the tenant's **entire** remaining interest; the assignee comes into direct
relationship with the landlord. **Sublease** transfers **less than** the entire remaining interest — a
shorter period or part of the premises — and the original tenant becomes a landlord to the subtenant
while remaining a tenant to the landlord.

**In neither case is the original tenant automatically released.** Release requires the landlord's
agreement, which is a **novation**. A tenant who "assigned the lease and moved out" remains liable unless
the landlord released them in writing.

chunks.heading: 64.2 Improvements — REEB 25.033(15)(e)
chunks.excerpt:
Most leases restrict both and require consent.

### 64.2 Improvements — REEB 25.033(15)(e)

**Trade fixtures** installed by a tenant for the tenant's trade or business remain the tenant's personal
property and must be removed before the term ends — after which they generally pass to the landlord by
**accession**.

**Tenant improvements** in a commercial lease are negotiated: who builds, who pays, what allowance the
landlord gives, what standard applies, and what happens at the end of the term.

**Alterations in a residential tenancy** are governed by the lease — and by the **reasonable
modification** rules from Module WI-10 Hour 57.2 where a disability is involved, under which the change
is at the tenant's expense and the landlord may where reasonable require restoration.

### 64.3 Maintenance — REEB 25.033(15)(f)

The allocation is a lease term sitting on a statutory floor. The landlord's obligations as to the
condition of the premises, and the tenant's as to their own conduct and the unit's care, are set by
Wisconsin law and cannot be reduced below the floor by agreement.

**This course states no Wisconsin habitability standard or repair obligation**, because the governing
provisions have not been read from primary text for this project.

What is certain and belongs to practice: **the record of what was reported and what was done is the
whole of the defence** in a habitability dispute. A request-to-completion tracking system with defined
response times, vendor accountability, and an escalation trigger when a scheduled visit does not happen
is not administration — it is the evidence.

### 64.4 Breach — REEB 25.033(15)(g)

chunks.heading: Hour 65 — Residential rental practices under ATCP 134
chunks.excerpt:
**Self-help is unlawful.** Changing locks, removing possessions, or shutting off utilities to force a
tenant out is prohibited, and a licensee who advises a landlord client to do any of it has advised a
violation — against **§ 452.133(1)(b)**'s reasonable skill and care and against the licensee's duty to
comply with the law.

Possession is recovered through a **statutory judicial process**, and **this course states no notice
period, no cure right and no procedure**, because the provisions have not been read from primary text
for this project. They must be read from the current statutes, and where the consequence of getting it
wrong is the loss of a remedy, confirmed with counsel.

**A tenant's remedies** for a landlord's breach likewise come from statute and from the lease, and a
licensee does not advise on whether rent may be withheld.

---

## Hour 65 — Residential rental practices under ATCP 134

### 65.1 What ATCP 134 is — REEB 25.033(15)(h)

**Ch. ATCP 134** is the Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection's rule on
**residential rental practices**, and REEB 25.033(15)(h) requires instruction on **ATCP 134.02, 134.06
and 134.09** specifically.

It is a **consumer protection rule**, which means two things a licensee must understand: a violation can
be enforced by DATCP and can support a private action, **independently of** anything the Real Estate
Examining Board does; and its requirements apply to a residential rental whether or not a licensee is
involved.

The targeted ATCP 134.07–.09 provisions were read on 2026-09-06. No comprehensive review of every deposit rule, exemption, or remedy is claimed. What follows is what each cited section governs and what a licensee
must therefore do.

### 65.2 The three sections the rule names

chunks.heading: 65.3 What ATCP 134 requires a licensee to do
chunks.excerpt:
The curriculum specifically names **ATCP 134.02 (definitions), 134.06 (security deposits), and 134.09 (prohibited practices)**. Those topics remain part of this hour. Identify the applicable defined terms under .02 and consult .06 for the actual deposit deductions, accounting, and return requirements; no unverified return period is supplied here.

**ATCP 134.07 — Promises to repair (additional applied instruction).** A repair promise must specify the completion date or time period. Promises made before the initial rental agreement must be in writing. The rule addresses timely notice of delays due to causes beyond the landlord's control; it is not permission to promise a repair without a completion commitment.

**ATCP 134.08 — Prohibited rental-agreement provisions.** The section identifies provisions that make a rental agreement void. Read the actual text and applicable law before advising on a disputed clause; an owner cannot use a private form to contract around every tenant protection.

**ATCP 134.09 — Prohibited practices.** Among its restrictions, paragraph (7) forbids self-help eviction outside the judicial eviction process. A manager does not remove doors, lock out a tenant, or use other self-help measures in lieu of that process. The section also addresses entry, automatic renewal, retaliation, and late fees; this lesson does not replace review of the exact provision for a real dispute.

### 65.3 What ATCP 134 requires a licensee to do

**Read it.** A Wisconsin property manager who has not read ATCP 134.02, 134.06 and 134.09 in current
text is managing without knowing the rules that generate most of the complaints.

chunks.heading: Hour 66 — Property management
chunks.excerpt:
**Use compliant documents.** The check-in and check-out condition report, the nonstandard rental
provisions document, and the required disclosures are ATCP 134's, and using an out-of-state lease form
in Wisconsin is how a manager creates violations wholesale.

**Handle deposits by the rule, not by habit.** The amount that may be withheld, the itemisation the
tenant receives, and the deadline are prescribed. **A remembered figure is how a landlord loses.**

**Screen by written, objective, uniform criteria** applied identically — which is the fair housing
answer from Module WI-10 Hour 57.5 and the consumer-protection answer at the same time.

**And never advise on a specific ATCP question from memory.** The method: classify the tenancy, read the
current section, read the lease, and refer the legal conclusion.

---

## Hour 66 — Property management

### 66.1 Functions of a property manager — REEB 25.033(16)(a)

A property manager is engaged to **operate real property**: to produce the income the owner wants, to
preserve the asset, and to do both within the law.

The functions: **leasing** — marketing, screening, and executing leases; **rent collection** and
delinquency management; **maintenance**, routine and emergency; **vendor management**; **accounting and
reporting** to the owner; **budgeting**; **compliance** with fair housing, ATCP 134, local ordinances and
the licensing law; **risk management**; and **records**.

**Property management is brokerage.** A person managing real property for another for compensation is
providing brokerage services, and the firm's **§ 452.133** duties apply — including the seven owed to
**every party**, which in a managed property means **the tenants as well as the owner.**

chunks.heading: 66.2 The management agreement — REEB 25.033(16)(b)
chunks.excerpt:
That is worth stating plainly, because managers frequently assume the tenant is nobody to them. In
Wisconsin the tenant is a **party**, owed honesty and fairness, reasonable skill and care, written
disclosure of material adverse facts, confidentiality that survives, accurate market information,
safeguarding of trust funds, and objective presentation of proposals.

### 66.2 The management agreement — REEB 25.033(16)(b)

It is an **agency agreement**, so **§ 452.135(2)(a)** requires the **Disclosure to Clients** **not later
than the time the firm enters into it**.

Its essential terms: the **parties and the property**; the **term**; the **scope of authority** — what
the manager may spend without approval and the threshold above which the owner decides; **leasing
authority** and the criteria to be applied; **rent collection and enforcement** authority; **maintenance
and emergency** authority; **compensation** — the management fee, any leasing fee, and how each is
calculated and paid; the **reporting package** and its frequency; **insurance** requirements on both
sides; **indemnification**; **handling of the owner's funds and of tenant deposits**; and
**termination**.

### 66.3 Trust accounting — where managers lose licences

**§ 452.133(1)(f)** requires the firm to **safeguard trust funds and other property held**, as required
by rules under **s. 452.13(5)**, and **ch. REEB 18** governs trust accounts — Module WI-13.

Safeguarding and accounting principles, applied with the actual REEB 18 exceptions:

chunks.heading: 66.4 Management considerations and the operating statement — REEB 25.033(16)(c)
chunks.excerpt:
**One owner's money is never used for another owner's property.** A pooled trust account may be
permitted; a **pooled ledger** is not. Every owner and every deposit has its own running balance, and
sufficiency is measured against the **sum of the ledgers**, not against the bank balance.

**Security deposits are not automatically earned owner income.** REEB 18.031(4) concerns a licensee who has an ownership interest in the rental property: those deposits go in a real-estate trust account or an owner account provided for in the lease. Separately, paragraph (5)(b) permits direct deposit of rental application deposits, rents, and security deposits payable to one or more owners into the owner account; disbursements by the firm or associated licensee need the owner's written authorization. Those conditions do not authorize deposit in the firm's operating account. See Module WI-13 for the distinction.

**Reconcile monthly** — bank statement to book balance to the sum of the individual ledgers — and retain
the reconciliation. A reconciliation that has never been performed is what an audit finds.

### 66.4 Management considerations and the operating statement — REEB 25.033(16)(c)

The manager builds an annual budget on the Module WI-09 structure: **potential gross income**, less
**vacancy and collection loss**, giving **effective gross income**; less **operating expenses**, giving
**net operating income**. **Debt service and capital expenditures sit outside NOI**; **replacement
reserves** are inside it.

Reporting to the owner, monthly: rent roll and occupancy; collections and delinquency; income and
expense against budget; the **trust account balance and the owner's ledger**; maintenance completed and
outstanding; and lease expirations coming up.

chunks.heading: 66.5 Renting and maintaining the property — REEB 25.033(16)(d)
chunks.excerpt:
**Treating a capital item as an operating expense understates NOI and misstates value**, which is why
the distinction matters beyond bookkeeping.

### 66.5 Renting and maintaining the property — REEB 25.033(16)(d)

**Marketing** under **§ 452.136** and REEB 24.04, with the fair housing rule from Module WI-10 Hour
57.5: describe the property, never the occupants.

**Screening** by written, objective, uniform criteria applied identically to every applicant, documented
for each — the only defensible practice under both fair housing law and ATCP 134.

**Leasing** on documents that comply with ATCP 134, with the check-in condition report completed.

**Maintenance** on a tracked request-to-completion path with defined response times, current vendor
insurance certificates on file, and an escalation trigger.

**Turnover** with a documented check-out inspection and a deposit accounting that follows **ATCP
134.06** rather than habit.

### 66.6 Risk management — REEB 25.033(16)(e)

**Written policies**, and a manager who knows what the firm's are.

**Documentation**, contemporaneous rather than reconstructed. A decision log entry records the date and
time, who said what by what channel, what was decided, **on what authority** — statute, rule, lease,
management agreement, or the owner's written instruction — who was notified, and the next step and its
date.

**Insurance** — the owner's property and liability coverage, the manager's own errors and omissions
coverage, and vendor certificates.

**Unlicensed assistants** — who may do administration and may not perform licensed activity.

**Escalation** to the supervising broker that people actually use.

chunks.heading: Module WI-11 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**And the duty that most often surprises a manager: § 452.133(1)(c) is owed to tenants.** A material
adverse fact about the physical condition of the property that the firm knows and a prospective tenant
cannot discover through reasonably vigilant observation must be **timely disclosed in writing** — to
them, not only to the owner.

### Module WI-11 engagement check

**Question.** You manage a twelve-unit building. A tenant reports that the furnace in unit 6 is failing;
you schedule a vendor who does not attend, and nothing further happens for three weeks. The owner's
ledger holds $1,900 and the replacement quote is $6,400. The owner is unreachable. A prospective tenant
for unit 9 asks whether the building has any problems. Work through it.

**Expected answer.**

**The maintenance failure is the case.** What was reported, when, by what channel, what was done, and
when — and a text message seen and not logged is the failure that decides a habitability dispute. I log
everything retrospectively with dates and sources, get the heat working, write to the owner, and escalate
to my **supervising broker**. Whether the tenant has a remedy is a **legal** question I do not answer.

**I may not pay the $6,400 from the trust account.** The owner's ledger holds $1,900, and spending
$4,500 of other owners' and tenants' money is **conversion** — the trust account's balance must be
sufficient at all times against the **sum of the ledgers**, not the bank balance. **§ 452.133(1)(f)**
requires trust funds to be safeguarded as the rules under **s. 452.13(5)** require. The management
agreement should have fixed the emergency spending threshold and the procedure in advance; if it has
not, that is the conversation to have with the owner and the broker now.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WI-11
chunks.excerpt:
**The prospective tenant for unit 9 is a party**, and **§ 452.133(1)(c)** requires the firm to **timely
disclose in writing** material adverse facts the firm knows that the party cannot discover through
reasonably vigilant observation. A failing furnace in unit 6 is not necessarily a material adverse fact
about unit 9 — but a building-wide heating problem, a systemic maintenance backlog, or anything
affecting unit 9's habitability is, and I must not answer the question with a reassurance I cannot
support. **§ 452.133(1)(a)** requires honesty and fairness to every party, and the tenant is one.

**And the screening of that prospective tenant** proceeds on the firm's **written, objective, uniform
criteria**, applied identically, documented — under fair housing law and under **ATCP 134.09**, which I
read in current text rather than recall.

---

## Instructor source note for Module WI-11

Wisconsin statements rest on text read directly from `docs.legis.wisconsin.gov` on 2026-08-20 and
recorded in `wisconsin/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`: **REEB 25.033(15)(a) through (h)** and
**(16)(a) through (e)**; and **§ 452.133(1)(a), (1)(b), (1)(c) and (1)(f)**, **§ 452.135(2)(a)**, and
**§ 452.136**.

The targeted ATCP 134.07–.09 primary-text review of 2026-09-06 supersedes the original unread-source limitation for those provisions. Hour 65 names **ATCP 134.02, 134.06 and 134.09** as REEB
25.033(15)(h) requires, states what each governs from its own rule title, explains why the rule matters
independently of the Board, and instructs the student to read the current text. **An instructor
supplementing this hour with a deposit figure or a deadline must obtain ch. ATCP 134 and date the
reading.**

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WI-11
chunks.excerpt:
**Deliberately not stated, for want of a primary reading:** Wisconsin's **habitability and repair**
obligations; the **eviction** notice periods, cure rights and procedure; **ch. REEB 18** trust account
requirements, which Module WI-13 names; and **s. 452.13(5)**.

**That the seven § 452.133(1) duties are owed to tenants as parties** is stated deliberately and
twice — at 66.1 and at 66.6 — because property managers commonly assume the tenant is owed nothing, and
in Wisconsin the tenant is a party to whom the firm provides brokerage services.

chunks.heading: Wisconsin Salesperson Pre-License — Module WI-12
chunks.excerpt:
# Wisconsin Salesperson Pre-License — Module WI-12

## Hours 67–69 · Land use control and environmental concerns

**Board topics covered:** REEB 25.033(17) Land use control and development · REEB 25.033(18)
Environmental concerns
**Clock hours:** 3 · **Hour allocation:** a StateCourse proposal for Board review.
**Course version:** 1.0 submission draft
**Regulatory status:** Development. Not approved. No Wisconsin pre-license credit is available.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this module the student will be able to:

- Distinguish public from private land-use control and say who enforces each.
- Explain the comprehensive plan, zoning, and the relief mechanisms.
- Describe Wisconsin subdivision regulation and the certified survey map.
- Name every environmental topic REEB 25.033(18) requires and the office that answers it.
- Route a flood, wetland, tank or farmland question correctly and record the routing.

## Timed sequence

| Hour | Content | Evidence |
|---:|---|---|
| 67 | Public controls; the comprehensive plan; zoning; building codes | Section completed |
| 68 | Subdivision regulation; land development; subdividing; private controls | Section completed |
| 69 | Environmental concerns and the disclosure documents | Module engagement check |
| **Total** | **3 clock hours** | |

---

## Hour 67 — Public controls, planning, zoning, and codes

### 67.1 Public controls — REEB 25.033(17)(a)

Every public limitation traces to the four powers of Module WI-04 Hour 18.1. **Police power** is the
source of everything in this module: zoning, subdivision control, building codes, shoreland and
floodplain regulation, and environmental permitting — none of which is compensated, because use is
regulated rather than taken.

chunks.heading: 67.2 The comprehensive plan — REEB 25.033(17)(b)
chunks.excerpt:
Wisconsin delegates the power to **counties, cities, villages and towns**, and the allocation between
them is itself a Wisconsin feature: **county zoning** governs in many unincorporated areas, **town**
authority varies with whether the town has adopted village powers and whether the county's ordinance
applies, and **shoreland zoning** is **county-administered** even inside some municipal boundaries.

**So the first question about any Wisconsin parcel is: which body regulates it?** A licensee who calls
the city about a property in the town has called the wrong office.

### 67.2 The comprehensive plan — REEB 25.033(17)(b)

**Amended by CR 23-075**, effective 9-1-24, and the version taught is the amended one.

Wisconsin requires local governments that exercise land-use authority to act **consistently with a
comprehensive plan** containing prescribed elements — housing, transportation, utilities and community
facilities, agricultural and natural resources, economic development, intergovernmental cooperation,
land use, and implementation.

Two consequences for brokerage. The plan is a **public document** stating where a community intends
growth, infrastructure and change — which is information a buyer of land or of a property whose value
depends on its surroundings should have. And **zoning must be consistent with it**, which makes the plan
evidence about the likelihood of a rezoning succeeding.

### 67.3 Zoning — REEB 25.033(17)(c)

Zoning divides a jurisdiction into districts and prescribes for each the permitted **uses** and the
**bulk** controls — minimum lot size, width and frontage, setbacks, height, lot coverage, impervious
surface, parking and often signage.

**The relief mechanisms, distinguished:**

chunks.heading: 67.4 Building codes — REEB 25.033(17)(f)
chunks.excerpt:
A **variance** relieves a **dimensional** requirement where strict application causes **unnecessary
hardship** arising from the property itself — shape, topography, soils. It is granted by the **board of
adjustment or appeals**. **A variance does not authorise a use the district forbids**, and self-created
hardship and mere financial disadvantage are not grounds. Wisconsin's unnecessary-hardship standard is
applied strictly, and **this course states no element of it**.

A **conditional use permit** authorises a use the ordinance **lists as permissible subject to review and
conditions**. It is the ordinance operating as written, not an exception to it.

A **nonconforming use or structure** was lawful when established and became non-compliant on a later
ordinance change. It may generally continue, typically may not be **expanded**, and may be lost on
**abandonment or destruction**.

**In Wisconsin the nonconforming-structure question is acute on waterfront**, where a very large share of
the shoreland housing stock predates current setbacks. What may be done to such a structure — expanded,
replaced, rebuilt after a loss, relocated — is governed by **county shoreland zoning** and by state
minimum standards, and the answer differs between counties.

A **rezoning** amends the ordinance itself and is a **legislative** act of the governing body.

### 67.4 Building codes — REEB 25.033(17)(f)

Wisconsin administers a **statewide uniform dwelling code** for one- and two-family dwellings, and a
commercial building code, through the Department of Safety and Professional Services and delegated
municipal inspectors.

chunks.heading: 67.5 The licensee's boundary
chunks.excerpt:
Practical consequences: **new construction requires permits and inspections**, and the **certificate of
occupancy** (where issued) is the document saying the building may lawfully be occupied. **An unpermitted
addition** is a code problem, a title and insurance problem, and a financing problem at once — and it is
discovered from the **building inspector's file**, not from the seller.

### 67.5 The licensee's boundary

Every question in this hour is answered by a public official and recorded in a public office. The
licensee's job is to know **that the question exists**, know **who answers it**, and send the client
there **in writing**.

**§ 452.133(2)(am)** limits advice to matters within the scope of the knowledge, skills and training
required under ch. 452, and zoning is outside it. **REEB 24.03**, competence in area of service, says the
same as a rule. Answering a zoning question from memory is how licensees create liability.

---

## Hour 68 — Subdivision, development, and private controls

### 68.1 Subdivision regulation — REEB 25.033(17)(d)

Wisconsin regulates the division of land at state and local level. **Ch. 236** is the state platting
statute, and municipalities and counties administer their own subdivision ordinances alongside it.

Two instruments a licensee must distinguish:

**A subdivision plat** — the instrument creating a subdivision as the statute defines it, reviewed by the
local approving authorities and by state agencies, and **recorded**.

**A certified survey map (CSM)** — Wisconsin's instrument for **smaller divisions**, prepared by a
surveyor, approved locally, and **recorded**. A great many Wisconsin parcels are described by reference
to a CSM, and a CSM is the ordinary route for splitting off a lot from a larger parcel.

chunks.heading: 68.2 Land development and subdividing — REEB 25.033(17)(g) and (h)
chunks.excerpt:
**A lot does not exist until the plat or CSM creating it is recorded**, and **an unlawful division is a
title and marketability problem** — which is why a seller asking whether they can "just split off five
acres" is asking a question for the municipality, the county, and a surveyor, in writing, and never for
the licensee.

**This course states no lot count, acreage threshold, or time period from ch. 236 or from any local
ordinance**, because they have not been read from primary text for this project.

### 68.2 Land development and subdividing — REEB 25.033(17)(g) and (h)

The sequence: concept and feasibility; **comprehensive plan consistency and zoning**; preliminary plat or
CSM; **engineering and public improvement plans** for streets, water, sewer and stormwater; **state and
county permits** — erosion control, stormwater, wetland, floodplain, driveway access; **construction of
improvements**, usually secured by a bond or letter of credit; **final plat or CSM recorded**; and
**dedication** of streets and utilities.

The feasibility questions that decide a Wisconsin land deal, each with its office: **zoning and permitted
use** — the municipality or county, in writing; **subdivision status** — the approving authority;
**wastewater capacity**, which on unsewered land means **soil testing and a septic permit** through the
county; **water supply**; **access**, including a **driveway or entrance permit** from the town, county
or state highway authority; **wetlands, floodplain and shoreland**; **farmland preservation zoning**;
and **utility availability**, where "available" is not the same as "permitted".

### 68.3 Private land-use controls — REEB 25.033(17)(e)

chunks.heading: Hour 69 — Environmental concerns
chunks.excerpt:
Module WI-04 Hour 19.4 set them out: **restrictive covenants**, recorded so they bind successors,
enforced **privately** by an association or a neighbour rather than by the municipality, and capable of
being **stricter than zoning** — in which case the owner must satisfy both.

**Discriminatory covenants are void and must not be honoured.**

**Associations** — condominium, planned community, road and lake associations — hold both the enforcement
power and the assessment power, and a buyer needs the documents, the budget, the reserve position, the
minutes and the assessment history.

---

## Hour 69 — Environmental concerns

### 69.1 The ten current topics — REEB 25.033(18)

The rule requires instruction on **radon**, **asbestos**, **lead-based paint**, **toxic waste**,
**underground storage tanks under ch. ATCP 93**, **floodplains under s. 87.30 Stats. and ss. NR 116.01
and 116.06**, **flood insurance**, **wetlands under s. 23.32**, **farmland preservation under ss. 91.01
and 91.60 to 91.70**, and **disclosure documents** under **REEB 24.07** and ch. 709.
**Paragraph (18)(j) was repealed by CR 19-128**, effective 2-1-21, and is not taught.

**None of ATCP 93, s. 87.30, NR 116, s. 23.32 or ch. 91 has been read from primary text for this
project, and no requirement, threshold, distance or exemption from any of them is stated.** What follows
is what each topic is, why it matters in Wisconsin, and **who answers it**.

### 69.2 The topics, and the routing

**Radon — (18)(a).** A naturally occurring gas, common in Wisconsin soils, measured by testing and
addressed by mitigation, which is a defined trade. **Test in the inspection period; a certified tester
answers it.**

chunks.heading: 69.2 The topics, and the routing
chunks.excerpt:
**Asbestos — (18)(b).** In insulation, flooring, siding, pipe wrap and textured finishes in older
housing. **A qualified assessor answers it, and disturbing it is regulated work.**

**Lead-based paint — (18)(c).** **Target housing built before 1978**: federal disclosure of known paint
and hazards, available records and reports, the EPA pamphlet, the prescribed contract warning and
acknowledgments, and — **for sales** — a **ten-day** opportunity to conduct a risk assessment or
inspection unless the parties agree otherwise in writing. The federal **Renovation, Repair and Painting**
rule requires certified firms for disturbing painted surfaces in target housing.

**Toxic waste — (18)(d).** Contamination from historic industrial, agricultural or commercial use.
Wisconsin's remediation and closure programmes are administered by the **Department of Natural
Resources**, and a property with a known or suspected release is an environmental consultant's and
counsel's question — never a licensee's.

**Underground storage tanks under ch. ATCP 93 — (18)(e).** Buried heating oil and fuel tanks are a
Wisconsin legacy issue. An abandoned tank never properly removed or closed is an environmental liability
attaching to the property. **The Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection administers
ATCP 93**, and a suspected tank goes there and to a qualified contractor.

**Floodplains — (18)(f).** **s. 87.30 Stats.** and **NR 116.01 and 116.06** are the state floodplain
provisions; municipalities administer floodplain zoning. **Whether a parcel is in a mapped floodplain,
and what may be built or altered there, is answered by the municipality and by the mapping — in
writing.**

chunks.heading: 69.3 The rule that governs the whole hour
chunks.excerpt:
**Flood insurance — (18)(g).** **Flood is excluded from a standard homeowners policy.** Coverage comes
from the **National Flood Insurance Program** or the private market. A property in a **Special Flood
Hazard Area** faces a **lender requirement** on a federally regulated or insured loan. **Maps change**,
being outside a mapped area is not the same as not flooding, and NFIP coverage has limits and a waiting
period. An insurance professional and FEMA's mapping answer it.

**Wetlands — (18)(h).** **s. 23.32** is the wetland provision, and the **Department of Natural
Resources** administers wetland identification and permitting. A wetland can make a physically buildable
parcel unbuildable, and its presence is answered by mapping and by a **wetland delineation**.

**Farmland preservation — (18)(i).** **ss. 91.01 and 91.60 to 91.70.** Wisconsin's farmland preservation
programme ties **county farmland preservation zoning** and **farmland preservation agreements** to
income tax credits, and it restricts non-agricultural use and division of enrolled land. **The county
land conservation department and the Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection answer
it**, and a buyer of enrolled land must understand the restriction and any consequence of withdrawal
**before closing** — which makes it a **contract term**, not an afterthought.

**Disclosure documents — (18)(k).** **REEB 24.07** and **ch. 709**, from Module WI-10 Hours 61 and 62.3.

### 69.3 The rule that governs the whole hour

chunks.heading: Module WI-12 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**The licensee is not the person who determines an environmental condition.** The licensee is the person
who **knows the question exists, discloses what the firm actually knows, and routes the question to the
office or professional who answers it — in writing, with the contingency deadline stated.**

**§ 452.133(1)(c)** requires timely **written** disclosure of material adverse facts the firm knows and
the party does not know or cannot discover through reasonably vigilant observation, subject to the statutory disclosure exception. **REEB 24.07(3) was repealed on March 1, 2026.** Apply the continuing inspection, disclosure, and inconsistency duties under 24.07(1), (2), and (6), and reasonable care and competence under 452.133(1)(b) and 24.03. Do not infer a technical environmental diagnosis from an unexplained observation or exceed the licensee's actual competence.

### Module WI-12 engagement check

**Question.** A buyer is under contract on 22 acres with a 1961 farmhouse, an old barn, a pole shed with
a rusted tank behind it, and a low wet area at the back that "dries out by July". The parcel is in county
farmland preservation zoning and the buyer intends to split off five acres for a second house. Build the
investigation list.

**Expected answer.** Every line names the question, the office, and the document.

chunks.heading: Module WI-12 engagement check
chunks.excerpt:
**The split.** Whether five acres can be divided off is a **subdivision** question under **ch. 236** and
the county or town ordinance, and it is compounded by **farmland preservation zoning** under
**ss. 91.01 and 91.60 to 91.70**, which restricts non-agricultural use and division of enrolled land.
**County zoning, the county land conservation department, and DATCP — in writing.** And the answer may
carry a consequence for any **farmland preservation agreement** and its tax credits, which makes it a
**contract term** the buyer must resolve before closing.

**The wet area.** Potential **wetland** under **s. 23.32**, answered by DNR mapping and, if it matters, a
**wetland delineation**. A wetland can make the intended building site unbuildable, and "dries out by
July" is not a determination.

**The rusted tank.** Potential **underground or above-ground storage tank** under **ch. ATCP 93** —
DATCP and a qualified contractor — and, if there has been a release, a **DNR** remediation question and
an environmental consultant.

**The 1961 farmhouse.** Pre-1978 **target housing**: the federal **lead-based paint** disclosure,
records, pamphlet, contract acknowledgments, and the **ten-day** assessment opportunity. Plus
**asbestos** and **radon** testing in the inspection period.

**The second house.** **Wastewater** — soil testing and a **septic permit** through the county — and
**water supply**, **driveway access** and a possible **entrance permit**, and **zoning** for a second
dwelling on the parcel.

**Floodplain** status under **s. 87.30** and **NR 116** from the municipality and the mapping, and
**flood insurance** availability from an insurance professional.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WI-12
chunks.excerpt:
**And what I disclose:** whatever the firm actually knows, **in writing**, under **§ 452.133(1)(c)** —
and I record and investigate the tank and wet-area observations under the current care, inspection, and competence duties. The observations are not a license to invent a diagnosis. The former 24.07(3) is repealed; disclose established facts and material inconsistencies under the provisions that remain operative.

---

## Instructor source note for Module WI-12

Wisconsin statements rest on text read directly from `docs.legis.wisconsin.gov` on 2026-08-20 and
recorded in `wisconsin/regulatory/primary-text-readings.md`: **REEB 25.033(17)(a) through (h)** and
**(18)(a) through (k)**, including the note that **(18)(j) was repealed by CR 19-128** effective 2-1-21
and that **(17)(b) was amended by CR 23-075** effective 9-1-24; and **§ 452.133(1)(c) and (2)(am)**.

**Deliberately not stated, for want of a primary reading:** every requirement, threshold, distance,

**ss. 91.01 and 91.60 to 91.70**, and **ch. 236**; Wisconsin's **unnecessary hardship** variance
standard; **county shoreland zoning** standards and the treatment of nonconforming structures; and the
**uniform dwelling code** and commercial code requirements. Each is named where the hour reaches it and
routed to the office that answers it.

**Hour 67.1 states that the first question about any Wisconsin parcel is which body regulates it** —
county, city, village or town — because the allocation varies, county zoning governs in many
unincorporated areas, and shoreland zoning is county-administered. That is a practice statement about
where to call, not a statement of any jurisdictional rule.

chunks.heading: Instructor source note for Module WI-12
chunks.excerpt:
Federal lead-based paint requirements, the NFIP, and the Renovation, Repair and Painting rule are
federal and are stated at the level of the well-settled requirement.
