The course uses simplified hypotheticals to teach categories, not to create a checklist for declaring real transactions unenforceable.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Categorize without overclaiming
chunks.excerpt:
Read the remedies in the contract as alternatives rather than labels of formation. Paragraph 15 addresses failures to comply with an existing contract. A party's termination under an existing right may end future performance without asserting that no contract ever existed. A release may settle money and claims. Neither should be confused with the formation question.

### Applied exercise: Categorize without overclaiming

Consider four independent files. A: competent adults sign and accept a lawful $240,000 residential purchase with definite terms. B: parties agree that payment is solely for an unlawful transfer, and counsel determines the agreement void for illegality. C: a purchaser alleges coercion and counsel identifies a potential right to avoid the contract, but no resolution has occurred. D: a real-estate sale agreement is entirely oral and no applicable exception to the writing requirement is established.

Make a chart with the most appropriate teaching category, the fact supporting it, an uncertainty to preserve, and a safe next administrative step. Then explain why “the seller missed closing” cannot be inserted as a fifth example of “void” without further analysis. Prepare a client-facing two-sentence distinction between a formation defect and failure to perform a formed agreement.

Feedback: A illustrates valid; B void on the expressly supplied legal determination; C potentially voidable, not conclusively avoided; D a potential unenforceability problem. Missing closing typically directs attention to the existing agreement and remedies, not erasure of formation. Preserve counsel's role in evaluating exceptions and contested facts. A good answer does not promise that the oral agreement can never matter under any circumstances.

chunks.heading: T01U3 — Executed and Executory Contracts
chunks.excerpt:
## T01U3 — Executed and Executory Contracts

The word executed has two common uses. A document is often called executed when signed. In a performance classification, an executed contract is one whose required performance has been completed; an executory contract still has obligations remaining. Ask which meaning a speaker intends. In the signature block of Form 20-19, the execution date is the effective date of final acceptance, not a representation that all closing duties have been performed.

After acceptance a sale agreement generally remains executory through inspections, document delivery, financing, and closing. Signing a closing packet does not necessarily mean funding has occurred. A transaction may close while specified obligations survive: the tax-proration adjustment under paragraph 13 is a practical example. “Closed” is therefore not a reason to destroy records or ignore an express surviving obligation.

The contract and deed perform different functions. The contract establishes the promised transaction and conditions; the deed conveys the interest described when properly executed and delivered. The broker should not draft a deed or give an opinion on its legal sufficiency. Track what must be delivered and identify the professionals preparing it. A receipt from escrow proves receipt of the identified payment, not that every duty in the sale agreement is complete.

### Applied exercise: A status report with four timestamps

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Outstanding promises after acceptance
chunks.excerpt:
On October 1, the parties finally accept a resale contract. On October 3, escrow receives the earnest money and option fee. On October 29, each party signs the closing documents. The lender disburses on October 30 and escrow confirms funding that afternoon. Possession is due at closing and funding. On February 2, the parties receive the current-year tax statement showing the estimate used at closing was $640 too low; paragraph 13 requires an adjustment.

Draw a five-event timeline. For each event state what it establishes and one thing it does not establish. Write the possession instruction for October 29 and identify the post-closing obligation on February 2. Finish by rewriting this inaccurate file note: “Executed October 1; everything is performed; release keys October 29 because they signed.”

Feedback: acceptance establishes the contract's effective date; escrow receipt establishes identified delivery; signing does not establish funding; confirmed closing and funding trigger the selected possession provision; the tax reconciliation remains to be handled under the contract. Correct the note to distinguish signed, accepted, closed, funded, and performed. The problem does not give a temporary lease, so one cannot be assumed.

### Applied exercise: Outstanding promises after acceptance

chunks.heading: T01U4 — Bilateral vs. Unilateral
chunks.excerpt:
For a second purchase, assume final acceptance on November 3, closing November 30, and an option period ending November 10. The seller must supply the existing survey and affidavit in seven days and repair a named broken bedroom window before closing. The buyer must apply for financing promptly under the attached financing addendum. On November 7 the survey is delivered without its affidavit, the window remains broken, and the buyer has not applied. No party has given a termination notice.

Produce a performance tracker with columns for actor, promise, trigger, due point, current evidence, and required follow-up. Identify which obligations are not yet overdue on the given facts and which require investigation now. Explain why incomplete performance on November 7 does not allow an agent to declare the whole agreement “unexecuted and therefore nonexistent.” State what additional financing facts are needed before advising any remedy.

Feedback: the survey package is incomplete even though part arrived, but its seven-day delivery period has not yet ended; the repair deadline is closing; the financing application obligation calls for prompt attention. The agreement already exists on the stipulated facts. Use the actual addendum and counsel for disputed consequences. The tracker records facts and deadlines; it does not invent a grace period or a right to terminate.

## T01U4 — Bilateral vs. Unilateral

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Separate promises from permissions
chunks.excerpt:
In a bilateral agreement, a promise is exchanged for a promise. The standard resale sale agreement expresses reciprocal promises in paragraph 1. Neither party can simply change its mind without an applicable right or consequence. In a unilateral arrangement, acceptance is invited through performance rather than a return promise. Classification is about how the obligation is undertaken, not the number of people signing a paper.

An option must be read with particular care. An option can give a party a right to act within a specified period without requiring that action. But the termination option in paragraph 5 exists inside an otherwise bilateral purchase contract. It permits the buyer to terminate under its terms; it does not change every obligation in the sale into an optional promise. A buyer who has paid for a termination option still must handle notices correctly and may still owe other performance until the contract is terminated.

A buyer's right and a buyer's promise may appear in adjoining sentences. Circle operative verbs: must, shall, may, and may terminate. The distinction helps a student identify a duty, permission, or remedial election. The word may is not a universal escape hatch: it is linked to the facts, timing, and notice described in the specific provision.

### Applied exercise: Separate promises from permissions

Use Form 20-19 paragraphs 1, 5A, 5B, 7A, and 9B. Hypothetical buyer Jonah agrees to buy for $305,000, promises $3,000 earnest money and a $250 option fee, receives a seven-day option period, and chooses whether to hire an inspector. The seller promises access and existing utilities; closing is set for December 10. Both have accepted the same agreement.

chunks.heading: T01U5 — Reasonable Time vs. Time is of the Essence
chunks.excerpt:
Create an eight-entry list of promises, permissions, and conditioned rights from these paragraphs. For each entry identify its actor and the form language that supports your category. Explain why Jonah's choice not to inspect does not erase his promise to close. Then write a plain-language explanation of the relationship between the bilateral sale and the termination option.

Feedback: the reciprocal purchase and conveyance promises, money delivery, access/utilities, and closing performance are duties under the identified provisions. Inspection is a permitted buyer action; option termination is a right conditioned on its requirements. The classification exercise should never imply that the buyer must terminate or must order an inspection. Choosing not to inspect is not equivalent to exercising the option.

## T01U5 — Reasonable Time vs. Time is of the Essence

A reasonable-time standard depends on context; a time-is-of-the-essence provision emphasizes strict compliance. Do not use one general “Texas deadline rule” across the contract. Paragraph 5 expressly makes time essential and supplies a weekend and legal-holiday extension for specified money deliveries. Its option notice deadline is 5:00 p.m. local time where the property is located. That money-delivery extension does not silently extend the option period itself.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Two deadlines, two rules
chunks.excerpt:
Dates can run from final acceptance, actual receipt of a document, title-company receipt, or another event. Record the trigger before counting. Count days after the trigger rather than treating the trigger as day one where the form says “after.” A calendar should show both the calculated deadline and its supporting evidence: acceptance email, delivery receipt, or notice. If a required fact is unknown, mark the deadline unresolved and obtain evidence urgently. Guessing creates an appearance of certainty without protection.

Time calculations do not authorize the agent to decide a disputed legal question. The important operational response is early performance, verified notice channels, and prompt advice to consult counsel if rights may have expired. Do not wait for the final afternoon to test an unfamiliar electronic delivery method.

### Applied exercise: Two deadlines, two rules

Assume final acceptance on Friday, October 2, 2026. The option period is nine days after the effective date; the option fee is $300 and earnest money $5,000. No relevant legal holiday affects these dates. Buyer plans to deliver both payments and wishes to preserve the option. October 5 is Monday, October 11 is Sunday, and October 12 is Monday. A colleague says both deadlines move to October 12 because the option ends Sunday.

Use paragraph 5 to create a day-by-day count for the delivery period and the option period. State the recipient and payee for the money, the time and locality for option notice, and whether the colleague's extension applies. Draft a factual reminder with both deadlines and a plan to obtain receipts. Explain what would change if the last money-delivery day, instead, fell on a qualifying holiday.

chunks.heading: T01U6 — Amendments and Addenda
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: the three-day payment delivery deadline is October 5. The nine-day option period ends October 11 at 5:00 p.m. local time at the property; the money-delivery extension does not move that option deadline. Money is delivered to the named escrow agent and payable to escrow. A qualifying holiday on the money deadline would activate the express payment extension. The hypothetical supplies the weekday and holiday facts; independently check the actual calendar and statutory holiday definition in a live file.

## T01U6 — Amendments and Addenda

An addendum supplements the agreement with terms for a specific condition or subject. An amendment changes an existing agreement. The label is useful but the actual language controls. A financing addendum often accompanies the offer; an amendment after inspection may change repairs, price, closing, or option terms. An unsigned proposed amendment does not automatically suspend existing deadlines.

Use the current [Amendment to Contract, 39-11](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/amendment) and the appropriate current addendum. Locate an existing field before considering special provisions. A standard form is not a collection of optional paragraphs to rewrite freely. Under 22 TAC §537.11, an agent may explain informational choices and complete authorized fields but may not draft or recommend language defining rights, obligations, or remedies. A principal's specific written direction is treated separately by the rule; it is not permission for the agent to compose a clause and ask the principal to adopt it.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: The unsigned repair proposal
chunks.excerpt:
Attachments must travel with the offer that is accepted. Checking an addendum box but failing to attach the document creates a missing-terms problem, not a completed agreement on whatever a party later remembers. In a revision, make the actual changes conspicuous, secure the necessary agreement, identify the contract by parties and property, and preserve both original and amended versions. Cross-check amounts and dates after a change.

### Applied exercise: The unsigned repair proposal

Marta and Chen have an accepted $412,000 contract with an option ending October 18 at 5:00 p.m. They ask seller Rosa on October 16 to reduce the price to $406,000, repair the leaking kitchen supply valve through a licensed plumber, and move closing from November 4 to November 9. Rosa signs only a message saying she will consider repairs. No amendment is signed by both parties. At noon on October 18, Marta believes the pending negotiation extends the option.

Prepare a change log with original term, requested term, accepted status, and consequence of leaving it unsigned. Identify the relevant fields in the current amendment for the proposed changes without drafting a new legal contingency. Write a buyer reminder distinguishing the negotiation from the existing option deadline, and list the documents to preserve if a fully accepted amendment arrives at 2:00 p.m.

chunks.heading: T01U7 — Performance of a Contract
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: the original price, closing date, and option deadline remain the documented terms absent an effective amendment or other legally operative event. Rosa's willingness to consider is not acceptance of all requests. The buyer must choose whether to act under existing rights in time, with counsel for legal advice. Preserve the accepted amendment, communication of acceptance, and revised tracker; never overwrite the original to make it appear it contained the new terms all along.

## T01U7 — Performance of a Contract

Performance means carrying out the actual agreement. A professional transaction tracker ties each task to a provision, a responsible party, a trigger, a deadline, proof, and a next step. It must track the buyer's duties and seller's duties independently. An unanswered request to the title company does not transfer the seller's obligation to a broker, and it does not prove timely delivery to the buyer.

Performance often requires coordination without authority to decide for a party. An agent can schedule an inspection, request repair documentation, send reminders, and identify a missing signature. The principal chooses whether to accept a proposed repair or waive a right. Attorneys advise on disputed remedies. Lenders decide loan approval. Title professionals identify requirements for issuance and closing. The agent should make these handoffs explicit, early, and documented.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Read the default provision against the rule
chunks.excerpt:
Specific performance is a remedy requesting that a court require contractual performance; it is not a service a broker can promise to deliver. Liquidated damages are a contractually specified alternative in the seller's default remedies under paragraph 15. A right to seek relief does not guarantee success, entitlement, or recovery. Do not replace the form's alternative structure with an assurance that the seller can automatically keep earnest money and compel closing at the same time.

### Statute reading exercise: Read the default provision against the rule

Read Form 20-19 paragraph 15 and [22 TAC §537.11(b), (c), and (e)](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/rules-and-laws/trec-rules). Buyer Aaron fails to appear on the stipulated closing date and sends “I found a better house.” Seller Dalia asks the agent to tell escrow to pay her the $6,000 earnest money and to file a suit forcing the sale. Assume no termination right has been exercised; do not assume the entire facts of default or defenses have been adjudicated.

Diagram the alternatives printed for seller and buyer. Then write a response identifying the factual failure, explaining where the alternatives appear, and referring legal election and disputed entitlement to counsel. Identify two sentences the agent should not say and why each crosses the rule. Finally list the evidence counsel needs: signed agreement and attachments, deadline history, notices, and performance records.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Repair completion is more than a photograph
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: paragraph 15 describes alternative paths, including enforcement/other relief or termination and earnest money as liquidated damages for buyer default. The agent should not promise that both requested outcomes automatically follow or issue an unsupported determination to escrow. Rule §537.11 permits explanation of informational items; it prohibits legal advice and opinions on legal effect. Preserving the record and arranging direct consultation serves the principal without substituting the agent's legal judgment.

### Applied exercise: Repair completion is more than a photograph

Seller Nia agreed to replace a failed water heater before a November 20 closing. The contract has no alternative repair arrangement. On November 19 the seller sends a photo of a new unit but no invoice, permit information, paid receipt, or transferable warranty. The installer is described only as “a friend.” The buyer's walkthrough notes an active leak. Paragraph 7F governs agreed repair completion.

Prepare a verification checklist and a request for the missing evidence. Separate factual observations from conclusions requiring a licensed trade, inspector, or attorney. Identify the printed closing-extension and remedy language for incomplete agreed repairs and explain who chooses whether to invoke it. Write a concise closing-status note that does not assert that a photo proves compliance.

chunks.heading: T01U8 — Statute of Limitations
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: investigate licensing or commercial-trade status as applicable, required permits, scope and payment documentation, transferable warranties, and actual completion. A photo does not resolve the observed leak or documentation duties. Paragraph 7F provides the buyer specified alternatives if agreed repairs are not completed, including extending closing up to five days if necessary; it is not an unlimited automatic extension. The buyer receives the facts and legal advice as needed before choosing an action.

## T01U8 — Statute of Limitations

A limitation period limits the time for bringing a claim. It is different from a contractual notice deadline, option period, or closing date. Texas Civil Practice & Remedies Code §16.004 includes a four-year period for specified actions, including debt and fraud; §16.051 supplies a four-year residual period for actions without another express limitation. Different claims and circumstances can involve different statutes, accrual rules, tolling, or defenses. Do not teach “every real-estate lawsuit is four years.”

A ten-day option does not become four years because a party mentions limitations. A limitations issue is also not permission to delay protecting records. A broker should promptly refer a threatened claim, notify appropriate supervisory and insurance contacts under applicable procedures, and preserve evidence. Whether a particular suit is timely is legal advice, not a date that an agent should calculate from a generic course memory.

### Applied exercise: Three clocks in one file

chunks.heading: T01U9 — Reasons for Termination
chunks.excerpt:
An accepted agreement has a financing-approval deadline November 12, a closing date December 1, and a dispute raised two years later alleging a material misrepresentation. A colleague tells the buyer to ignore November 12 because “Texas gives four years.” The facts do not establish when any claim accrued or which legal theories apply.

Create three separate clock entries: the contractual financing deadline, closing performance, and possible litigation limitation. State the source needed for each and the consequence of treating them as interchangeable. Prepare an immediate action list for the November 10 file and a separate preservation/referral list for the later claim. Do not calculate an ultimate lawsuit deadline on absent facts.

Feedback: the attached financing addendum controls its notice and approval deadlines, the sale contract controls closing, and applicable statutes and legal analysis control claims. A limitation period does not extend contractual conditions. The later file should preserve original documents, communications, and records and route the claim promptly to counsel and the broker; it should not state the claim is timely or barred from the supplied facts.

## T01U9 — Reasons for Termination

Identify a termination's source before preparing its notice: an unrestricted option, a financing provision, delayed disclosure, a title-document provision, casualty, default, or mutual agreement. The same notice form cannot create the right it records. A notice should identify the contract and valid applicable basis; it must be delivered as the contract requires within any applicable period. A receipt or release involving escrow money is a separate instrument with a separate purpose.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Select a basis before a notice
chunks.excerpt:
Termination by agreement requires actual agreement. One party writing “we mutually terminate” does not make the other party agree. Conversely, a unilateral right properly exercised under the contract does not necessarily require the other party's consent just because the other party disagrees. The agent gathers the contract, facts, and delivery evidence and refers contested rights to counsel. The escrow holder's ability to release money follows the governing instructions and procedures, not the agent's prediction of who deserves it.

### Applied exercise: Select a basis before a notice

File A: buyer has a paid, unexpired option and instructs the agent in writing to terminate today. File B: the option expired yesterday; buyer merely dislikes the paint, and no other contractual basis is supplied. File C: seller and buyer both agree to end their transaction but disagree over the $4,500 deposit. File D: buyer has a lender rejection letter but the financing addendum and notice deadline have not yet been reviewed.

For each file record whether the supplied facts identify a basis, what additional document or decision is needed, how delivery would be verified, and whether deposit release is resolved. Draft a factual communication for A and an internal follow-up for D; do not compose legal settlement language for C. Explain why using the correct termination-form title is insufficient by itself.

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: A supplies an option basis subject to the actual contract and timely delivery. B supplies no current right from the stated dislike. C calls for an agreed resolution of termination and money; do not assume the deposit disposition. D requires the actual financing clause, applicable deadline, required supporting evidence, and legal review if disputed. The form documents a choice under authority; it does not supply absent authority.

### Module recap

Without looking back, define formation, performance, termination, and deposit release in separate sentences. Use your marked Form 20-19 to identify a promise, a permission, a notice deadline, and a remedy. Check your ten applied worksheets and two source-review responses for statements that decide a disputed legal issue. Correct those statements into factual descriptions and appropriate referrals. Then explain why a paid option, an accepted contract, a signed closing packet, and escrow funding are four different events. You are ready for the topic quiz when you can support each answer with the relevant required unit and identify the missing facts in an incomplete file.

## Optional reference: Deeper reading on electronic transactions

Texas Business & Commerce Code Chapter 322 also addresses attribution, errors, retention, and the time/place of sending and receiving electronic records. Read those sections if your work involves unusual electronic-signature disputes. No required assessment depends on material in this optional section. Do not infer that the chapter overrides the specific agreed notice terms or resolves forgery and authority disputes automatically.

lessons.title: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 02

chunks.heading: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 02
chunks.excerpt:
# Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 02

Laws, Rules and Regulations. Required work in this module is an audit of authority: the authority to act as broker, select a form, fill a field, communicate an offer, or make a decision. Keep the current [Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1101](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/OC/htm/OC.1101.htm) and [TREC rules](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/rules-and-laws/trec-rules) open. Record the subsection for each conclusion. The statutes and rules supply professional limits; the parties supply transaction choices within those limits.

## T02U1 — Texas Real Estate License Act

Chapter 1101 is the Real Estate License Act. It defines brokerage activity, establishes licensing and supervisory requirements, authorizes the Commission, regulates conduct, and supplies enforcement mechanisms. Form preparation is one part of licensed brokerage. A license does not make the holder an attorney, title examiner, lender, engineer, tax adviser, or principal in the client's transaction. A signature line for broker contact information is not authority to sign the seller's conveyance promise.

Section 1101.155 addresses the Commission's power concerning contract forms. Section 1101.654 addresses unauthorized practice of law and recognizes specified form-completion activity incidental to brokerage. Read that statute together with current 22 TAC §537.11, which gives the detailed mandatory-use and practice-of-law rules. Selecting a familiar form is insufficient if a different form is required for the transaction. Completing a proper form is insufficient if an agent inserts impermissible legal drafting.

chunks.heading: T02U1 — Texas Real Estate License Act
chunks.excerpt:
Section 1101.652 identifies conduct that can support discipline. Contract work creates recurring risks: negligence or incompetence; material misrepresentation or failure to disclose a known significant defect; failure to make representation clear; handling another person's money improperly; using unauthorized sale terms; and failing to provide a signed document to its signer on request. An honest agent can still work incompetently by using an obsolete form, overlooking a contingency, or losing a time-sensitive notice. A good system anticipates these errors instead of relying on memory.

Representation must be established and disclosed independently of who pays. A broker may represent the seller, the buyer, or act as an intermediary under statutory requirements. The intermediary arrangement requires the prescribed written consent, including who will pay the broker, and restrictions on disclosure and advice. The contract's broker contact information records the capacity; it does not create the underlying consent. The Information About Brokerage Services notice explains relationships and duties; it is not itself a representation agreement.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Locate the disciplinary risk
chunks.excerpt:
The 2026 buyer requirements are part of current contract intake. Under §1101.563 a license holder performing brokerage for a prospective buyer of residential real property must have the required written agreement before showing residential property or, if no showing will occur, before presenting an offer on the buyer's behalf, subject to the statutory owner-representative exception. The agreement must include its services, termination date, exclusivity status, representation or showing-only status as applicable, compensation amount or rate and how determined, and a conspicuous statement that compensation is not set by law and is fully negotiable.

A showing-only agreement under §§1101.562–.563 is a narrow arrangement. It is nonexclusive, lasts no more than fourteen days, and cannot include advice or other brokerage acts for the prospect. Providing additional services requires a separate agreement. Calling a contract “showing-only” while negotiating price for the buyer does not preserve that limited status. Do not transfer the residential-buyer requirement indiscriminately to every tenant or commercial transaction; identify the scope of each subsection.

Money and documents require separate controls. Funds payable to the contractual escrow agent should be delivered as the contract directs. If a broker receives trust funds, applicable trust-account rules, written authorization, accounting, and proper disposition matter. Keeping a check in a desk to help a client postpone a deadline is not faithful performance. Give principals copies of what they sign and preserve the accepted version with its attachments and communications. The file should make the sequence understandable to someone who was not present.

### Statute reading exercise: Locate the disciplinary risk

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Read the 2026 buyer-agreement boundary
chunks.excerpt:
Read §1101.652(a-1)(3), (b)(1), (3), (4), (7), (9), (10), (20), (28), and (29). In one hypothetical file, broker Vera knows a structural pier has failed but calls the issue cosmetic. She changes seller's minimum accepted price from $390,000 to $380,000 without instructions, asks the buyer to write the deposit to her personal account, and refuses to send buyer a copy of the signed offer.

Build a four-row conduct/subsection/evidence/correction chart. Separate misrepresentation from failure to disclose, unauthorized price instructions from a negotiation recommendation, and trust-money accounting from money ownership. Identify the statutory written title-advice duty and the printed contract location that addresses it. Do not decide a penalty; identify the conduct and preserve facts.

Feedback: known significant structural information implicates the disclosure and misrepresentation provisions; unauthorized terms implicate (b)(20); personal handling of trust funds raises the separate accounting/commingling restrictions; refusing requested signed documents implicates (b)(28). The written title advice is in (b)(29), reflected in resale paragraph 6E(1). Actual discipline depends on established facts and process. The exercise requires a specific subsection, not merely “TRELA violation.”

### Statute reading exercise: Read the 2026 buyer-agreement boundary

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Repair the intake file
chunks.excerpt:
Read §§1101.562 and 1101.563 in full. Prepare a decision tree for these three prospective buyers: Farah wants a private residential showing with no representation and no advice; Micah wants the agent to submit an offer on a residential property he has already toured alone; Ruth asks the seller's listing agent for access to the listed house and receives disclosure that the agent represents the seller. Assume no hidden prior agreements or additional acts.

For each branch identify the statutory agreement/disclosure requirement, when it occurs, and the limit on services. For Farah list the showing-only duration and exclusivity limits and explain what must occur before the agent recommends offer terms. For Micah identify the before-offer trigger. For Ruth identify the owner-representative exception without turning it into buyer representation. Compare your tree to every condition in both sections.

Feedback: Farah's showing-only path requires satisfying the four no-representation/no-advice conditions, the appropriate advance disclosure or notice, and the residential written agreement with its fourteen-day and nonexclusive limits. Additional brokerage calls for a separate agreement. Micah triggers the required agreement before presenting the offer. Ruth's listing agent must clearly disclose the seller representation; the exception does not make Ruth a client or permit misleading her about representation. A compliant tree must distinguish showing-only from representing a buyer and from an owner representative showing the owner's property.

### Applied exercise: Repair the intake file

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Capacity is a separate field
chunks.excerpt:
Residential buyer Daniel has not toured 4410 Lantern Bend. Associate Tessa plans to show it at 3:00 p.m. Her only document is an IABS notice sent yesterday. Her notes promise price advice, inspection strategy, and negotiation. The proposed agreement has a 30-day showing-only term, says “exclusive,” and compensation “whatever seller offers.” Tessa's broker represents neither owner nor buyer yet.

Prepare a missing-information list and a corrected service-path recommendation for Daniel to consider before the showing. Identify five reasons the proposed document does not fit the stated services. State what must be definite concerning compensation without inventing a rate. Draft a file note distinguishing delivery of IABS from obtaining the appropriate agreement. Do not backdate any agreement.

Feedback: the described services exceed showing-only. A showing-only agreement cannot be exclusive or exceed fourteen days; unspecified compensation is not a substitute for the amount/rate and determination required by §1101.563. The representation status must match the services. The parties must negotiate a compliant agreement, including definite termination and negotiability language, before the applicable trigger. IABS delivery alone supplies neither service authority nor the required agreement.

### Applied exercise: Capacity is a separate field

Seller Kiran and buyer Mei each signed representation agreements with the same brokerage. Neither document contains written intermediary consent. One associate is working with each. The buyer's offer names the firm in the intermediary contact section. The seller offers to contribute $7,500 toward the buyer's brokerage obligation under resale paragraph 12B(1).

chunks.heading: T02U2 — Unauthorized Practice of Law, Examples of Common Mistakes
chunks.excerpt:
Create a three-part audit of representation, consent, and compensation. List the facts that cannot be inferred from the two associates, the contract contact page, or the contribution. Explain the needed escalation to the broker before negotiation proceeds. Write a client-facing explanation of why a seller contribution does not by itself determine whom the buyer's broker represents.

Feedback: two associates are not substitutes for the statutory intermediary process and written consents. Contact-page entries report an established capacity; they do not establish it. Seller contribution addresses payment toward an obligation under a separate agreement and is not representation consent. The broker must resolve whether and how lawful intermediary service will occur. The agent should not create a traditional dual-agency arrangement by using a familiar label.

## T02U2 — Unauthorized Practice of Law, Examples of Common Mistakes

Current §537.11 prohibits practicing law, legal advice, opinions on the legal effect of contract forms, and title-validity opinions. It specifically prohibits drafting or recommending language defining or affecting principals' rights, obligations, or remedies, including escalation, appraisal, and contingency clauses. “My broker has always used it” and “the client asked for protection” are not exceptions permitting agent drafting. An online clause library is not independent legal representation for the client.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Four kinds of editing
chunks.excerpt:
An informational item completes a blank, discloses a fact, or provides instructions. A specific repair description entered into a form's designated repair field is different from inventing a new remedy if repairs disappoint the buyer. The agent may explain the meaning of informational choices, but must not promise what a court will enforce. When another form is approved for mandatory use for that purpose, the agent must not replace it by adding an informational item elsewhere.

There is a carefully limited rule for a principal's specific written instructions: §537.11(d)(2) allows adding or striking language as directed, with conspicuous changes. This is not permission for the license holder to originate or recommend the clause and obtain a confirming instruction. Preserve the principal's original direction, show the edits visibly, and obtain needed agreement. Unusual matters or instruments to be acknowledged and recorded call for advising the principal to consult an attorney before execution.

An agent may employ counsel to represent the agent, and may reimburse a principal for legal fees. The rule prohibits obtaining legal advice, directly or indirectly, for a principal in the transaction in which the agent acts as agent. Facilitate the principal's direct consultation; do not treat the brokerage attorney as automatically representing every client. A transaction attorney needs to know whom the attorney represents and the client's facts.

### Statute reading exercise: Four kinds of editing

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: The attractive escalation clause
chunks.excerpt:
Read §537.11(b)–(f) and resale paragraph 11. Classify these edits: entering “September 30, 2026” in the closing-date field from both parties' instructions; composing “buyer may cancel whenever insurance is unsatisfactory” in special provisions; conspicuously striking text specifically identified in the principal's own written instruction; and replacing a mandatory mineral addendum with one sentence in special provisions.

For each, identify the controlling subsection, what the agent may do, and what additional facts or professional assistance may be required. Write a short explanation of why even a well-intended contingency changes rights and remedies. Then produce a recordkeeping checklist for the specifically instructed strike-through, including the original written instruction and assent by the affected parties.

Feedback: the closing-date entry is informational completion. An agent-authored insurance escape clause is legal drafting. The specific principal-written direction fits the narrow conspicuous-edit rule if its conditions are satisfied, but does not make the agent its author or adviser. Replacing a mandatory addendum with a special-provisions sentence violates the separate-form restriction. Required advice that an instrument is binding and advice to consult counsel on unusual matters remain important.

### Applied exercise: The attractive escalation clause

Buyer Ellis wants to offer $470,000 and automatically beat competing offers by $2,000 up to $492,000. The agent finds a paragraph online allowing the listing broker to disclose competing offer prices and bind Ellis to the cap without further signatures. Ellis says, “Just make it enforceable; I trust you.” There is no principal-written clause or attorney-approved transaction-specific direction.

chunks.heading: T02U3 — The Broker-Lawyer Committee
chunks.excerpt:
Identify every new right or obligation the proposed clause would introduce, the evidence issues it leaves unanswered, and the professional boundary. Draft a response that still helps Ellis decide a lawful next step: communicate an ordinary offer on definite terms, or seek direct attorney advice about a bespoke structure. Prepare the factual questions counsel would need, without recommending legal wording.

Feedback: the clause affects price, proof, disclosure, acceptance, and assent. It cannot be supplied by an agent under the label of filling a blank. Trust in the agent does not alter §537.11. A competent response presents the business objective and available process, refers legal drafting directly to counsel, and keeps an ordinary offer's terms definite if that is the buyer's choice. The agent must not send the copied clause for signature as if client approval cures authorship.

## T02U3 — The Broker-Lawyer Committee

The Texas Real Estate Broker-Lawyer Committee develops and recommends standard contract forms. Under §§1101.251–.253 it includes six broker members appointed by the Commission, six lawyer members appointed by the State Bar president, and one public member appointed by the governor. Its combination of professional perspectives is intended to support usable standard transaction forms. The Commission adopts forms; a committee draft or recommendation is not itself a mandatory form.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A version-control card
chunks.excerpt:
Follow the distinction from draft to adoption to effective use. A proposed form may be available for comment while the current form remains in effect. A form's printed revision date may differ from its effective date on TREC's listing. Save the official PDF, form number, effective-date evidence, and source. Do not identify currency merely by the most recent date printed somewhere in the file. Likewise, an old outline such as PCF-0 fixes the subjects to teach but does not require use of outdated operational forms.

Not every TREC-published form is mandatory. Current Chapter 537 includes forms approved for voluntary use as well as mandatory forms. A form's title, logo, or existence on the website does not answer that legal status. Check the adoption rule and intended transaction. A voluntary notice can still be a helpful way to satisfy a substantive disclosure duty, but do not tell a principal that the particular form is mandatory unless the controlling provision says so.

### Applied exercise: A version-control card

Your broker has three PDFs: a 20-18 resale form, a 20-19 committee discussion draft, and the 20-19 PDF linked from TREC's current resale page. The current page says effective July 1, 2026; the published PDF bears a May 4, 2026 revision date. The file will be offered September 21, 2026. No owner-required alternative form applies.

Create a version-control card stating the selected form, official source, rule, effective date, printed revision date, date checked, and rejected alternatives. Explain why the discussion draft is not interchangeable with the adopted PDF and why the May date is not proof of May mandatory use. Identify what should be checked again if the form is used after a later rule change.

chunks.heading: T02U4 — Use of Promulgated Forms
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: use the official current 20-19 linked by TREC and the current adoption rule §537.28. Preserve both distinct dates and their functions. Retire the obsolete transaction template for new offers under current requirements, while retaining older executed files as evidence of what was actually used. A later revision requires a new currency check, not editing an old signed contract to resemble the new form.

## T02U4 — Use of Promulgated Forms

Under §537.11(a), a license holder negotiating covered real-property transactions uses the Commission form approved for mandatory use for that transaction unless an exception applies. The stated exceptions include acting solely as a principal, a United States agency requiring another form, an owner-prepared form or attorney-prepared form required by the owner, and a transaction without a Commission mandatory form where the specified permissible alternatives are used. The details of the fourth exception matter; it does not allow the broker to draft a new commercial purchase agreement.

Choose the transaction family first. A resale condominium uses its own contract. A farm-and-ranch transaction needs its specialized property and agricultural treatment. A new home under construction requires construction provisions not found in the ordinary resale contract. Vacant land intended for one-to-four-family residential use may fit the Unimproved Property Contract; that does not make the form suitable for every commercial development. An unusual mixed transaction should be reviewed with counsel before an instrument is executed.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Test the exception, not the preference
chunks.excerpt:
Preserve the form's text and format. Section 537.11(h) permits reproduction with the published text, sizing, spacing, and pagination intact, subject to the stated logo/outside-border and screen-scaling exceptions. Course worksheets are field maps, not substitute execution forms. Students should complete the official PDF rather than sign a redesigned educational table. Technology can help fill blanks and track attachments, but it must not silently delete warning text or reflow the executed document.

### Statute reading exercise: Test the exception, not the preference

Read §537.11(a) and (h). Analyze four proposed transactions: a license holder selling only the holder's own home; a federal agency requiring its own sale instrument; a commercial warehouse transaction for which there is no TREC mandatory purchase form; and a standard residential resale where the agent prefers a private form because it is shorter. For the warehouse, assume the proposed form is prepared by a Texas attorney and contains the required identification, approved-use statement, restrictions, and applicable explanations.

Write the applicable exception or mandatory-form outcome for each. Then evaluate software that reproduces the entire TREC form but removes page breaks and replaces twelve pages with six. Identify the rule concern separately from the form-selection concern. Explain why an exception allowing an alternative form is not a general exception allowing legal advice.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A four-property selection memorandum
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: the first three may fit their specified exceptions on the supplied facts; preference for a shorter form does not. Reformatting the executed TREC document contrary to its text-and-format requirement is a separate problem. Even when a lawful alternative form is used, the agent's practice-of-law boundaries remain. A good answer states the conditions of the exception rather than simply marking “allowed.”

### Applied exercise: A four-property selection memorandum

Compare these hypothetical purchases: Unit 308 in a condominium regime; a completed new home being sold by its builder; an existing detached duplex with no condominium regime; and an unimproved five-acre parcel intended solely for a four-bedroom residence. All are ordinary agent-represented transactions with no required alternative form and no unusual matter yet identified.

For each property identify the current TREC contract family, one feature requiring that choice, and an intake question that could change it. Locate the corresponding form's official page and verify its number and effective date. Then explain why the detached duplex does not become a condominium because it has an association, and why acreage alone does not make the vacant parcel a farm-and-ranch transaction.

Feedback: residential condominium resale, completed new home, one-to-four-family resale, and unimproved residential property are the indicated families on the supplied facts. Legal ownership regime, construction status, use, leases, agricultural interests, and transaction complexity can change the analysis. Form choice must follow facts, not the agent's folder labels or a marketing description such as “townhome.”

## T02U5 — Presenting Offers and Multiple Offers

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Compare three offers accurately
chunks.excerpt:
The principal decides which terms to accept. Under §535.156, a license holder presents offers promptly unless the principal has instructed otherwise as the rule permits; an existing contract does not by itself erase the presentation duty. Under §1101.652(b)(20), offering unauthorized terms is a disciplinary concern. A broker's duty is to communicate and explain business features accurately, protect confidential information, and follow lawful instructions, not to select a winner based on the broker's compensation or personal preference.

Compare price with material terms: financing, approval conditions, option period, earnest money, closing, possession, contingencies, and seller contributions. A high price with an unresolved sale contingency is not equivalent to a lower price without it. A cash label does not justify representing undisclosed borrowing as cash. A reliable comparison states what the documents actually provide and identifies missing information.

Multiple-offer communication requires care. Do not invent competing offers, misstate their terms, promise secrecy you cannot guarantee, or disclose confidential information without authority. Discuss the seller's chosen process and lawful instructions with the supervising broker. The seller may choose among offers within legal limits; fair-housing restrictions still apply. Avoid collecting personal buyer narratives for discriminatory selection. Transaction terms provide the appropriate comparison.

### Applied exercise: Compare three offers accurately

chunks.heading: T02U6 — When does the Offer Become a Contract?
chunks.excerpt:
Seller Ana receives three complete offers at 10:00 a.m. A offers $510,000, conventional financing of 90%, $5,000 earnest money, ten-day option, and a $9,000 seller expense contribution. B offers $500,000, documented cash, $10,000 earnest money, seven-day option, and no requested contribution. C offers $520,000, 80% financing, $7,500 earnest money, ten-day option, and a sale-of-other-property contingency. All close November 16 and provide possession at closing and funding. None supplies buyer brokerage contribution beyond what is stated, and no seller selection instruction limits presentation.

Prepare a neutral comparison table and a list of questions requiring documents or seller decisions. Calculate price less the stated seller expense contribution for A and B, clearly label it a limited comparison rather than net proceeds, and explain why C's higher number does not resolve its contingency risk. Draft a prompt presentation message without selecting the winner or describing protected buyer characteristics.

Feedback: A's limited figure is $501,000; B's $500,000. Those are not closing-net calculations because other expenses and obligations remain. C's price is $520,000 but the condition needs separate evaluation. Promptly present all three with complete attachments; the seller chooses after relevant advice. Avoid implying that finance labels guarantee funding or that an agent may suppress an offer because it seems weaker.

## T02U6 — When does the Offer Become a Contract?

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Reconstruct final acceptance
chunks.excerpt:
Track final acceptance of the same terms and its communication. Form 20-19 directs the broker to insert the date of final acceptance as the effective date. A signature may occur before communication; the first signature date is not invariably the effective date. In a counteroffer sequence, the changed term must be accepted by the other party. A broker writing a date in the blank does not create an agreement that the evidence does not support.

Prepare a complete package before presenting it: property, parties, economic terms, selected alternatives, required attachments, signatures, and legible modifications. If the seller returns a counteroffer, compare it against the prior version and disclose every change to the buyer. Preserve the version actually accepted and the communication establishing final acceptance. Do not overwrite an earlier offer and lose the evidence of negotiation.

Different transactions can present difficult communication questions, revocations, competing acceptances, authority disputes, or electronic errors. Record exact facts and refer those questions promptly to counsel. An agent should not assume that a text saying “looks good” is full acceptance of every page when the sender asks for one more change. Likewise, later delivery to escrow may be administratively important without being the formation event.

### Applied exercise: Reconstruct final acceptance

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Preserve a clean offer trail without concealing edits
chunks.excerpt:
At 9:00 a.m. Tuesday, buyer Amina signs an offer at $352,000 with closing October 28. At 1:00 p.m., seller Bruno signs but changes price to $357,000 and closing to October 30. At 3:00 p.m., Amina initials the price but changes closing to November 2. At 6:00 p.m., Bruno initials November 2. On Wednesday at 8:15 a.m., the seller's agent communicates Bruno's unqualified acceptance of that exact package to the buyer's authorized agent. No earlier acceptance communication or revocation occurred. Escrow receives it Thursday.

Build a version table and identify the final price, closing date, and effective date on these stipulated facts. Explain why neither Tuesday's first signature nor Thursday's escrow receipt supplies the date. List the evidence needed before entering the effective date, and calculate the three-day payment delivery count without assuming weekend/holiday facts that the problem does not supply.

Feedback: final terms are $357,000 and November 2; the stipulated final-acceptance communication occurs Wednesday, making that the effective date in this simplified sequence. Count Thursday, Friday, Saturday, then apply paragraph 5's actual weekend/holiday rule after verifying the calendar. Retain every negotiated version and the acceptance communication. A correct answer does not invent authority or infer an earlier communication absent from the facts.

### Applied exercise: Preserve a clean offer trail without concealing edits

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt:
Seller Ezra receives version A of an offer with a $468,000 price, November 19 closing, a $7,000 ordinary-expense request, and a $6,000 brokerage contribution. Version B raises price to $473,000, removes the ordinary-expense request, leaves the brokerage contribution unchanged, and changes closing to November 23. The seller signs B without further change and final acceptance is communicated as stipulated. A staff member proposes replacing the stored A file with B, marking A as accepted, and telling the buyer that only price changed. The title company has not yet received either version.

Prepare a four-field version comparison, a truthful principal communication, and an archive index identifying which version is accepted and which is superseded. List the evidence supporting final acceptance, identify the undisclosed changes in the staff member's statement, and specify what escrow should receive. Explain why version preservation does not authorize distributing confidential negotiation information to unrelated people. Then identify the supervising broker's role in correcting the proposed recordkeeping failure without fabricating a receipt or acceptance time.

Feedback: the accepted B changes price, closing, and the ordinary-expense request; the brokerage contribution stays $6,000. Preserve A as an unaccepted prior version and B as the accepted document, with the actual acceptance communication and complete attachments. Send the complete accepted package and accurately describe its changes. Do not relabel history, hide a material change, or invent escrow receipt. The broker's supervision and an accurate confidential file support compliance; they are not substitutes for the principal's actual agreement.

### Module recap

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt: Review the four source worksheets and eight applied worksheets. Circle every decision that belongs to the principal, broker, attorney, lender, or title professional. On a blank page explain the difference between committee recommendation and Commission adoption; mandatory and voluntary use; informational completion and legal drafting; IABS and a representation agreement; presentation and acceptance. Use a current form and the source subsections to correct your answers before the topic quiz. The module's lesson is operational: authority must be identifiable at the moment the action is taken.

lessons.title: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 03

chunks.heading: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 03
chunks.excerpt:
# Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 03

Parties, Property and Financing. In this module you build the first part of an offer and choose the financing documents that make the stated price credible. Use the current official PDFs, not a rebuilt execution form. Required sources are [resale 20-19](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/one-four-family-residential-contract-resale), [Non-Realty Items 57-0](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/non-realty-items-addendum), [Third Party Financing 40-11](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/third-party-financing-addendum-0), [Loan Assumption 41-3](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/loan-assumption-addendum-0), [Seller Financing 26-8](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/seller-financing-addendum-0), and [Release/Restoration 12-3](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/addendum-release-liability-assumed-loan-andor-restoration-sellers-va-entitlement). A field map is a learning worksheet; the parties would sign the official documents in a real transaction.

## T03U1 — Information Needed to Complete Contract Forms (including financing costs

The official outline leaves this title's parenthesis unfinished. The subject is complete: collect identities, authority, property, money sources, loan terms, costs, and deadlines before presenting a supposed final bargain. Paragraph 1 names the actual parties. A nickname, team name, or employee's name may not identify the owner. Compare the seller with title information and confirm who will sign for a trust or entity. Do not assume that a married seller's assertion resolves all homestead or signature issues; counsel and the closing professional determine required signatures from the facts.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A complete intake sheet
chunks.excerpt:
Paragraph 2 defines the property through land, improvements, accessories, exclusions, and reservations. A promised refrigerator and a reserved chandelier require different analysis. Fixtures and listed accessories included by the form pass unless properly excluded or otherwise addressed; additional personal property uses the appropriate non-realty document. Fixtures may also be leased. A seller cannot promise to convey ownership of leased solar equipment merely because it is physically attached to the home. Paragraph 4 calls for residential, fixture, and natural-resource lease treatment.

The sales-price equation in paragraph 3 is cash plus all disclosed financing. The form's definition of cash excludes proceeds of borrowing or sale of other real property except as disclosed. “Cash offer” must therefore be checked against actual sources. Earnest money and option fee are not an extra addition to the sales price; their credits and disposition follow the contract. Closing funds also include expenses, prorations, and other adjustments, so paragraph 3A alone is not the buyer's complete cash-to-close estimate.

Financing costs include more than interest. The financing addendum identifies principal, term, rate limits, and origination charges as applicable. The buyer's Loan Estimate supplies lender disclosures; it does not rewrite the offer's agreed limits. Identify financed premiums separately where the form excludes them from principal figures. Do not assume an origination percentage is the total settlement cost. Lender, title, insurance, tax, and brokerage amounts must be reconciled without inventing rates or guaranteeing approval.

### Applied exercise: A complete intake sheet

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Cash-source reconciliation
chunks.excerpt:
Sellers Arlo and Beatriz Vega own Lot 12, Block 4, Copper Willow Addition, City of San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas, known as 118 Copper Willow Lane, 78230. Buyers Celia Hart and Nikhil Rao will both take title. Price is $425,000; savings fund $85,000 and a conventional first mortgage funds $340,000. The buyers have no sale contingency or other borrowing. The built-in oven stays, the dining chandelier is retained by sellers, and a freestanding freezer will be sold separately for $500. The solar panels are leased; sellers provide a $95/month agreement with 84 months remaining. No residential or natural-resource lease exists.

Prepare a field map for paragraphs 1–4 showing every supplied fact, the separate document needed for the freezer and solar lease, and the unresolved information needed before completing the lease addendum. Compute paragraph 3 and list at least four cash-to-close categories not included in $85,000. Explain why the solar panels should not be described as seller-owned equipment.

Feedback: use both sellers and both buyers, the full supplied land description, $85,000 cash, $340,000 financing, and $425,000 total. Address the chandelier under exclusions and the freezer under the non-realty document. The fixture lease needs its own review and addendum; obtain assignment/consent terms, documents, deadlines, and the buyer's informed decisions. Title expenses, lender charges, insurance/reserves, taxes/prorations, and brokerage obligations can affect cash needed. A good answer does not silently convert leased equipment into owned property.

### Applied exercise: Cash-source reconciliation

chunks.heading: T03U2 — Review Elements & Practice 1-4 Family Residential Contract (Resale), Non-Realty Items Addendum
chunks.excerpt:
Buyer Darius proposes a $600,000 purchase “all cash.” His source sheet shows $280,000 savings, $120,000 from a new unsecured line of credit, and $200,000 expected from the sale of his current home. That sale has not closed. The proposed offer has no financing addendum, no sale-of-other-property addendum, and paragraph 3A states $600,000. He asks the agent to leave the sources out because the seller prefers cash.

Reconcile the three sources and identify what is disclosed and undisclosed. Explain the paragraph 3A definition in plain language, identify the financing and sale-contingency questions requiring a buyer decision and appropriate documents, and draft a factual response to the requested omission. Do not assume that every source creates a termination right; distinguish disclosure from a negotiated contingency.

Feedback: the sources total $600,000, but their nature does not match an unqualified savings-only description. Borrowing and sale proceeds require accurate treatment under the actual contract; conditions and addenda must reflect the buyer's instructions and agreed bargain. A source disclosure is not automatically a sale contingency. The agent must not conceal material financing facts or promise that a lender will approve the funds. The correct work product lists questions and routes each source into the proper contract analysis.

## T03U2 — Review Elements & Practice 1-4 Family Residential Contract (Resale), Non-Realty Items Addendum

chunks.heading: T03U2 — Review Elements & Practice 1-4 Family Residential Contract (Resale), Non-Realty Items Addendum
chunks.excerpt:
The resale form covers an ordinary resale of one-to-four-family residential property and expressly is not for condominium transactions. Its opening page creates an integrated definition: land, improvements, and accessories collectively make up the property. Read the included-item lists before drafting exclusions. The refrigerator, stove, window coverings, wall-mounted television bracket, and smart controls may be treated differently by the actual wording and installation facts. Do not rely on “everything attached stays” as a complete reading of the form because listed accessories can be included even when not fixtures.

Specific exclusions identify what seller retains and must remove before possession. Avoid vague phrases such as “seller's personal items” when the object is an included fixture or accessory. If the seller intends to remove a chandelier, identify it distinctly and resolve resulting repair or replacement instructions using appropriate fields and professional advice. Mineral or other reserved interests belong in an attached addendum, not merely the household-property exclusions blank.

The current Non-Realty Items Addendum is 57-0, a voluntary-use form in the current TREC inventory; the older outline's generic title remains the curriculum heading. Non-realty items are separately identified, with their agreed consideration and condition provisions. They do not become part of the lender's real-estate collateral because the buyer wants to finance everything together. Give the lender and closing professional accurate information about the transaction rather than hiding a personal-property price inside the real-estate price.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Mark the property boundary
chunks.excerpt:
Paragraph 10B of 20-19 also matters when property changes hands: smart-device access must be transferred and seller access removed as stated. Identify physical devices, relevant software/app controls, and existing fixture leases. Account-transfer capability is a factual question; an agent should not promise that a subscription or license will transfer without checking its terms. Security and privacy at possession require a deliberate handoff.

### Statute reading exercise: Mark the property boundary

Read resale paragraphs 2, 4, and 10B, then the current Non-Realty Items Addendum. At 81 Birch Crossing the seller owns a built-in dishwasher, an attached television mount, a television hung on that mount, a freestanding washer, curtain rods and curtains, a hard-wired doorbell camera, and its paid cloud subscription. The proposed contract has no exclusions and no non-realty attachment. The seller wants to keep the television and washer; the buyer wants the mount, window coverings, and operational doorbell.

Create an item-by-item matrix with form classification, whether facts are sufficient, proposed document location, and transfer question. Do not reproduce the entire official form; mark it and prepare a field map. Explain the difference between transferring physical hardware and transferring access. Add a final entry for a leased propane tank not previously disclosed and identify the new document work it requires.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Correct the property draft
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: read the actual inclusion lists, which expressly include mounts/brackets and curtains/rods, and analyze the television and washer separately. The doorbell's hardware and account/control handoff require separate attention; the cloud subscription's transferability cannot be assumed. The leased tank belongs in the fixture-lease review. A strong answer distinguishes what the form includes from what an additional personal-property agreement or lease assignment must establish.

### Applied exercise: Correct the property draft

Using the Copper Willow facts from the intake worksheet, a draft says “all appliances excluded,” describes the freezer as included real estate for $500, leaves the chandelier out of exclusions, and checks “no leases.” The sellers confirm they intend to retain only the dining chandelier and sell the freezer; the built-in oven stays. The leased panels remain subject to their owner's rights.

Prepare a redline instruction sheet identifying each incorrect field, the factual correction, and the supporting instruction. Produce a separate inventory for the non-realty transaction with identifying details the parties still need, such as make, model, serial number, and condition. Write a delivery checklist for the complete offer package, including the financing and fixture-lease attachments. Explain why deleting “all appliances excluded” without verifying the remaining item list would be incomplete review.

chunks.heading: T03U3 — Review Elements & Practice Third Party Financing Addendum & Loan Assumption Addendum
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: correct the blanket exclusion, identify the chandelier, remove the freezer from the real-estate price equation unless the parties properly revise the bargain, and address the lease truthfully. The buyer must understand the actual panel arrangement. The package should contain the official resale form, relevant financing, fixture-lease, and non-realty documents with consistent property identification. The correction sheet records instructions rather than silently changing an already signed offer.

## T03U3 — Review Elements & Practice Third Party Financing Addendum & Loan Assumption Addendum

Third-party financing involves funds supplied by a lender other than seller or buyer. Form 40-11 requires prompt application and every reasonable effort to obtain the stated financing, including providing requested information. Its financing categories contain different fields. Complete only the applicable selections from actual instructions and lender information; do not populate every category or assume a conventional field fits a VA loan. Other-financing provisions include a specific property-approval waiver choice that requires careful explanation and the buyer's decision.

Buyer Approval and Property Approval are separate. Buyer Approval concerns availability of the stated loan terms and the lender's asset, income, and credit requirements. If the applicable subject-to box is selected, the buyer's termination under paragraph 2A requires both notice and a lender's written reasons within the negotiated days after effective date. If the buyer does not terminate under that provision, the contract is no longer subject to that approval condition. A prequalification letter is not a contractual extension.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Compare the two approval paths
chunks.excerpt:
Property Approval concerns lender underwriting of the property, including appraisal, insurability, and required repairs. Paragraph 2B generally requires the notice and lender statement on or before the third day before closing. Read any applicable waiver and the rest of the contract; failure to obtain a survey under resale paragraph 6C(2), for example, has its own stated limit on use of that financing provision. FHA/VA paragraph 4 supplies a separate required provision and expressly does not use paragraph 2B's three-day termination-notice requirement. Do not flatten these into one generic “financing deadline.”

An assumption under Form 41-3 is a different financing transaction: the buyer assumes an existing note and obligations under its deed of trust. Obtain actual documents and lender statements. The addendum addresses credit documentation and seller approval, balance variation, assumption fees/rate limits, noteholder consent, seller protection, and tax/insurance escrow. A quoted attractive rate is not proof that the noteholder will allow transfer or release the seller. Assumption consent, seller release, and restoration of VA entitlement must be examined separately.

### Statute reading exercise: Compare the two approval paths

Read 40-11 paragraphs 1, 2, and 4 and 41-3 paragraphs A–E. Prepare a comparison using these supplied facts: a new $288,000 conventional loan, 30-year term, 6.5% maximum interest for all 30 years, origination-charge limit 1.5%, buyer-approval period 18 days; alternatively, assumption of a $251,000 existing first lien with a $1,720 current total monthly payment, maximum assumption fee $1,200, maximum permitted interest 4%, and credit documentation due in seven days.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Complete conventional financing and costs
chunks.excerpt:
Map each fact to the appropriate form field and identify the different approval actors. Write the separate notices and supporting evidence required for failure of buyer approval in the new-loan path and failure of noteholder consent in the assumption path. Explain why $251,000 cannot simply replace $288,000 without reconciling price and cash. Include the source paragraph for each finding.

Feedback: new-loan underwriting uses the buyer/property distinction and the agreed loan parameters; assumption additionally involves seller's credit review and noteholder consent under its actual terms. The new-loan buyer-approval termination requires notice plus lender reasons within the selected period. Noteholder failure to consent under 41-3E gives either party the stated termination choice by notice. Different financing principal requires corresponding cash or price adjustment, not a hidden mismatch.

### Applied exercise: Complete conventional financing and costs

Use Copper Willow's $340,000 first mortgage. The parties instruct a 30-year term, interest not exceeding 6.75% for 30 years, origination charges not exceeding 1.25%, and a contract subject to buyer approval within 21 days. Effective date is October 6, 2026; closing is November 10. No FHA/VA or other-financing provision applies. The Loan Estimate later shows origination charges of $4,760, while the lender is willing to revise them to $4,100. No other lender determination is provided.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Balance variance in an assumption
chunks.excerpt:
Complete a field map for 40-11, calculate the dollar origination cap, and compare both lender amounts to it. Create distinct buyer-approval and property-approval deadline entries, including the required supporting statement. Write a follow-up explaining that a cost mismatch calls for prompt resolution and does not automatically terminate the contract. Identify which terms would require an agreed amendment if the buyer accepts different limits.

Feedback: the cap is $4,250; $4,760 exceeds it and $4,100 is within it. Buyer-approval period ends October 27 on the stated count; the ordinary property-approval notice point is November 7, the third day before November 10, subject to actual provisions and facts. Do not assume a weekend extension absent language applying to that deadline. The agent obtains lender clarification and the buyer's decision, preserving the original negotiated condition.

### Applied exercise: Balance variance in an assumption

Price is $370,000 with an assumed first lien stated at $250,000 and $120,000 cash. The assumption addendum selects adjustment of cash payable at closing, with a $2,000 total-variance threshold. The actual principal balance at closing is $248,600. The lender consents on unchanged terms and charges $900, within the $1,000 allowed fee. Seller has not yet obtained a release of liability.

chunks.heading: T03U4 — Review Elements & Practice Seller Financing Addendum
chunks.excerpt:
Recalculate cash and show why the price remains the same. Compare the $1,400 variance with the threshold, and distinguish the fee from principal. Prepare a closing inquiry identifying release, loan-document, and escrow-balance evidence still needed. Then analyze a separate version with actual balance $247,000 and no other party election yet made: identify the threshold issue and the addendum's next decision without announcing automatic termination.

Feedback: cash increases to $121,400 when the assumed debt falls, preserving $370,000 total. The variance is within $2,000. With $247,000 debt, cash would be $123,000, but the variance exceeds the stated threshold and invokes the specified right/election mechanism in 41-3C. Consent to assumption does not itself release seller liability; inspect the actual release and any required security. An assumption fee is a cost, not part of the principal balance variance calculation.

## T03U4 — Review Elements & Practice Seller Financing Addendum

Form 26-8 applies when the seller finances all or part of the price. Its opening notice directs consultation with an attorney and financial professional because lending arrangements may be regulated and create accounting or reporting obligations. The addendum describes agreed financing; it is not a substitute for a lawful note, deed of trust, servicing arrangement, and compliance analysis. Do not assure a seller that one occasional loan is exempt from every federal and state requirement.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: The seller-finance approval branches
chunks.excerpt:
Credit documentation and approval have distinct consequences. If required documents are not delivered, the seller's specified timely termination before complete delivery directs earnest money to seller. If documents are delivered but the seller timely disapproves credit, the specified termination refunds earnest money to buyer. Those are different facts. The agent should track the documents actually received, not label a package “complete” because one PDF arrived.

The note fields establish principal, interest, and payment structure. One lump sum, monthly installments, and interest-only followed by installments create different obligations. An amortization schedule may have payments calculated over thirty years with the remaining balance due in five; that is not a fully amortizing five-year loan. Explain the field choices, obtain agreed figures from qualified sources, and ensure that the principal reconciles to resale paragraph 3B. Do not calculate a number and guarantee its legal or financial suitability.

The deed-of-trust choices address transfer consent, insurance naming seller as mortgagee loss payee, tax/insurance escrow, servicing, and prior-lien default. Follow the exact choices and avoid contradictory checkmarks. Seller's financial security depends on more than an interest rate: lien priority, borrower capacity, insurance, servicing, default rights, and existing debt all matter. A seller may need direct counsel on due-on-sale, wraparound, or consumer-credit issues before agreeing.

### Statute reading exercise: The seller-finance approval branches

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Assemble an internally consistent seller note
chunks.excerpt:
Read every provision of 26-8, marking paragraphs A, B, C, and D in separate colors. Seller Faye finances $160,000 of a $200,000 purchase. Credit report, employment verification, deposit verification, and a current financial statement are due six days after effective date. On day six only the credit report and employment verification arrive. On day eight the remaining required documents arrive. No notice has been delivered. In a separate branch, all documents arrive on day six and the seller finds the credit unacceptable on day nine.

Write the delivery ledger, identify the distinct termination windows and money consequences from paragraph B, and explain why the agent may not merge the two branches.
