Then identify all note and security choices still missing from the supplied facts. Draft a referral list for direct attorney/financial consultation addressing the opening notice rather than inventing completed loan documents.

Feedback: before complete delivery in the first branch, paragraph B supplies seller's stated nondelivery termination path; complete delivery changes the analysis. In the second branch, timely credit disapproval uses the seven-day period measured from expiration of the delivery period or actual delivery, whichever is later, with earnest money refunded to buyer. Rate, maturity/payment structure, transfer consent, insurance, escrow, and servicing remain unresolved. The form itself directs professional consultation.

### Applied exercise: Assemble an internally consistent seller note

chunks.heading: T03U5 — Review Elements & Practice Addendum for Release of Liability on Assumed Loan and/or Restoration of Seller's VA Entitlement
chunks.excerpt:
Buyer Imani and seller Grant agree on $280,000 price, $70,000 cash, and $210,000 seller financing. Their attorney and financial professional supply these hypothetical agreed terms: 6% annual interest, interest-only monthly payments for 12 months, then $1,800 monthly including interest beginning 13 months after note date and continuing for 48 months when the remaining balance is due. Consent is required for transfers under the selected form provision; casualty insurance naming seller is required; tax/insurance escrow is required with a third-party servicer at buyer's expense. No superior lien exists. Credit documents selected are credit report and deposit verification, due seven days after effective date.

Map all fields in 26-8 and the corresponding resale financing amount. Calculate the initial monthly interest-only payment, identify the balloon risk, and create a checklist for the attorney-prepared note and security instrument. Explain why “$1,800 for 48 months” does not prove the debt is paid off. Do not calculate or promise the final balloon from an incomplete payment-history assumption.

Feedback: $210,000 × 6% ÷ 12 equals $1,050 initially. The later payment schedule has a remaining-balance maturity, not a representation of full amortization. Check the interest-only option and associated later-installment fields as supplied, and the stated D choices. Keep the $210,000 in paragraph 3B and $70,000 in 3A. Actual note drafting, legal compliance, and final amortization confirmation belong to the retained professionals.

## T03U5 — Review Elements & Practice Addendum for Release of Liability on Assumed Loan and/or Restoration of Seller's VA Entitlement

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Two approvals at the same closing
chunks.excerpt:
Form 12-3 separates release of seller's liability from restoration of VA entitlement. Neither follows merely from the buyer taking title or agreeing to assume payments. The release section calls for seller and buyer to apply within the stated days and provide required information. It offers a choice of contract termination with earnest money refund if approval has not occurred by closing, or proceeding without delaying closing. The choice must reflect the parties' instructions, not the agent's preference for saving the transaction.

The restoration section has its own application period and closing consequence. The form's notice states the buyer must be a veteran, have sufficient unused entitlement, and otherwise qualify for VA restoration in this assumption setting; it tells the parties to use both A and B when restoration is desired. A broker should not certify VA eligibility or promise restoration. Obtain written lender/VA determinations and distinguish submitted, under review, and approved.

Seller pays the cost of securing release and restoration under the form. The deed must contain any assumption clause required by the lender or agency. This calls for coordination with the closing attorney and title professional, not broker drafting. If the seller is willing to close without release, make sure the selected contractual choice is understood with direct legal advice about continuing liability.

### Applied exercise: Two approvals at the same closing

chunks.heading: T03U6 — Case Study/ Workshop
chunks.excerpt:
Seller Hector's VA-backed note will be assumed by buyer Jo. Their 12-3 selects both release and entitlement restoration, applications due five days after effective date, and termination/refund if either required approval is absent at closing. Both submit complete applications on day four. Three days before closing the lender approves assumption and release, while VA restoration remains pending. Jo is a veteran, but no eligibility or unused-entitlement determination has been supplied.

Make a three-row status chart for assumption consent, release, and restoration. Map the selected application deadlines and closing consequences to A and B. Draft a status message explaining what has and has not been approved, what evidence remains necessary, and who can evaluate eligibility. Explain why the release letter cannot be copied into the restoration box as proof. Do not assume an extension or change the selected consequence.

Feedback: assumption approval, liability release, and entitlement restoration are separate. Pending restoration has not satisfied the selected closing condition. The parties may consider lawful agreed changes with appropriate advice, but the original form does not become an automatic extension. The lender/VA must supply the actual determinations; veteran status alone does not prove sufficient unused entitlement or all qualification conditions.

## T03U6 — Case Study/ Workshop

This workshop requires an offer package and a review memorandum. It applies the earlier units to one coherent file but introduces new decisions. First make your own work, then compare feedback. Do not combine incompatible financing alternatives into one offer. A change in financing source is a new branch to analyze, not permission to overwrite a buyer's accepted instructions.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Draft the initial offer field map
chunks.excerpt:
### Applied exercise: Draft the initial offer field map

Buyers Soren Bell and Uma Ellis offer $480,000 to seller Yara Finch for Lot 22, Block B, Meadow Reed Addition, City of Austin, Travis County, Texas, 2608 Meadow Reed Drive, 78748. Verified savings provide $96,000 and a $384,000 conventional first mortgage provides the balance. Agreed offer limits are 30 years, maximum 6.8% interest for 30 years, maximum origination charges 1%, and buyer approval within 20 days. Earnest money is $6,000, option fee $400, option ten days, closing November 23, 2026. Escrow is Prairie Oak Title, 400 Congress Avenue, Austin, Texas 78701. A freestanding wine refrigerator is separately purchased for $700; the built-in range stays; a brass hallway chandelier is excluded. Seller owns all fixtures and there are no leases.

Produce a paragraph 1–5 field map, finance-addendum field map, and non-realty attachment inventory. Reconcile all figures, show the origination cap, identify remaining whole-contract information needed before presentation, and explain that the proposed closing date does not supply an effective date. Mark the work as hypothetical and unexecuted.

Feedback: price reconciles $96,000 + $384,000; the origination cap is $3,840. The refrigerator's separate $700 does not silently increase paragraph 3C; identify its agreed transaction treatment in the proper document. The chandelier must be specifically excluded. The form remains incomplete until title, survey, condition, notices, contributions, possession, attachments, and party instructions are resolved. No effective date exists merely because the offer proposes November 23 closing.

### Applied exercise: Audit the changed financing branch

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Explain a preclosing financing failure
chunks.excerpt:
Before acceptance, Uma asks instead to assume Yara's $290,000 loan at its existing 3.8% rate and pay the remaining price from verified savings. The lender has not consented. Current payment including reserves is $1,930. The parties propose an assumption-fee cap of $1,100, a rate cap of 3.8%, cash adjustment for balance variance with a $2,500 threshold, and seven-day credit-document delivery. Yara requires liability release by closing with termination/refund if it is absent. This is a conventional loan, so VA entitlement is irrelevant.

Create a new package list that replaces the incompatible initial financing choice, recalculates cash, and maps the assumption and release fields. Identify the documents the seller must supply, all approvals still unresolved, and tax/insurance escrow questions. Write a comparison explaining the change in funding risk. Do not retain the conventional new-loan addendum by habit when that loan is no longer part of the proposed bargain.

Feedback: cash becomes $190,000 against the $290,000 assumption. Use 41-3 and the applicable liability-release section of 12-3, with no VA restoration selection. Obtain notes, deeds of trust, recent statements, actual balance, lender consent, release, and escrow information. A lower historic rate does not prove transfer permission. The original financing package remains a superseded proposal, preserved for history but clearly distinct from the new offer.

### Applied exercise: Explain a preclosing financing failure

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt:
Return to the initial conventional branch, now accepted October 20 with closing November 23 and buyer approval within twenty days. On November 6 the lender states in writing that the borrowers' income cannot support the agreed loan. On November 7 the buyer instructs timely termination under the buyer-approval provision. Assume the agreement still is subject to that provision, no amendment changes it, and the written lender statement gives the reasons. The property appraisal was satisfactory; escrow holds the $6,000 earnest money and the $400 option fee has been released to seller.

Prepare a notice-package checklist, identify the clause and applicable deadline, and explain why satisfactory appraisal does not cure missing buyer approval. Write a money-status note distinguishing earnest money from the option fee and direct escrow release procedures. Identify the delivery evidence to retain. Do not use an expired option as the stated basis when the supplied facts identify a different right.

Feedback: twenty days after October 20 is November 9 on the stipulated calculation; the buyer's November 7 instruction can be acted on under the stated 2A condition with both notice and lender reasons delivered as required. Appraisal is a property issue and does not solve income qualification. The financing clause calls for earnest-money refund on proper termination; it does not turn the already released option fee into refundable earnest money. Preserve notice, attachments, delivery, instructions, and escrow correspondence.

### Module recap

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt: Review your field maps as one complete audit trail. Every dollar in price must have a disclosed source; every financing choice must have the correct applicable document; every approval must identify its actor and deadline. Explain assumption consent, seller release, and entitlement restoration without using them as synonyms. Check the current forms' warnings and signatures, correct your independent worksheets, and prepare for the topic quiz. No worksheet authorizes real-world execution without complete transaction facts and the appropriate professional review.

lessons.title: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 04

chunks.heading: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 04
chunks.excerpt:
# Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 04

Covenants, Commitments and Notices. Work with [resale 20-19](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/one-four-family-residential-contract-resale), paragraphs 5–7, and the linked official forms in each unit. Build a document-delivery ledger as well as a calendar. A deadline cannot be verified merely because a sender says the document was prepared; identify receipt, completeness, and the actual contractual trigger.

## T04U1 — Earnest Money Requirement

Paragraph 5A requires the specified earnest money and option fee to be delivered to the named escrow agent within three days after effective date. They are payable to escrow and may be combined. Additional earnest money has its own amount and days blank. The express extension applies if the last delivery day for those payments falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or qualifying legal holiday. Record payment type, amount, delivery evidence, recipient, and any returned or insufficient payment; a promise to initiate a wire is not the same as verified delivery.

The form applies received amounts first to option fee, then earnest money, then additional earnest money. Partial delivery can therefore leave the earnest money short even if the buyer intended the payment mainly as a deposit. Under paragraph 5C, failure to deliver earnest money in time gives seller the stated termination/remedy rights by notice before buyer delivers it. The contract does not say late earnest money automatically means there never was a contract.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Partial payment allocation
chunks.excerpt:
Earnest money is credited through closing or disposed of under the applicable termination and escrow provisions. It is not automatically the broker's money or automatically seller's money after a disagreement. Do not promise release without the actual contract and escrow process. Accurate records protect everyone when deposit receipt, timeliness, or entitlement is disputed.

### Applied exercise: Partial payment allocation

Effective date is Monday, October 5, 2026; no relevant holiday affects the three-day period. The contract calls for $4,000 earnest money and $350 option fee. Buyer delivers one $4,000 payment to the named escrow agent on October 7 and mistakenly writes “earnest money only” in the memo. The option period is eight days. The remaining $350 arrives October 9. No seller notice has yet been sent, and assume the payments clear.

Prepare a ledger showing contractual allocation, deficiency, delivery deadline, and later cure event. Identify the difference between the buyer's memo and paragraph 5A(3), and locate the seller's notice-before-delivery language. Write a same-day factual alert at the end of October 8 that states what is missing without declaring automatic termination. Separately record the option-expiration date and local-time requirement.

Feedback: first allocate $350 to option fee and $3,650 to earnest money; $350 earnest money remains missing at the October 8 delivery deadline. October 9 is later delivery, so the seller's paragraph 5C rights and timing must be evaluated on actual notice facts. The option period ends October 13 at 5:00 p.m. local time at the property on the supplied count. The money shortage is not an automatic erasure of formation or an instruction for the broker to decide a disputed remedy.

## T04U2 — Option Fee Requirement

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A late fee and an unrelated right
chunks.excerpt:
The option is an unrestricted buyer termination right for the agreed period when its requirements are met. Paragraph 5B states notice must be given by 5:00 p.m. local time where the property is located. Paragraph 5D removes the unrestricted right if no option-fee amount is stated or the fee is not timely delivered. That result is different from automatic termination of the purchase agreement. The buyer may still have other specific rights if their separate conditions are met.

Option fee is credited to the sales price at closing but is not refunded on a timely option termination under paragraph 5B. Escrow may release it to seller as authorized by paragraph 5A. Do not send it directly to seller merely because that was an older practice remembered from a prior form. The current document governs the current offer. Record the option-payment and option-notice deadlines separately.

The agent should help the buyer order investigations early enough to make an informed choice. Inspection reports received after the option deadline do not reopen that option automatically. A repair request does not suspend it; a seller's pending answer does not extend it. If the buyer wants an extension, use a properly agreed amendment and keep the original deadline active until the change is effective.

### Applied exercise: A late fee and an unrelated right

chunks.heading: T04U3 — Title Commitment, Title Policy & Endorsements
chunks.excerpt:
The parties accept on October 1. Option fee is $250, option period seven days, and all money is due under paragraph 5. Buyer timely pays earnest money but sends the option fee on October 6, after the applicable deadline; assume no extension applies. On October 7 the inspection reveals a failed sewer line. The contract is subject to a separate financing addendum, but the lender has made no property determination. Seller has not agreed to repairs or an option extension.

Write a rights inventory distinguishing the lost unrestricted option, the inspection/access right, potential negotiated amendment, and any financing issue still requiring facts. Draft an urgent factual explanation to buyer and a broker/counsel referral. Explain why the inspection finding alone does not establish a financing termination. Do not label the whole contract terminated or guarantee that another contingency will rescue the buyer.

Feedback: late option-fee delivery means no unrestricted paragraph 5 termination right on these stipulated facts. Inspection and negotiation remain distinct. Financing requires its own lender determination, evidence, timing, and applicable provisions; a failed sewer line in a general inspection is not the same as lender property disapproval. The agent communicates the status accurately and obtains appropriate advice before any asserted termination.

## T04U3 — Title Commitment, Title Policy & Endorsements

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Build the title-document clock
chunks.excerpt:
A commitment is the title insurer's undertaking to issue a policy subject to stated requirements and exceptions. It is not the issued policy and is not a broker's certificate of clear title. Review the parties, estate/interest, description, exceptions, and requirements with the buyer and refer legal effect to counsel. A title policy insures against covered loss under its terms; exclusions and exceptions matter. A lender policy protects the lender's interest and does not replace an owner's policy for the buyer.

Paragraph 6A identifies who pays for the owner policy and the title company, and lists permitted exceptions. The survey/area-and-boundary exception choice may change coverage and cost; the buyer must understand the choice and obtain title advice. Do not describe an endorsement or amended exception as unlimited boundary insurance. Paragraph 6B measures delivery from the title company's receipt of the contract, with the stated extension up to fifteen days or three days before closing, whichever is earlier. The buyer must receive both the commitment and legible exception documents as required.

Paragraph 6D has its own objection mechanism. Its initial objection deadline is the earlier of closing or the specified days after buyer receives the commitment, exception documents, and survey. Missing one of the required components may matter. Schedule C requirements are not waived by the buyer's failure to object. Timely objections trigger the stated cure period and potential closing extension, followed by a separate buyer termination/waiver choice if objections remain uncured. New matters in revised documents can create a new objection period for those new matters. These are several clocks, not one.

### Statute reading exercise: Build the title-document clock

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Commitment versus assurance
chunks.excerpt:
Read 20-19 paragraphs 6A–D. Escrow/title receives a contract October 2; closing is November 10. Buyer receives the commitment October 15, exception documents October 17, and the required survey October 20. The objection blank is five days. A recorded driveway easement not among the specified exceptions appears in the supplied materials. Buyer gives an appropriate written objection October 23. Assume seller receives it that day and the title issue is within the objection provision.

Map initial delivery, initial objection, cure, and after-cure election as separate rows, each with trigger, calculation, actor, and evidence. Identify the earliest initial objection deadline on these facts. Read the cure and closing-extension interaction rather than importing the money-delivery weekend rule. State what counsel should review about the easement and why the agent should not call it invalid.

Feedback: receipt of the final required component on October 20 makes the five-day date October 25, earlier than November 10. The October 23 objection is timely on the supplied facts. The fifteen-day cure period runs from seller receipt under 6D; the form then supplies the buyer's five-day election after an uncured period and any necessary closing extension. The agent identifies the issue and exact clause; counsel evaluates legal effect and the buyer's proposed use. Schedule C remains a separate nonwaiver point.

### Applied exercise: Commitment versus assurance

chunks.heading: T04U4 — Survey
chunks.excerpt:
Seller asks agent Noah to tell buyer the title is “guaranteed perfect.” The commitment names a prior owner, lists a recorded access restriction, requires release of a $190,000 seller lien in Schedule C, and excludes matters not covered by its terms. The owner-policy box names seller as payer. Buyer thinks the seller-paid policy also pays for every future fence dispute.

Prepare a correction request for the named-insured/owner information, a requirements checklist for the lien release, and a referral question concerning the access restriction. Draft a plain-language explanation distinguishing commitment, owner policy, lender policy, exceptions, and coverage decisions. Identify the relevant paragraph 6A coverage choice to discuss with the title professional without promising the result.

Feedback: the commitment is conditional evidence of intended coverage, not a universal title warranty. Correct identity information, satisfy closing requirements, and obtain review of the access restriction. Who pays does not enlarge the insurance. The buyer's fence-dispute assumption must be checked against the actual policy and survey-related choice. The broker should not opine on title validity or promise insurance for an uncovered matter.

## T04U4 — Survey

Choose one survey route in paragraph 6C. An existing-survey route requires both the survey and the TDI residential affidavit or declaration within the stated time. If seller fails to deliver both, buyer obtains a new survey at seller expense under the provision. If seller timely delivers the package but title or lender rejects it, the separate selected payer controls. The factual difference between nondelivery and rejection changes the cost result.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Who pays for the replacement survey?
chunks.excerpt:
The buyer-new-survey route and seller-new-survey route have different duties. Under buyer's route, the form includes deemed receipt and the stated limit on financing termination if buyer fails to obtain the survey. A survey must be by a registered professional land surveyor acceptable to title and lender. An old sketch, tax map, or online boundary overlay is not automatically an acceptable survey. Alterations since the survey can be critical.

### Applied exercise: Who pays for the replacement survey?

In File A, paragraph 6C(1) requires the existing survey and affidavit/declaration in eight days. Seller delivers the survey on day five but no affidavit or declaration by day eight. The rejection-payer box is buyer. In File B, seller delivers both valid documents on day five, but the lender rejects the old survey because a new garage was added; the rejection-payer box is also buyer. A new survey costs $780 in either file.

Write a separate cost determination for each using the actual paragraph, state the delivery deadline for the replacement, and identify the evidence distinguishing the branches. Explain why the selected rejection payer does not decide File A. Draft a neutral request for a current survey and required supporting documents, including who orders it and who the contract makes responsible for its cost.

Feedback: File A is missing required seller delivery, so the form places the new survey expense on seller. File B is rejection after delivery, so the selected buyer allocation applies. Under 6C(1) the new survey is to be obtained no later than three days before closing. Preserve dated receipt of each document and the lender/title rejection. Do not invoice the wrong party by using a single “survey rejected” label for both files.

chunks.heading: T04U5 — Affidavit & Notice to Prospective Buyer
chunks.excerpt:
## T04U5 — Affidavit & Notice to Prospective Buyer

The TDI [T-47 affidavit](https://www.tdi.texas.gov/title/documents/formT-47.pdf) and [T-47.1 declaration](https://www.tdi.texas.gov/title/documents/form-t-47-1.pdf) are different authorized ways of supplying the required existing-survey statements. The declaration is an unsworn declaration under the applicable law rather than a notarized affidavit. Read its certifications and identify the survey and property correctly. Neither form creates a new survey or guarantees a title company will accept an old one. The person with knowledge must answer accurately, including changes affecting the survey.

The current [Notice to Prospective Buyer, 58-0](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/notice-prospective-buyer-0), replaces the older OP-C designation. It addresses the written advice to obtain an attorney's abstract examination or a title policy and alerts the buyer to specified district notices. It is approved for use where a sale contract has not been promulgated by TREC and says it should be presented before the buyer signs an offer. On the resale form, paragraph 6E(1) supplies the title-advice language. Acknowledging general notice does not replace the seller's property-specific statutory utility or improvement-district notice.

### Statute reading exercise: Four documents, four jobs

Read T-47, T-47.1, Form 58-0, and resale paragraphs 6C and 6E. Seller Iris has a 2019 survey and knows a pool was installed in 2022. Buyer Leo receives an owner-prepared contract without the TREC title-advice text. The property is in a utility district and public improvement district. No district-specific notices have been provided.

chunks.heading: T04U6 — Property Condition: Inspection, Acceptance, Repairs
chunks.excerpt:
Create a purpose/signer/trigger/limitation chart for the two survey statements, title-advice notice, and statutory district notices. Identify the pool information that must not be omitted from the survey statement. Explain what the broker must do before the offer under the notice's instruction and what remains for the seller concerning districts. Do not certify that the old survey is acceptable.

Feedback: the affidavit/declaration addresses knowledge concerning the existing survey, while the buyer notice addresses advice and alerts. Pool construction needs accurate disclosure; title/lender decides survey acceptance. General 58-0 delivery does not supply the particular district's tax, indebtedness, assessment, or statutory acknowledgment information. The owner-prepared-contract exception does not erase the broker's statutory written title-advice duty.

## T04U6 — Property Condition: Inspection, Acceptance, Repairs

Paragraph 7A provides access at reasonable times for buyer and authorized inspectors, while seller maintains existing utilities. Hydrostatic testing requires separate written seller authorization; an inspection appointment is not that authorization. The buyer selects qualified inspectors within applicable licensing rules. An inspection is evidence about condition, not a title opinion, lender approval, or guarantee of future performance.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Authorize the investigation correctly
chunks.excerpt:
“As Is” in paragraph 7D describes acceptance of present condition with the stated exceptions. It does not prevent inspection, later repair negotiation, or timely option termination where that right exists. If selecting acceptance conditioned on specific repairs, identify actual repairs and treatments. The form warns against general phrases such as “subject to inspections.” A broad phrase does not supply an inspection contingency or explain what must be fixed.

Distinguish agreed repairs, lender-required repairs, and optional buyer upgrades. Paragraph 7E generally does not obligate either party to pay for lender-required repairs absent agreement; it states consequences if they do not agree and supplies the buyer's separate right where cost exceeds five percent of the price. Paragraph 7F regulates agreed repairs, including completion before closing, qualified repair providers, permits, documentation, and transfer of transferable warranties. An agent should not certify building compliance or draft a new remedy.

### Applied exercise: Authorize the investigation correctly

Buyer Mae's inspector proposes a general inspection, sewer camera observation, and a hydrostatic plumbing test on a 1992 house. The seller has permitted ordinary inspection access but has not signed separate hydrostatic authorization. Existing water and electricity are off. The buyer's option ends in five days. The inspector cannot complete a meaningful inspection without utilities.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Turn a report into specific repair instructions
chunks.excerpt:
Prepare an inspection action plan with permission status, responsible actor, utility requirement, scheduling deadline, and evidence for each task. Identify the official [hydrostatic testing addendum](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/addendum-authorizing-hydrostatic-testing-0) and the separate approval needed. Write a status note explaining why an inspection appointment does not authorize every testing method and why the option clock must still be tracked.

Feedback: obtain seller's separate written hydrostatic permission before that test; verify the scope of all requested methods with the qualified inspector. Seller's existing-utilities duty is in 7A. Schedule promptly, communicate limitations, and let buyer decide under existing rights before expiry. Do not conduct unauthorized testing, imply inspection extends the option, or give engineering assurances from the agent's own observation.

### Applied exercise: Turn a report into specific repair instructions

An inspection identifies a leaking main bathroom angle-stop valve, an inoperative garage-door safety reversal, a loose handrail at the rear steps, and cosmetic paint scuffs. The buyer requests repairs to the first three and accepts the paint. Seller agrees to have appropriately qualified trades complete them before closing and provide the paragraph 7F documentation. The parties do not agree to any new warranty or open-ended satisfaction contingency.

chunks.heading: T04U7 — Seller's Disclosure & Lead Based Paint Disclosure
chunks.excerpt:
Prepare a factual repair list identifying location, condition, and agreed corrective work suitable for the form's repair fields; do not write a new legal standard or remedy. Create a completion-evidence checklist and walkthrough plan. Compare the list with “fix all inspection items” and explain three ambiguities that phrase would create. Identify when attorney drafting would be necessary if the parties request a bespoke warranty.

Feedback: specific agreed work should identify the three distinct conditions and locations while excluding the unagreed paint upgrade. The inspector/trade provides technical scope if needed. Completion includes permits where required, appropriate qualification, scope/payment documentation, and transferable warranties under the form. “All inspection items” can incorporate observations, maintenance suggestions, and matters not actually negotiated. A new warranty or remedy exceeds informational completion.

## T04U7 — Seller's Disclosure & Lead Based Paint Disclosure

Texas Property Code §5.008 generally requires the seller's notice for covered previously occupied single-dwelling residential property, with specified exemptions. Determine the applicable exemption from actual facts rather than assuming every estate, investor, or never-occupied-by-this-seller transaction is exempt. A seller's absence of personal occupancy is not permission to fabricate “unknown” answers or omit known facts. The notice reports seller knowledge; it is not a warranty or a substitute for inspection. The agent's independent duty concerning known significant defects is not erased by a seller exemption.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Three disclosure timelines
chunks.excerpt:
Use current [Seller's Disclosure Notice 55-1](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/sellers-disclosure-notice). Paragraph 7B of resale separately records whether buyer received the notice, has not received it with an agreed delivery period, or seller is not required to provide it. Its nondelivery and postreceipt termination provisions must be read exactly. A late notice can create a different window from an expired option. Record actual buyer receipt and do not backdate a signature to conceal late delivery.

For most pre-1978 target housing, federal lead-disclosure requirements call for known information and available reports, the approved pamphlet, required acknowledgments, and the buyer's inspection/risk-assessment opportunity, subject to applicable exclusions and lawful waiver/modification rules. The [EPA explanation](https://www.epa.gov/lead/real-estate-disclosures-about-potential-lead-hazards) is the primary agency guide. Lack of known lead is not proof that no disclosure process is needed. The current TREC [56-0](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/addendum-sellers-disclosure-information-lead-based-paint-and-lead-based-paint-hazards-0) separately provides a waiver choice or inspection within ten days and termination notice within fourteen days if the specified hazard is present. Do not confuse that contractual fourteen-day point with the ten-day investigation opportunity or an option period.

### Statute reading exercise: Three disclosure timelines

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Complete the 2026 water-disclosure decision
chunks.excerpt:
Read [Property Code §5.008](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/PR/htm/PR.5.htm#5.008), resale 7B, and 56-0 B–F. A covered 1968 house is contracted September 8; closing is October 1. Seller's notice was not received at acceptance, is promised in five days, and actually reaches buyer September 14. The option expires September 15. Before the buyer becomes obligated, the federal lead information and pamphlet are delivered and the parties select 56-0's inspection option. No statutory exemption or lead waiver applies.

Build separate calendars for seller-notice delivery/postreceipt rights, option, lead investigation, and lead termination. Identify the required lead records and signatures and the fact that would support the selected lead termination. Explain why “option expired” does not answer every disclosure question. Record the actual receipt date, not merely the seller's form-signing date.

Feedback: the promised seller-notice delivery and actual receipt differ. Resale 7B(2) supplies a seven-day postreceipt window or prior closing, whichever occurs first, while the option has its own date. Under the selected 56-0 wording, the ten-day inspection point is September 18 and the fourteen-day notice point September 22, subject to the stated presence condition. The lead process includes known information, available reports, pamphlet, acknowledgments, and certifications; receipt does not itself certify that a hazard exists.

### Applied exercise: Complete the 2026 water-disclosure decision

chunks.heading: T04U8 — Environmental Assessment & Threatened or Endangered Species & Wetlands Addendum
chunks.excerpt:
Resale 20-19 paragraph 7I is new to many older course materials. Seller Nolan says the house receives municipal water and selects “not required.” His documents show an unused well behind the garage and a recorded groundwater lease. Buyer has received no Seller's Water Disclosure, Form 61-0. Closing is thirty days away and the draft has not been accepted.

Read 7I's five cumulative conditions for the “not required” choice. Create a condition-by-condition worksheet, identify the two supplied facts contradicting that choice, and map the correct received/not-received decision based on actual delivery. Draft a factual request for the seller-completed current disclosure and a delivery tracker. Explain why municipal service alone is insufficient and why the broker should not opine on the buyer's ability to pump groundwater.

Feedback: all five conditions must be true for 7I(3), including no known well and no known severance/sale/lease of groundwater rights. Municipal service does not cure the well or lease facts. If the disclosure has not been received, use the actual delivery status and agreed period rather than claiming receipt. The form supplies specified nondelivery/postreceipt rights; legal water rights and permitted use require appropriate expert and attorney review.

## T04U8 — Environmental Assessment & Threatened or Endangered Species & Wetlands Addendum

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Use the right report in time
chunks.excerpt:
Form [28-2](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/environmental-assessment-threatened-endangered-species-and-wetlands-addendum) permits selected buyer-paid investigations by the specified specialists: environmental assessment, threatened/endangered species or habitat, and wetlands. Its negotiated days run after effective date. Termination requires both a copy of a selected report that adversely affects property use and notice within that period; an unsupported fear or social-media photograph is not the stated report.

An ordinary property inspection may not investigate soil contamination, wetlands jurisdiction, or habitat. Identify the intended use and specialist needed early. An agent should not determine that a wet area is legally a wetland or promise that habitat protections do not apply. The addendum creates contractual investigation and termination mechanics; it does not issue a permit or remove environmental law.

### Applied exercise: Use the right report in time

Buyer Opal intends to build an additional residence on a wooded two-acre property. The accepted 28-2 selects wetlands and threatened/endangered-species reports with 24 days after effective date. On day 19 a qualified natural-resources professional issues a selected report finding habitat restrictions that adversely affect the intended building area. A landscaper separately texts “looks dry to me.” Buyer instructs termination on day 21. No extension or waiver exists.

chunks.heading: T04U9 — Residential Service Contract
chunks.excerpt:
Prepare a report-and-notice checklist, identify the professional and selected investigation, map the 24-day deadline, and draft a factual explanation of the report's role. Explain why the landscaper's text neither replaces nor negates the specialist report. Identify what counsel should review if seller disputes adverse effect. Do not guarantee permitting outcomes or omit the report from the notice package.

Feedback: the stated contractual path calls for the selected adverse-use report plus timely notice, with earnest-money refund under the addendum. The informal text does not answer the professional or legal questions. Preserve the intended-use record, report, buyer instruction, and delivery evidence; refer disputed entitlement to counsel. Completing the worksheet requires checking both the type of investigation selected and the actual deadline.

## T04U9 — Residential Service Contract

Paragraph 7H permits the buyer to purchase a residential service contract from an appropriately licensed provider/administrator and provides a negotiated seller reimbursement cap. Purchase is optional. A service contract has coverage, exclusions, limitations, fees, and claims procedures. It is not equivalent to property insurance, an inspection, a seller's promised repair, or a guarantee that any failed system will be replaced. Review actual coverage before recommending a product based solely on price.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Compare cost and coverage honestly
chunks.excerpt:
The seller reimbursement is a cap on the described cost, not automatically a cash credit for an unpurchased plan. A broker's relationship or compensation connected with the service company needs the applicable disclosure and legal analysis; use the TREC [Disclosure of Relationship with Residential Service Company, RSC-4](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/disclosure-relationship-residential-service-company) where applicable and follow the governing rule. Do not represent optional purchase as a lender or TREC requirement without a genuine source.

### Applied exercise: Compare cost and coverage honestly

The contract states a $650 maximum seller reimbursement under 7H. Buyer chooses a $720 plan with a $100 service-call fee, a $1,500 HVAC annual limit, and an exclusion for known preexisting failures. The inspection already reports an inoperative compressor. Seller separately promised to repair that compressor before closing. Agent receives a disclosed marketing relationship payment from the company, but the applicable relationship disclosure has not yet been furnished.

Prepare a cost worksheet, coverage-question list, and separate repair-completion checklist. Calculate the purchase-price portion above the stated reimbursement cap. Draft a buyer explanation distinguishing the plan from the seller's repair obligation and identify the disclosure task to review with the broker. Do not promise the plan will replace the compressor or treat the $100 fee as part of the original plan price without checking terms.

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: the plan price exceeds the cap by $70; service-call and coverage limits are additional terms to understand. Known preexisting failure raises the exclusion; it does not excuse the seller's agreed repair. Handle the relationship disclosure and applicable compensation rules before an uninformed recommendation. The worksheet should show separate contract obligations, product terms, and disclosure duties rather than one combined “warranty protection” label.

### Module recap

Audit your ledger for five distinctions: earnest money versus option fee; money delivery versus option notice; commitment versus policy; existing-survey nondelivery versus rejection; seller's notice versus lead and water disclosures. Review each independent worksheet and source exercise, correct deadlines against the exact paragraphs, and identify any question needing title, trade, environmental, insurance, or legal expertise. You should be able to explain both the required evidence and what that evidence does not establish.

lessons.title: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 05

chunks.heading: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 05
chunks.excerpt:
# Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 05

Closing, Possession and More. The required sources are [resale 20-19](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/one-four-family-residential-contract-resale), paragraphs 8–23 and its execution/contact/receipt pages; [Seller's Temporary Residential Lease 15-7](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/sellers-temporary-residential-lease); [Buyer's Temporary Residential Lease 16-7](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/buyers-temporary-residential-lease); and the current [Amendment 39-11](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/amendment). Closing is a coordinated performance event. It must not be reduced to an appointment at which someone signs whatever has arrived.

## T05U1 — Closing Paragraph & Buyer's Possession Paragraphs in Contract

Paragraph 9A states an on-or-before closing date, with the specified interaction for objections cured or waived under paragraph 6D. Read both paragraphs before telling anyone the original calendar date remains controlling. Paragraph 9B identifies seller's deed/title and tax documentation, buyer's good funds, necessary closing documents, satisfaction of liens except properly assumed loans, and transfer-fee treatment. The title professional prepares the settlement process; each party remains responsible for the promised performance.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Closing-day authority to release keys
chunks.excerpt:
Possession in paragraph 10A is a separate selection: at closing and funding, or under a written temporary lease. Signing before funding does not satisfy a closing-and-funding possession trigger. Buyer possession before closing and seller possession afterward require the correct written arrangement; otherwise the form describes a tenancy at sufferance. Insurance coverage may change when ownership and occupancy separate. Refer both parties to their insurers before the change, rather than promising a homeowner policy continues unchanged.

Paragraph 10B adds a practical modern handoff. At possession, seller provides access information necessary to operate and manage smart devices and removes seller's connections and access as specified. A key receipt should include gate, garage, alarm, doorbell, thermostat, and other agreed control information, while protecting passwords and personal data. Do not publicly email an entire security credential list to every transaction participant.

### Applied exercise: Closing-day authority to release keys

Buyer Owen signs on Monday morning, seller Petra signs Monday afternoon, and the lender funds Tuesday at 2:00 p.m. The contract selects possession at closing and funding with no lease. On Monday evening Owen's movers arrive and ask the agent for the lockbox code. Petra's personal account still controls the garage app and doorbell. Both parties expect Tuesday possession when funding is confirmed.

Prepare a possession checklist with the actual trigger, confirmation source, key/control inventory, insurance referral, and access-removal evidence. Draft Monday's factual response to the movers and Tuesday's transfer record. Explain why an agent's desire to avoid moving charges cannot substitute for an authorized lease or changed agreement.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A closing-document readiness table
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: Monday signatures alone do not authorize the selected possession. Confirm closing and funding before Tuesday release, coordinate the smart-device transfer/removal, and document delivery securely. Movers are not parties authorized to change the agreement. If the parties wish to change possession, use a proper written arrangement with appropriate advice before access, not a retroactive note after occupancy.

### Applied exercise: A closing-document readiness table

Closing is October 29. The settlement file has buyer's signed loan papers, an unsigned seller deed, a payoff quote expiring October 27, proof of earnest money, an unverified wire instruction email, and no final repair invoice. No document establishes that the lien is assumed. Seller promised completed roof flashing repairs and required documentation before closing.

Prepare a readiness table marking each item complete, incomplete, expired, or requiring verification. Assign each next step to the appropriate party/professional. Identify the contract provisions governing deed, lien satisfaction, repair evidence, and good funds. Draft a concise status message that identifies blockers without claiming the sale failed or the title is defective. Include an independent verification step for wire instructions using a known trusted contact.

chunks.heading: T05U2 — Special Provisions
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: obtain the executed deed through the closing professional, an updated payoff, verified good-funds instructions, and repair evidence. Loan papers and deposit receipt prove only their own events. An expiring payoff can change the amount needed; it is not a reason to fabricate a payoff. Verify wiring details through an independently known channel before funds move. The buyer and seller receive accurate status and make needed decisions with counsel if deadlines or remedies are at issue.

## T05U2 — Special Provisions

Paragraph 11 is for additional informational items, not a workshop for drafting legal protections. Current §537.11 defines informational items and expressly limits agent-authored language affecting rights, obligations, or remedies. A factual delivery instruction is different from a new termination right. A repair field or mandatory addendum should be used for its intended subject rather than repeating competing terms in special provisions.

Consistency is part of accuracy. If paragraph 9 says October 30 and special provisions say November 15, the document may create an interpretive dispute instead of a clear extension. If the standard financing addendum governs appraisal and another sentence announces a different deadline, the agent has introduced a potential conflict. Refer proposed bespoke language to the principal's attorney and preserve specific written directions for any allowed insertion. Never discourage attorney review because “the form already protects everybody.”

### Applied exercise: Route six requested terms

chunks.heading: T05U3 — Seller's Temporary Lease Form & Buyer's Temporary Lease Form
chunks.excerpt:
Buyer asks for: price $398,000; closing November 12; a seller contribution of $5,000 toward ordinary buyer expenses; $8,000 toward buyer's broker obligation; a seven-day option extension for an additional $200; and a new right to cancel if a nearby road ever becomes busier. The transaction is already under contract. No change has yet been accepted.

Build a routing sheet naming the applicable amendment/contract field for each standard change and identifying the bespoke request requiring direct legal assistance. Explain why brokerage contribution must not be hidden in the ordinary expense field under 20-19. List all original deadlines to keep active while the amendment is pending and the evidence needed before updating the transaction tracker.

Feedback: use current amendment choices and the corresponding price, closing, expense, brokerage, and option provisions, checking the exact 39-11 fields. The speculative road condition is a new legal contingency, not informational completion. Paragraph 12A(1)(b) excludes brokerage contributions now handled in 12B. Pending negotiations do not change existing terms; accepted written changes and their communication must be recorded.

## T05U3 — Seller's Temporary Lease Form & Buyer's Temporary Lease Form

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Reverse the roles correctly
chunks.excerpt:
The seller's temporary lease, 15-7, is for seller occupancy no more than ninety days after closing. Buyer becomes landlord and seller becomes tenant. The term begins on closing and funding and ends at the stated point, subject to the lease. Daily rent excludes the day of closing and funding and the anticipated rent is paid at funding. The deposit is security for lease obligations, distinct from purchase earnest money. The lease supplies its own deposit accounting, utility, pet, maintenance, inspection, default, holdover, notice, and attorney provisions.

The buyer's temporary lease, 16-7, is for buyer occupancy no more than ninety days before closing. Seller is landlord and buyer is tenant. The lease has a commencement date, anticipated rent paid at commencement, adjustment if actual term differs, and a termination provision tied to the contract and other stated events. The form expressly says rent is not applied to purchase-contract items. Do not casually promise that rent becomes a down payment. Deposit treatment must be read for whether closing occurs or the lease ends beforehand.

In both forms, identify all parties, property, dates, daily amounts, deposits, utilities, pets, holdover damages, and notice addresses from agreed instructions. Their repair provisions are subject to the Texas Property Code; a brief lease does not authorize ignoring nonwaivable duties. Current forms warn that changed possession can alter insurance coverage. Ninety-day intended use does not mean every short arrangement is suitable for the form, especially unusual commercial occupancy or an indefinite stay. Longer or unusual arrangements require appropriate forms and legal review.

### Statute reading exercise: Reverse the roles correctly

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Calculate seller lease rent and holdover
chunks.excerpt:
Read 15-7 and 16-7 in full. In File A, buyers Quinn and Rhea close and fund October 15; seller Silas stays through October 25 at $125/day, $2,000 deposit, all utilities paid by Silas, one cat allowed, and holdover damages $250/day. In File B, seller Tara lets buyer Uriel occupy October 10 before anticipated October 20 closing at $90/day, $1,500 deposit, utilities paid by Uriel, no pets, and $180/day holdover damages. No special modifications exist.

Prepare a field map for each form, identifying landlord/tenant, correct commencement/ending mechanism, rent-payment timing, deposit, utilities, pets, and holdover. Compare the insurance, inspection, repairs, and termination provisions in writing. For File B, identify the exact lease clause governing a sale that never closes rather than inventing a fixed end date.

Feedback: A uses 15-7 with the buyers as landlords and seller as tenant; B uses 16-7 with seller as landlord and buyer as tenant. Roles follow occupancy and ownership timing, not who originally hired the agent. Rent and deposit remain separate amounts. Use the actual printed termination mechanism in 16-7 and do not assume failure to close gives the occupant a continuing right to stay.

### Applied exercise: Calculate seller lease rent and holdover

Use File A from the source review. Closing and funding actually occur October 15. The stated temporary lease ends October 25, and the parties agree this exercise's rental count includes October 16 through October 25. Silas remains through two additional full days after termination. The lease's daily rent is $125 and its holdover damages are $250 per day. No agreed extension exists. Silas provides a forwarding address after surrender; no deposit deduction has yet been determined.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Early occupancy without the right documents
chunks.excerpt:
Calculate ordinary rent and the stated two-day holdover amount separately. Prepare a ledger identifying the deposit as security rather than automatic liquidated rent. Draft a possession follow-up and identify who should advise on removal or disputed remedies. Explain why paying holdover damages does not itself renew the lease.

Feedback: ten charged rental days produce $1,250; two stated holdover days produce $500 under the supplied rate. The $2,000 deposit is not automatically forfeited; follow the lease's accounting and applicable law. Holdover payment is not consent to extension. The landlord needs appropriate legal advice for enforcement; the agent should not attempt self-help removal or change locks based on a course calculation.

### Applied exercise: Early occupancy without the right documents

Buyer Veda asks to move into seller Wren's home seven days before closing. The purchase contract still selects closing-and-funding possession. The lender has not cleared the loan, buyer proposes to paint two rooms immediately, and neither insurer has reviewed early occupancy. Wren says “fine” in a phone call but no lease terms, deposit, rent, maintenance arrangement, or default provisions have been agreed.

Prepare an early-occupancy risk and information checklist, identify the contract/lease changes needed, and distinguish who approves alterations, insurance, and financing. Draft a neutral response explaining the missing agreement work. List the consequences that must be understood if the purchase fails. Do not treat the phone call as a fully completed 16-7 or improvise a lease in special provisions.

chunks.heading: T05U4 — Settlement & Other Expenses
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: obtain the appropriate written possession arrangement with complete agreed terms before access. The proposed painting raises alteration consent, condition, insurance, and failed-closing issues. A pending loan can fail while a tenancy exists. The principals and their professionals decide whether the arrangement is acceptable; an agent cannot guarantee coverage or erase occupancy rights by writing “buyer assumes all risk.”

## T05U4 — Settlement & Other Expenses

Paragraph 12A assigns seller and buyer expenses and gives a separate seller cap toward buyer expenses. In 20-19 that cap expressly excludes brokerage compensation and contributions under 12B. Paragraph 12B states compensation is fully negotiable and not set by law. Each party's obligation to its own broker is in separate written agreements; selected seller-to-buyer-broker or buyer-to-seller-broker contributions apply toward those obligations without changing them. Read the compensation agreement and contract together rather than assuming one replaces the other.

Separate a contractual cap, actual eligible expense, lender limitation, and broker obligation. A $6,000 concession does not guarantee the buyer can use all $6,000 if actual eligible costs are lower or loan rules restrict it. Nor may unused ordinary expense credit be silently diverted to brokerage compensation. Confirm with the lender and closing professional. Paragraph 12C addresses prohibited buyer charges in governmental loan programs and the priority application of the stated concession; it does not make the agent the authority on every loan-program rule.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Separate the two contribution fields
chunks.excerpt:
Settlement math should show gross price, applicable credits/debits, deposits, financing, prorations, and net cash. Avoid a misleading “net” figure that omits taxes or compensation. Use actual signed terms and verified invoices. If the statement disagrees with the contract, investigate and obtain a corrected statement or an authorized agreement change; do not simply tell the buyer the title company has the final say over negotiated terms.

### Statute reading exercise: Separate the two contribution fields

Read 20-19 paragraphs 12A–C and a hypothetical separate buyer representation agreement requiring $10,500 buyer brokerage compensation. Price is $420,000. The sales contract has $6,000 in 12A(1)(b) and a seller contribution of 2% of price in 12B(1). Eligible ordinary buyer expenses total $5,500; no lender limitation changes these figures. No other compensation credits or amendments exist.

Prepare a three-ledger worksheet for ordinary expenses, seller brokerage contribution, and the buyer's remaining brokerage obligation. Calculate each amount and explain why unused ordinary concession does not automatically move to brokerage. Identify who must approve any desired new arrangement and what must be checked with the lender. Write a buyer explanation that does not call 2% a standard rate.

Feedback: seller pays $5,500 eligible ordinary expenses under the $6,000 cap, not an automatic $6,000 cash gift. Two percent of $420,000 is $8,400 toward the $10,500 brokerage obligation, leaving $2,100 absent other agreed credits. The unspent $500 is not automatically brokerage money because 12A excludes it. Compensation is negotiated; any changed contribution or obligation needs the appropriate agreement and lender review.

### Applied exercise: Correct a settlement estimate

chunks.heading: T05U5 — Prorations, Casualty Loss, Default & Mediation of Contract
chunks.excerpt:
For that same transaction, the draft statement charges seller $6,000 ordinary concession although only $5,500 eligible costs are shown, applies a $9,000 brokerage contribution, and reduces buyer brokerage obligation to $9,000 despite no changed representation agreement. It also omits buyer's verified $4,000 earnest-money credit. Assume all other listed amounts are correct and no additional expenses or credits exist.

Create a correction table for each discrepancy, with correct amount, signed source, and party/professional to contact. Explain which errors are statement corrections and which would require new agreement if the parties actually want the draft amounts. Calculate the difference in each affected line without inventing a complete cash-to-close total from partial facts.

Feedback: ordinary eligible concession should be $5,500, brokerage contribution $8,400, contractual brokerage obligation remains $10,500, and verified earnest money must receive the proper credit. A desired $9,000 contribution or reduced broker fee requires the appropriate written change rather than a silent ledger edit. The exercise supplies partial settlement figures, so a final cash-to-close number would be fabricated.

## T05U5 — Prorations, Casualty Loss, Default & Mediation of Contract

Paragraph 13 prorates taxes, interest, rents, and regular periodic charges through closing. Estimated tax proration is adjusted when actual statements become available if amounts differ. Use the agreed day-count basis and identify who is charged or credited. Seller's current tax exemption may not reflect the buyer's future tax situation. Do not present an estimate as a guarantee of next year's taxes or appraised value.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Proration and a casualty election
chunks.excerpt:
Paragraph 14 requires seller to restore casualty damage to its previous condition as soon as reasonably possible and by closing. If restoration fails due to factors beyond seller's control, the printed buyer alternatives include termination/refund, an extension up to fifteen days, or damaged-condition acceptance with an allowed insurance-proceeds assignment and deductible credit. These are alternatives under specific facts. A casualty is not automatically a buyer-default event or a requirement to accept whatever insurance pays.

Paragraph 15's default remedies are distinct from ordinary contingency termination. Paragraph 16 requires unresolved buyer/seller contract disputes to go to mutually acceptable mediation after informal discussion, with costs shared equally, while preserving equitable relief as stated. Mediation is not a decision imposed by the mediator in the same manner as a judgment. Paragraph 17 addresses reasonable attorney fees and proceeding costs for the stated prevailing participants; it is not a broker's promise that counsel will be free.

### Applied exercise: Proration and a casualty election

Part A: annual taxes are estimated at $7,300, use a 365-day basis, and the agreed settlement count allocates 273 days to seller. Taxes are unpaid and buyer will pay the annual bill. Part B is a separate file: a storm damages the roof after effective date; seller cannot restore by closing because materials are unavailable, a factor stipulated beyond seller's control. The insurer permits assignment of proceeds; deductible is $2,500. Buyer has not chosen an alternative.

chunks.heading: T05U6 — Escrow Provisions
chunks.excerpt:
Calculate the seller tax debit/buyer credit and explain the later true-up. For Part B create an alternatives chart from paragraph 14, identifying what must be confirmed before damaged-condition acceptance and who chooses. Explain why a broker should not unilaterally select the fifteen-day extension or promise insurance coverage beyond the actual carrier decision.

Feedback: $7,300 ÷ 365 = $20/day; 273 days gives $5,460 seller debit and buyer credit on the supplied convention. Actual taxes can require adjustment. The casualty alternatives belong to buyer under the stipulated clause conditions; assignment requires carrier permission and the deductible credit must be addressed. This is separate from declaring default. Counsel and insurer should resolve disputed legal or coverage issues before a choice is implemented.

## T05U6 — Escrow Provisions

Paragraph 18 explains that escrow is not a party responsible for buyer's or seller's performance. It may require collected good funds, handle authorized expenses, and follow its release and demand procedure. At closing earnest money is applied first to cash down payment, then buyer expenses, with excess refunded. Without closing, authorized expenses and release requirements must be examined rather than treating every dollar as instantly payable on demand.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: An objected-to earnest-money demand
chunks.excerpt:
The demand process and objection receipt matter. A written demand by one party is copied to the other; the form describes fifteen days for written objection and permits specified disbursement if no objection is received. Paragraph 18E distinguishes effectiveness of escrow notices from receipt of an objection to a demand. “May disburse” is not “must wire immediately.” Wrongful refusal to sign a release has separate paragraph 18D consequences; an agent should not pronounce refusal wrongful without the relevant facts and legal advice.

### Applied exercise: An objected-to earnest-money demand

Seller sends escrow a written demand for $5,500 earnest money after a disputed termination. Escrow forwards it as required. Buyer delivers a written objection that escrow actually receives within the fifteen-day period. Seller asks the agent to say the funds must still be released because the buyer did not sign the seller's preferred release. No court order or mutual settlement exists.

Prepare a chronology showing demand, forwarding, actual objection receipt, and present dispute. Identify the paragraph preventing treatment of this as an unopposed demand. Draft an escrow-status message and a counsel referral preserving both parties' positions. Explain why receipt evidence is critical and why the agent should not characterize refusal as wrongful simply because one party demands it.

chunks.heading: T05U7 — Other Contract Provisions
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: timely received objection means the unopposed-demand disbursement condition is not established. Escrow follows the governing agreement and applicable process; the broker cannot adjudicate entitlement. Preserve the objection and proof of receipt. A release's wording, underlying termination, authorized expenses, and possible remedies require proper review, not an automatic payment instruction from the agent.

## T05U7 — Other Contract Provisions

Paragraph 19 states the contract's covenants, representations, and warranties survive closing; an untrue seller representation at closing puts seller in default under its wording. It also permits continued showings and receipt, negotiation, and acceptance of backup offers unless prohibited by written agreement. Do not tell a seller that a signed primary contract automatically forbids every backup discussion, and do not treat a backup as a replacement for the primary without its own terms.

Paragraph 20 addresses governmental requirements, including foreign-person tax withholding and requested reporting information. Citizenship, ethnicity, accent, and national origin do not establish tax-residency status. Refer the actual FIRPTA analysis to qualified tax and closing professionals. The buyer may have withholding duties under applicable law; a seller's assertion that withholding “is only the title company's problem” is unsafe. The course does not supply tax rates or exemptions for a real transaction without verified facts.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A late-page audit
chunks.excerpt:
Paragraph 21 governs written notices and provides party and agent contact fields. Accurate contacts are functional contract data. Paragraph 22 integrates the agreement, requires written changes, and organizes financial, lease, testing, statutory, and other attachments. It expressly warns that missing applicable statutory disclosures can create remedies. Paragraph 23 directs attorney consultation before signing. These late pages are not optional administrative decoration; they can determine how substantive rights are exercised.

### Applied exercise: A late-page audit

The draft's buyer notice email is missing one letter; seller notice address is an old property; 22 checks a fixture-lease addendum that is not attached; a required district notice is absent; and buyer's attorney has not been offered the chance to review an unusual water-right reservation. Seller says all the “important money pages” are complete. The draft is not signed.

Create a five-row defect/location/consequence/repair table. Identify how to verify each contact, who supplies the missing attachment/notice, and which matter needs direct legal review. Explain why checking an attachment box does not incorporate a nonexistent agreed document. Prepare an accurate remaining-work message without claiming the draft is ready for signatures.

Feedback: correct verified notice contacts, obtain and review actual attachments, satisfy applicable district notice requirements, and facilitate direct counsel review of the unusual reservation before execution. Paragraphs 21–23 affect delivery, completeness, and advice. A form that adds up financially can still be incomplete or dangerous to present as final. Preserve the corrected version and all attached documents together.

chunks.heading: T05U8 — Executing the Contract & Finalizing the Agreement
chunks.excerpt:
## T05U8 — Executing the Contract & Finalizing the Agreement

Final review works in two directions. Read from the first page forward for the bargain; then read from signatures and attachments backward to ensure every referenced term is actually part of the accepted package. Verify exact parties and capacities, all material changes, selected alternatives, agreed blanks, legibility, attachments, final-acceptance evidence, and current form version. Do not fill an unresolved choice with a customary value simply because the software requires a field.

On 20-19 the broker contact page says to print names and not sign. Parties sign the execution page; escrow completes the appropriate receipt acknowledgments for what escrow receives. These are different functions. A broker contact entry is not a compensation agreement, a party signature, or a new representation consent. The effective date is final acceptance, supported by the actual communication sequence. Do not backdate it to align with a lender's preferred schedule.

After acceptance distribute the complete accepted package, confirm escrow receipt and payment deadlines, and initialize the performance calendar. Keep amendments, notices, evidence, and superseded drafts distinguishable. An electronic-signature audit trail can support attribution and timing but must be reviewed with the actual record; technology does not cure the wrong party signing or an absent attachment.

### Applied exercise: Final package quality check

chunks.heading: T05U9 — Case Study/Workshop
chunks.excerpt:
Buyer Ximena and seller Yusuf accept a twelve-page 20-19 packet. Pages 1–10 name Lot 4; one attached finance form names a different street number; the seller's spouse is a required signer according to the closing attorney but has not signed; the broker signs the contact-only page; and escrow's receipt is blank because nothing has yet been delivered. The effective-date blank was prefilled a day before final acceptance.

Prepare an issue list separating incorrect data, missing required signature, unnecessary broker signature, unearned receipt, and wrong date. State the evidence and professional instruction required to resolve each. Explain why you must preserve the actual signed record and obtain a proper corrected agreement rather than quietly edit it after signatures. Draft a distribution checklist for the final verified package.

Feedback: the mismatched attachment and required signer need actual correction and assent; broker contact information is printed rather than signed; escrow alone acknowledges actual receipt; effective date follows real final acceptance. Silent post-signature changes would compromise the evidence. The attorney's supplied required-signature determination controls this hypothetical; do not substitute an agent's marital-status assumption.

## T05U9 — Case Study/Workshop

The workshop is a closing simulation, not a final examination. Produce separate artifacts for each stage. The facts below use a new transaction so that you must organize the workflow yourself. The assessed scenario assigned to this topic is a separate decision task and is not a second time credit for these worksheets.

### Statute reading exercise: Read the whole closing sequence

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Construct the buyer's simplified cash ledger
chunks.excerpt:
Read 20-19 paragraphs 9–23 in order and then trace every cross-reference back to its target. For a $460,000 purchase closing November 18, list every provision that might affect date, funds, possession, disclosures, notices, or post-closing obligations. The parties have $92,000 cash and $368,000 financing, $5,000 earnest money, $350 option fee, seller ordinary-expense cap $4,000, seller brokerage contribution $9,000, seller leaseback through November 24, and an agreed repair not yet documented.

Build a two-page checklist organized by before closing, at closing/funding, at possession, and after closing. Each line needs an actor, document, contractual citation, and evidence of completion. Identify which amounts cannot be combined and which details remain missing. Mark at least three cross-references that would be missed by reviewing only the closing paragraph.

Feedback: trace title objections into closing, repairs into completion/remedies, possession into lease and device access, expense/contribution fields into separate agreements, and escrow into good-funds/deposit handling. Include proration true-up and surviving representations after closing. Missing lease rate/deposit/terms, actual expenses, repair evidence, and complete notices are unresolved facts, not invitations to fill customary numbers.

### Applied exercise: Construct the buyer's simplified cash ledger

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Deliver possession after a leaseback
chunks.excerpt:
For this simulation only, all lender limitations have been checked. Price $460,000; loan proceeds $368,000; earnest money $5,000; option fee $350; eligible buyer ordinary expenses $6,200; seller ordinary contribution $4,000; buyer brokerage obligation $11,000; seller brokerage contribution $9,000; seller tax credit to buyer $5,900. No other charges or credits exist in this simplified worksheet. Do not include the separate seller lease rent or deposit in buyer purchase cash.

Compute the cash needed from buyer at closing, showing each line and its sign. Explain why the loan, earnest money, option fee, expense concession, brokerage contribution, and proration are six different entries. Prepare a verification note that labels the result a simplified exercise rather than an actual Closing Disclosure.

Feedback: starting with $92,000 price cash, subtract $5,000 earnest money and $350 option credit; add $2,200 uncovered ordinary expenses and $2,000 remaining brokerage obligation; subtract $5,900 seller tax credit. Result is $84,950. The number is valid only for the supplied closed set of facts. It is not a quote for a live purchase; actual settlement requires all verified charges, credits, funds, and program requirements.

### Applied exercise: Deliver possession after a leaseback

The simulated closing and funding occur November 18. The executed 15-7 gives seller occupancy through November 24 at $140/day excluding closing day, $2,400 deposit, seller-paid utilities, and $280/day holdover damages. Seller promises to deliver keys, access credentials, and control of the alarm/thermostat at surrender. On November 24 the buyer finds a new broken window and seller's boxes still in one bedroom. No agreement permits partial surrender or extended occupancy.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Resolve a closing-date change consistently
chunks.excerpt:
Calculate anticipated ordinary rent using the stated November 19–24 count. Prepare a surrender-condition record distinguishing observation from a legal conclusion, a device handoff checklist, and a deposit-accounting follow-up. Identify the professionals needed if surrender or damage is disputed and explain why the agent should not immediately release the entire deposit or remove the boxes.

Feedback: six days at $140 equals $840. Document the condition and remaining possession, obtain lawful instructions and advice, and follow the lease/deposit process. A broken window may support a claim but the exercise does not decide causation or allowable deduction. Smart-device access is part of the practical possession work. Partial occupancy is not automatically a renewed lease and does not authorize self-help eviction.

### Applied exercise: Resolve a closing-date change consistently

On November 16 the parties agree to move closing from November 18 to November 20 because a repair will be completed November 19. They want seller's lease to end November 24 unchanged, ordinary daily rent still $140, and all other terms unchanged. The lender and title company confirm they can perform November 20. No party has signed the current amendment yet.

Prepare a proposed change matrix identifying the amendment fields, lease-start interaction, rent recalculation, and financing/property-approval dates requiring fresh review. Keep original terms marked active until agreement is effective. Recalculate the seller lease's expected charged days using November 21–24 after the new closing/funding date. Write the document-distribution and calendar-update steps after final acceptance of the amendment.

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: the new anticipated lease rent is four days × $140 = $560 if closing/funding occurs November 20 and the end date remains November 24. Update date-linked provisions carefully rather than changing only the closing date in the software. The amendment is proposed until properly agreed; distribute the accepted version and recheck the financing, title, repairs, and possession deadlines against their actual wording.

### Module recap

Review all closing artifacts against the signed-source principle: every amount, date, and authority must trace to the actual agreement or verified document. Explain why signature, closing, funding, and possession may occur separately; why ordinary expense contribution is different from brokerage contribution; and why a demand does not decide a disputed deposit. Correct your independent calculations and field maps, then complete the topic's separate scenario and quiz. Preserve the limitations of the simplified financial exercises when discussing real files.

lessons.title: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 06

chunks.heading: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 06
chunks.excerpt:
# Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 06

The Remaining Promulgated Forms.
