The required comparison set is [resale 20-19](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/one-four-family-residential-contract-resale), [condominium resale 30-18](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/residential-condominium-contract-resale-0), [Farm and Ranch 25-17](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/farm-and-ranch-contract-0), [Unimproved Property 9-18](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/unimproved-property-contract-0), [New Home Incomplete Construction 23-20](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/new-home-contract-incomplete-construction-0), and [New Home Completed Construction 24-20](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/new-home-contract-completed-construction-0). These six currently listed contracts are effective July 1, 2026. The form number and actual terms must be checked again when TREC revises them.

## T06U1 — Overview of Forms

Select a form by the legal and physical transaction, not its marketing nickname. A “townhouse” may be a condominium unit or a fee-simple lot with an attached house. A “ranch-style home” may be an ordinary suburban resale. A rural parcel may involve agricultural equipment, crops, surface leases, mineral interests, acreage adjustment, and rollback taxes. Identify those facts before deciding that the familiar residential form is sufficient.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Verify all six form families
chunks.excerpt:
Current Chapter 537 identifies the adopted form and intended use. Sections 537.20, .28, .30, .31, .33, and .35 govern the unimproved, resale, incomplete-new-home, completed-new-home, farm-and-ranch, and condominium families respectively. A project involving commercial development, construction closing before completion, new condominium sales, or other complexity may not fit these standard forms. Apply §537.11's exception and attorney-review rules rather than forcing the facts into an unsuitable document.

Common structure creates efficiency but also traps. Several forms share price, money delivery, title, default, and notice concepts, yet paragraph letters, exceptions, attachments, and property-specific duties differ. A checklist copied from resale can incorrectly call a condominium objection paragraph “6D” or overlook a farm acreage adjustment. Build a form-specific field map every time. Similar headings are a prompt to compare, not proof of identical obligations.

### Statute reading exercise: Verify all six form families

Open the six official pages and the corresponding Chapter 537 adoption rules. Create a matrix of form number, current effective date, intended transaction, one explicit limit, and official source. Then place these six files in the matrix: occupied single-family resale; condominium unit resale; working cattle acreage; vacant platted residential lot; unfinished builder home to close after completion; completed never-occupied builder home.

For each, identify a fact that would force reconsideration, such as condominium ownership, a commercial purpose, or closing before completion. Explain the difference between a form's date and the 2016 course-outline date. Check the matrix directly against the source before continuing.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Diagnose a misleading property label
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: the course outline supplies the subjects; current adoption supplies the transaction forms. Each file has a likely indicated family, subject to the actual facts and exceptions. The unfinished-home form expressly excludes closing before construction completion and condominium transactions. A warehouse or new condominium is not automatically covered by one of these six simply because the course teaches six contracts.

### Applied exercise: Diagnose a misleading property label

Three listings say “townhome.” A conveys Unit 9 with an undivided interest in common elements under a recorded condominium declaration. B conveys Lot 9, Block 2, with the seller owning the land beneath an attached residence; a property owners association maintains the entry. C is an unfinished condominium unit sold by the developer. All will be used as residences.

Prepare a selection memo for each identifying the legal fact, likely form path, and missing documents. Explain why the common marketing word does not control and why the presence of an association does not make B a condominium. For C, identify the need for the appropriate developer/attorney instrument and statutory analysis instead of choosing a resale condominium form automatically.

Feedback: A fits condominium resale; B may fit ordinary resale with the appropriate association addendum; C requires analysis of a new condominium transaction. Read the deed/declaration and actual ownership regime. An association is not synonymous with condominium ownership. The memo should identify where counsel and title evidence are needed rather than declaring a legal regime solely from a listing photograph.

## T06U2 — Differences Between 1-4 Family Residential Contract & Other Contracts

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Produce a paragraph crosswalk
chunks.excerpt:
The property definition changes with ownership. The condominium form identifies the unit, building, project, declaration, common elements, limited common elements, and assigned parking. The farm form includes agricultural/residential improvements and accessories, crops, and an attached description suitable for the rural tract. The unimproved form's intended subject has no physical buildings, additions, or fixtures. New-home forms address completed or future improvements and their construction/warranty/insulation information.

Title and property-condition mechanisms must match those definitions. Condominium document and resale-certificate delivery can trigger buyer rights separate from ordinary title commitment or option deadlines. Farm property can have surface leases and acreage-price adjustment, with cost consequences that depend on selected fields. New construction has written change orders, allowances, completion criteria, and selected finishes that an existing-home repair paragraph cannot adequately represent.

Read even familiar late pages. The current Farm and Ranch form includes brokerage fee sections with stated restrictions; do not transplant the resale contact-only assumptions to every other form. A separate fee agreement or selected contribution may make signing a particular fee section inappropriate according to its instruction. A complete review asks what each form actually says, including its warning above signatures.

### Statute reading exercise: Produce a paragraph crosswalk

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Replace a copied checklist
chunks.excerpt:
Compare paragraphs 2, 6, 7, 12, and 13 of all six current forms. Build a worksheet with five rows per form: property description, title/documents, condition/construction, brokerage/expense contributions, and prorations/special taxes. For each row name one identical concept and one material difference or a confirmed absence of difference. Use pinpoint paragraph letters, not a general citation to the PDF.

Then trace the farm form's fee-section instruction and the resale contact-only page. Explain why copying a signature instruction between the two without reading is unsafe. Mark each finding as verified from the actual form, and preserve unresolved legal questions for direct counsel review.

Feedback: identify the condominium documents in paragraph 2 and its form-specific objection letters; farm crops, surface leases, acreage adjustment, and rollback allocation; incomplete-construction documents/allowances/completion; and completed-new-home warranty/insulation provisions. The crosswalk is successful only if it records actual provisions rather than filling every cell with “same as resale.” Fee/contact areas must be read on their own terms.

### Applied exercise: Replace a copied checklist

A staff member reuses a resale checklist for a condominium. It demands a seller T-47 survey package, ignores declaration/bylaws/rules and certificate, labels objections as 6D, and tells the buyer association approval is irrelevant because price is agreed. The supplied condominium declaration has a right of first refusal. No documents or association certification have yet been received.

chunks.heading: T06U3 — Residential Condominium Contract
chunks.excerpt:
Write a corrected checklist using 30-18 paragraphs 2B–D and 6. Identify each copied assumption that must be removed or verified, the required document-delivery blanks, the certificate-age requirement, and the right-of-refusal mechanism. Explain what happens to the effective-date analysis under the actual clause if the required certification arrives. Do not invent a waiver by the association.

Feedback: condominium-specific documents and certificate are central. Under 2D, the stated certification that refusal rights were complied with and not exercised/waived affects the effective date; failure within the negotiated period or exercise has the printed termination consequence. The current certificate must meet the form's age and content requirements. Use 30-18's title objection paragraph, not resale numbering. A price agreement does not erase the declaration's stated process.

## T06U3 — Residential Condominium Contract

Paragraph 2A identifies the unit together with its interests in common elements and appurtenant limited common elements. Assigned parking needs accurate identification. A seller's use of space P-14 does not prove ownership of it or the right to assign it. Read the declaration, plat, amendments, and any assignment. Storage, balconies, garages, and rooftop rights can have similar distinctions. Describe the interest verified by the documents; do not promise exclusive ownership when there is only a license to use.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: The two condo delivery records
chunks.excerpt:
Paragraph 2B addresses declaration, bylaws, and association rules as Documents. It records receipt or requires delivery within agreed days and supplies the stated seven-day termination right after receipt, while retaining statutory rights. Paragraph 2C separately addresses the Resale Certificate, which must be prepared no more than three months before delivery and include at least the information required by Property Code §82.157. A certificate is not the declaration; neither substitutes for the other. The form's special affidavit/waiver choice requires its stated facts and agreement; it is not a shortcut for an agent who forgot to order the certificate.

Read [Property Code §§82.156–.157](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/PR/htm/PR.82.htm#82.157) with the contract. Documents reveal governance, assessments, litigation, insurance, and use restrictions relevant to affordability and intended use. A lender's project approval is a different determination from the buyer's satisfaction with those records. Association right-of-refusal provisions under 2D may change the effective-date sequence and the contract's status. Calendar each receipt and decision independently.

### Statute reading exercise: The two condo delivery records

Read 30-18 paragraph 2 and Property Code §82.157. Seller Asha offers Unit 204, Building C, Lake Heron Condominiums, in Dallas County, with parking P-22 assigned by the declaration. Buyer Basil has not received Documents or Certificate. The parties specify ten days for Documents and twelve for Certificate. Effective date is October 1; Documents arrive October 8; Certificate arrives October 12 but was prepared June 1. No right of first refusal exists.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Evaluate a condo special assessment
chunks.excerpt:
Complete the paragraph 2 field map and separate receipt/deadline entries. Identify the problem with the certificate date and the professional/association follow-up needed. Extract five categories of certificate information that can affect the purchase. Explain why the Documents' receipt date does not also become the certificate receipt date.

Feedback: the June 1 certificate is more than three months old on October 12 and does not meet the form's age requirement. Obtain a compliant certificate and legal advice if timing/rights are disputed. The Documents and Certificate have distinct receipt and termination provisions. Relevant information includes assessments, association finances, litigation, insurance, and other statutory required items. The parking assignment must trace to the condominium records, not verbal assurances.

### Applied exercise: Evaluate a condo special assessment

Buyer Celeste receives a current certificate disclosing $410 monthly regular dues, an approved $6,000 roof assessment payable in six $1,000 installments, and pending litigation over a common wall. The certificate arrives during the applicable contract review period. Celeste's lender has not approved the project. The listing had described dues as $350 and “no assessments.” Seller confirms the certificate is accurate. No allocation of the special assessment has been resolved beyond the actual contract wording.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Parking and limited common elements
chunks.excerpt:
Prepare a corrected cost summary separating recurring dues and special assessment. Identify the discrepancy to correct in communications, documents counsel should review, lender follow-up, and buyer decision deadline. Read the actual contract allocation before stating who pays particular installments. Draft a factual explanation that neither promises lender approval nor treats litigation as automatic cancellation.

Feedback: use verified $410 dues and the disclosed $6,000 assessment schedule; correct the inaccurate representation. Contract allocation and legal advice determine the particular payment issue, and the buyer's document rights must be tracked. Project approval is separate. The existence of litigation matters but does not automatically prove default, bad title, or a right outside the actual agreement.

### Applied exercise: Parking and limited common elements

Seller Devon uses two garage spaces but the declaration assigns only P-8 to the unit. P-9 is rented under a revocable annual arrangement with the association; no transfer approval exists. The draft says “two owned parking spaces included.” Buyer Elise requires two long-term spaces. The offer is not accepted.

Create an interest/document/transferability chart, correct the unsupported draft claim, and list association questions and buyer decisions. Identify the 30-18 field for assigned parking and distinguish it from an attorney-reviewed arrangement for the second space. Explain why the agent cannot create a permanent real-property right by typing P-9 into the parking blank.

chunks.heading: T06U4 — Farm and Ranch Contract
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: P-8 is documented as assigned; P-9's rental/license status and transfer conditions require investigation. Correct the misleading ownership statement before presentation. The buyer may choose different terms or seek legal advice about a satisfactory arrangement. Contract language cannot convey rights the seller does not possess. The worksheet must keep the verified and desired interests separate.

## T06U4 — Farm and Ranch Contract

The farm form's property definition includes crops and rural improvements/accessories. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, seller may harvest growing crops until delivery of possession under paragraph 2D. If parties intend a different harvest arrangement, obtain proper written treatment; do not assume a crop belongs to buyer merely because closing happened before possession under a leaseback. Equipment ownership and exclusions require careful identification, including leased tanks or machinery.

Paragraph 3D allows selected survey-based price adjustment. Record reference acreage, dollars per acre, a termination-notice period for a price change greater than ten percent, and how the adjustment affects cash/financing. Ten percent is a change in sales price under this clause, not a generic permission to ignore acreage errors. If adjustment is not selected, do not assume a new survey automatically reprices the sale. Survey acceptance, title objections, access, and boundaries remain separate matters.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Read the rural differences in context
chunks.excerpt:
Paragraph 4 includes natural-resource and surface-lease treatment. Surface-only grazing or hunting rights can affect access and buyer use even when no residence is leased. Obtain the actual instruments. Mineral, water, and timber reservations require appropriate addenda and expert/counsel advice; a fence does not establish the subsurface estate. Paragraph 13B allocates rollback-type assessments based on whether the sale/buyer's later use or seller's preclosing use/change caused them, and the obligation survives closing. The contract allocation does not decide the taxing authority's assessment or exact statutory amount.

### Statute reading exercise: Read the rural differences in context

Read 25-17 paragraphs 2, 3D, 4, 7's water disclosure, and 13B. A 50-acre cattle tract includes a barn, fences, owned stock-water tanks, growing hay, a three-year grazing lease, and a severed mineral interest shown in title documents. The parties consider adjustment at $12,000 per acre and buyer's planned conversion of part of the land to nonagricultural use. Seller has supplied no water disclosure despite a known well.

Make a rural intake matrix linking each fact to the form location, needed document, buyer decision, and professional review. Distinguish existing mineral ownership from seller's proposed new reservation. Identify the rollback allocation principle without computing taxes from absent data. Explain why a residential resale checklist would omit at least three material issues.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Calculate an acreage adjustment
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: address crops, equipment, acreage adjustment, surface lease, mineral/title evidence, known well/water disclosure, and use-related tax consequences. A severed interest is not a new reservation of something seller owns. Tax and title professionals must establish actual consequences. The buyer's intended use makes leases, access, and water critical, not optional background.

### Applied exercise: Calculate an acreage adjustment

The accepted farm contract states $720,000 for reference acreage 60 acres. Paragraph 3D selects adjustment at $12,000 per acre, adjustment entirely to cash under 3A, and five days for notice if price changes more than ten percent. Original cash is $180,000 and financing $540,000. Survey shows 57.5 acres. In an independent alternative, the survey shows 53 acres. No other term changes and neither party has elected termination.

Calculate acreage difference, dollar adjustment, adjusted price, percent price change, and cash/financing for both cases. Identify whether the special termination threshold is implicated and what additional receipt/date evidence is required. Explain why the five-day period must not be invented from survey preparation date when the clause uses receipt.

Feedback: 57.5 acres reduces price by $30,000 to $690,000, a 4.1667% decrease; cash becomes $150,000. At 53 acres, reduction is $84,000 to $636,000, an 11.6667% decrease; cash would be $96,000 if the transaction proceeds. The latter exceeds ten percent and requires analysis of the stated notice option from actual receipt; it is not automatic termination. Financing remains $540,000 under the selected adjustment, subject to actual lender requirements and any needed agreement changes.

### Applied exercise: Harvest and a surface lease

chunks.heading: T06U5 — Unimproved Property Contract
chunks.excerpt:
Farm seller Finn closes November 1 but retains possession through November 15 under a written arrangement. Hay is growing; there is no different crop agreement. A grazing tenant has a written lease through December 31 covering the north pasture. Buyer Gia plans immediate fencing work across that pasture and assumes “all leases disappear when I buy.”

Prepare a possession/harvest/lease-rights timeline, identify the documents requiring review, and list questions for seller, tenant, buyer, and counsel. Explain the paragraph 2D crop default and why closing alone does not prove vacant possession of the leased pasture. Draft a factual correction to the buyer's assumption without interpreting the grazing lease's termination or assignment clauses beyond supplied facts.

Feedback: seller's default harvest right runs to delivery of possession absent a different written agreement. The surface lease is a separate instrument and must be reviewed for rights and transfer; sale does not supply a blanket conclusion that it vanished. The buyer needs actual lease and possession information before planning access or construction. Do not draft a unilateral cancellation of the tenant's rights.

## T06U5 — Unimproved Property Contract

Form 9-18 addresses unimproved property for intended one-to-four-family residential use under its adoption rule. Its official description refers to property without physical buildings, additions, or fixtures, commonly platted land. Do not use it mechanically for industrial land, an existing farmhouse, or a parcel whose intended transaction exceeds that scope. Verify the legal description and what actually exists on the land.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Review a vacant-lot file
chunks.excerpt:
Vacant does not mean ready to build. Paragraph 7A specifically advises buyer to determine utility availability suitable to the buyer's needs. Existing utilities and future service availability are different. A nearby line does not guarantee a connection, capacity, affordable extension, or service by the planned date. Ask the utility/provider and permitting authorities. Access, restrictions, floodplain, environmental conditions, setbacks, and sewage disposal may matter to intended use.

Use the form's title and survey objection choices, environmental addendum if agreed, and applicable district/coastal/utility notices. Do not invent a feasibility contingency in special provisions. If the buyer requires a custom development condition that available forms do not address, direct attorney involvement is appropriate before execution. A title policy generally is not a building permit or a promise of utility service.

### Statute reading exercise: Review a vacant-lot file

Read 9-18 paragraphs 2, 6, 7, and the attachment list. Lot 16, Block A, Cedar Cove Addition is vacant and intended for one residence. It is within a water service area, has no meter, and requires an on-site wastewater permit. A recorded drainage easement crosses the proposed building pad. Buyer Hugo has a preliminary sketch but no approved plans or specialist report.

Produce a due-diligence map identifying each source of uncertainty, the relevant contract mechanism, the professional/agency responsible for verification, and the deadline or negotiated condition needed. Explain why “utilities nearby” is inadequate. Identify appropriate disclosure and environmental-document checks and distinguish a preliminary sketch from a registered survey or approved permit.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Utility facts versus marketing claims
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: verify utility capacity/cost/timing, wastewater feasibility, drainage easement and use restrictions, survey, permits, and any applicable notices. The form's existing access/condition/title provisions must be read; they do not guarantee every proposed project. Obtain a suitable negotiated investigation structure and direct legal assistance for bespoke conditions. The map should name concrete records to obtain, not simply “do due diligence.”

### Applied exercise: Utility facts versus marketing claims

Lot seller Isabel advertises “water and sewer available.” The provider states water connection requires a $9,800 extension and six months, while no public sewer service is planned. Buyer Jalen wants to start building in sixty days and assumed a $1,500 meter charge. No independent sewage feasibility review has occurred. The offer is still a draft.

Create a verified cost/timing comparison and correct the unsupported advertisement/offer assumptions. Identify provider documents and permitting questions required before buyer decides. Explain which desired protections fit an existing form or addendum and which may need attorney drafting. Do not state that the lot is unbuildable or that the seller must pay all extensions without agreement.

Feedback: report the actual quoted water cost and timing, absence of public sewer, and unresolved alternative wastewater feasibility. The buyer's objective may not fit the known service schedule, but buildability requires professional/agency determinations. An agent must correct material statements and help obtain appropriate documents rather than transform expectations into an unsupported legal guarantee.

## T06U6 — New Home Contracts

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Compare new-home construction duties
chunks.excerpt:
Form 23-20 is for incomplete new construction to close after completion; its notice excludes condominium transactions and closings before completion. Paragraph 7B incorporates signed construction documents: plans/specifications, finish schedules, change orders, and allowances. A model-home tour is not an adequate substitute. Paragraph 7C requires written change orders and addresses cost increases, decreases, and unused allowances. Price and financing must stay consistent with agreed changes and lender requirements.

The incomplete form also addresses buyer selections, start and substantial-completion timing, specified delays, substitution of comparable materials, express warranties and assignable manufacturer warranties, and insulation information. Substantial completion refers to final inspection/approval by applicable governmental authorities and lender under the form. It is not merely the builder saying work looks nearly finished. Read the closing interaction; the stated delays do not create unlimited extensions beyond closing.

Form 24-20 is for completed new construction not previously occupied. It includes acceptance/repair choices, warranty and insulation information, and work-completion duties. New does not mean no inspection is needed or that every defect is covered by an unlimited warranty. Identify the actual written warranty and what law supplies; an agent should not invent an express warranty. Owner-required builder forms may fall within a §537.11 exception, but complex provisions still call for direct counsel review.

### Statute reading exercise: Compare new-home construction duties

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Change orders and allowances
chunks.excerpt:
Read 23-20 paragraph 7B–G and 24-20 paragraph 7A–F. In File A a builder's home lacks flooring and final approvals, and the buyer will choose counters from a $7,000 allowance. In File B a never-occupied completed home has final approvals and a damaged interior door to be repaired before closing. Both have written manufacturer warranties and insulation specifications.

Prepare parallel field/document maps identifying the correct form, incorporated documents, cost-adjustment treatment, completion evidence, warranty transfer, and insulation record. Identify one condition that would make the incomplete form unsuitable. Explain why a buyer selection above allowance must be documented and how an unused allowance differs from a verbal gift by the builder.

Feedback: File A needs 23-20 with signed construction documents and written change orders; File B fits 24-20 with the specific repair and relevant warranty/insulation provisions. Closing before construction completion is outside 23-20's stated use. The cost adjustment follows the actual clause, with price and financing reconciled rather than an undocumented side payment. Warranty and final approval are different evidence.

### Applied exercise: Change orders and allowances

Incomplete-home contract price is $540,000, cash $108,000, financing $432,000. Signed construction documents include a $7,000 counter allowance. Buyer selects $8,600 counters and the parties' written instructions require the $1,600 excess paid separately by buyer as allowed in the cost-adjustment field. A separate written change order removes $3,000 of work; lender instructs the resulting price reduction be allocated 20% to cash and 80% to financing. No other changes exist.

chunks.heading: T06U7 — Case Study/Workshop
chunks.excerpt:
Calculate adjusted price, cash, financing, and separate upgrade obligation. Produce a change-order ledger linked to signed documents and lender instruction. Identify what must be checked so that the separate payment is disclosed properly and not counted twice in price. Explain why an agent must not treat a texted upgrade request as the complete signed construction-document change.

Feedback: price becomes $537,000; cash $107,400 and financing $429,600; the separately agreed upgrade excess is $1,600 under the supplied payment treatment. Document and disclose it properly to lender/closing professionals. The price-reduction and upgrade-payment branches are distinct; avoid double counting. Written change orders and the parties' agreement govern rather than the agent's estimate of what the builder probably intended.

## T06U7 — Case Study/Workshop

The form-selection workshop starts before a contract is completed. Prepare an applicability memorandum with four distinct findings: the legal estate being sold, the property's present use and physical status, what the parties intend to transfer, and when closing and possession will occur. A memorandum that says only “residential property” has not answered enough. A condominium has governing-document and common-element issues even when its building looks like a house. A vacant tract has service and access questions even when a future house is planned. A new home may need construction obligations that cannot be reconstructed by borrowing a resale repair clause.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Build a condominium offer package
chunks.excerpt:
For each file, open the current applicable form and build its own issue index. Do not replace names and dollar amounts in an old completed form and assume the result is appropriate. Carry verified facts across documents, but carry paragraph references and deadlines only after checking the new form. If the form's scope warning excludes the intended closing arrangement, stop that selection and obtain an appropriate authorized contract; crossing out the warning does not cure the mismatch.

The review artifact should distinguish an incorrect selection from an incomplete field and an unresolved outside decision. A wrong ownership regime calls for correcting the contract approach. An unfilled negotiated cost allocation calls for principal instructions. A lender's unresolved survey acceptance calls for lender/title follow-up. A disputed title or mineral-right conclusion calls for legal analysis. These are different defects and should not all be marked “ask seller.” The following files require you to identify the defect, choose the proper source, state the correction or missing information, and preserve a record that a second reviewer can reproduce.

### Applied exercise: Build a condominium offer package

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Build a rural transaction risk memorandum
chunks.excerpt:
Seller Karina sells Unit 11, Building D, River Finch Condominiums, Austin, Travis County, with parking P-11 and appurtenant storage S-11 verified in the declaration. Buyer Landon offers $330,000, $66,000 savings and $264,000 conventional financing. Documents are received, Certificate is not received and is due ten days after acceptance. There is no right of first refusal. Earnest money is $3,500, option fee $250, option seven days, closing November 30, possession at closing/funding, seller ordinary-expense contribution $2,000, and no brokerage contribution. Buyer chooses inspections; no specific seller repairs are yet agreed.

Produce a form-specific field map and attachment list, identify missing loan parameters and title/company/notice information, and prepare the certificate review tracker. Explain why the ordinary association addendum for non-condominium subdivisions is not a substitute for condominium paragraph 2. Mark unresolved blanks rather than inserting defaults.

Feedback: use 30-18 and its separate Documents/Certificate choices with correct unit, parking, and storage interests. The $330,000 equation balances, but complete financing and title/notice information remains necessary. Condominium documents and the statutory certificate framework cannot be replaced with a generic association addendum. The worksheet must be internally consistent without pretending all intake facts are present.

### Applied exercise: Build a rural transaction risk memorandum

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Reject the unsuitable shortcut
chunks.excerpt:
Seller Mina offers 42 acres described by a verified attached metes-and-bounds survey. Price is $840,000, no acreage-price adjustment selected. Buyer Nolan proposes $336,000 cash and $504,000 financing. There is a hunting surface lease through February 28, a known stock well, an existing oil lease delivered to buyer, and growing hay. Seller wants to retain half of seller's currently owned mineral interest; the extent of current ownership is unresolved. Buyer plans a residence and grazing use.

Prepare a 25-17 package map identifying existing facts, proposed reservation, lease/document delivery, water disclosure, crop default, and tax questions. Explain what must be verified before a reservation can be described and why no acreage-price adjustment should be assumed. Draft direct questions for title/counsel concerning mineral ownership and surface-use consequences without writing a reservation clause yourself.

Feedback: keep the existing oil lease and proposed reservation distinct. Determine seller's actual owned interest, use the appropriate mineral addendum if suitable, and obtain counsel's advice on unusual matters. Address hunting rights, well disclosure, crop harvest through possession, and tax-use implications. The selected no-adjustment choice means a later survey alone does not activate 3D's price formula.

### Applied exercise: Reject the unsuitable shortcut

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt:
A developer asks the agent to use 23-20 for a buyer who will close next month on the land and unfinished shell, then separately hire the developer to finish construction over six months. The property is residential, but construction will not be complete at closing. Buyer also wants an enforceable fixed-price guarantee, delay damages, and an escrow holdback drafted by the agent. No attorney has prepared the arrangement.

Write a suitability review quoting only the relevant short form-use limit, identify each separate transaction component, and prepare a direct attorney/financial/closing referral list. Explain why familiar residential price fields do not cure the form's excluded use and why special provisions cannot be used to invent all requested construction remedies. Propose the administrative next step: gather documents and instructions for appropriate professional preparation.

Feedback: 23-20 expressly is not for closings before completion. Land acquisition, construction obligations, financing, security, holdbacks, and remedies need a suitable instrument and direct professional review. The agent should not force the deal into the wrong form or compose penalty clauses. A correct review remains helpful by organizing concrete facts and documents for the professionals who can structure it.

### Module recap

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt: Review your six-form matrix and all field maps. For each form, state the ownership/use facts that select it, a distinctive provision, an important limitation, and the required evidence for its special conditions. Recalculate the farm and new-home worksheets and confirm their chosen cash/financing allocations. You are prepared for the topic quiz when you can recognize when to use a specialized form and when the proposed transaction needs a different professionally prepared instrument.

lessons.title: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 07

chunks.heading: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 07
chunks.excerpt:
# Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 07

Promulgated Addenda, Notices and Other Forms. These documents have different jobs: add terms, provide required information, exercise a right, record receipt, or settle obligations. A title does not supply authority. In every worksheet identify the underlying contract, current form, factual trigger, selected choices, required actor, deadline, and delivery evidence. Required reading uses TREC's official form pages linked in each unit and the current [rules](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/rules-and-laws/trec-rules).

## T07U1 — Addendum for Sale of Other Property by Buyer

Form [10-6](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/addendum-sale-other-property-buyer) makes the purchase contingent on buyer's receipt of proceeds from the identified other property by the stated date, which should not be later than the purchase closing date. Listing the other house, accepting an offer on it, or signing its closing documents is not the same as receiving its proceeds. If the contingency is not satisfied or waived by the date, the form states automatic termination and earnest-money refund.

The seller's acceptance of another written offer can initiate the stated waiver requirement. Seller must notify buyer both of acceptance and the demand to waive. Buyer waives by written notice and the specified additional earnest-money deposit, not by reassurance that another closing is likely. Time is expressly essential. If buyer waives and then fails to close solely because those proceeds are unavailable, the addendum describes default. A broker must not recommend waiver without understanding the buyer's alternate funds and lender position.

### Statute reading exercise: Read the entire sale contingency

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A seller notice that omits a required component
chunks.excerpt:
Read 10-6 A–E. Buyer Adina needs proceeds from 90 Linden Walk by November 15; purchase closing is November 20. The waiver response blank is two days after seller notice and additional earnest money is $3,000. Seller accepts another written offer and gives the complete required notice November 2. Adina's existing buyer has merely signed loan documents; proceeds have not arrived. Adina sends a waiver email November 3 but does not deliver additional earnest money.

Create a chronology and identify the two waiver acts, the contingency's original date, and the deadline created by seller's notice. Explain whether the email alone meets paragraph C and what facts must be obtained immediately. Write a buyer explanation of the risk of waiving without replacement funds. Do not treat the other buyer's signed loan papers as received proceeds.

Feedback: paragraph C requires notice and additional deposit; one alone is incomplete. The stated two-day count leads to November 4, subject to the actual governing terms and notice facts. The original November 15 condition remains distinct from the accelerated waiver mechanism. The exercise calls for urgent factual review and appropriate advice, not an invented grace period or a promise that funds will arrive.

### Applied exercise: A seller notice that omits a required component

Seller Belen texts buyer Cyrus, “We accepted another offer today.” The accepted 10-6 requires the seller to notify buyer of acceptance and that seller requires waiver. The message says nothing about requiring waiver. Cyrus's agent immediately calendarizes the waiver deadline and tells him he must waive that night. The actual addendum specifies three days, not hours. No other notice exists.

chunks.heading: T07U2 — Addendum for Back-Up Contract
chunks.excerpt:
Prepare an evidence-based notice review, identify both missing/incorrect assumptions, and draft a factual clarification request. Explain why agents should not decide a contested notice's legal sufficiency from a casual message. List the buyer's funding information and instructions needed if a compliant waiver demand is later received. Preserve the original text without rewriting it as a complete notice.

Feedback: the supplied message does not expressly include the demand component described in B, and the response period was misstated. Obtain prompt clarification and legal review if rights are disputed. Never manufacture a deadline to pressure a waiver. If proper notice arrives, analyze the actual three-day period and both waiver requirements from the accepted form.

## T07U2 — Addendum for Back-Up Contract

The current [11-9](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/addendum-back-contract), effective July 1, 2026, has specific additional earnest-money and additional-option-fee provisions. The backup contract is binding upon execution; original earnest money and option fee are due under its paragraph 5. Other performance is generally deferred as the addendum states while the first-contract termination condition remains. Do not tell a backup buyer that nothing is binding and no deposit is due until first position.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Build a backup calendar
chunks.excerpt:
The amended effective date for performance is the date seller delivers notice of first-contract termination to buyer. It is not necessarily the day the first contract actually terminated. The new [Seller's Notice to Buyer of Removal of Contingency, 62-0](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/sellers-notice-buyer-removal-contingency-under-addendum-back-contract) provides a current notice tool. The backup addendum also has a deadline for first-contract termination, and states an amendment of the first contract does not terminate it. Preserve both contracts' distinct dates and records.

Additional payments after amended effective date have their own fields and extension/allocation consequences. Received additional money first satisfies the additional option fee, then additional earnest money. A missed additional option fee affects the unrestricted termination right; late additional earnest money invokes the stated seller notice-before-delivery remedy. If buyer has an unrestricted termination right, paragraph J describes its operation from original effective date through amended effective date and expiration. Read this provision with the actual paid fees and option period.

### Applied exercise: Build a backup calendar

Backup buyer Dena and seller Emil execute October 3. Original earnest money $4,000 and option fee $200 are paid timely. The first-contract termination deadline is October 25. First contract terminates October 14; seller delivers notice to Dena October 16. Backup addendum A(2) requires $2,000 additional earnest money and $150 additional option fee within three days of amended effective date. No holiday affects the relevant date. Closing will follow the actual contract terms; do not invent a new closing date.

chunks.heading: T07U3 — Addendum for Reservation of Oil, Gas & Other Minerals
chunks.excerpt:
Create original-date and amended-date tracks, calculate the additional-payment deadline, and state how a $2,000 combined payment would allocate. Identify what is still missing if only that amount arrives. Explain why October 14 is not the amended effective date on the supplied facts and why the original payments were due before first position.

Feedback: amended effective date is October 16 delivery; three days leads to October 19. A $2,000 combined additional payment first pays $150 option fee and $1,850 additional earnest money, leaving $150 earnest money short. Original payment duties arise as stated even while backup. Maintain actual evidence of notice delivery and check the entire contract for performance dates affected by the amended date.

## T07U3 — Addendum for Reservation of Oil, Gas & Other Minerals

Form [44-3](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/addendum-reservation-oil-gas-and-other-minerals-0) is used when seller reserves all or a portion of seller's mineral estate. Its definition includes specified minerals and associated royalty, executive, access, exploration/development, production, payment, and related rights. It expressly excludes water and listed surface materials from the defined estate, while addressing reasonable use of surface materials for mineral activity. Do not treat it as a general water-right reservation form.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Trace ownership and surface choices
chunks.excerpt:
The reservation percentage or fraction applies to the mineral estate seller owns, not necessarily the entire mineral estate beneath the land. Reserving half of seller's one-quarter interest retains one-eighth of the whole. The separate surface-right waiver choice affects seller's rights described in the form; it does not waive rights belonging to other mineral owners or lessees who are not parties. Failure to complete that choice has a stated deemed election. Precise ownership and legal effect call for an attorney with mineral expertise.

### Statute reading exercise: Trace ownership and surface choices

Read 44-3 A–D and its notices. Title counsel confirms seller Farid owns a one-half undivided mineral interest. Farid wishes to reserve one-half of the interest he owns and waive the stated access/reasonable-use rights. An existing mineral lessee is not a party. Seller knows that lessee's contact information. No other reservation exists.

Calculate the fraction of the entire estate retained and conveyed by Farid, map the reservation and surface-waiver selections, and identify the contact-information duty. Explain why Farid's waiver does not eliminate the lessee's rights and why the form cannot establish title ownership on its own. Add a separate warning against inserting groundwater into this mineral definition.

Feedback: Farid retains one-quarter of the whole and conveys his other one-quarter, on the supplied title determination. Choose the partial reservation and stated waiver from actual instructions. Because he does not reserve all his interest, paragraph D calls for known existing-lessee contact information within seven days. The nonparty lessee's rights are unaffected by seller's election. Water is excluded from this form's defined Mineral Estate.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: An unsupported “all minerals” claim
chunks.excerpt:
### Applied exercise: An unsupported “all minerals” claim

Seller Gemma says “I own all minerals because my parents owned the land,” but an old deed excepts a mineral interest of uncertain extent. Buyer Hale asks the agent to guarantee that a seller surface waiver prevents drilling anywhere on the parcel. The offer is unsigned and no mineral title opinion exists.

Prepare a missing-title-evidence list, direct questions for mineral counsel, and a factual buyer explanation. Identify why neither the seller's family history nor a form checkbox establishes complete ownership or binds nonparties. Propose the next administrative step for obtaining documents and instructions without drafting a bespoke severance or guaranteeing that drilling cannot occur.

Feedback: obtain deeds, reservations, leases, and qualified title analysis. The agent may identify the uncertainty and appropriate current addendum, but cannot guarantee the mineral estate or a nonparty's conduct. A seller waiver has the form's limited scope. The correct workflow makes the actual interest reviewable before the parties agree to a reservation.

## T07U4 — Buyers Termination of Contract

The current [Notice of Buyer's Termination of Contract, 38-8](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/notice-buyers-termination-contract) records the buyer's exercise of an identified termination basis. The form is not a universal cancellation entitlement. Check the actual accepted agreement and the facts before selecting a reason. Some provisions require supporting documents, such as lender reasons or an environmental report, in addition to notice. A bare notice may leave the requirement incomplete.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Notice package quality review
chunks.excerpt:
Preserve buyer's instruction, correct parties/property, chosen basis, relevant deadlines, attachments, and delivery evidence. Use paragraph 21 and any specific notice requirement; escrow objections have a separate receipt rule. Do not select a familiar option reason after the option expired simply because another valid right might exist. If a new current-contract right is not a printed checkbox, follow the applicable form and legal advice rather than inventing a false checked reason.

### Applied exercise: Notice package quality review

Buyer Inez has a valid lender property-disapproval statement under an applicable 40-11 paragraph 2B. Closing is November 30 and buyer instructs termination November 26. The statement specifically identifies unacceptable insurability. The draft notice incorrectly checks unrestricted option, omits the lender statement, and is addressed only to an assistant not identified as the party or agent in the agreement. The option expired two weeks earlier.

Write a correction checklist for basis, deadline, supporting document, recipient, property, signatures/instructions, and proof. Calculate the ordinary third-day-before-closing point and explain why the supplied November 26 instruction still requires proper delivery. Draft a factual money-status note distinguishing contractual refund entitlement from escrow's release process.

Feedback: use the actual property-approval basis and required lender statement, with notice under the agreement by the applicable November 27 point. An internal instruction is not completed delivery. Correct recipient and evidence; do not rely on the expired option checkbox. Proper termination may call for earnest-money refund, while escrow follows its separate release/demand procedures.

chunks.heading: T07U5 — Mutual Termination of Contract
chunks.excerpt:
## T07U5 — Mutual Termination of Contract

The outline's “Mutual Termination” is a legal event and document function, not proof that TREC currently publishes a mandatory form with that title. The current inventory must be consulted. Parties may agree to terminate and settle their rights using a suitable authorized instrument, with counsel where legal drafting or disputed claims are involved. The agent must not compose a settlement, release of claims, or new indemnity in special provisions.

Separate agreement to end performance from agreement about money, expenses, claims, and escrow's release. A release can do more than return a deposit; read the actual document and advise direct counsel review when appropriate. One party's proposed release is not mutual consent. A unilateral termination based on an existing right is different and should not be misdescribed as requiring mutual permission merely because escrow seeks release paperwork.

### Applied exercise: What has actually been agreed?

Buyer Jory and seller Kesia each email that they want to end the purchase. Jory wants the $7,000 deposit returned; Kesia demands $2,000 for alleged losses. Escrow requests an agreed release. An agent drafts “all claims waived forever” and tells Jory to sign because it is merely an administrative receipt. No party has agreed to the money split or claim waiver.

Prepare an agreement-status table for future performance, earnest money, expenses, claims, and escrow instructions. Identify the unauthorized drafting concern and draft a neutral next-step message requesting direct legal review and an appropriate agreed instrument. Explain why the desire to end the deal does not prove consent to every release term.

chunks.heading: T07U6 — Addendum for Property Located Seaward of the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway, Addendum for Coastal Area Property
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: ending performance may be a shared objective, but money and claims remain unresolved. A broad claim waiver is substantive legal language, not an administrative receipt. Counsel should help the principals resolve and document their actual agreement; escrow then follows valid instructions and governing procedures. Do not infer consent from pressure to close the file quickly.

## T07U6 — Addendum for Property Located Seaward of the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway, Addendum for Coastal Area Property

The [seaward addendum 34-4](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/addendum-property-located-seaward-gulf-intercoastal-waterway) and [coastal-area addendum 33-2](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/addendum-coastal-area-property) address different statutory geographic triggers and notices. Read Texas Natural Resources Code §§61.025 and 33.135 and the actual forms. One concerns property seaward of the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway and coastal/public-beach issues; the other concerns property adjoining or sharing a boundary with tidally influenced state waters. A view of the sea does not, by itself, establish either trigger.

The notices warn of matters such as public rights, shifting boundaries, erosion, and regulatory limitations. They are not a survey, building permit, flood-insurance determination, or guarantee of permanent private beachfront. Identify location from reliable maps/survey and appropriate authorities. A property may require multiple applicable notices; do not choose one merely because its title sounds broader. Missing required notices may have legal consequences that need direct advice.

### Applied exercise: Match geography to notice work

chunks.heading: T07U7 — Addendum for Property Subject to Mandatory Membership in an Owner's Association
chunks.excerpt:
File A is stipulated seaward of the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway. File B is stipulated landward of that waterway but shares a boundary with tidally influenced state waters. File C has an inland lake view with no tidal influence. No other geographic trigger is established. Buyers in all files ask whether the lot line can ever move.

Read the two current forms and statutory trigger sections. Prepare a notice-selection and verification chart for A–C, list additional location facts needed for any overlapping requirement, and draft a factual explanation of why a notice cannot guarantee permanent boundaries. Identify survey, coastal authority, insurer, and attorney roles without declaring a lot buildable or unbuildable.

Feedback: analyze A under the seaward trigger and B under the coastal-area trigger; C's lake view alone does not satisfy these supplied triggers. Additional facts may establish overlapping notices for A. The forms disclose risks and legal context; qualified survey and legal review determine boundary and public-right issues. The buyer's permanent-boundary question cannot be answered by checking a form box.

## T07U7 — Addendum for Property Subject to Mandatory Membership in an Owner's Association

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Association documents and fee buckets
chunks.excerpt:
Current [36-11](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/addendum-property-subject-mandatory-membership-property-owners-association) is not for condominiums. It defines Subdivision Information to include restrictions, bylaws, rules, and resale certificate under Property Code §207.003. It offers four distinct delivery/receipt choices: seller obtains and delivers; buyer obtains; buyer already received/approved with an updated-certificate choice; or buyer does not require delivery. Each has different timing and consequences. Do not check “received” because the listing includes an annual-dues number.

Under seller-delivery A1, the form supplies the stated three-day postreceipt or preclosing termination choice and a nondelivery remedy. Under buyer-obtains A2, deemed receipt can occur at the specified date even if buyer delays ordering. A3's requested updated certificate has its own ten-day delivery period after seller receives buyer's payment. Material changes in B have separate notice/termination treatment. Read the actual selection rather than applying the seven-day condominium rule to this form.

Paragraph C caps buyer's specified association transfer fees/deposits/reserves, with seller paying excess, and excludes regular prorated periodic charges and A/D costs. Paragraph D addresses cost of title-required information when buyer does not require the information/update. Current wording requires payment before title orders information. Association repair responsibility is another issue: seller cannot promise to compel an association repair without verifying authority and agreement.

### Statute reading exercise: Association documents and fee buckets

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A material association change
chunks.excerpt:
Read 36-11 A–D and [Property Code §207.003](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/PR/htm/PR.207.htm#207.003). Select A1: seller obtains/pays/delivers in ten days. Buyer receives complete information October 12; closing is October 30. Paragraph C buyer cap is $700. Association transfer-related charges within C total $950; regular quarterly dues prorated under paragraph 13 are $300; the A1 resale-package cost is $375.

Create three cost buckets and allocate each from the stated selections. Calculate the postreceipt decision date and identify what would change under A2's deemed-receipt rule. Explain why the $300 regular dues and $375 package cannot be thrown into C to exhaust the cap. Draft a delivery-and-fee inquiry to the closing professional.

Feedback: buyer pays up to $700 of C charges and seller $250 excess; regular dues follow proration rather than C; seller pays the A1 package. Three days after October 12 is October 15, subject to earlier closing if applicable. A2 changes receipt analysis by its deemed-date language. Accurate cost classification precedes arithmetic.

### Applied exercise: A material association change

Buyer Livia received subdivision information showing no special assessment and chose A3 without an update. Before closing, seller learns the association approved a major new assessment and prohibited the buyer's intended short-term rental use. Seller asks the agent to keep quiet because the buyer already approved the papers. Assume these are material adverse changes, not merely rumors, and no waiver changes paragraph B.

chunks.heading: T07U8 — Short Sale Addendum
chunks.excerpt:
Prepare a change-notice record identifying source, date learned, corrected information, buyer delivery, and applicable rights to review. Explain why prior approval does not erase paragraph B. Identify any association repair or lender questions arising from the new facts and route disputed legal effects to counsel. Do not silently replace the old certificate in the record and conceal the change history.

Feedback: seller must promptly notify buyer of known material changes under B; the stated adverse-change right requires the actual provision and preclosing notice. Prior A3 approval is not a blanket waiver of later B facts. Preserve both versions, disclose accurately, and let buyer obtain advice and decide under the agreement. An agent must not assist concealment to protect the closing.

## T07U8 — Short Sale Addendum

Form [45-2](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/short-sale-addendum-0) defines its short-sale arrangement with specific lender consent and agreement: consent to the sale, acceptance of seller's net proceeds in full satisfaction of seller liability, and a recordable lien release. A lender letter merely permitting release of its lien while retaining a deficiency may not satisfy that agreed definition. Seller needs direct legal and tax advice about actual liability and consequences. Never promise forgiven debt or harmless credit effects.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Read the lender letter for what it approves
chunks.excerpt:
The contract is binding upon execution and original earnest money/option fee are payable as required. Seller promptly applies and makes reasonable efforts to obtain the defined agreement, supplying required documents. Other performance is deferred as stated. Seller's notice of obtaining consent/agreement changes the effective date for performance; refusal or withdrawal before closing/funding has the stated termination consequence. If there is more than one secured loan or lienholder, the addendum applies to each. One approval is not all approvals.

### Applied exercise: Read the lender letter for what it approves

Seller Malik has a first mortgage and a second lien. First lender's letter accepts a proposed payment to release its lien but expressly reserves the right to collect the remaining debt. The second lienholder has not responded. The accepted 45-2 requires its defined Consent and Agreement by November 20. Buyer Nora paid earnest money and option fee timely and asks whether the sale is fully approved.

Create a lender-by-lender matrix for sale consent, full satisfaction of liability, recordable lien release, conditions, and status. Explain the first letter's mismatch with A2 and the missing second response. Draft a factual status message and legal/tax referral without predicting forgiveness or credit impact. Identify the deadline and notice evidence required before using an amended effective date.

chunks.heading: T07U9 — Noncontract Forms:
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: the supplied first letter does not establish every component of the addendum's defined agreement; its reserved deficiency is material. The second approval remains absent. Do not announce full approval or reset dates based on an incomplete letter. Seller's counsel and lenders must resolve terms, and buyer receives accurate status under the actual deadline and notice provisions.

## T07U9 — Noncontract Forms:

The outline places three untimed subentries within this thirty-minute unit: Promulgated Resale Certificates, Consumer Information Form, and Information About Brokerage Services Form. Their function is information, not a sale promise. A resale certificate reports association information supplied under its statutory framework. Use [Condominium Resale Certificate 32-5](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/condominium-resale-certificate-0) for its context and [Subdivision Information/Resale Certificate 37-5](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/subdivision-information-including-resale-certificate-property-subject-mandatory-membership) for its context. An agent must not invent the association's financial, insurance, litigation, or assessment answers.

The Consumer Protection Notice under §531.18 tells consumers about regulation and complaint resources and has display/link requirements. It is not a contract requiring the consumer to retain a broker, and a posted copy does not replace transaction-specific disclosures. The Information About Brokerage Services notice under §531.20 and §1101.558 explains brokerage relationships and duties and has its own delivery/link requirements. Current IABS 1-2 reflects current Texas law. Neither notice is a substitute for §1101.563's required residential buyer agreement.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Notices without accidental agency
chunks.excerpt:
Disclose whom the license holder represents as the statute requires at first contact with the other party, and provide the written notice at the applicable substantive-dialogue trigger with its stated exceptions. A conversation restricted to scheduling differs from advising about a specific transaction, but a website link alone does not automatically prove every transaction delivery duty was satisfied. Record how, when, and to whom the required notice was furnished. The broker's contact details must be accurate.

### Statute reading exercise: Notices without accidental agency

Read §§531.18 and 531.20, Occupations Code §1101.558, and current IABS. Prospect Orin emails a broker merely to ask open-house hours; later he calls for advice about how much to offer on that specific home. The broker represents the seller. Prospect Pia instead contacts an independent buyer broker for representation and a private residential showing. Neither has signed a representation agreement, and the only prior material is the firm's homepage footer link.

Prepare a contact-stage matrix identifying representation disclosure, IABS delivery analysis, consumer-notice display role, and the separate buyer-agreement requirement where applicable. Explain what each document establishes and does not establish. Record a compliant factual workflow for both prospects without silently converting the seller's broker into Orin's buyer agent.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Audit two resale certificates
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: the broker must make seller representation clear to Orin; substantive discussion triggers the applicable IABS analysis, with actual statutory exceptions considered. Pia's buyer-service path requires the appropriate agreement before the residential showing. A homepage link is relevant to website duties but not a universal substitute for the actual conversation delivery requirement. None of the informational notices alone creates buyer representation.

### Applied exercise: Audit two resale certificates

Association staff supplies a condominium certificate for a fee-simple subdivision lot, leaves the litigation field blank, and reports the seller's monthly payment rather than the association's regular assessment schedule. Buyer Quinn has a 36-11 seller-delivery agreement. The seller's agent proposes to fill “none” for litigation and use the condominium certificate because it looks official.

Identify the wrong-context form, missing authorized information, and delivery-completeness concern. Prepare an association correction request and buyer status note. Explain why the agent cannot certify “none” from silence and why receiving a document with a TREC logo does not prove the subdivision information package is complete. Keep the actual receipt history intact while corrected materials are requested.

Feedback: obtain the appropriate subdivision information/certificate from the responsible association source. The agent does not know that litigation is absent and must not invent an answer. Correct form context and complete required information are necessary; 36-11 includes restrictions/bylaws/rules as well as certificate. Counsel should address disputed deadline consequences if documents were deficient.

## T07U10 — Non-Realty Items

chunks.heading: T07U11 — Case Study/Workshop
chunks.excerpt:
Current voluntary [57-0](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/non-realty-items-addendum) concerns additional personal property not already included by the contract's property paragraph. Identify each item carefully, its agreed additional consideration, seller ownership free of encumbrances, and the form's absence of a condition/future-performance warranty. A leased item cannot truthfully be represented as owned free of encumbrances. The short official unit reinforces the earlier field work; it is not a second credit for the same exercise.

As a quick self-check, explain why a financed refrigerator subject to an unreleased security interest requires investigation before seller signs an ownership representation. State why a used appliance's separate conveyance does not guarantee future operation. This check is part of teaching prose, not a separately timed activity.

## T07U11 — Case Study/Workshop

An addendum packet is a system of selected conditions, not a stack of standard attachments. Start with the base contract, then identify exactly what each attachment changes or adds. A backup condition postpones specified performance but retains original money duties. A sale-of-other-property condition requires the buyer's actual proceeds or proper waiver, not merely another signed sale agreement. An association addendum has its own document and cost routes. A mineral reservation concerns the seller's owned estate and selected rights; it cannot establish ownership that title evidence does not support.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Assemble an association and sale-contingency package
chunks.excerpt:
Use two linked records for this workshop. The attachment inventory records form version, property identification, principal selections, consideration, signatures, and consistency with the base agreement. The event ledger records original acceptance, document delivery, waiver demand, required money, termination of another contract, seller notice, amended effective date, and any later notice. Linking the records lets a reviewer trace each calculated date back to the document that creates it. An attachment checkbox alone cannot prove that its missing terms were agreed.

When several conditions interact, identify the order without assuming that one event satisfies another. Receipt of a seller's backup notice may change a date but does not itself pay additional money. A buyer's waiver message may express intent but does not prove the additional earnest money was delivered. A termination can end a purchase duty without resolving a contested escrow distribution. The following exercises require separate findings for each step. If a fact is missing, state precisely what record or authorized decision is needed instead of inventing a convenient event.

### Applied exercise: Assemble an association and sale-contingency package

Buyers Rafi and Sonia offer $390,000 on seller Teo's fee-simple home in Aspen Gate Association. They need proceeds from 714 Morning Dove Road by November 25; purchase closing is November 30. They choose a three-day waiver response after a complete seller notice and $4,000 additional earnest money to waive. Association information is not received; seller will obtain/pay/deliver it in twelve days. Buyer transfer-fee cap is $600. No mineral reservation, coastal issue, or short sale is known.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Advance the backup without inventing termination
chunks.excerpt:
Prepare field maps for 10-6 and 36-11, identify the actual association name/contact still needed, and build distinct sale/waiver/document-review/fee ledgers. Explain why the buyer's sale contingency date should not be later than the purchase closing. List the attachments and notice evidence required before presenting a complete offer.

Feedback: use the specified dates, response days, additional deposit, seller-delivery route, and $600 C cap. Identify incomplete association contact/data rather than inventing it. The receipt of sale proceeds, complete waiver, association information, and closing are distinct events. The two addenda do different jobs; one does not cure a missing condition in the other.

### Applied exercise: Advance the backup without inventing termination

Seller Uma has an accepted first contract and an accepted 11-9 backup with buyer Vale. The first buyer requests an amendment extending closing ten days; seller accepts that amendment. Vale's agent says this makes the original contract “different” and therefore terminated, immediately declares the backup in first position, and invoices the additional option fee. No first-contract termination or seller notice to Vale has occurred.

Use 11-9 G–J to prepare a status memorandum, identify the erroneous inference, and list evidence needed to establish an amended effective date. Draft a correction to the premature fee demand without suggesting original backup payments were unnecessary. Explain what to monitor as the first-contract-termination deadline approaches.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Review three attempted shortcuts
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: paragraph I expressly says amendment/modification does not terminate the first contract. No supplied termination or delivered notice establishes first position or amended effective date. Original backup payment duties remain as stated, while additional-payment triggers require the actual amended date. Monitor the first-contract deadline and authentic notice, not rumor or changes in the primary bargain.

### Applied exercise: Review three attempted shortcuts

In separate files: Willa uses the mineral addendum to “reserve all well water”; Xander sends a short-sale approval letter that releases only one of two liens; and Yvonne replaces a required seaward notice with a map screenshot and the phrase “buyer aware of beach.” The offers are not yet signed, and no professional opinion resolves the missing issues.

Write three mini-memos identifying document function, missing fact or authority, appropriate official source, and next professional referral. Explain why each shortcut fails even though it mentions the right general subject. Produce a corrected package checklist for each without composing legal reservation or waiver language.

Feedback: 44-3's mineral definition excludes water; short-sale requirements apply to every relevant lienholder and include defined liability/release terms; required coastal notice language cannot be replaced by a casual map annotation. Match documents to actual legal function. The agent can organize and explain informational choices but should not invent substitute legal protections.

### Applied exercise: A termination and release handoff

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt:
Buyer Zora properly terminates under the stipulated applicable 36-11 material-adverse-change provision before closing, with written notice delivered as required. Escrow holds $4,800 earnest money and asks for release paperwork. Seller agrees the transaction has ended but disputes $300 of authorized escrow expenses. No settlement or order resolves the expense dispute, and the agent wants to mark the buyer paid in full immediately.

Prepare separate records for contract status, termination evidence, gross deposit, expense issue, release status, and actual disbursement. Explain why contractual termination can be established while money accounting remains unfinished. Draft a neutral handoff to escrow and counsel without deciding the expense dispute or falsifying the receipt record.

Feedback: record termination and delivery truthfully, keep the $4,800 held amount distinct from disputed expense deductions, and follow paragraph 18 and appropriate legal resolution. A completed termination notice is not proof of a completed bank transfer. The learning goal is a coherent file that does not conflate ending a contract, releasing escrow, and settling claims.

### Module recap

Sort every document studied into its actual function and explain its trigger. Review your source maps and independent worksheets for confused pairs: sale contingency and backup; assumption release and short-sale satisfaction; mineral and water rights; condominium and subdivision certificate; IABS and representation agreement; termination and release. Correct each error against the actual form before the topic quiz. Current form names and numbers matter, but the controlling task is using the correct instrument for the actual facts.

lessons.title: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 08

chunks.heading: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 08
chunks.excerpt:
# Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 08

Other Real Estate Matters. Accurate form completion does not cure dishonest facts, discriminatory instructions, improper fees, or missing disclosures. This module applies the [License Act](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/OC/htm/OC.1101.htm), [TREC rules](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/rules-and-laws/trec-rules), and the linked primary statutes to concrete transaction decisions. Every exercise is hypothetical and requires an independent written response before feedback.

## T08U1 — Real Estate Fraud

Fraud involves legal elements that must be established in a particular claim; it is not a label for every mistake. For license practice, the immediate standards are concrete. Section 1101.652 addresses dishonesty, misrepresentation, false promises, known significant defects, unauthorized terms, inaccurate accounting, and negligent/incompetent conduct. A transaction can be professionally improper even before a court determines common-law fraud. Do not wait for a completed lawsuit before correcting a known false statement.

Forms can be used to disguise a false transaction. Examples include misstated cash sources, concealed credits, a fake lease to satisfy underwriting, an inflated repair invoice, a forged signature, or a side agreement kept from the lender and closing professional. The document title does not make a false statement true. Refuse to create or transmit a materially false record, preserve evidence, inform the broker, and obtain appropriate legal guidance about the actual incident. Correct an error transparently rather than altering an executed document silently.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Match false documents to conduct rules
chunks.excerpt:
Known property defects require particular care. A seller's disclosure notice does not immunize an agent who independently knows a significant structural defect and conceals it. An “as-is” selection does not license misrepresentation. If the agent knows a roof repair failed, merely forwarding an older disclosure saying “repaired” can create a misleading impression. Record what is actually known, its source, what has changed, and what appropriate disclosure/review is required.

Wire fraud exploits trusted-looking instructions. An email with the correct property address and closing amount may still have a compromised sender or changed bank details. Verify funding instructions through a previously established, independently known channel with the closing professional. Never verify a changed bank account by calling only the phone number supplied in the suspicious email. If money has been sent to the wrong place, escalate immediately to the financial institution, broker, closing professional, and appropriate authorities through the incident process; speed and accurate facts matter.

Distinguish a recommendation from a guarantee. “An inspector can assess the foundation” is a process statement. “This house will never move” is an unsupported assurance. “The seller will consider your request” is not acceptance. “We have three offers” must be true if stated. Sales pressure never justifies inventing urgency, hiding a defect, or backdating a required agreement. Honest uncertainty is preferable to a fact the agent cannot support.

### Statute reading exercise: Match false documents to conduct rules

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Verify a changed wire instruction
chunks.excerpt:
Read §1101.652(b)(1)–(6), (20), and (24), and [Business & Commerce Code §17.46](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/BC/htm/BC.17.htm#17.46). Broker Alia is asked to show $20,000 more cash than buyer has, create a $5,000 repair invoice for work never performed, and assure lender that a relative occupies the house under a lease that does not exist. Separately, the seller admits a significant foundation defect omitted from the notice.

Prepare a conduct/evidence/rule/correction matrix for all four matters. Distinguish the licensing concerns from a final judicial determination of fraud or consumer-law liability. Draft a refusal to produce false paperwork that still identifies legitimate alternatives: accurate sources, actual repairs, true occupancy documentation, and appropriate disclosure. Record what should be preserved for broker/counsel review.

Feedback: the requested records are materially false and can implicate multiple conduct provisions; §17.46 supplies additional consumer-law concerns whose elements and applicability require legal analysis.
