Correct the facts and involve the broker/counsel. The foundation information requires attention independent of the requested financial falsification. Do not create a “practice version” of false records for use in the live transaction.

### Applied exercise: Verify a changed wire instruction

Buyer Ben is due to send $81,450 to title tomorrow. At 4:45 p.m. an email using the closer's display name directs funds to a new account and says to call a new number if needed. The message knows the property address and earnest-money amount. The buyer has the original title-company phone number from the verified opening package. No funds have been sent.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Correct a known defect record
chunks.excerpt:
Prepare a verification sequence identifying the trusted channel, data to compare, parties to alert, and evidence to preserve. Draft a short message to buyer that gives concrete next steps without repeating sensitive account details. Explain why knowledge of the transaction and a familiar display name do not authenticate the change. State what the immediate escalation would be if funds had already been sent.

Feedback: independently contact the known title office/closer using previously verified information and authenticate the actual instructions before transfer. Preserve the suspicious message and alert the broker/title team. Do not use only the new number or reply to the potentially compromised thread. If funds moved, promptly contact the sending institution and incident-response contacts; do not promise recovery or delay until the next business day to investigate.

### Applied exercise: Correct a known defect record

Seller Cora's older disclosure says a roof leak was repaired in 2024. Yesterday agent Dev saw active water entering the same area during rain and received the seller's message that the repair failed last month. Cora asks Dev to send only the old form and call the ceiling stain cosmetic. Buyer has not yet signed an offer.

Prepare a factual chronology, identify the misleading statements to avoid, and draft the broker/seller follow-up needed to provide accurate information. Distinguish the seller's notice responsibilities from Dev's independent known-defect duty. Identify qualified inspection/repair evidence to obtain without diagnosing the roof yourself. Explain why accepting property as-is would not authorize concealment.

chunks.heading: T08U2 — Broker's Fees
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: the active leak and seller admission are current known facts that cannot be disguised by forwarding stale wording. Correct or supplement the disclosure process appropriately and disclose known significant information as required. An agent need not diagnose engineering cause to report what was observed and learned. An as-is bargain does not turn a false cosmetic description into an acceptable statement.

## T08U2 — Broker's Fees

Broker compensation is negotiated; no TREC contract sets a universal percentage. Section 1101.563 requires the residential buyer agreement to state the amount/rate and determination and conspicuous negotiability language within its scope. Resale paragraph 12B repeats the negotiability principle and distinguishes each party's separate obligation from a contribution paid by the other party. A seller contribution does not automatically cap or increase the buyer's promised fee. Read both instruments and avoid charging beyond the actual agreement.

Compensation also has a lawful route. Section 1101.651 generally prohibits compensation for brokerage acts to an unlicensed person and controls how sales agents receive and pay transaction compensation through the sponsoring broker, with stated out-of-state-broker rules. Calling a commission a “consulting bonus” does not change the act performed. Section 1101.652(b)(8) requires full knowledge and consent for compensation from more than one party. Disclosure is not a cure for every prohibited payment; the underlying activity and law still matter.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A fee request outside the agreement
chunks.excerpt:
Settlement-service referrals can raise separate federal RESPA restrictions where applicable. Do not assume an association membership or a disclosed referral label authorizes payment for steering a covered settlement service. The provider's actual services, compensation, relationship, disclosures, and the governing law need examination. Route uncertain payments to the broker and counsel before promising them. The fee agreement should be understandable to the consumer and accurately reflected in closing records.

### Applied exercise: A fee request outside the agreement

Buyer Etta's written representation agreement specifies $9,200 total brokerage compensation for the covered purchase, with no other fee. Seller contributes $7,800 under the accepted contract. A sales associate asks Etta to pay the remaining $1,400 plus a new $600 “processing fee” directly to the associate's personal account. No amendment or broker authorization exists. A neighbor also requests $500 for negotiating the buyer's price despite holding no real-estate license.

Prepare a compensation ledger and identify the unsupported fee, improper payment route, and unlicensed-activity issue. Draft a factual explanation of the agreed remaining obligation and questions for the sponsoring broker. Explain why relabeling the extra amounts does not resolve the agreement or licensing problem. Do not assume any commission rate is mandatory.

chunks.heading: T08U3 — Fair Housing Laws
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: the supplied remaining contractual amount is $1,400; the new $600 is not authorized by the stated agreement. The sales agent's direct personal-account demand conflicts with the statutory broker compensation route. The neighbor's paid negotiation is not transformed into a permissible referral by calling it a bonus. Broker and counsel must evaluate the actual conduct and payment before it is made.

## T08U3 — Fair Housing Laws

Federal Fair Housing Act protections in 42 U.S.C. §3604 and the Texas Fair Housing Act in Property Code Chapter 301 apply to covered sales, rentals, terms, services, representations of availability, advertising, and related conduct. Protected categories in these core provisions include race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, and disability. Texas license-conduct provisions and §531.19 also expressly address ancestry. Identify applicable federal, state, and local law rather than assuming one short list resolves every jurisdictional issue.

Discrimination can enter form work through apparently routine questions: asking whether buyers have children to decide which offer to present, requesting a photograph to select a purchaser, steering families away from a subdivision, or adding a restrictive occupancy sentence based on protected status. Section 531.19 reaches asking, responding to, facilitating inquiries, or making disclosures intended to indicate prohibited preferences. An agent must not simply relay a discriminatory request under the excuse of acting as a messenger.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Instructions an agent cannot carry out
chunks.excerpt:
Compare offers on lawful transaction terms: price, financing, contingencies, timing, and ability to perform. A buyer's religion or ancestry is not a financing term. An owner's preference does not authorize the agent to discriminate. Exemptions are specific, limited, and do not necessarily remove advertising restrictions or separate licensing duties. The owner-sale exemption in §301.041 includes conditions concerning broker involvement; it is not a blanket exemption for every owner of one house.

Disability law can require reasonable accommodations in rules or services and reasonable modifications as provided by the governing law. Evaluate an actual request individually through the appropriate process. A policy against animals or alterations does not end the inquiry when disability-related accommodation or modification is implicated. Avoid unnecessary medical-detail requests or assumptions from appearance. The broker should use current legal guidance and obtain counsel for disputed or unusual requests. A course example cannot determine every accommodation's reasonableness.

### Statute reading exercise: Instructions an agent cannot carry out

Read 22 TAC §531.19, Occupations Code §1101.652(b)(32), and [Property Code §§301.021–.025 and .041](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/PR/htm/PR.301.htm). Seller Fia asks the agent to obtain each buyer's ancestry, whether they have children, and whether anyone has a disability, then to show only offers from households she prefers. The property is marketed through a broker, and no applicable exemption has been established.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Review a temporary-lease restriction
chunks.excerpt:
Create a request/rule/allowed-alternative table. Draft a response explaining the permissible financial and contractual comparison process. Identify why facilitating the questions itself matters even before an offer is rejected. Analyze the limits of an unsupported owner-exemption claim and distinguish equal treatment from an appropriate disability-accommodation process.

Feedback: the agent must not solicit or facilitate the stated discriminatory selection data. Offer comparison should use legitimate transaction factors. Broker involvement is material to the cited owner-sale exemption's conditions, and separate license duties remain. Accommodation requests are evaluated under their own legal standards, not used as reasons to exclude a buyer. A lawful alternative gives the seller useful contract information without protected-characteristic screening.

### Applied exercise: Review a temporary-lease restriction

Seller Gita will lease back for fourteen days after closing. Buyer/landlord Hamid asks to add “no children allowed on the property at any time” because he worries about damage. Gita's family includes two children, and the parties have agreed to ordinary residential occupancy. No senior-housing exemption or other lawful basis is supplied. The agent is also asked to add an automatic $5,000 penalty if a child visits.

Prepare a review identifying familial-status concerns, legal-drafting concerns, and legitimate property-care issues that can be addressed through lawful agreed terms. Draft a response and broker/counsel referral. Explain why a fourteen-day term does not itself authorize discriminatory language, and why an agent cannot cure the clause by replacing “children” with a coded phrase aimed at the same group.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: An accommodation request is not an automatic rejection
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: a blanket child exclusion and targeted penalty raise protected-status and drafting problems. Address actual occupancy, condition, deposit, permitted use, and damage responsibility through applicable lawful provisions and advice. Short duration does not erase all fair-housing or licensing duties. The agent should not recommend a disguised discriminatory substitute or assume the owner's concern creates an exemption.

### Applied exercise: An accommodation request is not an automatic rejection

During negotiation of an otherwise suitable temporary residential lease, a prospective occupant with a disability requests an exception to a no-animals policy for an assistance animal. The applicant has not asked for structural work, and no facts establish direct threat, property damage, or an applicable exemption. The owner instructs the agent to reject the request because all animals are forbidden and suggests asking for the applicant's complete medical records. The broker has a lawful accommodation-review process, but the agent has not used it.

Read Property Code §301.025 and prepare a decision log separating the stated policy, requested accommodation, known facts, missing information, and the professional responsible for review. Draft a neutral acknowledgment that does not promise approval or demand an unrestricted medical history. Identify the owner's two unsupported assumptions and the questions to route to the broker or counsel. Distinguish an accommodation involving a rule from a physical modification and explain why an agent should not invent an exemption merely because the lease is temporary.

chunks.heading: T08U4 — Other Disclosures (Required, Permitted, Prohibited)
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: an otherwise applicable rule can require reasonable accommodation when necessary for a person with a disability to use and enjoy a dwelling. The blanket no-animals rule is not itself a complete legal answer. Use the lawful review process, seek only appropriate information, and avoid unsupported disability inquiries or definitive entitlement decisions on incomplete facts. No structural modification was requested here. Duration alone does not establish an exemption. Preserve the request and response and obtain appropriate review rather than transmitting the owner's categorical rejection.

## T08U4 — Other Disclosures (Required, Permitted, Prohibited)

Classify information by actual authority. Required disclosure can include representation, license holder's personal interest under §535.144/resale paragraph 8, known significant defects, seller notices, lead information, and applicable water/district/coastal notices. The transaction facts determine which duty applies. A signature acknowledging one notice is not proof all required notices were delivered.

Some information has no inquiry/disclosure duty under a specific statute. Section 1101.556 addresses certain occupant health information and death by natural causes, suicide, or accident unrelated to property condition. That provision must not be converted into “all deaths and hazards may be concealed.” An accident caused by the property's condition raises a different question. Also distinguish no duty from affirmative permission to facilitate disability discrimination; §531.19 remains relevant to health-related inquiries.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Classify six disclosure requests
chunks.excerpt:
Confidential information and discriminatory information have separate limits. For an intermediary, §1101.651(d) restricts revealing bargaining positions and confidential information except under its stated exceptions. A party's written instruction does not authorize hiding material property-condition information contrary to the statute. A broker can disclose required facts while protecting unrelated personal financial or medical details. When duties appear to conflict, obtain prompt broker/counsel guidance and preserve the actual request rather than guessing.

### Applied exercise: Classify six disclosure requests

An intermediary's file contains: seller's private minimum price; a known foundation failure; buyer's private maximum price; seller's adult child's medical diagnosis unrelated to condition; a disclosed agent ownership interest above ten percent in the seller entity; and a report that a person died naturally in the home years ago. No separate written authority to disclose negotiation limits exists. No court order is supplied.

Build a six-row matrix identifying required, protected/restricted, no statutory inquiry duty, or further-analysis status with a pinpoint source. Explain the property-condition exception separately from the negotiation-price rules. Draft two safe responses to requests for the minimum price and medical diagnosis without supplying the confidential facts. Identify why “everything in the file is confidential” is also inaccurate.

chunks.heading: T08U5 — Review Occupancy Standards
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: bargaining positions have specific intermediary restrictions; material condition cannot be suppressed under a blanket confidentiality claim; license-holder interest has the applicable written disclosure duty; health-related discriminatory inquiry raises §531.19 and §1101.556; natural death is within the cited no-duty provision. Do not overgeneralize any category. The actual information and statutory exception control.

## T08U5 — Review Occupancy Standards

Texas Property Code §92.010 states, subject to its exceptions, a maximum number of adults a landlord may allow equal to three times the number of bedrooms. It defines adult as eighteen or older and bedroom as an area intended for sleeping, excluding the listed nonbedroom spaces such as kitchen, living room, bathroom, utility room, and storage. It is not a command that every landlord impose exactly three persons per bedroom, and children are not counted as adults under that section.

The section includes exceptions where state or federal fair-housing law requires a higher rate and for the specified temporary sanctuary from family violence for no more than one month. Read the whole provision before applying a number. Other building/safety standards, actual dwelling configuration, fair-housing considerations, and local rules may matter. A familiar “two per bedroom” practice is not a universal safe harbor that overrides all facts and law.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Count the statutory adults accurately
chunks.excerpt:
An occupancy policy should address legitimate space and safety needs consistently, not act as a proxy for excluding families with children, people with disabilities, or a national-origin group. Do not turn a living room into a legal bedroom on an application merely to make the arithmetic work. When an exception or accommodation may apply, gather the appropriate facts respectfully and obtain qualified guidance. The agent is not a building official and should not certify a room as compliant sleeping space from a photograph.

### Applied exercise: Count the statutory adults accurately

A two-bedroom rental application lists three adults aged 42, 39, and 20, and three children aged 16, 10, and 7. The landlord says six occupants exceed Texas's “two adults per bedroom law.” A second independent application lists seven adults for a two-bedroom dwelling; one seeks temporary sanctuary from family violence for three weeks. No other safety or local-rule determination has been made, and the statutory sanctuary facts are assumed genuine for this exercise.

Read §92.010 and compute the base adult count and threshold for both files. Identify the landlord's incorrect statement and the second file's exception needing review. Explain why the calculation does not by itself resolve every lawful occupancy policy or building requirement. Draft a factual intake note without labeling the children's presence a statutory adult-count violation.

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: the first file has three statutory adults, below the base six-adult maximum; the children do not become adults for this calculation. The second exceeds the base but raises the express temporary-sanctuary exception within the one-month limit. Fair-housing, legitimate safety standards, and other applicable law still require evaluation. The statute is neither a universal two-person rule nor permission to fabricate additional bedrooms.

### Module recap

Review the fraud, fee, fair-housing, disclosure, and occupancy worksheets as contract-completion controls. Explain how a fact can be accurate yet improperly requested for discriminatory selection; how a signed fee field can still conflict with a separate agreement; and how a no-duty disclosure statute differs from permission to lie. Correct every source citation and calculation, and retain clear referrals for issues requiring legal, financial, medical-privacy, or building expertise. Complete the topic quiz only after you can state each relevant limit without turning it into a blanket rule.

lessons.title: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 09

chunks.heading: Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 09
chunks.excerpt:
# Texas Promulgated Contract Forms — Module 09

Practice Makes Perfect. This required capstone workshop integrates the complete contract file. It is adapted for individual distance learning: complete every role's written artifact yourself, then compare feedback and correct the artifact. A study partner may discuss the reasoning, but no group attendance is assumed and another person's answer does not replace your work. These worksheets are formative instruction. The separately assigned assessed scenario and topic quiz have different facts and must be completed independently.

## T09U1 — Group Work Shop/Case Study/Discussion

Your role is the buyer's supervised sales agent in a hypothetical Texas residential resale. You have a valid current residential buyer representation agreement authorizing the services, with a definite termination date, negotiated compensation, and required disclosures. Seller has a separate listing broker; no intermediary or personal-interest disclosure is involved. Both sides are competent adult principals with verified authority. These supplied assumptions keep attention on the contract file; in a real transaction they would need evidence.

The objective is to create a coherent file, not merely fill every blank. A coherent file can explain why a form was selected, where each fact came from, who made each choice, when agreement occurred, what performance remains, and how a notice or payment was verified. An unanswered question should remain visible. A form with a plausible but invented value is less reliable than an uncompleted draft accompanied by a clear request for the missing instruction.

chunks.heading: T09U1 — Group Work Shop/Case Study/Discussion
chunks.excerpt:
Use current official [resale 20-19](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/one-four-family-residential-contract-resale), [financing 40-11](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/third-party-financing-addendum-0), [association 36-11](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/addendum-property-subject-mandatory-membership-property-owners-association), [lead 56-0](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/addendum-sellers-disclosure-information-lead-based-paint-and-lead-based-paint-hazards-0), [non-realty 57-0](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/non-realty-items-addendum), and [amendment 39-11](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/amendment). Other documents are added only if the facts call for them. Do not print or sign a redesigned course worksheet as if it were the promulgated form. Preserve TREC's official form text and formatting.

Work in passes. The first pass is identity and property: match the title description, actual parties, ownership regime, included items, exclusions, leases, and reservations. The second is money: reconcile price and financing, keep earnest money and option fee separate, distinguish ordinary expenses and brokerage contributions, and identify costs still needing outside confirmation. The third is conditions and disclosures: record actual receipt and whether a specific addendum changes the default. The fourth is performance: assign dates, actors, evidence, and notice methods. The fifth is integrity: match all attachments, signatures, modifications, and the actual final-acceptance communication.

chunks.heading: T09U1 — Group Work Shop/Case Study/Discussion
chunks.excerpt:
The current July 2026 contract must be read as a complete document. An older checklist can omit water disclosure, additional attachments, current compensation fields, or current broker-contact instructions. It can also import the wrong rule from another form. Current source control means checking the official version and preserving the one actually used; it does not mean changing old executed records to resemble today's form. The student should be able to show which version supports every field map in this workshop.

Keep a separate event log. A document can be signed one day, sent another, and received later. Some provisions depend on delivery; others use receipt, title-company receipt, final acceptance, or a changed effective date. The log should record the actor, date/time, document version, recipient, method, and proof. If the sender's claim and recipient's evidence disagree, do not choose whichever date saves the deadline. Preserve both and escalate the dispute promptly. The legal consequences may require counsel.

When money is involved, show the equation. Price cash plus financing must equal price. Closing cash then accounts for verified deposits, expenses, contributions, prorations, and other adjustments. A reduced loan amount can increase buyer cash or require an amended price; it cannot be silently ignored. A seller contribution may be limited by actual eligible expenses or the lender. A personal-property payment may need separate disclosure and cannot simply be hidden inside a lender's collateral value. Every figure needs a label and a source.

chunks.heading: T09U1 — Group Work Shop/Case Study/Discussion
chunks.excerpt:
When repairs are involved, separate observations, technical assessment, agreement, and completion. The inspector identifies conditions within the inspector's scope. Qualified trades supply proposed work and cost. The parties decide what work they agree to require. The contract describes completion, permits, documentation, and available remedies. The agent tracks that process and communicates facts. The agent does not promise that a foundation is safe, a repair complies with every code, or a party will win litigation if a repair fails.

Disclosure work is not one universal checklist marked “done” at acceptance. Seller's notice, lead information, water disclosure, association documents, district notices, personal-interest disclosure, representation disclosure, and IABS have different actors and triggers. A property's age matters to lead analysis; municipal water alone does not necessarily establish the current water-disclosure exception; an association does not automatically make the property a condominium. The student's job is to make each conclusion traceable to actual supplied facts and the appropriate provision.

An apparent problem does not always produce the same remedy. A missing option fee affects the unrestricted right under paragraph 5; missing earnest money invokes a different seller mechanism. A title problem can involve objection and cure. A financing problem can involve buyer approval, property approval, or FHA/VA protections. A casualty has its own alternatives. A proposed amendment does not suspend existing terms. A termination notice records a right; escrow release follows a separate procedure. Identifying the wrong mechanism can be more damaging than failing to name the form number.

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Establish the complete transaction map
chunks.excerpt:
Communication should be useful and precise. Tell the principal what is known, what document says, what deadline matters, what choices belong to the principal, and what question requires a professional. Avoid statements such as “you are protected” without explaining the relevant conditions. Avoid declarations that a contract is void, an estate has clear title, or a party must accept a settlement unless a proper authority has resolved the issue. A well-prepared referral includes documents and factual questions so counsel can act efficiently.

In a group classroom, students might divide buyer, seller, escrow, and reviewer roles. Here you complete all four perspectives to make the distance exercise equivalent in substance. As buyer's agent, prepare the proposed choices. As seller's reviewer, identify what the proposal asks seller to do. As closing coordinator, identify which documents and funds are needed. As auditor, find contradictions. Do not reuse an earlier role's conclusions uncritically; challenge them against the source. The final work product is a corrected set of worksheets with an explanation of changes.

Before reading any feedback, write your own answer. After reading it, annotate each error with the governing provision and a corrected explanation. If your answer differs because the exercise lacks a fact, identify the missing fact and an appropriate source instead of assuming the model answer gives permission to fabricate. A correct unknown is a valuable result. The point of the workshop is to develop a dependable professional process that remains useful when real facts are incomplete.

### Statute reading exercise: Establish the complete transaction map

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: Establish the complete transaction map
chunks.excerpt:
Read the official resale form in full, then the listed applicable addenda. Hypothetical sellers Arden and Briar Lee convey Lot 18, Block 3, Silver Wren Addition, City of Fort Worth, Tarrant County, Texas, known as 821 Silver Wren Lane, 76109, a 1974 detached resale home. Buyers Cassia Reed and Dorian Moss offer $450,000: $90,000 verified savings and $360,000 conventional financing. Both sides intend no natural-resource, residential, or fixture leases and no reservations; seller retains a named dining-room crystal chandelier. Buyer separately purchases a freestanding washer/dryer set for $900. Seller's disclosure notice is already delivered; available lead reports and the federal pamphlet are delivered before the buyer becomes obligated; buyer selects the lead inspection option. No well, pond/lake/tank, known surface-water permit, or severed/sold/leased groundwater rights exists; the property receives water only from the City of Fort Worth. Seller supplies that accurate paragraph 7I information. The property is subject to Silver Wren Property Owners Association. No statutory district/coastal/propane notice trigger is supplied.

Prepare an issue-to-form map for every fact. Identify which claims still would need verification in a live file and which attachments follow from the supplied assumptions. Read the forms' warnings and mark any instruction that prevents using a form for the wrong context. Do not fill the remaining negotiated fields until the next exercise supplies them.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Complete the economic and delivery fields
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: 20-19 fits the stipulated ownership/use; 40-11, 36-11, 56-0, and 57-0 address the supplied financing, association, lead, and personal-property subjects. Specify the chandelier exclusion. The cumulative supplied facts support the current water-disclosure no-delivery choice with the named utility; municipal service alone would not. No supplied facts authorize inventing leases, mineral reservations, or district notices, but a live file must verify them.

### Applied exercise: Complete the economic and delivery fields

For Silver Wren, the parties instruct a 30-year conventional first loan, maximum 6.6% annual rate for 30 years, maximum 1.5% origination charges, and a buyer-approval condition of 22 days. Earnest money is $5,500; option fee $350; option ten days. No additional earnest money is required initially. Escrow/title is Mockingbird Title, 100 Commerce Street, Fort Worth, Texas 76102. Seller pays the owner policy; survey exception is amended as the selected form allows at seller expense. Existing survey plus T-47/T-47.1 is due in seven days; seller pays for replacement if the timely package is rejected. Title objections: five days; intended use: single-family residence. Closing is November 23, 2026; possession at closing and funding. Buyer accepts as-is with no initial specific repair agreement. Seller ordinary buyer-expense cap is $4,500 and seller contribution toward buyer brokerage is $8,000. Buyer brokerage obligation under the separate agreement is $10,500. Residential-service reimbursement cap is $650. Association route A1: seller obtains/pays/delivers in twelve days; buyer C transfer-charge cap $700; seller pays D title-required information if D becomes applicable. All complete notice contacts will be supplied by the parties before presentation; none

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Record final acceptance and build the first calendar
chunks.excerpt:
are invented here.

Create a field map for every supplied choice and identify every remaining unresolved blank. Calculate origination-charge dollar cap and the buyer's uncovered brokerage obligation. Reconcile the $900 personal-property price separately. Prepare an attachment inventory with signature and property-consistency checks, not real signatures.

Feedback: price balances $90,000 + $360,000; origination cap is $5,400; uncovered brokerage obligation is $2,500 on the supplied separate fee and contribution. The $4,500 ordinary expense cap cannot automatically be used for that brokerage gap. Keep the $900 additional personal-property consideration distinct. Obtain actual contact details and any still-missing principal instructions rather than substitute fake addresses in a live instrument.

### Applied exercise: Record final acceptance and build the first calendar

The parties complete the offer and all required attachments, with final unqualified acceptance communicated by the seller's agent to buyer's authorized agent on October 20, 2026, at 4:10 p.m. No earlier communication establishes acceptance. Escrow receives the contract October 21. Assume no relevant holiday changes the stated money delivery date. October 20 is Tuesday. Use the initial Silver Wren terms without any amendments yet.

Build a calendar for earnest/option delivery, option termination, existing survey package, buyer approval, association delivery, title commitment from escrow receipt, lead inspection, lead termination if its presence condition is met, and closing. For each state trigger, calculation, actor, evidence, and any clause-specific cutoff. Do not apply paragraph 5's weekend extension to every other deadline.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Handle new document receipts
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: effective date October 20; initial payments October 23; ten-day option October 30 at 5:00 p.m. local property time; survey package October 27; buyer approval November 11; association twelve-day delivery November 1; initial title commitment twenty days after title receipt November 10, subject to its actual extension rule; lead inspection October 30 and applicable fourteen-day notice November 3; closing November 23. The association and other calculations require their own actual wording and receipt records. A correct calendar identifies later receipt-based periods separately.

### Applied exercise: Handle new document receipts

In Silver Wren, seller timely supplies existing survey and declaration October 25, but lender rejects them October 27. Buyer receives title commitment November 2 and all exception documents November 4. A new acceptable survey arrives November 6. Buyer receives complete association information October 29, showing a previously unknown $1,200 special charge classified by the association and contract as a paragraph C transfer charge; the ordinary dues/proration amount is separate. No adverse material change after receipt is supplied.

Update the survey cost and ordering task, title-objection receipt trigger and deadline, association review deadline, and C charge allocation. Prepare the supporting evidence list and explain why the existing survey's preparation date is irrelevant to the new-survey receipt trigger. Do not treat the transfer charge as regular dues or use the condo seven-day period.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Negotiate repairs without losing the option
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: seller pays replacement under the selected rejection choice. Final title component arrives November 6, so the five-day objection date is November 11, earlier than closing. Association three-day postreceipt point is November 1, subject to the form's earlier-closing limit. Buyer pays $700 of C charges and seller $500 excess. Actual statements and receipt evidence must support classifications and dates.

### Applied exercise: Negotiate repairs without losing the option

The October 27 inspection finds a leaking kitchen drain and a failed garage safety-reversal sensor. Buyer asks for both repairs, a price reduction to $447,000, and closing moved to November 25. Seller agrees only to the two repairs through qualified trades with permits if required and paragraph 7F documentation. On October 29 both parties sign and communicate acceptance of a current amendment containing only the agreed repairs; it does not change price, closing, or option. No lead hazard is found by the properly qualified lead inspector.

Prepare a requested-versus-accepted change table, repair evidence checklist, and updated calendar. Explain which original terms remain and why the repair amendment does not extend the option. Identify the buyer's remaining business decision before October 30 at 5:00 p.m. without recommending termination or promising the repair outcome. Record the lead result without falsely marking a lead-based termination right exercised.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Audit loan and closing figures
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: price remains $450,000; closing November 23; option October 30. Only the specific repairs became agreed obligations. Maintain the required provider/permit/documentation checks. A satisfactory lead result does not create the form's hazard-based termination fact. The buyer chooses whether to proceed or timely exercise an available right, with legal advice if needed; the agent should not invent an automatic extension while waiting for repairs.

### Applied exercise: Audit loan and closing figures

By November 10 the lender confirms buyer approval on the agreed terms; property approval is also established. For this simplified closing worksheet, eligible ordinary buyer expenses total $7,100; actual residential service plan costs $620; seller reimburses it separately under 7H within the $650 cap; buyer broker fee is $10,500 with $8,000 seller contribution; seller tax proration credit is $6,200; earnest money $5,500 and option fee $350 are fully credited. Loan proceeds remain $360,000. The $900 non-realty payment is paid separately outside this purchase cash worksheet and accurately disclosed. No other purchase charges/credits apply.

Calculate purchase cash needed at closing line by line, showing ordinary-expense contribution and service-plan reimbursement separately so the plan is not counted twice. Explain what the approval confirmations do and do not establish about closing/funding. Prepare a reconciliation request if the statement instead uses the entire $650 service cap despite actual cost $620.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Final walkthrough and a new factual problem
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: begin with $90,000 price cash; subtract $5,500 earnest and $350 option; add $2,600 uncovered ordinary expenses; add $2,500 remaining brokerage obligation; subtract $6,200 tax credit. The separately reimbursed $620 service plan nets to zero within this worksheet. Purchase cash is $83,050; the separate $900 personal-property payment is not silently included. Actual reimbursement is $620, not the cap. Approval is not evidence funds have already disbursed.

### Applied exercise: Final walkthrough and a new factual problem

At November 22 walkthrough, the drain is no longer leaking and seller supplies paid invoices from appropriately qualified providers plus any required permits and transferable warranty records for both repairs. The garage sensor still fails the inspector's operational check. Seller says the buyer must close because an invoice proves repair. Closing remains November 23; no extension or waiver has been signed. The buyer wants advice about the available choices.

Prepare a factual completion matrix distinguishing documents from observed function. Locate paragraph 7F's remedies/extension provision, identify who chooses and who supplies technical/legal advice, and draft an urgent buyer/broker status note. Explain why neither the invoice nor the agent's observation alone is a complete technical determination. Preserve the inspector's report and communications.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Close, transfer access, and archive accurately
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: documentation is necessary but does not erase the reported continuing failure. Obtain qualified clarification, communicate the actual status, and review the buyer's paragraph 7F choices, including the specified extension up to five days if necessary for completion or remedies under 15. The buyer's decision and any legal interpretation must be handled appropriately. Do not announce an automatic extension or pressure the buyer to sign a false completion acknowledgment.

### Applied exercise: Close, transfer access, and archive accurately

Assume the parties lawfully resolve the sensor issue with verified completion before closing; no date change is needed. They sign and fund November 23. Possession is delivered the same afternoon with the required property condition. Seller provides all keys and smart-device access and confirms seller's personal connections are removed. Escrow supplies final statement and receipts. In February, the actual tax bill differs from the closing estimate, requiring a $240 adjustment under the agreed proration allocation. No release waives that obligation.

Create a closing/possession record and an archive index containing accepted contract, attachments, amendments, notices, receipt evidence, inspections, repair verification, disclosures, approval communications, settlement, and access-transfer confirmation. Add a post-closing proration follow-up entry. Explain why closing does not justify deleting superseded drafts or ignoring surviving obligations, and why credentials should be stored/transmitted securely rather than in a public shared folder.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Reviewer challenge and correction memorandum
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: preserve the actual documentary sequence and distinguish final from superseded records. The $240 adjustment follows paragraph 13 and the actual allocation; do not assume every post-closing claim vanished. Record verified access transfer without exposing personal credentials unnecessarily. Retention and security follow applicable broker policies and law; a course archive index is not permission to destroy records prematurely.

### Applied exercise: Reviewer challenge and correction memorandum

An independent reviewer of your Silver Wren packet flags six statements: “The contract became effective when escrow received it”; “The $4,500 seller expense cap pays the buyer's broker gap”; “The seven-day condo review applies to the subdivision”; “The unsigned price reduction became binding during inspection”; “An invoice conclusively proves every repair”; and “The option-fee amount is refunded with earnest money whenever buyer terminates.”

Write a six-point correction memorandum. For each statement supply the accurate rule, pinpoint source, relevant Silver Wren fact, and a practical record correction. Identify any statement that lacks enough facts for a universal conclusion. Then reread your eight prior worksheets and mark any occurrence of the same misconception. This final reviewer pass must produce corrections, not merely a list of statements you recognize as wrong.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: Restore an audit trail after a communications error
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: use final acceptance October 20; separate 12A and 12B; use 36-11's actual three-day mechanism; only accepted repair changes occurred; repair completion needs the actual contractual/technical evidence; option fee and earnest money have distinct disposition rules and the applicable termination clause matters. Reject universal refund claims. The corrected packet should show the evidence behind each conclusion and preserve original records with transparent corrections.

### Applied exercise: Restore an audit trail after a communications error

This final quality-control exercise uses a separate post-closing training file, not a new Silver Wren contract event. The archived accepted price is $326,000 and the actual amendment changes only the closing date. A coordinator accidentally uploads an unaccepted $320,000 draft as the final contract and marks a lender email dated February 8 as received February 6. The original accepted document, actual amendment, and email headers remain available; no evidence supports the earlier receipt date. A reviewer has already relied on the mislabeled record. No party authorized a price change, and no legal conclusion about missed rights has been reached.

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt:
Prepare an incident correction note identifying each inaccurate field, its reliable source, who needs corrected information, and how the original and correction will remain auditable. Reconcile the correct price and amended closing without erasing the uploaded draft. List which reports or calendars must be recalculated from February 8 and which legal questions require prompt broker/counsel review rather than a backdated entry. Explain how access controls and version labels could prevent recurrence. Finally draft a factual notification to the reviewer that acknowledges the error without asserting that no one was affected.

Feedback: accepted price remains $326,000; only the accepted closing change belongs in the operative terms. Restore the actual February 8 receipt evidence and recheck every calculation that depended on it. Preserve the original records and transparent correction rather than deleting the discrepancy or changing metadata to make a deadline appear timely. Inform affected authorized participants accurately, route potential legal consequences promptly, and avoid an unsupported assurance that the error was harmless. Version control supports the substance of contract work: a correct rule applied to a false document or date still produces a wrong result.

### Module recap

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt: Submit the corrected field maps, timeline, document ledger, financial worksheets, repair record, possession/archive index, and correction memorandum. Explain the five most consequential mistakes you found and how your process would prevent each. Complete the separate assessed capstone scenario and the three primary topic quiz questions. Optional further practice is to rerun one worksheet with a changed financing source or ownership regime, but that optional repetition is not counted toward required instruction and is not needed for the quiz.

lessons.title: Module 01: The Nature & Cycle of Real Estate Finance

chunks.heading: Module 01: The Nature & Cycle of Real Estate Finance
chunks.excerpt:
# Module 01: The Nature & Cycle of Real Estate Finance

This module follows REF-0 topic T01, whose suggested allocation is 105 minutes. You will trace money and responsibilities through a mortgage transaction, calculate leverage, and distinguish evidence from forecasts. All borrowers, transactions, market figures, rates, and lender policies in this course's examples are hypothetical unless explicitly identified as current sourced facts. No example is a rate quote or a promise of approval.

## T01U1 — The Nature of Real Estate Finance

Real estate finance connects a purchase or investment today with income and capital available over time. A cash buyer supplies all purchase funds. A financed buyer supplies equity and borrows the remainder, promising repayment and usually pledging the property as security. The lender exchanges present cash for a stream of future payments. The property supports recovery if repayment fails; its value is not a substitute for determining whether the borrower can make the payments.

Keep three amounts separate: price, value, and debt. Price is the negotiated consideration. Appraised value is an opinion at a stated date under identified assumptions. Debt is the outstanding obligation. Equity is value less debt, not the amount originally paid as a down payment. A property worth $360,000 with $288,000 owed has $72,000 of gross equity. Sale expenses, other liens, and payoff interest reduce the owner's eventual net proceeds.

chunks.heading: T01U1 — The Nature of Real Estate Finance
chunks.excerpt:
Loan-to-value (LTV) expresses the first mortgage as a percentage of the value basis used by the program. For many purchase programs, the calculation uses the lower of price and appraised value. A $285,000 loan on a $300,000 price and $310,000 appraisal therefore has a 95% purchase LTV when that program rule applies. Do not divide by the higher appraisal to manufacture a lower ratio. Combined LTV includes subordinate mortgage balances in the numerator; a revolving credit line may require an additional ratio based on its full line amount.

Leverage magnifies changes in equity. If the first property rises from $360,000 to $378,000 while debt remains $288,000, the $18,000 gain equals 25% of the original $72,000 equity before costs. If value falls $18,000, equity falls by the same percentage. Borrowing has not created appreciation; it has changed who bears the result of a price movement. Cash flow is a separate test: a valuable property can still have unaffordable monthly payments.

Consider why lenders examine both equity and cash reserves. Suppose two buyers each put $80,000 into otherwise identical purchases. One retains $35,000 in documented savings; the other spends the last available dollar on closing. Their purchase LTVs can be identical, yet an uninsured repair or an interruption in wages affects them differently. Equity may require a sale, new loan, transaction expense, or lender approval to access. A bank-account reserve is not the same asset as an owner's estimate of market appreciation. Conversely, large reserves do not resolve a title defect or a property's ineligibility. Finance is a series of separate tests, not one number that substitutes for all others.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A01 — Equity and liquidity
chunks.excerpt:
An investment example adds another distinction. A rental produces $28,000 in annual income after operating expenses but before debt service. Its annual mortgage payments are $22,000. The resulting $6,000 cash flow is not identical to taxable income or total investment return. Some mortgage payment reduces principal; depreciation and tax treatment require separate analysis; future sale proceeds depend on value and costs. If a major repair requires $9,000 beyond the operating assumptions, the year can have negative cash flow despite positive operating income. Always state whether a figure includes vacancy, management, repairs, replacement reserves, taxes, insurance, and financing. An attractive percentage built from an incomplete numerator is not a reliable comparison.

Positive leverage describes circumstances in which borrowed funds improve an equity return under the stated assumptions. It is not a permanent property characteristic. A property earning less than its financing cost can experience the reverse. Even when expected return exceeds borrowing cost, timing matters: rents arrive on particular dates, while debt payments are due whether every tenant pays or not. A lender's collateral protection and an investor's return objective also differ. The lender generally seeks repayment of its agreed claim; the owner receives the residual benefit and bears the first loss in equity. This order explains why a modest change in property value can be substantial relative to the owner's invested cash.

### Applied exercise: A01 — Equity and liquidity

chunks.heading: T01U2 — Mortgage Lending Activities
chunks.excerpt:
Write a four-line calculation for a $425,000 purchase with a $340,000 first loan, a $21,250 second loan, and $12,000 closing costs paid by the buyer. Calculate first LTV, combined LTV, cash down payment, and total cash needed before any deposit credit. Then test a resale at $400,000 with unchanged balances and hypothetical selling costs equal to 6% of resale price. Explain whether original down-payment cash equals cash returned at sale.

Feedback: first LTV is 80%; combined LTV is 85%; the down payment is $63,750; cash required is $75,750. At resale, $400,000 − $24,000 − $340,000 − $21,250 leaves $14,750, before payoff adjustments. The loan balances did not shrink merely because the property fell in value. A $425,000 purchase does not establish a guaranteed resale value. Revise any answer that treats closing costs as equity or overlooks the second lien.

## T01U2 — Mortgage Lending Activities

Origination begins the credit relationship: a borrower applies, the originator discusses products and terms within the originator's authority, and the lender determines whether to extend credit. Processing assembles evidence. Underwriting evaluates that evidence against applicable law, program standards, and lender policy. Closing documents the transaction; funding supplies the money under the lender's conditions. Servicing collects payments, administers escrow when applicable, maintains records, and handles delinquency and loss mitigation. A business may perform several roles, but the roles remain distinct.

chunks.heading: T01U2 — Mortgage Lending Activities
chunks.excerpt:
A mortgage broker generally arranges financing with a lender. A mortgage banker makes loans in its own name and may fund them through a warehouse line before sale. Neither business label alone tells a consumer the interest rate, total cost, or likelihood of approval. Ask which legal entity is the creditor, which entity will service the loan, whether the quoted terms are locked, what remains subject to verification, and what compensation is disclosed. A real estate sales license is not a blanket mortgage-originator authorization.

Selling the loan transfers an asset from one owner to another. Transferring servicing changes the party administering payments. The events can occur together or separately. A borrower should use authenticated transfer notices and preserve payment records. A sale of a mortgage ordinarily does not permit the purchaser to replace the borrower's agreed fixed rate with a different rate simply because market rates changed. The enforceable documents, applicable law, and servicing notices govern the transaction.

Read approval descriptions precisely. A verbal estimate based on self-reported income is not an underwritten commitment. A conditional approval remains conditional; unresolved appraisal, title, employment, insurance, or asset issues can stop funding. A license holder should communicate deadlines, direct financing questions to the lender, and document material changes without guaranteeing approval. If a borrower loses employment before closing, concealing that fact is not a way to protect the transaction.

chunks.heading: T01U2 — Mortgage Lending Activities
chunks.excerpt:
Treat the file as a chain of evidence with accountable handoffs. An application describes the borrower's representations at a time. Source documents support or contradict those representations. An underwriting condition identifies something still needed. A clear-to-close message states a lender status but does not mean the title company already has authorized funds. A signed note creates the documented debt obligation under applicable law; recording gives public notice of an instrument but does not by itself prove that the correct loan funded. Asking “where is the file?” is therefore less useful than asking “which condition remains, who can clear it, and by what deadline?”

Conflicting information should move through that chain explicitly. If a buyer accepts a new auto loan, the lender may need to reassess the debt and available cash. If the property sustains storm damage, insurance, collateral condition, and completion evidence may matter. The real estate agent should not decide the underwriting result. The agent can notify the lender with the buyer's authorization, help coordinate the contract timeline within the agent's authority, and avoid representing an earlier conditional approval as unchanged. Good coordination preserves facts even when the facts threaten a commission or closing date.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A02 — Trace the file
chunks.excerpt:
A rate lock is another separate agreement. Its expiration, product, amount, pricing assumptions, extension terms, and conditions need review. A lock does not waive income verification or guarantee that a borrower qualifies after a material change. A floating quote is not a lock merely because it appears in an email. When comparing lenders, ask them to identify the same transaction assumptions and the exact status of the quote. This makes the comparison useful without asking an agent to make an unauthorized credit commitment.

### Applied exercise: A02 — Trace the file

Create a process chart for this file: Camila applies with Bridge Broker; Cedar Funding issues the Loan Estimate; an underwriter requests bank statements; a title company signs documents with Camila; Cedar funds; North Investor buys the loan; Cedar continues collecting payments. Label the broker, creditor, processor/underwriter task, settlement task, investor, and servicer. Identify two questions Camila should resolve before assuming she can close.

Feedback: Bridge arranges, Cedar is the originating creditor, North is the later owner, and Cedar retains servicing. The title company does not become the creditor by handling signing. Appropriate open questions include whether remaining approval conditions are satisfied and whether funds are available by the contractual deadline. A chart that uses one generic “bank” box hides accountability.

## T01U3 — Real Estate Cycles

chunks.heading: T01U3 — Real Estate Cycles
chunks.excerpt:
Real estate markets change through expansion, slowing demand, contraction, and recovery, but those labels describe patterns after examining data. They are not a timetable. Housing supply responds slowly because land acquisition, approvals, construction, and infrastructure take time. Financing can adjust quickly. A rapid change in payments may reduce demand while projects begun under older assumptions are still delivering inventory.

Follow several indicators together: active listings, months of inventory, closed sales, pending contracts, price changes, concessions, vacancy, construction starts, employment, and household formation. Months of inventory divides available inventory by the sales pace for a comparable period. With 1,200 listings and 300 monthly sales, the simple measure is four months. If sales fall to 200 with listings unchanged, it becomes six months even though no new listing was added. That arithmetic explains why one indicator can move for different reasons.

Geography and property type matter. A statewide median cannot establish the trend for a specific subdivision, price tier, apartment building, or rural tract. Median price may rise because expensive homes make up a larger share of closings, even if individual comparable homes have not appreciated. Transaction volume can fall while prices stay sticky because sellers withdraw listings rather than accept lower offers. Concessions may change the economic price before the recorded price changes.

chunks.heading: T01U3 — Real Estate Cycles
chunks.excerpt:
Lending and property cycles interact. Strong recent performance can encourage looser projections, more development, and greater leverage. Weak performance may produce tighter credit just when borrowers need refinancing. A maturing balloon loan exposes that interaction: the scheduled debt remains due even if the property's value and the availability of replacement credit have fallen. A stress test asks what happens under adverse assumptions without claiming to predict when adversity will occur.

Build a market explanation from observations before applying a cycle label. Suppose a builder offers a $15,000 financing incentive while maintaining a $400,000 recorded price. A resale seller reduces the price to $390,000 with no incentive. Those are not automatically identical economic offers. Restrictions on the incentive, lender choice, points, usable closing costs, loan balance, appraisal treatment, and intended holding period affect the comparison. An index based only on recorded prices may not show the entire change in negotiated terms. A license holder should describe documented terms and obtain qualified valuation or lending review instead of subtracting every advertised incentive from price as if it were cash.

Inventory also needs a consistent denominator. Comparing a single unusually slow holiday month with a twelve-month average can produce a different measure from using the same monthly method in both periods. A seasonally adjusted series and an unadjusted series answer different questions. A small number of rural sales can make a percentage change volatile. Record sample size and method before explaining a trend. These cautions do not make data useless; they make the conclusion proportional to what the data can establish.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A03 — Competing market signals
chunks.excerpt:
### Applied exercise: A03 — Competing market signals

A hypothetical county has 900 listings and 300 monthly sales in period one, then 1,100 listings and 220 monthly sales in period two. Its median closed price rises from $320,000 to $330,000. Calculate inventory months, write two plausible explanations for the rising median, and state what evidence you would need before advising that a particular house appreciated. Separately test a $200,000 balloon debt against a refinance lender willing to lend 75% of a $240,000 current value.

Feedback: inventory rises from three to five months. The median may reflect mix, actual appreciation, or both; comparable-property and concession evidence are needed. The refinance supports $180,000, leaving a $20,000 gap before costs. A higher county median does not eliminate that borrower-specific gap.

## T01U4 — Impact of the Economy

Mortgage pricing responds to expectations about inflation, longer-term yields, credit losses, liquidity, prepayments, servicing costs, capital requirements, and competition. The Federal Reserve influences financial conditions, but it does not publish the contractual rate every lender must give a household. A change in a short-term policy target is therefore not a promise that a particular 30-year mortgage quote will move by the same amount or on the same day.

Higher wages can improve repayment capacity; job loss can reduce it. Rising construction costs can constrain supply; falling demand can offset that pressure on prices. Inflation may erode purchasing power even if nominal income rises. The right explanation identifies the channel and the assumptions. “Rates rose, therefore every home must fall in price” skips local supply, incomes, credit standards, and seller behavior.

chunks.heading: T01U4 — Impact of the Economy
chunks.excerpt:
For a level-payment fixed-rate loan, payment is P × r ÷ [1 − (1 + r)^−n], where P is principal, r is the monthly periodic rate, and n is monthly payments. On a hypothetical $300,000 loan over 360 months, principal and interest are approximately $1,798.65 at 6% and $1,995.91 at 7%. The $197.26 increase excludes taxes, insurance, mortgage insurance, and association charges. A borrower comparing only house price can overlook a meaningful payment difference.

A payment sensitivity calculation holds selected inputs constant to isolate one change. That is useful, but it is not a forecast. If the interest rate rises while the loan amount falls, the actual payment difference will differ from the rate-only comparison. If property taxes increase, a fixed-rate borrower's total monthly housing cost can rise without any change in the note rate. If household income rises less than essential expenses, an unchanged mortgage payment can become harder to carry. Explain which variable moved and which were held constant rather than using the word “affordable” as a universal fact.

For a practical stress test, separate a base case, an adverse case, and a response. The base case uses documented income and realistic recurring expenses. The adverse case can reduce income, increase insurance, include a repair, or assume a longer vacancy for an investment. The response identifies usable reserves, discretionary adjustments, or the need to choose a different purchase. Do not assume access to a future refinance as the only solution. Credit conditions, property value, and personal eligibility may all be less favorable precisely when the borrower needs replacement financing.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A04 — Affordability explanation
chunks.excerpt:
Keep a borrower-facing comparison intelligible. Show the amount borrowed, term, rate assumption, P&I, other required housing charges, cash needed now, and reserves afterward. State whether a payment figure is quoted by a lender or calculated for education. If the offers use different balances or terms, explain that before discussing savings. A consumer should be able to reproduce the subtraction and see what was omitted. For an investment, label operating assumptions and financing separately. For an owner-occupied home, do not disguise maintenance as zero merely because it is not collected by the servicer. A clear comparison is a decision aid; it is not an appraisal, credit decision, tax opinion, or assurance that a future refinance will be available.

### Applied exercise: A04 — Affordability explanation

Using the two hypothetical payments above, calculate the annual payment difference. Write a client explanation that separates rate sensitivity from approval and includes at least three ownership expenses absent from principal and interest. Then explain why a lender still needs the borrower's documented income, debts, and assets.

Feedback: $197.26 × 12 = $2,367.12 using rounded monthly figures. Taxes, hazard/flood insurance when applicable, mortgage insurance, association dues, maintenance, and utilities can materially change the household budget. A calculated payment neither documents ability to repay nor commits the lender to a loan.

### Applied exercise: A71 — A financing decision under two stresses

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A71 — A financing decision under two stresses
chunks.excerpt:
Prepare a one-page comparison for two hypothetical buyers considering the same $350,000 residence. Both propose a $280,000 loan and $10,000 in buyer-paid closing costs. Buyer Elena has $105,000 of available cash before closing; buyer Noah has $83,000. The supplied all-in housing expense is $2,350 monthly, other essential monthly spending is $3,200, and each household's take-home income is $6,100. These are budgeting inputs, not lender qualifying income. Neither household has other liquid assets in this example.

First reconcile down payment, total cash required, reserves after closing, and normal monthly budget cushion for each household. Then model a $7,000 urgent repair and two months of a $1,200 monthly income reduction occurring together. Calculate reserves after those stresses, assuming the normal monthly cushion remains available and is applied during those two months. Finally model a sale immediately after closing at $330,000 with selling costs equal to 5% of price and an unchanged $280,000 payoff. Compare sale proceeds with the original cash investment, and write a four-sentence explanation that distinguishes lender qualification, liquidity, market loss, and the need for an individual decision. Do not recommend either buyer proceed solely because the LTV is 80%.

chunks.heading: T01U5 — Information Resources
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: the down payment is $70,000 and initial cash required is $80,000. Elena retains $25,000; Noah retains $3,000. The normal monthly cushion is $550. Each stressed month has a $650 deficit, so the combined repair and two-month deficit consume $8,300. Elena retains $16,700; Noah has a $5,300 shortfall requiring another lawful source or a changed plan. Resale net before loan payoff is $313,500, leaving $33,500 after the debt. That is $46,500 less than the original $80,000 cash outlay. This comparison intentionally omits other payoff adjustments and ownership cash flows. Correct work shows every assumption and does not confuse market equity with cash already available to pay bills.

## T01U5 — Information Resources

A financing claim is only as useful as its source, date, scope, and assumptions. For credit regulations, start with the implementing agency's current text. For Texas law, use the statute and current TREC or mortgage-regulator guidance appropriate to the issue. For program eligibility, use the administering agency and current lender program materials. For a mortgage offer, use the actual Loan Estimate and lock agreement. For market analysis, identify the dataset, observation period, geography, definitions, revisions, and limitations.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A05 — Evidence memo
chunks.excerpt:
Useful primary publishers include the Federal Reserve for monetary policy, the Bureau of Labor Statistics for employment and inflation, the Census Bureau for construction and housing data, FHFA for enterprise and housing finance information, CFPB for consumer-credit regulations, HUD for FHA, VA for veterans' lending, USDA for its programs, TDHCA for Texas housing assistance, and county offices for local public records. An article may help locate an issue but is not a substitute for the rule or program document that decides it.

Do not present an undated search excerpt as a current rate sheet. Record “verified on” separately from “effective on” and the period the data measure. A report published this month may describe last quarter. If sources conflict, check whether they cover different loan types, populations, dates, or stages of approval before declaring one wrong. Keep personal borrower documents in authorized secure systems; collecting information does not authorize publishing it in a training example.

Create a compact source log rather than a folder of unexplained links. Useful fields are the question, publisher, document title, operative section or data table, publication date, effective or observation date, date checked, and limitation. For an invented classroom calculation, say that the figures are supplied assumptions and show the formula; attaching an agency homepage does not turn an original example into an agency finding. For a genuine legal claim, a homepage is usually too broad: find the relevant section and read the exceptions. This distinction prevents a well-formatted reference list from giving unsupported advice an appearance of authority.

### Applied exercise: A05 — Evidence memo

chunks.heading: Statute reading exercise: S09 — Evaluate a monetary-policy explanation
chunks.excerpt:
Draft an evidence request for each claim: “The Fed guarantees that mortgage rates fall next week”; “Every Texas buyer receives down-payment assistance”; “The lender approved this buyer”; “The county's median proves this house's value.” For each, identify the appropriate primary source and the missing factual condition. Do not search for a quotation merely to endorse the claim.

Feedback: none of the claims is established as written. Policy information does not guarantee a retail quote; assistance requires program-specific eligibility and available funds; approval requires the lender's actual written status and remaining conditions; individual value needs property-specific analysis. A good memo converts an overstatement into a verifiable question.

### Statute reading exercise: S09 — Evaluate a monetary-policy explanation

Read the Federal Reserve's [policy tools overview](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/policytools.htm) and follow its open-market-operations and interest-on-reserve-balances explanations. These are official source readings, not a direction to use today's rate as a quote. Build a five-row evidence log: publisher, tool, institution or market directly affected, claimed connection to household credit, and a limitation. Then annotate this proposed client message: “A policy change means your mortgage quote and home's value will each move by the same percentage tomorrow, so the approval is certain.” Identify every unsupported leap. Replace it with a conditional explanation that distinguishes monetary-policy implementation, market pricing, a lender's actual offer, and borrower underwriting. Record the date and title of the pages used; do not copy a rate table into the answer.

chunks.heading: Module recap
chunks.excerpt:
Feedback: the official pages explain policy instruments, not a guaranteed retail mortgage, property-price movement, or loan approval. The revised message should connect policy to financial conditions while reserving the actual terms to the lender's verified offer and the approval to underwriting. An adequate log identifies a real page passage for the tool description and labels the remaining causal discussion as analysis. If the linked page changes, follow the Fed's current navigation and document the replacement source rather than inventing missing text.

### Module recap

Explain, in your own words, how a purchase, a loan, a security interest, loan ownership, and servicing fit together. Recalculate one leverage example without looking at the answer, then identify a source you would consult before giving current program information. Complete the separate T01 topic quiz and any assigned related replacement question.

Sources: [CFPB, buying a house and comparing loan offers](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/); [Federal Reserve, monetary-policy tools](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/policytools.htm); [FHFA, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac](https://www.fhfa.gov/about-fannie-mae-freddie-mac). Calculations and transaction examples are original instructional examples.

lessons.title: Module 02: Money & the Monetary System

chunks.heading: Module 02: Money & the Monetary System
chunks.excerpt:
# Module 02: Money & the Monetary System

REF-0 topic T02 suggests 100 minutes. This module distinguishes the institutions that issue money, conduct monetary policy, insure deposits, and supply liquidity to lenders. Its examples explain mechanisms; they do not predict rates or investment returns.

## T02U1 — What is Money & The Federal Reserve System

Money serves as a medium of exchange, unit of account, and store of value. A bank deposit is a claim on a bank and can function as money in payments. A house, bond, or stock may be valuable without being money that a seller routinely accepts for settlement. Liquidity describes the ability to meet obligations or convert an asset to usable funds without unacceptable loss. Net worth and liquidity are different: a borrower can have substantial home equity yet lack the cash required at closing.

The Federal Reserve is the United States central bank. Its structure includes the Board of Governors, twelve regional Reserve Banks, and the Federal Open Market Committee. The FOMC makes monetary-policy decisions; Reserve Banks perform operational functions such as payment services and lending to eligible depository institutions. The Federal Reserve is not a consumer mortgage lender and does not approve a buyer's credit application.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A06 — Classify the balance sheet
chunks.excerpt:
Banks connect funding sources with credit demand, subject to capital, liquidity, supervision, risk management, and legal constraints. A bank's ability to lend should not be explained solely as a mechanical multiple of cash in a vault. Deposits, borrowing, asset sales, payment flows, credit demand, and prudential requirements all matter. Distinguish bank capital, which absorbs losses, from liquid assets, which meet cash demands. An institution can encounter liquidity pressure even when its assets are expected to exceed liabilities over time.

### Applied exercise: A06 — Classify the balance sheet

A hypothetical lender holds $12 million in cash and $88 million in loans; it owes $90 million to depositors and other creditors. Calculate its accounting equity. If $18 million in deposits leave immediately, identify the liquidity gap before asset sales or new borrowing. Explain why the equity calculation does not itself solve the withdrawal problem.

Feedback: assets are $100 million and liabilities $90 million, so equity is $10 million. Cash is $6 million short of the requested withdrawals. Selling assets, collecting payments, or obtaining funding may supply liquidity, each with constraints and possible costs. Equity is not a separate $10 million cash account available to add automatically to the $12 million cash balance.

## T02U2 — Instruments of Credit Policy

chunks.heading: T02U2 — Instruments of Credit Policy
chunks.excerpt:
The Federal Reserve's published tool inventory includes open market operations, the discount window, interest on reserve balances, overnight reverse repurchase operations, reserve requirements, and other liquidity tools. Their functions differ. Buying or selling securities changes the central bank balance sheet and reserve conditions. Interest paid on reserve balances affects incentives for banks holding reserve balances. The discount window supplies collateralized central bank credit to eligible institutions subject to its terms. A reverse repurchase operation temporarily exchanges securities and cash under an agreement to reverse the transaction.

Do not teach that changing reserve requirements is the only or routine way monetary policy currently operates. A list of historically important tools is not evidence that each is being changed today. The relevant operating framework and tool settings must be verified from the Federal Reserve's current materials. This course asks you to understand functions, not memorize an unverified current target or reserve percentage.

Transmission takes time and is uncertain. Policy affects short-term funding conditions; expectations influence longer-term yields; financial institutions price credit; households and businesses respond. Mortgage-backed security investors also consider how quickly borrowers may prepay. A fixed mortgage's long cash-flow horizon and prepayment option make its pricing different from an overnight interbank transaction. A policy announcement and a mortgage quote are related through markets, not through an automatic one-for-one formula.

chunks.heading: Applied exercise: A07 — Trace a policy claim
chunks.excerpt:
Distinguish an administered rate from a market yield. An administered rate is set for an identified facility or balance under the Federal Reserve's operating framework. A market yield emerges from trading and expectations about future cash flows and risk. Even when they move together, they are not the same contractual number. A lender funding a long-term mortgage must also consider the possibility that borrowers refinance early, the cost of hedging a pipeline, and what investors will pay for the resulting asset. Those considerations help explain why a retail quote can move before an announced policy decision or move differently afterward.

Be cautious with the textbook claim that every dollar of reserves creates an exact fixed multiple of mortgage lending. That mechanical illustration omits capital, liquidity requirements, borrower demand, risk appetite, funding costs, and underwriting constraints. A bank with additional liquidity need not find an eligible borrower for every available dollar. A bank with strong loan demand still must fund its commitments and manage loss risk. The useful question is which constraint is binding in the actual institution and transaction. This course uses balance-sheet arithmetic to organize the facts, not to promise a fixed economy-wide lending multiplier.

### Applied exercise: A07 — Trace a policy claim
